t: The problems of the "platform rent thesis" in the light of Marx's theory of the circuit of capital, and how to correct them
zh: 马克思资本循环理论视域下“平台租金说”的问题及其矫正
source: Studies on Marxism (马克思主义研究), 2026 no. 2
paras: Are the huge profits of giant digital platforms best understood as "digital surplus value" or as "digital ground rent"? Huang Zaisheng takes up this debate and argues that the "platform rent thesis" (data rent, "cloud rent", the "techno-feudalism" line) misreads digital capital. In Huang's account, the thesis stays inside the sphere of circulation, ignores digital labour and the platforms' productive activity, and so cannot show the full circuit of digital capital. The author proposes to correct it with Marx's theory of the circuit of capital.

The article has four parts after the introduction. It first sets out the thesis's four "rents" (data, cognitive or knowledge, transaction and traffic, and cloud) and contrasts them with what the author calls four productive roles of platforms. These are forming data factors, researching and developing digital-intelligent technology, producing digital space, and supplying services. It then explains how the thesis reduces the circuit of digital capital and why it errs, and what harm follows. Finally it offers a corrected account. Huang draws on figures on platform R&D spending, AI model output and cloud-computing revenue, and cites Evgeny Morozov's criticism of techno-feudalism.

Huang's central move is that the thesis treats platforms as pure intermediaries, a new commercial capital whose circuit collapses into M–M′, like interest-bearing capital. The author traces this to three sources: free services that obscure production, platforms' self-description as mere "markets", and a mechanical reading of Marx's claim that circulation creates no value. Against this, Huang argues that platforms commodify digital-intelligent services (business intelligence, precision marketing, cloud computing) and that digital labour creates value, from user-generated data and crowd-sourced labelling to algorithm development. Digital capital is therefore a composite. It runs the full industrial circuit M–C…P…C′–M′. It also acts as commercial capital with a "dual circulation" pattern. In addition, it shows features of fictitious capital under the "growth first, profit later" model.

The author concludes that the thesis, if left to spread, would saddle platform economies with a bad reputation, erase the value contribution of digital labour and mislead regulators. Huang adds that the virtualisation of digital capital, driven by data worship and "intelligence fetishism", carries the seeds of a digital-capitalist economic crisis. The author presents this as a way to understand digital capital in China's socialist market economy and to promote high-quality development of the platform economy. Read the original if you work on digital capitalism, rent versus surplus-value debates, or Chinese Marxist readings of the platform economy.
quoteEn: Fundamentally, digital capital is a capital complex with complicated attributes and changeable characteristics.
quoteZh: 根本上讲，数字资本是一个属性复杂、特性多变的资本复合体。

glossary.explanation: The author's label for views holding that digital platforms profit mainly from rent (data rent, cloud rent and so on) rather than from producing surplus value. It covers ideas such as techno-feudalism and data colonialism.
An official Chinese policy goal since the late 2010s that stresses innovation, efficiency and sustainability over raw growth.
The official name for China's economic system, which combines market mechanisms with public ownership and state guidance. It was formally adopted in the early 1990s.

t: How Chinese modernization resolves the modernization predicament of the Global South, and why it matters
zh: 中国式现代化对全球南方现代化困境的破解及其意义
paras: Dai Xuehong asks why the countries of the Global South have struggled to modernize and how Chinese modernization answers that predicament. Opening from Xi Jinping's remarks on the collective rise of the Global South, the article argues that Western modernization created a structural predicament for latecomers. In Dai's account, Chinese modernization has broken through it and offers the wider South a path, momentum and theory.

The article has three parts. The first sets out four sources of the predicament: predatory colonial expansion, the "core–periphery" structure, the capitalist system of global accumulation, and ecological imperialism. The second pairs each with a Chinese answer. The third describes the world significance of that answer under three headings: path options, development momentum and theoretical contribution. Dai draws on world-systems and dependency theory (including Samir Amin), Marx's theory of capital and the notion of metabolic rift.

In Dai's reading, Western modernization depended on plunder, then on unequal exchange and conditional aid that locked the South into dependence, and on shifting capital's crises and pollution southwards. Chinese modernization is said to answer these with peaceful development, independent self-reliance combined with opening up, a people-centred approach that "harnesses" capital under a socialist framework, and harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature. Dai holds that China has crossed the "Caudine Forks" of capitalism, which the author treats as structurally similar to the situation of the Global South. Its aid carries no political conditions, and the Belt and Road Initiative supplies public goods. Dai also says it breaks the Western monopoly on modernization discourse, and presents the Four Global Initiatives as a theoretical contribution.

Dai concludes that Chinese modernization is not a model to be exported but offers distinctive path choices, such as a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical balance, ecological harmony and peace. It also supplies momentum and theoretical resources for the South's collective modernization, with a community with a shared future for mankind as its goal. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese Marxist scholarship uses dependency and world-systems arguments to present Chinese modernization as a response to the Global South's development problems.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization not only serves as a "weapon of criticism" that breaks the Western monopoly over modernization theory, but also, as the "criticism of weapons", confirms through successful practice the plurality of modernization theory.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化不仅作为“批判的武器”，打破了西方现代化理论的话语垄断，而且作为“武器的批判”，以成功的现代化实践确证了现代化理论的多元性。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, stressing a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical balance, harmony with nature and peaceful development. It was elaborated especially after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A collective term for developing countries and emerging economies. Chinese official discourse places China among them and presents itself as a driving force for their joint development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations based on cooperation, shared security and common development, used as a goal of Chinese foreign policy.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking Asia, Africa and Europe.
The official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as an essential requirement of socialism.
Marx's late metaphor, in his writings on Russia, for the possibility of a society bypassing the full capitalist stage of development. Chinese scholars apply it to China's socialist modernization.

t: Combining an efficient market with an effective government to promote "Little Giant" enterprises
zh: 有效市场与有为政府结合 推动“小巨人”企业发展
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in September 2026, asks how policy can best support the specialised, refined, distinctive and innovative "Little Giant" enterprises. Zeng Xiankui argues that these firms are a backbone of the real economy, especially manufacturing, and matter for advanced manufacturing, supply-chain resilience and new quality productive forces. In Zeng's view, the core task is an efficient industrial ecosystem that joins firms' rapid short-term growth with long-term sustainability, and the key is to combine market mechanisms with a more proactive government.
The piece sets out four lines of action: fiscal and tax tools, support for technological innovation, a wider industrial ecosystem, and locally tailored development models.

On the first, Zeng proposes rewards and subsidies to ease the weak finances of small and medium-sized firms, support for digital transformation and technical upgrading, and fiscal rewards or tax relief for firms that reach R&D thresholds. On innovation, Zeng wants government to broker cooperation with universities and research institutes, fund major technological projects, open large research instruments to shared use, and strengthen intellectual property protection so that competition rewards the strongest firms. On the ecosystem, Zeng calls for easing constraints on talent, capital and data through special loans, support for listing, postdoctoral workstations and fast-track channels for senior talent, together with graded cultivation systems and a "one enterprise, one policy" officer system.

Zeng concludes that regions should build on local industrial bases and resource endowments, giving the example of eastern regions backing "Little Giants" in artificial intelligence and robotics, and should design systematic policy packages suited to local difficulties. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style account of the policy instruments Chinese commentators link to the "Little Giant" programme.
quoteEn: The core task in promoting the high-quality development of "Little Giant" enterprises at present is to build an efficient industrial ecosystem and achieve an organic unity of firms' rapid short-term growth and long-term sustainable development.
quoteZh: 当前，推动“小巨人”企业高质量发展的核心任务，是建立高效产业生态体系，实现企业短期快速成长与长期可持续发展的有机统一。

glossary.pinyin: zhuān jīng tè xīn “xiǎo jùrén” qǐyè
glossary.literal: specialised, refined, distinctive and innovative 'little giant' enterprises
glossary.explanation: A government-designated category of small and medium-sized firms that specialise in niche products, with strong technology and market positions. It is used in industrial policy to support manufacturing and supply-chain security.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, such as advanced manufacturing and digital technologies.

t: New requirements and tasks for accelerating the building of a modern economic system
zh: 加快建设现代化经济体系的新要求和新任务
paras: Written in the wake of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) and its Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, this article asks what it takes to achieve a "major breakthrough" in building a modern economic system by 2030. Qiao Xiaonan argues that only by combining breakthroughs in key areas with coordinated advance across the whole system can China release its economic potential. The result, Qiao contends, would be an effective improvement in the quality of growth alongside a reasonable increase in its quantity, supporting decisive progress towards basically realising socialist modernization.

The article has four parts. The first explains why the modern economic system underpins Chinese modernization, and reads it through a systems perspective as six "systems" and one "mechanism": industry, urban-rural and regional development, green development, opening up, income distribution, a unified market, and the economic institutions. The second concerns technological and industrial innovation, new quality productive forces and the green development system. The third deals with strategic economic layout, and the fourth with production relations suited to new quality productive forces, including distribution, urban-rural and regional coordination, and the market economy.

Qiao's central claims are several. Growth remains a necessary basis for development: with 2024 per capita GDP of US$13,445, the article holds that average annual growth of 4.5–5 per cent is still needed to approach the level of moderately developed countries. A country of over 1.4 billion people cannot rely on export-led growth, so the domestic cycle must be strengthened, and investment in things must be balanced with investment in people. Drawing on Marx's theory of machine industry, Qiao argues that intelligent production raises the organic composition of capital, reduces employment absorption and the labour share and widens income gaps. Common prosperity, income rising in step with growth, and a high-level socialist market economy are therefore presented as conditions for accommodating advanced productive forces.

Qiao concludes with a programme: self-reliant science and technology, an "AI Plus" initiative, a manufacturing-centred industrial system that does not neglect traditional industries, carbon peaking and neutrality, a unified national market, institutional opening up and an income distribution tilted towards labour. Throughout, the article presents the Party's leadership and an effective market working with an enabling government as the framework. Read the original if you want a Marxist political-economy rationale, from within the Chinese academy, for the 15th Five-Year Plan's economic priorities.
quoteEn: Only by taking common prosperity as the orientation, promoting high-quality and full employment and working to raise the labour share can the demand structure be optimised and total demand expanded, capacity utilisation raised, and the domestic cycle genuinely strengthened.
quoteZh: 只有以共同富裕为导向，促进高质量充分就业，着力提升劳动报酬占比，才能够带动需求结构优化与需求总量扩张，提高产能利用水平，切实做强国内大循环。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping since the 19th Party Congress (2017), describing an integrated economy of industrial, market, distribution, green and open sub-systems. The article reads it as comprising six systems and one mechanism.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented as socialist in essence and distinct from Western models.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, especially in high-tech and digital fields.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, described as an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Socialist culture with Chinese characteristics for a new era: connotation, functions and guiding principles
zh: 新时代中国特色社会主义文化：内涵、功能与遵循
paras: Shang Zhixiao examines a concept given prominence by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025): "socialist culture with Chinese characteristics for a new era". The article asks what the concept means, what work it does and what should guide its development. Shang argues that the term gathers earlier formulations into one overarching idea, and that developing such a culture is now the central task of cultural construction in the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

The article has three parts. The first traces how Xi Jinping introduced the term in 2023 and used it again in 2024, and how the Fourth Plenum made it a core planning concept. The second sets out four functions drawn from Xi's formulation: ideological guidance, spiritual cohesion, value appeal and international influence. The third turns to guiding principles for implementation.

On meaning, Shang reads the concept through three anchors. Its essential character is socialist culture, since in the Marxist view culture takes its nature from the social formation on which it rests. Its practical basis is socialism with Chinese characteristics and Chinese modernization. Its historical position is the new era and the decisive stage of building a culture-strong nation by 2035. The term, Shang argues, narrows in extent but deepens in content compared with older labels. The four functions are said to form one whole, each tied to a different dimension: shared ideals, national identity, core socialist values and cross-civilisational exchange.

For implementation, Shang calls for adherence to the "three upholds" guidelines (serving the people and socialism, letting a hundred flowers bloom, creative transformation and innovative development). Shang also calls for cultural confidence, openness and inclusiveness, and keeping to fundamental principles while innovating. The author further urges linking past and present, China and abroad, and gives priorities: promoting core socialist values, developing cultural undertakings and industries, using digital technology, and strengthening international communication. Shang presents all this as implementing the Plenum's spirit and supporting Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a Party-theory account of how the new term consolidates earlier cultural vocabulary and how it is tied to cultural-policy priorities up to 2035.
quoteEn: The concept of \"socialist culture with Chinese characteristics for a new era\" has narrowed in extension but deepened in content.
quoteZh: “新时代中国特色社会主义文化”这一概念，在外延上收窄了，在内涵上却深化了。

glossary.zh: 新时代中国特色社会主义文化
glossary.pinyin: xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì wénhuà
glossary.en: socialist culture with Chinese characteristics for a new era
glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping first used in 2023 and the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) adopted as a core concept. The article presents it as bringing earlier cultural terms together.
A strategic goal, set out from the 18th Party Congress (2012) onward, of building China into a country with strong cultural capacity, with a target date of 2035.
The official term for the Party's account of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Twelve values promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), covering the national, social and individual levels, such as prosperity, democracy, patriotism and integrity.

glossary.en: keeping to fundamental principles while innovating
glossary.literal: preserve what is correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: A principle stressed by Xi Jinping for cultural work: maintain Marxism's guiding position while developing new ideas, forms and mechanisms.
A Party concept, part of the Four-sphere Confidence, calling for confidence in China's cultural tradition and in the culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Distinctive advantages of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics, viewed through social development
zh: 从社会发展看中国特色社会主义制度的显著优势
source: Contemporary World and Socialism (Dangdai shijie yu shehuizhuyi), 2026 no. 1
paras: Qin Gang asks where the institutional advantages of socialism with Chinese characteristics come from, how they show up in social development, and what lessons they offer. Starting from Xi Jinping's remark that institutional advantage is a country's greatest advantage, the article argues that these advantages are comprehensive. In Qin's account they rest on scientific socialism, Chinese cultural tradition, accumulated practice and the achievements of human civilisation, and are confirmed by results in economic and social development.

The article has three parts. The first traces four sources of the system's advantages: the institutionalisation of scientific socialist principles, the transformation of excellent traditional culture, the lifting of socialist practical experience into institutions, and the integration of civilisational achievements, including capitalist ones. The second part identifies five manifestations: centralised and unified leadership by the Party Central Committee; the people's principal position; concentrating resources on major undertakings; combining an effective market with a capable government; and scientifically drawn and effectively implemented national development plans. The third part draws four lessons.

Qin argues that Party leadership is the system's greatest advantage, since it produces unified will and common purpose, and that democratic centralism reconciles democracy with efficiency. The author presents the national-plan procedure (Party proposal, State Council drafting, National People's Congress approval) and the 'whole-nation chessboard' approach as sources of stability and rapid breakthroughs, citing projects from the 'two bombs and one satellite' programme to high-speed rail and poverty alleviation. The system is said to have solved the market–government problem and to have absorbed capitalist-era institutions such as the rule of law and modern enterprise systems by stripping out their original institutional character. Qin presents this as a transcendence of capitalism's internal contradictions.

The lessons Qin draws are that institutions must be built on specific historical conditions, with principles adapted rather than copied. They should take the people's well-being as their ultimate yardstick, be tested by practical results through pilot experiments and evaluation, and be improved through reform that perfects the system without overturning its basic framework. Qin concludes that the system secures China's rejuvenation and offers 'Chinese wisdom' and a 'Chinese approach' for humanity's search for fairer, more efficient and more inclusive institutions. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of how Party-school scholarship explains the sources and merits of China's institutional system, with the official vocabulary used throughout.
quoteEn: Whether an institution has advantages does not depend on theoretical deduction and exposition, but must be shown through its actual results in economic and social development.
quoteZh: 一种制度是否具有优势，不取决于理论上的推演和阐述，而是必须通过经济社会发展的实际成效来展现。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's official name for its path, theory and system since the reform era, combining Marxist principles with China's conditions.
The organisational principle of the Party and state, combining discussion and democratic participation with unified decision-making and discipline.

glossary.literal: concentrate strength to accomplish big things
glossary.explanation: A phrase used officially for the state's ability to mobilise resources nationwide for large strategic projects. It is often paired with 'the whole nation as one chessboard'.

t: The epochal basis, guiding principles and strategic measures of high-quality economic development
zh: 经济高质量发展的时代依据、指导原则与战略举措
source: Social Sciences in China (Zhongguo shehui kexue), 2026 no. 6
paras: Writing in the context of the Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), Liu Wei asks how China should understand and achieve high-quality development. The article argues that three elements form one logical system: grasping China's new historical position is the epochal basis, applying the new development philosophy is the guiding principle, and building the new development paradigm is the strategic measure. Together, Liu says, they answer why, on what principles and how high-quality development should proceed in order to advance Chinese modernization.

The article follows this three-part structure. The first section reviews the achievements that, in Liu's account, define the present position: GDP above 140 trillion yuan in 2025, the elimination of absolute poverty, a complete industrial system and expanding opening up. The second section treats the origins and content of the five-part new development philosophy and its link to high-quality development. The third discusses the new development paradigm, its basis in China's status as a large economy, and the relations it requires to be balanced. Liu draws on figures for GDP, trade, manufacturing, research spending and consumption throughout.

Liu's central argument is that the shift from rapid growth to high-quality development is demanded by changed conditions. Growth driven by factor inputs and low costs is no longer sustainable; reaching the 2035 modernization target needs about 4.8 per cent annual growth, which the old model is said to deliver at only around 4 per cent. Liu adds the pressure of the dual carbon goals, imbalances in development, Western containment and the technological revolution. The new development paradigm, presented as an extension of Marx's theory of capital circulation, is meant to turn this philosophy into practice. Its core is to strengthen the domestic circulation through a unified national market, integration of scientific and industrial innovation, secure industrial and supply chains and a dynamic balance of supply and demand, while promoting mutual reinforcement with international circulation.

Liu concludes that the Party's approach reflects a unity of historical, theoretical and practical logic and is a component of Xi Jinping's economic thought. The article also calls for coordinating relations between domestic demand and supply-side reform, self-reliance and openness, rural revitalization and urbanization, and market-economy reform and high-level opening up. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how the logic behind the 15th Five-Year Plan's economic approach is framed, with extensive statistics on China's development.
quoteEn: As a strategic concept and set of measures for achieving high-quality economic development, the new development paradigm answers in practice how to advance high-quality development and is the practical embodiment of the new development philosophy.
quoteZh: 新发展格局作为实现经济高质量发展的战略构想和方略举措，在实践中回应着如何推进经济高质量发展，是新发展理念的实践体现。

glossary.explanation: The five-part guideline of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, set out by Xi Jinping at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2015.
A strategy first put forward in 2020 that takes the domestic circulation as the mainstay, with domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other.
An official goal, stated at the 19th Party Congress (2017), of moving from high-speed growth to growth stressing quality, efficiency and new drivers.
The Party's official term for China's path to modernization, elaborated at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.
The idea that China's economy should rely mainly on internal production, distribution and consumption, with international trade complementing it.

t: Leading the building of a culturally strong country with the "six musts"
zh: 以“六个必须坚持”引领文化强国建设
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily, asks how the "six musts" set out in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) can guide the building of a culturally strong country. Zhou and Zhao argue that these six principles are the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and run through Xi Jinping's cultural thought. They hold that grasping this guiding role is important for stimulating cultural creativity and developing socialist culture.

The article takes the six principles in turn: putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, staying true to fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, a systems approach, and a global vision. Each is linked to one area of cultural work: the value orientation of culture, its subjective foundation, cultural inheritance, cultural security, the overall pattern of cultural development, and international exchange. The piece closes by looking ahead to the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

The authors tie each principle to a concrete task. The people-first principle, they say, unites the Party's cultural leadership with a people-centred orientation, and requires a modern public cultural service system and people's approval as the test of cultural work. Self-confidence and self-reliance mean consolidating the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation and promoting core socialist values. In the authors' account, the Two Integrations produce a "chemical reaction" rather than a simple addition, so that Marxism becomes Chinese and traditional culture becomes modern, while rejecting both revivalism and nihilism.

The problem-oriented principle is applied to the internet, described as the main front of ideological struggle, where the authors call for stronger guidance of public opinion and better online governance. The systems principle treats culture both as one field alongside the economy, politics, society and ecology and as a spirit permeating all of them. The global-vision principle is linked to the Global Civilization Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind, and Chinese modernization is said to have broken the equation of modernization with Westernization. The authors conclude that the six musts form an interconnected whole that gives China's cultural form of modernization the strength to support the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary links the Party Congress's methodological principles to cultural policy.
quoteEn: Staying true to fundamental principles provides the foundation for innovation, and innovation injects vitality into staying true; the two are dialectically unified and neither can be neglected even for a moment.
quoteZh: 守正为创新提供根基，创新为守正注入活力，二者辩证统一，须臾不可偏废。

glossary.literal: six things that must be adhered to
glossary.explanation: Six principles put forward in the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022): putting the people first, self-confidence and self-reliance, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, a problem-oriented approach, a systems approach, and a global vision. They are presented as the worldview and methodology of Xi Jinping Thought.
The body of Xi Jinping's ideas on culture, formally put forward in 2023, which is presented as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.
The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from the Western model.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations and global governance, promoted since 2012–13.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, referring to restoring China's strength and international standing by the middle of the twenty-first century.

An initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2023 that calls for respecting civilizational diversity, promoting common human values, valuing the inheritance and innovation of civilizations, and strengthening international cultural exchange.

t: The security implications of new quality productive forces
zh: 新质生产力的安全意蕴
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily, asks how development and security relate in the case of new quality productive forces. Qi Guang argues that security is an inherent attribute of these forces, rooted in their material, social and technical character and generated within their technological features and organisation. On this reading, developing new quality productive forces is also a continuous process of building security capacity.

The piece has four sections. It first sets out why new quality productive forces carry a security dimension. It then claims they resolve the traditional tension between development and security, and goes on to describe the security effects they show in the practice of Chinese modernization. It ends with proposals for using them as the productive-force base of a new security architecture. Qi relies throughout on quotations from Xi Jinping and on the 15th Five-Year Plan outline.

Qi's central move is to read the "high-tech, high-efficiency, high-quality" features of new quality productive forces as security conditions. Mastering frontier technology, reducing dependence on external resources and removing risks accumulated by extensive growth are each presented as sources of security. Qi contends that traditional productive forces rest on resource dependence, technological reliance and extensive scale expansion, which create vulnerability, subjection to others and accumulating systemic risk. New quality productive forces are said to overcome each of these. Qi also stresses supply-chain work (mending, extending, upgrading and building chains) and self-reliance in areas such as integrated circuits and industrial machine tools. The author sees this as moving the idea of balancing development and security from "security constraint" to "security empowerment", with the two reinforcing each other.

Qi concludes that new quality productive forces give the new security architecture its material and technological foundation, and that security capacity in turn widens the space for high-quality development. The author calls for a systems approach during the 15th Five-Year Plan period: a more prominent strategic place for new quality productive forces, joint advancement of education, science and technology, and talent, and stronger institutional design, policy supply and legal protection in key sectors. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary links productive-force theory to national security discourse.
quoteEn: The process of developing new quality productive forces is also a process in which security capacity is continuously generated.
quoteZh: 新质生产力的发展过程，也是安全能力持续生成的过程。

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official goal of the current development stage, which stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over scale and speed of growth.
An official formulation for a national security system that guarantees the new development pattern, linked to the holistic approach to national security.
A strategic principle in Xi Jinping Thought that treats development and security as mutually dependent and to be planned together.

t: Building an international communication narrative system for the four global initiatives
zh: 构建四大全球倡议国际传播叙事体系
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 2 July 2026, asks how China should communicate the Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilization Initiative and Global Governance Initiative to foreign audiences. Qiu and Chong open from the 15th Five-Year Plan outline, which calls for implementing the four initiatives. They argue that the initiatives need a scientifically complete international communication narrative system if they are to be understood and not misread abroad.

The authors define a narrative system as an organic whole made up of narrative logic, narrative text (content) and narrative techniques. The article is organised in three parts that follow these elements: establishing the logic, enriching the content and improving the techniques. Each part ends in concrete recommendations for communication work.

On logic, the authors propose three anchors: a problem orientation toward global challenges, described as the four deficits (peace, development, security and governance); guidance by the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind; and win-win cooperation as the main storyline. They want the initiatives presented as open platforms and public goods, not as an exclusive "small circle" or a tool of hegemony. On content, they say narratives should show the initiatives as a response to global problems, as practical support for building that community (material, security, spiritual and institutional dimensions), and as a path to cooperation, illustrated with concrete joint projects in each field. On technique, they recommend translating official policy language into forms suited to different cultures, with standardised multilingual terminology. They also propose coordinating government bodies, media, think tanks, universities, companies and civil groups, telling human stories through documentary and interview formats, and segmenting audiences, for example by offering light content to the general public and more theoretical analysis to scholars.

The authors conclude that a narrative system built this way would improve the effectiveness of international communication, help the international community reach consensus, and give China more initiative in international opinion. They also say it would help turn the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind from a declared value into an operational agenda. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese Party-school scholars frame the communication strategy for China's global initiatives.
quoteEn: Making win-win cooperation the main storyline of international communication can clearly show the four global initiatives' character as global public goods, and vividly convey China's firm conviction in promoting common development, upholding international fairness and justice, and joining hands with other countries to meet challenges.
quoteZh: 将合作共赢作为国际传播叙事主线，能够清晰彰显四大全球倡议的全球公共产品属性，鲜明传递中国推动世界共同发展、维护国际公平正义、携手各国共迎挑战的坚定信念。

glossary.explanation: A proposal put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021 focusing on poverty reduction, food security, development financing and climate change, linked to the UN 2030 Agenda.
A proposal introduced by Xi Jinping in 2022 advocating a common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security concept and the political settlement of conflicts.
A 2023 proposal calling for respect for the diversity of civilizations and for exchange and mutual learning among them.
The most recent of the four initiatives, presented as promoting reform of the global governance system through consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits, and upholding the UN's authority.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, presenting the world's countries as interdependent and sharing common interests.
Official shorthand for the peace, development, security and governance deficits that Chinese leaders say the world faces.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Taking the path of health development with Chinese characteristics is an inherent requirement of Chinese modernization
zh: 走中国特色卫生与健康发展道路是中国式现代化内在要求
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 4 June 2026, takes up Xi Jinping's call of 6 March 2026 to "unwaveringly follow the path of health development with Chinese characteristics" on the way to building a Healthy China by 2035. Wang argues that this path is the concrete expression of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the health field. In the author's view, given China's huge population and persistent urban–rural and regional gaps, it is the only appropriate path.

The article has three parts. It first defines the path and sets out its four components: guidance by the Party's theory, a people-centred practice, an institutional system sustained by reform, and a cultural foundation. It then links the path to five features of Chinese modernization: a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development. It closes with tasks for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030).

Wang's central claim is that the features of Chinese modernization determine how health development must be pursued. A huge population, with chronic and infectious diseases coexisting and rapid ageing, calls for prevention-first, integrated services that are low in cost and high in performance. Common prosperity calls for public-welfare orientation, with government-, public-interest- and public-hospital-led provision and resources tilted towards rural and central and western regions. The author also draws on traditional culture, citing ideas such as the unity of body and mind, as a source of "Chinese wisdom" for overcoming technocratic medicine. Further links are made to health-first development, health impact assessment, overseas medical teams and global health governance.

Wang concludes that the 15th Five-Year Plan period is critical for turning the advantages of the path into governance effectiveness. The author calls for continued Party leadership and better coordination mechanisms, firm constraints on planning, funding and resources to put health first, a stronger public health system, and a fuller policy and institutional system for health promotion. Read the original if you want to see how an official-media commentary connects the Healthy China 2035 goal to the established themes of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Health is the foundation of people's all-round development and also an important expression of their capacity to develop.
quoteZh: 健康是人的全面发展的基础，也是发展能力的重要体现。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own modernization path, defined by features such as a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development. It was elaborated in the 20th Party Congress report (2022).
A national strategy launched with the 2016 Healthy China 2030 Planning Outline, aiming to improve population health through policy across sectors. The article refers to a goal of building it by 2035.
An official goal of shared wealth for all, stressed in Party policy since the early 2020s and linked to reducing urban–rural and regional gaps.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, the fifteenth in the series of five-year plans.

t: Using New Era civilised practice to consolidate the grassroots foundation of Chinese modernization
zh: 以新时代文明实践夯实中国式现代化的基层基础
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 2 June 2026, asks how New Era civilised practice (a grassroots programme of propaganda, cultural and volunteer work) can be made to work in depth. Li Dingyi argues that it is a key vehicle for taking ideological work to the grassroots and for making cultural-ethical progress take effect there. Success depends on Party leadership, a people-centred stance and a grassroots orientation, and the programme should help strengthen the grassroots foundation of Chinese modernization.

The article is organised around five working areas: ideological guidance, county-level coordination, integration of venues and media, volunteer service, and long-term mechanisms. Each section opens with a rationale, often citing Xi Jinping, and then lists practical measures.

Li's central claim is that theory must be tied to everyday life. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era should be explained through local concerns such as employment, rural revitalisation and changing customs, using informal formats like courtyard meetings and short videos. The county is treated as the pivotal level: Li calls for unified county Party committee leadership, a three-tier chain of centres, stations and village-level posts, cross-department project lists, and joint planning between civilised-practice centres and county media centres. Volunteer work should respond to residents' needs and become part of village and neighbourhood affairs, instead of one-off events.

Li concludes that lasting mechanisms are needed for identifying needs, responding dynamically, running projects and giving feedback. Success should be measured by whether consensus, civilised norms, responsiveness to public concerns and grassroots governance have improved, not by event counts or online reach. The author presents the grassroots as the base for building a strong nation and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party propaganda officials describe the operational design of grassroots ideological and volunteer work.
quoteEn: New Era civilised practice values regularity above all and puts the emphasis on real results.
quoteZh: 新时代文明实践贵在常态、重在实效。

glossary.explanation: A grassroots programme, run through centres, stations and posts at county, township and village level, that combines theory outreach, cultural services and volunteer work. It is promoted by the Party's propaganda system.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to develop agriculture, villages and rural incomes.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, usually dated to 2049.

t: People's wellbeing first: an important contribution of Chinese modernization to the world
zh: 民生为大：中国式现代化的重要世界贡献
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily, takes up Xi Jinping's formula that in Chinese modernization 'people's wellbeing comes first' (minsheng wei da). Xin Xiangyang argues that the principle expresses the people-centred character of Chinese modernization and makes an important contribution to world modernization theory and practice.

The article is organised in four sections. Each presents one respect in which the principle is said to contribute globally: making the people the main force of modernization in a populous country, reconciling economic vitality with social order, addressing the principal contradiction of society, and advancing balanced, inclusive and sustainable global development.

Xin first contrasts Chinese modernization with the Western path, which the author describes as built on colonial plunder, capital-centred logic and exploitation that left most people outside modernization. By contrast, Chinese modernization is portrayed as self-reliant, rooted in common prosperity and measured by people's wellbeing rather than statistics. Second, the author argues that it resolves the common dilemma of vitality versus order by combining investment in things with investment in people, resolving disputes at the grassroots and developing whole-process people's democracy. Third, drawing on the Marxist account of capitalism's basic contradiction, Xin holds that socialism avoids that contradiction institutionally and addresses the principal contradiction through high-quality development, which the author characterises as responsive to popular opinion, caring, job-creating and sustainable.

Xin concludes that China's record offers lessons to other developing countries. The article cites the lifting of 770 million rural people out of poverty in about forty years, the Forum on China–Africa cooperation's poverty-reduction and agriculture projects under the 2035 vision, and the Belt and Road Initiative's emphasis on 'small and beautiful' livelihood projects. In Xin's reading, these show that a self-reliant, people-centred path and a global governance approach of joint consultation, contribution and benefit can help developing countries modernize. Read the original if you want an example of how official commentary presents Chinese modernization's livelihood agenda as a global contribution.
quoteEn: Modernization with the people as its main body fundamentally transcends the Western-centric narrative of modernization, abandons the capital logic of Western modernization, and highlights the people's logic of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 以人民为主体的现代化从根本上超越了西方中心主义的现代化叙事，摒弃西方现代化的资本逻辑，突出中国式现代化的人民逻辑。

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's official concept of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, rather than by a few, treated as a defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official term for China's democratic model, which stresses popular participation across all stages of decision-making rather than only in elections.
An official development goal emphasising innovation, coordination, green growth, openness and sharing over speed alone.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: Grasping the contemporary value of Chinese modernization from the depth of world history
zh: 从世界历史纵深把握中国式现代化的时代价值
paras: Writing in People's Daily, Zhang Guanzi asks what Chinese modernization means when set against the long history of world modernization. The commentary argues that Chinese modernization breaks the equation of "modernization = Westernization" and offers the world a new option. Zhang holds that the limits of the Western model are increasingly visible and that other countries are looking for new paths.

The piece has three parts. The first revisits world modernization as a process pursued jointly by all of humanity rather than by the West alone. The second sets out how Chinese modernization is said to surpass Western theory and practice. The third discusses its influence on the global modernization process. Zhang draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements and on Marx, Engels and Immanuel Wallerstein.

Zhang argues that Western modernization did not develop in isolation. It drew on inventions from other civilizations, such as Chinese papermaking, printing, the compass and gunpowder, and it pulled Asia, Africa and Latin America into a world market. In this account Western modernization is one particular form, driven by the unlimited expansion of capital. Zhang says it produced alienation, wealth polarisation and, through war, slave trading and colonialism, long-term underdevelopment elsewhere. Chinese modernization is said to surpass it in three ways: putting the people first instead of capital, harmonious coexistence instead of benefiting oneself at others' expense, and openness and inclusiveness instead of systemic monopoly. Zhang cites the Belt and Road Initiative as an example of the last.

Zhang concludes that Chinese modernization has exposed the myth of a single Western model and confirmed that paths to modernization are diverse. It also offers a development philosophy and approach to governance, including a strong political core, long-term strategic continuity and a socialist market economy combining an effective market with an enabling government. In Zhang's view, the modernization of more than 1.4 billion people will reshape the global modernization landscape, and a community with a shared future for mankind will open opportunities for the Global South. Read the original if you want an example of how official Chinese commentary presents the world-historical significance of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has not only profoundly changed China itself but also rewritten the long-standing Western-dominated narrative of modernization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化不仅深刻改变了中国自身，也改写了长期以来由西方主导的现代化叙事

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership. It stresses a large population, common prosperity, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since around 2012. It calls for shared interests and cooperation among states and underlies many Chinese international initiatives.
A term for developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America. In Chinese official discourse it refers to China's partners and to a presumed shared interest in reforming global governance.
An infrastructure and investment initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013 linking China with Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

t: Gathering the strength of Chinese modernization through high-quality labour and creation
zh: 以高质量的劳动创造汇聚中国式现代化奋进伟力
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 7 May 2026, takes up Xi Jinping's statement that high-quality development depends on high-quality labour and creation. Li argues that such labour runs through the course of Chinese modernization, expresses its people-centred values, drives high-quality development and points towards common prosperity and the all-round development of the individual.

The piece has three main sections. The first treats high-quality labour as an expression of the people-centred requirement, the second as the core engine of high-quality development, and the third as a condition of common prosperity and all-round human development. It closes with a brief call to action.

Li draws on Marx's account of labour as free, conscious activity and contrasts this with alienated labour under capital-driven older modernization. In this reading, high-quality labour returns labour to its authentic form: knowledge-based and skilled, marked by craftsmanship, and aimed at real social needs. Li links it to new quality productive forces, citing more than 220 million skilled workers at the close of the 14th Five-Year Plan. On distribution, the author holds that distribution according to labour, a rising labour share in primary distribution and better skill-grade systems enlarge the middle-income group and produce a cycle of creation, sharing and re-creation.

Li concludes that Chinese modernization is achieved by doing, not waiting. The author calls for promoting the model-worker, labour and craftsmanship spirits, strengthening protection of workers' rights, and fostering a social climate that respects labour and skills. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary connects Marxist labour theory to current policy themes.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is achieved by doing, not by waiting.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化是干出来的，不是等出来的。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models and elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth based on innovation, efficiency and better living standards.
A stated goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics: prosperity shared by all, involving both wealth creation and fairer distribution.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industries.

t: Persist in investing in people to promote the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 坚持投资于人 促进新质生产力发展
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 7 May 2026, asks how "investing in people" relates to new quality productive forces. Cheng and Zhang argue that the two form an organic unity. In their account, investing in people is a precondition for high-quality development and for building China into a modern socialist country. They take their cue from the 15th Five-Year Plan outline, which lists the talent pool as an advantage and calls for investing in things and in people together.

The piece has two parts. The first sets out four reasons why investing in people and new quality productive forces belong together. The second turns to four practical requirements, which cover local-government assessment, the direction of investment, the integrated development of education, science and technology, and talent, and the institutional setting for innovation.

The theoretical argument rests on Marx and on Xi Jinping's statements. The authors say investing in people helps relations of production fit the demands of the productive forces, because it raises workers' standing and skills and lets knowledge and technology share more fully in distribution. They cite Marx's Capital on training for skilled labour-power to claim that such spending is a productive investment with a multiplier effect, not mere welfare. They also hold that workers' free and comprehensive development upgrades consumption and widens demand. In their reading this creates a loop running from human capital to effective demand to better supply, and it pushes reform of income distribution and property rights. Retraining is meant to ease skill mismatches and prevent large-scale unemployment as traditional industries are upgraded.

In practice, the authors propose adding "people-centred" indicators, such as the share of human-capital investment, to assessments of local governments. They would tie the results to officials' promotion, project approval and fiscal transfers. They also call for balancing priority fields such as artificial intelligence with basic training, and for balancing present needs with future ones. Other proposals include merging the education, innovation and talent chains through industry-education integration, reforming ownership and profit-sharing for職务 research results, and adopting tolerant, error-correcting supervision. Read the original if you want to see how Party-state scholars connect human-capital policy, Marx's labour theory and local cadre evaluation to the new quality productive forces agenda.
quoteEn: Investing in people is by no means mere welfare spending, but the most essential productive investment, with the strongest multiplier effect.
quoteZh: 投资于人，绝非单纯的福利支出，而是最本质、最具有乘数效应的生产性投资。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023. It refers to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, and by a better combination of production factors.
The official aim of shifting from fast growth to growth that stresses efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
China's national plan for economic and social development for 2026–2030.
A policy slogan that treats spending on education, skills, health and livelihoods as investment in human capital, not as consumption or welfare.

t: Realising modernization in which humans and nature live in harmony
zh: 实现人与自然和谐共生的现代化
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today (24 March 2026), Ke Changwan argues that Chinese modernization is a modernization of harmony between humans and nature, and that building a solid ecological security barrier is both an inherent requirement and an important safeguard of it. The commentary takes its cue from the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025).

The piece is organised in three parts: why ecological security underpins national security and the nation's lasting development; which guiding ideas should govern the work; and what practical path to follow. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements and on the Party and State Council opinion on comprehensively advancing the building of a Beautiful China.

Ke contends that ecological security, as part of the holistic approach to national security, is a bottom line that protects territorial, resource, food, economic and social security. On ideas, the author calls for the "two mountains" principle, an integrated approach to mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts, and development planned within resource and environmental carrying capacity. In practice, Ke proposes a "three zones and four belts" spatial pattern with firm ecological red lines, tighter control of environmental, biological and climate risks, stronger legal, monitoring and emergency systems, and active participation in global ecological governance.

Ke concludes that Xi Jinping Thought on ecological civilization should guide efforts to build the barrier with greater resolve, laying an ecological foundation for the nation's lasting development and offering "Chinese wisdom" for a clean and beautiful world. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-aligned scholarship links ecological security to the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Safeguarding ecological security is, in essence, safeguarding the spatial, material and environmental foundations of national development, and protecting the homeland on which the people depend for survival.
quoteZh: 维护生态安全，本质上就是维护国家发展的空间基础、物质基础与环境基础，就是守护人民群众赖以生存的家园。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, with features such as a huge population, common prosperity and harmony between humans and nature.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on ecological civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's ideas on environmental protection and ecological civilization, which the Party treats as guidance for green development.
Xi Jinping's 2014 concept of national security covering political, economic, ecological and other fields together.
The slogan that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", used by Xi Jinping to present environmental protection and economic development as mutually reinforcing.
An official goal of building a country with a good ecological environment, written into Party documents since the 18th Party Congress.

t: Strengthening the real economy to consolidate the foundation of development in the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: 以壮大实体经济筑牢“十五五”发展根基
paras: This commentary, originally published in China Social Sciences Today in March 2026, takes up the 15th Five-Year Plan Outline's treatment of the real economy as an independent chapter. Gu Naihua argues that development in the 2026–2030 period should rest on the real economy, with a modernised industrial system built around advanced manufacturing as its "ballast stone".

The piece has two parts. The first reads three features of the Outline's approach to building a modernised industrial system. The second proposes three areas for targeted action: industrial resilience, the innovation ecosystem and industrial coordination.

In Gu's reading, the Outline is more strategic in its goals, which are the completeness, advancement and security of the industrial system. It is more coordinated in direction, since "integration" is added to intelligent and green development. It also modernises policy thinking by moving industrial policy from selectively backing particular sectors and firms towards inclusive, functional support. For action, Gu proposes "re-industrialising" traditional industries, which the author says account for over 80 per cent of the system, through integrated standards, technology and institutions, rebuilding basic industrial foundations and tiered cultivation of leading firms. Gu also calls for demand-led innovation, with published application-scene lists, full-chain incubation of future industries and "sandbox" regulation. Finally, Gu urges strengthening producer services and deeper integration of services and manufacturing.

Gu concludes that these measures would let the real economy anchor the Plan period, moving "Made in China" towards "created in China" and "intelligently made in China". Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how a Chinese economist interprets the industrial chapter of the 15th Five-Year Plan Outline.
quoteEn: Promote the transformation of industrial policy towards inclusiveness and functionality.
quoteZh: 推动产业政策向普惠化和功能性转型

glossary.explanation: China's national development plan for 2026–2030, whose Outline sets economic and social goals for the period.
A policy concept for an industrial structure that is complete, advanced and secure, with advanced manufacturing at its core.

t: Advancing the building of a strong country systematically during the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: 体系化推进“十五五”时期强国建设
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in March 2026, reads the Outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development as a systems project. Feng and Wei argue that the plan's 16 goals for building a strong country aim at "systemic autonomy" (体系化自主): the mutual support of all fields, not isolated breakthroughs.

The article has three parts. It first explains why systemic autonomy is now required, then sets out the internal logic of the expanded list of goals, and finally draws out what this means for governance during the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

The authors say that since reform and opening up, modernization followed a "catching-up" logic, benchmarking each field against international standards. Systemic autonomy, they stress, is neither self-sufficiency nor closure, nor the sum of separate fields becoming self-controlled. They read the increase from 11 to 16 goals as filling gaps in the system. Energy and finance supply underlying support, aerospace opens room for upgrading, and agriculture and tourism build resilience.

Feng and Wei call for three shifts: from sectoral management to cross-field coordination mechanisms; from single-indicator assessment to evaluating system-wide effectiveness; and from defensive responses to actively shaping an open order through institutional opening up. They warn against equating "autonomy" with "substitution". Read the original if you want a concise Chinese-language reading of how the 15th Five-Year Plan's strong-country goals are meant to fit together.
quoteEn: What systemic autonomy truly stresses is organic linkage among fields, producing an overall effectiveness greater than the sum of its parts.
quoteZh: 体系化自主真正强调的，是各领域之间的有机联动，形成大于各部分之和的整体效能。

glossary.explanation: A policy theme in Party and state planning for making China a leading power across fields such as science, manufacturing, finance and agriculture. The 15th Five-Year Plan Outline lists 16 such goals.
The authors' term for a state in which the various strong-country fields support one another so the national development system can run independently, without closing itself off.
Official term for opening that stresses alignment and shaping of rules, regulations and standards, going beyond trade and investment flows.

t: Pooling strengths to build momentum: developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions
zh: 集优成势推动因地制宜发展新质生产力
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in March 2026, takes up the principle in the Outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan that new quality productive forces should be developed in line with local conditions. Yang Hutao argues that the principle means regions each play to their strengths and combine them into a national whole, not that each goes its own way.
The piece is organised under three headings: the reasons for the principle, its purpose within high-quality development, and the routes the Outline sets out.

On the reasons, Yang points to the technical features of new quality productive forces. Their effectiveness depends on industry-specific data, application scenarios and local industrial knowledge, so they emerge through scenario-driven, path-dependent and locally embedded processes. Yang adds that regional endowments differ: the eastern coast can lead on frontier technology, the central region has solid manufacturing, and the western region has low factor costs and distinctive resources. On purpose, the author says differentiated paths provide the division of labour for strengthening the domestic circulation and help avoid involutionary competition. They also match supply to demand and open several parallel routes to new growth drivers.

Yang identifies three routes in the Outline: building on existing industrial bases to form strategic emerging industry clusters; cultivating and opening up application scenarios, which Yang says is a key institutional capacity for regions with limited research spending; and market-oriented reform of factor markets. Yang argues that, without free cross-regional flow of factors, differentiated development would fragment into local self-optimisation. Read the original if you want a short, official-aligned account of the economic rationale for regionally differentiated development of new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: Acting in line with local conditions does not mean everyone going their own way; it means each playing to its strengths and combining them into momentum.
quoteZh: 因地制宜不是各行其是，而是各展所长、合而成势。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 to describe advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and innovation, and now central to official economic policy.
A long-standing Chinese policy principle of tailoring development approaches to the specific conditions of each region.
The official guiding concept for China's economy since 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
A policy idea, prominent since 2020, of making the domestic market and internal production, distribution and consumption the main body of the economy.

t: Promoting intensive urban development through cultural construction
zh: 以文化建设助推城市内涵式发展
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in March 2026, asks how cultural construction can drive the shift to "intensive" (neihanshi) urban development. Liu Wugen argues that culture is the soul and endogenous driving force of a city, and that it therefore plays an important role in building the innovative, liveable, beautiful, resilient, civilised and smart "people's city" set out in the 15th Five-Year Plan outline.

Liu begins from the 2025 Central Urban Work Conference's judgement that urbanisation is moving from rapid growth to stable development, and that cities are moving from large-scale expansion to improving the quality and efficiency of existing stock. The article then offers three tasks, each supported by quotations from Xi Jinping: continuing the city's historical cultural lineage, shaping its distinctive features and appearance, and enriching residents' spiritual and cultural life.

On history, Liu holds that protecting heritage means handling the relationship between conservation, renovation and development, and that it must not become simple imitation of the past. Liu proposes better protection systems, long-term survey mechanisms, residents as the main actors in conservation, and digital technology for "living" preservation. On urban character, Liu distinguishes material expression (architecture, planning control, the "applicable, economical, green, attractive" building policy) from inner expression, namely urban spirit. On cultural life, Liu calls for a people-centred approach, a network of public cultural facilities and spaces, new cultural industries such as animation and film, and links with tourism, technology and sport.

Liu concludes that cultural construction should combine with the cultivation of core socialist values and the promotion of urban spirit, so as to raise residents' cultural standing and the level of urban civility. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party discourse links urban policy, cultural heritage and the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Culture is the soul of a city and the endogenous driving force of urban development, and cultural construction plays an important role in promoting intensive urban development.
quoteZh: 文化是城市的灵魂和城市发展的内生动力，文化建设对推动城市内涵式发展具有重要作用。

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping holding that cities are built by the people and for the people. It is used as a guiding principle in urban policy.
A set of 24 characters in three tiers (national, social, individual), promoted by the Party since 2012 as the basis of moral and cultural education.

t: Driving decisive progress in building a Healthy China during the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: 推动“十五五”时期健康中国建设取得决定性进展
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 26 March 2026, Wang Hesheng takes up Xi Jinping's remarks on building a Healthy China, delivered to CPPCC members during the March 2026 "two sessions". Wang argues that these remarks give direction and fundamental guidance at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030). The article calls for decisive progress in this period, so that a Healthy China is achieved by 2035.

The piece has three parts. The first explains what Wang sees in Xi's discourse on health: a development of the Marxist view of people's health, a people-first orientation, and dialectical thinking and method. The second sets out how to keep to the Chinese path of health development and the health work guideline of the new era. The third lists priority tasks for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

Wang's central claim is that the Chinese path, led by the Party and built on the public-interest character of basic medical and health services, has been proven by practice. The article contrasts it with the experience of other countries. It says that since the 1980s, under the influence of neoliberalism, some health systems suffered over-commercialisation, rising costs and declining equity. It also says Western medical models neglect prevention and social factors. Wang proposes drawing on traditional Chinese health culture and prevention-first policy to get greater health results at lower cost and avoid a "welfare trap". The article also stresses a health-priority development strategy and a systems approach to coordinating relationships such as government and market, and efficiency and fairness.

The article lists tasks: a stronger public health system with integrated medical care and disease prevention; high-quality, evenly distributed medical services and family doctors; coordinated reform of medical care, insurance and medicines, including promoting the Sanming reform experience; the patriotic health campaign; breakthroughs in key technologies and talent; the inheritance and innovation of traditional Chinese medicine; AI and data in health; and Party-building among medical staff. Wang urges working to a fixed timetable to deliver the Party Central Committee's decisions. Read the original if you want an official statement of the policy agenda for health in the 15th Five-Year Plan period, and of how Party leaders frame the Chinese health model against Western systems.
quoteEn: Public-interest character is the essential attribute of China's medical and health undertakings and an important expression of the superiority of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 公益性是我国医疗卫生事业的本质属性，是中国特色社会主义制度优越性的重要体现。

glossary.explanation: A national strategy launched in 2016 with a 2030 planning outline. It sets goals for public health and health services, and the article refers to 2035 as the target date for completing it.
The national development planning period 2026–2030, the fifteenth in China's series of five-year plans.

glossary.zh: 基本医疗卫生事业的公益性
glossary.pinyin: jīběn yīliáo wèishēng shìyè de gōngyìxìng
glossary.en: public-interest character of basic medical and health services
glossary.explanation: A principle that basic health care is a public good rather than a profit-making service. Reform of public hospitals is meant to reduce profit-seeking incentives.
A mass sanitation and hygiene mobilisation begun in the early 1950s, which the article treats as a lasting Chinese method of public health work.
Health system reforms from Sanming city in Fujian, covering hospital finance, drug procurement and staff pay. The Party has promoted them as a model for other regions.

t: A rule-of-law milestone towards modernization in harmony between humanity and nature
st: The Ecological and Environmental Code further highlights the guiding status of Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
zh: 迈向人与自然和谐共生的现代化的法治里程碑
zhSub: 生态环境法典进一步彰显习近平生态文明思想的指导地位
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 23 March 2026, was written by a vice-chair of the National People's Congress committee on environment and resources protection. It takes up the Ecological and Environmental Code, which the Fourth Session of the 14th National People's Congress had just adopted. Lü argues that the Code is a milestone in the history of Chinese and even world legal civilization. In the author's account, it turns the Party's theory, institutions and practice of ecological civilization since the 18th Party Congress (2012) into codified law.

The article is organised in four parts. It first presents the Code as a required application of Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization and Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law. It then considers how the Code inherits traditional Chinese legal and ecological culture. Next it treats the Code as an improvement of the socialist legal system with Chinese characteristics. Finally it describes the Code's contribution to global environmental governance.

Lü's central claims are as follows. The Code writes ideas such as "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets" and the "community of life" of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert into legal rules. It also consolidates the results of ecological civilization reform and protects the public's environmental rights, including information disclosure and participation. Domestically, Lü says it merges more than 30 laws and many regulations into a five-part structure: general provisions, pollution prevention, ecological protection, green and low-carbon development, and legal liability. The author argues this ends fragmentation, departmental interest and local protectionism, and strengthens source prevention, environmental damage compensation and public-interest litigation. Lü presents the "moderate codification" approach as a model for other countries and says the Code implements international conventions, extends extraterritorial rules and draws on the philosophy of harmony between humanity and nature.

Lü concludes that the Code will serve as a strong rule-of-law engine for Chinese modernization, in which humanity and nature live in harmony, and will push global ecological civilization to a new level. The author describes it as China's wisdom and approach for global environmental governance. Read the original if you want an official-leaning account of how the Code is framed in Chinese legal and Party discourse, including its claimed links to Xi Jinping's thought and to traditional culture.
quoteEn: Compiling the Ecological and Environmental Code is not simply a matter of writing the Chinese nation's long-standing ecological wisdom and cultural traditions into law, but of modern transformation, legal expression and institutional construction on the basis of careful screening.
quoteZh: 生态环境法典编纂，并不是简单地将中华民族自古以来形成的丰富生态智慧和文化传统写入法律，而是在认真甄别的基础上进行现代性转化、法律化表达与制度化建构。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on environmental protection and development attributed to Xi Jinping and formalised in Party discourse. It includes the slogan that "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets".

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas on law and governance attributed to Xi Jinping, centred on comprehensively governing the country according to law under Party leadership.
The official term for China's path of development, which Party documents describe as distinct from Western modernization. One of its stated features is harmony between humanity and nature.
A Party-state concept, adopted as national policy in the 2000s and 2010s, that makes environmental protection part of the overall strategy for development.

glossary.zh: 山水林田湖草沙是生命共同体
