glossary.pinyin: shān shuǐ lín tián hú cǎo shā shì shēngmìng gòngtóngtǐ
glossary.literal: mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert form a community of life
glossary.explanation: An official formulation holding that natural elements are interdependent and should be managed as one system rather than separately.
A drafting approach, used for the Code, that extracts common rules into a general part while leaving room for separate laws and for later adaptation.

t: Safeguarding and improving people's wellbeing in the course of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化进程中的民生保障和改善
paras: Zhao Jiping asks how livelihood protection (minsheng) should be advanced in the coming Fifteenth Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), after the achievements of the Fourteenth. Writing under the guidance of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), the author argues that safeguarding and improving people's wellbeing is both an essential expression of common prosperity and a yardstick of Chinese modernization's success. The article holds that this work needs forward-looking and systematic planning.

The article first sets out why livelihood work matters to Chinese modernization. It then reviews Fourteenth Five-Year Plan results in education, employment and social security, citing official figures. Next it identifies challenges for the Fifteenth Five-Year Plan period: population ageing, low fertility, regional, urban–rural and group inequalities, and the effects of digital technology and artificial intelligence on jobs. It closes with four policy directions.

Zhao presents livelihood work as the starting and ending point of Chinese modernization, a foundation of social stability and an engine of growth, because better livelihoods lift consumption and domestic demand and create new service markets. The review of achievements cites, among other figures, preschool gross enrolment of 92%, higher-education gross enrolment of 60.8%, 59.21 million new urban jobs, and basic pension insurance coverage above 95%. On challenges, the author stresses that 60-and-over residents reached 22.0% of the population by 2024, that public services remain unequal across regions and between town and country, and that automation may bring structural unemployment.

Zhao proposes combining doing one's best (jinli'er wei) with acting within one's means (liangli'er xing), so that spending stays fiscally sustainable. Further proposals are a population service system covering all people and the whole life cycle, balanced policies to narrow urban–rural and regional gaps, and institution-building as the main line, so that livelihood protection is stable, predictable and systematic. Read the original if you want a Party-school overview of Fourteenth Five-Year Plan livelihood statistics and the policy agenda for the Fifteenth Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: "Doing one's best" and "acting within one's means" are not opposed to each other; they form a dialectically unified organic whole.
quoteZh: “尽力而为”与“量力而行”并非相互对立，而是辩证统一的有机整体。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Its stated features include common prosperity for all.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, which the Party describes as an essential feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
A traditional term for the material wellbeing of ordinary people, now used officially for education, jobs, income, social security, health care and similar matters.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, following the Fourteenth Five-Year Plan (2021–2025).

t: Beyond the logic of capital: innovation and development in the people-centred path of new-type urbanization
zh: 超越资本逻辑：以人为本的新型城镇化道路的创新与发展
source: Teaching and Research (Jiaoxue yu Yanjiu), 2025 no. 11
paras: Yao Changcheng asks how China's people-centred new-type urbanization can avoid the urban crises of capitalist countries. The article argues that urbanization everywhere is driven by capital's general features, but that capital's specific character differs by ownership system. Under capitalism this produces an urbanization governed by the logic of capital, while under socialism with Chinese characteristics it produces one governed by a people's logic, in which the author sees an innovation in Marxist political economy.

The article distinguishes "capital in general" (profit-seeking, motion, limitlessness) from "capital in particular" (the class content set by ownership relations). It uses Lefebvre's contrast between the use value and exchange value of space, plus David Harvey's "spatial fix" and Arghiri Emmanuel's unequal exchange. Cases include British, Japanese, Swedish, Spanish and Australian new towns and vacant housing, Japan's land-price bubble, and urbanization in Latin America and Southeast Asia. It ends with policy measures and lessons for developing countries.

Yao's central claim is that capitalist urbanization lets exchange value swallow use value, favours "land urbanization" over "people's urbanization", and produces dormitory towns, "ghost cities" and bubbles. Unequal exchange between cities and countryside, arising from differences in the organic composition of capital and in wages, is said to reinforce the gap. In China, the author argues, state capital predominates, Party leadership amplifies capital's "people-oriented" character, and the principle "housing is for living in, not for speculation" restores use value. The contradiction between the two kinds of urbanization therefore remains but is not systemic and can be corrected through a "capable government" and an "effective market". Drawing on Lefebvre, Yao also says cities should move from "dominating space" to "appropriative space" guided by spatial justice.

Yao proposes balanced urban–rural development, fair distribution within urban space, a shift from "utilizing" capital to "harnessing" it, steering finance towards county towns and the countryside, wider public-service provision, and regulated capital in urban renewal. The article presents four features of China's model as lessons for developing countries: multi-centre city clusters, institutionalised control of capital, urban–rural integration, and coordination with new-type industrialization. Read the original if you want a Chinese political-economy account of urbanization that applies Marx, Harvey and Lefebvre to China and contrasts it with capitalist and developing-world cases.
quoteEn: Within the framework of the socialist system with Chinese characteristics, people-centred new-type urbanization can balance the inherent contradiction between "land urbanization" and "people's urbanization" and promote high-quality urbanization.
quoteZh: 以人为本的新型城镇化在中国特色社会主义制度框架下能平衡好“土地城市化”与“人的城市化”的内在矛盾，推动城镇化高质量发展。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese policy strategy, prominent since the early 2010s, that stresses quality, integration with the countryside and the settlement of rural migrants as urban residents, rather than simple expansion of urban land and population.

glossary.en: housing is for living in, not for speculation
glossary.explanation: A housing policy principle announced at the 2016 Central Economic Work Conference. It stresses housing's residential function and aims to curb speculation.
A term used in Chinese economics for an active government that guides development. It is often paired with the "effective market" in the socialist market economy.
The process by which rural migrants gain full urban residency rights and public services, beyond merely moving to cities. The article contrasts it with "land urbanization".

t: Governing the country through planning: an institutional guarantee for advancing Chinese modernization
zh: 规划治国：推进中国式现代化的制度保障
paras: Writing after the National People's Congress passed the National Development Planning Law on 12 March 2026, Tang Yalin argues that "governing the country through planning" is the dynamic mechanism that moves Chinese modernization forward step by step. The commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today, treats medium- and long-term planning centred on the Five-Year Plan as a key expression of the advantages of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

Tang first traces the history of 15 consecutive Five-Year Plans from 1953 to the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan in 2026. The article divides this into three periods: exploration and foundation (1953–1976), transition and adjustment (1981–2001), and stable maturity (2006 onwards). It then describes the institutional framework of planning and ends with five lessons it considers globally significant.

In Tang's account, planning has developed into a chain of "strategic guidance, consensus-building, vertical and horizontal translation, and implementation with adjustment". The Party Central Committee sets the direction through its recommendations, the State Council turns them into an outline, and the outline is then translated into local, sectoral and regional plans. Binding targets and annual plans carry it out. Tang says whole-process people's democracy is built into the consultation stage. The author presents the result as a holistic governance model that combines Party leadership, government and social mobilisation. They link its rise to China's position as a late-developing, very large country that needs to catch up and concentrate resources.

Tang concludes that planning marks a development path distinct from the "classic" Western model. The five lessons are Party leadership with strategic guidance, a people-centred orientation, concentrating resources on major tasks, combining staged goals with cumulative results, and a combined framework of an effective government, an efficient market and an orderly society. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese scholars present the Five-Year Plan as an institutional system and as a model with wider relevance.
quoteEn: Governing the country through planning has become the institutional model of the Party's governance and the dynamic mechanism of the development of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 规划治国成为党治国理政的制度模式，成为中国式现代化发展的动力机制。

glossary.explanation: The official concept for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.
The author's term for a governance model in which medium- and long-term plans, above all the Five-Year Plan, guide national development under the Party.
The official term for China's democratic model, which stresses popular participation at every stage of decision-making, including consultation and legislation.

glossary.literal: concentrate strength to accomplish big things
glossary.explanation: A phrase used officially to describe the capacity of the Chinese system to mobilise national resources behind priority goals.

t: The new development model underpins the building of a strong economy
zh: 新发展模式支撑经济强国建设
paras: Chi Fulin takes up the 15th Five-Year Plan outline's call for more growth models led by domestic demand, driven by consumption and based on endogenous growth. In this newspaper commentary, Chi argues that this is a strategic task for moving China from a large economy to a strong one. The author holds that it requires a higher-level dynamic balance between consumption and investment, and between supply and demand, with reform and innovation as the basic driving force.

The piece has three parts. The first summarises experience since the 18th Party Congress (2012) in four areas: development orientation, development pattern, structure and opening up. The second sets out three dimensions for joint effort: closing consumption gaps, strengthening trade in services and actively expanding imports. The third proposes reform measures covering investment and consumption, urban and rural areas, and government and market.

Chi's core argument rests on the claim that strong economies draw on domestic demand, especially consumption. The author cites figures to show progress: domestic demand contributed an average of 93.1% of growth in 2013–2024, and final consumption about 60% during the 14th Five-Year Plan period. Chi then points to gaps. The household consumption rate was 39.9% in 2024, and Chi projects 45% by 2030 and over 50% by 2035. Services account for 46.1% of per capita consumption spending, and Chi sees potential in raising that above 55% by 2035. Chi describes a structural contradiction of strong supply and weak demand. The proposed remedies are to invest in people as well as in things, to pursue people-centred urbanisation with household registration reform, and to build a unified national market. Chi also proposes widening market access in healthcare and education, clarifying central–local fiscal powers, and advancing institutional opening up, especially in services and digitally delivered trade.

Chi concludes that the next five to ten years are a historic window for economic transformation. In this period China can build a strong economy supported by the new development model, with a large home market that also offers the world opportunities. Domestic reform and high-level opening up are presented as mutually reinforcing, and Chi links imports and services trade to China's influence in setting global trade rules. Read the original if you want an example of how a Chinese reform-minded economist, writing in the Party's leading economic daily, turns the 15th Five-Year Plan's domestic-demand agenda into specific targets and policy proposals.
quoteEn: At present, China's economy faces a structural contradiction of strong supply and weak demand.
quoteZh: 当前，我国经济运行面临供强需弱的结构性矛盾。

glossary.explanation: China's national plan for economic and social development for 2026–2030. Its outline sets the main goals and policy directions for the period.
Opening that moves beyond the flow of goods and capital to align rules, regulations, management and standards with international norms.

t: A powerful domestic market as the strategic support of Chinese modernization
zh: 强大国内市场是中国式现代化的战略依托
paras: Guo Liyan, writing in Red Flag Manuscripts, examines the proposition in the Party Central Committee's recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) that "a powerful domestic market is the strategic support of Chinese modernization". The author argues that, as uncertainty grows, the market becomes a scarcer strategic resource. Over the next five years, Guo contends, China should hold to expanding domestic demand as its strategic base and move the domestic market from "big" to "strong".

The article has four parts: the meaning and features of a powerful domestic market; why building one is necessary and urgent in the 15th Five-Year Plan period; the internal and external conditions; and concrete measures. It is a policy commentary that follows and explains the Central Committee's recommendations, and it cites figures such as an economy of 140 trillion yuan by the end of the 14th Five-Year Plan and fixed-asset investment of 50 trillion yuan.

Guo defines "big" as aggregate size, market capacity and growth speed, and "strong" as quality, structure, competitive advantage and global influence. Building such a market is described as a systemic project that upgrades supply, distribution, circulation and demand systems together, including raising the household and labour share of income and moving consumption from subsistence to development-oriented spending. The author says a strong market supports people's needs, technological self-reliance and supply-chain security, and helps unblock circulation. It also helps counter de-globalisation and is described as open rather than closed. Guo sees opportunities outweighing challenges, citing a middle-income group projected above 800 million and the most complete industrial system. The challenges listed are unconverted demand potential, urban–rural gaps, weak brands, local protectionism and market fragmentation, and incomplete new infrastructure.

Guo's proposals include a special action to boost consumption, better government investment that links "investing in things" with "investing in people", and removal of barriers to a unified national market. They also include stronger private-sector vitality through the Private Economy Promotion Law, a national data market, and modern infrastructure such as 5G-A, 6G trials and intelligent connected transport. The author presents these as the practical path to turning market-size advantages into industrial competitiveness. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Chinese policy thinkers frame domestic demand and market-building for the 2026–2030 plan period.
quoteEn: To grasp the basic meaning of a powerful domestic market, the key is to understand the dialectical relationship between "strong" and "big".
quoteZh: 理解强大国内市场的基本要义，关键在于理解“强”和“大”的辩证关系。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030; the Central Committee issued recommendations for it in October 2025.

t: The distinctive strengths of China's governance as seen in the 15th Five-Year Plan
zh: 从“十五五”规划看中国之治的显著优势
paras: Li Zhijun asks what the drafting and implementation of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) reveals about the strengths of China's system of governance. Writing after the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) adopted the Party's Recommendations for the plan, Li argues that the plan's compilation logic and implementation mechanisms show four "unities" that together demonstrate the distinctive advantages of China's governance.

The article is a commentary in four sections, each opening with a statement by Xi Jinping. They treat scientific decision-making, strategic coordination across successive plans, overall planning that looks both inward and outward, and the conversion of blueprints into results. Li draws on the 14 five-year plans since 1953, the consultation timetable for the 15th plan, and the content of the Recommendations on industry, markets, opening up, security and the rule of law.

First, Li holds that top-level design and consultation with the public are combined. Central leadership, in Li's account, can rise above departmental interests, while consultation rounds (provincial research teams, an online solicitation, circulation of a draft) embody whole-process people's democracy and a "democracy first, centralism after" method. Second, long-term layout and continued effort are joined: Li presents the 14th, 15th and 16th plans as successive steps towards basic socialist modernization by 2035, citing growth and social insurance figures from the 14th plan period. Third, Li describes a plan that rests on domestic conditions, such as a unified national market and new quality productive forces, while expanding opening up and handling development and security together. Fourth, Li points to the planning law draft, task lists divided among central, local and departmental levels, and monitoring and evaluation, as a closed loop that turns plans into action.

Li concludes that the plan shows the advantages of Party leadership and the socialist system, including the ability to concentrate resources on major tasks and to implement decisions. Li calls on readers to rally around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and to study the plenum's spirit. Read the original if you want an example of how official commentary presents the planning system as evidence of governance strengths, and how it frames the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: This open-door way of drawing up plans makes the plan both consistent with national strategic direction and close to the real needs of the people, turns decision-making into a process of building consensus and gathering strength, and greatly raises the plan's scientific quality and feasibility.
quoteZh: 这种开门编规划的做法，让规划既符合国家战略方向，又贴合群众实际需求，使决策过程成为凝聚共识、汇聚力量的过程，极大提升了规划的科学性和可行性。

glossary.explanation: China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, whose drafting Recommendations were adopted by the Party in October 2025.

A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, which holds that democracy runs through every stage of governance rather than only elections. Official sources describe it as a distinct Chinese form of democracy.
A term introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological innovation and emerging and future industries.
An official phrase for China's system of governance and its record, often paired with "the China miracle" in Party discourse.

t: On the common features of socialist modernization
zh: 论社会主义现代化的共同特征
paras: Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that Chinese modernization shares common features with other countries' modernization while having its own national characteristics, Yin Xiaoen and Qin Xuan ask what features all socialist modernization has in common. They note that Chinese scholarship is rich on world modernization and on Chinese distinctiveness but thin on this question. Their thesis is that these features unite the basic principles of scientific socialism with the general laws of modernization, and form requirements every socialist country must follow.

The article proceeds through a historical survey followed by a structural analysis. The survey runs from Marx and Engels's theoretical outline of socialist modernization, through post-1917 Soviet industrialization and the Soviet model spread to Eastern Europe, Cuba and China, to the post-1991 shift towards all-round social development, which the authors trace through Chinese Party Congress documents. The second half sets out three dimensions (people, material things, institutions) and five paired unities that distinguish socialist from capitalist modernization.

The authors argue that the common features changed by stage: industrialization with priority for heavy industry under the Soviet model, then comprehensive social development after the Soviet and East European upheavals. The Soviet model, in their account, ignored institutional modernization and so slowed material progress and emptied all-round human development of content. Capitalist modernization, by contrast, achieved material abundance at the price of human alienation. Socialist modernization must therefore integrate the modernization of people (the fundamental goal), of material things (the material base) and of institutions (the fundamental guarantee). The five unities are advanced productive forces with advanced relations of production; material abundance with all-round human development; objective historical development with human agency; the integrity of civilizational forms with the coordination of civilizational processes; and critique of capitalist modernity with constructive building of an ideal society.

The authors conclude that socialist modernization has always sought the free and all-round development of the individual, while its features have evolved in stages and do not rule out national particularity. They call for firm adherence to fundamental and basic institutions, adaptive adjustment of important ones, and the development of new quality productive forces. They also call for systematically absorbing the achievements of capitalist civilization, as Lenin and Deng Xiaoping urged, while curbing capital's negative effects. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese theoretical account of how socialist modernization is defined against both capitalist modernization and the Soviet model.
quoteEn: The common features of socialist modernization reflect both its ideal state at the level of value goals and the actual general laws of its practice, and are an organic unity of the basic principles of scientific socialism with the universal laws of modernization.
quoteZh: 社会主义现代化的共同特征，既体现了社会主义现代化在价值目标层面的应然状态，也反映了社会主义现代化建设实践中的一般性规律等实然内容，是科学社会主义基本原则与现代化普遍规律的有机统一

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's path of modernization, described as socialist modernization led by the Communist Party and combining features shared with other countries with Chinese characteristics.
A concept promoted since 2023 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, such as high-tech and advanced industries.

t: The emergence, true meaning and practical path of the ecological wealth outlook of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化生态财富观的出场逻辑、本真涵义与实践路径
source: Journal of Harbin Institute of Technology (Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 6
paras: Liu Ying and Liu Xigang ask how the relationship between ecology and wealth should be understood within Chinese modernization, and argue that an "ecological wealth outlook" has taken shape as a concentrated expression of its essential requirements. Starting from Xi Jinping's 2018 statement that lucid waters and lush mountains are both natural and ecological wealth and social and economic wealth, the authors present this outlook as the unity of three things: a necessary logic of emergence, a distinctive meaning and a systematic practical path.

The article is organised in three parts. The first traces the historical, theoretical and practical logic by which the outlook emerged: the Party's attention to ecology from the new-democratic revolution to the new era, Marxist views of nature and wealth, and present resource and environmental bottlenecks. The second sets out the outlook's meaning along three dimensions: goal, core and demand. The third proposes a path of "directional guidance, multi-dimensional drivers, institutional safeguards".

The authors contrast the outlook with a Western "material wealth outlook" that, in their account, serves capital valorisation and treats unprocessed nature as outside social wealth. Against this, they say the ecological wealth outlook aims at harmony between humanity and nature and holds material, spiritual and ecological wealth to together make up social wealth. Its core, they argue, follows a logic of people rather than capital, aiming at common prosperity and fairness towards future generations. Its demand is the coordinated development of material and spiritual civilization. For practice, the authors propose building the goal of ecological wealth creation into every stage, field and driving force of modernization. They add three drivers: an effective market, a capable government and the endogenous energy of the people. They also propose institutional safeguards: stronger ecological laws, a fair distribution system for ecological wealth, and assessment and supervision of cadres, including lifelong accountability for ecological damage.

The authors conclude that putting this outlook into practice is a cornerstone for the sustainable development of socialist modernization and for achieving economic growth together with environmental protection. They treat it as a Marxist-grounded alternative to the Western modernization model. Read the original if you want a detailed Chinese-language account of how current Party theory links ecological civilization, the theory of wealth and Chinese modernization, including its proposals on law, distribution and cadre assessment.
quoteEn: The ecological wealth outlook is a concentrated expression of the essential requirements of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 生态财富观是中国式现代化本质要求的集中体现

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's model of modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). The Party presents it as having common features of modernization alongside Chinese characteristics.

The authors' term for a view of wealth that counts ecological resources and environment as social wealth alongside material and spiritual wealth. It builds on Xi Jinping's 2018 remark that green mountains are both ecological and economic wealth.
A goal of shared affluence for all the people, which the Party describes as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

t: Accelerating the green transformation of the development model against the background of new quality productive forces: rationale and pathways
zh: 新质生产力背景下加快发展方式绿色转型的理与路
source: Journal of Harbin Institute of Technology (Social Sciences), 2025 no. 6
paras: Hu Changsheng and An Xiaoxing ask how the green transformation of the development model can be accelerated now that new quality productive forces have become a Party priority. They argue that the two are not separate, one-directional agendas but mutually constitutive: green transformation supplies the ecological foundation and value orientation of new quality productive forces, while the latter supply innovation and technical support. The article, published in 2025 in the Journal of Harbin Institute of Technology (Social Sciences), builds on Xi Jinping's statement that new quality productive forces are themselves green productive forces.

The article is organised in three parts. It first sets out three logical reasons why green transformation is necessary: it is an essential requirement of new quality productive forces, an expression of their value stance, and a way to consolidate their green foundation. It then examines four dimensions of transformation (greening of economic growth, remaking the three elements of productive forces, resource conservation and intensive use, and green restructuring of production functions and consumer preferences) before analysing obstacles. It closes with practical paths in education, ecology, industry, institutions, consumption and international cooperation.

In the authors' account, conventional growth theory treats natural resources as unlimited exogenous inputs and equates GDP growth with development. New quality productive forces, by contrast, bring ecological boundaries into endogenous growth, so that environmental quality drives rather than constrains growth. The authors identify five obstacles: a tension between economic rationality and ecological rationality, in which market prices and national accounts fail to capture ecological value; path dependence and weak industrial coordination; technological and talent bottlenecks amid external technology restrictions; institutional gaps in structure, timeliness and policy coordination, including data rights; and weak public understanding of green living. The authors also stress the inertia generated by China's parallel pursuit of industrialization, urbanization, agricultural modernization, informatization and greening.

To respond, Hu and An propose integrating green education, green technology and green talent training; building systemic ecological governance with digital monitoring; developing green industries with price signals, subsidies and tax incentives; deepening institutional and legal innovation; promoting green consumption and lifestyles; and expanding international green cooperation, including through the Belt and Road Initiative, standard-setting and communication of Xi Jinping's ecological thought. Read the original if you want a systematic Chinese policy-academic account of how green transition is linked to the concept of new quality productive forces, with detailed lists of obstacles and measures.
quoteEn: Accelerating the green transformation of the development model and developing new quality productive forces are not isolated, one-directional undertakings, but strategic issues that are two sides of one coin, embedded in the green development paradigm of the era of digital ecological civilization.
quoteZh: 加快发展方式绿色转型与发展新质生产力并不是孤立的单向度发展，而是数字生态文明时代内嵌于绿色发展范式下互为表里的战略性议题

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new production factors and industrial upgrading, with digital and green technologies prominent.

glossary.en: green transformation of the development model
glossary.literal: green transition of the mode of development
glossary.explanation: A requirement set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and elaborated at the Third Plenum (2024) to shift economic and social development onto a low-carbon, resource-saving basis.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, here extended to green cooperation.

t: Systems integration in advancing comprehensive deepening of reform: theoretical foundations, objectives and practical path
zh: 系统集成推进全面深化改革的理论根基、目标指向与实践进路
source: Journal of Harbin Institute of Technology (Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 6
paras: The article takes up the methodological question raised by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for strengthening "systems integration" so that reforms in different fields work together efficiently. Zhang and Jia argue that systems integration has become the core methodology of further comprehensively deepening reform. In their account, reform logic is shifting from early "breakthroughs at key points" towards "systemic coupling" and overall effectiveness, which they present as a response to fragmented and department-bound reform.

The authors build a three-part framework: theoretical foundations, objective orientation and practical path. The foundations section covers Marxist systems thinking, traditional Chinese philosophy, modern systems science and the Party's own practice. The objectives section treats three goals: improving socialism with Chinese characteristics as an institutional system, modernizing national governance, and high-quality development. The practical section is organised around top-level design, coordinated advance and dynamic adjustment.

Zhang and Jia derive three features of systems integration (wholeness, systemic interconnection and dynamism) from each of their four sources. They draw on Engels, Marx, Bertalanffy and Laozi and Zhuangzi's idea of the unity of heaven and humanity. They illustrate these features with examples such as the "streamline administration, delegate power, improve regulation and services" reforms, the national unified market, rural revitalization and regional coordination. The three objectives are described as a closed loop in which institutions provide the vehicle for governance and governance underpins development. On practice, the authors describe the fundamental, basic and important institutions as trunk, branches and foliage of one system. They call for reform goals to be ranked by level, stage and priority, for measures to be coordinated across and within fields, and for monitoring and feedback mechanisms so that reform can adapt to changing conditions and to people's needs.

The authors conclude that systems integration gives reform a distinctive logical framework, one that helps turn institutional strengths into governance effectiveness and supports Chinese modernization. They call for adherence to systems thinking and stronger systems integration as national governance continues to be modernized. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars link the Party's reform method to Marxism, classical Chinese thought and systems science, and how that method is applied to policy fields.
quoteEn: Reform is not a simple superposition of subsystems but a unified whole of multi-level integration.
quoteZh: 改革不是各子系统的简单叠加，而是多层次交融的统一整体

glossary.explanation: A reform method stressed by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It means organising reforms across economic, political, cultural, social and ecological fields so that they reinforce one another.
The official Party formulation of China's modernization path, presented as distinct from Western models.
An official economic goal that emphasises quality, innovation and balance over speed of growth.

glossary.en: streamline administration, delegate power, improve regulation and services
glossary.explanation: A reform programme, launched in the 2010s, that reduces administrative approvals and improves oversight and public services.

glossary.literal: heaven and humans united as one
glossary.explanation: A traditional Chinese philosophical idea that people and nature form one organic whole. The article treats it as a cultural source of systems thinking.

t: Turning the institutional advantages of Party leadership over economic work into governance effectiveness: a perspective from the Five-Year Plans
zh: 切实把党领导经济工作的制度优势转化为治理效能——基于五年规划的视角
source: Journal of the China Jinggangshan Cadre Academy, 2025 no. 6
paras: Wu Zhiyuan asks how the institutional advantages of Party leadership over economic work can be converted into effective governance, and takes the Five-Year Plans as the vehicle for answering. The article argues that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the system of Party leadership over the economy has matured, but that weaknesses lie mainly in implementation: Wu lists institutional failure, idle or empty institutions and distorted execution. The Five-Year Plan, Wu contends, is the key mechanism by which Party leadership is embedded in economic governance.

The article opens by justifying its focus on execution rather than institutional design, offering four reasons: advantages must be proved through governance, the same institution performs differently in practice, designers should think like implementers, and economic governance is under pressure. It then analyses the Plans at three stages: drafting, framework and content, and implementation safeguards. A later section draws practical lessons for the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030), using the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) as its starting point.

Wu argues that the drafting procedure (Party Central Committee proposal, State Council outline, National People's Congress approval) embodies the Party's "overall command and coordination" and the relations between Party and government and between Party and masses. The Plans are also said to apply four governance methods: systemic, law-based, comprehensive and source governance. In Wu's reading, this unites Party leadership, the market's decisive role and an effective government, and lets the Plans overcome both "government failure" and "market failure". Because the National People's Congress must approve a plan, Wu calls it a "compulsory" legal route from institutional advantage to governance effectiveness.

For the 15th Five-Year Plan, Wu calls for strengthening Party leadership across the plan cycle, enforcing implementation responsibilities, monitoring and evaluation, and incentives and constraints. Wu also urges attention to a people-centred orientation, the development of new quality productive forces suited to local conditions, and a unified planning system that respects regional characteristics. Wu adds that governance, reform and policy must be deployed together. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic account of how the Five-Year Plan is presented as a mechanism of Party leadership and of what its authors expect of the 15th Plan.
quoteEn: The vitality of an institution lies in its execution, and governance is the "practical" form of an institution.
quoteZh: 制度的生命力在于执行，治理是制度的“实践”形式

glossary.explanation: China's medium-term national development plan, issued since 1953 (called a "plan" until the 11th, a "programme" or "plan" thereafter). The 15th covers 2026–2030.

glossary.literal: taking overall charge of the situation and coordinating all parties
glossary.explanation: A formula describing the Party's leading role over state organs, the legislature, the government, enterprises and other bodies.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation in emerging industries.

t: High-quality development as the theme of the 15th Five-Year Plan period: historical evolution, theoretical meaning and practical requirements
zh: “十五五”时期以推动高质量发展为主题：历史演进、理论内涵和实践要求
source: Journal of China Executive Leadership Academy Jinggangshan, 2025 no. 6
paras: Following the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), whose Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan name high-quality development as the theme of economic and social development for 2026–2030, Zhang asks how this theme emerged, what it means and what it requires in practice. The article argues that the theme is both a precise reading of China's current stage and a strategic choice aimed at basically achieving socialist modernization by 2035. It builds a framework that unites historical, theoretical and practical logic.

The article has three parts. The first traces three historical stages: the early People's Republic (restoration and heavy industry, solving the problem of 'having or not having'), the reform era from 1978 (growth-centred, with the first signs of attention to quality in successive plans), and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second part sets out the theoretical content of high-quality development and its links to the new development philosophy, the new development pattern and new quality productive forces. The third part turns to the practical requirements drawn from the Recommendations' 'five orientations' and their twelve areas of strategic tasks.

Zhang's central claim is that high-quality development is a 'brand-new development theory' that enriches Marxist principles. In this reading it embodies the new development philosophy's five dimensions (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing), the dialectic of 'effective improvement in quality and reasonable growth in quantity', and a people-centred orientation. The author says it surpasses the older 'growth equals development' view and cites China's Human Development Index rise from 0.713 (2012) to 0.788 (2023). New quality productive forces supply the new momentum, and the domestic–international 'dual circulation' is presented as a development of Marx's reproduction schemes. The practical requirements range from the real economy, modern industry and domestic demand to reform, innovation, opening up, common prosperity, cultural development and strengthening Party leadership.

Zhang concludes that high-quality development is a long and arduous task requiring a self-reliant Chinese economics, better policy tools and precise implementation. The author claims it offers Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to world development, and challenges the notion that modernization equals Westernization. Read the original if you want a Party-school account of how the 15th Five-Year Plan's guiding theme is justified historically and theoretically, and of its policy agenda.
quoteEn: High-quality development is a multidimensional, systematic and complex project of change, involving the development philosophy, pattern, drivers, mode, path and purpose, among many other aspects.
quoteZh: 高质量发展是涉及发展理念、发展格局、发展动力、发展方式、发展路径、发展目的等众多方面的多维度、系统性复杂变革工程

glossary.explanation: A Party economic-policy concept announced at the 19th Party Congress (2017), which holds that the economy has shifted from high-speed growth to a stage emphasising quality, efficiency and balance. The 20th Party Congress (2022) called it the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
Five principles (innovation, coordination, green, openness, sharing) first set out in 2015 as guidance for China's development.

A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023, describing advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new production factors and industrial upgrading, with higher total factor productivity as the core indicator.
A strategy announced in 2020 that takes the domestic cycle as the mainstay, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other ('dual circulation').
A goal of shared affluence for all the people, which official discourse treats as an essential feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

t: Adhering to correct work strategies and methods: studying the work methodology of Xi Jinping's economic thought
zh: 坚持正确工作策略和方法——学习习近平经济思想的工作方法论
paras: Zhu Andong asks how economic work should actually be carried out, arguing that sound theory, goals and strategy are not enough without a correct methodology. The article contends that since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Xi Jinping has built a systematic methodology for economic work from Marxist materialist dialectics and the Party's practical experience. Zhu presents it as an original contribution to Marxist political economy and as a sign of the Party's improved ability to manage the socialist market economy.

The article has three parts. The first traces the Party's tradition of attention to working methods, from Mao Zedong's 1945 call to learn to do economic work, through his methods such as "investigation" and "playing the piano", to the reform-era maxims of pilot projects and "crossing the river by feeling the stones". It then sets out the new conditions of the new era. The second part explains five elements of Xi's methodology, and the third turns to the 15th Five-Year Plan period and to what leading cadres should do.

Zhu describes the five elements as follows: keeping to the general tone of seeking progress while maintaining stability, with "breaking" and "building" handled together and building coming first; a systems approach, which treats economic work as interconnected and calls for coordinated policy; adapting measures to local conditions, as the essence of seeking truth from facts; combining goal orientation with problem orientation; and bottom-line thinking, which prepares for the worst in an uncertain, risky environment. Zhu says that economists have long studied the laws of economic movement but seldom the methods of economic work, although good policies can fail without good methods. Examples include the dual carbon goals, which Zhu says require building before breaking, and the real estate risks that call for bottom-line thinking.

Zhu concludes that the 15th Five-Year Plan period will bring more uncertainty and persistent problems, such as weak demand, limited innovation capacity and risks in key sectors. Zhu therefore calls on cadres to treat the methodology as required study, to internalise it and apply it, and to avoid selective implementation, localism, formalism and bureaucratism. Zhu also urges them to investigate local conditions, pursue differentiated development and aim for growth "without water", meaning no padding. Read the original if you want a concise official-line account of how Xi Jinping's economic thought frames method and what it asks of cadres.
quoteEn: Economics is in essence a practical science. Good policies without good methods cannot show an effective path to implementation, and policies often fail to reach their expected results or even run in the opposite direction.
quoteZh: 经济学本质上是一门实践的科学。光有好的政策，没有好的方法，不能指明政策落地的有效途径，政策也往往难以达到预期效果甚至出现南辕北辙的情况。

glossary.explanation: The general tone set for economic work in Party and government planning. It treats stability as the basis and progress as the direction and driving force.
A working method stressing that issues are interconnected and should be planned as a whole. Xi Jinping has often emphasised it.
A traditional principle that policy should fit the resources, stage of development and conditions of each place. Xi describes it as the essence of seeking truth from facts.
A mode of thinking that prepares for the worst case in order to secure the best result. Xi Jinping has promoted it since the 18th Party Congress.
China's economic and social development plan for 2026–2030. Its main goals were set at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee.

t: Guiding the construction of modern cities with the people's city concept
zh: 以人民城市理念引领现代化城市建设
paras: Writing in Qiushi (issue 2, 2026), Xiao Chaowei asks how the \"people's city\" concept can be built into the practice of urban development so that cities become spaces of high-quality life. The author's answer is that this concept, developed since the 18th Party Congress (2012), redirects urban construction from the \"appreciation of things\" to a people-centred orientation. It must be put into effect through coordinated action on regional planning, housing, heritage protection and governance.

The article has three parts. The first traces China's urban construction in three phases: the early People's Republic, when cities were reorganised around production and the \"work unit\" compound; the reform-era surge of urbanisation; and the period after 2012. The second sets out four problems facing modern cities. The third proposes four areas of action, drawing on the priorities of the 2025 Central Urban Work Conference and the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee.

In Xiao's account, past urban growth built up material wealth and housing but ran into diminishing returns, resource limits, uniform cityscapes and the loss of cultural continuity. The author lists four current challenges: new quality productive forces demand smaller, flexible and more compound spaces; an ageing population and the needs of both old and new residents change service demands; \"large-scale demolition and rebuilding\" threatens a city's historical \"soul\"; and governance remains reactive, fragmented and overburdened at the grassroots. Xiao names the Party's centralised leadership and new technologies such as AI and digital twins as advantages.

Xiao proposes four measures. First, integrate city clusters and metropolitan areas, with differentiated roles for megacities, medium-sized and small cities, and county towns. Second, make \"good housing\" the base of urban improvement, with life-cycle thinking from design to property management. Third, protect heritage at macro, meso and micro levels, with no further demolition of old districts. Fourth, build co-construction and co-governance through data-based \"check-ups\" and a closed loop from citizen complaints to feedback. Xiao concludes that modern urban construction is a systemic project that should run through planning, building and governance during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Read the original if you want an official-line overview of how Party theory frames urban policy and its practical priorities for the coming years.
quoteEn: The people's city concept goes beyond the production of material space dominated by instrumental rationality; in essence it is a profound change that reshapes the relationship between people and the city.
quoteZh: 人民城市理念超越了工具理性主导下的物质空间生产，实质上是一场重塑人与城市关系的深刻变革

glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's urban thought, summed up in the 2019 formula "people's cities are built by the people and for the people". It presents urban development as oriented to residents' needs and participation.
A term introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, such as AI and information technology.
A high-level Party and government meeting that sets national urban policy. The article cites sessions in 2015 and 2025.
A policy slogan, endorsed by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), for safe, comfortable, green and smart housing. It shifts housing policy from quantity to quality.

glossary.en: closed loop from citizen complaints to feedback
glossary.literal: respond to complaints as soon as received
glossary.explanation: A municipal governance practice, associated with Beijing, of handling citizen complaints promptly and feeding the results back into management.

t: Comprehensively advancing Chinese modernization through high-quality development
zh: 以高质量发展全面推进中国式现代化
paras: Yin Yanlin, writing in Qiushi (issue 1, 2026), interprets the Recommendations adopted by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Yin argues that high-quality development is the essential requirement of Chinese modernization and the theme of economic and social development in 2026–2030. Leading more than 1.4 billion people into modernization together is described as a rare feat in human history and a mission of Communist Party members in the new era.

The article first places the 15th Five-Year Plan in the two-step strategy set by the 19th and 20th Party Congresses, under which socialist modernization is to be basically achieved by 2035. It then assesses the growth target and the external and domestic environment. The second half sets out five areas of focus: the modern industrial system, scientific and technological self-reliance, a strong domestic market, deepening reform and opening up, and better living standards.

Yin presents the 15th Five-Year Plan period as one for laying foundations and exerting all-round effort, since only ten years remain before 2035. Working back from the goal of per capita GDP above US$20,000, double the 2020 level, Yin calculates that GDP must grow by 4.17% a year over the next two five-year periods. Yin suggests growth in the coming period could be somewhat higher, but says speed is not the only goal and calls for abandoning extensive, input-driven growth. Despite unilateralism, protectionism and domestic imbalances, Yin sees solid fundamentals and institutional advantages, including the Party's centralised leadership. The five priorities include keeping traditional industries while fostering emerging and future industries, expanding domestic demand and consumption, supporting the Two Unwaverings, and pursuing common prosperity patiently.

Yin concludes that development is the key to solving China's problems and that growth is its necessary basis. China should therefore pursue high-quality development with determination and answer external uncertainty with its own certainty. Realising the plan depends on officials' initiative in carrying out the Central Committee's decisions. Yin stresses that common prosperity is a long historical process that must rest on sustainable growth and fiscal capacity. Read the original if you want an official-line reading of the 15th Five-Year Plan Recommendations, including the 4.17% growth calculation and the five priority areas.
quoteEn: Although development is not the same as growth, growth is an indispensable component of development, its foundation and precondition; without economic growth, there can be little talk of development.
quoteZh: 虽然发展不等于增长，但增长是发展的一个不可或缺的组成部分，是发展的基础和前提，脱离经济增长也难言发展。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official economic goal since 2017 that stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability over raw growth rates.
The official policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A Party goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as an essential feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

t: Research progress and prospects on indicator systems for Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化指标体系的研究进展与展望
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2025 no. 6
paras: This literature review surveys work on how to measure Chinese modernization. Xing and Li treat an indicator system as a scientific tool that makes the process measurable, comparable and traceable. They see building a framework that reflects the essential requirements of socialist modernization and is also internationally comparable as a frontier topic across economics, sociology and public administration. They conclude that current research needs a unified theoretical core, common stage targets and a multi-level framework combining Chinese features with international consensus.

The article first traces world modernization indicator systems, from Rostow, Parsons, Huntington and Weber through the Hakone model, the Inkeles system and the Human Development Index to the Millennium Development Goals, the 2030 Agenda and the Chinese Academy of Sciences' world modernization index. It then runs a CiteSpace keyword-cluster analysis of 63 CNKI papers published between January 2020 and October 2025. Next it reviews dimension design and indicator selection, target-setting methods and weighting models, and closes with directions for future research.

The authors sort existing designs into five approaches: the "five-sphere integrated plan", the five features of Chinese modernization, the new development philosophy, the coordination of production, living and ecological space, and regional governance frameworks. Targets for 2035 and 2050 are set in three ways: calculation from policy documents, benchmarking against moderately developed or developed countries, and trend extrapolation. Weighting methods fall into subjective (Delphi, AHP), objective (entropy method, principal component analysis) and combined approaches. The review reports rising national scores since 2010 and regional gaps that are narrowing overall. It identifies three problems: the five-sphere plan, the five features and the "five civilizations" are not yet articulated at the level of thresholds and weights; there is no uniform definition of "developed" or "moderately developed" countries; and national distinctiveness competes with international comparability.

Xing and Li propose mapping the three theoretical frameworks onto one another to build a top-level design that unites goals, paths and values. They also propose a standard benchmark group of countries, and a three-tier framework of international consensus, Chinese features and local flexibility. They add linked outcome and process indicators, public parameters alongside scenario-flexible ones, and real-time data such as remote sensing and night-time lights. Read the original if you want a mapped overview of Chinese-language indicator systems, target-setting methods and weighting techniques for measuring Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: How to reflect China's distinctive institutional and cultural content while also connecting effectively with existing international evaluation systems has become one of the major practical difficulties in current modernization assessment.
quoteZh: 如何在指标构建时既体现中国特色的制度与文化内涵，又能与国际现行评价体系有效衔接，成为当前现代化评价实践中的重要实践难题之一。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization, elaborated since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization, with five stated features, including a huge population and common prosperity.
The official framework, adopted at the 18th Party Congress (2012), that places economic, political, cultural, social and ecological development within one overall plan.
The official guideline of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, which several indicator systems use as their organising dimensions.

t: Chinese modernization as a major innovation in world modernization theory and practice
zh: 中国式现代化对世界现代化理论和实践的重大创新
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2025 no. 6
paras: Huang Jianjun and Gao Wei ask in what sense Chinese modernization amounts to a major innovation in world modernization theory and practice. Their answer is that it is a socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China, which in their account moves beyond the "theoretical traps" of Western modernization and the paradoxes produced by "capital first". They present it as a new form of human civilization.

The article is organised around six innovations that Chinese modernization is said to contain: a worldview, a value outlook, a view of history, a view of civilization, a view of democracy and an ecological outlook. Each is set against a Western counterpart and grounded in Marx and Engels (world history theory, historical materialism, the centrality of the people) and in speeches by Xi Jinping. The discussion is mostly conceptual rather than empirical and draws on Party documents from the 18th Party Congress (2012) onward.

The authors contend that the Western path rests on capital accumulation, colonial expansion, "end of history" thinking and a mechanical, extractive treatment of nature. Chinese modernization, by contrast, is described as proceeding from a world "community with a shared future for mankind", as putting the people first in its aims, its reliance and its standard of evaluation, and as resting on independent, self-reliant exploration. It is also said to respect civilizational diversity, to practise whole-process people's democracy including consultative democracy, and to pursue green development and harmony between humanity and nature. The authors treat these as practical applications of historical materialism and as a rejection of the equation of modernization with Westernization.

Huang and Gao conclude that Chinese modernization widens the paths open to developing countries, enriches Marxist modernization theory, and offers a "Chinese approach" and "Chinese wisdom" to humanity's search for a better social system. They summarise its contribution as six commitments: shared world prosperity, people first and common prosperity, self-confidence and self-reliance, cultural renewal, people's democracy and green development. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of how current Chinese theory frames Chinese modernization against Western models, with its Marxist and Xi Jinping citations.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that "modernization equals Westernization", revealed another picture within the broad scheme of world modernization, widened the paths to modernization open to the many developing countries, and created a new form of human civilization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，展现了世界现代化宏观图式中的另一幅图景，拓展了广大发展中国家走向现代化的路径选择，开创了人类文明新形态。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, elaborated in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is presented as socialist in nature and distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and world-view concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It holds that countries' interests and fates are bound together and calls for cooperative global governance.
A concept advanced by Xi Jinping in 2019 to describe China's democratic model. Officially it stresses participation in every stage of governance, not only voting.
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, emphasised in recent official policy as an essential requirement of Chinese modernization.
A Chinese term for democratic consultation, for example through the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference. Official texts describe it as a distinctive form of socialist democracy.

t: The functions of the humanistic spirit in the process of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化进程中人文精神的功能
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2025 no. 5
paras: Zhang Wu asks what role the humanistic spirit (renwen jingshen) plays in Chinese modernization, which the author describes as a modernization that creates a new form of human civilization and therefore needs its own cultural form. The article argues that, as China enters the stage of building a modern socialist great country, the humanistic spirit has moved from passively adapting to the market economy to actively leading modernization. Zhang defines it as a cultural idea that respects human value, attends to human needs and pursues free and all-round human development.

The article first traces three stages of the humanistic spirit since the socialist market economy was established: passive adaptation, deep reflection and active leadership. It then examines three fields of leadership (the economy, politics and society), followed by the way the humanistic spirit works through diffuse cultural "nourishment" at three levels of culture. A final section considers its adjusting function in four social settings: the consumer, risk, trust and competition societies. Marx, Engels, Weber, Fromm and the Frankfurt School appear as reference points.

Zhang's central claim is that the humanistic spirit supports Chinese modernization by shaping culture at three levels: everyday psychology, mass culture and public values. It should cultivate everyday psychology against anxiety and anomie, guide mass culture away from commercialisation and fragmentation, and safeguard public values. For public values, the author holds that Marxism and fine traditional Chinese culture meet precisely in the humanistic spirit, so the Two Integrations can overcome the "ancient–modern, Chinese–Western" dispute and go beyond the capitalist modernity that Zhang says subordinates people to things. In economic, political and social terms, the author links it to high-quality development, shared values for modernizing national governance, and Marx's "real community".

On the four social settings, Zhang argues that the answer to unrestrained desire, mobility-driven loss of belonging, distrust and meaningless competition is not suppression but regulation through the humanistic spirit. The author calls for a rational ethics of desire, a rebuilt life-world, an interest mechanism that rewards honesty, and competition that carries a sense of value. The article concludes that this would anchor the cultural form of Chinese modernization in people's inner lives. Read the original if you want a Chinese-language account of how Party-aligned scholars assign cultural and psychological functions to humanism within Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: In other words, the crux is not whether there should be competition, but what kind of competition there should be.
quoteZh: 换言之，问题的关键不在于要不要竞争，而在于要什么样的竞争。

glossary.explanation: The official concept for China's own path of modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as distinct from Western modernization.
A cultural orientation that stresses human value, dignity and development. In Chinese debate since the 1990s it has been a key term for discussing the spiritual consequences of marketisation.
Xi Jinping's formulation of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture, alongside the first integration with China's concrete realities.
An official goal, emphasised since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth based on innovation, efficiency and better living standards.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system, adopted as a reform goal in 1992–93, combining market mechanisms with public ownership and Party leadership.

t: Coordinating high-quality development and high-efficacy governance in the course of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化进程中统筹推进高质量发展和高效能治理
source: Studies on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics, 2025 no. 4
paras: Zhu Fengming asks how China can raise the effectiveness of national governance so as to carry forward high-quality development, at a time of profound change in global governance and of domestic economic transition. Taking up Xi Jinping's May 2025 remarks in Henan, the article argues that high-quality development and high-efficacy governance are mutually supporting pillars of Chinese modernization. In Zhu's account they form an organic whole, linking development with governance and vitality with order.

The article first defines both concepts. It then sets out their relationship through the Marxist theory of the state, the practical logic of governance and the people-centred value orientation they share. It goes on to discuss five relationships that must be handled together: economy and society, government and market, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and development and security. The last section proposes institutional routes: rule of law across legislation, enforcement, adjudication and compliance; digital government; co-building, co-governance and sharing; and improvements in people's wellbeing as the test of governance.

Zhu's central claim is that the two concepts are dialectically linked. High-efficacy governance supplies institutional support, resource coordination and risk prevention for development, while the quality of development, measured by the new development philosophy, provides governance with its value direction and its yardstick. Drawing on Marx, Engels, Deng Xiaoping and Xi, the author argues that development and governance are not in tension but form a single system. For each of the five relationships the article traces a historical sequence from the early People's Republic through reform and opening up to the new era. In Zhu's account, China has repeatedly adjusted the balance between the two sides in each pair without giving up either, for example by combining the decisive role of the market with a more capable government, and by combining efficiency with redistribution.

Zhu concludes that governance efficacy must be judged by whether people's sense of gain, happiness and security actually improves. The article proposes a framework that identifies needs through big data, reforms social security and public services, and evaluates results with third-party assessment and monitoring platforms. It also urges legislation for the digital economy and AI ethics, unified law enforcement, and an end to departmental data silos. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese scholars present the link between economic development and state governance, or the policy measures they propose.
quoteEn: High-quality development answers the question of what to develop for the people, and focuses on the content and quality of development.
quoteZh: 高质量发展回答为人民发展什么的问题，聚焦于发展的内容与质量

glossary.explanation: An official goal since the 19th Party Congress (2017), describing a shift from fast, scale-driven growth to growth emphasising quality, efficiency, innovation and shared benefits.

A term popularised in Xi Jinping's recent speeches, referring to a governance system that effectively turns institutional strengths into results. The article treats it as an original concept drawn from Chinese practice.
The official name for the Party's path of modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022), which stresses features seen as specific to China.
The official formula of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, introduced in 2015 as guidance for development.

t: The theoretical logic of the step-by-step progression of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化阶梯式递进的理论逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 6 March 2026
paras: This newspaper commentary takes up a formulation from the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025): that realising socialist modernization is a step-by-step, progressive historical process requiring sustained effort. Zhang and Tian argue that this "stepwise progression" reveals an internal law of Chinese modernization and is both a summary of past experience and a strategic guide for the future.

The authors organise the argument in three mutually supporting dimensions: historical, theoretical and world. Each is presented as showing a different aspect of the concept, from the Party's political resolve to its philosophical grounding and its global significance.

Historically, Zhang and Tian trace a path from the First Five-Year Plan to the 15th Five-Year Plan, describing a spiral rather than linear ascent in which the scope of modernization widened from material production to a comprehensive layout. They hold that staged goals, from subsistence to common prosperity, spared China the upheavals of some late-developing countries. Theoretically, they read the concept through Marx's phrase "practice of principled height", claiming it is not a copy of Western paths but draws lessons from the Soviet collapse, Latin American dependency and Western ecological and social crises. Globally, they argue it offers non-dependent development options, underpins the Belt and Road Initiative and four global initiatives, and creates a new form of human civilization.

The authors conclude that Chinese modernization should be understood as a civilizational practice of principled height, which alone explains its world-historical meaning. They present it as a creative transcendence, not a replacement, of Western civilization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars frame the Plenum's wording in historical, theoretical and international terms.
quoteEn: Stepwise progression is not only a strategic arrangement for achieving national rejuvenation but also a practical path to creating a new form of human civilization.
quoteZh: 阶梯式递进不仅是实现民族复兴的战略安排，也是创造人类文明新形态的实践路径。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A goal of shared affluence for all, emphasised in Party policy as part of socialist modernization.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme launched in 2013.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official claim that Chinese modernization creates a civilizational form distinct from capitalist modernity.

t: The Communist Party of China's great practice in leading women's liberation and development
zh: 中国共产党领导妇女解放与发展的伟大实践
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in March 2026, reviews how the Communist Party of China has led women's liberation and development over more than a century. Zhang and Wang argue that the Party has consistently put gender equality on its banner and produced historic achievements.

The article proceeds chronologically through four stages: the founding of the Party, the establishment of the People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Each stage is described through legal, organisational and developmental measures.

The authors argue that the Party's founding was the origin and turning point of the process, giving the women's movement a leadership core, a Marxist theoretical basis (the 1922 Second Congress resolution) and the goal of equality between men and women. They then trace a path from the 1950 Marriage Law, the 1954 Constitution and the creation of the Women's Federation, through the Law on the Protection of Women's Rights and Interests, the Program for the Development of Chinese Women (from 1995) and the 1995 Beijing World Conference, to anti-domestic-violence legislation, the Civil Code, gender-equality review mechanisms and the Global Women's Summit in the recent period.

The authors conclude that the "core code" of this history is adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times: turning the universal truths of the Marxist view of women into action plans for each historical stage and merging women's development into national development. They link women's future to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned chronology of Party narratives on women's policy, laws and institutions.
quoteEn: The founding of the Communist Party of China was the great point of origin and the fundamental turning point in the course of Chinese women's liberation and development.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的成立，是中国妇女解放与发展进程的伟大原点与根本转折。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and to each era's tasks. It is used to present Party policy as a continuous theoretical development.
The Party-led mass organisation for women, created in 1949. Its charter describes it as a bridge between the Party and women.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: The 15th Five-Year Plan: the internal logic and practical path of a "strong domestic market" and the new development pattern
zh: “十五五”规划：“强大国内市场”与新发展格局的内在逻辑与实践路径
source: Studies on Mao Zedong Thought, 2025 no. 5
paras: Li Jiangtao and Qian Junhao take up the call of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) to "build a strong domestic market and accelerate the construction of a new development pattern" for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. They argue that a strong domestic market is not a stand-alone policy choice but a structural necessity, set by China's stage of development, a changed international environment and the laws governing a large economy. It is presented as the key lever for achieving both an effective improvement in quality and a reasonable growth in quantity, and so for high-quality development.

After a short review of Chinese literature linking the strong domestic market to the new development philosophy, the article first explains why the strategy is needed. It looks at the external environment, domestic structural problems, the sequence of Party decisions since 2020 and the advantages of a country with over 1.4 billion people. It then sets out a four-part analytical framework of demand, supply, driving force and security. This framework is filled out through four areas and nine focal points, each with concrete policy measures.

The core argument rests on two moves. First, the authors hold that the old international-circulation model of "both ends abroad" no longer fits, given external shocks and Western technology controls and decoupling, so domestic circulation must offset international uncertainty. They cite figures such as foreign-trade dependence falling from 55.5% in 2008 to 32.5% in 2024, and domestic demand contributing an average of 98.3% of growth since the international financial crisis. Second, they argue that demand and supply must reinforce each other: consumption and investment are to be expanded by linking improvements in people's livelihoods with consumption, and "investment in things" with "investment in people". They note a 2024 household consumption rate of 39.9%, about 28 points below the United States. The proposed measures include a unified national market, macroeconomic governance centred on consumption, and security in food, energy and industrial chains.

The authors conclude that building a strong domestic market will gradually reduce reliance on external markets and produce a higher-level dynamic balance in which demand pulls supply and supply creates demand. They describe it as essential to Chinese modernization and as a route to security, resilience and sustainable prosperity. The article also calls for further research that quantifies the contribution of the new development philosophy to market efficiency. Read the original if you want a detailed, policy-oriented account of how Chinese economists frame the 15th Five-Year Plan's domestic-demand strategy, including its statistics and nine-point agenda.
quoteEn: A strong domestic market is not only a timely arrangement for meeting external risks and challenges, but also an endogenous development advantage and core support of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 强大国内市场不仅是应对外部风险挑战的应势布局，更是中国式现代化的内生性发展优势与核心支撑。

glossary.explanation: A strategy put forward by Xi Jinping in 2020 that takes domestic circulation as the mainstay, with domestic and international circulation reinforcing each other.
A policy goal, set out in the 14th and 15th Five-Year Plan documents, of expanding domestic demand and supply so that the economy relies mainly on internal circulation.
The official term for the Party's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.
