The official guiding principle for the economy since 2017, which stresses quality, efficiency and innovation rather than speed of growth alone.
Five concepts announced in 2015: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.

t: Theoretical innovation and global significance of Chinese modernization from the perspective of the Global South
zh: 全球南方视角下中国式现代化的理论创新与世界意义
paras: Wang Yashan asks what Chinese modernization's theoretical innovations mean for the Global South, at a time the author describes as one of declining Western hegemony and the collective rise of developing countries. The article argues that Chinese modernization, built through the Two Integrations, breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization. In Wang's account it offers Global South states a non-dependent path and supports reform of global governance.

The article first clarifies the concept of the Global South, tracing it from its 1969 origin through the 1977 Brandt Line and the 1974 declaration on a New International Economic Order to its present use. It then sets out the internal and external tensions the concept faces. Wang next examines Chinese modernization in five dimensions: Party leadership and politics, the economic system, ecology, a conception of civilization, and common prosperity. The final sections discuss its practical effects and its discursive significance.

Wang defines the Global South as a successor to the Third World: a bloc of emerging and developing countries, formerly structurally marginal, that now carries an anti-dependence and decolonial charge. The author stresses its heterogeneity, citing divergent Latin American paths and states that remain dependent on Western security ties. Wang also holds that Western discourse tries to depoliticise the concept and spreads narratives such as the 'debt trap'. Against this background, the article contends that Chinese modernization transcends the single logic of capital. It does so through Party leadership, a basic economic system with public ownership as the mainstay and an 'effective market and capable government', green development, and common prosperity. Wang argues that these offer lessons for avoiding the 'middle-income trap'.

Wang concludes that Chinese modernization breaks the Western monopoly on defining modernization and promotes a decolonial turn in Global South theory. The article points to the Belt and Road Initiative, South-South cooperation mechanisms and the Global South think-tank alliance as practical channels. It also quotes Xi Jinping that each country is best placed to judge which modernization suits it, and calls on Global South states to remain independent. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist journal links Global South discourse to Chinese modernization and presents it as a development model.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that 'modernization equals Westernization'. It presents a different picture of modernization and offers Global South countries the possibility of breaking free from dependent development.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，展现了现代化的另一幅图景，为全球南方国家提供了突破依附性发展模式的可能性。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization under Communist Party leadership, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as socialist, as having Chinese characteristics, and as an alternative to Western models.
Official formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. It is used to describe how Marxism is adapted in China.
A term for developing and emerging countries, historically post-colonial. Chinese official discourse uses it to describe China's place among these states and its solidarity with them.
A goal of shared wealth for all people, described officially as an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It has been emphasised heavily under Xi Jinping.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme, launched in 2013.

t: The Chinese Communist Party's promotion of an international united front: historical course, basic experience and practical paths
zh: 中国共产党推动构建国际统一战线的历史进程、基本经验和实践路径
paras: Wang Xinying and Zhang Xianyan ask how the Chinese Communist Party has built an international united front over its history, and what that record implies for building a new one today. They treat the united front as a key instrument of the Party's success in revolution, construction and reform, and the international front as one of its component parts. Against the background of the interwoven "two overall situations" (national rejuvenation and global change), they argue that the Party's long experience offers a guide for a new-era international united front aimed at a community with a shared future for mankind.

The article has three parts. The first traces the history through the New Democratic Revolution and the War of Resistance against Japan, the early People's Republic, the period from the mid-1960s to the late 1970s, reform and opening up, and the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second distils three lessons from the century-long record. The third sets out four practical paths for the present. Throughout, the authors draw on Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping.

On history, the authors argue that the front's targets and tasks shifted with the main contradiction of each period. Examples include exploiting inter-imperialist conflicts, the wartime anti-fascist front, the "one line, one large area" policy, Mao's "three worlds" theory, and the partnership diplomacy and global initiatives of recent decades. The three lessons are: handling independence and self-reliance dialectically alongside international solidarity and aid; coordinating domestic and international fronts; and keeping strategy and tactics in organic unity. The authors hold that the Party's nature and purpose give its strategy constant features: fairness and justice, opposition to aggression and hegemony, a focus on developing countries, and an identity as a builder of world peace.

For the new era, the authors propose four paths. First, use the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind as the "greatest common denominator", supplying international public goods through the Belt and Road Initiative and four global initiatives (development, security, civilization, governance). Second, make Global South countries the main targets of the front and expand ties with major powers and neighbours. Third, build issue-based alliances on development and climate, and, in the face of US strategic competition, widen China's "circle of friends" while seeking cooperation with the United States on shared concerns. Fourth, improve China's international image and communication, moving from "one-sided telling" to "joint narrative". Read the original if you want a Party-historical account of how Chinese scholars link united front doctrine to present-day foreign policy and Global South strategy.
quoteEn: The key to a united front lies in uniting the majority, and building an international united front must likewise win over the majority of international actors.
quoteZh: 统一战线的关键在于团结大多数，国际统一战线的构建也必须抓住国际行为体中的大多数。

glossary.explanation: A Leninist-derived strategy by which the Party unites diverse classes, groups and forces around a shared goal while keeping its own leadership. The Party calls it one of its key "magic weapons".

A formula used since Xi Jinping's leadership for the strategic overall picture of national rejuvenation and the world's "great changes unseen in a century", which the Party says must be handled together.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's guiding concept for international relations, promoted since 2012–13. It stresses shared interests, cooperation and mutual benefit among countries.
A term for developing countries, which Chinese official discourse presents as a growing force in world affairs and as a main partner of China.
Mao Zedong's 1970s division of the world into the superpowers, the developed countries in between, and the developing countries of the Third World, with China placed in the Third World.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Realising Chinese modernization requires discursive innovation
zh: 实现中国式现代化需要话语创新
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 February 2026
paras: Pan Yong argues in this newspaper commentary that modernization begins with a change of ideas, and that Chinese modernization therefore depends on discursive innovation. Changes in behaviour, the author holds, follow changes in concepts, so a country's modernization requires the modernization of its own system of ideas.

The article defines "discursive innovation" as the creation of new, vivid and substantive expressions rooted in Chinese problems and contexts, taking the form of key words, key sentences or notable texts. It covers both the political discourse of the leadership and the scholarly expression of researchers in philosophy and the social sciences. It then introduces the notion of a "thought-rich China" (sixiang Zhongguo) and sets out three enabling conditions.

Pan contends that the social sciences contribute new discourse and ideas, as the natural sciences contribute new technology, and that coining new concepts is the starting point of discursive innovation. A "thought-rich China" is a state in which citizens' ideas flow freely and can be turned into material productive forces. The three conditions are an open cultural atmosphere in the spirit of "let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools of thought contend"; a focus on the new practice and problems of socialism in the new era; and platforms that let talented people raise and study problems. Examples include the Qian Xuesen Question, Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream" and Deng Xiaoping's "cat theory".

Pan concludes that cultivating the power of thought is now a strategic task of national development, with education as its cradle. Pan cites the educator Yu Yi's complaint that teachers lack intellectual depth and critical thinking, which leads to formulaic borrowing of language. Scholars, the article says, must root themselves in the practice of reform and opening up to produce ideas that suit the era and serve the people. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese education scholar links conceptual innovation, academic discourse and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Innovation in ideas is the fundamental logical starting point of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 观念创新是中国式现代化的根本逻辑起点。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: let a hundred flowers bloom, let a hundred schools of thought contend
glossary.explanation: A policy slogan associated with Mao Zedong in the 1950s, calling for diversity in the arts and academic debate.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A slogan Xi Jinping put forward in 2012, centred on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
A question posed by the scientist Qian Xuesen: why Chinese universities do not produce outstanding, innovative talent.

t: Contributing greater strength from state-owned assets and central enterprises to Chinese modernization
zh: 为中国式现代化建设贡献国资央企更大力量
authors: Party Committee of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council
paras: This commentary was written by the Party Committee of the State Council's state-owned assets regulator (SASAC) and published in the People's Daily on 2 March 2026. It sets out how central state-owned enterprises should study and apply Xi Jinping's instructions of late 2025 on their work. The authors argue that state-owned enterprises are a key pillar of the Party's governance and must be unwaveringly made stronger, better and bigger to contribute to Chinese modernization.

The text is organised in three parts. The first reviews the missions of state assets and central enterprises: serving the overall work of the Party and state, high-quality development, and the improvement of people's livelihoods. The second sets out priorities for reform and development. The third covers Party leadership and Party discipline within these enterprises. It places all of this at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period and links it to the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee and the Central Economic Work Conference.

The authors first claim a record of achievement. During the 14th Five-Year Plan period, they say, central enterprise assets passed 95 trillion yuan, cumulative tax contributions came to nearly 13 trillion yuan, and R&D spending exceeded 1 trillion yuan for four years running. They then present the priorities as four tasks: optimising the layout of the state economy through the "three concentrations" of state capital, integrating scientific and industrial innovation around new quality productive forces, deepening reform through the "Two Unswervings" of Party leadership and modern enterprise systems, and balancing development with security. Finally, they hold that Party leadership "can only be strengthened, not weakened", and that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party allows no exceptions in state enterprises, which they describe as rich in funds, resources and assets.

The authors conclude that central enterprises should hold to the theme of high-quality development, with new quality productive forces as the focus, reform as the driving force, and attention to both development and security. They also call for new Party-building arrangements suited to enterprises' new missions, including a long-term study mechanism, integration of Party work with production and operations, and regular accountability talks. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how SASAC frames the role, priorities and Party leadership of central enterprises at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Party leadership and Party building in state-owned enterprises can only be strengthened, not weakened.
quoteZh: 国有企业党的领导党的建设只能加强、不能削弱。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, emphasised since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as including common prosperity and high-quality development.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It refers to productivity growth driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging industries.
The official guiding goal for the economy since 2017. It stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's campaign of discipline, supervision and anti-corruption within its own ranks, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.pinyin: liǎng gè yǐ yī guàn zhī
glossary.literal: the two 'must be upheld consistently' principles
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula that Party leadership over state enterprises and the establishment of a modern enterprise system must both be upheld consistently. The commentary refers to it as a core principle of state-enterprise reform.

t: Using systems thinking to strengthen long-term mechanisms for governing the online ecosystem
zh: 以系统思维健全网络生态治理长效机制
paras: This commentary from Guangming Daily asks how China can build lasting mechanisms for governing its online ecosystem. Yao Hongzhi and Liu Dong argue that governance must shift from crude to refined methods, and from simply "keeping things under control" to "governing well". In their view this requires systems thinking applied to every stage and aspect of governance. They describe online governance as both a hard-fought and a protracted campaign, and say the security situation remains complex and serious.

The authors begin with the progress made since the 18th Party Congress (2012), when the Party Central Committee under Xi Jinping put online governance high on its agenda. They then quote Xi Jinping's remarks at the 23rd collective study session of the Political Bureau, which called for governance that is forward-looking, precise, systematic and coordinated. The body of the piece has four parts: overall planning, structural design, dynamic adjustment and coordination of means. Each is framed with a chess, ledger, initiative or boxing metaphor.

On overall planning, the authors call for stronger top-level design, the breaking down of barriers between departments and platforms, and a balance between vitality and order, and between development and security. On structure, they set out a pattern of multiple actors with matching powers and responsibilities: Party leadership, government regulation, platform duties, social oversight and netizen self-discipline. They also propose differentiated strategies. Open violations such as online violence, rumours and fraud call for severe legal punishment. Problems of fan-club culture and vulgar content call for moral, industry and guidance measures. Algorithmic discrimination and information cocoons call for technical and rule-design remedies. On dynamic adjustment, they propose tracking frontier technologies such as artificial intelligence, building big-data early-warning systems, and using "regulatory sandboxes" with regular policy review.

The authors conclude that governance tools should be combined: law with technology, regulation with guidance, and incentives with constraints. They want officials moved from "being made to govern" to "wanting to govern", so that long-term mechanisms are strengthened and the online space becomes a reliable security basis for building a strong country and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary translates systems thinking into a framework for internet governance.
quoteEn: Governing the online ecosystem is a shared responsibility of the whole society: it is not a "solo" performed by government or individuals alone, but a "symphony" in which many actors take part.
quoteZh: 网络生态治理是全社会的共同责任，不是单纯依靠政府或个人的“独奏曲”，而是多元主体共同参与的“交响乐”。

glossary.explanation: A method stressing wholeness, interconnection and the relation between part and whole. Chinese official writing links it to the "systems concept" promoted in Xi Jinping-era theory.
A controlled setting in which new technologies or policies can be tested under regulatory supervision before wider adoption.

t: Strengthening the leading role of leading technology enterprises in tackling key core technologies
zh: 强化科技领军企业在关键核心技术攻关中的引领作用
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 24 February 2026, Huo Chunhui and He Di ask how China's leading technology enterprises can be made to play a guiding role in breaking through key core technologies. They argue that, as part of the national strategic science and technology forces, these firms have strengths in innovation, talent and industrial leadership. In the authors' view, strengthening their role is a strategic measure for international technology competition and for high-level technological self-reliance.

The piece begins from the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), which list greater technological self-reliance among the main goals. It then sets out four areas of leadership: innovation decision-making, R&D investment, cooperation in research breakthroughs, and the transfer of results into production.

On decision-making, Huo and He propose treating leading firms as the "question-setters" who originate major technology needs, with more say in planning, project selection and expert panels. On investment, they call for long-term mechanisms linking policy support to R&D intensity, tax deductions, science-and-technology finance and open access to research facilities. On cooperation, they want these firms to lead innovation consortia with universities, institutes and supply-chain firms, with governance rules against free-riding, and to join global innovation networks. On transfer, they call for outcome evaluation by import substitution, market share and economic returns, government procurement and early-market support for first-of-kind products, and the gathering of talent in these firms.

The authors conclude that firm-led, demand-driven mechanisms can link the innovation chain to the industrial chain and reduce market and organisational failure. Their recommendations are institutional and policy measures rather than empirical findings. Read the original if you want a compact view of current Chinese policy thinking on enterprise-led innovation under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Leading technology enterprises should become the proposers of directions for tackling key core technologies, with rapid response to their urgent technological needs and encouragement for them to take the lead in proposing breakthrough projects.
quoteZh: 推动科技领军企业成为关键核心技术攻关方向的提出者，强化对科技领军企业紧迫技术需求的快速响应，鼓励和引导科技领军企业牵头提出关键核心技术攻关项目。

glossary.explanation: A policy category for large, technologically advanced firms expected to lead national innovation efforts. Official documents treat them as part of the national strategic science and technology forces.
Technologies seen as critical to industrial security and competitiveness, often those where China depends on foreign supply. Breakthroughs here are a stated priority of national policy.

glossary.literal: science and technology self-reliance and self-strengthening
glossary.explanation: A policy goal of reducing dependence on foreign technology and building independent innovation capacity. It has been emphasised in Party documents in recent years.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, drawn up on the basis of proposals adopted by the Party's Central Committee in 2025.
Cooperative bodies of firms, universities and research institutes organised around a shared research task. The article proposes that leading firms head them.

t: Anchoring on agricultural and rural modernization to build a strong agricultural nation
zh: 锚定农业农村现代化建设农业强国
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 11 February 2026, interprets the agricultural and rural parts of the Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). Peng Wei argues that agricultural and rural modernization bears on "the overall situation and quality" of Chinese modernization, and that the whole Party should anchor on it in order to move steadily toward building a strong agricultural nation.

The article is organised around three tasks drawn from the Recommendations: raising overall agricultural production capacity and quality and efficiency; building liveable, workable and beautiful villages; and making policies that strengthen agriculture and benefit farmers more effective so that rural incomes grow steadily. Each section cites Xi Jinping's statements ("if China is to be strong, agriculture must be strong"; "if China is to be beautiful, the countryside must be beautiful"; "if China is to be prosperous, farmers must be prosperous"), explains the Recommendations' wording, and then lists measures for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

On production, Peng distinguishes a narrow concept of capacity (the maximum output of farmland, with grain output stable above 1.4 trillion jin in 2025, as the article cites) from a broad one that includes higher factor efficiency and newly tapped factors. The author calls for food security as the first priority, farmland protection, high-standard farmland, seed breeding and machinery upgrades, new quality productive forces such as AI and biotechnology in farming, and a larger, extended agricultural value chain. On villages, Peng stresses a people-centred approach, adaptation to local conditions, the lessons of the "Thousand Villages Programme" and a new "cluster-based" approach to rural revitalization, while insisting that good rural living space does not mean making villages like cities. On incomes, the article cites rural per capita disposable income of 24,456 yuan in 2025 (up 6% in real terms) and proposes stronger price, subsidy and insurance support, county-level industries, extended land contracts, and urban–rural integration through citizenship for migrants and two-way flows of factors.

Peng concludes that these measures together would make agriculture a modern large-scale industry, give villages a high-quality living space and secure stable income growth for farmers, advancing the goal of "high-quality and efficient agriculture, liveable and workable villages, and prosperous farmers". Read the original if you want a concise, official-line reading of the agricultural and rural priorities of the 15th Five-Year Plan Recommendations and the policy measures a provincial Party-theory researcher draws from them.
quoteEn: Creating a high-quality living space in the countryside does not mean building villages to be just like cities, but proceeding from local realities and responding to farmers' needs.
quoteZh: 打造乡村优质生活空间不是把乡村建设得和城市一样，而是要从各地实际出发，回应农民需求

glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's path of national development, formally elaborated from the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for productivity growth driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging and future industries rather than by traditional factor inputs.
A rural environmental and village improvement programme launched in Zhejiang in 2003 under Xi Jinping, now promoted as a model for rural revitalization nationwide.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to develop rural industry, environment, governance and living standards, succeeding the poverty-alleviation campaign.
A Party goal, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022), of building a country strong in agricultural supply, technology, equipment, industry and competitiveness.

t: Making good use of the valuable experience of formulating and implementing Five-Year Plans
zh: 运用好制定实施五年规划的宝贵经验
paras: This People's Daily commentary, published in February 2026, studies Xi Jinping's speech at the opening of a study seminar for provincial and ministerial leaders on the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). Dong Yu takes up the question of what experience China has accumulated in drawing up and carrying out Five-Year Plans. The author argues that Xi's "five adherences" summarise this experience and should guide the 15th Five-Year Plan period so that it opens well and continues the "two miracles" of rapid growth and long-term social stability.

The piece takes the five adherences one by one: the centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee; proceeding from reality; the nationwide "one game of chess" approach; promoting democracy and drawing on collective wisdom; and the principle that planning has a statutory basis. Each section combines Xi's remarks with examples from the Five-Year Plans since the 12th, especially the recommendations for the 15th. A closing section assesses the theoretical significance of the experience.

On leadership, Dong describes a standard procedure: the Central Committee proposes recommendations, the State Council drafts an outline, and the National People's Congress approves it, which the author says turns Party leadership into governing practice. On reality and the national chessboard, Dong cites six research teams visiting 12 provinces and 35 commissioned research projects, as well as 165 major projects in the 13th and 102 in the 14th Five-Year Plan period, which the author credits with poverty alleviation and technological progress. On democracy, the author lists Xi's symposia and an online consultation that drew more than 3.113 million comments, and calls this a vivid expression of whole-process people's democracy. On legal status, Dong describes a unified planning system and a closed loop running from long-term strategy to Five-Year Plan to annual plan, with national planning legislation under way.

Dong concludes that this experience enriches Xi Jinping's thinking on development strategy and planning. The author calls it an important product of socialist political economy with Chinese characteristics and a contribution to development economics that offers developing countries a reference point. The author calls on officials to uphold institutional confidence and apply the five adherences to make plans more forward-looking, guiding and innovative, in support of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an official, People's Daily-style account of how the Five-Year Plan process is presented and the 15th Five-Year Plan is being framed.
quoteEn: Through institutionalised means, the Five-Year Plan turns the centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee into governing practice, providing a fundamental guarantee for socialist modernization.
quoteZh: 五年规划通过制度化方式将党中央集中统一领导转化为治理实践，为社会主义现代化建设提供了根本保证。

glossary.explanation: China's medium-term national development blueprint, first issued in the 1950s as a 'plan' and now called a 'plan' (规划). It is drafted by the Party and State Council and approved by the National People's Congress.
Xi Jinping's summary of lessons from Five-Year Planning: Party leadership, proceeding from reality, a nationwide approach, democracy and collective wisdom, and statutory planning.

glossary.literal: the whole country as one chessboard
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan for coordinating all regions and departments under a unified national plan, subordinating local interests to the overall situation.
The official term, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path to modernization under Party leadership.
The official description of China's democracy, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, which stresses participation across the whole policymaking cycle rather than only elections.

t: Actively expanding the content and direction of autonomous opening up
zh: 积极扩大自主开放的内涵和方向
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily on 11 February 2026, takes up "autonomous opening up" (zizhu kaifang), a key term in the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan and in the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference. Li Dawei argues that China's opening up must shift from "following" to "leading", and that autonomous opening is therefore the necessary choice, showing China's confidence and responsibility as a major country.
The piece defines the concept, explains its significance for domestic development and for the external environment, and then sets out three new directions and four priority tasks.

Li defines autonomous opening as innovating opening models, setting the pace and optimising the scope of opening according to China's own needs, rather than copying other economies, opening under external pressure or adopting their "opening lists". Domestically, the author says it addresses weak effective demand and blocked high-end factor circulation. Externally, it helps counter protectionism and "decoupling". The three directions are: aligning with high-standard international trade rules while creating new ones, for example in emerging and future industries; combining agreement-based opening with orderly unilateral opening, including in services market access and cross-border movement of people; and attracting quality factors while guiding supply chains to locate across borders in an orderly way, partly through the Belt and Road Initiative.

The four tasks Li proposes are: focusing on services opening, such as telecoms, culture, healthcare and education, together with data and talent measures; developing new trade and investment models; building varied opening platforms such as free trade ports and free trade pilot zones; and pursuing high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, including promoting the internationalisation of the renminbi. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Chinese economists frame the new policy keyword "autonomous opening" and its practical measures.
quoteEn: Autonomous opening takes account of both China's needs and the world's expectations.
quoteZh: 自主开放兼顾中国之需与世界之盼

glossary.explanation: A policy term in the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan, meaning opening that China designs and paces on its own terms rather than in response to outside models or pressure.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030.
A framework for infrastructure and economic cooperation with other countries, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
An annual meeting of Party and state leaders that sets economic policy priorities for the coming year.

t: How to develop service-oriented manufacturing with Chinese characteristics
zh: 如何发展有中国特色的服务型制造
paras: This newspaper commentary asks what service-oriented manufacturing is and how China should develop a version with Chinese characteristics. Huang argues that it is a key route for turning China's huge market and complete industrial system into lasting competitiveness, and a response to the pressures of manufacturing upgrading. The piece opens from a 2025 implementation plan issued by seven ministries and from the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan.

The article first defines the concept and its Chinese distinguishing features. It then sets out four reasons China has a foundation for it, and closes with four policy directions for high-quality development.

Huang defines service-oriented manufacturing as a shift from selling products to offering "product plus service", extending services across research and design, production, and operation and maintenance. The Chinese version is said to stress alignment with national industrial upgrading, a large-scale market that supports differentiated niches, and digital empowerment that merges the real and digital economies. The four supporting arguments are system solutions over the product life cycle, technological strength in high-end equipment, new energy and intelligent manufacturing, growth that eases resource and environmental limits, and ecosystem cooperation that brings small and medium-sized firms into industrial networks.

Huang calls for a full-chain digital service system with computing infrastructure and AI integration, and for fostering key producer-service sectors. The author also urges a unified national market that removes regional barriers and local protection, and stronger enterprise agency in exploring servitisation paths. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy rationale for service-oriented manufacturing and its recommended measures.
quoteEn: Developing service-oriented manufacturing with Chinese characteristics also means developing service-oriented manufacturing at a world-class level.
quoteZh: 发展具有中国特色的服务型制造，也意味着要发展具有世界水平的服务型制造。

glossary.explanation: A model in which manufacturers raise the share of services in their business, moving from selling goods to offering bundled products and services across the value chain. It is promoted in Chinese industrial policy.
An official economic goal since the late 2010s that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030. The recommendations for it were adopted by the Party leadership in 2025.
A policy aim of removing local protectionism and barriers so that goods, capital, data and labour flow freely across China.

t: Forming an economic order that is both "freed up" and "well managed"
zh: 形成“放得活”“管得好”的经济秩序
paras: This short commentary from Economic Daily takes up a formula taken from the Central Economic Work Conference: the economy must be both "fangdehuo" (freed up, or given room to thrive) and "guandehao" (well managed). Zeng Zheng argues that a good economic order is integral to a high-standard socialist market economy. In the author's account, the formula expresses the organic unity of an efficient market and a capable government, and is a requirement for modernizing national governance.

The article has three parts. It first reviews the history of the government–market relationship since 1978, from reforms that loosened controls and risked disorder, through the market-economy system of 1992 and WTO accession, to the new conditions after the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then compares "managing well" with the earlier wording "managing tightly" (guandezhu) across four goals: efficiency, fairness, stability and security. Finally it sets out three relationships to balance and three levels at which order should be maintained.

Zeng's central claim is that the change from "guandezhu" to "guandehao" is more than a single character. It signals governance based on law and institutions, more precise and flexible, and more forward-looking, moving from blocking to channelling problems. The author says the two halves must be balanced in three pairs: efficiency and fairness, innovation and stability, and development and security. "Freeing up" mainly promotes efficiency, innovation and openness. "Managing well" protects fairness, sets risk controls and holds security red lines.

For practice, Zeng proposes action at three levels. In macroeconomic regulation, the author calls for forward-looking, targeted and coordinated policy, including better expectation management and consistency between policies. In industrial promotion, Zeng urges a shift toward functional industrial policy, fair competition among all forms of ownership and a supportive ecosystem for firms. In market order, the author calls for stronger basic institutions, a unified national market, protection of property rights and inclusive, prudent, credit-based supervision. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese policy advisers interpret the "freed up yet well managed" formula in the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: "Managing well" versus "managing tightly" looks like a difference of a single character, but in fact it places higher demands on the way China governs its economy.
quoteZh: “管得好”相较“管得住”，看似一字之差，实则对我国经济治理的方式提出了更高的要求。

glossary.literal: released so that it comes alive
glossary.explanation: Shorthand for loosening controls so that market actors have vitality and room to innovate. It is paired with "managing well" in recent economic policy language.
Phrase from the Party's 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations (2025), replacing the earlier "guandezhu" (managing tightly). It stresses precise, law-based and forward-looking regulation.

glossary.en: an efficient market and a capable government
glossary.literal: effective market and government that accomplishes something
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the combined roles of market and state in the socialist market economy. It is used to argue that both should play active, complementary roles.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official name for China's economic system, adopted as a reform goal in 1992. It combines market allocation of resources with state leadership and public ownership.
Annual meeting of top Party and state leaders, held at year's end, that sets economic policy priorities for the next year.

t: Coordinated development of industry and employment as an important foundation of comprehensive rural revitalization
zh: 产业就业协同发展是乡村全面振兴重要根基
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how industry and employment in the countryside can be developed together so as to support comprehensive rural revitalization, whose core aim the authors describe as a strong agriculture, a beautiful countryside and prosperous farmers. Wang and Liu argue that deep integration of the two is a necessary requirement for that aim. They tie the point to the 2024 and 2025 Central Economic Work Conferences and the 2026 No. 1 Central Document, which stress industry and employment support and holding the line against large-scale return to poverty.

The article has three parts. It first defines the internal logic of coordinated industry–employment development, then sets out how it bears on each dimension of rural revitalization, and finally proposes practical paths. The dimensions are thriving industry, ecological livability, civilised rural customs, effective governance and prosperous livelihoods.

The authors define coordination as matching the quality and quantity of jobs that industry creates to workers' skills and career needs, so that industrial competitiveness and income growth advance together. In their account it rests on matching local resource endowments to comparative advantage, linking skills training to industrial demand, organisational innovation with benefit-sharing arrangements, and digital technology integrated with traditional industries. They claim the effects are multiplicative rather than linear: industrial clusters, green industry, local employment, cultural industries and cooperatives or common-prosperity workshops are said to strengthen the economy, the environment, community identity, governance and farmers' incomes. Stable employment is called the most effective firewall against falling back into poverty.

The authors propose three paths. First, county-level planning with a 'one village, one policy' approach and integrated industry–employment policy tools, using new jobs and wage growth as core indicators when allocating industrial funds. Second, developing distinctive local industries, deeper agricultural processing, regional brands, industrial clustering and digital rural commerce. Third, 'order-based' skills training, in which firms place orders, training bodies draw up the menu and government pays, together with cultivating local talent and attracting people back to the countryside. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the policy thinking behind industry and employment support in rural revitalization policy in 2026.
quoteEn: Industry is the carrier of employment, and employment is the support of industry.
quoteZh: 产业是就业的载体，就业是产业的支撑。

glossary.explanation: A national strategy launched in 2017 and elevated in later Party documents. It aims to modernise agriculture, the countryside and farmers' livelihoods across industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.
The first policy document the Party Central Committee and State Council issue each year. Since 2004 it has been devoted to agriculture, rural areas and farmers.
An annual meeting of top Party and state leaders, held at the end of the year, that sets economic policy priorities for the next year.
Small local production or processing sites, set up in villages under the common prosperity agenda, that provide nearby jobs and income for rural residents.

t: Cultivating new momentum for economic development with artificial intelligence
zh: 以人工智能培育经济发展新动能
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2026, asks how artificial intelligence (AI) can generate new momentum for economic development. Li Tao and Xu Xiang take their cue from the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) and the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference, which call for fully implementing the "AI+" initiative. The authors argue that AI is a strategic foundation for new quality productive forces and high-quality development, provided it is steered towards social harmony and common prosperity.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the logic of AI-driven change: its role in productive forces, the evolution of the digital economy, and the subordination of technology to high-quality development. The second examines how AI's potential can be released through domestic demand, supply quality, new growth space and the revitalisation of existing assets. The third proposes a system of policies on security, integration with the real economy, and social stability.

Li and Xu contend that AI transforms labourers, means of labour and objects of labour, so that workers become creators and masters of intelligent systems, algorithms and computing power become means of labour, and data becomes an object of labour. They describe a shift from informatisation to intelligence, and from human–machine collaboration to human–machine integration. On the demand side they cite online retail at 24.9 per cent of retail sales of consumer goods in the first half of 2025. On the supply side they point to Chinese firms among the World Economic Forum's "lighthouse factories". On growth they cite figures from the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology: a core AI industry above 900 billion yuan in 2024, up 24 per cent, and more than 5,300 AI firms by September 2025. They accept that AI may disrupt employment in the short term but expect it to create new jobs, such as data annotators and algorithm optimisers.

The authors call for coordinating development and security through algorithm filing and tiered, category-based supervision, safety assessment of large models, and rules on cross-border data flows. They also want AI moved from laboratories to production lines, with industry data spaces and open public data to lower costs for small firms. They further urge worker retraining, job-transition support, and fiscal and inclusive-finance measures against wealth concentration and the digital divide. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official-aligned economists link AI policy to the Five-Year Plan, new quality productive forces and common prosperity.
quoteEn: The development of artificial intelligence cannot be divorced from the fundamental goals of social harmony and common prosperity.
quoteZh: 人工智能的发展不能脱离社会和谐与共同富裕的根本目标。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and innovation rather than resource-intensive growth.
An official goal since 2017 that stresses efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
A socialist goal of shared wealth for all, given renewed policy emphasis under Xi Jinping.
A national action plan to integrate AI into industry, culture, public services and governance, building on the earlier "Internet+" idea.

t: Anchoring on agricultural and rural modernization to build a strong agricultural nation
zh: 锚定农业农村现代化建设农业强国
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily, interprets what the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) said about agriculture and the countryside. Peng Wei takes up the Plenum's Proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan, which hold that agricultural and rural modernization bears on the whole and the quality of Chinese modernization. The author argues that the country should anchor on this task and advance steadily towards building a strong agricultural nation.

The article is organised around three tasks drawn from the Proposals: raising overall agricultural production capacity and quality; building liveable, workable and beautiful villages; and making policies that strengthen agriculture and benefit farmers more effective so that farmers' incomes grow steadily. Each section cites Xi Jinping's formulas (a strong China needs strong agriculture, a beautiful countryside and prosperous farmers), explains the relevant passage of the Proposals, and then sets out what Peng sees as priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

On production, Peng distinguishes a narrow notion of capacity (the maximum yield of cultivated land, with 2025 grain output cited as stable above 1.4 trillion jin) from a broad one that includes higher efficiency and new factors of production. The author calls for food security as the first priority, new quality productive forces in agriculture through biotechnology, artificial intelligence and smart farming, and new modes of operation that link smallholders to modern agriculture. On villages, Peng stresses a people-centred approach, adapting measures to local conditions, and a 'cluster-based' approach that groups villages by proximity, endowments, industry and culture. The author adds that quality village life does not mean making villages like cities.

On incomes, Peng notes that farmers rely mainly on wages and transfer payments, and cites a 2025 rural per capita disposable income of 24,456 yuan, up 6 per cent in real terms. The author proposes stronger price, subsidy and insurance support, county-level industries that create local jobs, and measures to break down the urban–rural dual structure, including settling migrant workers in cities while protecting their rural land and property rights. Peng concludes that these steps together would make agriculture a modern industry and give farmers a better life. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of the rural content of the 15th Five-Year Plan Proposals and the policy vocabulary used to describe it.
quoteEn: Creating high-quality living spaces in the countryside does not mean building villages to be like cities, but proceeding from local realities and responding to farmers' needs.
quoteZh: 打造乡村优质生活空间不是把乡村建设得和城市一样，而是要从各地实际出发，回应农民需求

glossary.explanation: The Party's official concept of a distinctive path of modernization, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as the central task of national development.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 that stresses technology-driven, innovation-led productive forces such as AI and advanced manufacturing.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, whose Proposals were adopted at the Fourth Plenum.

t: Making good use of the valuable experience in formulating and implementing Five-Year Plans
zh: 运用好制定实施五年规划的宝贵经验
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 11 February 2026, this commentary is a study of Xi Jinping's speech at the opening of a seminar for provincial and ministerial leaders on the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). Dong Yu takes up Xi's summary of the Party's experience in making Five-Year Plans as "Five Adherences". The author argues that this experience should be grasped and applied so that the 15th Five-Year Plan period starts well and Chinese modernization continues.

The article opens with the achievements of the 12th to 14th Five-Year Plan periods since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then devotes one section to each of the five principles: the centralized and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee, proceeding from reality, a nationwide "single chessboard", promoting democracy and drawing on collective wisdom, and the statutory basis of planning. Each section mixes Xi's statements with examples from the 13th, 14th and 15th Five-Year Plan processes.

Dong presents the principles as a linked system. Central leadership is said to turn Party proposals into state will through a set procedure: the Central Committee proposes, the State Council drafts, and the National People's Congress approves. Proceeding from reality is illustrated by the drafting of the 15th Plan proposals, which involved six research teams visiting 12 provinces and 35 key research projects. The author also cites 165 major projects in the 13th Plan and 102 in the 14th as evidence of concentrating resources, including poverty alleviation and technological self-reliance. On democracy, Dong cites Xi's symposia and more than 3.113 million online suggestions, which the author calls an expression of whole-process people's democracy. On the legal basis, Dong describes a planning system that links national, spatial, sectoral and regional plans and a "long-term strategy–development plan–annual plan" loop, with national planning legislation under way.

Dong concludes that these five points enrich Xi's thinking on development strategy and planning. The author describes that thinking as a contribution to socialist political economy with Chinese characteristics and to development economics, and as a reference for other developing countries. The closing call is to strengthen confidence in the system and to make plans more forward-looking, guiding and innovative. Read the original if you want an authoritative Chinese account of how Five-Year Plans are presented as being drafted and legitimated, including the consultation figures and project counts the author cites.
quoteEn: The process of drawing up the Five-Year Plan is a process of broadly promoting democracy, pooling the wisdom of the whole Party and country, and listening to all voices.
quoteZh: 五年规划编制的过程，是广泛发扬民主、集中全党全国智慧、倾听各方声音的过程。

glossary.explanation: China's medium-term national development blueprints, issued since the 1950s. Called "plans" (jihua) until the 11th period and "programmes" or "plans" (guihua) since.

Xi Jinping's 2026 summary of experience in making Five-Year Plans: central leadership, proceeding from reality, a nationwide single chessboard, democracy and collective wisdom, and statutory planning.

glossary.literal: the whole country as one game of chess
glossary.explanation: A Party principle that regions and departments should coordinate under national priorities and subordinate local interests to the overall situation.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019. It holds that democracy covers every stage of policy-making, not only elections.
The official term for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses a large population, common prosperity and peaceful development.

t: Developing the new type of rural collective economy to advance common prosperity
zh: 以发展新型农村集体经济推动共同富裕
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2026, asks how the rural collective economy can be strengthened to deliver common prosperity for farmers. Zhang argues that developing a "new type" of rural collective economy is a key route to agricultural modernization and to raising rural productive forces and incomes, and that it matters for common prosperity.

The article first defines what is new in this form of collective economy, then lists the difficulties it currently faces, and finally sets out three capacities to be raised: the ability to lead others to prosperity, to create wealth and to become rich.

Zhang identifies three new features: clearly defined property rights, with collective operating assets converted into shares so that farmers become shareholders; diverse participants, including leading enterprises, cooperatives and family farms, which Zhang says makes decision-making more democratic; and varied business forms such as cooperation, share-holding, contracting, services and property leasing. The difficulties named are a shortage of talent amid rural hollowing-out and ageing, insufficient funding, and fragmented land and unclear property rights that weaken incentives. The proposed remedies are talent leadership through grassroots Party organizations and village Party secretaries, plus recruitment and retention of returning talent; wider financing through fiscal support, village-level vitality and rural financial and insurance products; and industrial development tailored to each village.

Zhang also calls for farmers' cooperative federations, local agricultural brands and paid agricultural services. They further call for giving collective economic organizations market legal-person status under the Law on Rural Collective Economic Organizations, mixed ownership with outside firms, and digital supervision of collective assets. Read the original if you want a concise policy-oriented outline of how Chinese scholars link rural collective ownership reform to the goal of common prosperity.
quoteEn: The new type of rural collective economy is a new economic form in which village collective members use new methods of operation to integrate collective resources and achieve common development through cooperation or association.
quoteZh: 新型农村集体经济是村集体成员利用新的经营方式整合集体资源，并通过合作或联合实现共同发展的一种新的经济形态。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal that the Party leadership has stressed in recent years, meaning prosperity shared by all rather than by a few. It is presented officially as an essential requirement of socialism.

glossary.en: new type of rural collective economy
glossary.explanation: A term for village-level collective ownership reorganised with clearer property rights, share-based distribution and market-oriented, cooperative forms of operation, in contrast to the traditional collective economy.
The Party's lowest-level units, such as village Party branches, which the article treats as the backbone of rural collective development.

t: Heroic narrative communication in the history of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army
zh: 东北抗联历史的英雄叙事传播
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 30 January 2026
paras: This short commentary asks how the history of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army (Dongbei Kanglian) can be communicated effectively in the age of intelligent media. Liu argues that heroic narrative is not simple retelling of facts but communication that strengthens collective memory, transmits core values and consolidates historical proof. The author links this to the state's growing emphasis on "red gene culture".

The article is organised in three parts: reconstructing communication scenes through micro-level "slices" of history, enriching communication carriers through narrative innovation, and conveying national belief through heroic spirit. Examples include a 2025 Jiangsu broadcaster series built around relics of Yang Jingyu and Zhao Yiman, the three-province live broadcast "Song of the Beacon Fires", films, television dramas, the CCTV documentary Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, and a 2025 exhibition of excavated relics in Beijing.

Drawing on communication theory, Liu treats memory as a social process built through media, narrative and ritual. Personal objects and individual stories are said to make grand history tangible and emotionally resonant, while commemorations, museum visits and live broadcasts work as ritual communication that turns audiences into participants. Liu adds that each change of medium, from novel to film to VR/AR reconstruction of sites, offers a new interpretation, and that audiences must be induced to actively "decode" the narrative. Such repeated telling is presented as a defence against the erosion of time and historical nihilism.

Liu concludes that the deepest value of this narrative lies in shaping values and spirit, answering "who we are" and "where we come from" and strengthening national identity. Continuous storytelling through social media and popular culture is likened to "spiritual drip irrigation" that consolidates the core value system. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official-leaning Chinese scholarship frames red-culture communication and war memory through media theory.
quoteEn: The heroic narrative of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army's history can quickly anchor historical coordinates, make every retelling of heroic deeds a confirmation of historical truth, and turn the public's conscious dissemination into a great wall of steel against the erosion of time and historical nihilism.
quoteZh: 东北抗联历史中的英雄叙事可快速锚定历史坐标，让英雄事迹的每一次传播变成对历史真相的确认，让社会大众间的自觉传播成为对抗时间侵蚀和历史虚无主义的钢铁长城。

glossary.explanation: Communist-led guerrilla forces that fought Japanese occupation in Northeast China from the early 1930s to the early 1940s. Yang Jingyu and Zhao Yiman are among its best-known figures in Chinese official memory.
A phrase in Chinese official discourse for the revolutionary heritage of the Communist Party, presented as something to be passed on across generations.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's revolutionary history and its accepted narrative.

t: Narrative problems and strategies in the international communication of China's War of Resistance stories
zh: 中国抗战故事国际传播的叙事难题与策略
paras: Meng Wei asks how China's stories of the War of Resistance against Japan can be made more credible and persuasive to audiences abroad. The commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 30 January 2026, holds that telling these stories well defends historical truth and promotes shared values of peace and justice. The author argues that despite real gains since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the narratives still suffer from problems that limit their reach and credibility, and that these can be addressed through six strategies.

The piece has two parts. The first diagnoses four weaknesses in current narratives. The second sets out six strategies for improving international communication. Meng draws on a 2025 Donghua University survey of ten "red" venues, the National Radio and Television Administration's 2013 campaign against "anti-Japanese thunder dramas", and its July 2025 notice on short dramas about the war.

On the diagnosis, Meng says that the narratives are "hard to explain, hard to spread and hard to believe". Wartime culture in China leans toward macro and collective storytelling and lacks the individual and third-party perspectives found in international memory of the Second World War. Translation and context gaps, "divine drama" excesses, and fragmented, entertainment-driven content such as memes and algorithm-boosted trivia further erode seriousness. The remedies start from historical materialism and call for a shift from didactic to dialogic address. Meng recommends linking grand narrative to personal experience through small objects such as a grain of rice or an IOU. The author also calls for reducing "cultural discount" by studying target audiences and avoiding divisive expressions, and for reaching young people. The other proposals are multimodal digital and immersive formats, with technology serving content rather than spectacle, and international education and scholarly cooperation.

Meng concludes that effective communication must correct distortion, context gaps and trivialisation while building a contemporary international influence for the culture of the War of Resistance. The author says that shifting foreign audiences' views is a process of layering and acculturation, not replacement. The stated aims are to counter historical revisionism and nihilism, oppose unilateralism and hegemonism, and win wider international respect and cooperation for China. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars frame the weaknesses and remedies of wartime-history communication abroad.
quoteEn: A mature and rational nation cannot treat its own history of blood and tears as material for frivolous dramatisation.
quoteZh: 一个成熟理性的民族，不能将自己的血泪史当作戏说对象。

glossary.explanation: The standard Chinese term for the 1937–1945 war against Japanese invasion, which official narratives present as the Eastern main theatre of the Second World War.
A popular label for television dramas about the war with absurd plots and superhuman heroes. The authorities criticised and curbed them from 2013.
A communication-studies concept for the loss of value when a cultural product is decoded by audiences from a different culture. The author uses it to explain obstacles to foreign understanding.

t: Promoting the deep integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation
zh: 推动科技创新和产业创新深度融合
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily, Zheng Qinghua takes up the call, made in the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), to promote the deep integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation. Zheng argues that, given a complex domestic and international environment, this integration needs systems thinking, a global outlook and a long-term view. It should be oriented to national strategic needs and rest on an innovation system in which diverse actors share goals and build jointly.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out why integration is necessary at this time. The second proposes an implementation path across five dimensions: overall planning, institutional reform, market allocation of factors, multi-party linkage and external cooperation. The third turns to the specific role of universities, which Zheng describes as an important actor in the integration.

On necessity, Zheng presents integration as a precondition for seizing the initiative in innovation, as the "only path" to developing new quality productive forces, and as the basis of new competitive advantages. Zheng holds that national strength depends less on R&D spending or patent counts than on how fast results are turned into industry and how closely the innovation chain and industrial chain are coupled. On the path, Zheng calls for national-level priorities in fields such as integrated circuits, artificial intelligence and new energy, and for new project-management models, evaluation beyond papers and patents, and technology finance. Zheng also calls for innovation consortia led by leading enterprises, pilot-scale testing bases and open cooperation, including with Belt and Road Initiative partners.

For universities, Zheng proposes restructuring disciplines around industrial bottlenecks, building platforms for cross-disciplinary research, pilot-scale conversion and joint talent training, and reforming evaluation, funding, property rights and staff mobility. Universities should also supply source innovation while enterprises handle engineering and marketisation. Zheng concludes that these measures would close the gap between laboratory results and industrial application. Read the original if you want a concrete example of how a university leader and academician translates current Party innovation policy into measures for industry, finance and higher education.
quoteEn: Scientific and technological innovation is the source of momentum for new quality productive forces, and industrial innovation is their practical carrier.
quoteZh: 科技创新是新质生产力的动力源泉，产业创新是新质生产力的实践载体。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than by resource and capital inputs.
China's international cooperation initiative, launched in 2013, centred on infrastructure and economic links with partner countries.

t: The multidimensional shaping of national identity in the early People's Republic
zh: 新中国成立初期国家认同的多维塑造
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Journal in January 2026, asks how the Communist Party built popular identification with the new state after 1949. Zeng and Tang argue that, through institutional and practical innovation, the Party restored the economy, consolidated the people's regime and won broad support and a high degree of national identity.

The article is organised around four dimensions, each given a role: political identity as the core, economic reconstruction as the foundation, social revolution as the safeguard and cultural reshaping as the support. Each section draws on policies and events from roughly 1949 to 1954.

On the political side, the authors point to the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, the Common Program, the 1954 Constitution and a four-tier administrative structure reaching down to the township, which they credit with creating a centralised and mobilising state apparatus. On the economic side, they describe the confiscation of bureaucrat capital, the stabilisation of prices and the First Five-Year Plan as the material basis of identification. Social revolution covers land reform, the 1950 Marriage Law and campaigns against prostitution, gambling and drugs. Cultural reshaping covers the guiding role of Mao Zedong's literary thought and the 1951–52 ideological remoulding of intellectuals, which the authors say established Marxism's guiding position.

The authors conclude that these measures together secured the people's wholehearted support for the new China. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars frame state-building and identity in the early 1950s.
quoteEn: Political identity was the core task in shaping the new China.
quoteZh: 政治认同是塑造新中国的核心任务

glossary.zh: 中国人民政治协商会议共同纲领
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó Rénmín Zhèngzhì Xiéshāng Huìyì Gòngtóng Gāngling
glossary.explanation: Provisional constitutional document adopted by the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference in September 1949. It served as the basic law until the 1954 Constitution.
The redistribution of land from landlords to peasants carried out in newly liberated areas from 1950 to 1952, accompanied by class classification.
A campaign in 1951–52 requiring intellectuals and educators to study Marxism and criticise their previous outlook.

t: Giving greater strategic prominence to developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions
zh: 把因地制宜发展新质生产力摆在更加突出的战略位置
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 January 2026
paras: This commentary in China Social Sciences Today takes up Xi Jinping's statement that, during the 15th Five-Year Plan period, developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions must be given a more prominent strategic position. Chen argues that this means the most comprehensive strategic layout, the deepest reform resolve and higher-priority resource input. The article reads the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) as building a strategic system for winning the initiative in future competition.

The piece is organised around three emphases of the Plenum's deployment: the modern industrial system as the core strategic priority, high-level scientific and technological self-reliance as the core engine, and institutional and mechanism innovation as the endogenous source of momentum.

On industry, Chen notes that the 15th Five-Year Plan expands the earlier goals into a "five strengths" framework that adds aerospace and transport, and stresses advanced manufacturing as the backbone and forward planning for future industries such as quantum technology and 6G. On technology, the author says its role shifts from supporting development to leading the development of new quality productive forces, with original innovation placed at the source and digital China providing a platform. On institutions, Chen calls for replacing a uniform framework with "precise adaptation", citing Guangxi's AI path linking research hubs, Guangxi integration and ASEAN application, and for coordinating education, science and talent systems and building science-and-technology finance.

Chen concludes that these measures together reshape the dynamics of Chinese modernization and display institutional advantages. Institutional barriers such as data silos, research evaluation and market access are named as the key constraints to remove. Read the original if you want a short, Party-line reading of how the Fourth Plenum's guidance links industrial policy, technology and regional adaptation to new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are essentially a form of productive forces in which scientific and technological innovation plays the leading role.
quoteZh: 新质生产力本质上是科技创新在其中起主导作用的生产力形态

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than by traditional resource- and input-heavy growth.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, whose recommendations were adopted at the Fourth Plenum in 2025.
The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
A principle of tailoring policy to the resources, industrial base and circumstances of each region.

t: Practical paths to promoting common prosperity in the digital age
zh: 数字时代推动共同富裕的实践路径
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily on 5 February 2026, asks how digital dividends can be turned into tangible well-being for ordinary people. Yang Jing starts from the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, which call for solid steps towards common prosperity for all. The author argues that this requires practical paths suited to the digital and intelligent era.

The piece is organised under four headings: planning from the overall picture, balancing key relationships, concentrating on breakthroughs in people's livelihood, and getting policies implemented. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements on common prosperity and the 15th Five-Year Plan.

Yang's core argument treats common prosperity as an overall concept to be pursued systematically, covering both material and cultural life. The author names three relationships to handle: government and market, efficiency and fairness, and production and distribution. For these Yang proposes guarding against platform monopoly, algorithmic discrimination and the digital divide, and improving wage mechanisms and the three-tier distribution system. On livelihood, Yang calls for stronger employment services, protection of workers in new forms of employment, and wider social security coverage through digital tools.

Yang concludes that policies should be integrated across the whole life cycle, from childcare to elderly care. Digital tools should equalise basic public services, break down data barriers between departments, and support whole-process digital management of policy. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link digital technology to the common prosperity agenda in the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: How to better turn digital dividends into real feelings of happiness and gain for the people is a practical question that must be answered in promoting common prosperity in the digital age.
quoteZh: 如何把数字红利更好转化为人民群众实实在在的幸福感和获得感，是数字时代推动共同富裕必须回答的现实课题。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal that Xi Jinping has made central to Party policy. It stresses shared affluence, a narrower wealth gap and a larger middle-income group.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030. Its recommendations were adopted by the Party leadership in 2025.

t: Comprehensive green transition in the context of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化语境中的全面绿色转型
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 January 2026
paras: Cai Huajie, writing in a newspaper commentary, asks how China's comprehensive green transition of economic and social development should be understood. The author argues that it must be read within the context of Chinese modernization, drawing on volume one of the Selected Works of Xi Jinping on Ecological Civilization, and not through international green-transition discourses.

Cai identifies three such discourses: green capitalism, ecocentrism and eco-socialism. The author rejects all three as guides for China, describing them as Western-centric "de-ideologised" ecological imperialism or as impractical extremes of "de-modernisation" and "de-capitalisation". The article then reads the transition through three keywords in Xi Jinping's definition of Chinese modernization as socialist modernization led by the Communist Party: Party, socialism and modernization.

First, Cai contends that the transition combines Party-led top-level design with orderly mass participation, in contrast to the "bottom-up" approaches of international narratives. Second, it is a reform, within the socialist system, of institutions unsuited to green development; Cai argues it is not a turn to capitalism and cites the principle of public ownership of natural resources. Third, it makes high-quality development and high-level protection mutually reinforcing, following the idea that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets. Cai says this treats capital as a productive factor to be steered towards green and low-carbon fields through market mechanisms.

Cai concludes that China's transition is a distinctive path of harmony between humanity and nature, with Chinese characteristics and a contribution to the world. Read the original if you want a short statement of how Chinese scholars position the green transition against Western green capitalism, ecocentrism and eco-socialism.
quoteEn: China's comprehensive green transition of economic and social development is not a turn onto the evil path of capitalism, but a promotion of the socialist system's self-improvement and development in the green dimension.
quoteZh: 我国经济社会发展全面绿色转型，不是转型至资本主义的邪路，而是促进社会主义制度在绿色维度上的自我完善和发展。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization, defined by the Party as socialist modernization under Communist Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official slogan, prominent since 2017, for growth that stresses efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed alone.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A phrase attributed to Xi Jinping (2005) holding that environmental protection and economic prosperity reinforce each other. It is central to official ecological-civilization discourse.
An official goal, written into Party documents since the 2000s and the constitution in 2018, of building a society in harmony with nature.

t: The 15th Five-Year Plan contributes Chinese wisdom to global development
zh: “十五五”规划为全球发展贡献中国智慧
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 27 January 2026, argues that the proposals for China's 15th Five-Year Plan, adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), offer "Chinese wisdom" to the international community facing global development challenges. He Qin presents the document as both a blueprint for national development and a contribution to shared development worldwide.

The article is organised under four headings: seizing the initiative through high-quality development, empowering common development through high-level opening up, safeguarding development through a safer China, and leading innovation-driven development through Chinese modernization.

In He's account, the Plan responds to a complex environment by concentrating on China's own affairs, building a new development pattern, advancing technological self-reliance and expanding institutional opening up. The author describes the Belt and Road Initiative as a platform for a community with a shared future for mankind, and presents China's security-building and "peaceful development" as contributions to world stability. On innovation, He cites 61 mentions of "innovation" in the proposals and China's rise in the Global Innovation Index from 34th in 2012 to 10th in 2025, and names Party leadership, working through the five-year planning mechanism, as the greatest advantage.

He concludes that China's own peaceful development and innovation experience offers other countries important lessons and a new option for pursuing modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary frames the 15th Five-Year Plan for an international audience.
quoteEn: Leadership by the Communist Party of China is the most distinctive feature and most outstanding advantage of Chinese modernization, and the primary principle that must be upheld in advancing it.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的领导是中国式现代化最鲜明的特征和最突出的优势，是推进中国式现代化必须坚持的首要原则。
