glossary.explanation: China's national development plan for 2026–2030. The Party's Central Committee first issues proposals, which are then turned into a detailed outline by the state.
An official development goal that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth alone.
The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation of a vision of international relations based on shared interests and cooperation.

t: Achieving an effective qualitative improvement and a reasonable quantitative growth
zh: 实现质的有效提升和量的合理增长
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 23 January 2026
paras: This newspaper commentary interprets Xi Jinping's guidance that the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030) should keep high-quality development as its theme and achieve "an effective qualitative improvement and a reasonable quantitative growth". Zhao argues that this formula marks a historic shift in Chinese modernization from extensive growth, focused on scale and speed, to intensive improvement, focused on quality and returns. Zhao presents it as a creative application of Marxist development philosophy.

The article is organised around four headings, each introduced by a statement of Xi's and followed by three or two numbered points. They cover the enrichment of the content of modernization, multi-dimensional and multi-level development, the period as a stage in a step-by-step historical process, and the stress on common prosperity for all the people. A short closing section sums up the period's significance in four "logics" and names its guarantees.

Zhao's central move is to treat quality as a system rather than a single economic indicator. The 15th Five-Year Plan goals are read as efficiency, innovation, cultural, distributional, ecological and security qualities, and the Party's overall leadership, people-first values, reform, and the combination of an effective market with an active government are named as foundations. The article also describes modernization as an incremental process in which the economy shifts from factor-driven to innovation-driven growth and governance from control to modernized governance, while institutions mature. Throughout, Zhao contrasts Chinese modernization with a Western model that the article characterises as capital-centred, materialist, expansionist and consumerist, and presents common prosperity, people-centred development and balanced material and cultural progress as its alternative.

Zhao concludes that the period is a shift from quantitative to qualitative change, with Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee, deepening reform as the driving force, putting the people first as the value goal, and coordinating development and security as the method. The article calls on Party members to grasp the Two Establishes, uphold the Two Upholds, and keep historical patience and strategic resolve. It holds that reaching basic modernization by 2035 requires better quality, not just faster growth. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 15th Five-Year Plan's quality-first formula is being explained in Party-affiliated academic commentary.
quoteEn: This \"step-by-step\" process logic requires that we neither rush for quick results nor wait passively, but grasp the pace and advance steadily.
quoteZh: 这种“阶梯式递进”的过程逻辑要求我们既不能急于求成，也不能消极等待，而要把握节奏、稳扎稳打。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, set out since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models, emphasising large population, common prosperity and peaceful development.
The official economic theme since about 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed and scale of growth.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
A formula adopted in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party and the Central Committee's authority and unified leadership.
China's national plan for economic and social development for 2026–2030, whose recommendations the Party adopted in 2025.

t: Advancing the building of a unified national market in depth
zh: 纵深推进全国统一大市场建设
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today on 22 January 2026, asks how China can remove the obstacles to a unified national market, a task set out in the Party Central Committee's recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan. Huang and Lin argue that the market should be built by combining an efficient market with an effective government, by identifying precisely the "choke points and blockages" and removing them resolutely. In their account, doing so strengthens China's capacity to withstand risks and gives momentum to high-quality development.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why the effort matters, the second identifies the main obstacles, and the third offers five groups of policy proposals. The authors treat the market as part of a chain that runs from reform to market to institutions, and they connect it to the new development philosophy's goals and to the new development pattern of domestic and international circulation.

On significance, the authors argue that a unified market is the spatial and institutional basis for reforming factor markets and building a high-standard market system. They also describe it as a systematic reshaping of production relations that no longer fit advanced productive forces, which they see as a precondition for cultivating new quality productive forces. They identify four obstacles: institutional barriers such as uneven property-rights enforcement, hidden entry thresholds and regional differences in credit systems; weak "soft connectivity" (standards, trading platforms, data rules) compared with physical infrastructure; poorly coordinated regulation and uneven enforcement; and local protectionism, which they say persists in disguised forms and is aggravated by weak local finances and flawed performance evaluation.

Their proposals are: strengthen Party leadership and central–local coordination, revise the Anti-Monopoly Law and draft a national unified market regulation with penalties for local barriers; unify basic market rules on property rights, market access, fair competition and social credit; improve interconnection through logistics hubs, trading platforms and data sharing; unify regulation and enforcement; and expand opening up, both internal and external, so that domestic experience feeds into international rules. Read the original if you want a concise policy-oriented statement of the official diagnosis of market fragmentation and the remedies proposed under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Building a unified national market is, in essence, a systematic reshaping of those production relations that do not suit the requirements of developing advanced productive forces.
quoteZh: 建设全国统一大市场，本质上是对这些不适应先进生产力发展要求的生产关系进行系统性重塑。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal of removing regional barriers and local protectionism so that goods, capital and labour move freely across China under common rules. It was given prominence in a 2022 Party–State guideline.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading.
The official economic development goal since 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation rather than speed of growth alone.
Xi Jinping's framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, introduced in 2015.

glossary.en: an efficient market with an effective government
glossary.literal: effective market and government that accomplishes something
glossary.explanation: An official formula describing the proper relationship between the market and the state in China's socialist market economy.

t: Understanding China's economy through five "news": a dialogue with Liu Wei, former president of Renmin University of China
st: Economic Daily interview on the 2025 results, "strong supply, weak demand" and the new development model
zh: 在五个“新”中读懂中国经济——对话中国人民大学原校长刘伟
paras: This is an interview published in Economic Daily on 4 February 2026 in its "Dialogue with Economists" series. The reporter (named at the end as Ouyang You) speaks with Liu Wei, former president of Renmin University of China, about the outlook for China's economy in 2026. Liu organises his answers under five headings: new situation, new contradiction, new policy orientation, new understanding of laws, and new development model. His overall view is that 2025 was stable and improving, that weak demand is the central problem, and that policy should shift towards a domestic-demand-led, consumption-driven, endogenous-growth model.

The interview opens with the 2025 results and the main pressures, then turns to the Central Economic Work Conference's judgement of "strong supply, weak demand" and its causes. It moves on to the stress on policy coordination, including existing and incremental policies and counter-cyclical and cross-cycle adjustment. It goes on to the "five musts" in the 2025 conference's summary of the laws of economic work, and closes with the development model written into the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan and the priorities of that period.

Liu summarises 2025 as "generally stable, progressing while stable, and trending better". He cites 5 per cent GDP growth, unemployment within the 5.5 per cent target, flat consumer prices that signal weak demand, and growth in high-tech manufacturing. He argues that "strong supply, weak demand" is relative and structural, not absolute overcapacity. In his account the main contradiction has shifted between demand and supply across periods since reform and opening up. He traces the present imbalance to market segmentation and local protection, insufficient innovation and a changed external environment. He reads the "five musts" as applications of Chinese-characteristic political economy, including the supply–demand contradiction, the government–market relationship and the relation between productive forces and relations of production. He presents "macroeconomic governance" as going beyond Western demand management by adding industrial and regional policy and treating reform as a driver of growth.

Liu concludes that the earlier model relied on external demand, investment and expanded factor inputs. Because the question has changed from "whether there is enough" to "whether it is good", he says a model of domestic-demand leadership, consumption pull and endogenous growth is needed. He treats these as mutually reinforcing, with endogenous growth as the deepest source of momentum. For the 15th Five-Year Plan period he stresses expanding domestic demand, building a modern industrial system, fostering new quality productive forces and self-reliance in science and technology. Read the original if you want a semi-official economist's account of how China's 2025 data and the shift towards domestic-demand-led growth are being interpreted.
quoteEn: "Strong supply, weak demand" is a relative, structural concept; it does not mean absolute oversupply, and this needs to be understood fully.
quoteZh: “供强需弱”是一个相对的、结构性的概念，不是指供给绝对过剩，对此要有全面认识。

glossary.explanation: The Central Economic Work Conference's description of the main contradiction in current macroeconomic operation: a strong production capacity set against insufficient effective demand.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 that refers to productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and emerging and future industries.
The annual meeting of Party and state leaders, usually in December, that reviews the year's economy and sets economic policy for the next year.
An official term that places macroeconomic regulation within the broader system of national governance, using fiscal, monetary, industrial, regional and structural tools together.

t: Upholding a people-centred approach to advance the modernization of social governance
zh: 坚持以人民为中心 推进社会治理现代化
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2026, asks how social governance can be improved and modernized in line with the Party's proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan. Gao and Wang argue that governance must be people-centred and rest on systematic, law-based, comprehensive and source-oriented governance, within a system of co-building, co-governance and sharing.

The piece sets out five principles, each tied to a practical requirement: Party leadership, the co-building, co-governance and sharing framework, a people-centred value orientation, a shift of focus to the grassroots, and a combination of autonomy, rule of law and moral governance.

The authors' central move is conceptual. They distinguish "good government" (shanzheng), which they describe as efficiency-oriented administration by managers over the managed, from "good governance" (shanzhi), which aims to maximise public interest and draws in market actors, social organisations and residents. In their account, co-building, co-governance and sharing embodies this shift. They also argue that the principal contradiction in society, as formulated by the Party, raises demands for timely, transparent and standardised governance, which requires institutions that gather, organise and answer public concerns.

Gao and Wang call for stronger Party organisation, including in new economic and social organisations and among new forms of employment. They also urge more resources for grassroots communities, the "Fengqiao experience" to resolve disputes early, and integrated data platforms using artificial intelligence while guarding against its risks. They propose reinforcing residents' self-governance, law-based governance and moral norms such as village rules and family traditions. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official framework for grassroots social governance in China's 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: It is not enough for social governance merely to maximise the total of efficiency-oriented rationality; it must also respond fully to the reasonable demands of plural actors such as the market, society and residents.
quoteZh: 社会治理仅仅追求效率理性的总量最大化是不够的，还必须充分回应市场、社会和居民等多元主体的合理诉求。

glossary.literal: jointly build, jointly govern, jointly share
glossary.explanation: An official formula for social governance in which the Party, government, enterprises, social organisations and residents all take part and share the results. It has been promoted in Party documents since the 2010s.
A model of grassroots dispute resolution from Fengqiao, Zhejiang, dating to the 1960s. It stresses resolving conflicts locally and early, and has been revived in the Xi Jinping era.

glossary.en: combination of autonomy, rule of law and moral governance
glossary.literal: combining self-governance, rule by law and rule by virtue
glossary.explanation: An official model of grassroots governance combining residents' self-government, law-based governance and moral persuasion, under Party leadership.

t: Institutional opening-up seen from the dimension of governance modernization
zh: 从治理现代化维度看制度型开放
paras: Liu Jiangning takes up the call in the Party's recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), to "steadily expand institutional opening-up". The commentary, published in Guangming Daily, argues that institutional opening-up is no longer just a policy for economic growth. In Liu's reading it is a strategic lever for restructuring the governance system, raising governance effectiveness and advancing Chinese modernization.

The piece has two parts. The first sets out the internal logic linking institutional opening-up to the modernization of national governance, and examines this along six dimensions: values, concepts, system, capacity, performance and outcomes. The second names remaining problems and proposes four lines of action. Liu draws on figures such as the number of free trade zone innovations and the shrinking foreign-investment negative list.

Liu's central claim is that the two processes are mutually reinforcing. Aligning with high-standard international rules pushes domestic institutional reform and removes bottlenecks, while modernized governance gives opening-up a firm base. Liu says opening-up shifts governance from "growth first" to equal weight for development and fairness, and from administrative commands to rule-based governance. As evidence the author cites 22 pilot free trade zones with nearly 200 institutional innovations, and a negative list cut from 151 items (2018) to 106 (2025). Liu also cites actual foreign investment of 476.9 billion yuan... as reported for 2025, specifically 747.69 billion yuan, and goods trade that has ranked first globally for eight years to 2024. Liu says these show that institutional strengths are converted into development momentum and public wellbeing.

Liu concedes gaps in rule alignment, institutional coordination and governance capacity. The author proposes four measures: actively aligning with high-standard trade rules such as those of the CPTPP and digital economy agreements; integrating institutions across departments and spreading free trade zone experience nationwide; strengthening governance capacity through trained personnel, risk monitoring and better public services; and holding a security bottom line on industrial, financial and data security. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-aligned scholarship links opening-up policy to the theme of governance modernization ahead of the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Institutional opening-up gives the modernization of national governance an external driving force and a practical path: by aligning with high international standards it forces domestic institutional reform and innovation and resolves blockages and difficulties in the governance system.
quoteZh: 制度型开放为国家治理现代化提供了外部动力与实践路径，通过对接国际高标准规则倒逼国内制度改革创新，破解治理体系中的堵点难点

glossary.explanation: A policy of opening up through alignment of rules, regulations, management and standards with international ones, rather than only through trade and investment flows. It has been stressed in Party documents since the late 2010s.
The goal, set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), of modernizing China's system and capacity for governance.
The Party's official framework for China's path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Designated areas where China pilots reforms in trade, investment and regulation, with successful measures later spread nationwide.
A list of sectors closed or restricted to foreign investment; everything not listed is in principle open.

t: Anchoring on the goals of a strong science and technology nation and a strong financial nation to develop science and technology finance
zh: 锚定科技强国与金融强国目标发展科技金融
paras: Chen Yulu, president of Nankai University, argues in this commentary (published in the People's Daily on 3 February 2026) that science and technology finance should be developed deliberately for the goals of building a strong science and technology nation and a strong financial nation. Starting from Xi Jinping's call to steer capital towards early-stage, small, long-term and hard-technology investment, Chen holds that such finance is a strategic institutional arrangement. It is not simply a branch of finance.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the meaning and strategic character of science and technology finance. The second assesses opportunities and challenges in the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030), citing policy documents from the previous plan period and the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). The third sets out strategic priorities and specific measures.

Chen argues that science and technology finance works along functional, spatial and temporal dimensions: it supplies funds, values assets and manages risk, it helps innovation factors move across regions, and it absorbs the risks of long, uncertain R&D cycles through risk-sharing and patient capital. On the challenges, Chen points to market failure, since knowledge spillovers leave innovators with less than the social return and intangible assets are hard to value as collateral. In China's case, Chen adds, the existing financial system suits large-scale standardised industrial production better than light-asset, high-uncertainty innovation, and legal frameworks, specialist staff and institutions are still incomplete. Chen's remedy is to combine an effective market with a capable government, balancing efficiency, fairness and security, and to use the new-type whole-nation system to fill gaps in major original innovation.

Chen proposes a financial service system suited to innovation, with banks, insurers, securities firms and funds sharing information. State-owned commercial banks would be encouraged to lead. Fiscal interest subsidies, policy guarantees and ultra-long special treasury bonds would be used to counter market failure, alongside tolerance of investment losses and due-diligence exemptions for fund managers. Chen also urges capital-market reform, including registration-based listing, more long-term institutional investors and priority listings for firms with key technology breakthroughs. Digital infrastructure, an innovation points system, interdisciplinary talent training and basic theoretical research are also called for. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of the policy logic and the measures behind China's science and technology finance agenda for 2026–2030.
quoteEn: Developing science and technology finance is a systematic undertaking, guided by top-level design, that involves cross-departmental coordination and broad participation by business entities, and it can clear the bottlenecks in R&D, the commercialisation of results and industrial upgrading.
quoteZh: 发展科技金融是一项在顶层设计指引下，跨部门协同与经营主体广泛参与的系统工程，能够打通科技研发、成果转化、产业升级的堵点

glossary.explanation: A policy concept for mobilising state and market resources across the country towards major science and technology goals. It updates the earlier 'whole-nation system' of centrally organised effort.
Financial services and institutional arrangements designed to fund technological innovation across its life cycle. It is the first of the 'five major articles' of finance named in Party policy.
Long-term investment funds willing to accept slow returns and high risk. It is promoted as suitable for original innovation.

t: The value orientation of building a cultural form of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化文化形态构建的价值旨归
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 2 February 2026, Bai Xianliang asks what value orientation should guide the cultural form of Chinese modernization, which he describes as a new culture produced by the Second Integration. Bai argues that this cultural form must answer the basic questions of whom it represents, for whom it exists and on whom it relies, and that the answer is its character as a culture of the people (renminxing).

The commentary has three parts. The first traces the people-centred character of this culture to three sources. The second sets out four ways in which a people-oriented culture serves the people. The third describes how cultural construction should rely on the people and look beyond China.

On the sources, Bai names the essential attribute of Marxism, the Chinese Communist Party's stance of putting the people first, and the orientation of advanced socialist culture, which is said to be created and enjoyed by the people. On service to the people, Bai lists meeting their spiritual and cultural needs, enriching their spiritual world, strengthening their spiritual strength, and promoting all-round human development. Bai holds that the essence of modernization is the modernization of people, and calls for investment in people alongside investment in things.

On reliance, Bai calls for drawing on popular creativity, deepening reform of cultural institutions, using digital means, and treating people as both the starting point and the end point of cultural work, judged by the cultural gains and well-being people experience. Bai also calls for upholding cultural subjectivity, creatively transforming traditional Chinese culture and drawing on the best of other civilizations, in order to build a new form of human civilization. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official rationale linking culture, people-centred governance and human development in Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The essence of modernization is the modernization of people.
quoteZh: 现代化的本质是人的现代化。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state concept of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
Xi Jinping's formula, stated in 2023, for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's fine traditional culture. It complements the first integration of Marxism with China's concrete realities.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official term for the civilizational outcome claimed for Chinese modernization, said to go beyond the Western model of modernization.
A term in recent Party discourse for China's cultural self-awareness and independence, grounded in Chinese civilization while remaining open to others.

t: The core cultural characteristics of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的核心文化特质
paras: In this commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 2 February 2026, Zhen Xiaoying asks what cultural characteristics define Chinese modernization and set it apart from Western modernization. Zhen argues that it is rooted in fine traditional Chinese culture, combined with revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture, and that this gives it a cultural structure which overcomes the inherent flaws of the Western path.

The piece names four traits: a people-centred value stance, an inclusive outlook of harmony in diversity, a development philosophy of upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, and the ultimate aim of the free and all-round development of the human being. Each is presented with a quotation from Xi Jinping and contrasted with Western modernization.

Zhen contends that Western modernization starts from capital and its accumulation, which in the author's account produces wealth polarization, claims of civilizational superiority, colonial expansion and the loss of value rationality to instrumental rationality. Chinese modernization, by contrast, is said to place the people first through poverty alleviation, rural revitalization and public cultural services. It is also said to treat civilizations as different but not unequal, through the Belt and Road Initiative and shared global governance, and to advance material and cultural-ethical progress together through core socialist values and public services.

Zhen concludes that these traits give Chinese modernization lasting spiritual momentum and make it a modernization of peaceful development, coordinated and sustainable, balancing efficiency and fairness. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary presents the cultural contrast between Chinese and Western modernization.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles is the foundation: it means holding to the core spirit of fine traditional Chinese culture, to the guiding position of Marxism, and to the socialist direction of development.
quoteZh: 守正是根基，即坚守中华优秀传统文化的核心精神，坚守马克思主义的指导地位，坚守社会主义的发展方向。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of development, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A guiding principle of Xi Jinping-era Party discourse, holding that development should serve the people and rely on them.

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.literal: keeping to the correct and innovating
glossary.explanation: A slogan in Party discourse that combines fidelity to core principles (Marxism, tradition, socialist direction) with innovation.
A classical Chinese idea, now used in official discourse to express respect for the diversity of civilizations.
China's global infrastructure and economic cooperation programme, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: Nurturing the foundations of the cultural form of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化文化形态的根基涵养
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily, Zou Guangwen asks how the cultural form of Chinese modernization is rooted in, and nourished by, excellent traditional Chinese culture. Taking Xi Jinping's statement that the Two Integrations make Marxism Chinese and traditional culture modern as his starting point, Zou argues that traditional culture is the deepest foundational resource of this cultural form. Deepening that nourishment is presented as a way to build cultural confidence, to address alienated cultural identity and the rupture between tradition and modernity, and to build a new form of human civilization.

The article is a newspaper commentary organised around three tasks. It first discusses how traditional culture shapes the national temperament of the cultural form of Chinese modernization. It then turns to cultivating cultural subjectivity in the practice of modernization, and finally to opening up a new horizon for cultural development. Zou cites ideas such as "the people are the foundation of the state" and "as heaven's movement is vigorous, the gentleman strives constantly" as examples of values that match the aims of Chinese modernization.

On national temperament, Zou describes three steps: the continuity of cultural genes and the sedimentation of a shared cultural-psychological structure; their creative transformation under the Two Integrations, with Marxism supplying the interpretive framework; and the defence of the cultural system against cultural alienation and wholesale Westernization. Examples include self-strengthening becoming the striving spirit of socialist modernization. On cultural subjectivity, Zou holds that the spiritual traits of the nation anchor cultural origins, orient development and unite identity, for instance by turning "the people as foundation" into a people-centred approach. On the new horizon, Zou sets out a progression from cultural subjectivity as precondition, through "creative transformation and innovative development" (including digital and media forms) as method, to a new form of human civilization as the guiding value. Zou describes this last aim as one that would counter Western discursive hegemony.

Zou concludes that the cultural form of Chinese modernization rests on excellent traditional culture and develops according to the Two Integrations. Tradition builds the base of cultural subjectivity by shaping national temperament, and it opens a new horizon through deep integration with modern culture. Zou says this should contribute to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to human civilizational progress. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Tsinghua scholar presents the role of traditional culture in the official theory of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The essence of cultural integration is the reshaping of the spiritual core on the basis of upholding subjectivity, and the key lies in avoiding the pitfalls of "wholesale Westernization" and "cultural restorationism".
quoteZh: 文化融合的本质是坚守主体性基础上的精神内核重塑，关键在于规避“全盘西化”与“文化复古”误区。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second integration was stressed from 2023.
A concept in recent official discourse meaning a nation's capacity to hold its own cultural standpoint and direct its own cultural development.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A method promoted by Xi Jinping for treating traditional culture: reworking its content and forms to fit contemporary needs.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official phrase for the civilizational model that Chinese modernization is said to represent, offered as an alternative to Western-style modernity.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and standing by the mid-21st century.

t: Developing the new rural collective economy: practical needs, pathways and institutional safeguards
zh: 发展新型农村集体经济的现实需求、推进路径与机制保障
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 2 February 2026, takes up the strategic task set by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) of accelerating agricultural and rural modernization during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. The authors, researchers at the Sichuan Academy of Social Sciences, argue that developing a "new-type" rural collective economy is a necessary strategic choice. They hold that it requires clear understanding of its purpose, diversified development paths and a supporting set of institutional mechanisms.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the new rural collective economy matters; the second proposes four development paths; the third outlines four mechanisms to underpin them. It begins from the claim that, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), reform of the collective property rights system has largely completed its phased tasks, but that the new collective economy still faces scattered resources, weak cooperation and narrow development routes.

On necessity, the authors link the collective economy to Chinese modernization. In their account it supports food security, activates rural endogenous momentum by reviving idle homesteads and farmhouses, smooths urban–rural flows of factors of production, and strengthens the Party's governing base in the countryside by raising the cohesion of village organisations. The four paths are: integrating and revitalising land and other resources through leasing, shareholding and cooperation; partnering with diverse market actors in processing, storage, tourism and similar fields; expanding services (production, management and public-interest services); and moving from single-village to whole-village, multi-village and cross-regional models, including enclaves and joint shareholding. The four mechanisms concern business operations suited to the market under the special legal person status, governance matched to the property structure (a "Party organisation + village collective + community" structure and reputation constraints), a closed-loop risk-prevention system, and a composite income-distribution system based on membership rights and factor contributions, with reserve and public welfare funds.

The authors conclude that the old organisational forms of the collective economy no longer fit market-oriented development, so systematic institutional reform is needed to preserve and increase collective assets and strengthen the capacity to deliver common prosperity. They present the collective economy as both an economic undertaking and a means of strengthening grassroots Party organisations and rural governance. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of how Chinese scholars frame the policy rationale, models and governance mechanisms of the new rural collective economy.
quoteEn: The development of the new rural collective economy is not only an economic act that promotes rural economic development, but also an important way of strengthening the political and organisational functions of grassroots Party organisations in the countryside and improving rural governance.
quoteZh: 新型农村集体经济的发展不仅是推动乡村经济发展的经济行为，更是强化农村基层党组织政治功能和组织功能以及完善乡村治理的重要途径。

glossary.explanation: A policy term for village-level collective economic organisations that own collective resources and assets and operate in the market, as distinct from the older, administratively run collective economy. It follows the reform of collective property rights.
The official name for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Communist Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
A category in China's Civil Code that includes rural collective economic organisations, giving them legal standing to hold assets and conduct business.
An official goal of shared wealth for all, stressed by the Party under Xi Jinping, including narrowing urban–rural and regional gaps.

t: Using the modernization of primary-level governance to build a higher-level Peaceful China
zh: 以基层治理现代化助力更高水平平安中国建设
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 2 February 2026, asks how primary-level (grassroots) governance can support a higher-level Peaceful China. Sun argues that such governance is the cornerstone of national governance, so its modernization directly shapes the modernization of national governance as a whole.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's statements on grassroots governance and the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). It links these to the opening year of the 15th Five-Year Plan period and to the goals of preventing and defusing risks. Four requirements then structure the text: Party leadership, joint governance, legal safeguards and technological empowerment.

On Party leadership, Sun calls for grassroots Party organizations to lead governance, and for deeper grid-based Party building. The grid is to serve as the basic unit for risk screening and real-time supervision. Sun stresses that this is not the Party organization taking everything on itself. The author instead points to a governance system combining Party leadership, government responsibility, democratic consultation, social coordination, public participation, legal safeguards and technological support. Sun also calls for developing the new-era "Fengqiao experience" and for forming a social governance community in which everyone has responsibility. On law, Sun urges better grassroots policies and regulations, public legal services and legal education. On technology, Sun proposes integrated online–offline platforms, data sharing and intelligent risk-prediction and early-warning models.

Sun concludes that these four measures together turn the Party's political and organizational strengths into grassroots governance effectiveness. The author presents this as a way for governance to become more predictive, precise and efficient. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary connects grassroots governance, the 15th Five-Year Plan and the Peaceful China agenda.
quoteEn: Grassroots governance under Party leadership does not mean the Party organization taking everything on itself; it means steadily improving a social governance system of Party committee leadership, government responsibility, democratic consultation, social coordination, public participation, legal safeguards and technological support.
quoteZh: 党建引领下的基层治理，不是党组织的大包大揽，而是要不断健全党委领导、政府负责、民主协商、社会协同、公众参与、法治保障、科技支撑的社会治理体系。

glossary.explanation: An official initiative aiming at social stability and public security, covering crime prevention, dispute resolution and risk control.
A grassroots model from Fengqiao, Zhejiang, dating to the 1960s. It stresses resolving disputes locally through mobilizing the masses; it has been recast in the "new era" as a governance model.
A practice that divides communities into small grids, each with assigned Party members and officials. It is used for service delivery, monitoring and risk screening.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, the fifteenth in the series of five-year plans.

t: Grasping the drivers of China's economic growth during the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: 准确把握“十五五”时期我国经济增长的动力特征
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 30 January 2026, Huang Kainan comments on one of the main goals set by the Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025): keeping growth in a reasonable range, steadily raising total factor productivity, markedly increasing the household consumption rate and strengthening domestic demand as the main driver of growth. Huang argues that in the 2026–2030 period growth must rely more on total factor productivity on the supply side and on domestic demand on the demand side, with the two interacting well.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first deals with raising the contribution of total factor productivity. The second deals with strengthening domestic demand, through boosting consumption and expanding effective investment. The third explains how supply and demand can reinforce each other. Huang draws throughout on the Recommendations and on statements by Xi Jinping on supply and demand.

On the supply side, Huang distinguishes growth driven by factor inputs from growth driven by innovation, and says the latter must matter more. Total factor productivity is to be raised through breakthrough technologies, innovative allocation of production factors (intellectual property, talent, data, finance) and deep industrial upgrading, all under the heading of new quality productive forces. On the demand side, Huang proposes raising household incomes, lifting the share of income spent on consumption through social security and better supply, and protecting consumers. Investment should keep growing at a reasonable pace while improving returns and efficiency, partly by curbing involution-style competition and building a unified national market. Huang then argues the two sides depend on each other. A lower savings rate and a shrinking labour force mean investment efficiency, and so productivity, must rise to sustain consumption. Conversely, a large domestic market allows the gains from higher productivity to be realised.

Huang concludes that the 15th Five-Year Plan period is a critical stage for laying the foundation for basically achieving socialist modernization. Supply and demand should be advanced together, and Huang calls for deeper construction of the unified national market to remove blockages in production, exchange, distribution and consumption. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned economist's reading of the growth model behind the 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations.
quoteEn: Only by raising total factor productivity can investment efficiency be improved and support be provided for the sustainable growth of consumption.
quoteZh: 只有提升全要素生产率才能够提高投资效率，才能为消费的可持续增长提供支撑。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading, in place of reliance on traditional factor inputs.
An economic measure of the output growth not explained by increases in capital and labour inputs, usually linked to technology and efficiency.
Destructive, low-return competition such as price wars, which official policy since 2024–25 has said should be curbed.
A policy goal of removing local protectionism and barriers so that goods, capital and labour move freely across China.

t: Continuing the new chapter of the "two miracles" in a spirit of historical initiative
zh: 以历史主动精神续写“两大奇迹”新篇章
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 9 January 2026
paras: This commentary takes up the Party Central Committee's recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030), which call for a spirit of historical initiative to overcome difficulties, guard against risks and continue the "two miracles" of rapid economic growth and long-term social stability. Chen argues that the coming five years combine strategic opportunity with mounting uncertainty. In the author's view, the "two miracles" can be extended only by vigorously promoting the spirit of historical initiative, which would lay a firmer base for basically achieving socialist modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first treats historical initiative as the key to creating the "two miracles". The second presents the "two miracles" as the concentrated expression of that spirit. The third sets out four areas of work for the 15th Five-Year Plan period: economic development, people's wellbeing, security, and Party building. It is a short Party-theory commentary rather than an empirical study, and it draws mainly on official documents and formulations.

Chen's core claim is that the miracles rest on three unities within historical initiative: conformity to objective laws with purposeful goals; theoretical innovation with practical development; and the people as the subject of history with the Party's people-centred character. The "two miracles" are then said to display a Chinese path (Chinese modernization), a Chinese model of governance, and a Chinese rationale, namely the success of Marxism adapted to China, culminating in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The author contends that this record answers Western claims and offers developing countries a model for balancing growth and stability.

For the next five years Chen proposes keeping economic development central and pursuing high-quality development, including new quality productive forces and a unified national market. The author also proposes combining investment in things with investment in people, so that gains are shared more fairly, and coordinating development with security under a holistic national security outlook. The Party's leadership is named as the decisive factor, to be strengthened through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform. Read the original if you want a compact example of how a provincial Party-academy leader frames the 15th Five-Year Plan in terms of historical initiative and the "two miracles".
quoteEn: Miracles do not fall from the sky; creating them requires taking the initiative while following objective laws.
quoteZh: 奇迹不会从天而降，创造奇迹需要在遵循客观规律的前提下主动作为。

glossary.explanation: Official shorthand for China's rapid economic growth and long-term social stability, used in Party discourse since the 2010s to describe the country's post-reform record.
A term emphasised in Party documents, notably the 2021 historical resolution, for the Party and people actively shaping history by grasping its laws and trends rather than reacting passively.
The official name for China's path to modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models and characterised by a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological breakthroughs, advanced industries and innovation rather than traditional resource-intensive expansion.
The official priority since 2017 of shifting from rapid expansion to growth emphasising quality, efficiency, innovation and balance.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: The Party's official line, prominent since 2012, covering discipline, anti-corruption and organisational standards within the Party.
A Xi-era formulation describing the Party's continuous internal self-correction and discipline as its means of staying in power and avoiding decline.

t: The new development model underpins steady and lasting progress of China's economy
zh: 新发展模式支撑中国经济行稳致远
paras: Writing in Economic Daily on 22 January 2026, Guo Chunli takes up the proposal in the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan to form more of an economic development model led by domestic demand, driven by consumption and based on endogenous growth. Guo argues that this is a major strategic arrangement that follows the laws governing large economies and is an important support for continuing the twin miracles of rapid growth and long-term social stability and for advancing Chinese modernization.

The commentary has three parts. It first sets out why the shift is important and urgent, then explains its underlying regularities and defining features, and finally proposes policy directions. Guo draws on international comparisons, including Germany and Japan, and on Chinese statistics on contributions to growth, per capita GDP and research spending.

On urgency, Guo gives three reasons. The shift is a strategic response to external risks such as weak global trade growth and protectionism, an internal requirement of high-quality development as demographic and investment structures change, and a precondition for smoother national economic circulation, given the strong-supply, weak-demand problem. On regularities, Guo contends that domestic demand leadership is a general law for large economies. The article cites an average 93.1 per cent contribution of domestic demand to growth in 2013–2024, and a U-shaped path for the consumption rate. It also says growth shifts towards total factor productivity in late industrialisation. Guo adds that domestic and external demand, and consumption and investment, are not opposed but complementary.

Guo calls for a systemic approach with three pairings. Investment in physical assets should be combined with investment in people, with private investment stimulated. Improving livelihoods should go together with boosting consumption, by raising incomes, expanding public services and pensions, and removing unreasonable restrictions on consumption. Scientific and technological innovation should be combined with deeper reform, including a new-type whole-nation system, a unified national market and higher-level opening up. Read the original if you want an official-economist account of the 15th Five-Year Plan's demand-side strategy, with the statistics used to support it.
quoteEn: Promoting more of an economic development model led by domestic demand, driven by consumption and based on endogenous growth is not simply a matter of expanding the scale of domestic demand, but of conforming to the trend of upgrading the demand structure.
quoteZh: 促进形成更多由内需主导、消费拉动、内生增长的经济发展模式，并不是简单地扩大内需规模，而是顺应需求结构升级趋势

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's path of modernisation, developed prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from speed-oriented growth to growth based on innovation, efficiency and better structure.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030. The Party's recommendations for it were adopted in October 2025.
An official term for mobilising state and market resources nationally to achieve major scientific and technological breakthroughs.
A policy goal of removing local barriers and protectionism so that goods, capital and labour move freely across China.

t: The development code from poverty alleviation to rural revitalisation
st: A dialogue with Wang Sangui, Dean of the China Institute for Poverty Reduction at Renmin University of China
zh: 从脱贫攻坚到乡村振兴的发展密码
zhSub: 对话中国人民大学中国扶贫研究院院长汪三贵
paras: This is an interview in the Economic Daily series "Dialogue with Economists" (29 January 2026), in which a reporter questions Wang Sangui, Dean of the China Institute for Poverty Reduction at Renmin University of China. Wang reads China's poverty-reduction record from an economic perspective. His main claim is that targeted poverty alleviation, the five-year transition period and the linking of both to rural revitalisation form one continuous, institutionalised path, which should now shift to regular, targeted support in the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

The interview has five parts. It starts with how targeted poverty alleviation worked, then explains why a transition period was needed after 2020. Next it turns to linking poverty alleviation with rural revitalisation, especially in industry, and to why regular support must continue after the transition period ends. It closes with the international significance of China's experience.

Wang describes targeted poverty alleviation as a systematic project: identifying nearly 100 million poor people household by household (for example by the "five looks" method), registering them in an information system, and matching measures to causes, including jobs, public-welfare posts, asset-income schemes, social-security floors and guarantees on schooling, health care and housing. Poverty is dynamic, he says, so the transition period and the "four no-lifts" aimed to prevent large-scale return to poverty, with monitoring of three groups of vulnerable households. He cites rising incomes in poverty-stricken areas, with 2024 per capita disposable income of 17,522 yuan, and finds continuing weaknesses: industries that are "small, scattered and weak", talent outflow, and funding gaps. He argues that the earlier emphasis on investing in things should move towards investing in people, especially children's human capital and the "endogenous motivation" of low-income groups.

Wang concludes that the aim now is a regular mechanism to prevent return to poverty, on a sustainable basis rather than through extraordinary measures, as a step towards common prosperity. He presents China's approach as a model for other developing countries, citing the shift from "flood irrigation" to "precise drip irrigation", the central-provincial-local work mechanism, and multidimensional support, together with overseas training projects. Read the original if you want an official-academic account of how Chinese scholars explain the logic of poverty alleviation, the transition period and the "regular support" phase, with the figures and policy mechanisms Wang cites.
quoteEn: Achieving common prosperity is a long historical process; it cannot rely on extraordinary measures as in the poverty alleviation campaign, and must rest on a sustainable basis.
quoteZh: 实现共同富裕是一个长期的历史过程，不能像脱贫攻坚那样采取超常规措施，必须建立在可持续的基础上。

glossary.explanation: A strategy first put forward by Xi Jinping in 2013 in Shibadong village, Hunan. It requires identifying poor households individually and tailoring support to each household's causes of poverty.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to modernise agriculture and the countryside. It covers industry, talent, culture, ecology and organisation.
The five years after 2020 in which poverty-alleviation policies were kept in place to consolidate results and link them with rural revitalisation. It ended in 2025.
The requirement that when a county is removed from the poverty list, responsibility, policies, assistance and supervision are not withdrawn.
Official term for a mass relapse of lifted households into poverty. Preventing it is set as a bottom line of rural policy.
A long-term goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, stressed in recent years, of raising all incomes and narrowing gaps between urban and rural areas and between regions.

t: The strategic significance and practical requirements of vigorously boosting consumption
zh: 大力提振消费的战略意义和实践要求
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 26 January 2026, Yu Weiping, a deputy director of the CPPCC Economic Committee, examines why the Party leadership has made boosting consumption a priority and what is required to do so. The commentary takes its cue from the Central Economic Work Conference held at the end of 2025, whose first task for 2026 was to "adhere to domestic demand as the mainstay and build a strong domestic market", and from the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). Yu argues that vigorously boosting consumption is a strategic choice of major importance for Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the strategic significance of boosting consumption. The second assesses the growth space and trends of Chinese consumption, drawing on international comparison, supporting factors and structural change. The third lists practical requirements for the coming period, linked to the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030). Yu cites figures such as retail sales above 50 trillion yuan in 2025 and a consumption contribution to growth of 52%.

Yu gives three reasons for the strategic significance. Boosting consumption follows economic law, since economies in late industrialisation and urbanisation shift toward consumption-led growth. It is also a strategic choice for building the new development pattern, given the author's description of China as currently marked by strong supply and weak demand. Finally, it is an inherent requirement of the people-centred development philosophy. On prospects, Yu notes that the household consumption rate is about 40%, 10–20 percentage points below developed countries. Yu expects room to grow from rising incomes, a growing middle-income group, urbanisation, and upgrading toward quality goods, services and digital, green and health consumption. Difficulties such as insecure income expectations are described as problems of development and transition that can be solved.

The practical requirements are organised around making people "able", "dare" and "willing" to consume. Yu calls for raising incomes and the labour share of primary distribution, strengthening social security and equalising basic public services, and expanding high-quality goods and services supply. Yu also calls for better policy coordination, direct-to-consumer subsidies and evaluation of consumption policies, balancing supply and demand, short and long term, and universal and targeted support. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how official policy thinking frames consumption-led growth and the policy toolkit for 2026.
quoteEn: Consumption is a function of income; households' ability and willingness to consume depend to a large extent on employment and income growth.
quoteZh: 消费是收入的函数，居民消费能力和意愿很大程度上取决于就业和收入增长状况。

glossary.explanation: The official formulation of China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022), which the leadership presents as distinct from Western models of modernisation.
An official strategy, put forward in 2020, centred on the domestic economic cycle with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other. It stresses expanding domestic demand.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: A principle associated with Xi Jinping holding that development should be for the people, rely on the people and have its fruits shared by them.
The annual meeting of the Party leadership, held at the end of each year, that sets the economic agenda and priorities for the following year.

t: The new development model underpins steady and sustained progress of China's economy
zh: 新发展模式支撑中国经济行稳致远
paras: Guo Chunli, a deputy director at the National Development and Reform Commission's macroeconomic research institute, comments on the recommendation for the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) to form more economic development patterns led by domestic demand, driven by consumption and based on endogenous growth. Guo argues that this is a major strategic arrangement. It follows the laws governing large economies, and the author presents it as an important support for Chinese modernization and for continuing the twin 'miracles' of rapid growth and long-term social stability.

The piece, published in the Economic Daily, has three parts. The first sets out why the shift is important and urgent. The second explains its underlying logic by taking domestic demand, consumption and endogenous growth in turn. The third offers three policy directions under a 'systems perspective'.

Guo gives three reasons for urgency: external risks such as weak global trade growth and protectionism, the needs of high-quality development, and the requirement to keep the national economic cycle unobstructed amid a 'strong supply, weak demand' contradiction. On the underlying logic, Guo says large economies tend to move from reliance on external demand to domestic demand, and cites average contributions of 93.1 per cent from domestic demand and 55 per cent from final consumption to growth in 2013–2024. Guo adds that Germany and Japan shifted from investment to consumption after passing US$10,000 per capita GDP. Endogenous growth is tied to a shift towards total factor productivity and innovation, with R&D intensity of 2.68 per cent in 2024. Guo stresses that domestic and external demand, and consumption and investment, are not opposed to each other.

Guo's policy proposals pair investment in physical assets with investment in people and expand effective investment, including by stimulating private investment. They also link improving people's livelihoods to consumption, through employment, income growth, public services and pensions, and link scientific and technological innovation to deeper reform, including a unified national market and high-level opening up. Guo presents the aim as stronger development momentum and better macroeconomic governance. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of the economic reasoning and policy priorities behind the shift to domestic demand and consumption in the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Promoting more economic development patterns led by domestic demand, driven by consumption and based on endogenous growth does not simply mean expanding the scale of domestic demand. It means following the trend of upgrading the demand structure, promoting more investment in people and development-oriented consumption such as education, and speeding up the accumulation of human capital.
quoteZh: 促进形成更多由内需主导、消费拉动、内生增长的经济发展模式，并不是简单地扩大内需规模，而是顺应需求结构升级趋势，推动更多服务于人的投资和教育等发展型消费，提升人力资本积累速度

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, emphasised since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official term for growth that stresses innovation, efficiency and quality rather than scale and factor inputs. It has been the stated priority of economic policy since 2017.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030. The Party's recommendations for it are issued first, ahead of the formal plan.
A policy phrase for spending on education, health care, childcare and social security, as opposed to investment in physical infrastructure and capital goods.

t: Expanding space for development by meeting people's livelihood needs
zh: 在满足民生需求中拓展发展空间
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 22 January 2026, takes up the relationship between economic development and people's livelihood (minsheng: education, health care, elderly care, housing, social security). Li Zhiming argues that the two are mutually dependent. Economic development supports improvements in livelihood, while meeting livelihood needs gives development a direction and opens new room for growth. The piece draws on Xi Jinping's recent remarks and the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), whose Recommendations call for "expanding space for development by meeting people's livelihood needs" in the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

The article has three main sections. The first treats livelihood demand as an internal driver of high-quality development. The second treats high-quality development as the foundation for guaranteeing and improving livelihood. The third sets out how to build a virtuous circle between the two. Li illustrates the argument with sectoral examples (health, elderly care, housing) and with provincial and city cases such as Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Chengdu. Statistics on ageing, urbanisation, housing renovation, high-speed rail and 5G coverage are cited as reported by the author.

In Li's account, China's principal social contradiction has changed, and demand is shifting from "having or not having" to "how good", from subsistence needs towards quality and developmental ones. This shift generates new industries, formats and models, and Li contends that demand-driven growth is more endogenous and sustainable than extensive growth. In the other direction, Li holds that high-quality development, through infrastructure and a fairer system of shared benefits under common prosperity, turns growth into tangible livelihood gains. Li frames this as balancing efficiency and fairness: enlarging the pie and also dividing it more fairly, so that both reinforce each other.

Li concludes that the two should form a spiral of industry development, livelihood improvement, consumption upgrading and renewed industrial development. Three measures are proposed: match supply precisely to needs, replacing broad-brush supply with targeted provision; coordinate livelihood and industrial policy to avoid fragmentation, holding a "bottom line" of basic public services and raising a "high line" for industry; and mobilise citizens as participants and beneficiaries through co-construction and sharing. Read the original if you want an example of how official commentary in early 2026 links the Fourth Plenum's livelihood agenda to high-quality development, with its regional case examples.
quoteEn: Expanding space for development by meeting livelihood needs requires building a virtuous circle of industrial development, livelihood improvement, consumption upgrading and renewed industrial development.
quoteZh: 在满足民生需求中拓展发展空间，需要构建“产业发展—民生改善—消费升级—产业发展”的良性循环。

glossary.explanation: A broad term for people's everyday well-being, covering education, health care, employment, housing, pensions and social security. It is a recurring priority in Party and government policy language.
The official goal for China's economy since the late 2010s, stressing quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability rather than speed of growth alone.
A long-standing socialist goal, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping, of prosperity shared by all rather than a few, pursued through development and distribution policy.

t: The South Manchuria Railway Company's responsibility for aggression cannot be concealed
zh: “满铁”的侵略罪责不容掩盖
paras: This newspaper commentary (China Social Sciences Today, January 2026) addresses the role of the South Manchuria Railway Company ("Mantetsu") in Japan's invasion of north-east China. The authors note that Mantetsu is still called Japan's "number one think tank" and argue that it was an instrument of aggression that colluded with the Kwantung Army in preparing the Mukden Incident of 1931.

The article begins with Mantetsu's dual character as a colonial agency and a state-monopoly capitalist enterprise. It then follows its dealings with the Kwantung Army, dividing the period at 6 October 1931, and closes with the rewards Mantetsu received. The authors draw on Chinese and Japanese scholars and on memoirs by company officials.

The authors contend that before 6 October Mantetsu's support was covert and limited to railway control and military transport. They reject the portrayal of president Uchida Yasuya as a "moderate", citing a Mantetsu director's memoir claim that Uchida foresaw even the date of the Incident. After 6 October, they say, Mantetsu openly backed the army, receiving control of most railways, industry and mining in return. They list its troop transport, armoured trains, intelligence and propaganda work, and report that 23,301 employees were decorated by the Japanese emperor.

The authors conclude that Mantetsu and the Kwantung Army both bear inescapable responsibility, quoting Matsuoka Yosuke's remark that the Incident was a joint action. They say that recalling this history supports a correct view of history, protects the victory in the War of Resistance against Japan and serves national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese account of Mantetsu's wartime role and the sources used to rebut its favourable image in Japan.
quoteEn: Mantetsu was the core instrument by which Japan launched its war of aggression against China and pursued colonial expansion, a conclusion long since settled.
quoteZh: “满铁”是日本发动侵华战争、推行殖民扩张政策的核心工具，这一论断早有定论。

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse since the 2010s, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation".
The staged explosion on the South Manchuria Railway near Mukden (Shenyang) on 18 September 1931, used by the Japanese Kwantung Army as a pretext to occupy north-east China.
The Japanese army stationed in the Kwantung Leased Territory and along the South Manchuria Railway zone, which carried out the 1931 invasion of Manchuria.
The Chinese term for the war against Japanese invasion, which official Chinese historiography dates from 1931 to 1945.

t: Using the innovative achievements of poverty alleviation to advance agricultural and rural modernization
zh: 以脱贫攻坚创新成果促农业农村现代化
paras: Writing in Economic Daily on 21 January 2026, the first year of the 15th Five-Year Plan period, Ye Xingqing asks what the experience of the poverty alleviation campaign offers for the next stage of agricultural and rural modernization. The commentary argues that the practical innovations from the campaign and the five-year transition period that followed should guide work on agriculture, rural areas and farmers in the coming years. It takes as its starting point Xi Jinping's instructions to anchor policy on agricultural and rural modernization and to keep the bottom line of no large-scale return to poverty.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the historical and global significance of eliminating absolute poverty, citing figures such as 98.99 million rural poor in 2012, 832 counties removed from the poverty list, and more than 7 million monitored households helped since the 14th Five-Year Plan began. The second draws five lessons from the campaign. The third turns these into proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

Ye's five lessons are: set goals in stages and pursue them precisely, using the successive poverty lines and programmes from 1986 to 2020 as the example; use redistribution, citing nearly 1.6 trillion yuan in special poverty funds and 850.5 billion yuan in central transfers during the transition period; combine investment in things with investment in people; realise the value of ecological products according to local conditions; and optimise village layout, including relocating more than 9.6 million people. The author contends that each lesson carries over into rural revitalization. The proposals include setting phased modernization targets, drawing on the experience of the "Thousand Villages Programme", and building routine assistance into rural revitalization from 2026, with households supported by type (skills training, incentives, or basic guarantees).

Ye also urges building agriculture into a modern industry, improving rural infrastructure and county-centred planning, and raising farmers' incomes. The author notes that the urban–rural income ratio stood at 2.34:1 in 2024 and suggests raising minimum basic pensions and rural minimum living allowances. Read the original if you want an official-adjacent economist's account of how China's poverty alleviation record is being turned into policy guidance for rural modernization after 2026.
quoteEn: Practice shows that investing in things creates the basic conditions for changing backwardness, investing in people stimulates endogenous drive for development, and combining the two achieves integrated gains in effectiveness.
quoteZh: 实践表明，投资于物能为改变落后面貌创造基本条件，投资于人能激发内生发展动力，把两者结合起来就能实现集成增效。

glossary.explanation: The campaign launched after the 18th Party Congress (2012) to lift all rural people out of poverty under the national standard by 2020. The government declared absolute poverty eliminated at the end of 2020.
The five-year period (2021–2025) after the campaign ended, during which poverty-alleviation policies were kept in place to consolidate the results and prevent people from falling back into poverty.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to develop rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards. It is now the framework into which routine poverty assistance is being merged.
Shorthand for the set of issues concerning agriculture, the countryside and peasants, which the Party treats as a priority area of work.
A rural improvement programme begun in Zhejiang Province in 2003 under Xi Jinping, then provincial Party secretary. It is now presented as a model for rural development nationwide.

t: Accelerating high-level scientific and technological self-reliance through systems thinking
zh: 以系统思维加快高水平科技自立自强
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily, Jiang Cheng takes up the call of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) to accelerate high-level scientific and technological self-reliance and lead the development of new quality productive forces. Jiang argues that this is a complex systems project involving many actors, links and levels, and that it requires systems thinking: forward-looking, comprehensive and integrated planning to move China from a major to a strong science and technology country.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first concerns integrating the innovation system, the second fostering an innovation ecosystem, and the third raising innovation performance on a continuing basis.

On the system, Jiang stresses wholeness, dynamism and openness. The author calls for deep integration of the innovation, industrial, capital and talent chains, and for clear roles for national laboratories, leading universities and leading enterprises. Jiang also urges a pattern with a solid core and open outer ring: open cooperation on general technologies, but self-reliance and the new whole-nation system in key core technologies. On the ecosystem, Jiang proposes "agile governance", more value-oriented research evaluation, enterprises as the main innovators, and integrated rather than single-point policy.

In conclusion, Jiang proposes stronger basic research, breakthroughs in key core technologies such as artificial intelligence and quantum information, and a culture that values science and innovation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars frame science and technology policy for the 15th Five-Year Plan period in systems terms.
quoteEn: The overall effectiveness of a system depends not only on the strength of individual actors, but even more on the network structure and cooperative efficiency among them.
quoteZh: 系统的整体效能不仅取决于单个主体的强弱，更取决于各主体间的网络结构与协同效率。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation.
An official term for mobilising state, market and social resources in a coordinated way to achieve major scientific and technological goals.

t: The theoretical content and practical orientation of adhering to the general keynote of seeking progress while maintaining stability
zh: 坚持稳中求进工作总基调的理论内涵和实践指向
paras: Following the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference, which called for adhering to the general keynote of making progress while maintaining stability in the 2026 economic work, Chen Hangyu explains what this principle means in theory and how it should guide policy. This Guangming Daily commentary argues that the principle is both a governing rule of the Party and a methodology for economic work. In Chen's account, Xi Jinping's statements on it form part of Xi Jinping's economic thought and make an original contribution to developing Marxist political economy.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical content of "stability" and "progress" in terms of endogenous growth in a large economy. The second turns to the policy logic of applying the principle. The third gives four priorities for economic work in the new situation: expanding domestic demand, leading the development of new quality productive forces, promoting high-quality and full employment, and expanding high-level opening up.

Chen's core argument is that stable economic operation, the transformation of the development model, and the mutual reinforcement of the two together drive endogenous growth. Cyclical volatility, the author says, undermines the conditions for technological accumulation and is magnified in a large economy by high multiplier effects. Citing South Korea against Latin America, Chen holds that a shift from factor-driven growth to total factor productivity is the key to escaping the "middle-income trap". Stability without progress, Chen warns, eventually turns expectations negative. On policy, the author calls for medium- and long-term planning, including the 15th Five-Year Plan, to align macro policies. Counter-cyclical and cross-cycle adjustment should be coordinated, and an expectation-management mechanism should make policy more predictable.

Chen concludes that high-quality development should meet uncertainty with certainty. The practical proposals include a consumption-boosting campaign, income-growth plans, AI-enabled consumption, closer integration of technological and industrial innovation, wage-growth mechanisms, AI-based job matching, wider market access in services, and institutional opening up with a deeper "dual linkage" of free trade zones and the Hainan Free Trade Port. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the 2026 economic work agenda is justified in terms of endogenous growth theory.
quoteEn: \"Stability\" and \"progress\" stand in a dialectical unity: stability creates a better environment and opportunity for progress, while progress supplies the driving force for the dynamic balance of stability.
quoteZh: “稳”和“进”是辩证统一的关系，“稳”为“进”创造更好的环境和时机，“进”为“稳”的动态平衡提供动力支撑。

glossary.pinyin: wěn zhōng qiú jìn gōngzuò zǒng jīdiào
glossary.en: general keynote of making progress while maintaining stability
glossary.literal: general keynote of seeking progress within stability
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding principle for economic work, repeated at each annual Central Economic Work Conference since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It requires stable growth, employment, prices and financial security alongside structural adjustment and reform.
An annual meeting of the Party and state leadership, usually in December, that reviews the year's economy and sets the next year's economic tasks and policy orientation.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, as opposed to traditional growth paths.
The official goal for China's economy since 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

t: Rectifying formalism to lighten the burden on the grassroots
zh: 整治形式主义 为基层减负
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2026, takes up the campaign against formalism and for reducing burdens on grassroots officials. The authors, Song Ge and Zhou Wenzhang, describe formalism as a major enemy of the Party and state's undertakings and argue that the grassroots is the "last mile" in carrying out central decisions.
