They contend that the problem must be tackled on four fronts: ideological education, institutional mechanisms, work methods and the prevailing climate.

The piece opens by citing Xi Jinping's repeated statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, which call for deepening this work. It then proceeds through the four areas in turn, each with concrete measures for Party members and officials.

On education, the authors call for theoretical study of the relevant regulations, immersive grassroots experience, routine self-examination and avoidance of formalism within education itself. On institutions, they propose slimmer assessment indicators with dynamic adjustment, power-and-responsibility lists, intelligent monitoring, cross-level supervision and precise accountability. On working methods, they urge positive and negative task lists, merged meetings, shorter documents, a unified national grassroots data platform and an end to compulsory check-ins and excessive record-keeping.

On climate, Song and Zhou advocate cultural immersion, good and bad examples as incentives, and judging work by whether formalism is removed and grassroots efficiency raised, not by paper trails. They also call for leaders to set an example, for upper levels to examine themselves, for cross-departmental coordination and for public participation. Read the original if you want a compact statement of the measures currently promoted for reducing formalism and grassroots burdens in China.
quoteEn: Abandon the formalistic value standard of "judging merit by traces and results by paperwork", and make whether formalism has been eliminated, grassroots burdens reduced and grassroots effectiveness raised the core yardsticks of the value of work.
quoteZh: 摒弃“以痕迹论优劣、以材料定成效”的形式化的价值标准，将形式主义是否破除、基层负担是否减轻、基层效能是否提升等作为衡量工作价值的核心标尺

glossary.explanation: In Party discourse, a style of work that stresses appearances, paperwork and procedure over real results. It is treated as a persistent problem in official conduct.
A common metaphor for the final stage at which central policies are implemented at the local level.
The Communist Party congress held in 2012, at which Xi Jinping became General Secretary.

t: The inherent logic and practical requirements of digital-intelligent development for health of the whole population
zh: 全民健康数智化建设的内在逻辑与实践要求
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily takes up the call in the Party Central Committee's Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) to "accelerate the building of a Healthy China" and "advance digital-intelligent development for the health of the whole population". Gao and Yang argue that merging universal health with digital-intelligent technology follows a clear internal logic and carries concrete practical requirements. In their view it supports building Healthy China and basically realising socialist modernization by 2035.

The piece has four sections. The first sets out why such development is needed in the current era. The other three cover the practical requirements: consolidating the technical foundation, widening integrated application scenarios, and improving institutional safeguards. It draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements on people's health, "Internet Plus" and cybersecurity, and on the wording of the Recommendations.

On the logic, the authors give four reasons. It serves the principle of putting the people first and answers ageing, chronic disease and emerging infections. It supports high-quality development and a stronger public health system, moving from "passive treatment" to "active health". It also represents new quality productive forces in the health field. For practice, they call for a unified national health information platform that breaks "data silos"; tiered data management, privacy computing and blockchain so that data are "usable but not visible"; and moderately advanced computing infrastructure. Applications they list include early-warning surveillance, remote consultation and imaging, and smart oversight of medical insurance funds and the coordinated governance of healthcare, medical insurance and pharmaceuticals.

On safeguards, Gao and Yang urge legislation first, including a dedicated regulation on health and medical data, together with unified technical standards and mutual recognition of data across institutions. They also call for ethical review that guards against algorithmic discrimination, protects informed consent and clarifies human–machine responsibility. They conclude that the work is a necessary path to Healthy China and should turn the plan's blueprint into benefits for the people. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party-aligned commentary frames health digitalisation within the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Digital-intelligent development for the health of the whole population can build an integrated health service chain of "prevention, treatment, management and rehabilitation", achieving a historic shift from "passive medical care" to "active health".
quoteZh: 全民健康数智化能够构建“防、治、管、康”一体化的健康服务链，实现从“被动医疗”到“主动健康”历史性转变。

glossary.explanation: A national strategy launched in 2016 that makes public health a policy priority, covering disease prevention, medical services and health industries.

glossary.en: digital-intelligent development for the health of the whole population
glossary.literal: digital-intelligent construction of health for all people
glossary.explanation: A phrase from the Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, referring to applying big data, AI and related technologies across the health system.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, such as digital technology and AI.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, whose Recommendations were adopted by the Party Central Committee in 2025.
The official goal for the economy since 2017, stressing quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth.

t: Building a Beautiful China to advance the modernization of harmony between humanity and nature in all respects
zh: 以美丽中国建设全面推进人与自然和谐共生的现代化
paras: This commentary, originally published in the People's Daily on 21 January 2026, is a study piece on the first volume of Selected Works of Xi Jinping on Ecological Civilization. Yu Xiang asks what the construction of a Beautiful China means for Chinese modernization. The author argues that it is the concentrated expression of a modernization marked by harmony between humanity and nature, that it reflects the Two Integrations, and that it offers a practical model for a clean and beautiful world.

The piece opens by placing Beautiful China within the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), which made "new major progress" in its construction a main goal of the 15th Five-Year Plan, and within the December 2025 Central Economic Work Conference. It then has three parts: Beautiful China as part of Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilization; Beautiful China as an outcome of the Two Integrations; and the new chapter it writes in global sustainability, backed by institutional, temporal and statistical evidence.

Yu contrasts the Western path, described as fossil-fuelled, consumerist and rooted in a subject–object split between humans and nature, with a Chinese path said to go beyond capital-centred development. The author cites a UN 2025 report that only 35 per cent of Sustainable Development Goal targets are on track. Under the Two Integrations, the article reads the concept of humanity and nature as a community of life, "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", and integrated protection of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts as a fusion of traditional Chinese ecological thought with Marx's view of nature and productive forces. In Yu's account, these ideas overcome the opposition between development and protection and modernise ecological governance.

Yu points to a basically formed institutional system and legal framework since 2012, and to a phased timetable running to 2035 and the mid-century. The article cites 2024 data: PM2.5 down to 29.3 micrograms per cubic metre, 90.4 per cent of surface-water sections at good quality, and forest cover above 25 per cent. It adds China's clean power system, carbon market and green Belt and Road Initiative cooperation. Yu concludes that Beautiful China is both a domestic achievement and a useful reference for global sustainable development. Read the original if you want an authoritative-line example of how Party theorists link ecological policy to Chinese modernization, the Two Integrations and the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: This means that Chinese modernization is not about completing humanity's conquest of nature but about promoting harmony between humanity and nature; it does not treat a good ecological environment as a luxury for a few, but makes it a livelihood benefit shared by all the people.
quoteZh: 这意味着中国式现代化不是完成人类对自然的征服，而是促进人与自然和谐共生；不是将良好的生态环境作为少数人的奢侈品，而是使之成为全体人民共享的民生福祉。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal of ecological civilization construction, introduced at the 18th Party Congress (2012), aiming at a cleaner environment and green development.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from the Western model.
Formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.pinyin: lǜshuǐ qīngshān jiù shì jīnshān yínshān
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are gold and silver mountains
glossary.explanation: A slogan attributed to Xi Jinping in 2005, holding that environmental protection and economic development are mutually reinforcing.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization

t: Eliminating "digital formalism" so that grassroots governance returns to real results
zh: 破除“数字形式主义” 让基层治理回归实效
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 6 January 2026
paras: This newspaper commentary asks why digital tools meant to empower grassroots governance have produced "digital formalism" instead. Li argues that it is the old problem of formalism in a digital guise, arising when technology, institutions and the actions of officials are misaligned. The piece takes its cue from the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), which called for rectifying formalism to reduce burdens on the grassroots.

The article first defines digital formalism from three angles: how it arises, what it looks like, and how it operates. It then sets out three areas for remedies: institutional and mechanism reform, correcting the way technology is understood, and shaping behaviour under public rationality.

In Li's account, digital formalism appears as duplicated or hollow platforms, excessive "trace-keeping" such as photographing work before doing it, and "image projects" built on false digital performance figures. Its causes are assessment pressures, the features of digital tools and officials' utilitarian attitudes. Li calls it a substitution of formal rationality for substantive rationality, and argues that its roots lie in institutions, organisations and environment rather than in technology alone. The proposed remedies include rules on admitting, supervising and tracing responsibility for digital technology, and assessment systems that reward real outcomes rather than quantified data. They also include treating technology as a tool, not a goal, raising digital skills with attention to the elderly, and orienting platforms toward public needs.

Li concludes that digital governance should be judged by whether it responds to people's needs, not by platform coverage or visible metrics. Officials are urged to value "latent" achievements as well as "visible" ones and to avoid a split between online and offline governance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholars frame the burden-reduction campaign and digital governance in the language of the Party's current policy.
quoteEn: Governance modernization should not be measured by how widely digital technology is promoted or how much it covers, so as to prevent technical "means and tools" from being mistaken for "ends and values".
quoteZh: 不以数字技术的推广度、覆盖率作为判断治理现代化的尺度，防止出现把技术性的“手段工具”当作“目的价值”。

glossary.explanation: In Party discourse, a style of work that stresses appearances, paperwork and procedure over practical results. It is a long-standing target of Party rectification campaigns.

t: The 15th Five-Year Plan period as a link between past and future, seen through the "big history" perspective
zh: 从大历史观看“十五五”时期的承前启后地位
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 6 January 2026
paras: This newspaper commentary takes up the judgement in the Party's recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). That judgement holds that the 2026–2030 period occupies an important position linking past and future in the process of basically realising socialist modernization. Zhang argues that the "big history" outlook shows this period to be a decisive foundation-laying stage within the longer course of Chinese modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first traces what Zhang calls a stepwise, cumulative history, from the first Five-Year Plan in 1953 through reform and opening up to the new era. The second explains why the 15th Five-Year Plan period is a critical window, both domestically and internationally. The third lists six areas of work for the period.

Zhang's central move is to read the planning tradition as continuous: each stage rests on the achievements of the one before, under Communist Party leadership. Plans became more strategic "five-year plans" under a socialist market economy and later added innovation, high-quality development and common prosperity. The author presents the coming period as consolidating the 14th Five-Year Plan's gains and preparing the final push of the 16th. Zhang sees global turbulence as bringing both risks and opportunities, and cites China's market size, industrial system and talent base as strengths.

Zhang calls for a stronger "historical initiative" in six areas: a modern industrial system; deeper reform and high-level opening up; a strong domestic market and coordinated regional development; green transition; livelihood protection and common prosperity; and security. The author concludes that only the big history perspective allows the nation to plan with a global and overall view. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars frame the 15th Five-Year Plan within the longer history of planning.
quoteEn: The big history outlook stresses both the continuity of history and the importance of key turning points in time.
quoteZh: 大历史观既强调历史的延续性，又突出关键时间节点的重要作用。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse for viewing events across long time spans and broad contexts, linking past, present and future. It is not the Western academic field of the same English name.
The official term for China's path to modernity under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been a central slogan since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, stressed in recent Party policy as a feature of socialism.
The official term for a growth model emphasising quality, innovation and efficiency over speed alone.

t: Getting the relationship between high-quality development and high-standard protection right
zh: 把握好高质量发展和高水平保护的关系
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 6 January 2026
paras: Zhang Youguo takes up what Xi Jinping calls a worldwide problem: how to handle the relationship between development and protection. The commentary argues that high-quality development and high-level environmental protection are dialectically unified, so advancing them in step is both necessary and feasible. Zhang presents this as a key thread for understanding and applying Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilization.

The piece defines both terms, using the new development philosophy for the first and the integrated protection of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert for the second. It then sets out why the two can advance together, how to do so, and what progress has been made. It closes with a short passage tying the argument to Chinese modernization.

Zhang gives three grounds for feasibility. Both serve people's needs and Chinese modernization, each supports the other, and both develop under unified Party leadership. For practice, Zhang's route is greening industry and industrialising ecology, guided by the idea that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets. This involves a green and low-carbon economy, strict institutions and rule of law that act as hard constraints on development, mechanisms to realise the value of ecological products, and cooperation between an effective market and a capable government.

Zhang reports that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) ecological civilization has undergone historic changes. The author cites falling energy and carbon intensity, falling pollutant emissions alongside steady growth, and the expansion of new-energy industries and ecological industries such as tourism and agriculture. Zhang concludes that persisting with both goals will contribute more to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official line on how development and environmental protection are meant to fit together.
quoteEn: High-quality development and high-level protection are dialectically unified, and advancing them in step is not only very necessary but also highly feasible.
quoteZh: 高质量发展和高水平保护具有辩证统一性，两者同步推进不仅十分必要，而且高度可行。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's ideas on environment and development, presented officially as the guiding theory for ecological civilization building.
The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership. The article describes it as modernization marked by harmony between humanity and nature.
An official framework of five principles: innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2005, holding that protecting the environment is itself a source of economic value.

glossary.zh: 生态产品价值实现机制
glossary.en: mechanisms to realise the value of ecological products
glossary.explanation: Policies that turn ecological resources, such as clean air, water and forests, into measurable and tradable economic value through surveys, property rights, accounting and compensation.

t: Be highly vigilant against Japan's reckless gamble and resolutely defend the post-war international order
st: A perspective from international law
zh: 高度警惕日本铤而走险 坚决捍卫战后国际秩序——国际法视角的透视
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 19 January 2026, Pu Ping argues that Japan's current leadership is challenging the post-war international order, and that international law shows why this must be resisted. The author points to the new prime minister Takaichi Sanae's remarks on Taiwan, her comments on 'collective self-defence' and Japan's reported interest in going beyond its 'three non-nuclear principles'. In Pu's account, these breach international law and challenge China's core interests. The article sets out to clarify Japan's militarist crimes and its obligations as a defeated state, so as to prevent a revival of militarism.

The commentary is organised around five legal pillars. It begins with the Cairo Declaration, the Potsdam Proclamation and the Japanese Instrument of Surrender. It then turns to the Tokyo Trial, to Japan's post-war 'peaceful constitution' and Article 9, and to the 'enemy state clauses' of the UN Charter (Articles 53, 107 and 77). It ends with the four China–Japan political documents signed between 1972 and 2008.

Pu's central claim is that these instruments form a connected chain of legal obligations. The first three documents, the author says, established Japan's status as an aggressor and defeated state and required the return of Chinese territory, including Taiwan. The Tokyo Trial, though less thorough than Nuremberg, is presented as a precedent whose findings now serve as a legal and institutional barrier against right-wing revisionism. Pu traces how Article 9 has been hollowed out since the Cold War, through the Self-Defence Forces, overseas dispatches and Abe Shinzo's push for revision, and argues that revision concerns East Asian order, not just Japanese domestic law. On the 'enemy state clauses', Pu holds that they remain formally in the Charter, and that Japan's status as an 'enemy' depends on its own choices, namely denying historical documents and seeking 'military normalisation'.

Pu contends that Japan's commitments in the four political documents, including adherence to Potsdam Proclamation Article 8, mean it must abandon the notion that Taiwan's status is undetermined. Takaichi's signal of possible armed involvement is described as the product of a long-running right-wing strategy of 'using Taiwan to contain China'. The author calls on Asia-Pacific countries and peace-loving peoples to unite against Japanese right-wing forces, and to uphold a correct view of the Second World War. Read the original if you want to see how an official-line Chinese international-law scholar frames the dispute over Japan, Taiwan and the post-war settlement for a general readership.
quoteEn: In essence, Article 9 of the constitution is the constitutional safeguard against a restoration of Japanese militarism; constitutional revision is not merely a question of Japan's domestic law, but one of whether the post-war East Asian order can be preserved.
quoteZh: 本质上，宪法第九条是阻止日本军国主义复辟的宪法保障，“修宪”不仅仅是日本的国内法问题，而是涉及战后东亚秩序能否得到维护的问题。

glossary.explanation: Provisions of the UN Charter (Articles 53, 107 and 77) that concern states that were enemies of the Allies in the Second World War. The article reads them as allowing action against such states without Security Council authorisation if they resume aggression.
Common name for Japan's 1947 constitution, whose Article 9 renounces war and the maintenance of war potential. The article presents it as a constraint imposed on a defeated state.
The right to use force in defence of an allied state under attack. Debate in Japan concerns whether Article 9 permits exercising it.
The International Military Tribunal for the Far East (1946–48), which tried senior Japanese leaders as Class A war criminals.

t: Guarding strictly against the revival of Japanese militarism
zh: 严防日本军国主义死灰复燃
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2026, Song Zhiyong, a professor of Japanese studies, argues that Japan's new prime minister, Takaichi Sanae, is reviving militarism. In Song's account, Takaichi has challenged China's red line on Taiwan, pushed to revise the "peace constitution" and Japan's security policy, sought to breach the "three non-nuclear principles" and raised military spending. Song contends that this worsens China–Japan relations and leads Japan down a ruinous path, and that postwar Japan never fully cleared the ground for militarism's return.

The commentary is built as a historical survey in three parts. The first traces the roots of modern Japanese militarism from the warrior class and the bushido ethic through Toyotomi Hideyoshi's invasion of Korea to late Edo expansionist thinkers and the Meiji "continental policy". The second divides modern militarism into three stages: formation (1868–1877), institutional consolidation (1878–1894) and expansion and collapse (1894–1945). The third covers Allied postwar measures, their reversal and the revisionism of recent decades.

Song's central claim is that postwar accountability was real but incomplete. He cites the Tokyo Tribunal, in which 28 defendants were tried and seven sentenced to death, and the purges of public officials and educators, which the article says removed over 200,000 public-office holders and 7,003 teachers and education officials. Song argues that under Cold War pressure and shifts in US policy, the purges were reversed and many war criminals and supporters returned to politics, Kishi Nobusuke among them. He says this allowed later leaders to glorify the war, visit Yasukuni Shrine, revise textbooks and rebuild armed forces despite Article 9.

Song presents Abe Shinzo, Kishi's grandson, as the culmination of this historical revisionism. Abe revised the interpretation of collective self-defence and pursued constitutional revision. Song says Takaichi openly inherits Abe's line, stirs nationalism and spreads the "China threat" theory, so that signs of militarist revival are increasingly clear. He calls on the international community to take this seriously and respond, to prevent a repeat of history and protect peace in East Asia and the world. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the Chinese academic and official-media case that Japan is remilitarising, together with its historical narrative from the Edo period to the present day.
quoteEn: Although Japanese militarism was called to account to a certain degree after the war, this was not thorough, and the basis for its revival remained.
quoteZh: 日本军国主义在战后虽然得到一定的清算，但并不彻底，残留了死灰复燃的基础。

glossary.explanation: The common name for Japan's 1947 postwar constitution, especially its Article 9, which renounces war as a means of settling disputes and bars maintaining war potential.
Japan's long-standing policy of not possessing, not producing and not permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons.
The term used in Chinese historiography for Meiji and later Japan's strategy of expansion onto the Asian mainland, especially Korea and China.
In this context, efforts to deny or play down Japan's wartime aggression and war responsibility.

glossary.literal: International Military Tribunal for the Far East
glossary.explanation: The International Military Tribunal for the Far East, convened by the Allies in Tokyo (1946–1948) to try Japan's leading wartime figures.

t: Adhering to the close integration of investing in things and investing in people
zh: 坚持投资于物和投资于人紧密结合
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 19 January 2026, takes up the principle that investment in physical assets ("things") and investment in human beings must be closely combined. The principle appears in Xi Jinping's remarks at the Second Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee's Fourth Plenum (2025) and in the Central Economic Work Conference of December 2025. Sun and Cui argue that it marks a historic shift in the mode of development from "things first" to "things and people in coordination". They present it as a strategic step for advancing Chinese modernization and as a basic guide for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the principle's value for the present era. The second explains its core meaning. The third proposes practical paths for carrying it out. The authors draw on Xi Jinping's statements, the Fourth Plenum's Recommendations and the 2025 Government Work Report, and they cite a few figures, including a 86.4 per cent average contribution of domestic demand to growth in 2021–2024.

On value, the authors say the principle drives high-quality development, because returns on physical investment are diminishing and growth now depends on accumulating human capital. They also say it underpins a new development pattern by combining "hardware" and "software" in domestic demand. In their account it serves common prosperity, citing a share of over 70 per cent of general public budget spending going to livelihood areas, and it helps win global competition, which they describe as now a contest over talent. On core meaning, Sun and Cui hold that physical investment is the material basis of investing in people, while human development is the ultimate purpose of accumulating things. They call for better investment structure, stronger institutional supply and a systemic approach to balancing government and market, short and long term, and region and whole.

For implementation the authors propose four paths: industrial upgrading linked to talent training; livelihood improvement, with more public investment in childcare, education, health and elderly care; innovation and entrepreneurship; and digital transformation. They stress that more investment in people does not mean replacing investment in things. They conclude that the principle should run through all areas of economic and social development as groundwork for basically realising socialist modernization by 2035. Read the original if you want an official-line explanation of this policy slogan and the concrete measures attached to it in the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Investing in things is the material basis for investing in people, and investing in people is the guarantee of the effectiveness of investing in things.
quoteZh: 投资于物是投资于人的物质基础，投资于人是投资于物的效能保障。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Communist Party's model of modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.
The official goal of shifting growth from scale and speed to efficiency, innovation and quality. It has been the stated theme of economic work since the late 2010s.
A stated socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given fresh emphasis under Xi Jinping. It is linked to narrowing gaps between regions, urban and rural areas, and income groups.
A strategy put forward in 2020 that treats the domestic market and "internal circulation" as the mainstay of the economy, with domestic and international circulation reinforcing each other.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030. Its Recommendations were adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in October 2025.

t: Why emphasise high-quality development of industrial chains
zh: 为什么要强调产业链高质量发展
paras: This commentary in Economic Daily, written in January 2026, asks how to understand the call of the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference to "implement a new round of action for high-quality development of key industrial chains". Deng Zigang notes that a similar round was launched in late 2023 to counter protectionism and fill gaps in manufacturing. The author argues that the new round differs in purpose: it aims to raise the overall competitiveness of industrial chains and to foster new quality productive forces.

Deng organises the discussion around three key terms: "key industries", "chain" and "high-quality development". The piece then turns to the link between technology and industry, to four types of chain-building work, and to three practical measures for implementation.

In Deng's reading, key industries form a "matrix" of advanced manufacturing, strategic emerging and future industries, and upgraded traditional industries. The word "chain" signals coordination between upstream and downstream firms led by core enterprises, rather than isolated breakthroughs. Deng holds that, after recent progress in areas such as new-energy vehicles and photovoltaics, the task is to move from patching weak spots to systematic upgrading towards high-end, intelligent and green production. Chain quality determines whether scientific results become products, so a good chain is described as a safe, efficient, low-cost conversion track. Deng distinguishes four tasks: filling gaps, strengthening existing links, building new chains and unblocking circulation. Local governments, the author adds, should avoid pursuing "large and complete" local systems and plan from the standpoint of a unified national market.

Deng proposes targeted work on weak links, including risk maps, open-competition research mechanisms and proof-of-concept platforms. Further proposals are regional innovation cooperation centred on Beijing, Shanghai and the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area, and better financial and intellectual-property support. Read the original if you want a concise official-style account of how Chinese policy commentary frames industrial-chain upgrading in the run-up to the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: High-quality development of the industrial chain means building a safe, efficient and low-cost track for conversion.
quoteZh: 高质量发展产业链就是打造一条安全、高效、低成本的转化跑道。

glossary.explanation: An official goal, prominent since 2017, that shifts emphasis from speed of growth to quality, innovation, efficiency and sustainability.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 to describe growth driven by technological breakthroughs and advanced industries such as AI and new energy.
An annual closed-door meeting of Party and state leaders, held at the end of the year, that sets economic policy priorities for the coming year.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030; the Party's recommendations for it were adopted in 2025.

t: The role and key to accelerating the cultivation and strengthening of new growth drivers
zh: 加紧培育壮大新动能的作用与关键
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily, takes up the Central Economic Work Conference's decision to list innovation-driven growth and the accelerated cultivation of new growth drivers among the priority tasks for 2026. Tian and Zhao argue that the substance of the task is to drive growth through innovation, which serves short-term growth targets and long-term international competitiveness. They contend that success requires a faster pace, adaptation to local conditions, and coordinated work on technological breakthroughs, industrial upgrading and application scenarios.

The article has three parts. The first traces how the conference wording on new drivers evolved from 2022 to 2025, when the word "accelerate" (jiajin) was added, and sets out domestic and international reasons for urgency. The second explains the internal relationship among scientific and technological innovation, industrial innovation and scenario innovation. The third names two keys to implementation: deep integration of technological and industrial innovation, and measures suited to local conditions.

On the domestic side, the authors say investment and consumption growth have slowed and old drivers are weakening. They cite a figure that the "three new" economy exceeded 18% of GDP in 2024, but say it must grow further. They also link new drivers to supply–demand balance, citing gaps in eldercare beds, in childcare places (4.08 per thousand people) and in low-altitude economy infrastructure. Internationally, they argue that AI-led general-purpose technologies shorten the window of opportunity, so turning research into industry quickly decides competitive outcomes. The three types of innovation form one chain: technology supplies the engine through key generic technologies, industry achieves scaled production matched to mass demand, and scenarios link technology to markets through real demonstration applications. The authors add that industrial innovation may now run ahead of technological innovation, while in China the two remain partly disconnected ("two layers of skin").

The authors call for removing institutional obstacles between the innovation chain and the industrial chain, and for better resource allocation, industry–university–research cooperation and industrial layout. They also call for local governments to explore differentiated paths, since no mature model exists yet. The aim, in their account, is for new drivers to become a strong engine of high-quality, sustainable growth. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of the 2026 Central Economic Work Conference's innovation priority by researchers from a State Council think tank.
quoteEn: Scientific and technological innovation, industrial innovation and scenario innovation each play a distinct role in generating new drivers; they are both different from and dependent on one another, and together form the complete chain through which innovation drives economic growth.
quoteZh: 科技创新、产业创新和场景创新三者在激发新动能过程中分别承担着独特的作用，既相互区别又相互依存、协同关联，共同构成创新驱动经济增长的完整链条。

glossary.explanation: An annual closed-door meeting of top Party and state leaders, usually held in December, that sets economic policy priorities for the coming year.
A policy term for emerging sources of economic growth based on innovation, such as new industries, business forms and models, replacing older investment- and factor-driven sources.
A statistical category covering new industries, new business forms and new models, used to measure the share of emerging activity in GDP.
Policy usage for creating real-world application settings in which new technologies and products can be demonstrated, tested and scaled.
A long-standing principle of tailoring policy to the specific conditions of each region rather than applying uniform models.

keywords: Development Research Center of the State Council

t: Continuously strengthening and leveraging the advantages of a super-large-scale market
zh: 持续增强和发挥超大规模市场优势
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily in January 2026, asks how China should strengthen and use the advantage of its super-large-scale market during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Guo Liyan argues that this advantage is not only a matter of scale effects but a systemic one, combining expansion of incremental demand, better quality and efficiency, and smoother economic circulation. Guo presents it as a stabiliser of the economy and a source of new momentum, and as a necessary basis for strategic initiative and high-quality development amid a changing external environment.

The piece opens by citing the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), which listed the super-large-scale market among China's institutional, industrial and talent advantages. It then runs through three sections on what the advantage provides: strategic confidence, a pull on factors of production, and economic vitality. A final section names current problems and sets out four policy directions.

Guo contends that the market is a scarce strategic resource in great-power competition. In Guo's account, it gives firms room to grow under protectionism and technology restrictions, supports long-cycle research with patient capital and application scenarios, and strengthens China's say in trade talks and standard-setting. It also acts as a gravitational field for capital, talent, technology and data. Scale supports finer specialisation, as in new energy vehicles, and fosters a cycle of factor concentration, industrial upgrading, consumption upgrading and stronger attraction. Guo further describes the market as an accelerator that speeds innovations from first validation to scaled-up iteration, citing mobile payment, livestreaming e-commerce and new domestic brands.

Guo acknowledges obstacles: local market segmentation and protectionism, strong supply but weak demand, overcapacity alongside a shortage of high-end supply, and bottlenecks in income distribution, market infrastructure and regional coordination. The proposed remedies are to build a unified national market and expand institutional opening up. They also include linking industrial and innovation chains through the "unveil the list and take command" mechanism and opening application scenarios, raising incomes toward an olive-shaped distribution and upgrading consumption, and coordinating regional development with better physical and institutional connectivity. The aim is to move from a "big market" to a "strong market". Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a state economic planning researcher links the domestic market to technological self-reliance and the 15th Five-Year Plan agenda.
quoteEn: The advantage of a super-large-scale market is not reflected only in scale effects; it is a systemic advantage spanning several dimensions, including expanding incremental demand, improving quality and efficiency, and keeping circulation smooth.
quoteZh: 超大规模市场优势并非只体现在规模效应上，而且是包含拓展增量、提升质效、畅通循环等多个维度在内的系统性优势。

glossary.explanation: An official term for China's huge domestic market, of over 1.4 billion people, treated in Party documents as a strategic economic advantage.
The official goal, set out since 2017, of shifting from speed-driven growth to growth based on innovation, efficiency and sustainability.
China's medium-term economic and social development plan for 2026–2030. Its guiding recommendations were adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in 2025.
A policy goal of removing local protectionism and regional barriers so that goods, services and factors of production move freely across China.

glossary.literal: take down the notice and take command
glossary.explanation: A research-funding mechanism in which key technological problems are publicly posted and any capable team may bid to solve them.

t: The fundamental purpose of advancing foreign-related rule of law work and the paths to achieving it
zh: 推进涉外法治工作的根本目的及其实现路径
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 16 January 2026, Huo Zhengxin, a professor of international law, asks what foreign-related rule of law work (涉外法治) is ultimately for and how it should be built. Huo takes Xi Jinping's formulation as the answer: its fundamental purpose is to use legal means to better safeguard the interests of the state and the people, promote progress in international rule of law, and help build a community with a shared future for mankind. The article presents this as the value orientation and scientific content of the concept.

The piece has three parts. It first traces the development of foreign-related rule of law work from the Fourth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2014) through the 19th and 20th Party Congresses and plenums, up to the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) and the Central Conference on Law-Based Governance of November 2025. It then explains the meaning of the stated purpose. Finally, it sets out five practical paths for strengthening the system and capacity of foreign-related rule of law.

Huo argues that, as China's integration with the world deepens, domestic and international rule of law no longer stand apart but interact. Foreign-related rule of law is therefore an open, two-dimensional concept. Its domestic dimension covers the parts of China's legal system that involve foreign and international factors: legislation, enforcement, adjudication, compliance, legal services and training. Its international dimension covers China's participation in international law-making, cooperation and legal services. The five paths are: strengthening the Party's overall leadership and strategic planning; putting legislation first to build a system that protects rights and combines offence with defence; improving enforcement and adjudication, including explaining counter-sanctions and anti-'long-arm jurisdiction' cases and strengthening the courts' international credibility; raising the standard of foreign-related legal services, including arbitration, mediation and the International Organization for Mediation; and taking an active, leading part in rule-making so that China is not a passive recipient of international law.

Huo concludes that foreign-related rule of law is needed both for the long-term goal of building a strong country through Chinese modernization and for the more immediate tasks of high-level opening up and responding to external risks. The author calls for study and implementation of Xi's statements and for faster building of the system and capacity. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese legal scholars frame the purpose, chronology and policy agenda of foreign-related rule of law.
quoteEn: In the new era China is not a passive recipient or simple implementer of international rule of law; the fundamental purpose of advancing foreign-related rule of law shows that China has the capacity, the will and the means to drive and promote change in international rule of law through its own exploration and rule-of-law practice.
quoteZh: 新时代中国不是国际法治的被动接受者和简单执行者，推动涉外法治的根本目的表明我国有能力、有意愿、有办法通过自身探索和法治实践推动和促进国际法治变革

glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping Thought on the rule of law covering the parts of China's legal system that deal with foreign and international matters, and China's participation in international law. It is paired with domestic rule of law under the principle of coordinating the two.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, presented as a vision of cooperative global governance.
The official name for the Communist Party of China's path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on the rule of law
community with a shared future for mankind

t: Building new advantages in the business environment to underpin high-quality development
zh: 以营商环境新优势构筑高质量发展新支撑
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily argues that high-quality development depends on the vitality of market entities, and that a better business environment releases it. Taking up the call of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) for a first-class market-oriented, law-based and internationalised business environment, Qin Pingshan contends that China must now build "new advantages" in this area to generate fresh momentum for growth.

The piece notes that reforms to streamline administration and delegate power have already lifted China's global business-environment ranking. It then sets out three tasks for the 15th Five-Year Plan period: an innovation-friendly ecosystem to nurture new quality productive forces, institutional opening-up to connect with the global economy, and further comprehensive deepening of reform to optimise the overall ecosystem.

On innovation, Qin proposes end-to-end intellectual property protection, a tolerant yet prudent innovation culture with regulatory "safe spaces", financing tools for intangible assets, and basic data institutions covering ownership, circulation and revenue sharing. On opening-up, the author calls for pre-establishment national treatment with negative lists, more transparent and stable policy, and alignment with high-standard rules such as CPTPP and DEPA, including competitive neutrality and cross-border data solutions. Qin holds that practical strengths in the digital and green sectors can be turned into rule-making strengths that offer a Chinese contribution to global governance.

Qin concludes that the business environment should be treated as a complex system, shifting from isolated breakthroughs to systemic integration. This means credit-based tiered supervision, the "dual random, one public" inspection model, online government services, and legislation, enforcement and judicial protection that treat all market entities equally. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the policy measures currently linked to business-environment reform in China's 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Building new advantages in the business environment is, in essence, constructing an innovation-friendly ecosystem suited to new quality productive forces.
quoteZh: 构筑营商环境新优势，本质上就是为适应新质生产力而构建的创新友好型生态系统

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, data and high-end industries rather than traditional resource-heavy growth.
The official goal, since about 2017, of shifting China's economy from rapid expansion towards efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
A reform slogan for cutting administrative approvals, improving regulation and improving government services for businesses and citizens, in use since the mid-2010s.
An approach to opening that focuses on aligning rules, regulations and standards with international ones, beyond tariff cuts and market access.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030.

t: Drawing lessons for governance from the Dujiangyan water-control approach
zh: 从都江堰治水之道中汲取治国理政智慧
paras: This newspaper commentary takes its cue from remarks Xi Jinping made at Dujiangyan, the dam-free irrigation system in Sichuan begun in the late Qin period. Speaking with French President Macron, Xi said he drew governance wisdom from the ancestors' adaptation to local conditions, going with the flow, unity of heaven and humanity, and water control for the people's benefit. Chu argues that these four principles carry a value beyond their time and bear on modernizing the system and capacity of national governance.

The article is organised in four numbered sections, one for each principle. Each first describes how the Dujiangyan works and how its builders, Li Bing and his son, approached the task. It then sets out what Chu presents as the matching practice of the Party and state since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The examples include poverty alleviation, regional coordination, rural revitalisation, economic reform, ecological civilization and livelihood protection.

In Chu's account, the Dujiangyan's three components divide the Min River's flow, discharge silt and floods, and regulate irrigation. Chu reads this design as scientific decision-making that fits local terrain and works with the river's nature. It also served an ecological aim and benefited the people of the Chengdu plain. Chu turns each point into a governance lesson. Policy must proceed from actual conditions, as in targeted poverty alleviation and differentiated regional policy. Government must follow objective laws, which Chu defines in Marxist terms, citing the socialist market economy and green transformation as cases. Development should harmonise with nature through the idea that green mountains are gold mountains. Governance should be people-centred, which Chu ties to the Marxist view that the people are the essential attribute of the doctrine.

Chu concludes that the ancient project and the Party's present governance share one logic, even though conditions have changed greatly. In this reading, decisions rooted in reality, respect for laws, ecological balance and service to the people strengthen governance capacity and win popular support. The piece, which cites the site's 2000 UNESCO World Heritage listing as recognition of its ecological ideas, is an example of how Party theorists use traditional Chinese culture to illustrate current policy. Read the original if you want to see how a Central Party School scholar links classical engineering heritage to Xi Jinping's governance language.
quoteEn: Governing a country is like controlling water: one must proceed from reality in everything and formulate policies and strategies on the basis of national conditions and the people's circumstances.
quoteZh: 治国理政如同治水，必须坚持一切从实际出发，立足国情民情制定政策方略。

t: Vigorously stimulating the innovative vitality of the digital economy
zh: 大力激发数字经济创新活力
paras: This commentary from Guangming Daily asks how China can stimulate innovation in the digital economy. The authors, Jin Siyuan and Chen Yanqing, describe the digital economy as the future direction of global development and a force that is reorganising factor resources and reshaping competition. Citing Xi Jinping and the Party's recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan, they argue that China must seize this opportunity so the digital economy can empower the real economy and drive high-quality development.

The piece is built as a policy agenda in five parts, each opened by a statement from Xi Jinping. The parts are: key core technologies, data as a factor of production, the "AI Plus" initiative, high-level opening up, and the governance system. Each part gives three or so concrete measures.

On technology, the authors call for using the new whole-nation system to unite an effective market with a capable government. They also want faster conversion of research results into applications, and a leading role for major technology enterprises. On data, which they call the fifth factor of production after land, labour, capital and technology, they propose expanding the supply of high-value data, building a nationally integrated data market with market-based pricing, and applying data in manufacturing, transport, finance and green industries. On AI, they say China's complete range of industrial categories offers an ideal testing ground, citing more than 1,500 industry models covering 50 key sectors and over 700 scenarios.

The authors also urge expanding opening up through the "Digital Silk Road", digital trade, and a role in international standards and rules such as DEPA negotiations. They propose governance with several participants, digitalised regulation and a balance between development and security, so that data can circulate and firms innovate with confidence. They conclude that these measures together will sustain the vitality of the digital economy. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Chinese discourse sets out digital-economy priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Data is the fifth major factor of production after land, labour, capital and technology, and it is also the core factor of production of the digital economy.
quoteZh: 数据是继土地、劳动力、资本、技术之后的第五大生产要素，也是数字经济的核心生产要素。

glossary.explanation: A model for mobilising state and national resources, combined with market mechanisms, to achieve breakthroughs in strategic science and technology.
An official goal emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth, promoted since the late 2010s.
A national initiative to embed artificial intelligence across industries and sectors of the economy.
The digital strand of the Belt and Road Initiative, covering digital infrastructure and technology cooperation with partner countries.

t: Building national ecological civilization pilot zones to a high standard
zh: 高质量建设国家生态文明试验区
paras: This short commentary, published in People's Daily on 14 January 2026, discusses how to build national ecological civilization pilot zones to a high standard. Tang Tao presents the zones as a major strategic decision of the Party Central Committee, repeated in the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). In Tang's account they serve as a "reform testing ground" for deep-seated problems in ecological work and a "demonstration window" for a beautiful China.

The piece links the zones to green development as the "distinctive underlying colour" of Chinese modernization. It then sets out three working principles, each illustrated by a provincial case: Fujian, Guizhou and Hainan.

First, institutional innovation should reconcile protection and growth. Tang says the zones have built evaluation, accountability and natural-resource property-rights systems, and cites Fujian's removal of GDP ranking for 34 key ecological-function counties as evidence that protection and development reinforce each other. Second, green science and technology should support green transition. Tang points to Guizhou's backing for green innovation and industrialisation of research results, and calls for more investment, including big data and artificial intelligence in environmental governance. Third, the zones should pursue people's wellbeing. Tang cites Hainan's tropical rainforest national park reforms as raising governance effectiveness while improving livelihoods.

Tang concludes that the zones should produce replicable, extendable institutional results and ensure that ecological gains reach all the people more fairly. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary frames ecological pilot zones in relation to the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Such institutional innovation drives a change in the mode of development, and strongly demonstrates that ecological protection and economic development are not opposed to each other but can promote and complement each other.
quoteZh: 这类制度创新推动发展方式变革，有力证明生态保护与经济发展并非相互对立，而是能够相互促进、相得益彰。

glossary.explanation: Provincial-level pilot areas (starting with Fujian in 2016, later Jiangxi, Guizhou and Hainan) where the central government tests institutional reforms in environmental governance before wider rollout.
Official term for China's path of modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models; it includes harmony between humanity and nature as one feature.
An official goal of building a cleaner, ecologically healthy country, promoted in Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Official principle that development should serve the people's interests; here it is applied to the ecological environment as a livelihood good.

t: Consolidating security through development, pursuing development through security
zh: 在发展中固安全 在安全中谋发展
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 15 January 2026, asks what it means to "coordinate development and security" as the 15th Five-Year Plan period begins. Li Pengfei and Wu Haijun argue that the principle, now summed up as "consolidating security through development and pursuing development through security", is both a distillation of governing experience since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and an inherent requirement of Chinese modernization. They present it as the basis for a positive interaction between high-quality development and high-level security.

The article has three parts. It first traces the theoretical lineage and innovation of the idea, then reviews the achievements of the new era in coordinating the two, and finally sets out practical paths for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. The lineage runs from the holistic approach to national security (2014) through the 19th and 20th Party Congresses, the 2023 Central Economic Work Conference and the Recommendations adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025).

In the authors' account, the idea is a creative fusion of Marxist views of development and security that moves beyond treating them as opposites. They contend that it innovates on three fronts. It treats security as an internal component of development, unlike what they describe as mainstream Western economics. It shifts security thinking from defensive to "development-oriented" security. It widens social governance towards risk prevention and multi-party participation. The authors cite figures to show progress: GDP of 134.9 trillion yuan in 2024, grain output of 1.43 trillion jin in 2025, and renewable capacity of 2.17 billion kilowatts by mid-2025. They also point to a falling government debt-to-GDP ratio relative to the G20 average and lower crime and accident rates. They acknowledge remaining weaknesses: dependence on foreign high-end chips and industrial software, uneven supply-chain resilience, financial and local-debt risks, and immature rules for AI, cross-border data and biosecurity.

For the 15th Five-Year Plan period the authors call for four steps: building a modern industrial system with advanced manufacturing at its core; achieving high-level scientific and technological self-reliance through the new-type whole-nation system; strengthening the national security system under centralised leadership; and building capacity in key areas. These areas include political, food, energy, supply-chain, cyber, data, AI and financial security. They stress that coordination is a dynamic, long-term task rather than a fixed balance. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how the Party's security-and-development principle is framed, with the official statistics and policy priorities attached to it.
quoteEn: Coordinating development and security is not a once-and-for-all static balance, but a long-term strategic task that requires continuous deepening and dynamic optimisation.
quoteZh: 统筹发展和安全不是一劳永逸的静态平衡，而是一项需要持续深化、动态优化的长期战略任务。

glossary.literal: overall planning of development and security
glossary.explanation: A governing principle emphasised by Xi Jinping since the 2010s. It holds that economic growth and national security must be planned together, not traded off against each other. The 19th Party Congress (2017) made it a major principle of Party governance.
A concept Xi Jinping put forward in April 2014. It treats security as spanning political, economic, technological, social and other domains.
The official term for China's development path under Party leadership, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official goal, in use since 2017, that shifts emphasis from speed of growth to efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
A model for mobilising state, market and social resources behind national priorities such as key technology breakthroughs.

t: Raising the effectiveness of macroeconomic governance
zh: 提升宏观经济治理效能
paras: Taking its cue from the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference's call to raise the effectiveness of macroeconomic governance, this commentary (published in Guangming Daily on 13 January 2026) asks how China should move from "macro-control" to "macroeconomic governance". Wang Yiming argues that changes in the economy make this shift necessary, that it produced results during the 14th Five-Year Plan period, and that the 15th Five-Year Plan period and 2026 call for more active, better coordinated policy.

The article has four parts. It first sets out the logic of the shift from macro-control to governance, then reviews the achievements of the 14th Five-Year Plan period. It then turns to priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan period, drawing on the Recommendations adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), and ends with policy orientation for 2026, the first year of the new plan.

Wang contends that the economy now shows weak demand against strong supply, weaker investment-driven growth, a technology-led divergence in economic structure and a less stable external environment. Against this background he contrasts governance with traditional macro-control on five points: the actors (government and market as joint means of resource allocation, not subject and object), the goals (aggregate balance, structural optimisation, quality and risk prevention rather than smoothing cycles), the focus (supply and demand together), the methods (coordination across fiscal, monetary, industrial and other policies, plus expectation management) and the horizon (domestic and external balance). For the next plan period he stresses counter-cyclical and cross-cyclical adjustment, policy coordination, expectation management and a growth model led by domestic demand and consumption. He ties the last to reforms: shifting the consumption tax to the point of consumption and down to local government, extending public services to migrants from rural areas where they live, and easing market entry in services.

For 2026 Wang calls for a more proactive fiscal policy that keeps necessary deficit and spending levels while preserving sustainability and "investing in people", and for a moderately loose monetary policy that treats prices as an anchor and keeps liquidity ample. He credits the 14th Five-Year Plan period with GDP passing 130 trillion yuan and a contribution of around 30 per cent to world growth, figures he reports from official sources. Read the original if you want an official-leaning economist's summary of how Chinese policy thinking frames the move from macro-control to governance and the priorities for 2026.
quoteEn: The shift from traditional "macro-control" to "macroeconomic governance" is an inevitable choice for adapting to changes in the stages of economic development and meeting complex and severe challenges, and is also a major innovation in the Party's concepts and practice of macroeconomic management.
quoteZh: 从传统的“宏观调控”向“宏观经济治理”转变，是适应经济发展阶段性变化、应对复杂严峻挑战的必然选择，也是我们党宏观经济管理理念与实践的重大创新。

glossary.explanation: Official term, in use since the 2020s, for a broader approach to managing the economy than traditional macro-control. It stresses coordination among many policies, supply as well as demand, and domestic and external balance.
The long-standing Chinese term for state management of the overall economy, mainly through fiscal and monetary policy to smooth cycles.

glossary.pinyin: nì zhōuqī hé kuà zhōuqī tiáojié
glossary.explanation: Counter-cyclical policy offsets short-term swings in the economy. Cross-cyclical policy looks across several cycles, aiming at structural balance and avoiding long-term side effects.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030, whose Recommendations were adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in 2025.
Annual meeting of the Party and state leadership, normally in December, that reviews the year's economy and sets policy tasks for the next year.
Policy slogan for directing public spending to education, childcare, elder care, health and other livelihood areas, in order to raise household consumption capacity.

t: Grasping the "five musts" in depth to get the 15th Five-Year Plan period off to a good start
zh: 深刻把握“五个必须” 推动“十五五”良好开局
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 13 January 2026, interprets the "five musts" that Xi Jinping set out at the Central Economic Work Conference at the end of 2025. Zhong presents them as regular patterns drawn from recent practice for economic work under new conditions. The author argues that they both summarise past experience and guide future development, and that they enrich Xi Jinping's economic thought. Applying them well, Zhong says, is the way to get the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030) off to a good start.

The article has five sections, one for each "must". They cover fully tapping economic potential; pursuing policy support and reform and innovation together; making sure the economy is both "liberalised effectively" and "well managed"; closely combining investment in physical assets with investment in people; and meeting external challenges by building up internal strength. Each section follows the same pattern: a rationale, supporting figures and practical tasks for 2026.

Zhong's argument has three main strands. First, China's large size, huge market, complete industrial system and skilled workforce are said to supply the potential, while the socialist system gives certainty. Zhong cites room to raise consumption, which is about 40 percent of the economy, and per capita infrastructure stock, said to be only 20–30 percent of the level in developed countries. Second, short-term macro policy is likened to treating symptoms and reform to building long-term strength, so each is said to fail without the other. "Liberalising" is defined as equal treatment for all forms of ownership, and "managing" as building a law-based economy and curbing "involution-style" competition. Third, Zhong argues that investment priorities should shift as development advances, from physical capital towards education, health, childcare and elderly care. The author cites education and health spending below developed-country levels and insists that the two kinds of investment reinforce each other.

On external challenges, Zhong describes rising tariffs, unilateralism and what the article calls Western containment of China. It contends that history shows China's strength in meeting such shocks, citing the fall in the export share of GDP from about 34 percent in 2007 to about 19 percent. The proposed response is to concentrate on one's own affairs. This means a modern industrial system, self-reliance in science and technology, a unified national market, more diverse export markets and wider opening up. Zhong concludes that China is confident of meeting outside pressure and of advancing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an authoritative, official-line reading of the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference and the economic priorities of the first year of the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Only when policy "blood transfusion" and reform "blood production" work together can short-term stability and long-term health be organically unified.
quoteZh: 只有政策“输血”与改革“造血”协同发力，才能实现“短期稳定”与“长期健康”的有机统一。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, prominent in official discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official body of ideas on economic work associated with Xi Jinping, treated as part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

t: Expanding the international science and technology innovation centres carries strategic significance
zh: 国际科技创新中心扩围具有战略意义
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily in January 2026, asks why the Central Economic Work Conference of 2025 decided to widen the scope of the country's international science and technology innovation centres, and what follows from that decision. Qiu argues that the move, which extends the Beijing centre to the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region and the Shanghai centre to the Yangtze River Delta, is a major strategic decision. In Qiu's account it responds to intensifying great-power rivalry in technology and is meant to make China a leading source of original innovation.

The article has three parts. The first reviews the achievements of the three centres (Beijing, Shanghai and the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area) since the 18th Party Congress (2012), citing China's first place for three consecutive years in the World Intellectual Property Organization's 2025 ranking of top 100 innovation clusters. The second explains why expansion is necessary and what orientations should guide it. The third identifies each region's weaknesses and proposes region-specific measures.

Qiu's central claim is that technological competition has shifted from single-point contests to competition between systems. Single-city centres, the author says, now suffer from limited space, constrained industrial conversion and incomplete innovation chains, whereas leading centres worldwide operate through city clusters. Expansion therefore changes the logic of construction: from gathering resources to coordinating systems, from research capacity to comprehensive innovation capacity, and from city competition to national strategy. Qiu then assigns each region a task. Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei must bridge the gap between basic research and industrialisation. The Yangtze River Delta must strengthen basic theory and the division of labour among its provinces. The Greater Bay Area must reinforce basic research and align rules across its distinct legal and customs systems, using Hong Kong's strengths.

Qiu concludes that coordinated and differentiated development of the three centres should move China from "single-point breakthroughs" to "system leadership". The author expects this to produce a multipolar, tiered strategic pattern on the global innovation map. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the expansion of the innovation centres is justified and what regional tasks are proposed for it.
quoteEn: Looking at the world's influential science and technology innovation centres, nearly all operate on the basis of city clusters or metropolitan areas, and international technological competition is shifting from single-point contests to system-level competition.
quoteZh: 纵观全球具有重要影响力的科技创新中心，基本上都依托城市群或都市圈的形态运行，国际科技竞争正在由单点比拼转向体系竞争。

glossary.en: international science and technology innovation centres
glossary.explanation: City or regional hubs designated by the Chinese state to lead in research, technological innovation and industrial upgrading. Three have been designated: Beijing, Shanghai and the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area.
The region comprising Beijing, Tianjin and Hebei province, treated in Chinese policy as a single area for coordinated development.
A regional development cluster linking nine cities in Guangdong with Hong Kong and Macao, which the article notes operate under different legal, tax and currency systems.
An annual meeting of the Party and state leadership, usually held in December, that sets the economic policy agenda for the coming year.

t: Guiding financial institutions to step up support for expanding domestic demand
zh: 引导金融机构加力支持扩大内需
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in January 2026, asks how finance can better support the expansion of domestic demand. It takes its cue from the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference, which made 'adhering to domestic demand as the driver and building a strong domestic market' a key task for the first year of the 15th Five-Year Plan. He and Zhang argue that financial support must shift from scale-driven to quality-and-efficiency-driven, so that its fit with demand and its sustainability improve.

The piece has four parts. It first explains why the shift is needed, then identifies structural problems in financial support, seen from the standpoint of households, enterprises and financial institutions. It closes with three groups of policy proposals: coordination of fiscal and monetary policy, reform of financial institutions, and a broader support ecosystem. It draws on central bank reporting, loan data for the first 11 months of 2025 and IMF and World Bank growth forecasts.

The authors argue that slower growth in total financial aggregates is natural as the economy moves from high-speed to high-quality development. Easing in total volume alone, they say, cannot energise households and firms facing high savings rates, weak propensity to consume and mismatched financing. They propose optimising structure, strengthening transmission and promoting circulation. They identify gaps: consumer credit products that are homogeneous and do not reach flexible workers or those with imperfect credit records; a shortage of medium- and long-term funding for small manufacturers and specialised 'little giant' firms; and banks squeezed by narrowing interest margins and rising bad loans.

The authors call for systemic reform rather than piecemeal adjustment. Their proposals include special relending tools or quotas for consumer credit, fiscal interest subsidies and tiered loss compensation through local guarantee systems, and assessment indicators that reward inclusive consumer lending. They also urge a shift from collateral-based to credit-based lending using digital credit profiles, and county-level inclusive finance outlets. Capital-market channels such as real estate investment trusts for community commercial facilities are another proposal. Read the original if you want a concise view of how mainstream Chinese economists frame financial policy for domestic demand at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Optimising structure is the precondition for raising the efficiency of fund use, strengthening transmission is the key to clearing the 'last mile' of policy implementation, and promoting circulation is an important condition for expanding domestic demand.
quoteZh: 优化结构是提升资金使用效能的前提，强化传导是打通政策落地“最后一公里”的关键，促进循环是扩大内需的重要条件。

glossary.explanation: China's national development plan for 2026–2030, the successor to the 14th Five-Year Plan. 2026 is its first year.
An annual meeting of Party and state leaders, usually held in December, that sets the main economic tasks and policy tone for the coming year.

glossary.literal: specialised, refined, distinctive, innovative 'little giant' enterprises
glossary.explanation: A government-designated category of small and medium-sized firms that are specialised, refined, distinctive and innovative, and that receive policy support, often in advanced manufacturing niches.

A long-standing policy aim of raising household consumption and investment within China so that growth relies less on exports. The article treats it as the strategic base of the 'new development paradigm'.

t: Fully tapping China's economic potential
zh: 充分挖掘中国经济潜能
paras: This newspaper commentary explains one of the "five musts" set out by the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference: that the country "must fully tap its economic potential". Yuan Lei argues that China's economy is large not only in volume but in latent potential, and that turning this potential into momentum for high-quality development is a strategic task for the coming Five-Year Plan period.

The article has three parts. It first asks why potential deserves attention, citing achievements of the 14th Five-Year Plan period. It then identifies where the potential lies, in four "dividends". Finally it sets out how potential can be converted into growth drivers, and closes with remarks on method.

Yuan holds that tapping potential is both a lesson from past experience and a guide for future work. The article cites an economy of about 140 trillion yuan in 2025, final consumption contributing close to 60% of growth in 2021–2024, and per capita GDP of 13,445 US dollars in 2024. It links potential to the goal of reaching the level of a moderately developed country by 2035 and to building the new development pattern. The four dividends are institutional (the leadership of the Communist Party and the capacity to concentrate resources), market (over 1.4 billion people and more than 400 million middle-income earners), industrial (the most complete industrial system in the world, in the author's account) and talent (about 860 million working-age people and rising education levels).

To convert advantages into momentum, Yuan proposes four lines of work: build a high-level socialist market economy and a unified national market; expand domestic demand on both the consumption and investment sides; drive industrial innovation through scientific and technological innovation, including key technologies and emerging industries; and link education, science and technology, and talent in a virtuous circle. The author calls for strategic, systemic and bottom-line thinking and for coordinating short- and long-term, macro and micro policies. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese economists frame "economic potential" at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: China's economy is large in volume, and large also in potential.
quoteZh: 中国经济，大在体量，也大在潜能。

glossary.explanation: An annual closed-door meeting of Party and state leaders, held at the end of the year, that reviews economic performance and sets the policy agenda for the next year.
An official formulation since 2017 that shifts the emphasis from speed of growth to quality, efficiency, innovation and balance.
A strategy announced in 2020 that centres on the "domestic big circulation", with domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other.

t: The meaning and paths of industrial innovation during the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: “十五五”时期产业创新的内涵与路径
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in January 2026, Shi Jianxun takes up the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). The article asks how industrial innovation, the step that turns scientific and technological innovation into real productive forces, should be understood and advanced in 2026–2030.
