Shi argues that it is a key lever for avoiding "involution-style" competition and for responding to external suppression, and that it must be coordinated with technological innovation and regional development.

The commentary is organised under five headings: the content and driving logic of industrial innovation; science and technology as its lead; its link to regional development; integration into international industrial and supply chains; and the improvement of the development environment. It draws throughout on wording from the Plan recommendations, such as implementing an "industrial innovation project", building a modern industrial system and developing new quality productive forces.

Shi first sets out six forms of industrial innovation: creating new industries from scratch, upgrading traditional ones with advanced technology, restructuring through industrial transfer, new cooperation models such as clusters and ecosystems, better industrial policy and capacity governance, and innovation arising from international division of labour. Four forces drive it: market demand, technological innovation, industrial competition and policy. Shi then argues that technological innovation is the endogenous driver and industrial innovation its realisation of value. Shi acknowledges gaps in key core technologies and calls for breakthroughs in integrated circuits, industrial machine tools and high-end instruments, with enterprises as the main innovators. Regions should avoid blind duplication of projects and develop in complementary ways according to their endowments, and China should integrate more deeply into global supply chains, including through the Belt and Road Initiative.

Shi concludes that, because industrial innovation demands heavy investment, long cycles and high risk, the state must set strategy, back basic research and build a favourable environment. Shi calls for a unified national market, stronger intellectual property protection, a shift of industrial policy from selective to inclusive and functional forms, and capacity governance with anti-monopoly enforcement and early-warning systems to curb disorderly expansion. Read the original if you want a concise, policy-oriented statement of how the 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations frame industrial innovation and its links to technology, regions and global supply chains.
quoteEn: Technological innovation is the endogenous driving force of industrial innovation, and industrial innovation is the realisation of the value of technological innovation.
quoteZh: 科技创新是产业创新的内生动力，产业创新是科技创新的价值实现。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 for productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging and future industries, as opposed to resource-intensive growth.
An official term for intense, often price-cutting competition that yields little real gain and leads to overcapacity and falling profits. It has been targeted in policy since 2024–2025.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030. The Party's recommendations for it were adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in October 2025.

An official goal of an industrial structure that is technologically advanced, integrated and anchored in the real economy, and that includes manufacturing, strategic emerging industries and future industries.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: Building a solid foundational and strategic support for the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 筑牢新质生产力发展的基础性战略性支撑
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 6 January 2026, asks how education, science and technology, and talent can be advanced as one integrated whole to support new quality productive forces. Liu Hongda takes up the question in light of the 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) and the 2025 Central Economic Work Conference. Liu argues that such integration is the foundational and strategic base for developing new quality productive forces.

The piece first sets out the concept and its context of technological revolution and industrial restructuring. It then diagnoses obstacles to integration and closes with three sets of measures: top-level design, collaborative integration and evaluation reform.

Liu defines new quality productive forces as a leap in labourers, means of labour, objects of labour and their combination, driven mainly by technological breakthroughs. On this basis Liu casts education as the foundation, science and technology as the core element and talent as the primary resource. Liu identifies breaks between the innovation, industrial and talent chains: barriers to the flow of resources, weak links between university programmes and industry, limited corporate leadership in innovation, and poor conversion of research results into industry.

Liu proposes coordination mechanisms and legislation, innovation consortia of universities, research institutes and leading firms, and decentralised decision-making over research. The author also calls for a pyramid-shaped talent pipeline and multi-party evaluation that moves away from fixation on scores, diplomas and papers. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official-aligned scholarship links the new quality productive forces agenda to education and talent policy.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are mainly generated by revolutionary technological breakthroughs, and scientific and technological innovation is the core element in developing them.
quoteZh: 新质生产力主要由技术革命性突破催生而成，科技创新是发展新质生产力的核心要素。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and high efficiency, as an engine of high-quality development.

t: Basic characteristics and development direction of the modern industrial system
zh: 现代化产业体系基本特征与发展方向
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in January 2026, Zhang Hui asks how China should build a modern industrial system during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Zhang takes the recommendations adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) as the starting point. The article argues that the system should develop along three directions, intelligentization, greening and integration, and should end up complete, advanced and secure. The author presents this as the material and technological basis of Chinese modernization and as a way to break development bottlenecks and gain strategic initiative in international competition.

The commentary has four main sections. The first three take intelligentization, greening and integration in turn. Each sets out current achievements, remaining difficulties and a list of proposed measures. The fourth section turns to the three qualities of completeness, advancement and security, and to the directions for further work. Evidence includes China's new energy vehicle output in 2024, which the author gives as over 12 million units, and the claim that traditional industries account for about 80 per cent of manufacturing.

Zhang presents intelligentization as the key to replacing old growth drivers with new ones, through the deep fusion of artificial intelligence and the real economy. The author lists obstacles: dependence on foreign core technologies, shallow digital transformation in traditional industry, and small firms that are unwilling, afraid or unable to change. Greening is described as a route to high-quality development and the dual-carbon goals, with the new energy vehicle chain as the model. Integration covers services in manufacturing, science with industry, and the real with the digital economy, and calls for equal attention to upgrading traditional sectors and fostering emerging and future ones. Completeness is called the foundation, advancement the key and security the bottom line, and the three are said to depend on one another.

Zhang concludes that these three directions must be pursued together under a systems approach. The approach would combine technological innovation, industrial policy, institutions and opening up, and would balance development with security. Proposals include basic AI research, open application scenarios, a unified data market, a standard for product carbon footprints, and rebuilding the industrial base. The author expects a systemic change in quality, efficiency and drivers of growth, laying a material and technological foundation for a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned economist's statement of the policy agenda for industrial upgrading under the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: The integrated development of the industrial system is a notable feature and development trend of the modern industrial system.
quoteZh: 产业体系的融合化发展，是现代化产业体系的显著特征和发展趋势。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept for an industrial structure that is technologically advanced, complete and secure. It is treated in Party documents as the material basis of Chinese modernization and of economic modernization.
The official name for China's path to modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
The official goal for China's economy since 2017, emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, whose recommendations were adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in 2025.

t: Resolutely block any attempt to revive Japanese militarism
st: Interview with Hu Dekun, senior professor of humanities and social sciences at Wuhan University
zh: 坚决阻击任何妄想复活日本军国主义的图谋——访武汉大学人文社会科学资深教授胡德坤
paras: This is an interview in Guangming Daily in which reporter Zhou Xiaofei questions Hu Dekun, a senior professor at Wuhan University, about remarks on Taiwan by Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae. The interview presents the remarks as a sign that Japanese militarism has not disappeared. Hu argues that they echo a long tradition of aggression and breach the postwar international legal order.

The interview has five questions. They cover the historical roots of the remarks, earlier cases where Japan invoked a "survival crisis" to justify war, the suffering caused by Japanese aggression, the international and bilateral legal documents Takaichi's words allegedly violate, and the measures the international community should take.

Hu traces Japanese militarist thought from Toyotomi Hideyoshi's plans against Korea and China, through Tokugawa-era scholars and Yoshida Shōin, to the Meiji state's expansion. In his account, the Allied Tokyo Trial and the American occupation reforms removed its basis, but Cold War "support" for Japan let right-wing revisionism survive. He gives the Mukden Incident, the Marco Polo Bridge Incident and Pearl Harbor as cases of "survival crisis" and "self-defence" pretexts. He says Takaichi's link between a "Taiwan contingency" and Japan's survival repeats this rhetoric. He also argues that the Cairo Declaration, the Potsdam Proclamation and the Japanese Instrument of Surrender, together with four China–Japan political documents, make the remarks illegal and contrary to Japan's "peace constitution".

Hu proposes three responses. The first is stronger international supervision and legal restraint, working through the United Nations. The second is historical warning, with Chinese scholars continuing to expose and rebut right-wing revisionism. The third is a public statement of China's resolve to defend its sovereignty and unification. He concludes that the international community should draw on the wartime anti-fascist alliance to block any attempt to revive militarism. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese historian in an official newspaper frames the 2025–26 dispute over Takaichi's Taiwan remarks, and which historical and legal arguments he uses.
quoteEn: The question of Japan's war responsibility is both a historical question and a real-world one.
quoteZh: 日本的战争责任问题，既是历史问题，也是现实问题。

t: Coordinating development and security to better serve the overall work of the Party and the state
zh: 统筹发展和安全 更好服务党和国家工作大局
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2026, takes up Xi Jinping's recent instruction that central state-owned enterprises should better serve the overall work of the Party and the state and coordinate development with security. Wang Peng argues that these enterprises are not ordinary market actors but a pillar of both the economy and national security, and that their role matters for building a national security barrier and advancing Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. It first reviews what central enterprises do in key security fields, then explains why they can act as a backbone, and finally sets out tasks for the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

Wang lists contributions in food, energy, industrial and supply chains, finance, cyber and information security, and the ecological environment. The structural explanation rests on three dimensions. Domestically, state ownership and governance place national goals and the public interest first, allowing long-term investment in strategic sectors. Internationally, the enterprises carry out Belt and Road projects and protect overseas interests. In technology, they can organise large innovation consortia to overcome "chokepoint" problems that other firms cannot replace.

Wang calls for six lines of action: embedding Party leadership in corporate governance and pursuing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party; focusing on core business in line with national strategy; strengthening the real economy and industrial chains; driving innovation towards technological self-reliance; building comprehensive risk management; and deepening state-enterprise reform towards world-class firms. Read the original if you want a concise official-style account of how the state-owned sector's security role is framed ahead of the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Central enterprises are not ordinary market actors: their operations are deeply integrated into national strategy, and at critical moments they can mobilise resources and overcome difficulties, making them the most trustworthy force for safeguarding core national interests and meeting major risks and challenges.
quoteZh: 中央企业并非一般市场主体，其运营深度融入国家战略，在关键时刻能够调集资源、攻坚克难，是维护国家核心利益、应对重大风险挑战最可信赖的力量。

glossary.explanation: Large enterprises owned by the central government and supervised by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, concentrated in strategic sectors such as energy, telecoms and heavy industry.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's campaign to strengthen discipline, organisation and anti-corruption work, promoted since 2012.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030.

t: Upholding the organic unity of law-based governance of the country and rule-based governance of the Party
zh: 坚持依法治国和依规治党有机统一
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 12 January 2026, Ma Huaide takes up the principle, listed as the twelfth of the "twelve upholds" in the 2025 edition of the Study Outline on Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, that governing the country by law and governing the Party by its own rules must form an organic unity. Ma argues that this is a landmark judgement, which shows what distinguishes the socialist rule-of-law path with Chinese characteristics and deepens the Party's understanding of how a communist party governs.

The article follows the Study Outline's own logic in four steps. It first sets out how the two forms of governance complement each other, then examines law-based governance of the country, then rule-based governance of the Party, and finally the linking of Party discipline with law enforcement. Throughout, Ma draws heavily on Xi Jinping's statements.

Ma's central claim is that the two are complementary in four respects. They share an origin, since both Party policy and state law express the fundamental will of the people. They share a goal, the modernization of national governance. Their functions differ, with state law setting the bottom line of conduct and Party regulations setting a higher bar. And in practice they depend on each other, above all through the "critical minority" of leading cadres. Law-based governance gives Party rules a foundation and external oversight, while rule-based governance, built on the Party Constitution and the principle that discipline is stricter than law and comes before it, is said to lead and secure the rule of law. Ma notes problems in enforcement, such as selective or watered-down implementation of Party regulations. The article also credits the reform of the national supervision system, adopted at the 19th Party Congress (2017), with joining Party discipline and state supervision into one system. It says this system strengthens deterrence, preventive controls and cadres' self-discipline against corruption.

Ma concludes that combining the Party's discipline inspection with the enforcement of state law turns institutional advantages into governance effectiveness. He calls for the system to be kept and improved so that it supports Chinese modernization, national strength and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a representative, authoritative statement of how Party-discipline and state-law frameworks are meant to fit together in official theory after the 2025 Central Conference on law-based governance.
quoteEn: Upholding their organic unity means making the process of comprehensively governing the country by law a process of deepening and extending full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and making the process of governing the Party by rules a process of consolidating and raising the rule-of-law mindset and methods.
quoteZh: 坚持二者有机统一，就是要使全面依法治国的过程成为全面从严治党深化拓展的过程，使依规治党的过程成为法治思维和法治方式巩固提升的过程

glossary.literal: governing the Party according to regulations
glossary.explanation: The practice of managing the Party through intra-Party regulations, including the Party Constitution and discipline rules. It has been emphasised since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and is paired with governing the country by law.

glossary.literal: governing the country according to law
glossary.explanation: The Party's basic strategy for running the state through the legal system under Party leadership. It was placed in the "Four-Pronged Comprehensive Strategy" in 2014.
Formal rules issued by the Party to bind its organisations and members. They are distinct from state law and, in official theory, stricter than it.

glossary.pinyin: jì yán yú fǎ, jì zài fǎ qián
glossary.en: discipline is stricter than law and comes before it
glossary.literal: discipline stricter than law, discipline ahead of law
glossary.explanation: A principle that Party discipline sets a higher standard than state law and should be applied first, so that violations are caught before they become legal offences.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on law and governance formally put forward in November 2020 at the Central Conference on law-based governance. It is part of Xi Jinping Thought.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law

t: Digital public governance: practice and frontiers
zh: 数字公共治理的实践与前沿
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily, Yu Jianxing asks where digital public governance is heading, what limits constrain it, and how its future should be shaped. Yu defines it as public governance in the digital age. It covers governing by means of technology, governing technology itself, and managing the tension between technological logic and public-value logic. Against the background of building a Digital China, Yu argues that the frontier of contemporary public governance is shifting towards this field, and that the future should be shaped by placing people at the centre.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out four directions and trends: the knowledge base, methodology, relations among governing actors, and the governance ecology. The second identifies four sets of limits: those of the technology itself, of instrumental rationality, of institutional adaptation, and of governance logic. The third proposes four ways of putting people at the centre.

On trends, Yu describes a shift from experience-based induction to a data–modelling–simulation chain. Policy moves from linear reasoning and after-the-fact summary to prediction, experiment and digital twins. Actors move from a single centre to a multi-dimensional set that includes technology itself, and governance moves from network logic to ecological logic. On limits, Yu points to data distortion, algorithmic bias, systemic risk, blurred accountability, the efficiency paradox, standardisation that excludes the elderly or digitally unskilled, and the illusion of a single optimal solution. Yu adds institutional lag behind rapid technical iteration and difficulty in ranking conflicting values. Yu concludes that these limits erode the centrality of the human being in governance.

Yu proposes recognising human diversity, treating people as the end of governance, cultivating "public persons" (gonggongren), and raising digital governance capacity. Concretely, Yu calls for informed consent, human channels in social assistance, outcome-oriented evaluation indicators, and humanities education for technology developers. Yu also wants lower barriers to public data and computing power so as to stimulate creativity. Yu describes the frontier as an endless one of reshaping order between technology and values. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese academic framing of digital governance that links trends, limits and a human-centred normative agenda.
quoteEn: Placing people at the centre of digital public governance matters for guarding against risks and maintaining order, but more important is to stimulate human creativity through institutional design and technological application.
quoteZh: 把人置于数字公共治理的中心，防范风险或维持秩序固然重要，但更重要的是通过制度设计和技术应用激发人的创造性。

glossary.explanation: A national strategy for building China's digital economy, digital government and digital society, promoted in official documents since the late 2010s.
Virtual replicas of physical systems or places, used here to test policy options in simulated environments before real-world implementation.
The author's term for individuals who understand public affairs, take public responsibility and take part actively in governance through institutions and digital platforms.

t: Building a new security architecture requires adhering to systems thinking
zh: 构建新安全格局需要坚持系统思维
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily after the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), Yuan Zhenlong asks how China should build the "new security architecture" the plenum called for. The commentary argues that this requires the Marxist method of systems thinking, guided by the holistic national security outlook. Yuan holds that security issues are now so complex and interlinked that fragmented governance no longer suffices.

The piece has two parts. The first defines systems thinking, with its stress on wholeness, coordination and dynamism, and sets out three applications. The second turns these into an action framework with three features: coordination of all elements, governance of the whole chain and use of all means.

In Yuan's account, holistic thinking builds a "big security" system. It treats political, economic, technological and biological security as one organic whole, with political security as the foundation. Coordinated thinking links many actors: departments, regions and the military and local authorities in disaster relief. Dynamic thinking sets up a closed loop of early warning, response during an incident and post-incident evaluation, supported by big data and AI. Yuan then proposes consolidating the institutional system under the National Security Law, shifting governance down to communities, and strengthening regional joint prevention and security for the Belt and Road Initiative. The commentary also proposes risk assessment at source, algorithm-based warning and drills, ideological security work, a "chain leader" system for industrial chains, quantum and blockchain applications for cybersecurity, and a fuller body of security law.

Yuan concludes that systems thinking must become an executable and assessable framework, so that national security governance becomes more scientific, precise and efficient. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-aligned scholars translate the holistic national security outlook into governance recommendations.
quoteEn: Security risks are transmissible and coupled and are constantly changing, which requires us to use dynamic thinking to build a closed-loop security governance mechanism of early warning, response during the incident and post-incident evaluation.
quoteZh: 安全风险具有传导性和耦合性等特点，处在不断的发展变化过程中，这要求我们运用动态性思维，建立“事前预警—事中处置—事后评估”的安全治理闭环机制。

glossary.explanation: A security doctrine introduced by Xi Jinping in 2014. It covers political, economic, technological, cultural, biological and other domains of security together, and treats security and development as linked.
A phrase from the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee, which called for speeding up its construction as part of modernizing the national security system and capabilities.
A method presented as Marxist that examines things as interconnected wholes. The author stresses wholeness, coordination and dynamism.
China's international economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, covering infrastructure and trade links with many countries.
A governance practice in which a designated official or leading enterprise takes responsibility for the stability and security of a particular industrial chain.

t: The scientific connotation of high-efficacy governance and paths to advance it
zh: 高效能治理的科学内涵与推进路径
paras: Mao Peijin takes up the concept of high-efficacy governance (高效能治理), which Xi Jinping stressed in April and May 2025 in connection with planning for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. This newspaper commentary asks what the concept means and how it can be advanced. Mao argues that it is a necessary part of modernizing national governance and a guarantee of high-quality development. It also underpins a dynamic balance between development quality, governance effectiveness and security resilience, which Mao links to Chinese modernization.

The article is organised in four parts. The first three define high-efficacy governance through three pairings: effective results with efficient process, a sound governance system with strong governance capacity, and high-quality development with high-level security. The last part sets out practical measures under four headings: technological empowerment, sound governance mechanisms, stronger rule-of-law guarantees, and coordinated, joint action.

Mao defines governance efficacy as the unity of effect (the degree to which goals are achieved) and efficiency (the ratio of input to output), and says the two must improve together rather than simply be added up. The article describes a dual logic: top-level design that gives continuity and authority, combined with enough flexibility to adjust to new problems. As an example, Mao cites the national economic and social development planning system, in which the Party Central Committee proposes, the State Council drafts and the National People's Congress approves. Mao sees this as joining long-term strategic stability to short-term policy flexibility, and as an advantage of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Mao also treats system and capacity as mutually reinforcing, and argues that high-efficacy governance supplies order for development and institutional tools for security, through risk prevention, process control and emergency response.

For implementation, Mao proposes digital platforms and data governance, with attention to algorithmic fairness, privacy and the digital divide. Mao also calls for developing the "Fengqiao experience" and grid-based grassroots governance, new legislation and closer links between administrative enforcement and criminal justice, and a governance community of shared responsibility. The commentary also proposes an evaluation system built on mutual assessment among governance actors, with third-party review. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Central Party School scholar presents high-efficacy governance in official policy language.
quoteEn: High-efficacy governance is not a simple addition of governance effect and governance efficiency, but the synergistic improvement of the two.
quoteZh: 高效能治理并非治理效果和治理效率的简单叠加，而是二者的协同提升

glossary.explanation: A term in current Party discourse for governance that is both effective in outcomes and efficient in process. Xi Jinping stressed it in 2025 alongside high-quality development.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models. It has been a central slogan since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth that is innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared.
A grassroots dispute-resolution model that began in Fengqiao, Zhejiang, in the 1960s. The Party now promotes it, in updated form, as a way to settle conflicts locally with mass participation.

t: Raising quality and expanding capacity: strategic priorities for higher education in the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: 提质扩容：“十五五”时期高等教育战略重点
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily (6 January 2026), Li Liguo takes up a line from the proposals adopted by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) for the 15th Five-Year Plan: promote "raising quality and expanding capacity" (tízhì kuòróng) in higher education and enlarge enrolment in high-quality undergraduate programmes. Li argues that this is one of the strategic priorities of higher education for 2026–2030, a concrete expression of "investing in people", and an essential requirement if higher education is to serve high-quality development and Chinese modernization.

The commentary is short and organised in five parts. It first explains why quality-plus-expansion is necessary, then links it to the shift from investing in things to investing in people. Three further sections set out what it must be combined with: restructuring the pattern of talent training, adjusting the disciplines and majors on offer, and optimising the geographical and institutional layout of universities.

Li's core reasoning is that growth must be "connotative" rather than a simple increase in numbers. According to the author, China has built the world's largest higher education system, yet school-age cohorts will keep growing during the period before ageing and low birth rates bite, so the aim is to turn a demographic dividend into a talent dividend. Li cites 2024 figures: vocational and junior-college enrolment exceeds 50% of intake, postgraduates number 4.0954 million of 48.46 million students (under 10%), and the 147 "Double First-Class" universities account for under 6% of undergraduate admissions through the national examination. Developed countries, Li notes, typically have 20% or more postgraduates. The author therefore calls for moving from a "pyramid" to an "olive-shaped" structure.

Li further urges expansion only in disciplines tied to national strategy, emerging and future industries and universities' own strengths, with early warning for weak programmes and more autonomy for universities to set up new interdisciplinary fields. On layout, Li notes that ministry-run universities are under 5% of institutions and calls for differentiated development of research, applied and skills-oriented universities, with high-quality resources tilted towards central, western and local institutions. Read the original if you want a concise statement, by a Tsinghua education scholar, of how the 15th Five-Year Plan's higher education priorities are being interpreted, with the enrolment figures the author cites.
quoteEn: This growth is by no means a simple increase in numbers or extensive expansion; its core is to use raising quality and expanding capacity as an opportunity to promote connotative development of higher education, giving equal weight to quality and quantity and lifting both together.
quoteZh: 这种增长绝非简单的数量增长和外延扩张，其核心在于以提质扩容为契机，促进和实现高等教育内涵式发展，实现“质”“量”并重、协同跃升。

glossary.explanation: A phrase used in the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan for higher education, meaning enlarging places in good institutions while improving standards.
A policy slogan in the 15th Five-Year Plan proposals stressing spending on education, health and skills rather than mainly on physical infrastructure.
A national programme launched in 2015 to build world-class universities and disciplines, designating a list of universities for extra funding.
The official term for the Party's model of modernization, prominent in Party documents since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official economic goal stressing quality, innovation and efficiency over scale of growth, made the central theme in the Party's recent planning.

t: Intelligentization, greening and integration: directions for building a modern industrial system
zh: 智能化、绿色化、融合化：现代化产业体系的构建方向
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily takes up the recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan adopted by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). That document names intelligentization, greening and integration as the direction for building a modern industrial system, which it calls the material and technological basis of Chinese modernization. Wang and Zhang argue that the three must be understood both individually and in their mutual connections, because they work as an organic whole rather than as three parallel goals.

The article has four sections. The first defines each of the three; the second sets out their logical interaction; the third proposes practical paths; the fourth lists supporting safeguards. It is a policy-oriented piece that draws on official documents and gives examples from new energy vehicles, photovoltaics, smart agriculture and platform business.

In the authors' account, intelligentization is the technological engine and the core driver of new quality productive forces. Greening is the value orientation and the backdrop of high-quality development. Integration is the structural feature, a systemic change in how industries are organised and how value is created, not mere "physical stacking". The core argument is that each empowers the other two. Intelligent technologies supply tools for green transition and act as a "binder" of integration. Green standards and carbon constraints push firms towards intelligent technology and spawn hybrid models such as "photovoltaics plus agriculture". Integration opens new application scenarios and spreads green technology across sectors. From a systems perspective, the authors describe a positive feedback loop whose combined effect exceeds simple addition, which they present as an application of systems thinking and dialectics.

The authors propose five practical paths: stronger top-level design and coordination; market-based allocation of factors such as data; breakthroughs in core technologies through the new-type whole-nation system; demonstration zones and pilot cases; and standards with inclusive, prudent regulation. Safeguards include deeper reform, fiscal, tax and financial support, international cooperation and institutional opening up, and broader social consensus and talent training. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Chinese policy commentators link technology upgrading, decarbonisation and cross-sector integration in the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Integration is not a simple "physical stacking", but a systemic transformation of how industry is organised and of the logic of value creation.
quoteZh: 融合化不是简单的“物理叠加”，而是产业组织方式和价值创造逻辑的系统性变革。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022). The article calls the modern industrial system its material and technological basis.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023. It denotes innovation-driven productive forces based on advanced technology and high efficiency.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth that stresses quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
A model of mobilising state, market and research resources nationally for major scientific and technological breakthroughs. It adapts the earlier whole-nation system to a market economy.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030.

t: The three inherent determinations of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的三重内在规定性
paras: Zhao Jianying asks what makes Chinese modernization qualitatively different from Western modernization. Drawing on the Marxist idea that every thing has an inherent qualitative determination (neizai guidingxing), the article argues that Chinese modernization is defined by three such determinations: value, history and culture. It builds on Xi Jinping's statement that Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party and on the five features set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

The piece, published in the Guangming Daily, is organised in three sections, one for each determination. The first treats the value dimension and the aim of free and all-round human development. The second traces the historical dimension from the late Ming and the Opium War era through the Party's founding, the Mao period, reform and opening up, and the years since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The third examines the cultural dimension through three components: fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture.

On value, Zhao holds that the aim of human emancipation and free and all-round development comes from Marxism and from the Party's founding mission, and that it sets a people-centred "human-oriented logic" against what the author calls the "logic of capital" in Western modernization. On history, the author argues that Chinese modernization is the necessary outcome of six overlapping histories, including those of the Party, modern China, world socialism and Chinese civilization. In this account, peasant uprisings, reformism and the bourgeois republic all failed, so the task fell to the Party. On culture, Zhao says the three cultural strands feed one another. The author presents their fusion through the Two Integrations as a "chemical reaction" between Marxism and traditional culture that creates a new form of human civilization.

Zhao concludes that Chinese modernization follows the general laws of modernization while resting on China's own traditions and conditions. The author presents it as a historic transcendence of the Western model and a new option for developing countries. The article insists that Party leadership and the socialist path are the guarantee of its direction, and that historical and cultural confidence are needed. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party theorists distinguish Chinese from Western modernization along value, historical and cultural lines.
quoteEn: The cultural determination of Chinese modernization is, in essence, a profound "chemical reaction", grounded in practice, between the essence of Marxist thought and the best of fine traditional Chinese culture.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化的文化规定性，本质上是马克思主义思想精髓与中华优秀传统文化精华在实践基础上发生的深刻“化学反应”。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's path to modernization under Party leadership. The 20th Party Congress (2022) summarised its five Chinese features, and the term is presented as distinct from Western modernization.
The formula of integrating Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities (the first integration) and with fine traditional Chinese culture (the second integration, stressed since 2021–23).
The policy launched in 1978 of economic reform and opening to the outside world. Official history treats it as the start of the socialism with Chinese characteristics era.

t: The growth of Japanese militarism as a serious threat to the postwar international order
st: Interview with Zhang Haipeng, Academic Member of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
zh: 日本军国主义滋长是对战后国际秩序的严重威胁——访中国社会科学院学部委员张海鹏
paras: This is an interview, published in Guangming Daily on 5 January 2026, in which reporter Zhao Fan questions the historian Zhang Haipeng, an Academic Member of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. The occasion is Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae's statement in the Diet that a "Taiwan contingency" could constitute a "survival-threatening situation" permitting collective self-defence. Zhang argues that the claim repeats a long pattern of Japanese aggression justified by appeals to survival and self-defence, and that it threatens the postwar international order.

The interview moves through five questions. It first traces the history of Japan's "survival" rhetoric, then lists the crimes of Japanese militarism, then turns to the rightward drift of Japanese politics. It goes on to the international legal instruments Takaichi's remarks are said to breach, and ends with how the international community should respond.

Zhang's central move is historical. He cites the "line of sovereignty" and "line of interest" doctrine of 1890, Tanaka Giichi's 1927 Eastern Conference and the "lifeline" language of the early 1930s. In his account, these terms were pretexts for the Mukden Incident and the wider war, so "survival crisis" is a synonym for aggression. He then reads Takaichi's statement against the Cairo Declaration, the Potsdam Proclamation, the Japanese Instrument of Surrender, the 1972 Sino-Japanese Joint Statement and the UN Charter's "enemy state" clauses (Articles 53, 77 and 107). He concludes that Japan has no right of collective self-defence and that Taiwan's return to China has a firm basis in international law. He also describes a long rightward trend, from Yasukuni visits and textbook revisions to attempts to revise Article 9 of the constitution.

Zhang calls for the international community to return to the positions of the Cairo Declaration, the Potsdam Proclamation and the UN Charter. He says China, as a victim state, a signatory to those documents and a permanent member of the Security Council, is entitled to issue an international warning. He proposes four areas of monitoring: Japan's adherence to the 1945 surrender terms, its respect for the "peace constitution", the composition and budget of its Self-Defence Forces, and its compliance with the Potsdam territorial provisions. Read the original if you want to see how a leading Chinese historian frames the Takaichi controversy in historical and legal terms for a Chinese official audience.
quoteEn: Looking back at history, raising banners such as the so-called "right to survival", "self-defence" or "survival crisis" has been Japan's habitual trick for launching foreign aggression.
quoteZh: 回顾历史，打出所谓“生存权”“自卫”或者“存亡危机”这样的旗号，是日本发动对外侵略的惯用伎俩。

t: Understanding the operating mechanisms and key advantages of China's Five-Year Plans
zh: 深刻理解我国五年规划的作用机制和重要优势
paras: Yang Yongheng, writing in People's Daily on the eve of the 15th Five-Year Plan period, asks how China's Five-Year Plans actually work and why they count as an institutional strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article argues that, since the move to a socialist market economy, the plans have changed from purely mandatory plans into strategic, macro-level and policy-oriented guidance. Yang contends that their effect rests on three mechanisms: consensus, guidance and balance.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's statement that formulating and continuously implementing Five-Year Plans is an important Party experience in governance. It then takes each mechanism in turn, illustrating it with examples from the 14th and 15th Five-Year Plan drafting processes, and ends with a short assessment of the plans' wider significance. It is a commentary built on Xi's remarks and official documents, not an empirical study.

On consensus, Yang distinguishes scientific, political and social consensus. Scientific consensus comes from expert research, such as the 200-plus projects commissioned for the 14th plan; political consensus comes from drafting the Central Committee's proposals under Xi's leadership with several rounds of consultation; and social consensus comes from channels such as the online consultation for the 15th plan, which the article says drew over 3 million submissions. On guidance, Yang says the plans give the public information, steer government departments through targets, task allocation and evaluation, send signals to businesses (carbon peaking and neutrality targets, platform-economy regulation) and shape individual expectations. On balance, the plans are said to handle five relationships: government and market, domestic and international, short and long term, economic and spatial development, and whole and part.

Yang concludes that China is the only country to have sustained Five-Year Plans while achieving rapid growth and long-term social stability. The article presents the plans as an institutional innovation that has helped shape the socialist market economy, and says they offer ideas to both developing and developed countries on handling the state–market relationship. Read the original if you want an official-leaning, scholar-authored account of how Chinese planning is described as working in the lead-up to the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: The development of the Five-Year Plans is a process in which the consensus, guidance and balance mechanisms have continually evolved and matured.
quoteZh: 五年规划的发展历程，是共识机制、引导机制和平衡机制不断演进并日趋成熟的过程

glossary.explanation: China's medium-term national development blueprints, first issued in 1953. The 15th covers 2026–2030, and the plans are now strategic guidance rather than mandatory production quotas.
The official description of China's economic system since the 1990s. It combines market allocation of resources with state leadership and public ownership.
The Communist Party's official name for its path and system since the reform era.

t: Understanding the global significance of China's path, China's governance and China's principles
zh: 深刻把握中国之路中国之治中国之理的世界意义
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 8 January 2026, Liu Haixing, identified as head of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee, takes up the Proposals adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Liu argues that the Proposals embody a "China's path, China's governance and China's principles" that is distinctive and also benefits the world. The article calls on Party officials to explain this global significance to the international community and to project a good international image of the Communist Party of China.

The piece is built in three parts, each on one of the three terms. The first covers the path: socialism with Chinese characteristics, Chinese modernization and peaceful development. The second covers governance, which Liu defines as the Party's theory and experience of ruling the country. The third covers the principles, meaning the theory behind the path and governance. Throughout, Liu cites Xi Jinping and reports favourable remarks by foreign parties and politicians, especially from the Global South.

On the path, Liu contends that socialism with Chinese characteristics has moved world socialism to a new stage. Chinese modernization is said to break the equation of modernization with Westernization, and the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind are presented as public goods for the world. On governance, Liu draws four lessons for other parties: the Party's leadership core, a people-first orientation, the Party's self-reform, and long-term planning through successive five-year plans. Liu portrays foreign parties as caught in polarisation, electoral infighting and welfare populism, and says that replacing "capital logic" with "people's logic" offers an answer. On principles, Liu says Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, China's traditional culture and the Party's worldview should be explained abroad in internationally accessible language.

Liu concludes that the Party's external work will follow Xi Jinping Thought and Xi's diplomatic thought, and will keep strengthening the global network of party partnerships. Its aim is to explain the world significance of China's path, governance and principles, and so to support national rejuvenation and human progress. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how the Party's international liaison work frames China's experience for foreign parties at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Putting the people first, as the core value of China's governance, replaces capital logic with people's logic, fully transcends mistaken ideas such as "private interest first" and "capital first", and offers an answer to the development and governance problems of parties worldwide.
quoteZh: 人民至上作为理解中国之治的核心价值内涵，以人民逻辑取代资本逻辑，彻底超越“私利至上”“资本至上”等错误理念，为世界各国政党破解发展和治理难题提供了答案。

glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's model of modernization, developed in its own account from the 2020s. The article presents it as an alternative to Western-centred modernization.
An official formulation for the Party's efforts to correct itself and maintain its discipline without outside checks.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's flagship foreign-policy concept, which the Party presents as a vision for international relations and global governance.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.
A term for developing countries, used in Chinese official discourse to denote China's main international partners.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions.

t: Striving unremittingly to advance national defence and military modernization with high quality
st: Studying in depth Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China
zh: 为高质量推进国防和军队现代化不懈奋斗
zhSub: 深入学习《习近平谈治国理政》第五卷
authors: Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Strengthening the Military
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 29 December 2025, is a study guide to Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. It argues that national defence and military modernization are an integral part of Chinese modernization and a matter of paramount national importance. The authors present the three documents collected in the volume's twelfth section as the latest development of Xi Jinping Thought on Strengthening the Military, and call on the armed forces to study them together with Volumes I–V and the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025).

The text has three parts. The first explains why defence modernization belongs within Chinese modernization, drawing on China's modern history and the current international situation. The second sets out the strategic plan in the volume: the new 'three-step' strategy, the four modernizations, and the goal of a world-class military. The third lists tasks for opening a new phase: political strengthening, military governance, strategic capabilities in emerging fields, and the armed forces' role as a force the Party and people can trust.

The authors reason that a strong country requires a strong military, citing the 'century of humiliation' and Xi's remark that military backwardness has fatal consequences for national security. They also argue that China is a large but not yet strong power, that defence strength must match economic strength, and that technological and military revolutions are making warfare informatized and intelligent. Against this background they present the plan: a centenary goal for the army by 2027, basic modernization by 2035, and a world-class military by mid-century. They define the 2035 goal through four components: military theory, organizational form, personnel and weaponry.

The authors conclude that the armed forces must put the Party's absolute leadership first, through the Central Military Commission chairman responsibility system and continued political rectification. They also call for modernized military governance, closer integration of new quality productive forces with new quality combat strength, and constant combat readiness. They describe the plan as a blueprint for the next 20 to 30 years. Read the original if you want to see how official Chinese military-theory circles present defence modernization within Chinese modernization, and the priorities set for the armed forces.
quoteEn: A strong country must have a strong military, and national security depends on military strength; this is an iron law of the rise of the world's great powers.
quoteZh: 强国必须强军、军强才能国安，这是世界大国崛起的铁律。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, developed under Xi Jinping and stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is the organizing theme of Volume V of The Governance of China.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Strengthening the Military
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas on military affairs attributed to Xi Jinping. It is treated as the Party's guiding theory for national defence and army building.

glossary.en: Central Military Commission chairman responsibility system
glossary.explanation: The institutional arrangement under which the chairman of the Central Military Commission, currently Xi Jinping, takes overall responsibility for the armed forces. It is presented as the main way the Party's absolute leadership over the military is put into practice.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation. In the military context it is linked to 'new quality combat strength'.

t: The spirit and practical character of comprehensively deepening reform in the new era
st: Studying Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China in depth
zh: 新时代全面深化改革的精神特质和实践品格
zhSub: 深入学习《习近平谈治国理政》第五卷
authors: Office of the Commission for Deepening Overall Reform of the CPC Central Committee
paras: This study-guide article, published in the People's Daily by the office serving the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform, reads the reform material in Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China together with Volumes I–IV. It argues that Xi Jinping's leadership of comprehensive reform since the 18th Party Congress (2012) has a distinctive spirit and practical character. The article presents this as a historic undertaking of unprecedented difficulty and complexity.

The text is organised around eight dashed headings: steering and leadership, guidance by ideas, strategic planning, putting the people first, determined assault on hard problems, scientific advancement, and rigorous implementation. It draws on the Party's plenary sessions from the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It also cites reform examples in household registration, health care, education, population services, state-owned enterprises, ecological civilization and external challenges. A closing section briefly introduces the new thematic section on further comprehensively deepening reform.

The article's central claim is that the Party's overall leadership, and Xi's personal role, are the fundamental guarantee of reform. It notes that Xi chairs the commission, which was upgraded from a leading group in 2018, and has presided over more than seventy of its meetings. It says Xi's reform thinking forms the reform chapter of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, with principles such as reform led by the Party, centred on the people and guided by problem orientation. It also holds that reform follows the principle of neither returning to the closed old path nor taking the 'evil path' of changing course. In its account, reform is a 'revolution' aimed at institutions and vested interests. It lists achievements: the removal of drug mark-ups in public hospitals, unified urban and rural household registration, a strengthened Party role in state-owned enterprises, and more than thirty environmental laws and regulations. Method is summarised as combining top-level design with 'crossing the river by feeling the stones', using pilots, and following the maxim 'one part planning, nine parts implementation'.

The article concludes that no other country or party has carried out reform on such a scale, speed and intensity, and attributes this to the leadership of the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core and to Xi's thought. It calls on readers to study the latest theoretical results on reform and to push reform forward with greater historical initiative, so as to provide momentum and institutional guarantees for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Party commentary presents the reform record and its guiding principles at the close of 2025.
quoteEn: Reform is a revolution: it changes institutions and mechanisms and touches vested interests, so it cannot be carried out without real determination.
quoteZh: 改革是一场革命，改的是体制机制，动的是既得利益，不真刀真枪干是不行的。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The official formulation of China's path of development, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

The official name for the reform agenda launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2013. It covers economic, political, cultural, social, ecological, military and Party-building reforms.

glossary.zh: 中央全面深化改革委员会
glossary.en: Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform
glossary.explanation: A Party body chaired by Xi Jinping that reviews and coordinates major reform plans. It replaced the Central Leading Group for Comprehensively Deepening Reform in 2018.

t: Advancing education, science and technology, and talent development as one: accelerating high-level scientific and technological self-reliance
st: Studying in depth Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China
zh: 一体推进教育科技人才发展 加快实现高水平科技自立自强
zhSub: 深入学习《习近平谈治国理政》第五卷
authors: Party Leadership Group of the Ministry of Science and Technology
paras: This study-and-implementation article, written by the Party leadership group of the Ministry of Science and Technology, takes up the chapter on advancing education, science and technology, and talent as one whole in Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. It argues that Xi Jinping's statements on this theme are a new development of Marxism and a strategic support for Chinese modernization, and that they must be carefully studied and put into practice.

The text has three parts. The first sets out the meaning and significance of Xi's statements. The second reviews the practical basis built since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and states four general requirements. The third lists five major tasks for implementation, linked to the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) and the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

The authors present the integrated approach in three ways: as a development of Marxist productive-forces theory (citing Marx, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping on science and education), as a strategic step for high-quality development, and as a necessary response to a new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial change. They cite achievements such as higher education gross enrolment of 60.8%, 22 million talent resources in total and a rise in the national innovation ranking from 14th in 2020 to 10th in 2024. They also acknowledge structural mismatches: a shortage of top talent, engineering training detached from production, flawed evaluation, poor mobility and weak coordination. The four requirements are high-quality development as the goal, high-level scientific and technological self-reliance as the driver, training and use of scientific talent as the focus, and institutional innovation as the guarantee.

The authors call for strengthening Party leadership and coordination mechanisms, linking national strategic science and technology forces with talent training, and reforming discipline and engineer training around fields such as artificial intelligence and integrated circuits. They also call for systematic deployment of strategic talent, including young talent, and for evaluation and incentive reform, including "breaking the four onlys" and curbing reliance on academic titles. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how the Ministry of Science and Technology interprets and plans to implement the integrated education–science–talent policy, with the official data it cites.
quoteEn: Innovation-driven development is in essence talent-driven; a systemic outlook must be strengthened, the meaning and priorities of integrated advancement grasped accurately, and the training and use of scientific talent made the point where education, science and technology, and talent development meet.
quoteZh: 创新驱动本质上是人才驱动，必须增强系统观念，准确把握一体推进的内涵和重点，把培养使用科技人才作为教育科技人才一体发展的结合点

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official goal of the current development stage, stressing innovation, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth.

glossary.literal: high-level science and technology standing on its own feet and strengthening itself
glossary.explanation: An official goal of mastering key technologies independently, stressed in Party documents since the 2020 Fifth Plenum.
A reform slogan against evaluating researchers only by papers, titles, academic credentials and awards.

keywords: Xi Jinping: The Governance of China

t: Scientific and technological innovation and science popularisation as the two wings of innovation-driven development
zh: 科技创新、科学普及是实现创新发展的两翼
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily takes up Xi Jinping's formula that scientific and technological innovation and science popularisation are the "two wings" of innovation-driven development, and that popularisation should be given equal importance with innovation. Zhang and Qiao argue that building a leading science and technology power by 2035 requires sustained effort on popularisation as well as breakthroughs in research. They contend that the two must be planned and advanced together.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out a historical case: past scientific revolutions in the West and the course of China's own history, from the Yan'an period through the Mao era and reform and opening up to the present. The second argues that coordinated development is now imperative, citing statistics and policy measures. The third proposes how to form a "big science popularisation" pattern.

The authors present popularisation as the social foundation of innovation. They say China still faces "chokepoint" problems in key technologies, and that innovation must reach "to the sky" while popularisation takes root "on the ground". They point to a lingering habit of stressing research over popularisation. Citing national statistics, they report R&D spending in 2023 of 3,335.71 billion yuan against 21.506 billion yuan raised for popularisation work, and a citizen scientific literacy rate of 15.37% in 2024, which they say trails developed countries. Their remedy has three strands: institutional innovation that brings government, enterprises, universities and society together; a "popularisation plus" approach linking science to industry, education and culture; and wide public participation through science lectures, museums, school and community programmes, rural "5G cloud classrooms", and animation, short video and games.

Zhang and Qiao conclude that popularisation is both a foundational project for becoming a science and technology power and part of fully implementing the new development philosophy. They hold that only by pursuing innovation and popularisation together can China gain the commanding heights in the global technological revolution and advance Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated commentary links science popularisation policy, historical narrative and the 2035 science and technology goal.)
quoteEn: Without a general rise in the scientific literacy of the whole population, it is hard to create fertile soil for scientific and technological innovation.
quoteZh: 没有全民科学素质的普遍提升，就难以形成科技创新的丰沃土壤

glossary.explanation: A framework introduced in 2015 that stresses innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development. It is used as a guiding principle in Party economic policy.
The official term for China's path of modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
Public education in science and scientific thinking, known in China as kepu. It is governed by the Law on Science and Technology Popularization, revised in December 2024.

t: The grand historical outlook of contemporary Chinese Communists
zh: 当代中国共产党人的大历史观
paras: Huang Yibing, a deputy director of the Central Institute of Party History and Literature, explains the "grand historical outlook" (da lishiguan) that Xi Jinping has advanced since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The article, a theoretical commentary in Guangming Daily, argues that this outlook applies and develops the Marxist materialist conception of history in a creative way. It also presents the outlook as a sublation of traditional Chinese views of history and as an intellectual tool for Party members seeking to grasp their historical position and the direction of development.

The article is organised in four parts. The first sets out the outlook's scientific character through five features: objectivity, continuity, progress and subjectivity of the people. The second describes its broad perspective in time and space, and the third its deep historical logic, traced through Chinese civilisation, the history of socialism, modern China and the Party's own history. The fourth turns to its practical functions.

Huang's central claim is that the outlook rests on dialectical-materialist foundations while stretching the time-scale of analysis. On objectivity, Huang treats recognition of historical facts as the test that separates materialist from idealist history. Huang stresses that the "two historical periods", before and after reform and opening up, must not be set against each other. The outlook also places China's development within world history and within the long span of world socialism, which Huang says shows socialism with Chinese characteristics to be the unity of scientific socialism's theoretical logic and China's own historical logic. Huang adds that the people are both the makers and the final judges of history.

Huang concludes that the outlook gives practical guidance in four ways: grasping historical laws, grasping major trends, keeping historical patience and seizing the historical initiative. Huang links these to Chinese modernization, high-quality development, the Party's self-reform and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. The article presents the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation as a relay in which each generation must persevere while staying proactive. Read the original if you want an authoritative Party-history account of how the grand historical outlook is framed and justified within Xi Jinping's thought.
quoteEn: The grand historical outlook is the Chinese Communists' innovation, in keeping with fundamental principles, on the Marxist materialist conception of history in the new era.
quoteZh: 大历史观是新时代中国共产党人对马克思主义唯物史观的守正创新。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping has promoted since the 18th Party Congress, urging that China's development be viewed across long spans of time and in a world-historical frame.
The official term for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models and as a new form of human civilisation.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the outside world launched in 1978.
An official development goal stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, central to Xi-era Party-building discourse.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations and global governance.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal, framed as restoring China's strength and standing after the 'century of humiliation'.

t: Adhering to integrated protection and systematic governance: building a protection and governance framework from mountain peak to ocean
zh: 坚持一体化保护和系统治理 构建从山顶到海洋的保护治理大格局
paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 19 November 2025, asks how China should carry out integrated protection and systematic governance of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert. Zhang Bo argues that this approach puts into practice the idea that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets and expresses the force of Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilization.

The piece opens by grounding the approach in the Marxist view of universal connection and in Xi Jinping's idea of mountains, waters, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert as a community of life. It then sets out three working areas: top-level design, major ecological projects and technology-enabled supervision.

On top-level design, Zhang calls for a zoning-based control system covering all territory, one planning "map" that integrates ecological protection into economic and social plans, improved survey and monitoring systems, and cross-departmental platforms for sharing information and responsibility. On major projects, the author cites the 52 integrated protection and restoration projects and the national park system built since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and urges whole-life-cycle management of new projects. On supervision, Zhang stresses strict inspection under the Regulations on Ecological and Environmental Protection Inspections, holding local Party committees and governments responsible, and a monitoring network combining satellites, drones and sensors with big data and artificial intelligence for prediction and early warning.

Zhang concludes that planning through one map, implementing through one coordinated effort and supervising through one network will secure the protection and restoration of ecosystems as a whole and strengthen the national ecological security barrier. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present Xi Jinping's ecological thought and its institutional and technological measures.
quoteEn: Ecology is a unified natural system, an organic chain of interdependent and closely linked elements.
quoteZh: 生态是统一的自然系统，是相互依存、紧密联系的有机链条。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on environmental protection and development attributed to Xi Jinping and formalised in Party documents. It includes the principle that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets.

glossary.zh: 山水林田湖草沙一体化保护和系统治理
glossary.pinyin: shān shuǐ lín tián hú cǎo shā yītǐhuà bǎohù hé xìtǒng zhìlǐ
glossary.en: integrated protection and systematic governance of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert
glossary.explanation: An official policy principle treating land and water ecosystems as one interconnected whole to be protected and restored together rather than separately by sector.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: clear waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2005, holding that environmental protection and economic development are mutually reinforcing.

t: Opening up a new path for humanity's march towards modernization
zh: 开辟人类迈向现代化的新道路
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in November 2025, asks what kind of modernization path is open to developing countries and what Chinese modernization offers them. Zhang argues that the Western path is marked by structural flaws and cannot serve as a universal template. In Zhang's account, Chinese modernization, developed under the Communist Party's leadership, opens a new path and carries world significance.

The piece has three parts. It first criticises Western modernization, then traces how the Party explored Chinese modernization through revolution, construction and reform, up to the 20th Party Congress period and the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), which adopted proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan. The final and longest part sets out the global meaning of the Chinese path.

Zhang describes Western modernization as capital-centred and dependent on plunder. Citing Marx on primitive accumulation and Wallerstein's world-system theory, Zhang says it rests on extraction from the periphery, produces alienation and wealth polarisation, and shows weakening governance, financialisation and recurring crises, and hegemonism and interventionism. Against this, Zhang presents Chinese modernization as people-centred, with the Party ensuring long-term strategic stability, a socialist market economy, and an independent and complete national economic system.

Zhang concludes that Chinese modernization breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization and refutes the 'end of history' thesis. It offers developing countries lessons in independent development, people-centred aims and pragmatic reform, and it influences the world through the Belt and Road Initiative and the Global Development Initiative. Zhang holds that its world significance will grow, as a new form of human civilization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary contrasts Chinese modernization with the Western model for a developing-world audience.
quoteEn: The successful experience of Chinese modernization originates in China and belongs to the world.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化的成功经验源于中国，属于世界。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is characterised as modernization of a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation programme, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: The value of culture in empowering a new image for manufacturing, and ways to explore it
zh: 文化赋能制造业新形象的价值与探索
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 4 November 2025, asks how culture can help build a new image for Chinese manufacturing. Huang and Gu argue that integrating culture into manufacturing is a requirement of high-quality development. In their account it can move China from a large manufacturing country to a strong one, with products that are powerful yet elegant, efficient yet warm, and intelligent yet humane.

The authors start from Xi Jinping's statements on manufacturing as the foundation of the nation and on moving from "Made in China" to "Created in China". They then proceed in three steps: why culture and manufacturing must be combined, what cultural content shapes manufacturing competitiveness, and which practical routes can carry the idea forward. The core concept throughout is "manufacturing aesthetics" (zhizao meixue), presented as a form of soft power built on China's industrial hard power.

On the first point, Huang and Gu say the idea follows from the coordinated development of material and spiritual civilization. They also tie it to humanistic economics, to emotional consumption that values visual beauty and cultural meaning, and to new quality productive forces such as cultural equipment manufacturing and digital creative industries. On the second, they analyse manufacturing beauty in four dimensions: design, craftsmanship, production and the finished product. They claim that future competition is a contest over cultural narrative as well as technology, so that "Made in China" can carry national spirit. Their proposed routes are to refine the aesthetic quality of industry, to shape city brand images, and to carry forward cultural spirit. Under the first they list industrial-cluster culture, wider cultural-industry applications and exporting "product plus culture". Under the second they list reusing industrial heritage sites for theme parks and tourism. Under the third they list the craftsman spirit, a collective image of entrepreneurs and joint development of "people, industry, city and culture".

The authors conclude that culture should be the soul and craft the backbone of manufacturing, taking it from "making things" to "making beauty". They hold that this should follow a people-centred approach and let industrial civilization enter a new stage of high-quality development. The text is policy-oriented and largely programmatic, with little empirical evidence. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-aligned economic commentary links Xi Jinping's cultural thought, humanistic economics and industrial upgrading.
quoteEn: Future competition in manufacturing will be a contest not only of technology but even more of the power to shape cultural narrative.
quoteZh: 未来制造业竞争不仅是技术之争，更是文化叙事权之争。

glossary.explanation: The article's term for building aesthetic perception, cultural symbols and emotional experience into design, craft, production and products. It is presented as China's soft power in industry.
A concept in recent official discourse stressing that economic activity should be people-centred and attentive to quality of life, spiritual satisfaction and culture.
A term promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for innovation-led productive forces, often linked to advanced technology and new industries.
The official economic goal since the late 2010s, emphasising quality, innovation and efficiency over speed of growth alone.
A value promoted in official discourse: devotion to precision, quality and continual improvement in one's work.

t: Creating high-quality urban living spaces
zh: 营造高品质城市生活空间
