paras: This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 6 November 2025, asks how Chinese cities can build high-quality living spaces. Zhao Zheng, a researcher at the Development Research Center of the State Council, takes the July 2025 Central Urban Work Conference and the Party and State Council opinions on high-quality urban development as his starting point. He argues that cities must become livable, comfortable and convenient homes for all residents.

Zhao first explains why living-space quality matters and what it now means, then sets out three areas of work: housing, infrastructure and public services. Each area is illustrated with a local case, in Hangzhou, Chongqing and Sichuan.

In Zhao's account, urbanization is shifting from rapid growth to stable development, and cities from large-scale expansion to improving the quality and efficiency of existing stock. High-quality living space therefore needs a people-centred orientation. It combines "investing in things" (housing, roads, pipelines) with "investing in people" (education, healthcare, elderly care, childcare). On housing, Zhao calls for "good houses" and complete communities, together with the renovation of urban villages and old neighbourhoods. On infrastructure, he calls for upgrading underground pipelines and transport networks and building 5G and computing networks. On public services, he wants more balanced, higher-quality provision tailored to the elderly, young families and flexible workers.

Zhao concludes that these measures would turn policy aims into tangible living environments and support common prosperity. Read the original if you want a concise official-policy statement of the 2025 urban agenda, with brief Chinese case examples.
quoteEn: The quality of urban living space bears directly on the people's experience of a better life and is an important dimension of how well modern urban construction is performing.
quoteZh: 城市生活空间的品质，直接关系到人民群众的美好生活体验，是体现现代化城市建设成效的重要维度。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal that Xi Jinping's leadership has made central since 2021. It stresses more even distribution of wealth and services, including cultural and spiritual life.

t: Opening a new chapter in Chinese modernization with a spirit of historical initiative
zh: 以历史主动精神奋力开创中国式现代化建设新局面
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today on 30 October 2025, reads the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) through the idea of "historical initiative" (lishi zhudong). Lü Xinbin argues that modernization does not fall from the sky but has to be achieved through this spirit. In Lü's account, the plenum communiqué, Xi Jinping's work report and speech, and the Party's proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan embody it. The aim is to open a new chapter in Chinese modernization.

The article is organised around three kinds of initiative: theoretical, spiritual and practical. Each is tied to a pairing that Lü calls a unity: conformity to laws and purposiveness, historical consciousness and confidence in China, and strategic resolve and innovation. Lü presents these as one process of theoretical consciousness, spiritual self-strengthening and practical action, aimed at basically achieving socialist modernization. The piece ends with a short call to philosophy and social science researchers.

On theory, Lü says historical initiative rests on Marxist historical materialism. Historical actors must grasp objective laws and also use their agency to make history. The plenum's judgement that the 15th Five-Year Plan period is a critical one is said to reveal the internal laws of socialism with Chinese characteristics and Chinese modernization. On spirit, Lü links historical initiative to the Party's courage in self-reform, its habit of learning from history, and its pioneering outlook. Lü also stresses the creativity of the people, citing Xi's call to arouse the historical initiative of all the people.

On practice, Lü names three tasks. The first is shouldering the mission through continuity, holding to high-quality development and "one blueprint to the end". The second is seizing opportunity through reform, with Party leadership running through comprehensive deepening of reform. The third is guiding development with systems thinking, above all balancing development and security, so that high-quality development and high-level security reinforce each other. Lü concludes that social scientists should build historical initiative into studying and implementing the plenum's spirit. Read the original if you want an example of how official commentary frames the Fourth Plenum and the 15th Five-Year Plan in the language of historical initiative.
quoteEn: Modernization does not fall from the sky; it has to be achieved by promoting the spirit of historical initiative.
quoteZh: 现代化不会从天上掉下来，而是要通过发扬历史主动精神干出来。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse. It means consciously grasping historical laws and trends and acting on them, rather than waiting passively for events.
The official term for China's development path, presented as distinct from Western modernization. It was elaborated mainly after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The official goal of growth based on quality, innovation and efficiency rather than speed alone. It is described as the primary task of the new stage.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2026–2030. The Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee adopted the Party's proposals for drawing it up.
The programme, launched in 2013, of extending reform across the economy, politics, society and Party-building. The article calls it the key move for the new era.

t: Continuing to expand higher-level opening up
zh: 持续扩大更高水平对外开放
paras: This newspaper commentary, published after the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), asks how China should expand high-level opening up during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Jin argues that opening up is a distinctive mark of Chinese modernization and that, over the next five years, China should focus on institutional opening up and key sectors to raise its opening to a new level.

The article has two parts. The first reviews achievements of the 14th Five-Year Plan period in four areas: foreign trade, two-way investment, institutional opening up and the Belt and Road Initiative. The second sets out four strategic directions for the coming period.

Jin cites figures such as goods trade ranking first globally for eight consecutive years, services trade passing 1 trillion US dollars, and over three-quarters of countries joining Belt and Road cooperation. Drawing on these, the author describes a shift from opening based on flows of goods and factors to opening based on rules, regulations, management and standards. The proposed directions are: expanding autonomous opening, from "passive adaptation" to "active design"; innovating trade by moving up value chains and expanding services and digital trade; widening two-way investment cooperation; and building the Belt and Road to higher quality, from a "bold sketch" to a "meticulous painting".

Jin concludes that, despite unilateralism, protectionism and hegemonism, China's determination to expand high-level opening and share development opportunities will not change. The author calls for a higher-level open economy system. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned summary of how Chinese economists frame the opening-up agenda for 2026–2030.
quoteEn: Over the next five years, we must grasp precisely the rich connotations of high-level opening up, take institutional opening up as the focus, concentrate on key areas, and proactively raise China's opening up to a new level.
quoteZh: 未来五年，我们要精准把握高水平开放的丰富内涵，以制度型开放为重点，聚焦关键领域，积极主动把我国对外开放提高到新水平。

glossary.explanation: Official Party term for China's own path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Opening that aligns domestic rules, regulations, management and standards with international ones, rather than only freeing flows of goods and capital.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
The 2026–2030 period of China's national medium-term economic and social development planning.

t: Building a powerful green engine for high-quality development
zh: 为高质量发展打造强劲绿色引擎
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily on 31 October 2025, responds to the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) and its proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan. Li Weiming argues that the goals of "new major progress" in building a Beautiful China and of a comprehensive green transformation of economic and social development show the Party leadership's consistent priority on ecological civilisation. In Li's view, green development can serve as a strong engine for high-quality development.

The piece has two parts. It first reviews achievements of the 14th Five-Year Plan period, citing figures on air and water quality, ecological restoration, clean energy, the national carbon market and green factories. It then sets out five tasks for the coming period.

Li draws on the 14th Five-Year Plan record to argue that environmental protection and economic growth are not opposed but dialectically unified. Good ecology is presented as both part of a better life and an internal requirement of high-quality development. The five tasks are: strengthening green growth momentum through industrial restructuring and cleaner key sectors; deepening pollution control and ecosystem protection; building a new energy system on the principle of establishing the new before breaking the old; pursuing the carbon peak steadily; and fostering green modes of production and living through social mobilisation.

Li concludes that, guided by Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilisation, these measures will secure the carbon peak on schedule and lay the base for carbon neutrality. Read the original if you want a concise official-economist overview of the green transition's reported results and the policy priorities linked to the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: The green development practice of the 14th Five-Year Plan period fully shows that ecological protection and economic development are by no means opposed, but form a dialectically unified, mutually reinforcing organic whole.
quoteZh: “十四五”时期的绿色发展实践充分说明，生态环境保护和经济发展绝非对立关系，而是辩证统一、相辅相成的有机整体。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal of ecological civilisation first formally set out at the 18th Party Congress (2012), aiming at a cleaner environment and harmony between people and nature.
The official guiding concept for economic development since the late 2010s, stressing quality, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilisation
glossary.literal: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on environmental governance attributed to Xi Jinping, including the slogan that clear waters and green mountains are invaluable assets.

glossary.en: establishing the new before breaking the old
glossary.explanation: A policy principle for the energy transition: build reliable new energy capacity before phasing out existing fossil sources, so as to protect energy security.

t: A scientific plan for opening a new phase of Chinese modernization
zh: 开创中国式现代化建设新局面的科学谋划
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 31 October 2025, interprets the Recommendations for formulating the 15th Five-Year Plan for national economic and social development, adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). Huang and Zhang argue that the Recommendations are a programmatic document that sets out what kind of development is to be achieved in 2026–2030 and how, and that they express the Party Central Committee's 'historical initiative' in opening a new phase of Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the 15th Five-Year Plan period occupies a pivotal position, linking what came before with what follows, in the effort to substantially realise socialist modernization by 2035. The second describes the plan as a further general mobilisation and deployment, covering its historical bearings, key tasks and the consultation behind it. The third sets out the 'six upholds' principles that are to guide the period.

In the first part, the authors view the period from three angles: history, the demands of the times and value orientation. Historically, it is one of three five-year periods needed to reach the 2035 goal. In terms of tasks, it is a critical period for laying foundations, with per capita GDP reaching the level of moderately developed countries as one marker. In terms of values, it is a window for making more evident progress towards common prosperity. The second part lists seven main goals and twelve fields of strategic tasks, from a modern industrial system to national defence. It reports that Xi Jinping chaired the drafting group and that an online consultation in May and June drew more than 3 million valid suggestions. The third part argues for upholding Party leadership, the people first, high-quality development, comprehensive deepening of reform, an effective market combined with an enabling government, and coordination of development and security.

The authors conclude that the Plenum's guidance should be implemented with a spirit of historical initiative, concentrating on China's own affairs so as to continue the 'two miracles' of rapid economic growth and long-term social stability. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned reading of how the 15th Five-Year Plan Recommendations are framed and justified for a Party and public audience.
quoteEn: The 15th Five-Year Plan period follows on from China's sustained development since reform and opening up, especially the deepening implementation of the 14th Five-Year Plan, and leads into the goal of basically realising socialist modernization by 2035. It is an important stage on the unwavering path of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: “十五五”时期上承改革开放以来我国持续发展特别是“十四五”规划的深入实施，下启2035年基本实现社会主义现代化目标，是坚定不移走中国式现代化道路、基本实现社会主义现代化进程中的重要一程。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as distinct from Western models.
A goal of shared affluence for all, given greater weight in Party policy since the 2010s and especially under Xi Jinping.
An official formulation that shifts the emphasis from speed of growth to quality, innovation and sustainability.
China's medium-term national planning documents, issued since the 1950s. The 15th covers 2026–2030.

t: Anti-Japanese patriotic propaganda in overseas Chinese periodicals in the Americas during the War of Resistance
zh: 抗战时期美洲侨刊的抗日爱国宣传
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2025, asks what role periodicals run by Chinese students and overseas Chinese in North and South America played in the resistance to Japan after the Mukden Incident of 1931. Yan argues that these publications spread information, mobilised opinion and gathered donations. In the author's account, they energised Chinese communities abroad, drew echoes from opinion in the host countries and helped shape international anti-fascist forces.

The article proceeds by country. It first treats the United States, where it distinguishes publications run by Chinese students, by long-settled people of Chinese descent and by Chinese cultural figures who went there. Its examples are the Chinese Students' Monthly, the English-language Chinese Digest (San Francisco, founded 1935) and the Chinese-language Free World (New York, 1942). It then turns to the Chinese-language Canadian paper Tai Han Kung Pao (Da Han Gong Bao) and, finally, to two Peruvian periodicals, Gong Yan Bao and Oriental Review (Dongfang Yuebao).

Yan's central claim is that these periodicals used the languages and channels available to them. The Chinese Students' Monthly reported on Japanese aggression. Chinese Digest, in English, reached second- and third-generation Chinese Americans and reprinted pieces from the New York Times and reports of American boycotts and relief funds. Tai Han Kung Pao, the organ of the Chinese Freemasons' Zhigongtang, criticised Japan's Twenty-One Demands. After 1931 it called for an end to civil war, and after 1937 it ran war-telegram columns, urged fundraising and bond purchases and encouraged skilled overseas Chinese to return. Yan reports that in Peru, Gong Yan Bao organised donations, and that Zhou Enlai praised the Peruvian community's fundraising in an inscription.

Yan concludes that overseas Chinese periodicals are an extension of China's external communication and a source of international soft power. They used Chinese, English and Spanish to expose Japan's ambitions, call for donations and promote patriotism, and Yan describes this as the American chapter of a shared national effort at home and abroad. Read the original if you want a brief survey of specific Chinese-diaspora newspapers and magazines in the Americas during the war, with their titles, editors and themes.
quoteEn: Overseas Chinese communities in the Americas used these periodicals as platforms for opinion, working in Chinese, English, Spanish and other languages to expose Japan's ambitions in China, call on overseas Chinese to donate money and goods, and promote patriotism.
quoteZh: 美洲华侨社区利用这些报刊舆论平台，使用中文、英文和西班牙文等多种语言媒介形式，揭露日本的侵华野心、号召华侨捐款捐物、弘扬爱国主义精神

glossary.explanation: The 18 September 1931 incident near Shenyang that Japan used as a pretext to occupy Northeast China. Chinese historiography treats it as the start of the War of Resistance.
An overseas Chinese fraternal organisation linked to the Hongmen (Heaven and Earth Society) tradition, with branches in North America. It ran Tai Han Kung Pao as its organ in Canada.

t: The Spanish International Brigades and China's anti-Japanese national united front
zh: 西班牙国际纵队与中国抗日民族统一战线
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 29 October 2025
paras: Writing for the 80th anniversary of the victory in the War of Resistance against Japan and the world anti-fascist war, Wang treats the Spanish Civil War and China's resistance as the western and eastern battlefields of a single global struggle. The article argues that the International Brigades and the anti-Japanese national united front were two different but complementary anti-fascist models. The first was an internationalist model of support across borders; the second was a nationwide resistance front rooted in China itself.

The commentary opens with the International Brigades: volunteers from more than 50 countries, over 30,000 people in total, including Chinese volunteers. Wang then traces how the united front took shape, from the Comintern's Seventh Congress (1935) and the August 1st Declaration to the Wayaobao meeting and the second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation. A third section looks at exchanges between the two battlefields, and a final section compares the two models and draws lessons.

Wang's central claim is that the two cases differ in structure. The Brigades are described as an 'external aid internalised' model, in which outside forces fought inside the country, though the author says they failed to integrate Spain's local social forces. The Chinese front is described as 'internally generated, externally linked': it mobilised domestic forces first and then sought foreign help. The author points to interaction between the two sides, including Zhu De's and Mao Zedong's messages to the Spanish people, the song 'Defend Madrid', Chinese volunteers in Spain, and the 'Spanish doctors' such as Norman Bethune who later came to China. Effective anti-fascism, Wang argues, requires the dialectical unity of local initiative and a global outlook.

Wang concludes that the Chinese Communist Party drew lessons from Spain. Mao named the united front first among the 'three magic weapons' in 1939. The author holds that victory required a strong, mature party leadership, the broadest possible domestic and international united front, and no abandonment of independence and self-reliance. Wang links the Brigades' vow to save freedom in Spain and across the world with the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind, and treats the two as continuous in essence. Read the original if you want a short, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholars connect the Spanish Civil War to the united front and to present-day internationalist rhetoric.
quoteEn: The practice of Spain and China shows that an effective anti-fascist struggle must achieve a dialectical unity of local self-awareness and a global outlook.
quoteZh: 西班牙和中国的实践表明，有效的反法西斯斗争必须实现本土自觉与全球视野的辩证统一。

glossary.explanation: The broad political alliance, led by the Chinese Communist Party and including the Kuomintang and other groups, formed in the 1930s to resist Japanese invasion. Its second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation was announced in 1937.
A 1935 appeal drafted by the Chinese Communist Party delegation to the Comintern. It called on all classes and parties to stop civil war and unite against Japan.
Mao Zedong's 1939 formulation of the Party's key instruments of revolution: the united front, armed struggle and Party building. The article stresses that he ranked the united front first.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It stresses shared interests and joint responses to global challenges.

t: Chinese modernization of the rule of law and its global significance
zh: 中国式法治现代化及其世界意义
paras: Lin Wei, in a commentary for the Chinese Social Sciences Today (29 October 2025), asks what global significance the Chinese path of rule-of-law modernization holds. Lin describes it as a new path, led by the Communist Party, that combines Marxist legal theory with China's realities and with excellent traditional legal culture. The author argues that it will help reshape the world legal order and create a new form of human legal civilization.

The piece sets out seven aspects of this significance. They are a self-reliant model for developing countries, an autonomous Chinese legal knowledge system, a people-centred orientation, the coordination of domestic and foreign-related rule of law, the creative transformation of Chinese legal civilization, legal support for high-quality development, and the rule of law in cyberspace.

Lin's core claim is that a path based on national conditions offers developing countries a way to avoid dependence on Western models. The author presents the legal knowledge system, guided by Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law, as a new theoretical resource. For global governance, Lin cites figures: as of June 2025, 306 laws in force, 55 of them specifically foreign-related; 26,000 foreign-related civil and commercial cases concluded by courts in 2024; and 207 overseas branches of Chinese law firms. Lin also holds that property protection and a better business environment give investors stable expectations, and that laws on cybersecurity, data and algorithms offer a Chinese approach to digital governance.

Lin concludes that China's practice is a milestone in the history of the rule of law and will provide experience and ideas for other countries. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how an official-aligned legal scholar presents the international relevance of China's legal development, with statistics on foreign-related legal work.
quoteEn: This spirit of an autonomous rule of law, grounded in national realities and self-directed exploration, offers a reference model for the many developing countries seeking to escape dependence on Western models and to find rule-of-law modernization paths suited to themselves.
quoteZh: 这种立足本国实际、自主探索的主体性法治精神，为广大发展中国家摆脱西方模式依赖、探索适合自身的法治现代化路径提供了参考样本。

glossary.explanation: A policy area covering laws, enforcement, adjudication and legal services that deal with foreign and international matters, including the protection of China's overseas interests.
An official goal, stressed since the late 2010s, of shifting from rapid growth to development emphasising quality, innovation and efficiency.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law
glossary.explanation: The official body of ideas on law and governance attributed to Xi Jinping, formally put forward in 2020 as a guide to comprehensively advancing law-based governance.

t: Advancing society-wide general education in artificial intelligence
zh: 推进人工智能全社会通识教育
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 30 October 2025, asks how general education in artificial intelligence (AI) can be extended from schools to the whole of society. Starting from Xi Jinping's call to promote AI education at all school stages and general education across society, Ai and Zhu argue that it would raise national AI literacy, spread the benefits of technology and guard against risks. They contend that it should be built as a system.

The article sets out five components: differentiated target groups, a tiered curriculum, varied delivery channels, a mechanism linking learning and assessment, and a multi-party support structure. Each is treated briefly and with practical examples.

On content, the authors propose a principle of tiered, categorised, all-age and lifelong learning. Primary, middle and high schools, vocational and general higher education, working professionals and older people would each follow their own path. The curriculum would move from what AI is, to how to use it, to how to use it responsibly, so that the public shifts from being able to use AI to using it well. Delivery would combine online courses and question-answering systems with AR and VR exhibits in science museums, libraries, community centres and village halls. A credit-bank system would record learning outcomes, and group-specific indicators would assess results.

For support, Ai and Zhu call for Party committee leadership and government direction, including standards, evaluation and dedicated funds. Enterprises would open training platforms and application sites, universities would build courses and train teachers, and science associations and the media would produce and spread popular materials. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese policy writing translates a leadership directive on AI into an implementation framework for education.
quoteEn: Work should start from systematic construction, improving and innovating the target groups, curriculum, carriers, mechanisms and support system, so that society-wide general AI education takes firm root and goes deeper.
quoteZh: 应从体系化建设入手，通过教育对象、课程、载体、机制和保障体系等方面的完善和创新，切实促进人工智能全社会通识教育走实、走深。

t: The united front as a powerful instrument for winning hearts and pooling strength
zh: 统一战线是凝聚人心汇聚力量的强大法宝
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 30 October 2025, asks how the united front can continue to rally popular support and unite forces in the new era. Jiang Rui argues that, as the Party leadership has put it, winning hearts and minds is "the greatest politics", and that the united front is a "powerful magic weapon" for this task. The article presents it as a political advantage of the Communist Party of China that matters for building a modern socialist country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article opens with the historical record of the united front, from the National Revolutionary united front to the patriotic united front of the reform period, and with the framework developed since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then turns to current policy: the 2022 Central United Front Work Conference, the 20th Party Congress report, and the proposals for the 15th Five-Year Plan, which call for improving the "broad united front work" pattern. The text is organised in three numbered sections: the united front's strategic position, the practice of great unity, and consensus-building.

Jiang's central argument is that great unity must grow in both breadth and quality. The article links this to harmony in five sets of relations: political parties, ethnic groups, religions, social strata, and compatriots at home and overseas, including Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. For each, the author sets out tasks, such as the new type of party system, forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, and the sinicisation of religion. On consensus, Jiang says the Party must hold the "centre of the circle" while widening inclusiveness, so that unity and diversity coexist. The author describes shared political foundations as upholding Party leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics, and supporting national reunification.

Jiang concludes that, with society more diverse and the internet changing the united front's work, ideological guidance and consensus-building must be strengthened and methods innovated, online and offline. The author gives the people's political consultative conference a role as a specialised consultative body that resolves conflicts and builds consensus. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how united front work is framed in late 2025, including its themes of unity and diversity and its five relationships.
quoteEn: A distinctive feature of the patriotic united front in the new era is that diversity has developed markedly on the basis of steadily growing unity.
quoteZh: 新时代爱国统一战线的一个鲜明特征，就是在一致性不断增强的基础上多样性显著发展

glossary.explanation: A broad political alliance led by the Communist Party of China, bringing together non-Party groups and individuals. It has been used since the pre-1949 revolutionary period and is described as one of the Party's key instruments.
A slogan describing the aim of united front work: uniting the widest possible range of social forces around the Party's goals.

The official description of China's multi-party cooperation system under Communist Party leadership, in which the democratic parties participate in consultation and supervision rather than compete for power.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: firmly forging the consciousness of the Chinese national community
glossary.explanation: A policy formula, prominent since the late 2010s, that makes a shared national identity the main line of ethnic work. The formula is often illustrated with the image of ethnic groups as pomegranate seeds held tightly together.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term goal of making China prosperous and strong, associated with the Chinese Dream.
The Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, a consultative body that brings together Party and non-Party figures and is a main institution of the united front.

t: Guiding principles for economic and social development during the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: “十五五”时期经济社会发展的指导方针
paras: This is a programmatic article by Li Qiang, published in the People's Daily on 30 October 2025, explaining the guiding principles for economic and social development set out in the Central Committee's Recommendations for formulating the 15th Five-Year Plan. These were adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). Li argues that the 2026–2030 period is a link between past and future in the drive to basically achieve socialist modernization by 2035, and that the guidelines must be fully understood and carried out in drafting and implementing the plan.

The article has three parts. The first locates the 15th Five-Year Plan period historically, within the course of Chinese modernization and within what it calls profound changes in the world unseen in a century. The second sets out the guiding ideology and the "six adherences" that together make up the guidelines. The third lists practical requirements in four areas and ends with instructions on drafting the plan outline.

Li's core claim is that the period should be approached through two formulas: "consolidating the foundation" and "exerting full force". The first means strengthening resilience on matters basic to development and security; the second means coordinated breakthroughs across all fields under the "five-sphere" and "four-pronged" overall plans. Facing an uncertain international environment, Li says China should pursue certainty through high-quality development and the six adherences: Party leadership, putting the people first, high-quality development, comprehensive deepening of reform, combining an efficient market with a capable government, and coordinating development and security. The practical tasks are building the new development pattern, with a stronger domestic cycle and a unified national market; integrating scientific and industrial innovation to develop new quality productive forces according to local conditions; improving livelihoods and advancing common prosperity; and securing the new development pattern with a new security pattern.

Li concludes that the State Council will draft the plan outline on the basis of the Recommendations. Drafters are to consult widely, work out major policies, reforms and projects, and ensure that special, regional, spatial and local plans reflect the guidelines. The article closes with a call to rally around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. Read the original if you want an authoritative statement of how the leadership frames the priorities and official vocabulary of the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: A major feature of the work in the 15th Five-Year Plan period is to do certain things well in an uncertain environment; the six adherences provide certain principles for China's development and must be firmly grasped.
quoteZh: “十五五”时期工作的一大特征就是在不确定环境下做好确定性的事情，“六个坚持”为我国发展提供了确定性原则，必须牢牢把握。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging and future industries.
The official term for China's path to modernization, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as an essential feature of Chinese modernization.
The official development theme since 2017, emphasising quality, innovation and efficiency over growth in scale alone.
A strategy centred on a strong domestic cycle with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other, put forward from 2020.

t: Methodological self-awareness: building a narrative system for Chinese modernization through Marx's method of presentation
zh: 方法自觉：马克思叙述方法视域下中国式现代化的叙事体系构建
source: Socialism Studies (社会主义研究), 2025 no. 3
paras: Huang Jing and Bao Jin take up a question raised by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for accelerating a Chinese discourse and narrative system: how can China's own narrative of Chinese modernization reach an international audience? The authors argue that existing scholarship studies the theory, practice and values of this narrative but neglects its methodology. They contend that Marx's method of presentation (Darstellungsmethode, 叙述方法) offers the missing guide, and that using it would also break what they call the Western monopoly on narrative methodology.

After a short review of the literature, the article has three main parts. The first sets out the basic determinations of Marx's method of presentation, drawing on the Afterword to the second edition of Capital Volume I, the critique of Hegel and The German Ideology. The second applies these to diagnose three obstacles facing the narrative of Chinese modernization. The third draws three lessons from Marx for building the narrative system.

On Marx, the authors distinguish the method of presentation from the method of research. Research appropriates material and traces inner connections. Presentation then reproduces the results as a concrete whole, shaped by its object and its readers, and it should take the form of a 'real' rather than an 'ideal' narration of history. On this basis, they identify three obstacles. The first is a shortage of narrative depth, with too little movement from the abstract to the concrete. The second is the one-track Western narrative of modernization, which they say is backed by capital power and used to stigmatise Chinese modernization, including in digital and algorithmic spaces. The third is a barrier of discourse between Chinese narrators and foreign readers. They locate its causes in Western-centric readings, a propaganda-oriented and one-way style of outward communication, and Western control of digital technology.

The authors propose three remedies. Research and presentation should be unified, combining systematic study of Chinese modernization with a systematic account of it. Narrative discourse should pursue a 'revolution in terminology' and reader-awareness. This means new concepts that can win international recognition, a balance between universality and particularity, and reframing for foreign contexts. The narrative should follow 'real historical narration', avoiding both the imposition of Western schemas and the pursuit of speculative concepts, and it should rest on the 'big historical view'. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese scholars use Marx's methodological texts to frame the international communication of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Building the narrative system of Chinese modernization must by no means stop at summarising concepts and categories; it must also follow the 'correct path' of 'ascending from the abstract to the concrete'.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化叙事体系的建构绝不能停滞于概念和范畴的概括，还必须按照“抽象上升到具体”的“正确道路”

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models and became a central slogan after the 20th Party Congress (2022).

Marx's term (Darstellungsweise) from the Afterword to Capital Volume I, for the way research findings are set out, as distinct from the method of research. The authors treat it as a method for building narrative systems.

glossary.zh: 中国话语和中国叙事体系
glossary.pinyin: Zhōngguó huàyǔ hé Zhōngguó xùshì tǐxì
glossary.literal: Chinese discourse and Chinese narrative system
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan calling for China to develop its own concepts and ways of telling its story, especially in international communication. It features in the 20th Party Congress report and the Third Plenum decision.
Engels's phrase in the preface to the English edition of Capital: every new scientific insight brings a revolution in the terms of that science. The authors use it to call for new Chinese concepts.

A concept in Xi Jinping's discourse that urges viewing events across long historical stretches and world-historical contexts. The authors present it as a contemporary form of Marx's 'real historical narration'.

t: What Chen Yun's methods of investigation and research teach us
zh: 陈云同志的调查研究方法给予我们的启示
paras: Zhu Jiamu draws lessons for today from the investigation and research (diaocha yanjiu) practice of Chen Yun, the Party's long-serving economic leader. The article opens with Mao Zedong's remark at the 1962 Seven Thousand Cadres Conference that Chen Yun understood socialist construction better than most and that "his method is investigation and research". Zhu argues that Chen's methods remain a valuable legacy that should be studied and applied. The piece was published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2025.

The article is organised around four requirements of good investigation: approaching it without preconceptions, being thorough and meticulous, listening to differing views, and having the right purpose. Each section combines Chen's own statements with episodes from his career, including the 1949 Shanghai prices mission, the 1953 grain purchase and sale policy, the 1959 coal industry symposium and his 1961 fieldwork in Qingpu. Each also cites Xi Jinping's remarks on research work, and the closing section refers to the March 2023 Central Committee work plan on investigation and research.

Zhu's central claim is that Chen's "fifteen-character formula" ("not bowing to superiors, not bowing to books, only to reality; exchange, comparison, repetition") underpins his method. In Zhu's reading, "not bowing to superiors" does not mean disregarding them: Chen insisted on carrying out central directives while starting from local reality, and Zhu cites his 1961 proposal on household contracting. Zhu points to Chen's 15 days in a Qingpu village, his detailed sow-rearing observations and his arithmetic against double-cropping rice as models of depth. On listening, Chen sought out dissenting views and truth-tellers and took responsibility for the leadership's errors. On purpose, Zhu stresses that Chen treated research as a means to solve problems, and that he put people's livelihood first, as in his proposals on vegetables, soybeans and private plots.

Zhu concludes that, amid what the article calls great changes unseen in a century and deep-seated contradictions in reform and development, investigation and research is a "family heirloom" to be used more fully. He calls for grasping real conditions more thoroughly and understanding objective laws more deeply, so as to carry socialism with Chinese characteristics for a new era forward. Read the original if you want a Party-historian's account of Chen Yun's working methods, with concrete episodes and the official framing of the 2023 campaign to promote investigation and research.
quoteEn: The fundamental purpose of investigation and research is to solve problems.
quoteZh: 调查研究的根本目的是解决问题。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing Party working method of fact-finding through fieldwork, interviews and analysis before making policy. It is associated with Mao Zedong and was promoted again in a 2023 Party-wide campaign.

glossary.pinyin: bù wéi shàng, bù wéi shū, zhǐ wéi shí
glossary.en: not bowing to superiors, not bowing to books, only to reality
glossary.literal: not defer to superiors, not defer to books, defer only to reality
glossary.explanation: The first nine characters of Chen Yun's "fifteen-character formula", formulated in Yan'an. It urges cadres to base decisions on actual conditions rather than on instructions or texts alone.
Chen Yun's summary of a sound way of thinking: not bowing to superiors, books or anything but reality, plus "exchange, comparison, repetition".
An enlarged Central Committee work conference held in 1962 that reviewed the Great Leap Forward and the ensuing famine years.

t: Unifying the yardstick of government conduct to advance the building of a unified national market
zh: 统一政府行为尺度推进全国统一大市场建设
paras: In this commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in October 2025, Wang Tinghui asks how to remove the obstacles that block a unified national market. Citing Xi Jinping's formula of "five unifications and one opening", Wang argues that obstacles such as impeded factor flows, local protectionism and market fragmentation largely stem from inconsistent conduct by local governments, differing policy standards and deviations in implementation.

The article sets out three groups of measures: establishing institutional standards for government conduct, building cross-regional and cross-departmental coordination, and strengthening supervision along the whole chain of government action. Each group is broken into three sub-measures.

On standards, Wang proposes a unified negative list for policy-making covering market access, subsidies, tax breaks and financing, with fairness and legality review of local rules. Wang also calls for national standards for public resource trading to end "local preference" and for enforcement guidelines that narrow discretion and ensure like cases receive like penalties. On coordination, Wang proposes policy coordination among provinces, starting with pilots in Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, the Yangtze River Delta and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Wang also urges departmental coordination lists and a shift in local performance evaluation away from GDP and investment attraction towards market integration, with a "one-vote veto" for regions practising market fragmentation.

On supervision, Wang advocates a national big-data monitoring platform combined with reporting channels for firms, graded correction by higher authorities, and an accountability measure that reaches local leaders, balanced by policy incentives for regions that perform well. Read the original if you want a concise, policy-oriented account of how Chinese scholars propose to discipline local government behaviour in building the unified national market.
quoteEn: The key to unifying the yardstick of government conduct is to set rules, draw boundaries, fix standards and clarify responsibilities for government action.
quoteZh: 统一政府行为尺度，关键在于对政府行为立规矩、划边界、定标准、明责任

glossary.explanation: A policy goal, formalised in a 2022 Party and State Council opinion, of removing regional barriers so that goods, capital and labour move freely across China.

A formula for the basic requirements of the unified national market: unified basic institutions, infrastructure, information, standards and regulatory enforcement, plus opening to the outside world. The article treats unifying government conduct as part of it.
Practices by local governments that favour local firms or restrict outside ones, which fragment the national market.
A list of what is prohibited or restricted; anything not listed is permitted. Here it is applied to local policy-making powers.

t: Breaking structural barriers to curb "involutionary" competition
zh: 以打破结构性壁垒整治“内卷式”竞争
paras: Ling Yongnhui's commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in October 2025, asks why "involutionary" competition (neijuan) has spread in some traditional and emerging Chinese industries, and how to remedy it. Ling defines it as excessive competition in which disorder in the market pushes competition costs far above returns. The thesis is that, in institutional-economics terms, the key cause is a structural contradiction between administrative barriers that are too high and market barriers that are too low.

The piece first explains how such competition arises, then sets out remedies. Ling treats it as a problem that must be cleared away in building a unified national market, because it squeezes firm profits and, in Ling's account, can feed a vicious chain from lower profits to weaker incomes, insufficient demand and surplus capacity.

Ling traces two paths. In the first, high administrative barriers, vertical (state control over factor allocation) and horizontal (local protectionism and local industrial policy), block firms from upgrading and from exiting, so they compete passively on price. In the second, low market barriers draw many firms into low-end sectors, where they imitate rather than innovate and keep industry concentration low, so competition is active but destructive. The remedy follows the principle of "establishing and breaking in parallel": subtract from administrative barriers and add to market barriers.

To subtract, Ling proposes shifting industrial policy towards consumer-side subsidies and upstream innovation, extending cross-regional fair-competition review to local investment incentives, and reforming taxation so that consumption taxes become a stable local revenue source. To add, Ling proposes higher national and industry standards, tighter control of new capacity, support for mergers led by leading firms, and stronger industry self-discipline and credit systems. Read the original if you want a concise policy-oriented account of how a Chinese economist links anti-involution measures to the unified national market.
quoteEn: From the perspective of institutional economics, the key cause of "involutionary" competition is a structural contradiction between excessively high administrative barriers and excessively low market barriers, which locks large numbers of Chinese firms into the middle and low end of industrial chains.
quoteZh: 从制度经济学视角看，“内卷式”竞争的关键诱因是行政性壁垒过高而市场性壁垒过低的结构性矛盾导致我国大量企业被锁定在产业链的中低端环节

glossary.explanation: A term in recent Chinese policy and public debate for excessive, mutually damaging competition, typically price wars, in which firms gain little. Authorities have promoted campaigns to curb it since 2024–25.
A policy goal of removing local protectionism and market segmentation so goods, capital and labour move freely across China.
A principle of building new institutions or practices while dismantling outdated ones.
A review mechanism in which government policies and measures are checked for rules that exclude or restrict competition.

t: The Five-Year Plans as a relay advancing the process of Chinese modernization
zh: “五年规划”接力推进中国式现代化进程
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2025, Zhang Guanzi asks what the Five-Year Plans reveal about the Chinese Communist Party's leadership and about the institutional advantages of Chinese governance. The author argues that continuous five-year planning is a distinctive Chinese model of national governance, and that it works as the key mechanism for both driving and measuring Chinese modernization. The commentary is framed as groundwork for carrying out the coming 15th Five-Year Plan.

The piece is a short commentary in four sections. It first traces the origin of the plans from the First Five-Year Plan of 1953 to the shift to the term "five-year plan" (规划) from the 11th plan. It then describes how plans are drafted and promulgated, how they embody a people-centred approach to development, and how they secure long-term strategic stability while allowing dynamic adjustment.

Zhang's central claim is that the plans combine scientific and democratic procedure with Party leadership. Drafting is described as a closed loop of investigation, scientific verification, consultation and legal enactment, with top-down coordination and bottom-up participation. The author calls Party leadership the single most fundamental lesson of plan-making. Poverty alleviation serves as the main example: it ran as a priority from the 11th to the 13th plans, became a binding target in the 13th plan, and shows how a "goal guidance, resource coordination, coordinated execution" system mobilises national resources. Zhang also argues that targets link successive plans to the "three-step" strategy and the Two Centenary Goals, that approval by the National People's Congress gives plans legal force, and that mid-term evaluation, annual plans and emergency adjustments let plans adapt without abandoning long-term aims.

Zhang concludes that the plans' continuity, legal backing and flexibility, a unity of "strategic resolve" and "tactical vitality", make them an important methodology for steady progress in Chinese modernization, which is presented as a dynamic process rather than a fixed blueprint. The author also holds that plans measure success by people's sense of gain, happiness and security rather than by growth rates alone. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic account of how the Five-Year Plan system is explained and justified as the 15th Five-Year Plan approaches.
quoteEn: The dynamic adjustment of the Five-Year Plans is not a departure from established goals but a scientific optimisation made while holding to the long-term strategy; in essence it is a unity of "strategic resolve" and "tactical vitality".
quoteZh: “五年规划”的动态调整并非偏离既定目标，而是坚守长期战略前提下的科学优化，本质是“战略定力”与“策略活力”的统一。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path to modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
Medium-term national development blueprints adopted since 1953. Since the 11th plan (2006–2010) the official term has been "guihua" (programme) rather than "jihua" (plan).

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: A Party formula holding that development is for the people, relies on the people and is shared by the people.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary (2049).

t: Unwaveringly following the path of ecological priority and green development
zh: 坚定不移走生态优先绿色发展之路
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in October 2025, asks how China should handle the relationship between economic growth and environmental protection now that its economy has moved from high-speed growth to high-quality development. Han Bin argues that Xi Jinping's call to follow the path of ecological priority and green development is a theoretically grounded break with conventional growth models. The author presents it as the direction for high-quality development and long-term national competitiveness.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical logic of the path, the second reviews practical results since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and the third outlines tasks for the 15th Five-Year Plan period, following the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025). Evidence comes from policy documents issued in 2024 and 2025 and from statistics on emissions and energy.

In the theoretical section, Han presents the path as a development of Marxist ideas on the dialectical unity of humans and nature and of production and ecology. The author contrasts it with a Western modernization model described as capital-centred, materialist and based on pollution first, cleanup later. Han describes the shift as one from instrumental to value rationality, with ecological protection a priority in economic decisions and well-being rather than GDP as the goal. The article cites progress such as the 'new three' export industries (new-energy vehicles, lithium batteries, photovoltaics) and the 2024 fall in carbon dioxide emissions per 10,000 yuan of GDP of 3.4 per cent. It also cites a non-fossil share of energy consumption of 19.8 per cent and coal power below 40 per cent of installed capacity.

Han calls for three further steps: stronger ecological protection and restoration, with zoning-based controls and integrated management of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grasslands and deserts; greener and lower-carbon urban and rural construction; and cautious but steady progress towards the carbon peak before 2030 and carbon neutrality before 2060. Concrete proposals include carbon-intensity targets, local assessment systems and product carbon footprint management. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary links Marxist theory, new quality productive forces and the 15th Five-Year Plan agenda to green transition policy.
quoteEn: A good ecological environment is the fairest public good and the most inclusive benefit for people's livelihood.
quoteZh: 良好的生态环境是最公平的公共产品，是最普惠的民生福祉。

glossary.explanation: The official term, in use since 2017, for the stage in which China prioritises efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to innovation-led, technology-intensive and green productive forces.

t: An action guide for the green transformation of the development model
zh: 推动发展方式绿色转型的行动指南
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily on 29 October 2025, takes up the question of how the green development concept can guide the shift of China's development model. Jian Xiaowen argues that green development, as one element of the new development philosophy, is the 'underlying colour' of high-quality development and supplies a basic guideline and action guide for the comprehensive green transformation of economy and society. The piece takes its cue from the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025), which called for accelerating that transformation and building a beautiful China.

The article has three parts. The first draws lessons from home and abroad, the second looks at meeting the people's need for a fine ecological environment, and the third sets out how to move the development model towards green and low-carbon forms. It refers to China's reform-era record, to the Western 'pollute first, clean up later' path and the 'eight major pollution incidents', and to green manufacturing strategies in the United States, Japan, Europe, India and Brazil.

Jian's core reasoning is that the concept answers both historical and present conditions. In the author's account, China's extensive growth model produced air, water and soil pollution and unsustainable patterns, while the Western path imposed heavy costs and shows what to avoid. Rising popular expectations have moved from 'having enough' to 'having good', so ecological quality is both a livelihood and a political matter. Jian also contends that green development drives industrial upgrading by writing ecological benefits into evaluation systems and encouraging green consumption, and that new quality productive forces are by nature green productive forces, so that greenness should be a test of them.

Jian calls for applying the green concept across production, distribution, circulation and consumption. Proposed measures include pollution control, ecological compensation between protected and benefiting regions, market trading and clearer ecological rights, realising the value of ecological products, green-oriented assessment systems, fiscal, financial and pricing policy support, and public education. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary links green development to high-quality development, new quality productive forces and the people-centred approach after the Fourth Plenum.
quoteEn: Green development is an important link connecting the improvement of the ecological environment, the meeting of the people's need for a better life, and the realisation of high-quality development.
quoteZh: 绿色发展是连接改善生态环境、满足人民群众对美好生活的需要、实现高质量发展的重要纽带。

glossary.explanation: A framework introduced in 2015 holding that development should be innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared. It is presented as the guiding principle of China's economic policy.
The official goal for China's economy since about 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth.
A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, high efficiency and high quality.

t: Making vigorous innovation cities a priority
zh: 着力建设富有活力的创新城市
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily takes up the call, made at the Central Conference on Urban Work in Beijing in July 2025, to build "vigorous innovation cities". Zhou Lin argues that innovation is the main engine of urban modernization and that cities, as the places where innovation clusters, have become the main arena of global competition. Building such cities is presented as both an internal requirement of high-quality development and a strategic choice for national competitive advantage.

The article has two parts. The first sets out the contemporary meaning of an innovation city under three headings: a people-centred stance, a systems-integration orientation, and the fusion of humanistic and technological values. The second proposes coordinated action along five dimensions: innovation resources, innovation space, innovation scenarios, innovation services and innovation culture. Zhou draws on Xi Jinping's remarks on the "people's city" and on systems thinking.

In Zhou's account, the people's city idea means an innovation system in which everyone takes part and shares the results. The systems orientation calls for top-level design that lets knowledge, technology, talent and capital flow freely and links basic research to industrial application. The five dimensions carry the practical proposals. For resources, Zhou proposes innovation consortia led by leading technology firms and regional city-cluster mechanisms. For space, the proposals are stronger innovation capacity in development zones, mission-list and "open competition" models for key technologies, and land-use flexibility. For scenarios, new technologies would be applied in urban renewal. For services, Zhou offers full-lifecycle support for innovators, science-and-technology finance with "patient capital", and integrated services for talent. For culture, the author advocates tolerance of failure, science education in schools, and drawing on traditional Chinese culture.

Zhou concludes that an innovation city is a multi-level, multi-actor systems project that has to be adapted to each city's circumstances. The author holds that technology should be guided by humanistic spirit, with socialist core values and traditional Chinese virtues informing frontier innovation, rather than following a logic of technological supremacy. Read the original if you want a concise outline of the policy measures that urban innovation is expected to involve after the July 2025 Central Conference on Urban Work.
quoteEn: Building innovation cities must go beyond a simple logic of \"technology above all\" and grasp the dialectical relationship between humanities and technology, in which substance and function interpenetrate and the Way and the instrument complete each other.
quoteZh: 创新城市建设必须超越简单的“技术至上”逻辑，深刻把握人文与科技“体用贯通、道器相成”的辩证关系

glossary.explanation: A high-level Party meeting that sets the direction of urban policy. The one discussed here was held in Beijing in July 2025, with Xi Jinping attending and speaking.
A concept associated with Xi Jinping, summed up as "people's cities are built by the people and for the people". It is used as the guiding principle of urban development.
The official name for a growth model that stresses innovation, efficiency and quality over scale. It has been a central economic policy goal in Party documents since 2017.

A policy term for real-world settings, such as city districts, buildings and public services, where new technologies and products are trialled and applied. Local governments publish lists of such opportunities.

t: Grasping in depth the thesis that "the essence of modernization is the modernization of people"
zh: 深刻把握“现代化的本质是人的现代化”
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 29 October 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's statement that "the essence of modernization is the modernization of people". Zhang Ruifen argues that the formulation gives people a foundational place in Chinese modernization. In the author's reading it identifies the fundamental force behind that project and sets its value direction. The article sets out the thesis's core meaning, its value and the practical routes for carrying it out.

The text has three parts. The first explains the core meaning. The second sets out the theoretical, historical and practical grounds for the thesis. The third proposes ways to advance the modernization of people within Chinese modernization. It draws on Xi Jinping's speeches, Marx's Theses on Feuerbach and The German Ideology, and examples such as poverty alleviation, rural revitalization and the common prosperity demonstration zones.

Zhang's central move is to treat people as the fundamental driver, the ultimate purpose and the core yardstick of modernization. People's changing needs, skills and rights propel change in industry and institutions. The aim is their free and all-round development, not material abundance as such. Progress is judged by whether people's ideas, abilities and rights match a modern society. The author then gives three grounds. The thesis develops Marx's theory of free and all-round human development. It is said to transcend the alienation found in capital-centred Western modernization. It also responds to the principal contradiction of the new era, which the author breaks down into mismatches of supply and demand, unequal resource distribution and gaps in capabilities.

For practice, Zhang calls for carrying out the strategic plans for Chinese modernization, including industrial upgrading, education and science reform, employment and public-service equalization, and household registration and social security reform. Zhang also wants rising needs and skills to feed back into growth through new consumption, lifelong learning and wider participation in grassroots governance. A third proposal is a mutual-reinforcement mechanism. It would add indicators of people's modernization to evaluation systems, monitor changing needs and keep a people-centred orientation. The author says this would form a closed loop in which strategy supports people's development and people empower the strategy. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link Xi Jinping's formulation to Marx's theory of human development and to policy proposals.
quoteEn: Modernization is by no means a "piling up of things", but a systematic undertaking focused on "the development of people".
quoteZh: 现代化绝非“物的堆砌”，而是聚焦“人的发展”的系统性工程

glossary.explanation: The official concept for China's path to modernization, developed under Xi Jinping and prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
A long-term official goal of shared wealth for all, emphasised under Xi Jinping. It is linked to narrowing gaps between regions, urban and rural areas, and social groups.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A core principle of Xi Jinping's governance thought. It holds that development should serve the people's interests and be judged by their sense of benefit.

t: An important lesson of the Party's self-reform in the new era
st: Advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party by starting with conduct
zh: 新时代党的自我革命一条重要经验
paras: The article takes up a statement by Xi Jinping on 30 June 2025, at a Politburo study session, that advancing full and rigorous self-governance of the Party by starting with conduct (zuofeng) is an important lesson of the Party's self-reform in the new era. Li Neng, an executive vice-president of the Jiangxi Provincial Party School, argues that this formulation reveals the inherent links between conduct building, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform. The author calls on readers to grasp its origins, content and practical path.

The piece has three parts. The first traces where the lesson comes from, the second explains what it means, and the third sets out how to uphold and apply it. It is a Party-school commentary built around Xi's own formulations, with little outside evidence, and it focuses on the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

In explaining the origins, Li names three sources: the practical innovation of implementing the Central Committee's eight-point regulation, which the author says broke a series of long-standing bad practices; institutional innovation in building a system of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party; and theoretical innovation in understanding self-reform, including Xi's claim that self-reform is the Party's second answer to the historical cycle of rise and fall. On content, Li lists Xi's "five adherences": setting iron rules, leading from the top beginning with the Politburo, targeting the "four malpractices" with campaigns and special rectifications, sustained and detailed effort, and treating Party spirit, conduct and discipline as one whole in which conduct, discipline and anti-corruption work are linked.

For application, Li proposes four requirements. The first is to strengthen Party spirit through theoretical study, intra-Party political life and the Party's mass line. The second is to regulate the exercise of power, with a proper view of power, clear authorisation and checks, and a system of rules centred on democratic centralism. The third is to use strict supervision and discipline, including handling conduct problems and corruption together. The fourth is to fulfil Party-governance responsibilities through accountability. Li presents all of this as safeguarding Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party theorists present conduct building as the entry point for Party discipline and self-reform.
quoteEn: Solving conduct problems fundamentally means solving the problem of Party spirit.
quoteZh: 解决作风问题，根本上就是要解决党性问题。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed under Xi Jinping: the Communist Party's capacity to correct itself and rid itself of corruption and bad practices. Xi calls it the Party's second answer to the question of escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name of the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, supervision and anti-corruption work within its own ranks.

Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, bureaucratic habits and formalism among officials. The Party presents them as the starting point of its conduct-building campaign.
The official shorthand for formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, the targets of the conduct campaign.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, used since the early 2020s as a central framing of national goals.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining discussion within the Party with unified decisions that all members must carry out.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China to a position of strength and prosperity, in Party discourse by the mid-twenty-first century.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The origins of the "revolutionary discourse" of modern China: early explorations in adapting Marxist "revolutionary discourse" to China
zh: 现代中国“革命话语”的起源：马克思主义“革命话语”中国化的早期探索
paras: Scholars have studied modern China's "revolutionary discourse" with growing interest, but Wang and Wu observe that its origins are seldom examined. Taking a social-history approach, the article argues that this discourse arose from the spread of Marxism during the May Fourth period. In its account, early Chinese Marxists read revolution through classical Marxist "revolutionary discourse" and applied class-struggle theory creatively to Chinese conditions.

The article covers Chinese thought between 1919 and 1927. It opens with the basic content of classical Marxist revolutionary discourse, then sets out three social-historical conditions for its Chinese formation: the discourse environment left by the bourgeois revolution, the model of the October Revolution, and the radicalisation of May Fourth "social reconstruction". The final section identifies eight themes of the early Chinese discourse, drawing on Li Dazhao, Chen Duxiu, Qu Qiubai, Cai Hesen, Zhao Shiyan, Yun Daiying, Deng Zhongxia and Zhou Enlai.

The authors summarise classical Marxist discourse in six points: revolution arises from the development of the productive forces; it changes the social system, centred on ownership; its subject is the oppressed proletariat; it is led by a proletarian party; it proceeds by armed force; and it aims at a communist society. They argue that early Marxists then adapted this framework to a semi-colonial, semi-feudal China. The eight themes they identify are the nature of Chinese society and its revolutionary history, the aims of the "national revolution", Marxism as guiding thought, Communist Party leadership, the mass character of revolution, armed struggle, the united front, and the claim that the Chinese revolution is part of the world revolution.

Wang and Wu conclude that the discourse took shape in a May Fourth context, but mainly through the efforts of early Marxists and early Communists to adapt Marxist revolutionary theory to China. They hold that it rested on the Party's political practice of transforming Chinese society. In their view it supplied the logical starting point and discursive conditions for the theory of New Democratic revolution and became part of China's Marxist political science. Read the original if you study the intellectual history of the early Communist movement and want a detailed account of how its leaders framed revolution in the 1920s.
quoteEn: Modern China's "revolutionary discourse" originated in the spread of Marxism during the May Fourth period; it is the intellectual product of early Chinese Marxists, who read revolutionary phenomena through classical Marxist "revolutionary discourse" and creatively applied class-struggle theory to explore social revolution in the Chinese setting.
quoteZh: 现代中国“革命话语”起源于马克思主义在五四时期的传播，是中国早期马克思主义者依据经典马克思主义“革命话语”解读革命现象，在中国环境下创造性地运用阶级斗争理论进行社会革命探索的思想结晶。

glossary.explanation: The set of concepts, categories and ways of speaking about revolution that express and shape a body of revolutionary thought. The article treats it as the outward form of Marxist revolutionary theory.
Mao Zedong's term for the stage of the Chinese revolution, led by the proletariat through the Communist Party, aimed against imperialism and feudalism before any socialist transition.
The anti-imperialist, anti-warlord revolution of the mid-1920s, carried out through cooperation between the Communist Party and the Kuomintang.
The anti-imperialist protest movement of 4 May 1919 and the wider New Culture ferment around it, during which Marxism spread among Chinese intellectuals.
The Marxist characterisation of modern China, formalised in 1930s debates, as nominally independent but dominated by imperialist powers and retaining feudal relations.

t: Guiding smart city construction with the concept of the people's city
zh: 以人民城市理念引领智慧城市建设
paras: Writing in China Social Sciences Today (October 2025), Li Zhisong takes up the 2025 Central Urban Work Conference's call to put the people's city concept into practice and to build convenient and efficient smart cities. Li argues that smart city construction has achieved results but is held back by practical difficulties, and that it needs the people's city concept and a multi-actor governance mechanism to move forward.

The short commentary has three parts. It first reviews progress since the 18th Party Congress (2012) in policy design, coverage, intelligent infrastructure and governance performance. It then identifies problems in implementation. It ends with two proposed paths.

On achievements, Li cites a 2024 guideline on citywide digital transformation, with targets for 2027 and 2030, and a 2022 white paper reporting more than 500 pilot cities. On problems, Li points to weak grassroots consultation, such as poorly designed questionnaires and inadequate explanation, and to poor data updating and system maintenance. Li also describes the tension between the traditional "departments and localities" (tiao-kuai) administrative pattern and systemic governance. Grassroots units lack authority over technology partners and depend on fiscal funds, while departments build data silos. Li attributes these failures partly to the lack of a scientific governance concept, which leads to evaluation by indicators such as GDP.

Li proposes, first, that governments apply the people's city concept, summed up as "people's cities are built by the people and for the people", across the whole governance cycle. Second, Li proposes multi-actor collaborative governance. This would clarify vertical powers and responsibilities, fund and staff grassroots work, introduce data-sharing lists across departments and ensure residents take part in goal-setting, supervision and evaluation. Read the original if you want a brief official-line account of how the people's city concept is applied to urban digital governance.
quoteEn: Cities exist because of people, and the ultimate aim of their development should be to serve the all-round development of the human being.
quoteZh: 城市因人而存在，其发展的最终目的应服务于人的全面发展。

glossary.explanation: A principle associated with Xi Jinping, first stated in 2019 in Shanghai, that cities should be built and governed by the people and for the people. The article presents it as the guiding idea of urban work.

A description of China's administrative structure, in which vertical lines of functional departments (tiao) intersect with territorial governments (kuai). Critics use the term for fragmentation and poor coordination.

A city that uses digital technologies such as sensors, big data and artificial intelligence in planning, public services and governance. China has run national pilot programmes for such cities since around 2012.

t: New quality productive forces leading the building of a modern economic system
zh: 新质生产力引领现代化经济体系建设
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how China should build a modern economic system under a new round of technological and industrial change. Yuan Lei argues that new quality productive forces are the core engine of this effort and must be matched by new production relations. Building the system, in this reading, is the process of developing productive forces and forming relations of production suited to them.

The article has three parts. It first sets out what the modern economic system consists of, namely four linked sub-systems of production, distribution, circulation and consumption. It then reviews progress made in recent years, citing figures for each sub-system, and lists remaining problems. It closes with directions for improving each sub-system.

Yuan's central move is theoretical. The author distinguishes two kinds of interaction between productive forces and production relations: gradual improvement of relations that broadly fit, and, where innovation lifts the quality of productive forces, an adaptive reconstruction of production, distribution, circulation and consumption. Economic change driven by new quality productive forces is placed in the second category. On results, the article cites GDP above 130 trillion yuan in 2024, disposable income of 41,314 yuan per head, over 170 billion parcels delivered, and retail sales of over 48.3 trillion yuan. It also names weaknesses: many industries remain in the middle and lower ends of global value chains, income gaps persist, and supply and demand are mismatched.

Yuan proposes innovation-driven upgrading of production, including self-reliance in core technologies and "AI+" transformation of traditional industries. In distribution, the author calls for coordinating primary distribution, redistribution and the third distribution, with common prosperity as a goal. For circulation, Yuan urges a unified national market under the formula "five unifications and one opening". For consumption, the author recommends combining short-term stimulus with long-term institutional reform. Read the original if you want a concise official-style economic overview of how Chinese policy writers link new quality productive forces to production, distribution, circulation and consumption, with the statistics they cite.
quoteEn: The modern economic system is an organic whole composed of the interrelations and internal connections among all links, levels and fields of socio-economic activity.
quoteZh: 现代化经济体系，是由社会经济活动各个环节、各个层面、各个领域的相互关系和内在联系构成的一个有机整体。
