glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023. It refers to productive forces driven by original and disruptive technological breakthroughs rather than traditional growth models.
A strategic goal set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017) and reaffirmed since. It denotes an integrated economic structure spanning production, distribution, circulation and consumption.
A policy aim to remove local protectionism and market fragmentation, so that goods, services and production factors move freely across China.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, which Xi Jinping has stressed as a requirement of socialism. It is used here to guide redistribution policy.

t: Three dimensions for promoting high-quality development of university research
zh: 推动高校科研高质量发展的三重维度
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2025, Wu Chen starts from the headline figures of the 14th Five-Year Plan period. These include total R&D spending of over 3.6 trillion yuan in 2024, 48% above 2020, and first place worldwide in research personnel, high-level journal papers and international patent applications. Wu asks what research should pursue behind such numbers. The answer is that universities need to treat research quality as the central task, practical application as the fundamental mission, and international leadership as the direction of effort.

The commentary is organised in three parts, one for each dimension. The first examines the gap between publication volume and real quality. The second draws on the Ming-Qing idea of jingshi zhiyong to define what research is for. The third looks at paradigm change in science and at how China might lead rather than follow. Each part ends with proposals on university philosophy, resource allocation and evaluation.

On quality, Wu argues that paper counts do not equal competitiveness. Chinese papers are on average cited less than American, British or EU papers, and China publishes fewer papers in Nature and Science and has won fewer Nobel Prizes and Fields Medals. Wu calls for an end to performance-first thinking, KPI pressure and short-cycle evaluation, and for long-term funding of basic, curiosity-driven work. Wu also wants evaluation based on value rather than journal rank, citing the 2025 Nobel laureate Shimon Sakaguchi, whose key 1995 result appeared in a mid-ranked journal.

On application and leadership, Wu holds that publication is not the endpoint of research. Wu proposes a three-in-one model of basic research, technology development and applied transfer, with resources directed to core national problems and evaluation based on problems solved. Wu says this is compatible with free exploration. On leadership, Wu urges targeting the frontier in AI, quantum physics, controlled nuclear fusion and hydrogen energy, shifting research paradigms towards complex systems, simulation and data science, and taking bold steps into uncharted fields to achieve overtaking by changing lanes. Wu concludes that these shifts would give research lasting momentum and underpin China's drive to become a strong country in education, science and talent. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese education scholar links research evaluation reform to national science and technology goals.
quoteEn: The quantity of papers does not equal quality, nor can it simply be equated with core competitiveness and influence.
quoteZh: 论文的数量不等于质量，也不能简单等于核心竞争力和影响力。

glossary.explanation: A Confucian-derived tradition, associated with Ming-Qing thinkers such as Wang Fuzhi, holding that learning should serve practical governance and social needs. Wu uses it to define the purpose of scientific research.
A slogan in Chinese industrial and science policy meaning to surpass competitors by entering new fields or technological paths rather than following established ones.
An official goal of building China into a global leader in education, often paired with strength in science and technology and in talent.

t: Advancing the building of a unified national market in depth
zh: 纵深推进全国统一大市场建设
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2025, no. 14), Li Yuju takes up the instructions Xi Jinping gave at the sixth meeting of the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission on 1 July 2025 on advancing the building of a unified national market. Li argues that this is a strategic deployment by the Party Central Committee. In Li's account it underpins the new development pattern and high-quality development, and it requires that the basic requirement of "five unifications and one opening" be put into practice.

The article has three parts. The first traces the continuity of Party theory and practice on the unified market, from Deng Xiaoping's 1979 remark that socialism can also have a market economy to the 2022 Central Committee and State Council opinions and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). The second reviews results since the 18th Party Congress (2012): top-level design, market rules and institutions, and the use of several market advantages. The third sets out concrete measures under each of the six requirements.

Li's central claim is that the Party's line has been continuous: the market's role moved from "basic" to "decisive" in resource allocation, and the goal moved from a socialist unified market to a high-standard market system. Drawing on Marxist political economy, Li holds that a unified national market keeps the circuits of social reproduction open. As evidence of progress, Li cites a shorter negative list for market access (117 items in the 2022 edition, 106 in 2025), a logistics-cost ratio of 14.1% of GDP in 2024, and 63% of electricity traded through markets. For the remaining problems, Li names local government conduct rooted in a distorted view of performance, such as disorderly investment attraction and low-price competition. The remedies Li proposes include a single national negative list, fair-competition review, unified regulation and enforcement, integrated land, labour, capital, power and data markets, and appraisal systems that penalise breaches of market unity.

Li concludes that the unified national market must be open to the world rather than closed. Li calls for cutting the foreign-investment negative list, giving foreign firms national treatment, implementing the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, and pursuing accession to the CPTPP and DEPA. Li also calls for integrating domestic and foreign trade. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how Chinese policy-makers link market unification to local-government behaviour, regulation and opening up, with the policy documents and figures cited.
quoteEn: In building a unified national market, \"national\" stresses integrity, \"unified\" stresses consistency and \"large\" stresses scale, and its main features include efficiency and standardisation, fair competition and full openness.
quoteZh: 建设全国统一大市场，“全国”强调整体性，“统一”强调一致性，“大”强调规模性，高效规范、公平竞争、充分开放等是其主要特点。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal of removing regional barriers and local protectionism so that goods, services and production factors move freely across China. A 2022 Central Committee and State Council opinion set out its main requirements.

Xi Jinping's summary of the basic requirements for deepening the unified market, given in July 2025. It covers unified basic market systems, infrastructure, government conduct, regulation and enforcement, and factor markets, plus continued opening up.
A strategy announced in 2020 that centres on the domestic economic cycle while linking it with international circulation.
The official economic goal since 2017 of favouring quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
A list of sectors closed or restricted to investors; anything not listed is open to them ("what is not prohibited is permitted").

glossary.en: Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission
glossary.explanation: A Party body chaired by Xi Jinping that sets the direction of major economic policy.

t: Heroes of the War of Resistance inscribed on the motherland's soil
st: Memorials, place names and the memory of the anti-Japanese war
zh: 祖国大地铭刻抗日英雄的名字
paras: Published in Red Flag Manuscript in 2025, this commemorative essay asks how the heroes of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression are remembered in the physical landscape of China. Hu Yuhan argues that monuments, mountains, counties, schools and streets named after them each fix a particular wartime memory and together form an epic of the Chinese nation. The essay presents these heroes as the basis of a spirit that should be honoured and emulated today.

The essay is organised in three parts. The first covers heroic military units and the sites that commemorate them: the Hundred Regiments Offensive monument at Shinao Mountain, the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain, the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army and its eight women fighters, and the Liulaozhuang Company of the New Fourth Army. The second turns to senior commanders, among them Zuo Quan, Dai An'lan, Peng Xuefeng, Tong Linge, Zhao Dengyu and Zhang Zizhong. The third treats civilians and non-combatants, including the Yimeng "Red Sister-in-law" Ming Deying, the overseas Chinese fighter Li Lin and the writer Yu Dafu.

Hu's method is narrative: each case combines a short battle account, a death in action and the way the person is now commemorated. Examples include the county renamed Zuoquan, a school renamed after Peng Xuefeng, and three Beijing streets named after Tong, Zhao and Zhang. The author credits the Communist-led Eighth Route Army and New Fourth Army with holding the enemy rear, and also includes Kuomintang generals such as Dai An'lan and Zhang Zizhong. The essay quotes tributes from Zhou Enlai, Mao Zedong and Zhu De. It stresses the endurance, self-sacrifice and patriotism of soldiers and civilians alike, and describes the war as one fought by the whole nation and won by the whole nation over fourteen years.

Hu concludes that a nation with hope cannot do without heroes, and that the great spirit of resistance is a precious spiritual asset and a driving force. The best way to honour heroes, the author says, is to revere, learn from and strive to become heroes, so that heroic spirit gathers strength for building a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an example of how official Chinese commemorative writing presents war memory, with its place names, named heroes and tributes from Party leaders.
quoteEn: A nation with hope cannot do without heroes, and a country with a future cannot do without vanguards.
quoteZh: 一个有希望的民族不能没有英雄，一个有前途的国家不能没有先锋。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is used here as the goal to which the heroic spirit is to contribute.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party slogan, closely tied to Xi Jinping, for restoring China's strength and international standing. It is presented as a national goal for the mid-twenty-first century.

A large 1940 offensive by Communist-led Eighth Route Army forces against Japanese-held railways and positions in North China. It is a major episode in official accounts of the Party's role in the war.

An official formulation for the patriotism, heroism and endurance attributed to the Chinese people in the war against Japan. It is invoked in Party commemoration as a source of present-day motivation.

t: A dialectical-materialist epistemological interpretation of the great founding spirit of the Party
zh: 伟大建党精神的辩证唯物主义认识论阐释
paras: Ouyang Song asks how the 'great founding spirit of the Party' can be understood through the epistemology of dialectical materialism. The spirit was first formulated by Xi Jinping on 1 July 2021, at the centenary of the Communist Party, in 32 characters: upholding truth and ideals, practising the original aspiration and shouldering the mission, fearing no sacrifice and fighting heroically, and being loyal to the Party and faithful to the people. Ouyang argues that it arose from the practice of founding the Party, was tested and strengthened in a century of Party-building, and so illustrates the Marxist account of how practice and consciousness interact.

The article has three parts. It first sets out the content of the founding spirit, treating the four pairs of phrases as an organic whole and as both the 'source' and one specific strand of the Party's spiritual lineage. It then examines how the founding of the Party gave rise to the spirit, using the early Party organisations, the spread of Marxism associated with Li Dazhao and Chen Duxiu, and the labour movement, including the strikes in Shanghai and the work of Mao Zedong, Peng Pai and Deng Zhongxia. Finally it traces the spirit's effects over the Party's history.

Ouyang's central move is to map the spirit onto the 'two leaps' of cognition. The early communists' practice carried them from perceptual to rational knowledge, which is the first leap. The second leap, from rational knowledge back into practice, is shown in the spirit's later influence on the Party's course. Ouyang argues that it is the common thread of the Party's 'spiritual lineage', from the Jinggangshan and Yan'an spirits to the poverty-alleviation spirit. It also spurs the Party's self-reform, drives the successive leaps in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and inspires the achievements Ouyang attributes to the Party across four historical periods.

Ouyang concludes that the founding spirit upholds materialism, since practice is the source and driving force of knowledge, and dialectics, since consciousness acts back on practice. It is described as a 'success code' of the Party's century of struggle and an inexhaustible spiritual resource for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article ends by calling on Party members to rally around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and to work toward a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want an example of how Party historians use epistemological categories to frame the official narrative of the Party's founding and century of history.
quoteEn: The great founding spirit of the Party both came from the extraordinary process of founding the Party and drove the Party's century of exploration and struggle, and it has stood the test of the Party's century of practice.
quoteZh: 伟大建党精神既来自创建党的非凡历程，又推动了党的百年探索、百年奋斗，经受了党的百年实践检验。

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A 32-character formula first put forward by Xi Jinping on 1 July 2021. It names the ideals and conduct attributed to the Party's early pioneers and is presented as the source of the Party's 'spiritual lineage'.

The official term for the series of named 'spirits' the Party says it formed in successive periods, such as the Jinggangshan spirit and the Yan'an spirit. Official accounts treat the founding spirit as their source.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official phrase for the Party's project of fitting Marxist theory to China's conditions and to each era. Official histories describe it as a series of 'leaps' from Mao Zedong Thought onward.
党的自我革命, a term stressed under Xi Jinping. It denotes the Party's claimed capacity to correct itself and maintain discipline through its own efforts.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since it was written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: An official goal of national revitalisation, tied to the aim of building a modern socialist country by the middle of the century.

keywords: great founding spirit of the Party
adapting Marxism to the Chinese context

t: Promoting positive interaction between high-quality development and high-level security
zh: 推动高质量发展和高水平安全良性互动
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in October 2025, asks how China should coordinate development and security. Ma and Zhang argue that the Party Central Committee's strategic deployment on this question rests on scientific principles. They hold that it should be pursued through a positive interaction between high-quality development and high-level security.

The piece has three parts: the philosophical logic of coordinating development and security, the supply of policy, and local practice. It draws on materialist dialectics and systems thinking, then turns to policy documents on hazardous chemicals and to provincial examples from Jiangsu, Gansu, Jiangxi and Jilin.

The authors read development and security as a unity of opposites. Development is dynamic and carries competition and risk, while security is relatively static and requires stability, so the two are in tension. Yet development guarantees security and security is the precondition of development. In policy terms, Ma and Zhang present "intrinsic safety" (本质安全), a preventive approach that removes risks at source without hampering development, as an effective measure. They cite documents such as the 14th Five-Year Plan for hazardous chemicals work safety (2022), and say Jiangsu, Gansu, Jiangxi and Jilin have issued intrinsic-safety measures across chemicals, mining, construction and water conservancy.

The authors conclude that China is gradually building a policy supply system for coordinating development and security, and that local governments are producing rich practice, with Jiangsu reporting falling accident numbers and deaths. Read the original if you want a brief official-style account of how intrinsic safety in work-safety governance is presented as an example of coordinating development and security.
quoteEn: Consolidating security through development and seeking development through security is the necessary choice in following materialist dialectics.
quoteZh: 在发展中固安全、在安全中谋发展是遵循唯物辩证法的必然选择。

glossary.explanation: An official goal since the late 2010s that shifts emphasis from growth speed to quality, innovation and efficiency.

glossary.literal: overall planning of development and security
glossary.explanation: A Party policy principle that treats economic development and national security as to be planned together rather than separately.
An engineering and safety-management concept of removing hazards at source through design, used here as a model of preventive governance.

t: Chinese modernization offers lessons for development in the Global South
zh: 中国式现代化为全球南方发展提供经验启示
paras: Xu Xiuli and Li Xiaoyun ask what Chinese modernization can contribute to development studies and to the Global South. They argue that it offers useful lessons for resolving three classic dilemmas in global development theory. The first is how to balance independent national development with integration into the international order. The second is how to handle relations among government, market and society so that they combine forces while keeping a productive tension. The third is how to "go out" into development cooperation while moving beyond colonial and hegemonic models toward a more equal community of development.

The article presents Chinese modernization as a driver of a "third academic transformation" in China, in which researchers move beyond a dependent centre–periphery position in global knowledge. It is organised in three sections, one per dilemma, each setting China's experience against comparative cases. These include African structural adjustment, Mexican and Venezuelan import substitution and "delinking", Argentina's instability, fragmented African states with strong civil-society organisations, and the divide between "big" and "small" development.

On the first dilemma, the authors argue that integration and sovereignty need not be opposed. They credit sustained reform and opening up, "selective learning" and keeping control of the development process, and they cite Deng Xiaoping's remark to the World Bank president. They contrast this with Africa, where adjustment programmes allegedly produced debt, aid dependence and unrest, and with Mexico and Venezuela, where radical delinking brought inflation and crisis. On the second, they present poverty reduction as a model in which government, market and society are embedded in one another, and they link Argentina's decline to weak political institutions. On the third, they describe China's "win-win" platforms, new institutions and global initiatives, together with "parallel experience sharing" that matches the partner's stage of development and treats partners as equals.

The authors conclude that developing countries should keep independent development as the core goal, integrate into the existing international system pragmatically and step by step, and allow trial and error. They should build an "effective government, efficient market and vigorous society" around priorities fixed for each stage, and draw on South–South cooperation's principles of no political conditions and mutual benefit. They also call on Global South states to revive the tradition of "uniting for self-strengthening". Read the original if you want a Chinese development-studies account of Chinese modernization, set against African and Latin American cases and framed for Global South audiences.
quoteEn: The precondition for an effective market is governance by a capable government.
quoteZh: 有效市场的前提是有为政府的治理。

glossary.explanation: The official Party-state term for China's own path to modernization, prominent in official discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as distinct from Western models.
A term for developing and emerging countries, mainly in Africa, Asia and Latin America. Chinese official discourse uses it to stress solidarity among these states.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Origins and discursive innovation of the concept of a "high-standard socialist market economy"
st: A conceptual-history study
zh: “高水平社会主义市场经济体制”概念的源流考释与话语创新
paras: Hu Rongtao and Peng Yiming ask where the concept of a "high-standard socialist market economy" (高水平社会主义市场经济体制) comes from and what is new about it. They note that existing scholarship has treated its challenges, features, logic and tasks but has paid little attention to its conceptual history. The article argues that the concept, presented as a "new type of relations of production" suited to new quality productive forces, took shape over a long process of Party exploration of the government–market relationship. In their account it is an original concept produced by the Two Integrations.

The article has three parts. The first traces the concept's discursive sources: the economic-system ideas of Marx, Engels and Lenin (including the New Economic Policy), late Qing and early Republican thinking on state and market (Wang Tao, Zheng Guanying, Liang Qichao, Sun Yat-sen, Zhang Jian), and early Communists such as Li Dazhao, Chen Duxiu and Cai Hesen. The second follows its formation from the 1930s planned-economy debates, through Mao Zedong, Chen Yun and Zhang Wentian, to the "socialist market economy" of the reform era. The third assesses its discursive innovation.

In the authors' reading, the formation runs from planning with some market elements, through a "planned commodity economy", to the socialist market economy system proposed under Deng Xiaoping and Jiang Zemin. Party documents then moved from the market's "basic role" to its "decisive role" and from "macro-control" to "better playing the role of government". The 19th Central Committee's Fifth Plenum formally introduced the "high-standard" formulation, and the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) placed it first among the reform priorities. The authors identify three innovations. It enriches the discourse through "upholding fundamental principles while innovating", and it criticises Western neoliberal economic discourse. It extends dialectical thinking on an "efficient market and a capable government". And it contributes to a "revolution in terminology" in the discourse of Chinese modernization, covering its desired form, its actual form and its means of realisation.

Hu and Peng conclude that the concept marks a more mature and settled basic economic system of socialism with Chinese characteristics. They also hold that it gives Chinese modernization an institutional content and offers legitimacy resources for the Party's long-term rule. They present building such a system as a necessary path for deepening reform comprehensively. Read the original if you want a detailed genealogy of this Party formulation and a view of how Chinese scholars present its conceptual history.
quoteEn: The concept of a "high-standard socialist market economy system" is an original, signature concept that results from combining Marxist thinking on economic systems with China's realities.
quoteZh: “高水平社会主义市场经济体制”概念是马克思主义经济体制思想与中国实际相结合的原创性标识概念

glossary.explanation: A formula in Party theory: combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with China's fine traditional culture. Xi Jinping stressed it in 2021–2023.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, describing advanced productivity driven by technological innovation and high-tech industries.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.pinyin: gāo shuǐpíng shèhuì zhǔyì shìchǎng jīngjì tǐzhì
glossary.explanation: A formulation first introduced at the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020) and made a reform priority at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It denotes a more advanced stage of the socialist market economy system.

glossary.en: an efficient market and a capable government
glossary.explanation: A Party formula for combining market mechanisms with active state intervention, which Xi Jinping has contrasted with neoliberal "big market, small government" thinking.
A phrase drawn from Engels, used in Chinese scholarship to mean that new concepts mark theoretical innovation in a discipline.

t: The methodology by which the "Second Integration" creates a new cultural organism
zh: “第二个结合”造就新的文化生命体的方法论探赜
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 8
paras: Ma Mingchong takes up a formula from Xi Jinping's 2023 speech on cultural inheritance and development: the combination of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture is not a "platter" or a physical mixture but a "chemical reaction" that produces an organically unified new cultural organism. The article asks what methodological foundations, components and functions lie behind this process. Ma argues that the Second Integration rests on a Marxist philosophy of practice and gives rise to five modes of thinking that serve the building of a socialist cultural power and Chinese modernization.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the philosophical basis: Marx's critical inheritance from Kant and Hegel, and the contemporary activation of traditional Chinese philosophical resources. The second presents the methodological components, namely strategic, historical, dialectical, systems and innovative thinking. The third considers the methodological functions, first as a window on the laws governing the building of socialist culture with Chinese characteristics, and then as a dialectical method for handling relations such as active and passive, tradition and modernity, and universal and particular.

In the first part, Ma reads Kant's cultural theory as bound to a dualism of subject and object, and Hegel's as the self-movement of the Absolute Spirit. Marx, in Ma's account, grounds culture in the material practice of the working people and thereby gives it subjective initiative and a practical ontology. Ma then argues that Chinese ideas can be reactivated on this basis, such as "the people are most important" becoming a people-centred philosophy of governance, and the ideal of great harmony becoming a community with a shared future for mankind. The five modes of thinking are described as an organic whole that dismantles "Western centrism", the "end of history" thesis and historical nihilism. Ma also rejects Karl Popper's reading of Marxism as economic determinism, stressing culture's independence and its reaction on the economy.

Ma concludes that the five dimensions of methodology form a rigorous theoretical system that supplies a philosophical coordinate for socialist cultural construction. He also presents it as offering a Chinese approach to global cultural governance and to a new form of human civilization. The article traces a historical line from Mao Zedong's "make the past serve the present" through Deng Xiaoping's cultural policy to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), which it describes as a move from "theoretical transplantation" to "independent innovation". Read the original if you want a detailed example of how Chinese Marxist scholars ground the Second Integration philosophically and tie it to claims about civilization and global order.
quoteEn: The new cultural organism created by the "Second Integration" uses the truth-power of Marxism to activate the genes of Chinese civilization and promotes the creative transformation and innovative development of fine traditional Chinese culture, marking a leap in the path of socialist cultural development with Chinese characteristics from "theoretical transplantation" to "independent innovation".
quoteZh: “第二个结合”造就的新的文化生命体，以马克思主义真理力量激活中华文明的基因，推动了中华优秀传统文化的创造性转化、创新性发展，标志着中国特色社会主义文化发展道路从“理论移植”到“自主创新”的跨越

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula, set out in 2023, for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. It is often paired with the first integration, that of Marxism with China's concrete realities.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and civilizational concept associated with Xi Jinping, calling for cooperation and shared interests among states.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official phrase describing the civilization that Chinese modernization is said to create, presented as an alternative to Western-led models.

t: The theoretical implications, institutional innovation and practical paths of "the Eight-Point Regulation changes China"
zh: “八项规定改变中国”的理论意蕴、制度创新与实践路径
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育), 2025 no. 8
paras: Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), the Central Committee headed by Xi Jinping has treated the Central Committee's Eight-Point Regulation on Party conduct as the opening move in governing the Party. Cai Zhiqiang and Xiao Ruining ask what theoretical meaning, institutional innovation and practical path this measure represents. They argue that, by using concrete behavioural bans as a "small entry point", it has reshaped the institutional framework of Party conduct and become a "golden calling card" of Party governance. In their view its significance goes well beyond conduct itself.

The article has three parts. The first places the regulation within the adaptation of Marxist Party-building theory to Chinese conditions, under three heads: the people-centred values of a Marxist party, new routes for the Party's self-reform, and a new paradigm of Party building. The second treats it as a revolutionary creation in governing the Party and the country, covering its roots in the Party's traditions, its institutional breakthroughs and its political functions. The third sets out four paths for implementation in the new era.

The authors argue that the regulation inherits the Party's fine style, from the Yan'an rectification to the "Two Musts", while changing the mode of governance. They say it moved from temporary, campaign-style requirements to a standing, closed-loop system of rule-making, inspection, accountability and improvement. It also combines inner-Party supervision with popular supervision, and joins the "first answer" (democracy) and the "second answer" (self-reform) to the Party's historical-cycle question. They describe it as a shift from guarding mainly against external threats such as "colour revolution" to a self-reforming type of Party building. They link conduct to corruption, noting that "wind and corruption" often appear together and need to be investigated together. They also credit it with restoring public trust and cutting the corrosive influence of capital on political power.

For implementation, the authors call for four steps. These are regular study and education; precise special campaigns against new, disguised forms of the "Four Undesirable Work Styles", using big data and similar tools; long-term institutions, including a responsibility system, tailored local rules, supervision loops, technology-enabled oversight and a culture of integrity; and systematic, coordinated governance that links the regulation to national and grassroots governance. They conclude that the regulation should be sustained until good conduct becomes custom, and built into Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a detailed Party-school account of how the Eight-Point Regulation is framed theoretically and how current anti-formalism and anti-corruption work is meant to be taken forward.
quoteEn: The formulation and implementation of the Central Committee's Eight-Point Regulation marks a shift in Marxist party building from mainly guarding against external risks such as "colour revolution" to a self-reform paradigm focused on the Party's own capacity for self-reflection.
quoteZh: 中央八项规定的制定和施行，标志着马克思主义政党建设从主要抵御“颜色革命”的外部风险防控，向聚焦主体自反性建构的自我革命型范式转变

glossary.explanation: A set of rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to improve Party and official conduct. It restricts extravagant banquets, official travel, meetings and publicity, and bureaucratic practices, and later received detailed implementing rules.
The four problems of formalism, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance, which the Party campaigns against in its conduct-building work.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party's capacity to correct its own problems. It is presented as the Party's answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.
The official name for China's current path of national development, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The evolution of ancient Chinese supervisory legislation and its lessons for today
zh: 古代监察立法的流变与当今镜鉴
paras: Shu Shaofu asks what the long history of supervisory (jiancha) legislation in imperial China can offer to present-day anti-corruption lawmaking. Starting from Xi Jinping's calls at the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection plenary sessions to continue national anti-corruption legislation and revise the Supervision Law, the author argues that the best of ancient supervisory law is part of fine traditional Chinese culture. Drawing on it, Shu contends, can help advance anti-corruption legislation and the effort to make officials unwilling, unable and not daring to be corrupt.

The article is a historical survey that moves through three stages. It first covers the "embryonic" stage from the pre-Qin period to the Qin, with the Rites of Zhou, the Lü Xing and the Qin bamboo slips from Shuihudi. It then traces the "flourishing" of local supervisory regulations from the Han through the Wei, Jin, Northern and Southern Dynasties, Sui and Tang. Finally, it examines the "maturing" of the system under the Song, Yuan, Ming and Qing, ending with the Qing Qinding taigui as the fullest supervisory code. A closing section draws lessons for today.

Shu's central claim is that supervisory law developed from provisions scattered inside criminal and administrative codes into stand-alone regulations and finally into comprehensive codes. Examples include the Han Six Articles for Inquiry, the Song rules for mutual monitoring among supervisory officials, and the Yuan regulations for establishing the censorate. The author stresses that these laws bound the supervisors as well as the supervised, and formed a network covering the centre and the localities. From this the author draws three lessons: keep revising and refining law, build a complete and well-connected body of regulations, and develop a supervisory culture.

Shu proposes keeping the Supervision Law up to date, especially against new and hidden forms of corruption. The author also calls for filling gaps in the law on anti-corruption procedure, oversight and remedies, and for amending the Legislation Law so that the National Supervisory Commission has equivalent legislative powers. Shu further proposes aligning the Supervision Law with the Criminal Procedure Law and the Audit Law, and cultivating a supervisory culture that draws on traditional integrity ideals. Read the original if you want a detailed dynasty-by-dynasty survey of ancient supervisory statutes, or want to see how Chinese legal scholars link historical precedent to current anti-corruption legislation.
quoteEn: Ancient Chinese supervisory legislation moved from rudimentary beginnings to completeness, and it also leaves rich inspiration and historical lessons for supervisory legislation in the new era.
quoteZh: 中国古代监察立法从草创走向完备，也为新时代监察立法留下丰富启示与历史镜鉴。

glossary.explanation: The term covers both imperial-era censorial oversight of officials and the modern supervisory system built around the National Supervisory Commission, which was created in 2018.
The 2018 law of the People's Republic of China that sets out the powers and procedures of supervisory commissions, which investigate public officials. It was revised in 2024.

glossary.pinyin: bù gǎn fǔ, bù néng fǔ, bù xiǎng fǔ
glossary.en: unwilling, unable and not daring to be corrupt
glossary.literal: not dare to be corrupt, not able to be corrupt, not want to be corrupt
glossary.explanation: A Party formula for a three-part approach to fighting corruption through deterrence, institutional constraints and moral-ideological cultivation, pursued together.
The Communist Party's top internal discipline body, which works closely with the state supervisory commission.

t: Writing the early industrial history of the Republic: a field report on the "156 Projects" research team
zh: 书写共和国早期工业发展史——“156项工程调研”项目组纪实
paras: This is a newspaper feature by a reporter for China Social Sciences Today (22 October 2025), based on interviews with the "156 Projects" research team at the Institute of Economics, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. The 156 Projects were the key industrial construction projects of the First Five-Year Plan period. Zhang presents them as the foundation of New China's industrialisation and reports on how the team has studied them. The article's thesis, in the team's words, is that reform of state-owned enterprises cannot simply copy a market template. It must balance historical experience, national strategy and social responsibility.

The report describes several years of fieldwork across more than ten provinces and cities, covering 30 key enterprises. It visits Yunnan Tin (Gejiu), North China Pharmaceutical, Lanzhou Petrochemical, Wuhan Iron and Steel, China First Heavy Industries, Harbin Turbine and Angang. The team is led by Zhao Xuejun, and Yu Wenhao is also quoted. Work was divided into overall, industry and regional-economy studies, and the team has gathered over a hundred types of enterprise materials.

Zhang highlights two of the team's moves. The first is method: a \"three-generation interview method\" with old, middle-aged and young technical and managerial staff. It is paired with cross-checking of Russian archives, factory gazetteers and meeting minutes where company records were incomplete or restricted. Zhang reports that this comparison led the team to conclude that the share of independent innovation, set against Soviet technical aid, was very high. The second is evaluation: the team says it moved beyond a \"GDP-only\" view of state firms. It stresses their contribution to core technology, supply-chain security, worker training, environmental upgrading and social stability. Zhao is quoted as saying efficiency is only one measure of such firms.

The article reports that draft manuscripts are done on topics such as the projects' construction and commissioning, their links with Luoyang and Anshan, and the steel and petrochemical industries. The team has also submitted policy recommendations. These include using state-owned enterprises' Party-history resources for education and balancing public-interest and corporate functions in reform. Zhang describes the projects' legacy as a spirit of self-reliance that still drives efforts to overcome technological chokepoints. Read the original if you want a journalistic, officially framed account of how this research project works and what conclusions it draws on state enterprise.
quoteEn: Through solid fieldwork, the research team has shown that state-owned enterprise reform cannot simply copy a marketisation template, but must seek a dynamic balance among historical experience, national strategy and social responsibility.
quoteZh: 调研组以扎实的调研工作证明，国企改革不能简单复制市场化模板，而需在历史经验、国家战略与社会责任间寻找动态平衡。

glossary.explanation: The key industrial projects built in the 1950s during the First Five-Year Plan (1953–57), largely with Soviet technical assistance. They covered steel, nonferrous metallurgy, coal, power, chemicals and machinery.
China's first five-year plan for economic development, 1953–1957, which prioritised heavy industry.
Colloquial term for key technologies on which China depends on foreign suppliers, who could cut off access.

t: Developing agricultural new quality productive forces requires attention to policy direction
zh: 发展农业新质生产力需关注政策方向
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 23 October 2025
paras: This short commentary asks what institutional and policy direction should guide the development of agricultural new quality productive forces. Zhang defines them as a new form of productive force, relying on modern science and technology, innovation and new organisational forms, and oriented towards digitalisation, intelligence, greening and integration. The author argues that policy should be adapted to local conditions and focused on a few key areas.

The article has two parts. The first explains why development must suit local conditions, covering regional differences, distinctive local industries and sustainability. The second sets out priority areas for policy: regional planning, agricultural technology support, fiscal, tax and financial measures, infrastructure and public services, and research and talent training.

Zhang's central claim is that respecting regional differences avoids one-size-fits-all policy and makes resource use more efficient while protecting the ecology. Examples include eco-livestock farming in the fragile west, flowers in Yunnan, and cotton and fruit in Xinjiang. The author calls for differentiated support: grain-producing areas would get farmland and seed-breeding support, specialty zones would get subsidies, tax relief and tailored credit, and mountain or remote areas would get suitable machinery, roads and remote services.

Zhang concludes that a sound institutional and policy framework for agricultural new quality productive forces matters greatly for implementing the rural revitalisation strategy. The author expects continued policy improvement to give rural revitalisation stronger momentum and to move agricultural and rural modernisation to a new stage. Read the original if you want a concise, policy-oriented overview of how agricultural new quality productive forces are being framed in Chinese development discussion.
quoteEn: Respecting regional differences is the basis for building an effective institutional and policy system; it helps avoid "one-size-fits-all" policies and makes agricultural development fit local realities better.
quoteZh: 尊重地域差异的原则，是制定有效制度政策体系的基础，有助于避免“一刀切”式的政策，使农业发展更加贴合各地实际情况。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than traditional resource-heavy growth. Here it is applied to agriculture.
A national strategy announced at the 19th Party Congress in 2017 to promote the development of rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.

t: Building a unified national market requires both breaking and establishing
zh: 建设全国统一大市场须破立并举
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2025, Xie Lijuan asks how the unified national market should be pushed deeper during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Xie argues that construction is moving from removing barriers to unifying rules and opening institutions, and that this will make the economic cycle flow more smoothly.

This short commentary starts from the basic requirement of "five unifications and one opening" and the shift in official wording from "accelerating" to "advancing in depth". It then takes up four areas: the modern circulation system, fair competition and market order, coordinated improvement of the business environment, and data as a factor of production.

Xie reads opening in two directions: internally, removing hidden institutional obstacles between regions; externally, using the domestic market to attract global factors and help national brands go abroad. Circulation is described as the core hub of the large market, and Xie calls for lower logistics costs, more efficient commerce and data empowerment. On competition, Xie cites the revised Anti-Monopoly Law and the Fair Competition Review Regulations, and reads the 2025 call to tackle "involution"-style competition as a calibration of corporate values. Xie also warns that regions competing alone on policy raise uncertainty for cross-regional business, and urges backward regions to close gaps faster.

Xie concludes that integrating data with traditional factors will lift factor-market integration and release consumption potential. A deeper unified market, in Xie's view, will let the huge domestic market offset external uncertainty and raise the quality and resilience of the dual circulation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Chinese economist frames current policy priorities for the unified national market.
quoteEn: Only when the gaps in business-environment improvement are narrowed to the minimum can the ease of cross-regional capital flow be maximised, effective investment expanded and a virtuous interaction with consumption potential created, so that the building of the unified national market can go steady and far.
quoteZh: 只有把营商环境优化差距压至最小，资本的跨区域流动便利才能放至最大，才能扩大有效益的投资，并与激发有潜能的消费形成良性互促，全国统一大市场建设方能行稳致远。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal, set out in a 2022 Party and State Council opinion, of removing local protectionism and market fragmentation so that goods, capital and factors flow freely across China.

The author's formula for the basic requirements: unified basic market institutions, infrastructure, government conduct, regulation and enforcement, and factor markets, plus continued opening up. It updates the earlier "five unifications and one removal".
An economic strategy that stresses a domestic cycle of production and consumption as the mainstay, interacting with international trade and investment.
Intense, often price-cutting competition that wastes resources without raising value. Official documents have called for curbing it.

t: The logic and practice of the digital economy empowering high-quality development
zh: 数字经济赋能高质量发展的逻辑与实践
paras: Gao Zhigang asks how the digital economy, described as a new economic form produced by the latest scientific-technological revolution and industrial transformation, drives high-quality development. The article, a newspaper commentary, argues that the digital economy embodies the internal requirements of the new development philosophy and delivers high-quality development through industrial upgrading and better allocation of production factors. It opens by citing Xi Jinping's calls to accelerate the digital economy and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) decision on building supporting institutions.

Gao cites figures showing the digital economy growing from 11.2 trillion yuan in 2012 to 53.9 trillion yuan in 2023, with core industries accounting for about 10% of GDP in 2024. The piece has three parts. The first links the digital economy to each of the five elements of the new development philosophy: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. The second sets out two implementation paths, industrial structure upgrading and factor allocation. The third lists weaknesses and policy proposals.

The core claim is that data, as a new production factor, combines with land, labour and capital and permeates production, distribution, circulation and consumption. In Gao's account, this lifts total factor productivity, lets lagging regions leapfrog, cuts energy use and emissions through industrial internet and monitoring networks, lowers barriers to cross-border trade and investment, and spreads education, healthcare and jobs more widely, contributing to common prosperity. In practice, Gao says, it raises industrial structure towards high-tech, high-value-added activity, and creates a cycle of precise matching, higher efficiency and multiplied value through platforms, algorithms and digital finance.

Gao concedes that China's digital economy remains big but not strong, citing weak governance, insufficient core technology innovation and shallow integration of the digital and real economies. The author proposes stronger top-level design and data legislation, new infrastructure, self-reliant digital technology innovation with support for leading firms, and faster digital industrialization and industrial digitalization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official-media economics links the digital economy to the new development philosophy and to current policy priorities.
quoteEn: The digital economy is not a simple stacking of technological tools, but provides powerful momentum for high-quality development by activating the "innovation gene" of the economic system.
quoteZh: 数字经济并非简单的技术工具叠加，而是通过激活经济体系的“创新基因”，为高质量发展提供强大动能。

glossary.explanation: An official goal since the late 2010s that shifts emphasis from fast growth to quality, efficiency and satisfying people's needs for a better life.
Xi Jinping's formulation of 2015 comprising innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, used as the guide to economic policy.
A stated socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, which Xi Jinping has made a central policy objective.
An economic measure of output growth not accounted for by increases in labour and capital inputs, often used to indicate efficiency and technological progress.

t: Empowering the high-quality development of women's causes through scientific and technological innovation
zh: 以科技创新赋能妇女事业高质量发展
paras: This newspaper commentary responds to Xi Jinping's keynote at the Global Leaders' Meeting on Women, held in Beijing on 13 October 2025. Wang takes up his call to use scientific and technological innovation to drive the high-quality development of women's causes. Wang argues that the call sums up Chinese practice, answers the risk of setbacks for women worldwide, and meets the need to seize the new round of technological and industrial change.

The article has two parts. The first reviews how technology has strengthened women's development in China, through policy support for women in science and through digital technology. The second turns to the international dimension and to what remains to be done.

Wang cites figures: 40 million women in science and technology in 2024, over 45% of the total; 2.846 million women in research and development, 1.692 million more than in 2012; and an upper age limit for a national young-scientist fund raised from 45 to 48. In the digital economy, the article reports that women make up over half of internet entrepreneurs and about a third of those in digital trade and livestreaming. Internationally, Wang points to China's Global AI Governance Initiative, a UN General Assembly resolution on AI capacity-building, a global centre for digital empowerment of women, and training courses for women from developing countries. Wang calls for stronger digital infrastructure, digital skills in national education, a gender-inclusive digital industry, and better protection of women's labour rights.

Wang concludes that China aims to build an open, fair and just environment for technological development. It would let women take part in and lead digital change, and would remove bias against women at the source of digital and intelligent technologies. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary links Xi Jinping's remarks on women to technology policy, with the statistics and initiatives it cites.
quoteEn: In future, digital infrastructure should be further consolidated and the gender gap closed, with women's digital literacy and skills built into the national education system, training made institutional and systematic, and specialised digital skills training provided for women with special needs.
quoteZh: 未来应进一步夯实数字基础设施，消弭性别鸿沟，将妇女数字素养和技能纳入国民教育体系，实现教育培训制度化、体系化，为特殊需求的妇女提供专门化数字技能培训。

glossary.explanation: An official goal since the late 2010s that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency of growth over speed alone. Here it is applied to women's causes.

t: Promoting high-quality development of the nationwide fitness programme
zh: 推动全民健身事业高质量发展
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2025, Hu Deping asks how China's national fitness programme can move to high-quality development. The commentary argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Party Central Committee has made nationwide fitness a national strategy, and that further progress now depends on improving the public service system behind it. Hu ties this to the aim of building China into a leading sports nation and a healthy China.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews what Hu describes as the vigorous growth of mass fitness, citing popular grassroots events such as the "Village Super League", "Village BA" and "Su Super League". The second discusses how to improve public services for fitness in line with the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). The third sets out directions for the coming 15th Five-Year Plan period, when a new National Fitness Plan (2026–2030) is being drafted.

Hu presents growth in three respects: participation, integration and novelty. The article cites official figures for the end of 2024: 4.8417 million sports venues, 3.0 square metres of venue space per person, and national physical-fitness monitoring covering all 31 provinces. On services, Hu calls for standards at national, sector and local level, a system of rules that is adjusted to changing public needs, and a mix of "an effective government" and "an efficient market" with social forces taking part. Hu then names remaining problems: uneven development between urban and rural areas, regions, groups and sports, and resources that are scattered and lack drive.

Hu proposes three lines of work: problem orientation, balanced and accessible provision, and coordinated integration. Fitness services should be equalised across groups and places, and Hu would use artificial intelligence, big data and cloud computing to match supply to demand. Fitness should also link up with health, education, tourism and other sectors under the "sports plus" idea, so that it does not circulate only within sport. Hu presents this as a contribution to Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style account of how Chinese policy discourse frames mass fitness, public services and health in the run-up to the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Nationwide fitness cannot simply circulate within the small circle of sport; it must give full play to its combined value and varied functions in raising public health, promoting people's all-round development, driving economic and social development and showing national cultural soft power.
quoteZh: 全民健身不能在体育的小圈子里“自循环”“小循环”，必须充分发挥全民健身在提高人民健康水平、促进人的全面发展、推动经济社会发展、展示国家文化软实力等方面的综合价值与多元功能

glossary.explanation: A national policy to promote mass participation in sport and exercise. It was raised to a national strategy after the 18th Party Congress, and it is governed by the National Fitness Regulations and successive five-year National Fitness Plans.
An official goal of making China a world leader in sport. It is linked in Party discourse to the slogan "when sport is strong, China is strong".
The official name for the Party's path of national development, set out in the 20th Party Congress report (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030. It is being drawn up in 2025, after the 14th Five-Year Plan period ends.

t: Understanding the "commonness" of the common values of all humanity
zh: 深刻认识全人类共同价值的共同性特征
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 24 October 2025, Wang Gonglong asks what is distinctive about the common values of all humanity (peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom) advanced by Xi Jinping. Wang argues that their defining feature is "commonness", and that this commonness is concrete, respects difference and serves the shared interests of humanity, in contrast to Western "universal values".

The short commentary opens by presenting the values as an original concept of Xi Jinping's diplomatic thought and a product of the Two Integrations. It then has two parts: the theoretical, historical and practical logics behind the commonness, and a contrast with Western "universal values".

Wang grounds the commonness in three logics. Theoretically, the six values express needs shared by people across systems, ideologies and faiths. Historically, citing Marx and Engels on world history, Wang says growing universal exchange lets values that serve common interests settle into shared ones. Practically, deepening interdependence and global challenges make the community with a shared future for mankind both a community of interests and of values. Wang says Western "universal values" rest on an abstract view of human nature, deny particularity and aim at uniformity, leading to "sameness without harmony". Wang also rejects the opposite view that values are wholly plural. Drawing on the dialectic of the general and the particular, Wang says the common values allow diverse interpretations and routes of realisation, and cites Marx and Engels to argue that Western universalism presents particular interests as general ones.

Wang concludes that promoting these values requires not imposing one's own values or models, distinguishing values from their forms of realisation, and respecting each country's own paths. Wang calls for the values to be embodied in practice that benefits each country's people. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic statement of how Chinese commentators distinguish the common values of all humanity from Western universalism.
quoteEn: The commonness of the common values of all humanity is a commonness that faces reality and responds to and solves real problems.
quoteZh: 全人类共同价值所具有的共同性，是直面现实、回应和解决现实问题的共同性。

glossary.literal: shared values of the whole of humankind
glossary.explanation: A formulation promoted by Xi Jinping since 2015 listing peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom as values shared across civilisations. Official texts present it as distinct from Western "universal values".
Official formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, presented as a vision of interdependent states pursuing shared security and development.
In official Chinese discourse, a term for Western claims that liberal-democratic values apply to all societies, usually used critically and in scare quotes.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Amplifying the multiplier effect of the deep integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation
zh: 放大科技创新和产业创新深度融合的乘数效应
paras: This commentary, first published in the Economic Daily in October 2025, asks how China can deepen the integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation. Yan Xiangbin takes up Xi Jinping's statement that the two are the basic path for developing new quality productive forces. Yan argues that the integration should be pushed to produce a "multiplier effect", meaning a non-linear amplification of innovation value, which would turn research results into real productive capacity and support high-quality development.

The piece has three parts. The first defines the multiplier effect and gives three reasons it matters. The second reviews evidence that science and industry already reinforce each other. The third sets out institutional measures. Yan stresses that artificial intelligence and other fast-moving technologies make the matter more urgent, and that China should draw on its super-large market and complete industrial system.

Yan defines the multiplier effect as the result of coupling the innovation chain with the industrial, capital and talent chains. The author gives three reasons it matters. It supplies endogenous growth momentum, since growth driven by inputs and scale is no longer sustainable. It supports autonomous and controllable industrial chains, because "chokepoint" problems partly stem from research stranded in laboratories. It offers a route from "low-end manufacturing" to "high-end leadership". As evidence, Yan cites 2024 R&D spending above 3.6 trillion yuan (2.68% of output), an enterprise invention-patent commercialisation rate of 53.3%, and 9.5% growth in high-tech manufacturing value added in the first half of 2025. The article also describes joint "technology communities" in intelligent connected vehicles as an example of industry feeding back into research.

Yan calls for institutional innovation so that "systemic coordination" replaces isolated development and two-way empowerment replaces one-way support. The proposals are enterprise-led, market-oriented evaluation of research results; diversified investment and financing for commercialisation; regular mechanisms for collecting and publishing industrial technology needs; stronger intellectual property protection and technology intermediaries; and a larger role for firms in setting research agendas, including specialised and innovative small and medium-sized enterprises. Yan also urges classified management of innovation and a culture that tolerates failure. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official economic commentary links new quality productive forces to innovation policy and the commercialisation of research.
quoteEn: Stimulating the multiplier effect of the deep integration of scientific and technological innovation and industrial innovation is not a simple addition of science and industry, but requires replacing "isolated development" with "systemic coordination" and "one-way support" with "two-way empowerment".
quoteZh: 激发科技创新和产业创新深度融合的乘数效应，并非科技和产业的简单叠加，而是要以“系统协同”替代“孤立发展”、以“双向赋能”替代“单向支撑”

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, emerging industries and innovation rather than by resource and capital inputs.
The official goal, set out since 2017, of shifting China's economy from fast, input-driven growth to growth based on efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
A colloquial term for key technologies or components on which China depends on foreign suppliers, which can be restricted by others.

glossary.en: specialised and innovative small and medium-sized enterprises
glossary.explanation: An official category of small and medium-sized firms that focus on niche markets with advanced technology. They receive policy support as potential leaders in key industrial links.

t: Accelerating the cultivation of a nationally integrated data market
zh: 加快培育全国一体化数据市场
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in October 2025, asks how China can turn its large stock of data and its wide range of application scenarios into economic momentum. Wang Xuhui argues that the answer lies in accelerating the cultivation of a nationally integrated data market. In the author's view, such a market would let data work as a multiplier on economic development during the 15th Five-Year Plan period.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out China's advantages in data volume and use cases, citing figures for 2023 and 2024 on data production, AI-related data growth, the digital economy's share of GDP and patents. The second explains why efficient allocation of data matters. The third proposes ways to make data marketable and valuable, and mentions ten provincial-level pilot zones for data factors.

Wang's central claim is that data, as a new type of production factor and a basis for new quality productive forces, can raise total factor productivity and help recombine technology, capital, labour and land. The author gives two reasons for building the market: it is needed for the new development pattern and high-quality development, and it is needed to win new advantages in international competition in the digital economy. Wang says the market should be unified, secure and open, and based on reciprocal cooperation. It should bring together public, enterprise and personal data, remove regional barriers and 'data silos', and build trusted-circulation mechanisms.

The author lists four tasks: speed up basic data institutions, including a structurally separated system of data property rights and rules for circulation and cross-border flows; strengthen data infrastructure; improve the quantity and quality of data supply through classified and graded management; and design a multi-level system of data trading venues with national, regional and sectoral platforms that complement and compete with one another. Wang says the market should let the market play the decisive role in allocating resources while the government plays its role better. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of China's data-market policy priorities, with the latest figures the author cites.
quoteEn: Accelerating the cultivation of a nationally integrated data market and raising the efficiency of market-based allocation of data are both an urgent task for releasing the value of data and a strategic move to turn China's vast data and rich application scenarios into new momentum for growth and new national competitive advantages.
quoteZh: 加快培育全国一体化数据市场，提升数据要素市场化配置的效率，既是加快释放数据要素价值的当务之急，也是推动我国海量数据与丰富场景优势转化为经济增长新动能和国家竞争新优势的战略举措。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, such as digital technology and AI, rather than resource-intensive growth.
A strategy announced in 2020 that centres on the domestic market ('dual circulation') while remaining open to international markets.
The official goal, set out since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth based on efficiency, innovation and sustainability.

t: The 14th Five-Year Plan period: solid steps forward for Chinese modernization
st: A dialogue with Wang Yiming, Vice Chairman of the China Center for International Economic Exchanges
zh: “十四五”：中国式现代化迈出坚实步伐——对话中国国际经济交流中心副理事长王一鸣
paras: This is an interview, published in the Economic Daily's "Dialogue with Economists" series, in which reporter Ouyang You questions Wang Yiming, Vice Chairman of the China Center for International Economic Exchanges. It takes stock of the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021–2025). Wang argues that, despite a severe external environment, China kept its economy stable and took solid steps in advancing Chinese modernization through high-quality development.

The conversation has four parts: achievements in scale, quality and structure; the shift in growth drivers and the upgrading of comparative advantage; the general lessons drawn from the period; and the outlook for the 15th Five-Year Plan. Wang supports the first part with figures on GDP, research spending, industrial structure, urbanisation, trade and China's contribution to world growth. He also reviews the new development philosophy under its five headings: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.

Wang holds that the new development philosophy was turned into concrete projects and reforms, and that China's old low-cost-labour advantage is giving way to new ones: an ultra-large market, a complete industrial chain, technological innovation, the digital economy and new energy. He presents the main lessons as "five must-coordinate relationships": an efficient market and a capable government; aggregate supply and demand; nurturing new and updating old growth drivers; improving the incremental and revitalising the existing; and raising quality while expanding total volume. He attributes the period's results fundamentally to the leadership of the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core.

Looking ahead, Wang describes the 15th Five-Year Plan period as a critical one for laying the base for basically realising socialist modernization. He lists external pressures, including a new technological revolution, slower world growth, supply-chain restructuring and what he calls US containment. He also lists domestic ones: weaker labour and capital contributions, a maturing industrialisation and urbanisation, and tougher green transition tasks. He calls for adhering to high-quality development, developing new quality productive forces according to local conditions, and treating Chinese modernization as the greatest political task. Read the original if you want an official-leaning economist's statistical review of the 14th Five-Year Plan and a view of the policy priorities for the next plan.
quoteEn: We must treat adhering to high-quality development as the unyielding priority of the new era, and treat advancing Chinese modernization as the greatest political task.
quoteZh: 必须把坚持高质量发展作为新时代的硬道理，把推进中国式现代化作为最大的政治

glossary.explanation: The official Party framing of China's development path toward a modern socialist country, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official economic policy goal, in place since 2017, that stresses innovation, efficiency, and balanced and green growth over rapid expansion in volume.
Five principles set out in 2015 as guides for development: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging and future industries.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2021–2025, the last in a series of medium-term plans.

glossary.en: an efficient market and a capable government
glossary.literal: effective market and government that acts
glossary.explanation: An official formula for the relationship between market and state in the socialist market economy, with the market allocating resources and the government correcting market failures.

t: Coordinating supply and demand: practical results and theoretical innovation
zh: 统筹供需的实践成效与理论创新
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in October 2025, Chen Yanbin examines the principle that China must "coordinate the relationship between aggregate supply and aggregate demand", put forward by Xi Jinping at the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference. Chen argues that this principle sums up the practice of macroeconomic governance since the 18th Party Congress (2012). In Chen's account, it also breaks through Western macroeconomic policy theory and contributes to building an autonomous Chinese system of economic knowledge.

The commentary has four parts. It first traces how understanding of supply–demand coordination deepened, then compares this with Western macro-policy theory. It next sets out three features of the new understanding and ends with policy proposals for reaching a higher-level dynamic balance of supply and demand.

Chen presents the Party's understanding as developing in three steps: supply-side structural reform to improve supply quality; demand-side management to expand domestic demand; and finally the combined push of both. Western theory, rooted in industrial-era economies and centred on short-term counter-cyclical demand management, is said to pay little attention to aggregate supply. Chen holds that it therefore struggles with multi-source supply shocks and with the data-driven changes of the digital economy, and that Western economies have been unable to escape weak growth since 2008. Chinese practice, by contrast, combines stabilisation, growth and structural policies ("three policies in one"), which the author says lets it handle both supply and demand shocks and lift potential growth. Chen also stresses expanding external as well as domestic demand, and keeping total supply at a reasonable level, citing the campaign against "involution-style" competition.

Chen calls for deepening supply-side structural reform through innovation and data as a production factor. On the demand side, Chen urges treating domestic demand as a long-term strategy, with measures on employment, incomes, social welfare, the consumption environment and the quality, efficiency and structure of investment. Chen also calls for greater consistency among monetary, fiscal, stabilisation, growth and structural policies. Read the original if you want to see how a CASS economist presents supply–demand coordination as an official theoretical innovation and policy agenda.
quoteEn: The key to coordinating the relationship between aggregate supply and aggregate demand lies in strengthening the consistency of direction among the various types of macroeconomic policy.
quoteZh: 统筹好总供给和总需求的关系，关键在于增强各类宏观政策的取向一致性。

glossary.explanation: A policy approach first put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015. It aims to raise the quality of supply, cut inefficient and low-end capacity, and expand effective, mid- to high-end supply.
Policy tools that expand and shape demand, especially domestic consumption and investment. Official texts pair it with supply-side reform as mutually complementary.
Intense, often price-cutting competition that yields little real gain and leads to overcapacity. The 2024 Central Economic Work Conference called for it to be tackled.
An annual meeting of Party and state leaders, usually held in December, that sets the economic agenda for the coming year.

t: How a small county became the "world's vegetable basket": an investigation of Anqiu, Weifang, Shandong
zh: 小县城如何变身“世界菜篮子”——来自山东潍坊安丘市的调查
paras: This is a field report from the Party newspaper Economic Daily, written by reporter Wang Jinhu. It asks how Anqiu, a landlocked county-level city in Weifang, Shandong, became known as the "world's vegetable basket". According to the report, Anqiu exports more than 600,000 tonnes of vegetables a year to over 80 countries and regions, and its farm exports have led Shandong's counties for 16 years. The article answers that Anqiu has followed a path of "ecology first, brand empowerment and alignment with international standards", which it presents as high-quality development in agriculture.

The report moves through three sections: the area's natural endowments, the building of an international "passport" of standards and traceability, and the spread of ecological farming. It draws on visits to farms and firms, with named farmers, managers and officials, and on figures supplied by them. Products covered include volcanic-soil millet, tomatoes, ginger, spring onions, garlic, sweet potato products and chicken skewers.

The core argument has three steps. First, natural conditions such as volcanic and selenium-rich soils, abundant sunshine and 500 years of ginger breeding give the produce its quality. Second, the report credits institutional innovation: a national base for technical trade measures and a real-time platform comparing standards of 56 trading partners, which it says warned firms six months ahead of Japan's tightened onion pesticide limits in March 2024. It also describes a "dual-code" system, an electronic safety code plus an ecological origin traceability code, which it says brings price premiums of 30 to 40 per cent. Third, the report describes a shift towards ecological farming and deep processing: organic fertiliser supplied at cost through a state-run mechanism, subsidies of up to 50,000 yuan per mu for new greenhouses, 1,397 farms converted, and 2,000-plus processed products. It also describes an integrated domestic and export "dual circulation" approach, with one standard for both markets.

The article concludes that Anqiu's experience rests on strict regulation to earn trust abroad, ecological transformation to create premium value, and extended value chains so that farmers gain most from the added value. It cites 60,000-plus smallholders linked to the export chain and 2.6 billion yuan in extra farmer income in 2024, and notes the local aim of moving from a major agricultural city to a strong healthy-food city. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially framed case study of a county-level export agriculture model, with local figures and named enterprises.
quoteEn: Anqiu's path is clear: rigid regulation lays the foundation of quality and wins the trust of international markets; ecological transformation multiplies value and builds the capacity for premium prices; and chain extension finally widens the channels to shared prosperity, making farmers the biggest beneficiaries of value added along the industrial chain.
quoteZh: 安丘的实践路径清晰。以刚性监管筑牢质量根基，赢得国际市场信任；以生态转型驱动价值倍增，塑造高端溢价能力，最终以链式延伸拓宽共富渠道，让农民成为产业链增值最大受益者。

glossary.explanation: An official slogan, prominent since 2017, for growth that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation rather than speed alone.
An economic strategy announced in 2020 that stresses the domestic market (internal circulation) while keeping links with international markets (external circulation).

t: Building a science and technology finance system suited to scientific and technological innovation
zh: 构建同科技创新相适应的科技金融体制
paras: Writing in Economic Daily on 10 October 2025, Guo Tianyong asks how China should build a financial system that fits its drive for technological innovation.
