Guo argues that science and technology finance is a key lever for strengthening national strategic scientific and technological strength and for upgrading the economy. It must be developed on the basis of China's national conditions and stage of development.

The commentary has three parts. It first sets out why science and technology finance matters, then reviews recent achievements and remaining problems, and finally proposes five measures. It draws on policy documents from 2024 and 2025 and on statistics for science and technology lending and bonds.

Guo argues that finance links capital to innovation and helps shift growth from factor-driven to innovation-driven. The article cites 44.1 trillion yuan in science and technology loans by June 2025, up 12.5 per cent year on year, and about 600 billion yuan in innovation bonds. Guo also lists problems: bank reluctance to lend to asset-light start-ups, weak venture capital with low private participation, and a tendency in government funds to invest heavily but manage poorly. The central claim is that China should not copy Western models. Banks, which hold about 90 per cent of financial-sector assets, should remain the main channel and adapt their products and risk assessment.

Guo's five proposals are to strengthen bank-led indirect finance, improve banks' ability to serve innovation, refine investment–loan linkage, make government investment funds more market-oriented and patient, and open direct financing channels through multi-level capital markets and private capital. Guo presents these as the basis of a science and technology finance system with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy approach to science and technology finance, with recent figures and a list of proposed measures.
quoteEn: A science and technology finance system with Chinese characteristics cannot copy Western models. It must build on the main role of indirect finance and comprehensively improve its concepts, mechanisms, products and risk control, so as to fit better the features of technology firms.
quoteZh: 构建具有中国特色的科技金融体系，不能照搬照抄西方模式，而要在充分发挥间接融资主渠道基础上，推动间接融资理念、机制、产品、风控等全面优化，更好适配科技型企业的发展特征。

glossary.explanation: Financial services and instruments aimed at supporting technological innovation and technology-based firms. The Central Financial Work Conference (2023) ranked it first among five 'big articles' of finance.
A mechanism that combines bank lending with equity investment in the same firm, so that banks share in the firm's growth.

t: Making better use of fiscal policy to boost consumption
zh: 更好发挥财政促消费的作用
paras: This commentary, published in the Economic Daily in October 2025, asks how fiscal policy can do more to lift household consumption at a time of weak domestic demand and greater external uncertainty. Ma and Yao argue that public finance, as a pillar of state governance, is a key lever for stimulating consumption and sustaining economic recovery. They set this within the strategic goal of expanding domestic demand, which this year's Government Work Report placed first among the year's tasks.

The article has two main parts. The first reviews what fiscal policy has done since the 18th Party Congress (2012) in four areas: income distribution and social security, structural tools for big-ticket consumption, services consumption, and green consumption. The second identifies remaining problems and sets out four sets of proposals: fiscal spending, tax structure, government investment, and fiscal-financial coordination. The authors illustrate the first part with figures from official sources.

The authors credit personal income tax reform, the merging of rural and urban residents' pension schemes in 2014, and rising basic pensions with strengthening consumer expectations. They cite 2024 ultra-long special treasury bonds for equipment renewal and consumer-goods trade-ins, and say these drew in more than 1.3 trillion yuan of related sales. They also report that services rose from 39.7% to 46.1% of per capita consumption spending between 2013 and 2024. Despite this, they say consumption remains structurally narrow and confidence is lacking, with weak primary healthcare, thin community elderly-care coverage and uneven public services between regions. Their proposals include more targeted transfers to low- and middle-income and flexibly employed groups, more spending on education, childcare, primary care and elderly care, and employment support schemes. They also propose a higher share of personal income tax from high earners, moving the consumption tax collection point to the retail stage and devolving part of it to localities, using fiscal funds to draw in private capital, and interest subsidies, risk-compensation funds and guarantees for consumer credit.

Ma and Yao conclude that fiscal resources should be allocated more precisely across supply and demand. They call for income security, tax optimisation, better service provision and expectation management, aiming at a mechanism in which fiscal support underpins, finance amplifies and the market responds. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of the fiscal measures China has used to stimulate consumption and the policy direction commentators close to the Party's economic policy debate propose next.
quoteEn: Boosting consumption is the key to keeping the economic cycle flowing; fiscal policy must play a better supporting and guiding role, tackle the pain points and difficulties that hinder consumption, further optimise the allocation of fiscal resources, and work on both the supply and demand sides together.
quoteZh: 提振消费是畅通经济循环的关键，需更好发挥财政的支持、引导作用，着力解决阻碍消费提振的痛点难点问题，进一步优化财政资源配置，从供需两端协同发力

glossary.explanation: The annual report delivered by the Premier to the National People's Congress. It sets the year's economic targets and tasks.
Long-maturity central government bonds issued for specific purposes outside the regular deficit. They have funded the Two New programmes.

t: Building a new system of high-quality, efficient services
zh: 着眼优质高效构建服务业新体系
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 17 October 2025, asks how China should build a new system for the services sector that is both "high-quality" and "efficient". Zhang Yingxi starts from Xi Jinping's call to build such a system and to integrate modern services deeply with advanced manufacturing and modern agriculture. The author argues that this is needed to extend industrial chains and add value, and to meet people's rising demand for better and more varied services. The task should be pursued together with high-quality development.

The piece has three parts. The first explains what is "new" about the new system, under three headings: innovation-driven growth, quality first, and structural coordination. The second sets out three relationships to manage: comprehensive advance versus breakthroughs in key areas, efficiency versus fairness, and domestic development versus opening up. The third proposes four practical paths: optimising supply, digital transformation, cross-sector integration and standards-building.

Zhang's central claim is that the "new" system is a systemic project, not an accumulation of new business forms. It combines technological innovation, such as AI and big data, with institutional change such as simpler approvals and better standards. Quality governance should run from standard-setting to evaluation, with policy support so that "high quality, high price" becomes normal in the market. Coordination should link sectors (technology, finance, logistics), supply chains, regions and industries. On efficiency and fairness, the author holds that the two reinforce each other, citing online education for remote areas, vocational training and smart elderly care. On domestic and external development, Zhang points to the huge domestic market, more open market access, and wider reach for Chinese services standards abroad.

The practical proposals include strengthening producer services such as R&D, logistics and finance, and personalising consumer services. They also include building AI-native firms and new consumption scenarios, developing integrated models such as culture-tourism and blockchain-based farm-to-table supply chains, and filling standards gaps in elderly care, childcare, domestic services and digital services. Zhang also calls for a feedback loop of implementation, evaluation and improvement, backed by sanctions for dishonesty and mechanisms for exiting the industry. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of current Chinese policy thinking on services-sector upgrading.
quoteEn: The building of the new services system concentrates a profound renewal in development philosophy, structural functions and operating mechanisms.
quoteZh: 服务业新体系的构建，集中体现了发展理念、结构功能和运行机制上的深刻革新。

glossary.explanation: An official policy goal since the late 2010s that shifts emphasis from fast growth to quality, efficiency and innovation in the economy.
Services that support production, such as R&D and design, logistics and finance, as distinct from services consumed directly by households.
Services aimed at everyday life and household consumption, such as elderly care, childcare, tourism and domestic services.

t: The connotations and path of agricultural modernization with Chinese characteristics
zh: 中国特色农业现代化的内涵和路径
paras: This commentary, first published in the Economic Daily in October 2025, asks what distinguishes China's agricultural modernization and how it should be advanced. Tu Shengwei, a researcher at a state macroeconomic research institute, builds on Xi Jinping's statements that there can be no national modernization without agricultural and rural modernization, and that modernizing agriculture is the basic requirement for building a strong agricultural country. Tu argues that, although agricultural modernization has features common worldwide, there is no universal standard, and China has followed a path of its own.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out five features of the Chinese path. The second identifies five new requirements arising from changes in the domestic and external environment for agriculture, rural areas and farmers. The third proposes four key measures. It is a short policy-oriented commentary and does not engage in extended theoretical debate.

Tu's five features are reliance on the two-tier operating system (household contract operation as the base, combined with collective management), the principal position of farmers, coordination between an efficient market and a proactive government, the long-term coexistence of large and small operations, and the fusion of farming-culture heritage with green development. The new requirements are cultivating new quality productive forces in agriculture, deepening reform to strengthen endogenous momentum, smoothing circulation between industry and agriculture and between city and countryside, promoting green and low-carbon development, and safeguarding agricultural industrial security amid protectionism and geopolitical conflict. Tu holds that agricultural modernization is the foundation of Chinese modernization and determines its quality.

For action, Tu calls for strengthening food security through the strategies of storing grain in the land and in technology, adapting new quality productive forces to local conditions with a focus on core technologies such as seed sources and key machinery, building a modern rural industrial system by integrating primary, secondary and tertiary industries, and improving market-based allocation of factors. On land, Tu proposes orderly pilots extending the second round of land contracts by 30 years on expiry, stabilising contract relations, and exploring voluntary compensated exit from the 'three rights'. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the current official framing of agricultural modernization in China and its policy priorities.
quoteEn: China has not adopted a single model of large-scale operation and heavy mechanised work, but insists that agricultural operations be large where large suits and small where small suits.
quoteZh: 我国没有采取单一的大规模经营、大机械作业模式，而是坚持农业经营规模宜大则大、宜小则小

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path of modernization, promoted by the Communist Party especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022), presented as distinct from Western models.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by innovation, especially in science and technology, rather than by traditional growth models.
The rural basic economic system formed in the reform era, combining household contract operation on collectively owned land with collective-level unified management and services.
A standard shorthand in Chinese policy for agriculture, the countryside and peasants as a single policy field.

glossary.pinyin: cáng liáng yú dì, cáng liáng yú jì
glossary.en: storing grain in the land and in technology
glossary.literal: store grain in land, store grain in technology
glossary.explanation: An official food-security strategy that stresses protecting farmland and advancing agricultural technology to secure long-term grain production capacity.
An official goal of building China into a country strong in agricultural supply, technology, equipment and industry, emphasised in Party documents since 2022.

t: Using fiscal policy to serve and underpin medium- and long-term planning
zh: 发挥财政作用服务和支撑中长期规划
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in October 2025, as the 14th Five-Year Plan ends and the 15th is being drafted, Lü Wei asks how public finance can best serve and support medium- and long-term planning. The commentary argues that finance is a pillar of national governance, and that the plan should set direction while fiscal policy provides the guarantee. Lü calls for macro policies to work in step with development planning so that plan decisions are carried out in practice.

The article is organised around three roles that Lü assigns to fiscal policy: a foundational role, an institutional role and a guaranteeing role. Each role is tied to concrete policy areas. It opens with a statement from Xi Jinping on how the 15th Five-Year Plan period should be planned, and it proceeds as a list of policy recommendations.

Under the foundational role, Lü says fiscal policy should drive high-quality development in four ways. It should build innovation momentum through more basic-research funding, tax incentives and support for new quality productive forces. It should back a comprehensive green transition through incentives and a green tax system. It should widen the domestic circulation by shifting fiscal emphasis towards people's livelihoods and consumption. And it should promote common prosperity through inclusive social security and redistribution. Under the institutional role, Lü treats deepening fiscal and tax reform as the key step: zero-based budgeting and performance management, clearer central–local fiscal relations with more local own revenue and more general transfers, and a modern tax system based on statutory taxation. Under the guaranteeing role, Lü distinguishes anticipatory from binding plan targets and calls for better management of fiscal resources. Lü also calls for closer coordination of fiscal and financial policy, and for removing institutional bottlenecks such as tax rules that hinder a unified national market and burdens on private firms.

Lü concludes that deeper fiscal and tax reform, together with coordinated policy tools, will give the plan the financial and institutional backing it needs. The piece is a policy-oriented statement of how the economic establishment frames the fiscal agenda for the 15th Five-Year Plan. Read the original if you want a compact outline of the fiscal priorities that Chinese commentators link to the 15th Five-Year Plan, including budget, central–local and tax reform.
quoteEn: Finance is the foundation and an important pillar of national governance, and a sound fiscal and tax system is the institutional guarantee for optimising resource allocation, safeguarding a unified market, promoting social fairness and achieving lasting national stability.
quoteZh: 财政是国家治理的基础和重要支柱，科学的财税体制是优化资源配置、维护市场统一、促进社会公平、实现国家长治久安的制度保障。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to productivity growth driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging and future industries.
The official goal, set out since 2017, of moving the economy from rapid expansion towards efficiency, innovation, green growth and better living standards.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, stressed under Xi Jinping. It is linked to narrowing income, regional and urban–rural gaps.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, which succeeds the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021–2025).
A strategy announced in 2020 that makes domestic demand and internal supply chains the main driver of growth, supported by international circulation.

t: Doing economic work in accordance with the new development philosophy
zh: 遵循新发展理念做好经济工作
paras: This commentary, first published in the Economic Daily in October 2025, asks how officials should carry out economic work under the new development philosophy. Zhou argues that the philosophy, made up of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, is the most important of the theories advanced since the 18th Party Congress (2012). In Zhou's account it plays a strategic, programmatic and guiding role in the new journey of building a modern socialist country. Zhou ties the argument to a Political Bureau meeting at the end of July, which called on leading cadres to adopt a correct view of political achievements.

The article has three parts. The first goes through the five concepts one by one. For each it sets out recent achievements, remaining problems and tasks ahead. The second part addresses how to turn the philosophy into practice, through systemic coordination, stronger cadre capability and institutional safeguards. The third part sets out what a correct view of political achievements means for leading cadres.

Zhou's central claim is that the five concepts form one interconnected whole and cannot be pursued separately. Innovation must be balanced against regional coordination and ecological protection. Fiscal, monetary and industrial policy should work together, and the Yangtze River Delta is offered as an example of coordination. The most extended section lists the attitudes required of cadres. They should treat benefiting the people as the greatest achievement, seek progress while maintaining stability, and reject formalism and "vanity projects". They should adapt policy to local conditions, think systemically, and treat the country as "one chessboard". Zhou criticises GDP-centred thinking, excessive local debt, blind expansion into new energy vehicles and big data, and "involutionary" competition among localities over investment. Zhou calls for a unified national market and for evaluation indicators that give more weight to innovation, environment and livelihoods.

Zhou concludes that a leader's view of political achievements is bound up with their view of development. Only by holding the right values, strategic composure, a practical working style and a systemic outlook, the author says, can the new development philosophy become high-quality development. Zhou presents this as a foundation for the 15th Five-Year Plan period and for socialist modernization. Read the original if you want a detailed example of how official commentary links the new development philosophy to cadre evaluation, local-government behaviour and the economic priorities for the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Leading cadres must change the traditional view of political achievements and adopt one consistent with the new development philosophy of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, so that a scientific value orientation guides economic work.
quoteZh: 领导干部必须改变传统政绩观，树立与创新、协调、绿色、开放、共享的新发展理念相契合的政绩观，以科学的价值导向引领经济工作实践。

glossary.explanation: A framework put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015 that names five principles for development: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. Official texts treat it as a guide for economic policy.

The values by which officials judge their own work and are judged by the Party. Official discourse has repeatedly criticised a narrow focus on GDP growth and urged a "correct" view that stresses people's welfare and long-term results.
An official goal, in use since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to development that emphasises quality, efficiency and sustainability.
A term used in recent official discourse for wasteful, mutually damaging competition, here among local governments competing for investment through subsidies and tax incentives.

t: The accelerating evolution of changes unseen in a century and high-standard opening up
zh: 百年变局加速演进与高水平对外开放
paras: Writing in Economic Daily on 22 October 2025, Hong Junjie asks how China should respond to what official discourse calls the accelerating "changes unseen in a century". The commentary argues that closing off cannot meet these changes and that China must steadfastly pursue high-standard opening up. In Hong's account, such opening up shapes new development advantages, turns China's development into opportunities for other countries and creates a favourable external environment for Chinese modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first describes four trends: a rebalancing of the international political order as Global South countries rise, a deep adjustment of the economic development paradigm under artificial intelligence and new energy, severe challenges for global governance, and more frequent clashes between civilizations. The second explains, from the standpoint of historical materialism, why opening up is the right response. The third sets out four practical directions for advancing it.

Hong argues that the core of the present upheaval is a deep adjustment of the relations of production and the economic base. High-standard opening up is said to do four things: solve development problems and support high-quality development; build a strong science and technology country through open cooperation; take part in reforming global governance; and promote mutual learning among civilizations, thereby refining a "Chinese approach" to the changes. Hong presents opening up and security as one organic whole, to be handled with systems thinking and bottom-line thinking.

For action, Hong calls for steadily expanding institutional opening up, aligning domestic rules with high international standards and countering Western "small yard, high fence" containment. Hong also proposes a comprehensive pattern of opening up that coordinates regions and platforms such as pilot free trade zones, and wider multilateral and bilateral cooperation, including a network of high-standard free trade areas and unilateral opening to the least developed countries. The fourth direction is to put the four global initiatives (on development, security, civilization and governance) into practice, in support of a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese university president links the "changes unseen in a century" to the official case for high-standard opening up.
quoteEn: We must persist in advancing high-standard opening up, and meet the uncertainty of the changes unseen in a century with the certainty of high-quality development.
quoteZh: 必须坚持推进高水平开放，以高质量发展的确定性应对百年变局的不确定性。

glossary.literal: great changes not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese Party discourse since about 2017 to describe a period of major shifts in the global balance of power, technology and governance.
The official policy of widening China's openness to the world through better rules, institutions and platforms, as part of reform and opening up.
Opening that goes beyond tariffs and market access to align domestic rules, regulations, management and standards with international ones.
A term for developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America, which Chinese official discourse presents as a rising force in world affairs.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of a world order based on cooperation and shared interests, which the Chinese government promotes in foreign policy.
The Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilization Initiative and Global Governance Initiative, proposed by Xi Jinping between 2021 and 2025.

t: The historical position, rich connotations and contemporary value of the Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era
zh: 新时代党的治疆方略的历史方位、丰富内涵和时代价值
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 15 October 2025, this commentary takes up Xi Jinping's call of 24 September to implement the Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era "completely, accurately and comprehensively". Su Cheng argues that this requires grasping the strategy's historical position, its rich connotations and its contemporary value. The author presents the strategy as the concentrated expression of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era on Xinjiang work.

The article has three sections. The first places the strategy in the era that began with the 18th Party Congress (2012) and in Xinjiang's role in national rejuvenation. The second sets out its content, including the "eight adherences" and five guiding principles. The third assesses its value in guidance, theory and international example, and closes by pointing to the achievements of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region over its 70 years.

On historical position, Su describes Xinjiang as a security barrier in the north-west, a gateway for opening to the west, an energy and agricultural base and a core area of the Silk Road Economic Belt. The author states that terrorism, separatism and religious extremism, together with Western forces that fabricate a so-called "Xinjiang issue", heighten its strategic importance. On content, Su lists the "eight adherences", including social stability and lasting peace and order as the overall goal, forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, the sinicisation of religion and high-quality development. The guiding principles are governing Xinjiang by law, stabilising it through unity, enriching it through culture, building it through prosperity and building it for the long term. Su reads the strategy as showing Marxist dialectics: balancing the two-sided and the focal, the whole and the part, and continuity and innovation.

On value, Su claims the strategy offers scientific guidance, enriches border governance theory by tying frontier regions to national strategy, and gives multi-ethnic states a "Chinese solution". The author asserts that it curbs terrorism and extremism at source while protecting citizens' basic rights and freedoms. Su concludes that Xinjiang's achievements demonstrate the strategy to be entirely correct and show the strength of the Party's leadership and of China's path on ethnic questions. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative-style statement of how official Chinese commentary frames Xinjiang policy in 2025.
quoteEn: The Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era is an organic unity of the logic of the times, theoretical logic, historical logic and practical logic.
quoteZh: 新时代党的治疆方略是时代逻辑、理论逻辑、历史逻辑、实践逻辑的有机统一

glossary.pinyin: xīn shídài dǎng de zhì Jiāng fānglüè
glossary.en: the Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era
glossary.literal: the Party's Xinjiang-governing strategy of the new era
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's policy framework on Xinjiang since the 18th Party Congress (2012), associated with Xi Jinping. It combines a general goal, eight principles and five guiding lines of work.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: firmly cast the consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official formula for ethnic policy, promoted since the late 2010s, that stresses a shared national identity among all ethnic groups. It is presented as the main line of ethnic work.

glossary.en: social stability and lasting peace and order
glossary.literal: social stability and long-term order and peace
glossary.explanation: The overall goal officially set for Xinjiang work. It pairs present-day stability with long-term security.

glossary.literal: Chinese-isation of religion in our country
glossary.explanation: An official policy requiring religions in China to adapt to Chinese culture and socialist society, under Party leadership.
An official economic goal, prominent since 2017, that stresses quality, innovation and balance over growth rates alone.

t: Correctly grasping the relationship between commonality and difference
zh: 正确把握共同性和差异性的关系
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in October 2025, takes up a principle Xi Jinping set out at the 2021 Central Conference on Ethnic Affairs: that ethnic work must correctly handle the relationship between commonality and difference. Chu argues that the two stand in a dialectical unity. Commonality presupposes difference, and difference is oriented towards commonality, so the Party's ethnic work can be done well only if both are handled properly.

The article first sketches the historical formation of a pluralistic, integrated Chinese nation. It then treats the two sides in turn: increasing commonality, and respecting and accommodating difference. It closes by drawing on historical experience and the Party's adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

On commonality, Chu holds that it is not homogenisation but the largest common denominator produced by exchange among ethnic groups. It rests on the 'four togethers' community concept and the 'five identifications' (with the motherland, the Chinese nation, Chinese culture, the Party and socialism with Chinese characteristics). On difference, Chu says customs, culture and arts should be protected and passed on, and cites a figure that over one-third of China's UNESCO intangible heritage items come from minorities. Chu adds that commonality must remain dominant: difference must not weaken it, and Han chauvinism and local ethnic nationalism are opposed. Differentiated regional support policies are proposed.

Chu concludes that forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation requires upholding the Party's overall leadership and increasing commonality while respecting difference. The aim is to strengthen the ideological, social, cultural-psychological and security foundations of ethnic unity in support of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party-school framing of ethnic policy and its key slogans.
quoteEn: It should be noted that commonality is not homogenisation or uniformity, but the largest common denominator that emerges from continuous exchange and mutual learning among ethnic groups in the course of modernisation.
quoteZh: 需要注意的是，共同性不是同质化、同一化，而是各民族在现代化进程中不断交流互鉴所呈现出来的最大公约数。

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: cast a firm consciousness of the Chinese national community
glossary.explanation: Official guiding line of ethnic work since the 2010s, stressing a shared national identity across all ethnic groups. It was emphasised at the 2021 Central Conference on Ethnic Affairs.
Required identification with the motherland, the Chinese nation, Chinese culture, the Communist Party and socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Official national goal of restoring China's strength and standing, central to Xi Jinping-era discourse.

t: Forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation and building a modernized socialist Xinjiang
zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识 建设社会主义现代化新疆
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 17 October 2025, shortly after Xi Jinping led a central delegation to the celebrations of the 70th anniversary of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region (September 2025), Bu Lingquan sets out how Xinjiang should carry out its work in the new journey of building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation. The author argues that Xinjiang must fully, accurately and comprehensively implement the Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era, centred on forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, in order to build a harmonious, prosperous, civilised, secure and ecologically sound modernized socialist Xinjiang.

The commentary is a Party-line policy exposition in three parts. The first deals with forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation as the main thread of work. The second covers the overall goal of social stability and lasting peace and order, and the five pillars of the governing strategy. The third deals with Xinjiang's role in the national picture and the contribution it is to make to Chinese modernization. Throughout, Bu draws on Xi Jinping's statements.

In the first part, Bu calls for deepening education in ethnic unity and progress, promoting interaction, exchange and integration among ethnic groups through the embedding of communities in space, culture, economy, society and psychology, and carrying forward fine traditional Chinese culture, citing heritage sites such as Jiaohe and Niya. The second part presents the strategy as governing Xinjiang by law, ensuring stability through unity, enriching Xinjiang through culture, making the people prosperous, and long-term building of Xinjiang. In Bu's account this includes opposing ethnic separatism and religious extremism and teaching that Xinjiang has been an inseparable part of Chinese territory since ancient times. The third part calls for developing distinctive industries, new quality productive forces, cultural tourism, ecological protection, the core area of the Silk Road Economic Belt, and improved livelihoods.

Bu concludes that Xinjiang should anchor itself to the "five major strategic positions" assigned by the Centre, including a gateway for opening to the west, an energy and resource base, and a barrier for national geopolitical security. The author calls for shifting from "blood transfusion" assistance to "blood-making" co-existence, so that people of all ethnic groups share in development. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative statement of how Party-aligned scholars in Xinjiang present current policy priorities, framed around the Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang.
quoteEn: Forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation and advancing the building of that community is Xinjiang's unshirkable historical task and political responsibility.
quoteZh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识、推进中华民族共同体建设，是新疆义不容辞的历史任务和政治责任。

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: cast firm the consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A formulation promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and made the main thread of ethnic work in the new era. It stresses a shared national identity above ethnic identities.

glossary.pinyin: xīn shídài dǎng de zhì Jiāng fānglüè
glossary.en: the Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era
glossary.explanation: The official body of policy ideas on Xinjiang attributed to Xi Jinping, with the overall goal of social stability and lasting peace and order. It is summarised as governing by law, ensuring stability through unity, enriching Xinjiang through culture, making the people prosperous, and long-term building.
A policy line promoting cultural activities and education to strengthen identification with Chinese culture and the Chinese nation among Xinjiang's population.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological innovation and emerging industries rather than traditional resource-heavy expansion.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, with features such as common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature.

keywords: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation

t: Understanding the rich meaning and practical requirements of "investing in people"
zh: 深刻理解和把握“投资于人”的丰富意蕴和实践要求
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily, takes up the policy concept of "investing in people" (投资于人). The 2025 government work report called for more funds and resources to go to people's livelihoods, and Xi Jinping has asked that "investing in things" be tightly combined with "investing in people". Sun and Zhang argue that the concept is a historically necessary response to current conditions and that it must be put into practice systematically. They present it as important for high-quality development and for building a modern socialist country.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the context in which the concept appeared. The second analyses its scientific meaning. The third lists its practical requirements. The authors draw on Marx and Engels on the all-round development of human capacities, on Xi Jinping's statements on talent, and on official economic language.

The authors give three grounds for the concept: the Marxist aim of the free and all-round development of the person, the shift from factor-driven growth to innovation-driven high-quality development, and global competition that they say is ultimately competition over talent. Its meaning has three sides. Human resources are recast from a "cost" into "capital". Investment is paired between "hard skills" (education, vocational training, digital literacy) and "soft welfare" (social security, healthcare, childbirth support). Individual development and social value are said to reinforce each other. The authors stress that investing in people does not oppose investing in things. They say it should balance livelihood-oriented and productive investment and contribute to common prosperity.

For practice, Sun and Zhang call for spending to be tilted towards livelihood areas, in light of the change in the principal contradiction in Chinese society. They also call for continuous investment across the life cycle, with coordination between government, market and society. Other proposals are a shift from scale-oriented to quality-oriented investment using big data and closer university–industry ties, a social culture that honours labour and skill, and talent evaluation and pay systems based on contribution. They add a dynamic system of monitoring and feedback, since investment in people is not a one-off outlay. Read the original if you want to see how the concept of "investing in people" is being explained in Party-state media and which policy measures it is linked to.
quoteEn: "Investing in people" is not a one-off outlay but a dynamic management process that requires continuous monitoring, evaluation and adjustment.
quoteZh: “投资于人”并非一次性投入，而是一个需要持续监测、评估和调整的动态管理过程

glossary.explanation: A policy slogan featured in the 2025 government work report. It calls for more funds to go to employment, incomes, consumption, education, healthcare and elderly care, and it is paired with "investing in things" (投资于物).
The official term for a growth model that prioritises innovation, efficiency and sustainability over scale and speed. It has been the stated central task of China's economic work since 2017.
A socialist goal, emphasised under Xi Jinping, of prosperity shared by all. It is linked to narrowing gaps in income and public services.

t: Understanding the institutional advantages shown by Five-Year Plans
zh: 深刻认识五年规划彰显的制度优势
paras: Writing in the People's Daily as the 14th Five-Year Plan period nears its end, Wang Yiming asks what institutional advantages China's Five-Year Plans display. Wang notes that such plans are neither unique to China nor invented there, but contends that China alone has kept compiling and implementing them in succession. The article argues that the plans are embedded in the system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and yield five advantages, which it credits with an economic development "miracle" and long-term social stability.

The article is organised around five headings: upholding the centralised and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee; concentrating resources on major undertakings; combining an efficient market with a capable government; "one blueprint followed through to the end"; and treating the whole country as a single chessboard. Each section opens with a statement by Xi Jinping and then draws on the history of the 14 plans since 1953, from the first plan's heavy-industry priority and 156 key projects to reform-era changes and the post-2012 period.

Wang's central claim is that the plans work as the vehicle that turns Party strategy into state will and mobilises resources. On resource concentration, the author says the plans define each period's "major undertakings" and then use sectoral and regional plans to carry them out, citing the new national system for science and technology and a rise to tenth place in the Global Innovation Index. On market and government, Wang traces the shift from mandatory to guiding, strategic plans, and says the plans now set long-term direction and expectations while resting on market mechanisms. Wang adds that continuity across plans expresses strategic resolve and a relay-race spirit, and that regional strategies and a unified national market avoid duplicated construction and market fragmentation.

Wang concludes that, amid what the article calls profound global change, the advantages of the Five-Year Plans must be upheld and used well as the 15th Five-Year Plan is drawn up. The aim is to gather national strength for building a modern socialist country and advancing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an authoritative Party-aligned account of how Five-Year Planning is presented as a system and what themes may shape the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: The Five-Year Plan is an important form through which the concentration of efforts on major undertakings is realised.
quoteZh: 五年规划是集中力量办大事的重要实现形式。

glossary.literal: concentrate strength to do big things
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Party discourse for the socialist system's capacity to pool national resources behind priority projects. Xi Jinping has called it a key advantage of China's system.

glossary.zh: 有效市场和有为政府相结合
glossary.pinyin: yǒuxiào shìchǎng hé yǒuwéi zhèngfǔ xiāng jiéhé
glossary.en: combining an efficient market with a capable government
glossary.literal: effective market and promising/active government combined
glossary.explanation: Official formula for the relationship between market and state in the socialist market economy. It pairs the market's decisive role in allocating resources with a strategic role for government.

glossary.en: one blueprint followed through to the end
glossary.literal: draw one blueprint to the end
glossary.explanation: A slogan stressing continuity of strategy across successive leaderships and plan periods.

glossary.en: treating the whole country as a single chessboard
glossary.literal: the whole country as one game of chess
glossary.explanation: A principle of coordinating regions and sectors under overall national planning rather than letting each pursue local interests.
The official name for the Party's model of national development, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official term for mobilising state, market and research institutions nationwide to achieve breakthroughs in key technologies.

t: Understanding and implementing the Global Governance Initiative from a systematic and holistic perspective
st: Study notes on volumes one and two of Xi Jinping's "On Upholding Comprehensively Deepening Reform"
zh: 从系统和全局把握践行全球治理倡议
zhSub: 学习习近平总书记《论坚持全面深化改革》第一卷、第二卷
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 10 October 2025, is a study piece on the Global Governance Initiative that Xi Jinping put forward at the "Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Plus" meeting. Sun Jisheng, a vice president of China Foreign Affairs University, argues that the initiative is a further original contribution to Xi Jinping's diplomatic thought. In Sun's account it offers Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to reforming global governance at a time when, as Xi put it, governance has reached a new crossroads.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the initiative's core concepts as answers to who governs, how, and for whom. The second places the initiative within the four global initiatives, on development, security, civilization and governance. The third proposes how to put it into practice, and cites support from several countries and from UN Secretary-General Guterres.

Sun presents five core concepts. Sovereign equality is the first precondition. International rule of law is the fundamental safeguard, and the author criticises double standards and the imposition of a few countries' \"house rules\". Genuine multilateralism is the basic path, with the UN at its centre. People-centredness is the value orientation. Action-orientation is the key principle, so that governance does not lag behind need. Sun describes the present system as dominated by Western powers, with developing countries underrepresented and the Global South's voice weak. Drawing on materialist dialectics, Sun argues that the four deficits (peace, development, security, governance) are interlinked, so the four initiatives form a closed loop in which a fairer governance system underpins the other three.

For implementation, Sun calls for three things: a correct view of global governance based on extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits; institutional reform of the UN, the WTO, BRICS and the SCO that improves the existing architecture without starting over; and visible results. As an example of delay, Sun cites the 100 billion US dollars a year in climate finance pledged at Copenhagen in 2009 for 2020, a target first met in 2022. Sun concludes that putting the initiative into practice would have a wide and lasting effect on how humanity meets global challenges. Read the original if you want a concise official-aligned account of how Chinese scholars frame the Global Governance Initiative and its relation to the other three global initiatives.
quoteEn: Global governance has to address global problems that may affect all of humanity, and whether it genuinely serves the peoples of all countries has become an important standard for testing its effectiveness.
quoteZh: 全球治理需要解决可能影响全人类的全球性问题，能否切实服务各国人民，成为检验全球治理有效性的重要标准。

glossary.explanation: A proposal announced by Xi Jinping at the SCO Plus meeting in 2025. It sets out principles for reforming global governance: sovereign equality, international rule of law, multilateralism, a people-centred approach and a focus on action.
A term for developing and emerging countries, used in Chinese diplomacy to stress their shared interests and call for a bigger say in international affairs.

glossary.zh: 全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议
glossary.pinyin: Quánqiú fāzhǎn chàngyì, Quánqiú ānquán chàngyì, Quánqiú wénmíng chàngyì
glossary.literal: global development, security and civilization initiatives
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's proposals on development (2021), security (2022), civilization (2023) and governance (2025). Official texts present them together as the action framework for building a community with a shared future.

glossary.pinyin: gòng shāng gòng jiàn gòng xiǎng
glossary.en: extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits
glossary.literal: jointly discuss, jointly build, jointly share
glossary.explanation: A slogan that sums up the Chinese approach to global governance: decisions are made jointly, institutions are built jointly, and the results are shared by all.

t: As the pattern of international cultural trade evolves, China is becoming a powerful engine
st: A lecture by Professor Hua Jian at Fudan University
zh: 伴随国际文化贸易格局演变 中国正在成为强力引擎
zhSub: 花建研究员在复旦大学的演讲
paras: This text, published in Jiefang Daily on 30 September 2025, is based on a lecture given by Hua Jian at Fudan University. Hua argues that cultural consumption has become a new engine of economic growth, that digitalisation and intelligent technology are redrawing the landscape of international cultural trade, and that China has been the fastest-growing and fastest-rising force in this field over the past two decades.

The lecture has three parts. It first defines international cultural trade (trade in cultural goods and cultural services) and describes it as a global 'super network chain' of investors, producers, distributors and users. It then turns to digital cultural trade as the most dynamic new track, using music, art-market and Ireland examples. Finally it sets out China's position, its proposals for the trade order and its export record.

Hua's central claim is that digitalisation reshapes the rules of cultural trade around the combination of production factors. Trade competitiveness depends on high-end factors such as content, technology and capital, so countries must cultivate or import them to move up the global cultural value chain. Hua cites streaming's 69 per cent share of 2024 global music revenue and Ireland's creative-service exports of US$231.3 billion in 2022. On the order of trade, Hua contrasts the US 'free competition, efficiency first' approach and the French 'cultural exception, controls and protection' approach, which Hua says cannot satisfy all parties, with China's 'development first, inclusiveness and shared benefit' approach. Rooted in building a community with a shared future for mankind, this approach is summarised as development, inclusiveness, joint effort and linkage between domestic reform and global order.

Hua reports that between 2002 and 2022 China's creative-service exports grew 39.4-fold and creative-goods exports 7.8-fold. In 2022 goods exports reached US$249.9 billion, first in the world, and services exports US$67 billion, fifth. Hua concedes that China's service exports still trail those of the United States, Ireland, the United Kingdom and Germany, so there is large room to improve in technology-, capital- and creativity-intensive services. The lecture ends by committing China to keep moving up the value chain. Read the original if you want an official-leaning scholarly account of how Chinese researchers frame China's role and proposals in global cultural trade, together with the trade statistics Hua cites.
quoteEn: Over the past twenty years China has been the powerful engine whose scale has grown fastest in global cultural trade and which has climbed fastest up the value chain.
quoteZh: 中国是近20年来在全球文化贸易中规模增长最快、在价值链上攀升最快的强力引擎。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s as the basis of China's vision of international relations, stressing shared development and cooperation. Here it is the stated foundation of China's approach to cultural trade.
A principle, associated with France, that cultural goods should be exempt from ordinary free-trade rules so that states may protect and support national culture.

t: From "irreversible" to "unstoppable": how to understand the historical process of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
st: Q&A interpretation published in Study Times, 29 September 2025
zh: 如何认识中华民族伟大复兴历史进程从“不可逆转”到“势不可挡”？
paras: This Q&A-style commentary, originally published in Study Times, responds to a question from Zhu Hongjun of Anhui University of Finance and Economics. The question concerns a shift in Xi Jinping's wording: at the centenary of the Party (2021) he called national rejuvenation an "irreversible" historical process, and at the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance (2025) he called it "unstoppable". Dong Zhenhua, head of a department at the Central Party School, argues that the shift marks a process that, on the basis of historical necessity, has gathered further irresistible strength. In Dong's reading it is both a summing-up of the past and a declaration about the future.

The article is organised in four sections, each naming a source of that strength: the leadership of the Communist Party, Marxist theory, reliance on the people, and the Chinese path of modernization. A closing section places these within the international situation and China's relation to the world. Dong draws on Party resolutions, the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and statements by Xi Jinping, and follows the story from the modern semi-colonial period through the revolution, socialist construction and reform to the present.

Dong's central claims are that the Party is the "backbone" that turned a humiliated nation into one that has "stood up, grown rich and become strong", and that Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions gave it accurate strategic judgement. Dong adds that rejuvenation can only come through the people, by pursuing development for the people, by the people and shared by the people, and by common prosperity and whole-process people's democracy. Dong presents Chinese modernization as an independent exploration that rejects what the article calls the Western path of capital-centred, polarising, materialist and expansionist modernization, and as avoiding the trap of the "one-dimensional man". Dong also holds that China's peaceful, cooperative approach to a community with a shared future for mankind places it on the side of historical progress.

Dong concludes that, under the Party's leadership and on the path of Chinese modernization, time and momentum are on China's side and the cause will advance. The strength of truth, the people, faith, morality and practice together form what the article calls an unstoppable historical torrent. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party Central School scholars explain official rhetoric on national rejuvenation, and how they link it to Party leadership, Marxism, the people and foreign policy.
quoteEn: There is no fixed model for the road to modernization; what suits one's own country is best, and one must not cut the feet to fit the shoes.
quoteZh: 现代化道路也并没有固定模式，适合自己的才是最好的，不能削足适履。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's development path, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization.
An official concept, promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019, describing China's democratic system as covering every stage of decision-making rather than only elections.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, emphasised in Xi Jinping's policy since 2021.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world of cooperation and shared interests, introduced in 2012–13.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Empowering the building of modern people's cities through innovation
zh: 以创新赋能现代化人民城市建设
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily in September 2025, asks how innovation can drive the building of modern people's cities. Feng and Xu take as their starting point the Central Urban Work Conference of July 2025, which listed innovation first among six dimensions of the modern people's city. They argue that innovation marks a strategic shift in urban development thinking and offers a practical path to high-quality development.

The authors organise the piece around three tasks: redefining urban functions so that technology serves the people, accelerating coordination among cities, and improving urban quality so that the innovation ecosystem works better. They sketch the historical growth of urban functions and cite examples from the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei, Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta and middle Yangtze regions, as well as Shanghai.

Feng and Xu contend that technology should serve three goals: resilient and secure cities, efficient smart governance through digital public services and unified city management, and green, liveable cities with technologies for an ageing population. They then argue that cities should look beyond their own boundaries, specialising and cooperating within city clusters and metropolitan areas through shared platforms, innovation enclaves and benefit-sharing mechanisms. Finally, they hold that competition between cities will become competition between innovation ecosystems, driven by new quality productive forces, and that what matters is connecting innovation actors rather than merely concentrating resources. Shanghai's large-model innovation community is offered as an example.

The authors propose building connected ecosystems through diverse collaborative networks of firms, universities, government and finance, through high-quality urban renewal that creates innovation spaces, and through a culture that tolerates failure and honours scientists, craftspeople and entrepreneurs. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese policy researchers interpret the 2025 urban work agenda in terms of innovation.
quoteEn: The key lies in valuing the connection of innovation actors, not merely the concentration of resources.
quoteZh: 关键在于重视创新主体的联结而不仅仅是资源集聚。

glossary.explanation: A concept from the Central Urban Work Conference of July 2025, building on Xi Jinping's phrase that cities are built by the people and for the people. It sets out six dimensions of urban development, with innovation listed first.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 to describe growth driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than by traditional resource-intensive inputs.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to development that is efficient, innovative and sustainable.
A high-level Party and government meeting that sets the direction of urban policy. The commentary refers to the session held in July 2025.

t: The new development philosophy leading high-quality development in Xinjiang
zh: 新发展理念引领新疆高质量发展
paras: This newspaper commentary argues that Xinjiang's high-quality development should be guided by the new development philosophy. Xing presents Xinjiang work as holding a special place in the overall work of the Party and state, bearing on the building of a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The author credits Xi Jinping's guidance on border governance with enabling major breakthroughs in the region.

Xing opens with figures on recent achievements: the end of absolute poverty, a moderately prosperous society built together with the rest of China, and 2024 regional GDP growth of 6.1%, passing 2 trillion yuan. Total imports and exports are said to have crossed 200 billion, 300 billion and 400 billion yuan in 2022, 2023 and 2024 respectively. The article is then organised around the five elements of the new development philosophy: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.

On innovation, Xing calls for developing new quality productive forces suited to local conditions, avoiding over-reliance on resource extraction and fostering digital and emerging industries. The author cites Xinjiang's first intelligent computing centre in Karamay as an example. On coordination, Xing proposes linking Xinjiang to major national regional strategies, deepening paired assistance, and promoting urban–rural integration. On green development, openness and sharing, the article lists carbon-peaking pilots, Belt and Road rail links and free trade zone reforms, and employment, social security and rural revitalisation measures. Xing treats improving livelihoods and building unity as the core of Xinjiang's development.

Xing concludes that high-quality development in Xinjiang is a systemic project requiring full and accurate implementation of the Party's governance strategy for Xinjiang in the new era. The author calls for balancing development with security, deepening reform and expanding opening up, so that Chinese modernization takes firm new steps in Xinjiang. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how official discourse links the new development philosophy to Xinjiang policy, with the statistics Xing cites.
quoteEn: Improving people's livelihoods and bringing people together are the core essence of Xinjiang's high-quality development.
quoteZh: 改善民生和凝聚人心是新疆高质量发展的核心要义。

glossary.explanation: A framework put forward under Xi Jinping in 2015 that calls for innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development. It is used as a guide to economic and social policy.
An official goal since 2017 that stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability of growth over speed alone.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 that refers to growth driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging and future industries.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out by the Party from the 20th Party Congress (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Writing a new chapter of Xinjiang's practice of Chinese modernization
zh: 谱写中国式现代化新疆实践新篇章
paras: Marking 70 years since the founding of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region in 1955, this newspaper commentary (published in Economic Daily, 24 September 2025) argues that Xinjiang's achievements, especially since the 18th Party Congress (2012), prove the Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era to be "completely correct" and to be upheld in the long term. Su Cheng contends that Xinjiang work must be understood at the level of national strategy and the overall project of Chinese modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why Xinjiang matters to the national whole: as the author describes it, it is a security barrier on the north-western frontier, the core area of the Silk Road Economic Belt, an energy and agricultural base, and a multi-ethnic home where the Chinese nation community is being built. The second reviews economic and social results since 2012. The third sets out tasks for the new journey.

In the second part Su cites figures: regional GDP rose from 749.947 billion yuan in 2012 to 2.053408 trillion yuan in 2024, and per capita GDP from 33,495 to 78,660 yuan. Imports and exports grew from 158.96 billion to 434.16 billion yuan, and the number of open ports reached 19. Su also reports that absolute poverty has been eliminated, employment has grown to 13.91 million, and incomes have risen. The author further cites education enrolment above the national average, better air and water quality, and the closing of a 3,046-kilometre ring of ecological barrier around the Taklamakan Desert. The third part sets out three tasks: implementing the new development philosophy in full, including technological innovation and new quality productive forces; building a modern industrial system that reflects Xinjiang's strengths in energy, agriculture, new energy, new materials, tourism and cross-border e-commerce; and fostering a new growth pole in southern Xinjiang through industrial layout, urbanisation, rural revitalisation and infrastructure.

Su concludes that Xinjiang work should be planned within the whole of Chinese modernization, balancing development with security and opening up with security, and pursuing governance by law, ethnic unity, cultural enrichment, prosperity and long-term construction under the overall goal of social stability and lasting peace and order. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary presents Xinjiang policy, with statistics, on the 70th anniversary of the region.
quoteEn: Xinjiang's stability, development and prosperity bear on the whole of the construction of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 新疆的稳定、发展和繁荣关乎中国式现代化建设全局。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the central task of national development.
A term introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, used in policy to guide high-quality development.
The Party's guideline, adopted in 2015, that development should be innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared.

glossary.pinyin: xīn shídài dǎng de zhì Jiāng fānglüè
glossary.en: the Party's strategy for governing Xinjiang in the new era
glossary.explanation: The official framework for Xinjiang policy since 2012, with the overall goal of social stability and lasting peace and order, and tasks such as governance by law, ethnic unity, cultural enrichment, prosperity and long-term construction.
An official concept stressing a shared national identity across China's ethnic groups; "forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation" is the stated main line of ethnic work.

t: The contemporary value and global significance of high-level opening up
zh: 高水平对外开放的时代价值与世界意义
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in September 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's recently published article on steadfastly advancing high-level opening up. Wang Heng argues that high-level opening up is, internally, a route to developing new quality productive forces suited to local conditions and, externally, an extension of Chinese modernization that fits the modernization aims of developing countries. In this reading it carries contemporary value and global significance for stabilising the world economy, improving global governance and driving sustainable development.

The piece is organised in three sections, each pairing an account of significance with practical measures. The first deals with building an innovative and inclusive open world economy through mutually reinforcing domestic and international circulations. The second deals with institutional opening up as a way to build a fairer and more rational global governance system. The third deals with making the fruits of opening up benefit people in all countries more widely and fairly. It closes by linking opening up to a community with a shared future for mankind.

In the first section, Wang argues that the new development pattern and an open world economy support each other. The first draws on China's industrial system and market scale, and the second lowers transaction costs and widens factor flows. The article cites an average annual contribution of about 30 per cent to world economic growth during the 14th Five-Year Plan period. In the second, Wang presents institutional opening up, meaning alignment of rules, regulations, management and standards, as the basis of governance coordination. Wang says it shifts governance from Western-led to pluralist co-governance and moves China from adapting to rules to co-creating them, citing the Belt and Road Initiative and the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership. In the third, Wang says opening up should aim at people's livelihoods, citing the China–Laos Railway and the Jakarta–Bandung high-speed railway as examples of local benefit.

Wang calls for strengthening the domestic circulation, upgrading free trade zones and ports, deepening cooperation with Global South countries, and improving the business environment and intellectual property protection. Wang also urges building platforms such as trade expos, and channelling industry, innovation, finance and talent exchange towards livelihood projects. Opening up is described as an essential road to prosperity that creates a favourable external environment for deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary links high-level opening up, institutional opening up and the Global South to Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Global governance is to move from Western domination towards pluralistic co-governance, and from power games towards consensus on rules.
quoteZh: 推动全球治理从西方主导转向多元共治、从权力博弈转向规则共识。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023. It refers to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, and is used in policy on high-quality development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation of China's vision for international relations, promoted since 2012–13. It stresses shared interests, cooperation and joint governance.
The official strategy, announced in 2020, of making the domestic circulation the mainstay while domestic and international circulations reinforce each other.
Opening up focused on aligning rules, regulations, management and standards with international high-standard economic and trade rules, rather than on flows of goods and capital alone.
A term used in Chinese official discourse for developing countries, with which China stresses solidarity and cooperation.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: The Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression made a major contribution to saving human civilization
zh: 中国人民抗日战争为拯救人类文明作出了重大贡献
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in September 2025, this short commentary takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the 80th anniversary commemoration of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. Liu and Li argue that the Chinese people, through enormous national sacrifice, made a major contribution to saving human civilization and defending world peace, and that Xi's remark offers a new reading of the war's place in world history.

The article moves from the war itself to the present. It covers the defence of Chinese civilization, China's role in the global anti-fascist war and postwar order, China's later peace and development diplomacy, and the tasks ahead.

The authors first claim that victory safeguarded more than five thousand years of civilizational achievement and restored China's standing as a major country. They then argue that China's theatre, the earliest and longest of the war, was the Eastern main battlefield, tied down the bulk of Japan's forces and enabled the Soviet Union to move troops west. They cite Chinese military and civilian casualties of over 35 million. The Cairo Declaration, Yalta arrangements and China's permanent seat on the UN Security Council are presented as the legal and institutional outcomes. From this the authors derive a continuity: because Chinese civilization is peaceful by nature, China upholds the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, the Global Security Initiative and the Global Development Initiative, alongside high-quality Belt and Road cooperation.

The authors conclude that remembering the war serves to shape the future. They call for building a community with a shared future for mankind, implementing the Global Civilization Initiative, and upholding a UN-centred international system. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Chinese commentary links the memory of the anti-Japanese war to current foreign-policy initiatives.
quoteEn: The victory of the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression not only ended Japanese militarism's expansionist ambitions but also became the historical turning point at which the global governance system moved from collapse to reconstruction.
quoteZh: 中国人民抗日战争的胜利不仅终结了日本军国主义的扩张野心，也成为全球治理体系从崩溃走向重建的历史转折点。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, describing China's vision of international relations based on shared security, development and cooperation.
A proposal announced by Xi Jinping in 2022 setting out principles for international security, summarised in the article as 'six commitments'.
A proposal put forward by Xi Jinping in 2021 that prioritises development cooperation, especially with developing countries.
Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression and non-interference, equality and peaceful coexistence, associated with Chinese foreign policy since the 1950s.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Deepening implementation of the "AI+" action to provide strong momentum for high-quality development
zh: 深入实施“人工智能+”行动 为高质量发展提供强大动能
paras: This commentary, issued by the National Development and Reform Commission and published in the People's Daily on 12 September 2025, explains why and how the "AI+" action should be implemented in depth. It takes as its starting point the State Council's recent Opinions on Deepening the Implementation of the "AI+" Action, which set a timetable and roadmap for AI applications across sectors. The article argues that integrating AI with every area of the economy and society is both an urgent task and a long-term strategic question, and that it will supply strong momentum for high-quality development.

The text has three parts. The first sets out four reasons for the action's importance. The second lists China's favourable conditions: data, industrial system, application scenarios, market size and talent. The third outlines the Commission's own work plan under five headings: an innovation-driven intelligent economy, a more caring intelligent society, stronger supporting factors, a better environment for application, and security safeguards.

On significance, the article presents the action as a strategic choice to seize the new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation, as an inherent requirement of cultivating new quality productive forces, as a way to meet the people's needs for a better life, and as a step to help all countries take part equally in intelligent development. It treats AI as a "lead goose" technology that raises total factor productivity and shifts growth from factor-driven to innovation-driven. For conditions, it cites figures: 41.06 ZB of data produced in 2024, or 26.67% of the global total; a full set of industrial categories; more than 1,500 industry models; about 200 million business entities; and the world's largest pools of R&D personnel.

For implementation, the Commission pledges coordination among departments, between central and local levels, and with society. Measures include high-quality corpora, data property rules, the "East Data, West Computing" hubs, open-source ecosystems, pilot-test bases, financial support and demonstration roles for state enterprises. It also promises AI skills training, employment-risk assessment, and monitoring and early-warning systems to make AI applications compliant, transparent and trustworthy. Read the original if you want an official statement of the policy rationale, figures and work priorities behind the "AI+" action.
quoteEn: Deepening the implementation of "AI+" is a long-term and complex systematic undertaking.
quoteZh: 深入实施“人工智能+”是一项长期、复杂的系统工程。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productivity growth driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and innovative factor allocation rather than traditional resource-heavy growth.
The official goal, since about 2017, of shifting China's economy from rapid expansion toward efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
A State Council initiative to integrate AI into industry, public services and other sectors, following earlier "Internet+" policy. The 2025 Opinions set targets and a roadmap.
A national project that moves data-processing demand from the eastern coast to computing hubs in western China, where energy and land are more available.

glossary.zh: 国家发展和改革委员会
glossary.explanation: A State Council body responsible for macroeconomic planning, major projects and coordinating development policy.

t: Scientifically and rationally promoting the realization of the value of ecological products
zh: 科学合理推动生态产品价值实现
paras: This short commentary in the People's Daily asks how the value of ecological products can be realized in a scientific and rational way. Meng Fan argues that a sound value-realization mechanism is a key route for putting into practice the idea that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets. In the author's account it is also part of Xi Jinping's thinking on ecological civilization and of modernizing environmental governance.

The article opens by citing Xi's call, in the Selected Works on Ecological Civilization, for protection and restoration to earn fair returns and for damage to carry a cost, and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) decision on the mechanism. It then proceeds in three steps: the meaning of ecological products, the institutional logic of realizing their value, and a set of practical measures.

Meng defines ecological products as clean air, clean water and a pleasant climate, divided into material supply, regulating services and cultural services. The value-realization mechanism turns their ecological, economic and social value into benefits through compensation and market development, so that protectors benefit, users pay and damagers compensate. The author holds that the process converts natural resources into ecological products and then into economic returns, requiring reforms in rights registration, performance assessment, compensation, market development and green finance. A 2021 central opinion set out six mechanisms covering the whole chain.

Meng calls for locally adapted policies, standardized and branded ecological products, and a refined compensation system based on the principle of 'whoever benefits compensates; whoever protects benefits', including cross-regional pilots. The author also urges diversified development models, such as rural leisure tourism, under strict protection. Read the original if you want a concise official-style statement of how ecological product value realization is framed in Chinese policy.
quoteEn: The basic process of realizing the value of ecological products is to turn natural resources into ecological products, and then to turn ecological products into economic returns.
quoteZh: 实现生态产品价值的基本过程，就是将自然资源转化为生态产品，再将生态产品转化为经济效益。

glossary.zh: 生态产品价值实现机制
glossary.explanation: An institutional arrangement, formalized in a 2021 central opinion, for turning the ecological, economic and social value of natural systems into compensation or market income.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thinking on ecological civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on environmental protection and green development attributed to Xi Jinping and treated as part of official Party theory.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2005, holding that environmental protection and economic development are mutually reinforcing.
Payments, often fiscal transfers, to those who protect ecosystems, including between regions.

t: The fundamental guidance for advancing urban–rural integrated development in the new era
zh: 新时代推进城乡融合发展的根本遵循
