paras: Wei Houkai argues that Xi Jinping's body of statements on urban–rural integrated development is the fundamental guidance for the new era and an integral part of Xi Jinping's economic thought. In Wei's account, these statements reveal the trends and laws governing city and countryside, set out the goals and direction of integration, and develop the Marxist theory of urban–rural relations. Urban–rural integration is presented as an inherent requirement of Chinese modernization.

The article, a commentary in the Party-run Economic Daily, has four parts. The first covers the trends and laws of urban–rural change; the second the goals and direction of integration; the third the practical path; the fourth the theoretical innovations. Wei traces Xi's remarks from 2013 to recent Party meetings, including the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), and follows the shift in policy language from coordinating urban and rural development to integrating it.

Wei makes three main moves. First, citing Xi's 2018 statement, Wei holds that while the urban share rises and the rural share falls, the countryside will not disappear and the two will coexist over the long term. Wei adds that villages may vanish without the countryside doing so, and that cities and villages each follow their own laws. Second, the goals are the 'five equalizations' of basic rights, public services, incomes, factor allocation and industrial integration. Third, the path combines strategic coordination of new-type industrialization, new-type urbanization and rural revitalization with institutional reform, and takes the county as the entry point. Wei notes that counties hold about 90 per cent of national land and over 50 per cent of the population.

Wei concludes that Xi advances Marxist theory in two ways. One is the theory of an urban–rural community, building on Marx and Engels, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. The other is the conception of a new type of industry–agriculture and urban–rural relationship, whose wording changed from 'comprehensive integration' in 2017 to 'coordinated development' in 2020. Wei reads this change as reflecting the new development philosophy and the aim of common prosperity. Read the original if you want a Party-theorist's systematic account of how official urban–rural policy language has evolved and how it is justified.
quoteEn: Advancing urban–rural integrated development requires a scientific grasp of the trends of urban–rural change, and recognising, respecting and conforming to the laws of urban and rural evolution and development.
quoteZh: 推进城乡融合发展必须科学把握城乡演变趋势，认识、尊重、顺应城乡演变和发展规律。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's development path, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022), presented as distinct from Western modernization models.
The official name for the body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, treated as part of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party goal of prosperity shared by all, which Xi Jinping has made a central objective of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official framework, put forward in 2015, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
A national strategy announced at the 19th Party Congress (2017) to develop agriculture, villages and farmers' livelihoods.

The policy concept, emphasised since the 19th Party Congress, of two-way integration and shared construction between city and countryside. It succeeded earlier formulations such as coordinating urban and rural development and urban–rural integration.

t: Contributing "silver-haired strength" to advancing Chinese modernization
st: Studying and implementing General Secretary Xi Jinping's important statements on work for the next generation
zh: 为推进中国式现代化贡献“银发力量”
zhSub: 深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于关心下一代工作的重要论述
authors: China National Committee for the Care of the Next Generation
paras: Published in the People's Daily in 2025, the 35th anniversary year of the China National Committee for the Care of the Next Generation, this commentary is written by the committee itself. It takes up how retired cadres and other elders can contribute to Chinese modernization by nurturing young people. Its answer is that the committees should study Xi Jinping's statements on the subject, gather the "silver-haired strength" of the "Five Elders", and make moral education central to their work.

The text has three parts. The first sets out Xi Jinping's statements on work for the next generation under five headings: ensuring worthy successors, fostering virtue through education, treating older people as a resource, and the committees as an institutional arrangement. The second draws lessons about how the committees should work. The third lists concrete tasks for the committees. The authors give figures for the committees' reach: over 1.07 million organisations, more than 13 million "Five Elders", 70,000 "Five Elders" workrooms and 424,000 off-campus tutors.

The authors argue that raising young people as "socialist builders and successors" is a strategic task on which the future of the Party and country depend. They present the committees, approved by the Party Central Committee in 1990, as an institutional innovation for using older comrades in the ideological and political education of youth. Their account of how the committees should operate has four elements: Party leadership, moral education with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, service to the Party's central tasks through local organisation, and use of elders' distinctive strengths.

The proposals centre on three projects: moral education, care for the next generation, and the committees' own high-quality development. They include getting Xi's thought into textbooks and classrooms, teaching Party and national history, promoting legal awareness, supporting left-behind and migrant children, and training young rural talent and industrial workers. The committees are also to widen their organisational coverage and strengthen coordination among member units. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-led mass organisation for retired cadres describes its mission and organisation in official language.
quoteEn: Work for the next generation is an important component of the Party's cause, and the committees are the key organisational base for carrying it out.
quoteZh: 关心下一代事业是党的事业的重要组成部分，关工委组织是开展关心下一代工作的重要组织依托。

glossary.zh: 关心下一代工作委员会
glossary.en: China National Committee for the Care of the Next Generation
glossary.literal: Committee for Work of Caring for the Next Generation
glossary.explanation: A Party-sponsored organisation approved by the Central Committee in 1990, staffed largely by retired officials and professionals. It engages in ideological, moral and welfare work with children and young people.
Shorthand for five groups of retired people: veteran cadres, veteran soldiers, veteran experts, veteran teachers and model workers. They form the core volunteer force of the committees.
A phrase for the contribution of older people to social and national development. It is used in Xi Jinping's encouragement of elderly volunteers.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented in Party documents as distinct from Western models.
A principle of Chinese education policy that makes moral and ideological formation the fundamental task of schooling.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since the 19th Party Congress (2017). It is taught across the education system.

keywords: Care for the Next Generation Committee

t: Using rule-of-law thinking to create a healthy environment for the development of the private economy
zh: 用法治思维营造民营经济健康发展环境
paras: Writing in the People's Daily (11 September 2025), Xu Hong takes up the question of how rule-of-law thinking can support the sustained, healthy and high-quality development of the private economy. Xu argues that the Private Economy Promotion Law, in force since 20 May 2025, is a milestone, and that implementing it requires, among other things, a criminal-justice environment that protects the lawful rights of private enterprises and entrepreneurs while still punishing genuine offences.

The commentary begins with Xi Jinping's statements on the private economy and with figures it cites: private firms are over 92 per cent of all enterprises, contribute over half of imports and exports and tax revenue, and provide over 80 per cent of urban employment. It then traces the Party's policy line and constitutional amendments, the Civil Code and other laws. Its second half turns to criminal law and sets out three principles: no crime without explicit legal provision, the rule of applying the older law unless the newer one is more lenient, and criminal punishment that is necessary, appropriate, reasonable and fair.

In Xu's account, the rule of law gives market actors a stable, predictable environment, marks the boundary between government and market, and strengthens integrity and compliance. Xu treats current difficulties as partial, temporary and surmountable, arising from structural change and from firms' weak legal awareness. On criminal justice, Xu calls for clear lines between economic disputes and crimes, administrative violations and crimes, and corporate and individual liability. Xu also calls for guarding against profit-driven enforcement and the use of criminal means in civil disputes. The older-law-or-more-lenient-law principle is meant to treat firms' past irregularities in historical context, with wrongful cases corrected.

Xu concludes that criminal punishment must be assessed for its effects on employees, supply chains and industries, and be consistent with macro policy. Because private firms are credited with over 70 per cent of technological innovation results, Xu proposes a judicial tolerance-of-error mechanism and a restrained approach to criminalising innovative conduct, so that entrepreneurship and the tolerance of failure are encouraged. Read the original if you want an official-line account, by a criminal-law scholar, of how the new law is meant to shape policing and prosecution of private businesses.
quoteEn: Upholding the principle of applying the old law unless the new one is more lenient means viewing, with a historical and developmental eye, any irregularities in private firms' operations, observing non-retroactivity, and declaring not guilty, in accordance with the law, those with insufficient grounds for conviction.
quoteZh: 坚持从旧兼从轻原则，就是要以历史和发展眼光客观看待和依法妥善处理民营企业经营发展中可能存在的不规范问题，遵循法不溯及既往原则，对定罪依据不足的依法宣告无罪。

glossary.literal: Law on Promoting the Private Economy
glossary.explanation: A national law in force from 20 May 2025 that, according to the article, for the first time defines the legal status of the private economy.

glossary.en: no crime without explicit legal provision
glossary.literal: crimes and punishments fixed by law
glossary.explanation: The criminal-law principle that conduct is a crime, and punishable, only if the law expressly says so (nullum crimen sine lege). It is set out in Article 3 of China's Criminal Law.

t: How the Party identified and trained military-industrial talent in the base areas during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 抗战时期党对根据地军工人才的发掘与培养
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2025, An Na asks how the Communist Party built a workforce for the arms industry of its anti-Japanese base areas during the War of Resistance (1937–1945). The article argues that the Party, recognising the importance of independent military production, drew in talent from many fields and so formed a technically skilled and politically reliable corps of military-industrial personnel. In An's account, this corps kept production running and laid the personnel foundation for the arms industry of the Liberation War and the People's Republic.

The piece is a short historical commentary organised under three headings: combining the recruitment of highly trained specialists with the absorption of skilled craftsmen; founding military-industrial schools to train technical backbone staff; and using several measures to nurture and motivate such personnel. It draws on Party documents, including the Sixth Plenum of the Sixth Central Committee (1938) and a 1941 Central Military Commission directive, and on local military-history sources. Its cases come mainly from the Taihang base area of the Eighth Route Army and from the New Fourth Army's central China bases.

An's central claim is that recruitment came from two directions. The Party brought in returned students from Europe and Southeast Asia and university professors and students, many of whom joined the Eighth Route Army's mobile working group, and it also drew skilled workers from arsenals in Hebei, Shanxi and Shandong. The Huangyadong arsenal is cited as a training ground, with output figures such as tens of thousands of rifles and over 580,000 hand grenades. Schools such as the Taihang Industrial School, said to have trained nearly 400 mid-level managers and technicians, and the Huaibei Industrial School of the New Fourth Army's Fourth Division supplied further staff. The article then stresses a mix of political study, including a minimum 15 per cent of class time at Taihang, technical training and incentives. These included higher grain wages, medical and family benefits, and awards for inventions and above-quota output.

An concludes that these political, technical and material measures released the creativity of military-industrial personnel and strengthened the base areas' military capacity, even in the hardest years of 1942–1944. Individual designers such as Liu Guifu, creator of the 'Bayi-type' cavalry rifle, are presented as products of this system. Read the original if you want a brief, source-referenced overview of the Party's official narrative on talent policy in the wartime arms industry, with named schools, factories and incentive measures.
quoteEn: The Party's ability to keep expanding the base areas' military industry within just a few years was inseparable from the establishment and refinement of incentive mechanisms for military-industrial personnel.
quoteZh: 党在短短数年间使根据地军工事业不断发展壮大，这与军工人才激励机制的建立完善密不可分。

glossary.explanation: Territories under Communist administration and military control during the anti-Japanese war and civil war, used as bases for government, production and operations.
The main Communist-led force in northern China during the War of Resistance, formally part of the National Revolutionary Army from 1937.
A Communist-led army operating in central China during the War of Resistance, formed in 1937.

t: The historic contribution of the Communist Party of China to building the community of the Chinese nation during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 抗战时期中国共产党推进中华民族共同体建设的历史贡献
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily shortly after the 80th anniversary commemoration of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan (2025), Chen Jinlong asks how the Communist Party of China advanced the building of the community of the Chinese nation during the war. Chen argues that the war was an important stage in that history. Four things consolidated the community's foundations: the practice of a nationwide war of resistance, new relations among nationalities, the construction of a discourse of the Chinese nation, and emotional closeness among the nationalities.

The article is organised in four numbered sections matching these four themes. It draws mainly on Party documents of 1935–1945 collected in the multi-volume compilation of key documents since the Party's founding. It also draws on Mao Zedong's wartime writings and speeches by Mao and Zhang Wentian at the Sixth Plenum of the Sixth Central Committee. Examples include appeals to Hui and Mongol peoples, policy outlines on Hui and Mongol questions, and the formation of resistance forces in Daqingshan and in Hebei and Bohai.

Chen's core argument is that mobilising all nationalities was both a military necessity and a means of community-building. In Chen's account, the Party's anti-Japanese national united front covered every nationality as well as every party and class, and the Party worked to raise the confidence of minority peoples and helped form armed units among them. Chen says the Party then built new nationality relations on equality in economic, political and cultural life, on unity, and on economic measures such as tax limits, protection of Mongol pastures and support for Hui production. Chen adds that Party narratives of a shared multi-ethnic history, of civilisational achievement and of revolutionary tradition gave historical and political support to the community. Chen presents emotional bonds, citing Xi Jinping's 2024 remark that emotional closeness is a 'strong bond', as resting on trust built through communication, the address of minority peoples as 'brothers', and national self-confidence and pride.

Chen concludes that the war's shared struggle laid the foundations of the community of the Chinese nation, and that the Party's wartime practice contributed historically to its construction. The piece is a short commentary that links wartime policy to current official language on ethnic unity. Read the original if you want a concise account, with archival citations, of how current Chinese official historiography presents wartime Party nationality policy as the origin of the community of the Chinese nation.
quoteEn: The struggle in practice of the nationwide war of resistance, the shaping of new ethnic relations, the construction of a discourse of the Chinese nation, and emotional closeness among the nationalities consolidated the foundations of the community of the Chinese nation and advanced its construction.
quoteZh: 全民族抗战的斗争实践、新型民族关系的塑造、中华民族话语体系的建构和各民族情感上的相互亲近，夯实了中华民族共同体的基础，推动了中华民族共同体建设。

glossary.explanation: A concept in current Party nationality policy. It describes the Chinese nation as a single community formed by all of China's nationalities over history, and underpins calls to strengthen a shared national identity.
The wartime alliance of the Communist Party with other parties, classes and groups against Japanese invasion. The Party promoted it from the mid-1930s.
The Party's wartime line of mobilising all classes and nationalities, not only the army, to fight Japan. It contrasts with a resistance conducted by government forces alone.

t: Talent training in the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army
zh: 东北抗日联军的人才培养
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 8 September 2025
paras: This short commentary asks how the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army (abbreviated as "the United Army") organised study and training under wartime conditions, and what that study achieved. Zhang Kuan argues that learning in the United Army was adapted to war. In the author's account it shaped the force's ideological cohesion and fighting strength, and produced many cadres and fighters with both military skill and firm political conviction.

The article has three parts. The first surveys the forms of study: political-military schools, schools attached to units, temporary training classes, and company-level groups such as literacy classes, shooting and tactics groups, political discussion meetings and Lenin study circles. The second describes a distinctive model summed up as "rifle plus pen". The third assesses the results under three headings. The piece draws on statements by the commander Zhou Baozhong and on period documents and reports.

Zhang notes that the formal schools often existed in name only. The Third Army, for example, sent its instructors and students to frontline units, and the United Army had little printing equipment. Fighters copied textbooks by hand, made their own teaching aids or used captured materials. Because attacks by Japanese and puppet forces were frequent, regular classroom teaching gave way to self-study in gaps between fighting. In the "rifle plus pen" model, the "rifle" meant weapons, guerrilla tactics and special skills such as skiing, boat handling and winter survival. The "pen" meant political education and basic literacy, together with Japanese, Russian and Korean. Zhang credits the training with three results. It produced cadres, including about 300 military-political cadres from the school in the Tangwang River area. It raised tactical ability through practice-based discussion. It raised cultural and political levels together.

Zhang concludes that the United Army's study practice was a microcosm of the Chinese Communist Party's fourteen years of resistance to Japan. The author draws the lesson that fighting strength depends not only on better equipment and technology. It also depends on "using study to promote fighting", and on ideological education that builds absolute loyalty in the sense of "the Party commands the gun". Read the original if you want a brief, officially framed overview of education and training in the Northeast guerrilla forces in the 1930s and 1940s, or an example of how the history is used in Party-building discourse today.
quoteEn: The United Army's study practice was a microcosm of the Chinese Communist Party's fourteen years of arduous resistance to the Japanese invaders.
quoteZh: 抗联的学习实践是中国共产党14年艰苦卓绝抵抗日本侵略者的缩影

glossary.explanation: A coalition of Communist-led guerrilla forces that fought the Japanese occupation of Northeast China from the mid-1930s. Its units later withdrew in part into the Soviet Union.
The author's phrase for combining military training (the rifle) with political and cultural education (the pen).
A principle of Chinese Communist Party doctrine that the armed forces are under the Party's absolute leadership. It is often traced to Mao Zedong.
Training schools set up within or alongside army units to train lower-level political and military cadres quickly.

t: The Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army spirit remains ever fresh
zh: 东北抗联精神历久弥新
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today on 8 September 2025, argues that the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army (Dongbei Kanglian) retains lasting value today. Wang opens with Xi Jinping's 2016 remark in Heilongjiang that this spirit, with others such as the Daqing spirit, should still be used to educate Party members and cadres. The author defines the spirit as three elements: firm faith in the Party, national righteousness in answering the national crisis, and heroic determination to fight to the end.

The article is organised under three headings, one for each element. Each is illustrated with episodes from the fourteen-year struggle that the Party-led force waged against a far larger enemy. Wang draws on figures such as Yang Jingyu, Zhou Baozhong, Zhao Yiman, Chen Hanzhang and the eight women fighters who drowned themselves in the Wusuli River.

On Party faith, Wang cites Yang Jingyu's resistance despite starvation and Zhao Yiman's refusal to betray secrets under torture, and presents both as expressions of Marxist conviction. On national righteousness, the author points to the united-front declaration of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, which offered cooperation to all anti-Japanese forces regardless of faction. Wang says this awakened the national consciousness of people in the Northeast. On fighting to the end, Wang describes sub-zero conditions, Japanese policies of forced relocation and collective punishment, and the refusal of Chen Hanzhang and the eight women to surrender.

Wang concludes that, as the world undergoes what the text calls changes unseen in a century, today's readers should draw on this spirit. The author calls for a willingness to struggle, for firm ideals and convictions as a lifelong task, and for lasting commitment to communist ideals and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party commemoration of the anti-Japanese war links wartime heroism to present-day ideological education.
quoteEn: The Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army spirit was born of the army's arduous struggle; the spiritual outlook and noble character it embodies have an enduring value that transcends time and space, and are a precious spiritual wealth of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 东北抗联精神孕育于东北抗日联军艰苦卓绝的斗争历史，其中所展现的精神风貌和崇高品格具有超越时空的恒久价值，是中华民族弥足珍贵的宝贵精神财富。

glossary.explanation: The united anti-Japanese armed force formed from various guerrilla units in Northeast China under Communist leadership after the 1931 Mukden Incident. Chinese official history presents it as the Party's armed force in the region.

t: Outlook for the integration of artificial intelligence and consumption during the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: “十五五”时期人工智能与消费融合发展前瞻
paras: Writing in September 2025, Xia Jiechang and Wang Wenji ask how "AI plus consumption" can help release domestic demand during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030). They tie the topic to Xi Jinping's call to "vigorously boost consumption" and to the State Council's August 2025 opinions on the "AI Plus" initiative. Their thesis is that AI will reshape supply–demand relations and consumer behaviour, moving the consumption system into a digital, intelligent and personalised stage.

This short commentary has two parts. The first sets out four features of the current stage: technological evolution, supply and demand structure, inclusiveness, and the institutional environment. The second sets out four policy directions: intelligent supply, key application scenarios, underlying capabilities, and flexible institutional safeguards. The authors cite 249 million users of generative AI products in China by December 2024 and project 40 per cent compound annual growth for the AI large-model market.

Xia and Wang argue that large models are moving AI consumption from isolated scenarios to full-chain, ecosystem-based penetration. They see consumers shifting from data providers to active participants, and platforms building "data + algorithms + computing power + scenarios" ecosystems. They also identify risks: an "intelligence divide" that excludes lower-income and older groups, and algorithmic recommendation that may induce irrational consumption and homogenise tastes. They also point to unclear data ownership, weak algorithm transparency, vague platform responsibility and fragmented enforcement. For supply, they urge firms to turn products such as appliances, wearables and cars into emotional carriers and platforms into intelligent ecosystem operators.

The authors call for more widely accessible computing power, public high-quality data (including "data public-interest pools") and open-source model ecosystems. They also propose pilot scenarios in health care, elderly care, culture and tourism, plus ex ante risk warning against algorithmic discrimination and false interaction. They further propose tiered, classified and dynamically adjustable governance: stronger accountability and transparency duties for large platforms, and guidance with tolerant regulation for small firms. They conclude that policy should give equal weight to development and governance. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy agenda for AI-driven consumption and its governance ahead of the 15th Five-Year Plan.
quoteEn: Therefore, while promoting the expansion of intelligent consumption, inclusive mechanisms must be strengthened to prevent technological dividends from turning into barriers of division.
quoteZh: 因此，要在推动智能消费扩展的同时，加强普惠机制设计，防止科技红利变成分化壁垒。

glossary.explanation: China's national development plan for 2026–2030. Its guidelines are drawn up in 2025.
A State Council initiative to integrate AI into sectors of the economy and society. The August 2025 opinions set out its deployment, including for consumption.

t: The mainstay of the nation's all-out resistance and the staunch leadership core of national rejuvenation
zh: 全民族抗战的中流砥柱民族复兴的坚强领导核心
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan (2025), this newspaper commentary by Zhang Taiyuan takes up Xi Jinping's description of the Communist Party as the mainstay of the nation's all-out resistance. Zhang argues that this role is shown above all in the Party's initiation, advancement and defence of the Anti-Japanese National United Front.

The piece follows the history chronologically. It starts with the Party's early calls for a united front, then covers the formal adoption of the policy at the Wayaobao meeting (1935), the Xi'an Incident (1936), the founding of the Kuomintang–Communist united front in 1937, and the Party's conduct during the war, including after the Southern Anhui Incident. It ends with lessons for the present.

Zhang's central claim is that the Party was the first to call for, and then consistently pushed, a united front. He traces this from a January 1933 declaration and the August First Declaration through the shift from "pressing Chiang to resist Japan" to "allying with Chiang". In Zhang's account, the Party's peaceful settlement of the Xi'an Incident reflected its confidence in contending for leadership of the resistance. Zhang says the Party behind enemy lines kept to independent guerrilla warfare and avoided further military action against the Kuomintang even after the Southern Anhui Incident. He concludes that without the Party there would have been no national united front, and without that front no all-out resistance.

Zhang draws the lesson that winning hearts is the greatest politics and that the united front remains a means of gathering strength. He calls for consolidating the broadest patriotic united front under Party leadership, improving the overall united front work structure, and uniting people at home and overseas to advance Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a short, official-line account of how Party historians frame the Party's role in the wartime united front.
quoteEn: Without the Communist Party of China there would have been no national anti-Japanese united front, and without the Anti-Japanese National United Front there would have been no all-out national resistance.
quoteZh: 没有中国共产党就没有全民族的抗日统一战线，没有抗日民族统一战线就没有全民族抗战

glossary.explanation: The wartime alliance of political and military forces against Japan, based on Kuomintang–Communist cooperation and formally established in 1937. Official Chinese history credits the Communist Party with first proposing it.
The official name for China's development path as presented by the Party leadership since the early 2020s. It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
An idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm in a crisis. Xi Jinping uses it for the Party's role in the War of Resistance.

The December 1936 detention of Chiang Kai-shek by Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng to press him to stop the civil war and resist Japan. It led to a peaceful settlement and moved the two parties towards cooperation.
The January 1941 clash in which Kuomintang forces attacked the Communist-led New Fourth Army, causing heavy losses and straining the united front.

t: Historical lessons on the key to victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression
zh: 中国人民抗日战争胜利关键的历史启示
paras: Writing after Xi Jinping's speech at the commemoration of the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), Qu Qingshan asks what was decisive in the Chinese people's victory. The answer is that the Communist Party of China's role as the "mainstay" (zhongliu dizhu) was the key to victory. Qu presents this as a historical conclusion and as a lesson for upholding Party leadership in the new era. The piece first appeared in the People's Daily on 8 September 2025.

The article is organised in five parts, each opening with a statement from Xi. It treats the Party as the earliest advocate and organiser of resistance; as the builder of the anti-Japanese national united front; as the source of the strategy of all-out resistance and protracted war; as the leader of the rear-area battlefield behind Japanese lines; and as the forger of the great spirit of resistance. It draws on declarations, dates, military statistics, and remarks by Mao Zedong, Ye Jianying and some Japanese and American observers. A short closing section draws lessons for the present.

Qu argues that after the 1931 Mukden Incident the Nationalist government pursued non-resistance, while the Party issued declarations, led guerrilla war in the Northeast and backed the national salvation movement. It then promoted the united front, from the 1935 August 1st Declaration through the peaceful settlement of the Xi'an Incident and the second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, and defended it against anti-Communist offensives. Qu credits Mao's On Protracted War and the guerrilla strategy with guiding the war. The article holds that the enemy-rear battlefield became the main battlefield once the war reached the stage of strategic stalemate. It cites figures for the share of Japanese forces in China that Party-led troops fought, ranging from about 58 to 75 per cent a year from 1938 to 1945, and reports that the liberated areas covered nearly 1 million square kilometres and had a population of nearly 100 million. Qu also credits Communists' vanguard role with shaping the national spirit, while mentioning Nationalist officers who died in battle.

Qu concludes that the Party's mainstay role is the most fundamental point to remember when commemorating the war. In his reading, Party leadership is the foundation and lifeline of the Party and the state. He calls for a deep grasp of the Two Establishes, strengthened awareness, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds. He also calls for unity under Xi Jinping to advance national strength and rejuvenation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an authoritative example of the current official Party-history account of the war and the way it links that account to present-day political demands.
quoteEn: In commemorating the great victory of the Chinese People's War of Resistance today, the most fundamental point is to remember that the Communist Party's role as the mainstay was the key to victory.
quoteZh: 今天，我们纪念中国人民抗日战争的伟大胜利，最根本的一条，就是要牢记中国共产党的中流砥柱作用是中国人民抗日战争胜利的关键。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm in turbulent times. In official history writing it describes the Communist Party's claimed role in the War of Resistance.
A formula from the Party's 2021 historical resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party formula that calls for upholding Xi Jinping's core position and the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The official concept of China's own path to modernization, which the Party has promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The broad coalition formed from 1937 around Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, which also drew in other parties, groups and overseas Chinese against Japanese invasion.

t: On Protracted War: a strategic beacon that lit the way to victory in the War of Resistance
zh: 《论持久战》：照亮抗战胜利的战略灯塔
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2025, assesses Mao Zedong's 1938 work On Protracted War. Ji presents it as a model of adapting Marxist military theory to China. The author argues that its scientific foresight and practical guidance shaped the course of the War of Resistance against Japan, and that it still inspires efforts toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece is organised under three headings: how the work cleared away confusion and set the direction of resistance, how its analysis of the situation revealed the laws of the war, and how it guided practice and built national spirit.

Ji argues that Mao answered two harmful positions of the early war, the 'theory of national subjugation' and the 'theory of quick victory', by comparing the two sides. Japan was strong but waged an unjust war with limited resources, while China was weak but fought a just war with large territory and population. From this Mao drew the three stages of strategic defence, stalemate and counter-offensive. Ji also highlights Mao's tactical principles of offence within defence, quick decision within protracted war, and exterior lines within interior lines. In practice, the author credits trading space for time, raising guerrilla warfare to strategic status, and mass political mobilisation through the anti-Japanese national united front.

Ji concludes that the work gave the nation a firm faith in victory and turned the spirit of resistance into a wider commitment to justice. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style Chinese account of how On Protracted War is now presented in the 2025 commemoration of the war's victory.
quoteEn: On Protracted War gave comprehensive and detailed guidance to the military practice of China's War of Resistance and became the key theoretical support for reshaping the pattern of the battlefield.
quoteZh: 《论持久战》为中国抗日战争的军事实践提供了全面且细致的指导，成为重塑战场格局的关键理论支撑。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central slogan of Chinese Communist Party policy, associated especially with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream. It refers to restoring China's national strength and international standing.
The wartime alliance between the Communist Party and the Kuomintang and other social forces against Japanese aggression. In Party history it is a key example of united front strategy.
The defeatist view in the early war that China could not resist Japan and would inevitably be conquered. Mao's work rebuts it.
The opposite view that China could defeat Japan rapidly. Mao criticised it as underestimating the enemy.

t: The great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression took shape in the Changbai Mountains and Heilongjiang waters
zh: 伟大抗战精神在白山黑水间发轫
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 5 September 2025
paras: Written for the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression (3 September 2025), this short commentary asks where the "great spirit of resistance" began. Wang Xiliang argues that it took shape in China's north-east after the Mukden Incident of 18 September 1931, forged by Communists who fought in the front line. In the article's account, the 14 years of struggle show that the Chinese Communist Party deserved to be called the mainstay of the war.

The article opens with a quotation from Xi Jinping's anniversary speech, then follows the north-east resistance in three steps: the Party's immediate call to resist, the building and sacrifice of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, and the way the "spirit" of that army fed into the national one. Wang draws on Party documents from September 1931 and on figures for troop strength, losses and named commanders.

Wang stresses that the Manchurian Provincial Committee and the Central Committee issued declarations and resolutions within days of the incident. In this account they condemned Japanese imperialism and the Nationalist government's non-resistance policy, and called on the masses to fight. The author says that Communists sent over 500 members into the volunteer armies, then set up their own guerrilla units, which took up the banner alone after the volunteer armies' main force collapsed in early 1933. These units were renamed and in 1936 reorganised as the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, which reached more than 30,000 men in 11 armies across over 70 counties. Wang describes the Japanese and puppet authorities' encirclement campaigns, collective-responsibility rules and forced "collective hamlets", which cut the army to about 1,000. More than 30 senior commanders, including Yang Jingyu and Zhao Shangzhi, died, along with over 80 division-level cadres.

Wang concludes that the north-east army's spirit was a "trickle" that joined the wider national spirit and enriched it. He places it alongside later heroes of the full-scale war, such as Zuo Quan, Zhang Zijing and the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain, including figures from Nationalist forces. He holds that the victory shows justice, peace and the people will prevail, and that this spirit still drives the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a brief example of how the Party's current narrative places the north-east resistance within the great spirit of resistance, with the main organisations and casualty figures it cites.
quoteEn: The spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, nurtured in the early period of the resistance in the north-east, was both a trickle feeding the great spirit of resistance and something that was carried forward throughout the full-scale war, enriching its content.
quoteZh: 东北抗战初期孕育的东北抗联精神，既是伟大抗战精神的一股涓流，又在全面抗战的历史过程中不断发扬光大，丰富和充实了伟大抗战精神的内涵。

glossary.literal: great spirit of resisting the war
glossary.explanation: A Party formulation for the patriotism, national integrity, heroism and conviction of victory attributed to the Chinese people in the War of Resistance against Japan. It is one entry in the Party's "spiritual lineage".
Communist-led guerrilla forces in Manchuria, formed from 1936 from earlier units, that fought the Japanese and the puppet state of Manchukuo until 1945.
The 18 September 1931 events, in which Japan's Kwantung Army seized Shenyang (Mukden) and began its occupation of north-east China.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term goal of the Party under Xi Jinping: restoring China's strength and international standing, often linked to the Chinese Dream.

t: The far-reaching significance of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan from the perspective of civilizational history
zh: 从文明史视域看抗日战争胜利的深远意义
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today (5 September 2025), Yu Zuhua asks what the victory of the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, and of the World Anti-Fascist War, means when viewed through the history of civilization. Yu argues that the war was a life-and-death struggle at a moment when both Chinese and human civilization were under grave threat, and that the Communist Party led the Chinese people to a victory of civilization over barbarism.

The short commentary is organised in two parts. The first concerns the defence of Chinese civilization, including its territory, its cultural relics and its national spirit. The second concerns the rescue of human civilization and the upgrading of civilizational forms.

In the first part, Yu describes the war as the first fully victorious anti-invasion struggle of modern China. Yu cites the southward evacuation of Palace Museum treasures and the relocation of universities such as the Southwest Associated University as examples of protecting cultural memory. Yu further argues that the war preserved the continuity of Chinese civilization while launching its rebirth. In this account, Mao Zedong's New Democracy, the 1939 definition of a pluralistic and unified Chinese nation, and the call to concretise Marxism in China all emerged from the war. In the second part, Yu contends that China's resistance helped defeat fascism, secured China's place among the "Big Four" Allies and the founding of the United Nations, and fed anti-colonial movements. Yu also presents New Democracy as an early exploration of Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilization.

Yu concludes that the victory will be remembered both for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and for the advance of human civilization. In Yu's view, Chinese modernization's creation of a new form of human civilization shows that China will again contribute to world peace. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholars in 2025 framed the war's anniversary in civilizational terms.
quoteEn: Victory in the War of Resistance not only defended the civilizational achievements of the Chinese nation's more than 5,000 years of development, but also committed itself to building a new society and a new state for the Chinese nation, opening bright prospects for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 抗日战争的胜利，不仅“捍卫了中华民族5000多年发展的文明成果”，而且致力于“建设一个中华民族的新社会和新国家”，开辟了中华民族伟大复兴的光明前景

glossary.explanation: The official term for the Chinese Communist Party's path of modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A phrase in official discourse that describes Chinese modernization as creating a new kind of civilization, different from Western modernity.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's strength and standing after the 'century of humiliation'. It is closely tied to the Chinese Dream.
Mao Zedong's theory, set out in 1940, of a transitional stage of revolution led by the Party and a multi-class alliance. It was meant to precede socialism in China.

t: Consolidating and expanding the systemic advantages of high-quality development in the 15th Five-Year Plan period
zh: 巩固扩大“十五五”时期高质量发展体系优势
paras: Taking its cue from the Political Bureau meeting of 30 July 2025, this commentary asks how the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026–2030) should be understood and what advantages China should build on. Ma Yide argues that the period is a decisive stage on the way to basically realising socialist modernization by 2035, and that consolidating and expanding China's systemic advantages is the key to high-quality development.

The article has two parts. The first locates the period historically; the second examines four advantages named by the Political Bureau: the socialist system, the super-large market, the complete industrial system and abundant talent.

Ma describes the period as a link between past and future, a time of strategic breakout amid global change, and a phase of deepening high-quality development. Citing per capita GDP of 95,749 yuan in 2024, the article says reaching about US$30,000 by 2035 requires average growth above 4.5 percent. It also cites weak global growth forecasts, rising R&D intensity and a middle-income group of over 400 million. On the advantages, Ma holds that the new national system will sharpen efforts on "chokepoint" technologies. Domestic demand and industrial upgrading are said to reinforce each other. Because human-capital spending is still below the OECD average, Ma proposes treating education, science, health and training as "broad human-capital investment" with a binding indicator.

Ma concludes that consolidating these advantages will lay a solid foundation for basic modernization in 2035, and that the period requires understanding change accurately and responding to it actively. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line account of how Chinese policy scholars frame the priorities of the 15th Five-Year Plan period, including the statistics and the human-capital proposal.
quoteEn: The 15th Five-Year Plan period will be a critical stage in which China's high-quality economic development deepens and expands from concept to practice and from the local to the whole.
quoteZh: “十五五”时期将是我国经济高质量发展从理念到实践、从局部到全局深化拓展的关键阶段

glossary.explanation: An official goal, in place since about 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth driven by innovation, efficiency and better structure.
An official formulation for mobilising state, market and social resources behind major scientific and technological goals.
The period 2026–2030, covered by China's 15th Five-Year Plan for economic and social development.

t: Carrying forward the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression to advance national strength and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 弘扬伟大抗战精神 奋进强国建设民族复兴伟业
paras: Written for the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), this commentary asks what the wartime experience offers to the present drive to build a strong country. Yan Xiaofeng argues that understanding the war as a great national awakening, and carrying forward the great spirit of resistance, supplies the unity and self-reliance needed to advance national strength and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization.

The piece is organised in five parts. It covers the Communist Party's role in the war; the three truths of 'justice, peace and the people will prevail'; the components of the resistance spirit; the creativity the war elicited; and China's contribution to the anti-fascist war and to modernization in the wider developing world. Each part pairs a wartime lesson with a present-day task, drawing on Mao Zedong's wartime writings and speeches by Xi Jinping.

Yan contends that the Party was the mainstay of the war and the vanguard of the nation, through the anti-Japanese national united front, the protracted-war strategy and people's war. From this the author concludes that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of the Second Centenary Goal, and calls for the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds to be put into practice. The spirit of resistance is broken into patriotism and a consolidated sense of community of the Chinese nation, unyielding integrity, self-reliance, and firm belief in victory. Yan reads each as a guide for current struggles, including the need to take the nation's fate in its own hands and avoid copying foreign models. In the author's account, the war also showed creativity: with no precedent to follow, the Party devised united-front policy, military strategy and the rectification movement, just as Chinese modernization today must open its own path.

On the international side, Yan describes China's resistance as the main Eastern theatre of the anti-fascist war that tied down the bulk of Japan's forces. The author presents China today as part of the Global South, neither imitating a 'Western model' nor asking others to copy a 'Chinese model', and as pursuing a community with a shared future for mankind and a new form of human civilisation. The author also says the aim of peaceful reunification of the country will not be accompanied by any pledge to renounce force over Taiwan. Read the original if you want a Party-theorist's example of how the memory of the war is tied to Party leadership, Chinese modernization and the Global South in official discourse in 2025.
quoteEn: No nation or country in human history has become strong and rejuvenated by relying on outside forces, copying foreign models, or following slavishly in others' footsteps.
quoteZh: 人类历史上没有一个民族、一个国家可以通过依赖外部力量、照搬外国模式、跟在他人后面亦步亦趋实现强大和振兴。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of a distinctive path to modernization, stressing a huge population, common prosperity and Party leadership. It has been prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A formula from 2022 that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the Party's centralised, unified leadership.
The goal of building China into a great modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world order based on shared interests and cooperation, promoted since 2012.
A term used in Chinese official discourse for developing countries, with which China identifies itself.

glossary.en: sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A Party policy concept, stressed since 2017, that calls for strengthening a shared national identity among all ethnic groups in China.

t: The great War of Resistance forged a spirit; the Party as mainstay built the victory
zh: 伟大抗战凝精神 中流砥柱铸辉煌
paras: Published for the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan, this newspaper report by Liu Yue gathers the views of five Chinese historians. It argues that the Communist Party's role as the "mainstay" (zhongliu dizhu) of the war and the Great Spirit of Resistance should be understood through solid historical evidence and carried forward today.

The report has three parts. The first covers the meaning of the Party's mainstay role, from the 1931 Mukden Incident to the 1945 surrender. The second sets out the content and legacy of the Great Spirit of Resistance. The third reviews recent research trends and future directions. The scholars quoted come from the Central Party School, Zhejiang University, Nankai University, Beijing Normal University and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

The scholars credit the Party with a leading role in the war. They cite its early call for resistance, Mao Zedong's three-stage theory in On Protracted War, guerrilla warfare, the battlefield behind enemy lines and 19 anti-Japanese base areas. Wang Meiping cites Japanese archives, including a 1937 Home Ministry report, as showing that Japan itself saw the Party as central to resistance. Wang Binglin describes the Spirit of Resistance as patriotism, national integrity, heroism and conviction of victory. The scholars hold that this spirit and the Party's leadership reinforce each other. Hou Zhongjun sees scholarship moving from the question of who led to who played the decisive role.

The report calls for interdisciplinary work, including digital and AI methods, and for more study of the Party's institutional innovation, governance and links to the global anti-fascist war. It also urges sharing international archives and answering Japanese right-wing efforts to downplay aggression. It concludes that the spirit and the Party's mainstay role still inspire the drive to build a strong country and achieve national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a compact view of how Chinese historians and the official press frame the Party's wartime role on the 80th anniversary.
quoteEn: The Great Spirit of Resistance and the Party's role as the mainstay are dialectically unified and mutually reinforcing.
quoteZh: 伟大抗战精神与党的中流砥柱作用之间是辩证统一、相互促进的关系。

glossary.explanation: An idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm amid turmoil. In official history it describes the Communist Party's claimed role in the War of Resistance against Japan.

glossary.literal: great spirit of the War of Resistance
glossary.explanation: An official formulation for the patriotic, heroic and resolute qualities attributed to the Chinese people during the war against Japan. It is promoted in patriotic education.
Mao Zedong's 1938 work, which set out three stages of the war (strategic defence, stalemate, counter-offensive). It is presented in Party history as the strategic guide to resistance.
Territories behind Japanese lines governed by the Communist Party during the war, serving as bases for military operations and mobilisation.

t: Remembering history in order to better create the future
zh: 铭记历史是为了更好地开创未来
authors: Commentator of China Social Sciences Today
paras: This commentary from China Social Sciences Today (3 September 2025) marks the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. It argues that upholding a correct view of the history of the Second World War is necessary for respecting historical truth, defending historical justice and safeguarding the postwar international order. It frames the commemorations, including China's military parade, as a responsibility towards the future as well as respect for the past.

The piece opens with a quotation from Xi Jinping and a warning that Japanese right-wing forces, in the commentator's account, deny responsibility for aggression and refuse to admit guilt. It then proceeds through three stated needs, each introduced as a reason for a correct view of the war, and closes with a short statement on the present world situation.

On historical truth, the commentator describes China's battlefield as the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war, the earliest, longest and costliest in national sacrifice. The article cites Chinese military and civilian casualties above 35 million and direct and indirect economic losses of 100 billion and 500 billion US dollars at 1937 prices. It credits the Communist Party of China with a pivotal role. On justice and order, it says China's victory saved world peace and gave rise to the great spirit of resistance. The commentator presents the war as the product of hegemonism and power politics, and calls for supporting the UN-centred system and a community with a shared future for mankind.

The commentary concludes that, amid accelerating global change, humanity stands at a crossroads between unity and division, dialogue and confrontation, win-win and zero-sum outcomes. It calls for firm opposition to hegemonism, power politics, historical revisionism and the revival of fascism and militarism. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official Chinese narrative around the 2025 anniversary and its link to current foreign-policy language.
quoteEn: A correct view of the history of the Second World War stresses reverence for history and respect for historical facts, and is increasingly becoming a consensus of the international community.
quoteZh: 正确二战史观强调敬畏历史、尊重历史事实，日渐成为国际社会的共识。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.literal: community of common destiny for humankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13, holding that countries' fates are interlinked and should be managed through cooperation and multilateralism.
The official Chinese description of China's battlefield in the Second World War, used to stress its central place in the global anti-fascist war.

glossary.en: a correct view of the history of the Second World War
glossary.literal: correct Second World War historical outlook
glossary.explanation: A phrase used in Chinese official discourse for an interpretation that stresses Axis responsibility and China's contribution, and opposes revisionist accounts, especially in Japan.

t: Fully recognising China's major contribution to victory in the world anti-fascist war
st: Interview with Richard Overy, historian of the Second World War at the University of Exeter
zh: 充分认识中国抗战对世界反法西斯战争胜利的重大贡献
zhSub: 访英国埃克塞特大学历史学教授、二战史研究专家理查德·奥弗里
paras: This is an interview, conducted by Chen Mirong for Chinese Social Sciences Today and published in September 2025, with Richard Overy, professor of history at the University of Exeter and a specialist on the Second World War. It begins from the Western textbook date of 1 September 1939 and from Overy's view, first set out in 1987, that the war began in 1931. The occasion is the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance and the world anti-fascist war.

Chen's questions cover three topics: why Overy moved the start of the war to 1931 and how Western historians responded; why China's theatre is underrated in global literature; and which research areas and cooperation could correct the bias.

Overy argues that the war should be seen as the result of three rising empires (Japan, Italy and Germany) expanding in China, Africa and central and eastern Europe. In his account, the Mukden Incident of 18 September 1931 was the first armed challenge to the order dominated by Britain and France since 1919, and appeasement of Japan encouraged later aggression in Ethiopia, Austria and Czechoslovakia. He attributes under-recognition of China's role to the scarcity of detailed English-language studies, language barriers and the war's vast geography. In his view, Japan never defeated Chinese forces, and China's prolonged resistance blocked Japan's planned "new order" and tied down its main army.

Overy suggests further work on the social history of the war, on how China sustained resistance with scarce weaponry, and on the Communist Party's leadership and the base areas, using archives. He notes that public perceptions remain tied to national narratives, so change will be slow. He hopes that translation of Chinese scholarship and open archives will lead to joint research. Read the original if you want a short statement, by a Western historian, of the case for dating the Second World War from 1931 and of the research gaps he sees on China's wartime role.
quoteEn: Only by moving the start of the Second World War from 1939 back to 1931 can we see the whole picture: it was the product of resonance among three crisis zones, East Asia, Africa/the Middle East and Europe.
quoteZh: 把二战起点从1939年前移至1931年，我们才能看清这场战争的全貌：它是东亚、非洲/中东与欧洲三大危机地带共振的产物。

t: Reconstructing the discourse on the main Eastern theatre from a global-history perspective
zh: 重构全球史视域下东方主战场话语体系
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2025, asks how the Chinese theatre of the Second World War should be placed in global history. Cai Sheng argues that mainstream Western narratives treat it as secondary, and that a global-history approach, free of Western-centrism, shows it to be the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war.
The article is organised around three dimensions: time, space and value. Each is set against a Western-centric account that Cai presents as fragmenting or belittling China's war of resistance.

On time, Cai rejects 1939 as the start of the war and proposes the Mukden Incident of 1931, placing Japan's invasion alongside Italy's attack on Ethiopia and Germany's annexation of Austria. Cai divides the war into three phases: containing expansion (1931–1937), resisting alone (1937–1941) and allied cooperation (1941–1945). On space, the article contends that China tied down Japan's army, disrupted Axis coordination, supported the Allied 'Europe first' strategy, cooperated with other theatres through the Burma campaign and the Party-led base areas, and served as a rear base. On value, Cai credits the Chinese theatre with undermining colonial legitimacy, enabling China's role in founding the United Nations, and offering experience, including the Three-Thirds system and On Protracted War, to later independence movements.

Cai calls for fixing 1931 as the start date, rebuilding the theatre's links with other fronts, and creating a multi-dimensional value assessment covering military, political and civilizational contributions. Cai presents this as both historical restoration and a resource for new international relations and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese scholars argue for a 1931 start date and a central place for China in global anti-fascist history.
quoteEn: The Western narrative's spatial belittling of the Chinese theatre is in essence a continuation of the colonial view of history.
quoteZh: 西方叙事对中国战场的空间矮化，本质是殖民史观的延续。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2012–13, calling for shared interests and joint global governance. Chinese commentators often invoke it to frame historical and international arguments.
The Chinese designation of China's war of resistance against Japan as the principal theatre of the anti-fascist war in the East, parallel to the Soviet-German front in Europe.
A power-sharing arrangement in the Communist-led anti-Japanese base areas, in which Communists, non-Party progressives and middle-of-the-road figures each held roughly one third of government seats.
Mao Zedong's 1938 work setting out a three-stage strategy for defeating Japan through prolonged resistance.

t: How the Tokyo Trial reshaped understandings of the international rule of law
zh: 东京审判重塑国际法治认知
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 3 September 2025
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the anti-fascist war in 2025, this newspaper commentary asks what the Tokyo Trial contributed to modern international law. Xu Chi argues that, together with the Nuremberg Trial, it ended an old order in which war was a sovereign right, and that its significance is still underrated because of Western-centred narratives. The author holds that recovering its meaning matters now, amid unilateralism and hegemonic politics.

The piece is organised in four sections. The first sets the Tokyo Trial against the power-politics logic of traditional international law. The second treats its dismantling of the nineteenth-century discourse of "civilization". The third examines the Asian dimension: victim states, the judges Mei Ru'ao, Jaranilla and Pal, and regional legacies. The last turns to present-day relevance and calls for a pluralistic international rule of law.

Xu contends that the two trials created the crimes against peace and crimes against humanity and established that launching aggressive war is itself a crime. In reply to critics who invoke nullum crimen sine lege, the author argues that the principle exists to restrain state abuse of criminal law, and that aggressive war is the sum of serious "natural crimes" whose criminality needs no written statute. Individual criminal responsibility, applied to figures such as Tojo Hideki, is said to have broken the myth of absolute state immunity. Xu also argues that the trial reversed the roles of China, the Philippines and India, once labelled "barbarous", and Japan, which had styled itself "civilized", thereby exposing the hierarchy of civilizations as hypocritical.

Xu says Asian participation gave the trial its legitimacy. Chinese suffering since 1931 widened its jurisdictional frame, and Pal's dissent is quoted as criticising colonial double standards. The author links the trial to the 1951 San Francisco Treaty, Article 9 of Japan's constitution and later victims' lawsuits. The author calls for defending a UN-centred international system and an order based on international law, and for rejecting the use of law as an instrument of power politics, in line with a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese official-academic framing of the Tokyo Trial's legacy and its use in current arguments about international law.
quoteEn: The Tokyo Trial proved that the true measure of civilization is not region, race or ideology, but universal respect for the rights to life and dignity.
quoteZh: 东京审判证明，文明的真正尺度不是地域、种族或意识形态，而是对生命权、尊严权的普遍尊重。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s, envisioning cooperative international relations based on shared interests and values. Chinese writers often invoke it in discussing international order and law.

t: Interdisciplinary methods boost research on ecological civilization
zh: 跨学科方法助推生态文明研究
paras: Cao argues that ecological civilization is an inherently cross-disciplinary field, and that studying it requires interdisciplinary methods rather than a simple stacking of disciplinary knowledge. In Cao's view, genuine exchange between disciplines allows researchers to grasp the complexity of ecological civilization construction more comprehensively and to find new solutions.

The short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in September 2025, is organised around three groups of disciplines: natural sciences, social sciences and the humanities. For each group Cao sets out three ways it contributes to the study of ecological civilization.

For the natural sciences, Cao lists theoretical support from ecology, environmental science and climatology; technological innovation such as geographic information systems for real-time monitoring; and science popularisation that builds public awareness. For the social sciences, the three contributions are social surveys and data collection, qualitative analysis and case studies, and quantitative analysis and modelling for forecasting. For the humanities, Cao points to historical methods such as environmental history, literary reading of ecological writing, and philosophical reflection on ecological ethics, including environmental justice and ecological responsibility.

Cao concludes that interdisciplinary methods have significant application value and prospects, and calls for more exchange and cooperation among disciplines to support more scientific and rational environmental protection and sustainable development strategies. The piece is a stage result of a National Social Science Fund project on ecological philosophy in Capital and its manuscripts. Read the original if you want a concise overview of how Chinese scholars map the disciplinary landscape of ecological civilization research.
quoteEn: The application of interdisciplinary methods will cross the boundaries between disciplines and integrate their knowledge and resources, giving ecological civilization construction more scientific and systematic interdisciplinary support.
quoteZh: 跨学科方法的应用将跨越不同学科之间的界限，整合各个学科知识和资源，为推动生态文明建设提供更为科学、系统的跨学科支撑。

glossary.explanation: A concept in Chinese Party and state policy that treats harmony between humans and nature as a goal of development. It has been written into official documents and the Party and state constitutions.

t: The historical standing of the Eastern main battlefield, seen through the international order
zh: 从国际秩序看东方主战场的历史地位
paras: Chen Haiyi, writing in a Chinese Social Sciences Today commentary of September 2025, takes up the standing of the Chinese theatre in the Second World War. Western mainstream accounts date the war's start to Germany's invasion of Poland in 1939, and Chen says foreign scholarship has long neglected or ignored China's role. The article argues that the evolution of the international order, from the League of Nations to the United Nations, offers a useful lens for understanding China as the Eastern main battlefield of the world anti-fascist war.

The piece follows three stages. It covers China's appeal to the League after the Mukden Incident of 1931, the long resistance after the full-scale invasion of 1937, and China's part in building the postwar order from 1942 to 1945.

Chen first holds that the Chinese theatre was the earliest anti-fascist battlefield. After 1931 the League's appeasement, led by Britain and France, and American inaction left China to bear Japanese aggression largely alone. The article credits the Chinese Communist Party with organising anti-Japanese guerrilla forces in the Northeast. Second, Chen cites the League's own journal Headway, which in 1942 called China the first victim of the aggression that set off the war. Third, Chen argues that China's resistance tied down Japan. It forced Japan to give up the "northward advance", delayed the "southward advance" and, through the expedition to Burma, helped frustrate a Japanese–German link-up. This, the author says, made China one of the "Four Powers", a signatory of the Declaration by United Nations, a founding member of the UN and a permanent member of the Security Council.

Chen concludes that the shift from the weak League to the more authoritative UN carries the lessons of China's war and the strategic contribution of the Eastern main battlefield. China moved from being an object of aid to a builder of the international order. Read the original if you want a short statement of the Chinese historiographical case for the war's earlier start and China's role in founding the UN.
quoteEn: It was precisely the enormous sacrifices and the key role of the Chinese theatre that made China one of the "Four Powers" and brought about, within the UN system, a historic shift from recipient of aid to builder of the international order.
quoteZh: 正是中国战场付出的巨大牺牲与发挥的关键作用，使中国成为“四强”之一，并在联合国机制中实现从被援助对象向国际秩序构建者的历史性转变。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese official and scholarly designation for the Chinese theatre of the Second World War, used to stress its central place in the war against Japan and fascism in Asia.
The Japanese Kwantung Army's staged attack of 18 September 1931 and subsequent seizure of Northeast China. Chinese historiography treats it as the start of the war against Japan.
The clash at the Marco Polo Bridge on 7 July 1937, which opened Japan's full-scale war on China.

t: The historic contribution of China's War of Resistance in a global perspective
zh: 全球视野下中国抗战的历史性贡献
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2025, Gao Guorong asks what place China's War of Resistance against Japan (1931–45) holds in the global anti-fascist war. The article argues that China shouldered the main Eastern theatre, was the decisive force in defeating Japanese fascism, made an indispensable contribution to the Allied victory in Europe, and inspired national liberation movements in colonial and semi-colonial countries.

This is a short commentary in three parts, followed by a brief conclusion. The first part treats China's role in resisting and defeating Japan. The second examines China's support for the Allied strategy of "Europe first, Asia second". The third discusses the war's effect on China's own rejuvenation and on liberation movements elsewhere. The article closes with positive assessments from wartime leaders: Mao Zedong, Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill.

Gao holds that China began the world's anti-fascist war with the Mukden Incident of 1931, opened the first large-scale anti-fascist battlefield in Asia after 1937, and fought largely alone for over a decade because of Western appeasement. According to the article, the Chinese theatre consumed 4.55 million Japanese troops (killed, wounded, captured or surrendered), 70 per cent of Japan's total losses. Gao argues that by pinning down Japan's main army, China let the Soviet Union avoid a two-front war, because Japan's "northward" plan failed and Japan did not attack the USSR after Germany invaded it. China also delayed Japan's "southward" advance and the outbreak of the Pacific War, according to the article. The article adds that China supplied airfields, harbours, materiel and intelligence, and sent an expeditionary force to Burma in 1942.

Gao concludes that victory in the war was a turning point in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation: the first complete victory over a foreign invader in modern times. The article says it brought the abolition of many unequal treaties, the recovery of territory including Taiwan, a higher international standing and a stronger Communist-led revolutionary force. It also claims the war exposed the falsehood of Japan's "Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere" and heralded postwar decolonisation across Asia, Africa and Latin America. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Chinese account of the war's global significance, including the wartime leaders' statements it cites.
quoteEn: The victory of China's War of Resistance became the forerunner of the surging national independence movements around the world after the war, promoted national liberation movements across Asia, Africa and Latin America, and greatly changed the postwar international order.
quoteZh: 中国抗战的胜利成为战后世界各地风起云涌的民族独立运动的先导，促进了亚非拉广大地区民族解放运动的发展，极大地改变了战后国际秩序。

glossary.explanation: The Allied grand strategy of giving priority to defeating Germany before concentrating on Japan. The article argues that China's resistance made this strategy workable.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'. Here it is used to frame the War of Resistance as a historical turning point.
The Chinese historiographical claim that the Chinese theatre was the principal Asian theatre against Japan, paired with the Soviet-led European theatre in the West.

t: Awakening good people's longing for peace and commitment to it
st: New progress in research on evidence of Japan's crimes in China and its value
zh: 唤起善良的人们对和平的向往和坚守
zhSub: 日本侵华罪证研究的新进展及其价值
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), Zhang Lianhong surveys recent research on evidence of Japanese military crimes in China. The article, originally published in the People's Daily, takes its framing from Xi Jinping's remark that condemning aggressors is meant not to perpetuate hatred but to awaken longing for peace. Zhang argues that research in China and abroad has reached unprecedented breadth and depth, and that its value lies in historical justice and in safeguarding peace.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews new source material: archives, oral history and online databases. The second examines interdisciplinary and big-data methods. The third sets out the contemporary significance of this work. Cases include the Nanjing Massacre, bacteriological and chemical warfare, Unit 731, the "comfort women" system, indiscriminate bombing and forced labour.

On sources, Zhang notes that Japan's government destroyed core wartime files before the war ended, leaving a shortage of first-hand documents. The article cites 370 sets of Khabarovsk trial documents released online by Russia's federal archives, soldiers' diaries and archival finds by Japanese scholars, and oral testimony from victims and Japanese veterans. It also cites the databases of the Institute of Modern History at CASS, Japan's Asia Historical Resources Center and a Korean database. On method, Zhang points to microhistory of villages near Nanjing, global-history comparison, legal analysis of war crimes, and work in sociology, medical history and environmental history. Examples of big-data work include GIS analysis of oral accounts of germ warfare and sentiment analysis of The Diary of John Rabe, which the article says rebuts right-wing doubts about the diary's objectivity.

Zhang concludes that this research counters historical nihilism and Japanese right-wing denial, strengthens national spirit and collective memory, and carries a warning for the world about extreme nationalism and militarism. The article cites Chinese casualties of over 35 million and describes victory as a turning point in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It links remembering history to building a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a brief official-register overview of the new sources and methods in studies of Japanese war crimes in China, and of how they are framed in the 2025 anniversary commemoration.
quoteEn: Every newly discovered archive and every deepening of research reinforces the bastion of historical truth, so that any attempt to distort or whitewash history has nowhere to hide before the facts.
quoteZh: 每一件新档案的发现、每一次研究的深化，都是对历史真相堡垒的加固，使任何企图歪曲、粉饰历史的言行在事实面前都无所遁形。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's accepted historical narrative. Here it is applied to Japanese denial of wartime aggression.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s as the aim of China's foreign policy and vision of world order.
