glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Party discourse since Xi Jinping's leadership began, presenting modern Chinese history as a path from humiliation to renewal.

t: The historical turning point from deep crisis to great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
st: Commemorating the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression
zh: 中华民族从深重危机走向伟大复兴的历史转折点
zhSub: 纪念中国人民抗日战争胜利80周年
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan (2025), Ju argues that the war was the turning point at which the Chinese nation moved from the deep crisis of the modern era towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article presents the war as the longest, largest and costliest national liberation struggle China had fought against foreign invasion, and as the first complete victory in such a struggle since 1840. It frames this with Xi Jinping's formulation of the victory as a historical turning point.

The article is organised in three parts followed by a short conclusion. The first covers the awakening and unification of the nation, from the Japanese advances of 1914–1937 to the Party's call for resistance, the student movement of 9 December 1935 and mass mobilisation at home and overseas. The second asks why China won after a century of defeats, and answers through the Party's leadership, the people's army and the spirit of resistance. The third examines China's changed international standing, the abolition of unequal treaties and the road to the founding of New China.

Ju's central claim is that the Communist Party was the mainstay of the national war effort. The article credits the Party with building the anti-Japanese national united front, with Mao Zedong's strategy of protracted war, with the war behind enemy lines and with sustaining the united front despite Guomindang attacks such as the Southern Anhui Incident of 1941. In the author's account, national awakening required both an unprecedented threat and a visible way out, which the Party supplied. The author also argues that the victory restored China's great-power status, citing the Declaration by United Nations, the Security Council seat and the 1943 treaties ending extraterritoriality. After 1945, Ju says, the Guomindang chose civil war and lost popular support, which accelerated the victory of the New Democratic Revolution.

Ju concludes that the 105 years from 1840 to 1945 were a period of decline, and that the 80 years since have seen the Party found New China, carry out socialist construction and reform and opening up, and build a moderately prosperous society in all respects. In the author's view, the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has now entered an irreversible historical process. Read the original if you want an example of how the official Party narrative, as carried in the journal Qiushi, presents the War of Resistance and links it to the present.
quoteEn: The War of Resistance was not only a contest of military and economic strength, but even more a confrontation of will and spirit.
quoteZh: 抗日战争，不仅是军事实力和经济实力的较量，更是意志和精神的对垒。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China's strength and standing after the humiliations of the modern era. It has been closely associated with Xi Jinping since 2012.

The wartime alliance policy, centred on cooperation between the Communist Party and the Guomindang, aimed at uniting all social groups against Japan. The Party formally adopted it as its line in December 1935.

Mao Zedong's term for the stage of the Chinese revolution led by the Communist Party against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism, seen as preceding socialism. In Party history it ends with the founding of the People's Republic in 1949.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the world economy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A long-standing Party goal of broad, modest prosperity. Officials declared it built in all respects in 2021.
Mao Zedong's 1938 strategy in On Protracted War. It held that China would win through a long struggle in three stages, mobilising the people to wear down a stronger enemy.

t: Drawing on the history of the War of Resistance against Japan to advance political army-building
zh: 镜鉴抗战历史 推进政治建军
authors: Research Centre for Party History and Military History of the PLA, Academy of Military Sciences
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan, this commentary from the PLA Academy of Military Sciences' Party and military history research centre asks how the Party's wartime experience can guide political army-building (zhengzhi jianjun) today. The authors argue that during the war the Party deepened its understanding of how to build the army politically, and that this understanding enabled a weaker force to defeat a stronger one. They hold that it remains essential as world, national, Party and military conditions change.

The article is organised around four relationships that, in the authors' account, the war revealed: military affairs and politics, the Party and the army, the army and the people, and spirit and matter. Each section first recounts wartime evidence, drawing on Mao Zedong's On Protracted War, Party documents, the Eighth Route Army and New Fourth Army, and the 1944 report by Tan Zheng. It then sets out what the authors call tasks for the new journey, citing Xi Jinping's statements since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

First, the authors argue that war is politics by other means. They say the Party's judgement that the Sino-Japanese contradiction had become principal let it forge the united front and reorganise the Red Army, so that the army's tasks followed national tasks. Today this means judging military questions by a political yardstick and giving priority to "upholding political guidance", the first of Xi Jinping's "five upholds" of military thinking. Second, the authors cite the Party's insistence on its own command of the gun: the army's wartime bodies, such as military-political committees, and the stance that Communists should fight for the Party's, the people's and the nation's military power. They draw from this the need to uphold absolute Party leadership, the chairman responsibility system of the Central Military Commission and the Two Establishes. Third, they present the people as the basis of victory and call for stronger military–civilian unity, combat-readiness and integration of new quality productive forces with new quality combat capability. Fourth, they stress fighting spirit, citing about 35 million Chinese casualties and calling for ideological education, realistic training and a martial culture.

The authors conclude that upholding political army-building is the fundamental reason the people's army moves from victory to victory. They call for absolute Party leadership, the army's original purpose, and a will to fight and win, so that the army becomes purer, more glorious and more reliable. In their view this will support Chinese modernization and national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want to see how the Party's military research establishment links wartime history to current army-building doctrine and to Xi Jinping's military thought.
quoteEn: For the army to win battles, the people are its mainstay.
quoteZh: 军队打胜仗，人民是靠山。

glossary.explanation: A principle of Party doctrine that the armed forces must be built first on political loyalty and Party leadership. It is traced to the 1929 Gutian Conference and revived under Xi Jinping.
A formula from the 2021 Party resolution on history. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023 for advanced, technology-driven productive forces. The article pairs it with "new quality combat capability" in the military sphere.
The official term for China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central long-term goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, often linked to the centenary goals for 2049.

glossary.en: chairman responsibility system of the Central Military Commission
glossary.literal: Central Military Commission chairman responsibility system
glossary.explanation: The constitutional and Party arrangement under which the CMC chairman, currently Xi Jinping, bears overall responsibility for the armed forces.

t: Drawing strength for advancing from the great spirit of resistance to Japanese aggression
zh: 从伟大抗战精神中汲取奋进力量
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 1 September 2025
paras: Writing for the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), Liu Guopu examines Xi Jinping's series of statements on the war. The commentary argues that these statements are more than a historical summary. In Liu's account they apply historical materialism creatively, serve as a weapon against historical nihilism, supply spiritual momentum for Chinese modernization, and offer Chinese historical wisdom for building a community with a shared future for mankind.

The piece is organised into four sections, one for each of these claims. It moves from the theoretical and methodological character of Xi's statements to their polemical function, then to their domestic role in national rejuvenation, and finally to their international significance for global governance and the writing of Second World War history. It closes with a short call to deepen the scholarly study of these statements.

Liu makes three main moves. First, working within the Two Integrations, Xi's account is said to treat the "people" as the deepest source of victory. It folds the frontline and behind-the-lines battlefields, the base-area governments, the rear-area salvation movements, and overseas Chinese and foreign friends into a framework of "people's war". It also places the war in both the long span of Chinese civilisation and the global anti-fascist struggle, which Liu says rebuts Eurocentric readings and narrow nationalism. Second, against historical nihilism, which Liu says fragments and distorts the record, the statements stress the Communist Party's role as the mainstay of resistance and China as the main Eastern theatre. They also ask people to remember Japanese militarist crimes while rejecting "historical revenge" and respecting other peoples' contributions. Third, the great spirit of resistance (patriotism, indomitable integrity, heroism, confidence in victory) is presented as matching the values needed to face today's risks, such as technological bottlenecks and unbalanced development.

Liu concludes that Xi's statements unite historical, theoretical and practical logic, and that the war's lessons ("justice, peace and the people will prevail") bear on peace and development today. As examples of putting them into practice, Liu cites the National Memorial Day for Nanjing Massacre victims and commemorations of victory. Liu calls for turning historical memory into drive for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academic commentary in 2025 presents Xi Jinping's war narrative as theory, as ideological defence and as international message.
quoteEn: Great history gives birth to a great spirit, and a great spirit drives great undertakings.
quoteZh: 伟大的历史孕育伟大的精神，伟大的精神推动伟大的事业。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), of a modernization path said to be distinct from Western models. It is used as the central framework for national development goals.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views seen as denying or distorting the Party's and the nation's revolutionary history and achievements.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, introduced around 2012–13, calling for shared international responsibility and cooperation.

glossary.literal: great spirit of the War of Resistance
glossary.explanation: The official term for the values attributed to the Chinese people in the war against Japan, summed up by Xi Jinping as patriotism, integrity, heroism and confidence in victory.

glossary.literal: great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the 2010s.

t: Drawing wisdom and strength for the road ahead from the great victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression
zh: 从中国人民抗日战争伟大胜利中汲取不断前行的智慧和力量
authors: Party History and Literature Research Institute of the CPC Central Committee
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, this commemorative article asks what lessons the victory holds for the present. Its authors, the Party's central research institute for history and documents, present the war as the first complete victory in a national liberation war against foreign invasion since modern times and as a turning point towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They argue that its wisdom and strength should be drawn on to advance national strengthening through Chinese modernization. The piece appeared in Qiushi, 2025 no. 17.

The article is organised around five "musts" drawn from the war experience: uphold the Party's overall leadership; keep to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics; put the people first; uphold the fighting spirit; and unswervingly follow the path of peaceful development. Each section recounts wartime history, quoting Mao Zedong, Xi Jinping and figures such as Nie Rongzhen and Wen Yiduo, and then turns to present-day tasks.

On leadership, the authors credit the Communist Party with proposing the anti-Japanese national united front, devising the strategy of protracted war and opening the enemy-rear battlefield. They cite figures of 19 base areas covering nearly 1 million square kilometres and almost 100 million people, and say guerrilla warfare tied down 58–75 per cent of Japanese forces in China. On the path, they describe Mao's wartime writings on New Democracy as answering Nationalist claims that the Three Principles of the People made socialism unnecessary. On the people, they argue that mass mobilisation, the "three-thirds" system and rent reduction made the base areas decisive. They present the war as the world's eastern main battlefield, and reject any denial or glorification of aggression.

The authors conclude that the Party must remain the people's backbone through the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, hold to confidence in socialism with Chinese characteristics, serve the people, and show a readiness to struggle against mounting internal and external risks. They also call for true multilateralism, a correct view of Second World War history and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want an authoritative example of how the Party's central research institute draws present-day political lessons from the anti-Japanese war.
quoteEn: The question of the path bears directly on the rise or fall, success or failure, of the cause of the Party and the people.
quoteZh: 道路问题直接关系党和人民事业兴衰成败。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernisation, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as the main framework for national development.
A Party formula, adopted in 2021–22, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation".

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world of shared interests and cooperation, used to frame China's approach to global governance.
The Party's official name for its path since reform and opening up, combining Marxist principles with China's conditions.

t: Gathering the strength to remember history and strive for national rejuvenation
st: Qiushi editorial on the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 《求是》杂志编辑部：凝聚起铭记历史、矢志复兴的强大力量
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, this editorial from Qiushi (no. 17, 2025) argues that remembering the war is a basis for building the future. It presents victory as the historical turning point from national catastrophe towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The editorial introduces itself as a study guide to Xi Jinping's remarks on the war, collected in an excerpted article covering July 2014 to May 2025, and to the speech he was due to give on 3 September in Beijing.

The text is organised in four sections: the Chinese Communist Party's role as the mainstay of victory; China's opening of the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war; the lesson that China must unwaveringly follow the path of peaceful development; and the call to carry forward the great spirit of resistance for national rejuvenation. It also lists post-2012 commemorative measures, including a statutory victory day, a national memorial day and a commemorative medal.

On the first point, the editorial argues that the Party led on three questions: whether to resist, whom to rely on, and how to fight. It cites the Party's early calls for armed resistance, its advocacy of the anti-Japanese national united front, and its strategy of protracted war and people's war. It gives figures for the forces it led, including 1.714 million Japanese and puppet troops eliminated and 19 base areas. On the second point, it says China fought longest and tied down Japan's main forces, which, in its account, helped the Soviet Union avoid a two-front war and supported the Allies' 'Europe first' strategy. It cites estimates of 35 million Chinese military and civilian casualties and says that some forces play down China's role. It calls for a correct view of the Second World War and links this to the Taiwan question.

The editorial concludes that peaceful development remains China's firm choice. It says China will not give up its legitimate rights or core interests, and it criticises unilateralism and hegemonism while backing a community with a shared future for mankind. It treats the spirit of resistance as a resource for the present. It names the 2035 goal of basically realising socialist modernization and the mid-century goal, and says the spirit should help meet external pressure, domestic economic risks and ideological diversity. Read the original if you want to see how Party media currently frame the war's memory, its Party leadership narrative, and its links to foreign policy and rejuvenation goals.
quoteEn: Historical facts prove that it was precisely the anti-Japanese national united front, which the Communist Party advocated and led, that raised the awakening and unity of the Chinese nation to an unprecedented height and merged it into a surging torrent against foreign aggression, providing an inexhaustible source of strength for victory.
quoteZh: 历史事实证明，正是因为中国共产党倡导建立和领导的抗日民族统一战线，使中华民族的觉醒和团结达到了前所未有的高度，凝聚成反抗外来侵略的滚滚洪流，为抗战胜利提供了不竭的力量源泉。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s as the aim of China's foreign policy. It stresses shared interests, multilateralism and win-win cooperation.
The wartime coalition between the Communist Party and the Nationalists, together with other social forces, formed in 1937. Party histories treat it as a key element of resistance.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, popularised under Xi Jinping. It means restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.
The official line that China pursues development without seeking expansion or hegemony. The editorial pairs it with a firm defence of China's core interests.

t: The spirit of the War of Resistance: a powerful spiritual force enabling the Chinese nation to overcome all difficulties and obstacles
zh: 抗战精神：中华民族战胜一切艰难险阻的强大精神动力
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times on 29 August 2025, takes up the 'great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression' (the spirit of the War of Resistance). Guo Fang argues that the spirit formed during the war is a precious spiritual asset that still motivates the Chinese people to overcome difficulties and pursue the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The piece builds on Xi Jinping's 2014 speech, which named four components of this spirit.

The article first sketches the war as a just struggle against Japanese fascism, from the Mukden Incident of 1931 to the full-scale invasion of 1937. It cites a cost of 35 million casualties over 14 years and calls the outcome the first complete victory in modern China against foreign invasion. It then devotes one section to each of the four components, with examples of battles and martyrs.

Guo presents the four components as a structure: patriotism, in the sense that everyone is responsible for the nation's fate, is the core; national integrity is its expression in character; heroism that fears no violence is its outward quality; and belief in ultimate victory is its inner driving force. In the account, the Communist Party's early declarations and its call for a united front shaped national mobilisation, while both Nationalist and Communist forces fought, on the frontal and enemy-rear battlefields respectively. Examples include Yang Jingyu, the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain and the battles of Pingxingguan, Taierzhuang and the Hundred Regiments Offensive. Guo credits Mao Zedong's three-stage prediction of the war with sustaining confidence.

The author concludes that this conviction let a poorly equipped people defeat a stronger enemy, which the piece calls a miracle in the history of warfare. Its framing is the continuing relevance of the spirit to national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official narrative of the War of Resistance and its 'spirit' is presented in Party media around the 2025 anniversary.
quoteEn: Belief burns like a torch, undimmed even after nine deaths.
quoteZh: 信念如炬，九死未悔。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Chinese Communist Party discourse, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'. It has been emphasised especially since Xi Jinping became leader in 2012.

glossary.en: the spirit of the War of Resistance
glossary.literal: spirit of the War of Resistance
glossary.explanation: The official term for the patriotic values attributed to the Chinese people in the war against Japan of 1931–45. Xi Jinping summarised it in 2014 in four components.
The cooperation between the Communist Party, the Nationalist Party and other forces against Japan, formed in the late 1930s. Chinese official history credits the Communist Party with advocating it.

t: The world significance of the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression
st: Perceptions and writings from Western scholarship
zh: 中国人民抗日战争的世界意义
zhSub: 来自西方学界的认知与书写
paras: Writing in a Chinese social science newspaper in August 2025, Liu Bensen asks how Western scholarship now assesses the world significance of China's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. Liu argues that Western historians increasingly recognise the Chinese theatre as the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war. In this reading, China's resistance made a decisive contribution to Allied victory and to the post-war order, and offered a model for national liberation movements elsewhere.

The article is a short commentary built around works by mainly American and British historians and journalists, set against Xi Jinping's statement that the war was from the start of great significance for saving human civilisation and defending world peace. It has three sections: the Chinese theatre as historical starting point and strategic fulcrum of the anti-fascist war; China's role in forming the anti-fascist alliance and reshaping the post-war order; and the war as a strategic example for national liberation movements.

In the first section, Liu cites scholars such as Andrew Buchanan and Ted Uldricks, who treat the 1931 Mukden Incident as the beginning of the Second World War, and Ronald Spector and Rana Mitter, who argue that China tied down the main Japanese army forces and supported Allied operations. In the second, Liu draws on Mitter, Uldricks and Graham Peck's contemporaries such as Stilwell to present the Shanghai battle, the Yunnan–Burma campaigns and China's part in founding the United Nations as shaping the war's course and the post-war order. In the third, Liu cites Spector, Max Boot, Mark Selden and others on people's war, guerrilla warfare, protracted war, the united front and base-area building as models taken up by revolutionaries abroad.

Liu concludes that the war made a decisive contribution to victory and restored China's standing as a major power. Remembering it and deepening understanding of its world significance, Liu says, serves the common values of humankind and the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a quick guide to the Western-language scholarship that Chinese academics cite to support the claim of the war's global significance.
quoteEn: As a firm strategic fulcrum of the world anti-fascist war, the Chinese theatre not only drained and weakened Japan's war strength and slowed the pace of Japanese aggression, but at critical moments strongly underpinned the Allies' global counter-offensive strategy, laying a solid Eastern foundation for the final defeat of the fascist Axis.
quoteZh: 中国战场作为世界反法西斯战争中一个坚强的战略支点，不仅消耗和削弱了日本的战争实力，减缓了日军的侵略步伐，更在关键时刻有力地支撑了盟军的全球反攻战略，为最终战胜法西斯轴心国奠定了坚实的东方基石。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–2013 as the guiding idea of China's foreign policy and vision of international relations.
Mao Zedong's strategy of mobilising the whole population, politically and militarily, in a protracted struggle against a stronger enemy.
The official Chinese description of the Chinese theatre within the global anti-fascist war, used to stress China's central role.
The 1931 incident that Japan used as a pretext to occupy north-east China; Chinese scholarship treats it as the start of the anti-Japanese war.

t: Raising the level of social security governance in the digital age
zh: 提升数字时代社会安全治理水平
paras: This commentary from Guangming Daily asks how China should manage the social security risks that accompany the digital economy. Wang argues that these risks are more complex and more prone to cascading effects than traditional ones. The author holds that they call for coordinated, systematic governance, in line with policy documents such as the Overall Plan for Building a Digital China and the 2025 key tasks for the digital economy.

The piece is organised around four tasks: building mechanisms to identify social security problems precisely, improving the governance system, building smart management platforms, and responding better to public concerns and expectations.

On identification, Wang calls for real-time monitoring and early warning around data rights, circulation and income distribution. Wang also wants attention to market volatility and to emerging gaps between groups and regions, balancing an efficient market with an effective government. On governance, Wang urges a holistic outlook of prevention first, cross-departmental coordination, and more detailed rules building on the Cybersecurity Law and Data Security Law, with stricter penalties for personal data leaks. The platform proposal envisions a closed-loop process of sensing, analysis, pushing alerts, response and linkage, with digital twins used to forecast risks such as supply-chain disruption.

Finally, Wang proposes using both traditional and digital channels to gauge public opinion, providing tailored services for the elderly, and strengthening social assistance. The author also wants workers in new forms of employment brought into social insurance. Wang presents this as a way to protect workers' rights and promote social fairness and harmony. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official-leaning Chinese scholarship frames digital-era risk governance and its policy priorities.
quoteEn: The vigorous development of digital technology has also brought a series of challenges to social security governance.
quoteZh: 数字技术的蓬勃发展，也为社会安全治理带来了一系列挑战。

t: The historical contribution of the Counter-Japanese Military and Political University to the Anti-Japanese National United Front
zh: 抗大在抗日民族统一战线中的历史贡献
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, asks what the Counter-Japanese Military and Political University (Kangda) contributed to the Anti-Japanese National United Front. Gao argues that Kangda, the Communist Party's highest military academy, trained more than 100,000 military and political cadres and helped consolidate and develop the Front. The author also calls it a "revolutionary furnace" in modern Chinese educational history.

The article opens with the background of the national crisis after the 1931 Mukden Incident and the founding of the school in 1936 as the Chinese Anti-Japanese Red Army University. It then examines three areas of contribution: spreading anti-Japanese theory, safeguarding national unity in the war of resistance, and taking part in actual combat. Examples include course content, songs, student recruitment, responses to Kuomintang actions and named battles.

On theory, Gao says Kangda made the Party's united front policy and Mao Zedong's writings compulsory study, and sent students out as propaganda and work teams, including performance troupes whose shows reportedly even persuaded a garrison of puppet troops to defect. On unity, the author stresses that students came from different provinces, ethnic groups and parties, including Kuomintang members, and that the school did not require belief in communism. After the Southern Anhui Incident (1941) and the 1943 troop concentration against the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, Kangda staff and students are said to have denounced the Kuomintang and prepared defences. On combat, Gao cites the anti-"mopping-up" campaign, the Hundred Regiments Offensive and other engagements.

Gao concludes that Kangda put the Party's united front line into practice, took it deep among the people, and contributed to national independence and popular liberation. The author quotes Mao Zedong's view that Kangda was the most revolutionary and progressive military school. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese scholarship presents Kangda's wartime role in united front work.
quoteEn: On the whole, Kangda actively put into practice the Party's call for an anti-Japanese national united front, drove the Front deep and wide among the people, played an important role in achieving national independence and popular liberation, and was a "revolutionary furnace" in the history of modern Chinese education.
quoteZh: 总的说来，抗大积极践行党的抗日民族统一战线主张，推动抗日民族统一战线广泛深入人民群众，为实现民族独立和人民解放发挥了重要作用，是中国近代教育史上的“革命熔炉”。

glossary.explanation: The broad political alliance, centred on Kuomintang–Communist cooperation, that the Communist Party promoted from the mid-1930s to resist Japanese invasion.
Short name for the Counter-Japanese Military and Political University, the Communist-led military and political academy founded in 1936 and based mainly in Yan'an and the base areas.
The January 1941 clash in which Kuomintang forces attacked the New Fourth Army, a major strain on the united front.

t: The Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression opened the main Eastern theatre of the World Anti-Fascist War
zh: 中国人民抗日战争开辟世界反法西斯战争东方主战场
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News (Zhongguo Jijian Jiancha Bao), 28 August 2025, p. 8
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), the authors take up Xi Jinping's formulation that the Chinese people's resistance to Japan opened the main Eastern theatre of the anti-fascist war. They argue that China began fighting earliest, fought longest, tied down the main body of Japan's forces and played a decisive part in Japan's final defeat.

The article is a commentary in a Party newspaper, organised in three parts. The first sets out the chronology and the sacrifices China suffered. The second examines how the Chinese theatre constrained Japan and supported the Allies in Europe and the Pacific. The third deals with the Communist Party's role and the distinctive character of the Chinese front. It draws on statements by Xi, Mao Zedong, Zhu De, Roosevelt, Stalin, Churchill and Japanese sources.

The authors define the anti-fascist war by its nature, so any war against fascist aggression counts. On this basis, they say, the war began with the Mukden Incident of 1931, 14 years of fighting, against under six years for other Allies. They argue Japanese plans for 'northward' or 'southward' expansion both required control of China. They say China's resistance pinned down most of Japan's army and so prevented an attack on the Soviet Union and a Japanese–German link-up in the Middle East. It also bought the Allies time and supported their 'Europe first' strategy. They credit the Communist Party as the 'mainstay' of national resistance: it led the united front, opened the rear-area fronts behind enemy lines and rejected capitulation. They cite figures of over 35 million Chinese military and civilian casualties and over 1.5 million Japanese troops killed.

The authors warn that judging China's front by Western-theatre standards, such as the absence of decisive set-piece battles, is shallow. They say the Sino-Japanese war was a protracted war of attrition between a weak country and a strong one. They conclude that the victory raised China's international standing and helped build the postwar order centred on the United Nations. They call for a 'correct view of the history of the Second World War' and opposition to distortions of it and to hegemonism. Read the original if you want to see how Party historians present China's role in the anti-fascist war in the 80th-anniversary commemoration.
quoteEn: To belittle the role of China's anti-Japanese theatre because it lacked major battles like those of the Western theatre is undoubtedly shallow.
quoteZh: 如果以中国战场没有西方战场那样的重大战役来贬低中国抗日战场的作用，无疑是浅薄的。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm in a crisis. Party historiography uses it to describe the Communist Party's role in the War of Resistance.
The alliance of the Communist Party and the Kuomintang, and of other parties and social groups, against Japan. It formally took shape in September 1937 as the second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation.

The guerrilla fronts and base areas that Communist-led forces built behind Japanese lines in North, Central and South China. Chinese historiography contrasts them with the Kuomintang-led 'frontal' battlefield.

glossary.en: correct view of the history of the Second World War
glossary.explanation: Official Chinese phrase for an account of the war that stresses China's contribution and rejects revisionism. It is often paired with defending the postwar international order.

t: Commemorating victory is to win forever
zh: 纪念胜利是为了永远胜利
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, 28 August 2025, p. 3
paras: Written for the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), this newspaper commentary asks what the commemoration is for. Xiang's answer is that remembering the victory serves to draw confidence and strength for the future and to secure the great victory of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

The piece is short and moves from the war to present-day tasks. It recalls the 14 years of resistance and its results, then takes up three themes in turn: the role of the Communist Party, the spirit of the resistance, and the war's international significance and its lessons for peace and national strength. It closes with a 1945 editorial from Liberation Daily.

Xiang argues that the Party was the "mainstay" of the victory, because it raised the banner of the anti-Japanese national united front and its members stood on the front line. From this the author concludes that the Party's overall leadership must be upheld and strengthened today, including the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. The author also credits the war with producing a great spirit of resistance, made up of patriotism, national integrity, heroism and conviction of victory, which people are urged to carry into the present. Citing China's role as the main Eastern theatre of the anti-fascist war, Xiang draws four lessons: uphold Party leadership, remember that backwardness invites attack, strengthen national defence awareness, and keep to peaceful development.

Xiang concludes that the Chinese people will defend and extend the hard-won fruits of victory and advance the building of a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party media link the memory of the War of Resistance to Party leadership and current political goals.
quoteEn: We enter history in order to move towards the future; we commemorate victory in order to win forever.
quoteZh: 走进历史是为了走向未来，纪念胜利是为了永远胜利。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), affirming Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the Party's centralised, unified leadership.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, prominent in official discourse since the 2010s.

t: Upholding and promoting the correct view of the history of the Second World War
zh: 坚持和弘扬正确二战史观
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, Yu Pei argues that the results of the Second World War cannot be challenged. The commentary holds that upholding a "correct view of the history of the Second World War" is an urgent task at a time of rapid global change, and that it protects historical justice.
Yu sets out four components of this view, then explains why it counts as correct and what defending it requires. The piece is a short commentary that ends with a call for international cooperation.

The four components are as follows. The war was a deliberate war of aggression launched by Germany, Italy and Japan, and appeasement by Britain and France hastened its arrival. Victory resulted from the joint struggle of an anti-fascist alliance of states with different social systems. China and the Soviet Union, as the main Asian and European theatres, made decisive contributions, and Yu credits the Communist Party of China with leading national resistance. Documents such as the Cairo Declaration and the Potsdam Proclamation, the founding of the United Nations, and the Nuremberg and Tokyo tribunals shaped the postwar order. Yu calls the view "correct" because it respects historical facts, laws and dialectics and reflects the interests of the great majority. The author describes historical revisionism, historical nihilism, neo-Nazism and militarist revival as betrayals of historical justice.

Yu concludes that defending the historical truth means guarding the bottom line of human civilization. Citing Xi Jinping, Yu says humanity stands at a crossroads between confrontation and dialogue. The author calls on peoples to draw on this view, to uphold a fair multipolar order and to help build a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary framed Second World War memory in the 80th anniversary year.
quoteEn: The correct view of Second World War history is a precious part of humanity's historical memory and a real guarantee that human civilization will be guided toward a bright future.
quoteZh: 正确二战史观是人类历史记忆的宝贵内容，是指引人类文明走向光明未来的切实保证。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2013. It calls for cooperation and shared interests among states.
In Chinese Party discourse, a label for views that deny or distort established official historical narratives, especially of the revolution and Party history.

t: Passing on and carrying forward the great spirit of the War of Resistance in the new era
zh: 在新时代传承和弘扬伟大抗战精神
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression (2025), and prompted by the film Dead To Rights (Nanjing zhaoxiangguan), this newspaper commentary asks how the great spirit of the War of Resistance should be passed on today. Xiao argues that this spirit remains an inexhaustible source of strength for the new era and must be handed down from generation to generation.

The article first explains what is "great" about the spirit: its sacrifice and character, its cultural content, its historical thinking and the leadership of the Communist Party. It then turns to practical measures, grouped under two headings: basic infrastructure for transmission and institutional safeguards.

Xiao contends that the spirit combines traditional and revolutionary culture and so supports cultural confidence. It also holds historical lessons, such as that those who love war perish and those who forget war are endangered, which the author says help the country reach modernization. Xiao stresses the Party's role in uniting a fragmented society, building the anti-Japanese national united front and the "three-thirds" system of government, and coordinating fronts and forms of warfare. The practical proposals include using biotechnology and artificial intelligence to protect and reconstruct sites, building digital archives of letters and oral history, and bringing the spirit into textbooks and classrooms. They also include regulating film and literature so that history is neither deified, belittled nor stigmatised, and strengthening legal protection for martyrs and sites.

Xiao concludes that, as China enters a critical period for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the Party's leading role and the spirit of resistance must be carried forward so that the country can pass the tests of the new era. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school scholarship in 2025 links wartime memory to cultural confidence, Party leadership and heritage and education policy.
quoteEn: The inevitable victory in the War of Resistance was, in essence, a victory of justice and a victory of unity.
quoteZh: 抗战必胜，本质上是正义的胜利、团结的胜利。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse since the 2010s, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.
The wartime alliance policy under which the Communist Party cooperated with the Nationalists and other forces against Japan, as presented in Party history.
A model used in the Communist-led base areas in which Communists, left-progressives and middle forces each held roughly one third of government seats.
A term in Party discourse for confidence in China's traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture, promoted prominently since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Research on the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression must uphold a correct view of history
zh: 深入开展中国人民抗日战争研究必须坚持正确历史观
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), this commentary from the People's Daily argues that deeper research on the war must rest on a correct view of history. Xu Zhimin takes up Xi Jinping's call to "let history speak" and contends that distortions of the war's history are still current both abroad and at home.

Xu first sets out what a correct view of history means: historical materialism, a Party-led and people-centred reading, and a perspective that places the war in world history. The piece then identifies three targets of rebuttal: historical nihilism inside China, the views of Japanese right-wing figures and some politicians, and what Xu calls the political and academic bias of Western scholars. It closes with the practical tasks of future research.

Xu argues that the Chinese Communist Party led the resistance as its "mainstay". As evidence against Nationalist-era rumours, Xu cites the 1932 Declaration of War on Japan and the 1933 offer of a joint-fighting agreement. Xu also states that Communist-led forces fought 58–75 per cent of Japanese troops in China during the stalemate stage and cites the Hundred Regiments Offensive. Xu criticises Japanese denial of the Nanjing Massacre and glorification of aggression, and Western accounts that treat the Chinese theatre as subordinate. Xu adds that more Western scholars are now revising these views in light of Chinese-supplied sources.

Xu concludes that research remains insufficient relative to the war's significance. Xu calls for fuller overall and thematic studies, stronger collection of archives at home and abroad with critical scrutiny of selectively opened foreign records, and unified study of the 14-year war from 1931. Xu also calls for continued international exchange, citing joint Chinese–Japanese–Korean histories and the Sino-Japanese Joint History Research. Read the original if you want an official-line statement of how Chinese historians are directed to frame the war, historical nihilism and international scholarship.
quoteEn: Whether a view of history is correct concerns not only the authenticity of sources, the accuracy of facts, and the soundness of historical understanding and the advance or retreat of historiography, but also the allegiance of the people, the rise and fall of the nation, and the survival of the state.
quoteZh: 历史观的正确与否，不仅事关史料真假、史实对错、史识正误、史学进退，而且关乎民心向背、民族盛衰、国家存亡。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Party discourse for views seen as denying or belittling the Party's historical record and the revolutionary tradition. It is mainly invoked against reassessments of Party history.

The Marxist theory that social being determines consciousness and that productive forces and relations of production drive history. Chinese official writing treats it as the only scientific view of history.

t: Lessons from Chen Yun's methods of investigation and research
zh: 陈云同志的调查研究方法给予我们的启示
paras: Zhu Jiamu asks what present-day officials can learn from the way Chen Yun, a leading economic policymaker of the first and second generations of Party leadership, carried out investigation and research (diaocha yanjiu). Opening with Xi Jinping's call to study Chen's scientific ways of thinking and working, Zhu argues that Chen made investigation the precondition of decision-making. In Zhu's account, this was a direct application of seeking truth from facts, and Mao Zedong himself said at the 1962 Seven Thousand Cadres Conference that Chen's method was investigation and research.

The commentary is organised around four requirements: coming to the facts without preconceptions, being thorough and detailed, listening to dissenting views, and having the right purpose. Each is illustrated with episodes from Chen's career: his Yan'an-era formula, the 1961 fieldwork in Qingpu, the 1959 coal-industry symposium, the 1949 Shanghai prices mission, the 1953 grain purchase and supply policy, and the food-supply measures of the early 1960s. Zhu supports each point with passages from Xi Jinping's speeches and notes the March 2023 Central Committee General Office plan to promote investigation across the Party.

Zhu's central claim is that reliable research begins with the principle 'not bowing to superiors, not bowing to books, only to reality', which Chen distinguished from disobedience: policies must be carried out, but adapted to local conditions. Zhu stresses Chen's thoroughness, citing his fifteen days living with farmers in Qingpu, his detailed calculations showing double-cropping rice to be less profitable than single-cropping, and Mao's praise for 'speaking with figures'. Zhu also describes Chen's deliberate search for opposing views and unwelcome truths, and his use of trusted friends and aides as a second channel of information. The purpose of all this, Zhu says, was to solve problems affecting people's livelihood, which Chen treated as a political matter.

Zhu concludes that investigation remains a Party 'family heirloom' to be used more fully. He points to what he calls a world undergoing changes unseen in a century and to deep-seated contradictions in reform and development. Deeper research, he argues, will help officials grasp actual conditions and objective laws and carry socialism with Chinese characteristics forward in the new era. Read the original if you want a Party-history-based account of how Chen Yun's working methods are being held up as a model for the current campaign to revive investigation and research.
quoteEn: For investigation and research to grasp the true situation, the precondition must be coming to it without preconceptions.
quoteZh: 调查研究要做到掌握真实情况，前提必须是不带框框。

glossary.explanation: A Party working method of fieldwork and inquiry before making policy, strongly associated with Mao Zedong and revived as a campaign under Xi Jinping, including the 2023 Party-wide plan.
A core principle of Chinese Marxism that policy should proceed from actual conditions rather than dogma or directives, promoted by Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping.

glossary.pinyin: bù wéi shàng, bù wéi shū, zhǐ wéi shí
glossary.en: not bowing to superiors, not bowing to books, only to reality
glossary.literal: not only-superiors, not only-books, only reality
glossary.explanation: Nine characters from Chen Yun's 'fifteen-character formula' on avoiding errors; they urge basing decisions on reality instead of simply following superiors or texts.
The enlarged Central Committee work conference of early 1962 that reviewed the failures of the Great Leap Forward.

t: The Anti-Japanese National United Front as the basic guarantee of victory in the War of Resistance
zh: 抗日民族统一战线是抗战胜利的基本保证
authors: Theoretical Study Group of the Party Leadership Group, Central Institute of Socialism
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), and the 90th anniversary of the August 1st Declaration and the Wayaobao meeting, this commentary asks why the Anti-Japanese National United Front deserves to be called the basic guarantee of victory. The authors, a Party theory study group at the Central Institute of Socialism, answer that the Front, led by the Communist Party of China, turned a divided China into a united force against aggression. The piece was published in Qiushi, 2025 no. 16.

The text is organised in three parts: the Front as the political foundation of victory, as its foundation of strength, and as the creator of a favourable external environment. It draws on the 1935 declaration and the Wayaobao Politburo meeting, the shift from opposing Chiang Kai-shek to pressing and then allying with him, the Xi'an Incident, the Southern Anhui Incident of 1941, and the building of an international anti-fascist front. It closes with lessons for today, citing Xi Jinping's statements on the united front.

The authors argue that the Party first proposed and promoted the broadest united front, contrasting this with what they describe as the Kuomintang government's retreat and passivity. Within the Front, they say, the Party held the leadership through independence and unity in resistance and the formula of developing progressive forces, winning over the middle forces and isolating the diehards. They credit the Front with coordinating the Kuomintang's frontal battlefield and the Communist-led battlefield behind enemy lines, mobilising the national bourgeoisie, enlightened gentry, ethnic minorities, religious figures and overseas Chinese, and turning the war into a people's war. Externally, they present the Party as pushing for an international anti-fascist front, culminating in the Declaration by United Nations (1942), and as drawing support from foreign doctors, journalists and fighters.

The authors sum up the history as 'without the Communist Party, no Front; without the Front, no victory'. They draw four lessons: uphold Party leadership, the theme of great unity, the correct handling of unity and diversity, and sound tactics. They call for further developing the patriotic united front of the new era to gather the strength of Chinese at home and abroad for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an example of how the Party's official narrative links the wartime united front to present-day united front work.
quoteEn: Without the Communist Party of China, there would have been no Anti-Japanese National United Front; without the Front, there would have been no victory in the War of Resistance.
quoteZh: 没有中国共产党，就没有抗日民族统一战线；没有抗日民族统一战线，就没有抗战的胜利。

glossary.explanation: The broad coalition of parties, classes and groups against Japanese invasion, whose strategy the Communist Party adopted at the Wayaobao meeting in December 1935. It centred on cooperation between the Communists and the Kuomintang.
A Party strategy of building alliances with non-Party groups and forces to pursue its goals. The Party continues to describe it as a key instrument ('magic weapon') of its work.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse since Xi Jinping took office, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing.
A 1935 appeal drafted by the Chinese Communist delegation to the Comintern, calling for an end to civil war and united resistance to Japan.

t: Shaping China's international image during the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 抗战时期中国国际形象的塑造
paras: Wang and Zhou ask how China presented itself in international opinion during the War of Resistance against Japan (1937–45) and what that did for its standing. Opening with Xi Jinping's statement that victory restored China's great-power status and earned it respect and a high national reputation, they argue that China's active voice abroad helped win international sympathy, support and aid. The piece appeared in the China Social Sciences Today on 18 August 2025.

The article sets out three channels of image-building. These are presenting the true picture and will of the resistance, using Chinese culture as a vehicle of influence, and using foreign media as a window for China's voice. Each is illustrated with examples of statements, exhibitions and press reports from the 1930s and 1940s.

The authors cite Churchill, de Gaulle, the American officer Evans Carlson, the Japanese historian Inoue Kiyoshi and Anna Louise Strong as outside witnesses to the justice of China's cause and the discipline of the Communist-led forces. They describe cultural diplomacy: the 1935–36 London international exhibition of Chinese art, a 1940–41 exhibition in the Soviet Union, Mei Lanfang's performances and Gao Jianfu's anti-Japanese paintings in Macao and Hong Kong. On media, they point to coverage in The New York Times, The Times and Time, to Edgar Snow's Red Star Over China, and to the 1944 US Army Observation Group's report on Yan'an. The authors stress that American press attitudes shifted from "neutrality" early in the war to closer attention to the shared interests of anti-fascist states, which they say affected the US government and public.

The authors conclude that the wartime experience of building a national image offers lessons for today. They propose that China should innovate its narrative mode in international communication in the new era and build an effective, powerful system for international opinion. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese academic commentary uses wartime history to frame present-day international communication.
quoteEn: The experience of building a national image in the international opinion arena during the War of Resistance offers important inspiration for innovating China's narrative mode in international communication in the new era and building an efficient and powerful system of international opinion communication.
quoteZh: 抗日战争时期，中国在国际舆论场中关于构建国家形象的经验，对于我国在新时代创新国际传播的中国叙事模式，构建高效有力的国际舆论传播体系具有重要启发意义。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese name for the war against Japanese invasion, dated in official Chinese history from 1931 or 1937 to 1945.

t: The Marco Polo Bridge Incident as the starting point of the Chinese nation's all-out resistance to Japanese aggression
zh: 七七事变是中华民族全面抗击日本侵略者的起点
paras: Published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in August 2025, this short commemorative commentary asks what the Incident of 7 July 1937 (the Marco Polo Bridge Incident) meant for China's War of Resistance. Zhao argues that it marked the start of the whole nation's resistance to Japan, and opens with Xi Jinping's warning against denying or distorting the history of aggression.

The piece is organised under three headings: the Incident's role in bringing about the anti-Japanese national united front, in awakening the whole nation, and in raising the national spirit. It draws on Communist Party declarations of 1937, the reorganisation of the Red Army, a statement by Zhu De, and examples of wartime heroes.

Zhao describes the Party calling for unity at once and the 15 July 1937 declaration on Guomindang–Communist cooperation. According to the author, the Red Army was renamed the Eighth Route Army and southern guerrillas became the New Fourth Army. In Zhao's account the Incident made the national contradiction between China and Japan the principal one, and Japanese bombing, the 'three alls' policy, the Nanjing atrocities and biological and chemical warfare tied each person's fate to the nation's. The Party, Zhao says, upheld the united front, opposed capitulation, put forward a line of all-out national resistance and a protracted-war strategy, and acted as the mainstay of victory.

Zhao concludes that patriotism-centred national spirit was the decisive factor in victory and remains a spiritual driving force for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The author calls for deeper and broader academic research to refute Japanese denial of the history of aggression, and for remembering the martyrs. Read the original if you want a brief example of how the Incident is presented in current Chinese commemorative writing.
quoteEn: The 7 July Incident showed that the national contradiction between China and Japan had risen to become the principal contradiction, that the Chinese nation had no other choice, and that all-out national resistance was the only way to survive.
quoteZh: 七七事变表明，中日之间的民族矛盾已经上升为主要矛盾，中华民族已别无选择，全民族抗战才是唯一的生路。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central slogan of Party leadership, especially under Xi Jinping, referring to restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.
The broad alliance of parties, classes and groups, centred on Guomindang–Communist cooperation, formed against Japan from 1937.
The clash between Chinese and Japanese troops near Beijing on 7 July 1937, which Chinese historiography treats as the start of full-scale war.

t: The important role of "journalistic resistance" in the early War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 抗战初期“新闻抗战”发挥重要作用
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in August 2025, asks what part the press played in the early years of the War of Resistance against Japan. Zhang argues that Chinese journalists took up the pen as a weapon of resistance and built a "spiritual national defence front". In Zhang's account, "journalistic resistance" (xinwen kangzhan) and the related idea of "saving the nation through journalism" made a distinctive and irreplaceable contribution to the war effort.

The article covers roughly 1936 to 1938, from the years before full-scale war to its first phase. It is organised in three parts: how the press community assembled in response to the national crisis; how a united front was built among journalists after full-scale war began; and the activities of the Chinese Youth Journalists' Association (known as "Qingji"), founded in Wuhan in 1938.

Zhang's first move is to show journalists organising before the war: the Pingjin Journalism Society (January 1936), Yenching University's fifth and sixth journalism seminars, and a joint declaration issued on 2 October 1936 by more than twenty Shanghai and Nanjing newspapers. According to the article, news organisations in many other cities endorsed the declaration within about ten days. The second move is the wartime united front. Zhang cites 15 works on wartime journalism published in 1937–1938 and describes Wuhan as a national propaganda centre once major papers had relocated there. Qingji, with branches including Yan'an and Hong Kong, is presented as a journalists' united front operating under the anti-Japanese national united front. Zhang then lists Qingji's work: front-line reporting teams, welcome and send-off gatherings for war correspondents, and "reporters' forums" where Fan Changjiang urged that "national interest is above everything". It also published the journal Journalist, with special issues on war-time news policy and front-line newspapers.

Zhang concludes that journalists did more than report the news. In the national crisis they took on the mission of saving the nation through journalism, and in doing so they helped steady public belief in eventual victory. The article treats the press as a distinct front in the war and ends by calling its contribution indelible. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned overview of how Chinese journalists organised themselves in 1936–1938 and how the Chinese Youth Journalists' Association is remembered in current Chinese historiography.
quoteEn: Journalists not only kept to their duty of news reporting but, at the critical moment of national crisis, took the initiative to shoulder the historic mission of "saving the nation through journalism".
quoteZh: 新闻记者不仅恪守着新闻报道的职责，而且在国难危机的重要关头主动肩负起了“新闻救国”的时代使命

glossary.explanation: A 1930s idea that the press could contribute directly to national survival in the face of Japanese aggression. It echoes wider slogans of "national salvation" (jiuwang) in that period.
The idea that reporting and propaganda were themselves a form of resistance to Japan, alongside military struggle.
The broad alliance of parties and social groups, including the Communist Party and the Nationalists, formed against Japanese invasion in the later 1930s.

glossary.zh: 中国青年新闻记者学会
glossary.explanation: A journalists' organisation founded in Wuhan on 30 March 1938, abbreviated "Qingji". It brought together young reporters and published the journal Journalist.

t: The evolving logic of Party building leading the modernization of primary-level governance in the new era
zh: 新时代党建引领基层治理现代化的逻辑演进
source: Journal of South-Central Minzu University (Humanities and Social Sciences), 2025 no. 4
paras: Sun Shaoyong and Xiao Jianxun ask how "Party building leading the modernization of primary-level governance" should be understood as a political concept that has developed over time. The concept entered central documents in 2021 and was repeated at the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). The authors argue that existing studies are mostly static and that a dynamic account is needed. They conclude that the concept is a distinctively Chinese governance paradigm and grounded in the Party's self-reform.

The article first reviews three strands of earlier scholarship: a "generative" account, an "advantage" account that stresses the Party's ability to overcome bureaucratic dilemmas, and a "model" account built on local case studies. It then applies a three-part framework of logical foundation, logical mechanism and logical pathway. The foundation is traced through theory, history from the revolutionary base areas to reform-era village and residents' self-government, and the shift in discourse since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The mechanism and pathway are developed in the later sections.

Sun and Xiao treat the concept as a concrete form of "using the Party's self-reform to lead social revolution". They identify "Party suspension from grassroots society", meaning the Party's detachment in terms of actors, capacity, values and resources, as the starting problem. They also name three governance difficulties: structural imbalance, missing governance actors and weak capacity. They add that weaknesses in primary-level Party organizations are the main point of leverage. The shift from "Party leadership of primary-level governance" to "Party-building guidance" is described as a move from rigid leadership to a softer guiding role that gives more weight to local autonomy. Four practical pathways follow: political guidance (including "Party building plus" models such as building-based and business-district Party work), ideological education (including value consensus and moral governance), organizational construction (cross-organization platforms and mobilization mechanisms) and capacity building (political ability and service ability, including digital tools).

The authors conclude that primary-level governance is the foundation of national governance and that Party building plays a fundamental role in late-developing modernizing countries. They contend that Western society-centred, corporatist and state-centred approaches cannot resolve government, market and social failure at the grassroots. In their view, the Chinese approach also differs from Western bureaucratic models because the Party and the government are not separate. Read the original if you want a systematic, official-line account of how Chinese scholars justify and periodise Party-led grassroots governance, including its concepts and local practices.
quoteEn: The conceptual shift from "Party leadership of primary-level governance" to "Party building leading the modernization of primary-level governance" marks the Party's continuously deepening understanding of the laws of governing and of primary-level governance.
quoteZh: 从“党领导基层治理”到“党建引领基层治理现代化”的概念转换，标志着我们党对执政规律和基层治理规律的认识持续深化

glossary.zh: 党建引领基层治理现代化
glossary.en: Party building leading the modernization of primary-level governance
glossary.literal: Party building guiding grassroots governance modernization
glossary.explanation: A formula first put in a central document in 2021. It holds that strengthening Party organizations should guide and improve governance in villages, neighbourhoods and other grassroots units.
A term in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse for the Party's continuing efforts to purify, improve and renew itself. Official texts present it as the basis for its leadership of society.

t: The Chinese Communist Party's exploration of combining political work with economic work, and its significance
zh: 中国共产党坚持政治工作与经济工作相结合的探索历程及其意义
paras: Wang Yu and Liu Libo ask how the Chinese Communist Party has handled the relationship between political work and economic work, which they treat as the two most important practices of social governance. They argue that the Party has consistently combined the two in every period. In their account, this combination secured victory in the New Democratic Revolution and underlies the 'two miracles' of rapid economic growth and long-term social stability.

The article first defines the terms. 'Political work' here mainly means ideological and political work, which the authors place in the realm of the relations of production and the superstructure. It then traces the practice through the revolutionary years, the socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It closes with the theoretical significance of the practice. The authors draw on statements by Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping.

The authors' central claim is that political work stands in a relationship of service and guarantee to economic work, not one of leadership over it. It secures the socialist direction of economic work, supplies spiritual motivation and helps create a harmonious social environment. Economic work in turn gives political work its material basis. They illustrate this with the principle of material interests in political education, the Yan'an production campaign, and Deng's call to attend to both material and spiritual civilization. They also name costs when the balance failed: neglect of economic work in some socialist-era years, and weak ideological work in the 1980s. For the new era, they list five contributions to Chinese modernization: political direction, ideological consensus, internal motivation, all-round human development and social stability.

The authors present the practice as a creative development of historical materialism, building on Marx, Engels, Lenin and Mao. They say it offers lessons for socialist countries, which should avoid both over-politicization and a one-sided pursuit of economic interest. They conclude that proletarian parties can win popular support and strengthen confidence in socialism only by combining the two kinds of work under Party leadership. Read the original if you want a systematic Party-history account of how ideological work and economic work have been linked in official thinking, from Mao to Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: The Party's political work can put the cause of socialist construction on a path of healthy development only by being combined with economic work.
quoteZh: 党的政治工作只有与经济工作相结合，才能推进社会主义建设事业走上健康发展的轨道。

glossary.explanation: The Party's work of ideological education, organization, propaganda and mass mobilisation. The article treats it as the core of what is meant by 'political work'.

The official term for China's development path as formulated under Xi Jinping. It is presented as socialist modernization led by the Party, with material and spiritual civilization advancing together.
An official term for ethical, cultural and ideological progress. It is paired with 'material civilization' (economic development) in Party discourse since the 1980s.
Mao Zedong's term for the stage of the Chinese revolution led by the Communist Party before 1949. It is distinguished from the old bourgeois-led democratic revolution.

t: Deng Xiaoping's creative contribution to the world socialist movement
zh: 邓小平对世界社会主义运动的创造性贡献
paras: Sun Jinsong asks what Deng Xiaoping's concept of the 'Chinese model' (Zhongguo de moshi) contributed to the history of the world socialist movement. The article argues that Deng was the first to use the term explicitly and that, with the successful opening of socialism with Chinese characteristics, it marks a creative contribution to scientific socialism. In Sun's view, the Soviet model and the 'Chinese model' represent two stages of socialist practice: a founding period and a new period of deeper exploration.

The article has three parts. The first traces Deng's use of the term from 1980 to 1988, including his remarks to foreign leaders, and sets out six dimensions of its meaning: concept, content, lineage, time and space, frame of reference, and level of understanding. The second examines its intellectual sources in Mao Zedong Thought and in Party experience. The third places the concept within the world history of scientific socialism, including the Soviet model and the reform attempts in Eastern Europe.

Sun argues that Deng treated 'the Chinese model', 'taking our own road' and 'socialism with Chinese characteristics' as equivalent expressions. According to Sun, the concept rests on Mao's principles of seeking truth from facts and independence, and is defined against two reference points: the Western model, from which it differs in essence, and the Soviet model, from which it differs only within a shared Marxist framework. Sun describes scientific socialism as passing through three stages: the founding of the theory by Marx and Engels, the Soviet model after 1917, and the Chinese path opened at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). The Soviet model, in the article's account, supplied the first socialist standard and inspired anti-colonial struggles in Asia, Africa and Latin America, but became rigid and ended in collapse. Sun adds that the Eastern European reform paths failed, whereas China's path combined Marxist direction with selective use of capitalist instruments, such as a socialist market economy.

Sun concludes that the 'Chinese model' moved socialist practice from the general to the particular. It freed world socialism from the constraint of a single model and opened an era in which several paths coexist. The author quotes Xi Jinping's 2013 statement that the so-called 'China model' was created by the Chinese people themselves and is not a product to be exported. Read the original if you want a Chinese Party-school account of how Deng's 'Chinese model' is placed in the lineage of Mao Zedong Thought and the history of world socialism.
quoteEn: From the Soviet model to the 'Chinese model', the practice of scientific socialism worldwide has passed through a course of development from the general to the particular.
quoteZh: 从苏联模式到“中国的模式”，世界科学社会主义的实践经过了从一般到特殊的发展历程

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path since reform and opening up. Deng Xiaoping popularised it in the early 1980s, notably at the 12th Party Congress in 1982.

The phrase Deng Xiaoping used in talks with foreign leaders to say that China had its own path of development. The article distinguishes it from the Western use of 'China model' as a product to be exported.
A principle central to Mao Zedong Thought, later emphasised by Deng Xiaoping. It calls for starting from actual conditions rather than from doctrine or foreign templates.
The term for the socialist theory founded by Marx and Engels, as distinct from utopian socialism. Chinese scholarship also uses it for the world history of socialist theory and practice.

t: Economic construction in the anti-Japanese democratic base areas and its lessons
zh: 抗日民主根据地经济建设及经验启示
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how the Communist-led anti-Japanese democratic base areas, mostly behind enemy lines and short of resources, managed economic construction during the War of Resistance. Wu Minchao argues that this construction carried a double mission: supplying the armed forces for a protracted war and relieving the hardship of the local population. In Wu's account, only by balancing the two could the Party build the popular cohesion that underpinned victory.

The article is organised in three parts: the policy of fighting and producing at the same time; placing the people's interests first; and unity between army and people. Its main case is the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, with references to the Jin-Sui, Jin-Cha-Ji, Shandong and Central China bases, and to Anhui. It ends with general lessons for the present.

Wu traces the Great Production Movement to earlier preparation, from small-scale production by garrison troops, through Mao Zedong's 1939 call for people to rely on their own hands, to the 1940 Central Committee directive and the Nanniwan land reclamation by the 359th Brigade in 1941. The article cites Mao's claim that each soldier needed only three months of farming a year, and says the movement spread even to front-line and guerrilla areas. Wu then describes how the Party put the people first: land reclamation (97 万 mu, or 970,000 mu, against a plan of 390,000 in 1943), a dyke built by 210,000 labourers in central Anhui, and cooperatives. Wu presents Mao's instruction that officials spend ninety per cent of their effort helping peasants produce and ten per cent collecting taxes as an expression of the mass line. According to the article, this earned popular support, contrasted with corruption the author attributes to the Nationalists, and trained cadres for later economic work.

Wu concludes that three conditions made the base areas' economic work succeed: emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts, relying closely on the masses to develop the economy and improve livelihoods, and cadres sharing hardships with the people. These lessons are presented as relevant to building a strong country and achieving national rejuvenation today, through innovation, people's livelihood and unity, together with independence and self-reliance. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned account of how the Great Production Movement is now presented in Chinese public history and how it is tied to present-day policy themes.
quoteEn: Only by relying closely on the masses, and by doing everything to develop the economy and improve people's livelihood, can the base areas be consolidated and a firm foundation provided for protracted resistance.
quoteZh: 只有紧紧依靠群众，全力发展经济、改善民生，才能巩固根据地，为持久抗战提供稳固依托

glossary.explanation: A campaign launched in the Communist-led base areas, above all from 1941, in which troops, officials and civilians produced their own food and goods to offset blockade and fiscal strain.
The territories behind Japanese lines held by Communist-led forces during the War of Resistance (1937–45), where the Party built its own administration and economy.
The Party's method of leadership, in which it draws on the masses' views and experience and takes policies back to them. Mao Zedong formulated it in the 1940s.
Official shorthand for the goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, usually phrased as the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
