t: Getting organised as the source of strength behind victory in the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 组织起来是抗日战争胜利的力量之源
paras: Written for the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, this commentary asks how the Chinese nation organised itself, why it could, and what this means today. Wang Binglin argues that getting organised (组织起来) was the source of strength behind victory, because the awakening of the Chinese people and the nation's cohesion against foreign aggression proved decisive. The piece first appeared in Guangming Daily on 30 July 2025.

The article has three parts. The first describes how organisation was built in the political, military, economic and popular spheres. The second explains the Communist Party's role as advocate and defender of that organisation. The third draws lessons for the present. Wang's evidence includes the Three-Thirds system of government, the National Political Council, Pingxingguan, mine warfare, rent and interest reduction, and mass associations in the Jin-Cha-Ji border region and Shandong.

In Wang's account, Mao Zedong's diagnosis in On Protracted War was that Japan dared to bully China mainly because the Chinese people were unorganised. The anti-Japanese national united front joined all classes, parties, ethnic groups and overseas Chinese, and fighting was organised through two coordinated battlefields. Wang credits the Communist Party with the united front line, with maintaining independence within it, and with theory such as On Protracted War and New Democracy. Wang also credits Communists' self-sacrifice and the Party's use of traditional culture, such as the 1937 rites at the Yellow Emperor's Mausoleum and works like the Yellow River Cantata, as a spiritual bond.

Wang draws three lessons for the new journey. Upholding the Party's overall leadership is the fundamental guarantee of consensus, and Wang cites Xi Jinping on the Party's strength coming from organisation. Party members must act as vanguard models to bind the masses. Patriotism, as the core of the national spirit, should be promoted through the creative transformation of traditional culture. This is meant to gather strength for building a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-aligned scholarship reads the War of Resistance as a lesson in organisation and Party leadership, with the historical examples Wang selects.)
quoteEn: Getting organised was the source of strength behind the Chinese people's victory in the War of Resistance against Japan.
quoteZh: 组织起来是中国人民抗日战争胜利的力量之源。

glossary.explanation: The broad alliance of the Communist Party, the Kuomintang and other parties, groups and individuals against Japan, formed after 1937 and built on Kuomintang–Communist cooperation.
A power-sharing arrangement in the Communist-led base areas. Communists, non-Communist progressives and middle elements were each meant to hold about one third of government seats.
Mao Zedong's 1938 lectures setting out a strategy for a long war against Japan in three stages, relying on mobilising the people.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
The official term for China's path to modernisation, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models.

t: Starting from how the Yan'an style defeated the Xi'an style
zh: 从延安作风打败西安作风谈起
paras: Why did the Communist Party win power in China? Lin Jingwei takes up Xi Jinping's remark that the Party prevailed in the New Democratic Revolution partly by keeping flesh-and-blood ties with the people and so "defeating the Xi'an style with the Yan'an style". Writing in Qiushi in 2025, as the Party ran a study and education campaign on the Eight-point Regulation, Lin argues that conduct and work style decided who won popular support and, with it, the country.

The article first defines the Yan'an style and contrasts it with the Xi'an style, which stands for Kuomintang conduct. It then gives three reasons for the Yan'an style's success and ends by asking how it can be passed on. Lin relies on anecdotes and testimony: Mao Zedong's 1940 rebuke over an escort, Chen Jiageng's visits to Chongqing and Yan'an, the accounts of Edgar Snow, Theodore White and John Davis, and Zhu De's letter asking for a loan.

Lin reads the Yan'an style as the Party's moral and personal strength, set beside its strength of truth, which Lin identifies with correct theory. It rested on three things: faith in revolutionary ideals, close ties to the masses, and self-reliance with hard struggle. Lin sets Mao's "ten absences" against the Kuomintang's corruption, which the article illustrates with the phrases "five ways to success" and "tight at the front, feasting at the rear". In Lin's account, the shift of popular sentiment by late 1947 was a turning point, and it confirms that those who win the people's hearts win the country.

Lin warns that holding power tests a party's style, and cites Song Meiling's remark that the Communists had not yet tasted power. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Lin says, the Eight-point Regulation and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party have restored its vitality and are a key lesson of the Party's self-reform. Lin calls for the Yan'an style to be carried forward, with work-style building made routine and long-term, in support of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-affiliated historian uses Yan'an-era episodes to support current work-style campaigns.
quoteEn: Work style is tied to the hearts of the people and decides the life or death of a party and of a regime.
quoteZh: 作风连着民心，决定一个政党、一个政权的生死命运。

glossary.explanation: The conduct and ethos the Party developed in its wartime base at Yan'an (1935–48). It is usually described as frugality, equality between officials and people, and service to the masses.
Shorthand in Party rhetoric for Kuomintang-ruled areas, portrayed as corrupt and bureaucratic. Mao Zedong used the contrast in 1940.
Rules adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucratism among officials. They are the base of the Party's work-style campaigns.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official term, prominent since 2012, for tighter discipline, anti-corruption work and Party-building.
Official concept that the Party can correct itself through internal discipline and renewal, presented as the answer to the historical cycle of rise and decline.
The official name for the Party's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: The opening-up effects of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的开放效应
paras: Xu Xiujun takes up the place of openness in Chinese modernization and the effects that a more open China has on the world. Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that reform and opening up is the key move deciding the success or failure of Chinese modernization, Xu argues that Chinese modernization is open and inclusive by nature. In this account it develops through exchange and mutual learning among civilizations, and higher-level opening will bring more positive effects for world peace and prosperity.

The article is built in three parts. The first presents opening up as the distinctive mark of Chinese modernization, in three respects: a necessary condition, an important driving force, and a necessary response to economic globalization. The second sets out how Chinese modernization promotes common development worldwide. The third argues that it leads change in the global governance system and order.

On the first point, Xu traces how China drew on foreign capital, technology and management experience after reform and opening up to achieve rapid growth. Xu also holds that, amid rising unilateralism and protectionism and attempts to contain China, continued opening is needed to build new international competitive advantages and the new development pattern. On the second point, Xu cites figures: average annual growth of 8.9% in 1979–2023, a 24.8% average contribution to world growth, and nearly 800 million people lifted out of poverty. Xu adds China's huge market, its trade and investment position, and the Belt and Road Initiative and three global initiatives. The article says Chinese modernization breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization and offers developing countries another path. On the third, Xu says it promotes equal and orderly multipolarity, inclusive economic globalization that benefits all, and fairer global governance. Xu describes the present system as built mainly by Western powers after the Second World War and as failing to meet the demands of developing countries.

Xu concludes that Chinese modernization follows a path of peaceful development, rejecting war, colonialism and plunder. Xu says it advances a community with a shared future for mankind and leads towards more just and reasonable global governance. The text is a short policy-oriented essay in Party-theory language that relies on official statements and statistics. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese official scholarship links opening up, global development and global governance reform.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that "modernization equals Westernization", broadened the modernization paths of late-developing countries, offered a Chinese approach to developing countries seeking a path suited to their own conditions, and given humanity a new path option for achieving modernization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，拓展了后发国家现代化道路，为发展中国家探索适合本国国情的现代化道路提供了中国方案，为人类实现现代化提供了新的路径选择。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), for China's own path to a modern socialist country. It is characterised by features such as huge population size, common prosperity and peaceful development.
The policy course launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented reforms and opening the economy to foreign trade, capital and technology.
A Chinese initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013 to build infrastructure and economic cooperation links across Asia, Europe, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations, stressing shared interests and joint global governance.
An official strategy put forward in 2020 that treats the domestic market as the mainstay while linking domestic and international circulation.

t: Chen Yun's rich leadership experience in managing economic work
zh: 陈云负责经济工作的丰富领导经验
paras: Song Yuehong takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the symposium marking the 120th anniversary of Chen Yun's birth, to learn from Chen's rich leadership experience, especially in economic work. The article argues that Chen, a member of the first and second generations of the Party's central leadership, was one of the pioneers and founders of China's socialist economic construction. In Song's account, he put forward important views and measures and found creative ways to solve problems and open up new situations.

This short newspaper article is organised in three parts. The first deals with Chen's thinking on modernization and the Four Modernizations. The second covers industrialization, economic recovery after 1949, and the handling of food, livelihood and construction. The third examines his exploration of the socialist economic system, the market and the plan, and reform, and closes with his working method. Song draws throughout on Chen's collected works and selected works.

Song stresses that Chen insisted on a clear grasp of national conditions before modernizing, quoting his remark that for backward countries the issue is having something at all. He also stressed that modernization must be socialist, led by the Party, and pursue material and cultural-ethical progress together. Song presents Chen as always viewing economic law politically and from the standpoint of the whole country. Construction had to match national financial and material strength, with priorities and proper proportions among sectors, grain security and agriculture taking first place. At the Eighth Party Congress (1956) he described state and collective operation as the mainstay, with individual enterprise, free production within the plan and free markets as supplements. After reform and opening up he favoured comprehensive balance, macro-control that keeps the economy lively without disorder, and cautious, pilot-tested reform.

Song concludes that Chen's methods rested on seeking truth from facts, summed up in his fifteen-character formula "not by authority, not by books, only by reality; exchange, compare, repeat", and in his view that policy-makers should spend over ninety per cent of their time on investigation. Song holds that this experience still offers important lessons. Read the original if you want a brief, official-register overview of how Chen Yun's economic thought and working method are presented in Party-affiliated scholarship on the 2025 anniversary.
quoteEn: The distinctive feature of Comrade Chen Yun's handling of economic work was that he always viewed and grasped the laws of economic construction from a political standpoint.
quoteZh: 陈云同志负责经济工作的鲜明特点是始终站在政治上认识和把握经济建设规律

glossary.explanation: The goal of modernizing agriculture, industry, national defence, and science and technology, associated with Zhou Enlai and later Deng Xiaoping's post-1978 programme.
The policy of domestic economic reform and opening to the outside world launched at the end of 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
A principle of basing policy on actual conditions, associated with Mao Zedong and stressed by Deng Xiaoping; the Party treats it as the core of its ideological line.
The Eighth National Congress of the Communist Party of China, held in 1956, which assessed the completion of socialist transformation and the new tasks of construction.
A planning concept associated with Chen Yun, calling for overall balance among finance, credit, materials and other economic sectors.

t: "Servants of the people, not officials": the "Yan'an style" in the eyes of foreign visitors
zh: “只见公仆不见官”
zhSub: 外国人士眼中的“延安作风”
paras: This short commentary asks what foreign visitors to Yan'an saw of Chinese Communist Party leaders, and what that record means for Party conduct today. Sun argues that journalists, officers and diplomats who went there in the Yan'an period left accounts presenting leaders as "servants of the people, not officials". In Sun's view, this image helped build the Party's reputation and support, and it carries lessons for current efforts to uphold the central Party leadership's eight-point decision on conduct.

The article draws on testimony from Edgar Snow, Anna Louise Strong, Agnes Smedley, Theodore White, John S. Service, Harrison Forman and members of the 1944 US Army Observation Group, among others. It is organised under three headings: the leaders' simplicity, their contrast with the Nationalists and their service to the people, and democratic practice in the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region.

Sun's central move is to treat these outsider accounts as evidence of a new view of power. In their reports, as Sun reads them, power served the people rather than personal privilege: the visitors noted austere living, the absence of ranks, titles and bodyguards, and leaders who talked with peasants and worked in the fields. Sun also cites visitors who judged the border region's government to be elected by the people and not authoritarian, as Nationalist propaganda claimed. The article presents this as the concrete form of the "Yan'an style": hard struggle, close ties with the masses, integrity and opposition to privilege.

Sun concludes that these qualities remain a Party "family heirloom" and calls for them to be carried forward in the new era. Sun urges standing with the people, keeping close ties with them, and implementing the eight-point decision persistently so that work-style building becomes regular and long-term. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-aligned writing uses foreign eyewitness accounts of Yan'an to support current conduct campaigns.
quoteEn: The narrative image of "seeing servants of the people, not officials" is in essence a concrete expression of the Yan'an style.
quoteZh: “只见公仆不见官”的形象叙事，本质是延安作风的具象化表达

glossary.explanation: The ethos attributed to the Party during its wartime base in Yan'an (1937–1947): frugality, closeness to the masses, integrity and anti-privilege. Party writing invokes it as a model for present conduct.

A set of rules on official conduct adopted by the Politburo in December 2012 to curb formalism, bureaucracy, extravagance and official privilege. It has since become a staple of Party discipline campaigns.
The Communist-led base area in northwest China, with Yan'an as its centre, during the War of Resistance against Japan.
A Party term for efforts to improve officials' conduct and everyday working habits, usually through education campaigns and discipline rules.

t: The historical contribution of the victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression to building a strong country and national rejuvenation
zh: 抗日战争胜利对强国建设、民族复兴的历史贡献
paras: Writing in a Chinese newspaper in July 2025, ahead of the anniversary of the victory over Japan, Chen Jinlong asks what the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression contributed to building a strong country and to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Chen argues that the victory was the historical turning point from deep national crisis towards rejuvenation. In this reading, the war taught the importance of national strength, strengthened national cohesion, brought the Communist Party to maturity and raised China's international standing.

The commentary is organised in four parts. It treats in turn the development of productive forces, the unity of political parties, ethnic groups and the people, the Party's leadership, and China's international position after 1945. Chen supports each part mainly with statements by Mao Zedong and Zhu De, wartime editorials in Liberation Daily, and a statement by Xi Jinping on the war's global significance.

Chen's first claim is that Japan could attack China in the 1930s because its productive forces were far more developed, and that the Party concluded national strength ultimately rests on developing productive forces. Industrialisation, science and technology, and the use of intellectuals followed from this, and Chen cites Mao's wartime calls to recruit intellectuals in large numbers. Second, Chen holds that the Party's united front, its ethnic equality policies and its mobilisation of the people through democracy, production and popular culture built the forces on which later national strengthening would rely. Third, Chen argues that the war established the Party's leadership position, improved its capacity to govern and mobilise, produced a central leadership around Mao, and trained cadres through theoretical study and clear selection standards.

On the international side, Chen describes China as the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war, which tied down most of Japan's army and eased pressure on the Soviet Union, the United States and Britain. Chen adds that China took part in founding the United Nations and became a permanent member of the Security Council, which laid the basis for its standing as a major power. The article concludes that the victory should be viewed through a "grand historical outlook" as part of the long course of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 2025 official narrative links the wartime experience to present-day goals of strengthening the country and national rejuvenation.
quoteEn: The great victory of the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression was the historical turning point at which the Chinese nation moved from the deep crisis it had been in since modern times towards great rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 中国人民抗日战争的伟大胜利，是中华民族从近代以来陷入深重危机走向伟大复兴的历史转折点。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and prosperity after the "century of humiliation". It has been prominent in official discourse since the early 2010s.
A slogan in Party discourse for developing China into a powerful, modernised country. It is closely tied to the goal of national rejuvenation.
A phrase in Xi Jinping-era discourse that calls for judging events within long historical processes and wide global contexts.

t: The world-historical significance of China's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression
zh: 中国抗日战争的世界历史意义
paras: Hu Dekun, a historian at Wuhan University, asks what place China's War of Resistance against Japan holds in world history. In this commentary, published in Beijing Daily in July 2025, Hu argues that the war was both an integral part of the global anti-fascist war and a source of historic contributions to its victory.

The article is organised around four claims. China opened the earliest and longest-lasting Eastern main battlefield of the anti-fascist war; Chinese resistance supported the Soviet Union, the United States and Britain in their theatres; China helped to build the postwar international order; and the war laid the foundation for the founding of New China. Hu moves chronologically from the Mukden Incident of 1931 through the full-scale invasion of 1937 to the Allied alliance of 1942.

Hu dates the start of the Second World War in the East to 18 September 1931, and treats the period to 1937 as one of local resistance, with guerrilla warfare led by the Communist Party in the north-east. After 1937, Hu says, the Kuomintang-led frontal battlefield and the Communist-led battlefield behind enemy lines together tied down the bulk of Japan's army and part of its navy. In Hu's account this prevented Japan from attacking the Soviet Union, delayed and weakened its southward and westward advances, and relieved pressure on Allied forces in the Pacific, North Africa and Burma. Hu also credits China with early calls for an anti-fascist alliance, with a place among the 'Big Four' in the 1942 Declaration by United Nations, and with involvement in creating the United Nations, the World Bank and the IMF. Hu presents the war as a test that exposed Kuomintang autocracy and corruption while strengthening the Communist Party's prestige, which Hu says prepared its victory in the War of Liberation.

Hu concludes that at the turning point from world war to postwar peace and development, China wrote a 'glorious chapter' in world history. The piece reflects the official narrative that stresses the Communist Party's central role. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese historians present the Eastern main battlefield thesis and the war's link to the founding of New China.
quoteEn: During the eight years of the nation-wide war of resistance, China consistently fought the main body of Japan's army and part of its navy, and was truly the Eastern main battlefield of the world anti-fascist war.
quoteZh: 在长达八年的全民族抗战时期，中国始终抗击着日本陆军主力和海军部分兵力，是名副其实的世界反法西斯战争东方主战场。

glossary.explanation: A Chinese historiographical term for China's theatre in the Second World War, presented as the principal Asian front against fascism. It is common in official Chinese accounts of the war.
The theatre in Japanese-occupied areas where Communist-led forces such as the Eighth Route Army and New Fourth Army set up base areas and waged guerrilla war.
The conventional front where Kuomintang-commanded armies fought Japanese forces, as in the battles of Shanghai, Taierzhuang and Wuhan.

t: Evidence of Unit 731's atrocities and a rebuttal of Japanese denial of the invasion of China
st: An interview with Jin Shicheng of the Exhibition Hall of Evidence of Crimes Committed by Unit 731 of the Japanese Imperial Army
zh: 实证731部队残暴行径 驳斥日本否认侵华言论
zhSub: 访侵华日军第七三一部队罪证陈列馆馆员金士成
paras: This is an interview, conducted by a reporter for China Social Sciences Today (Zhao Xuzhou) with Jin Shicheng, a staff member of the Exhibition Hall of Evidence of Crimes Committed by Unit 731 of the Japanese Imperial Army. It was prompted by the Hall's first domestic release of the complete 83-minute video testimony of Kurumizawa Masakuni (胡桃泽正邦), a former Unit 731 member. The video was recorded in August 1991 in Iida, Japan, and the Hall obtained it in August 2024 from the Japanese researcher Hara Fumio.

The interview has three parts: what the testimony confirms about Unit 731's crimes, what value such materials have for scholarship and for rebutting denial of the invasion, and what the Hall has done and still plans to do in collecting evidence. Jin also explains why Kurumizawa's account was dropped from later editions of Morimura Seiichi's Akuma no hoshoku (The Devil's Gluttony).

Jin argues that the testimony shows bacteriological warfare to have been an organised, top-down state crime. As evidence, Jin cites Kurumizawa's route into the unit through the army medical school and the puppet Manchukuo's Dalu Academy of Sciences, and his claim to have dissected 300 people. Jin adds that it corroborates earlier research on test subjects called "maruta", on a special prison holding at least 40 people, and on the production of two tonnes of germs a day. In Jin's account the testimony is first-hand, detailed and from the perpetrator's side, and it also shows the unit's strict secrecy. Jin says the US exempted Unit 731 from prosecution in exchange for its experimental data, so most members stayed hidden, and that the testimony helps international opinion face the nature of Japanese militarism.

Jin outlines the Hall's work: protecting 27 sites, 23 of them national key cultural relics; recording over 400 hours of oral testimony in Japan; holding over 300,000 pages of archives; and carrying out 12 state and provincial projects, including ones funded by the National Social Science Fund of China. The Hall's stated aim is to have the site listed as World Heritage and its archives entered in the Memory of the World Register. Next steps include collecting materials held by former members' descendants and Japanese civic groups, linking research with public outreach through the Hall's role as a patriotic education demonstration base, and strengthening international communication. Read the original if you want a Chinese museum specialist's account of the Kurumizawa testimony and of how Chinese institutions plan to document and publicise Unit 731.
quoteEn: Unit 731 was kept secret during the war and, shielded by the United States after it, was never tried for war crimes, so its wartime crimes, its war responsibility and its postwar influence have to be uncovered bit by bit.
quoteZh: 731部队在战时处于保密状态，战后在美国掩盖下，没有受到战争审判，其战时犯罪、战争责任及战后影响需要一点点挖掘出来。

glossary.en: National Social Science Fund of China
glossary.explanation: The main state funding body for humanities and social science research in China. It supports projects including special programmes on the War of Resistance against Japan.
The term Unit 731 staff used for the prisoners subjected to experiments, treating them as materials rather than people.

glossary.zh: 爱国主义教育示范基地
glossary.explanation: An official designation for museums and memorial sites that are used for patriotic education programmes in China.

t: Modern Japan's road to the war of aggression against China
zh: 近代日本的侵华战争之路
paras: Published in the China Social Sciences Today on 9 July 2025, ahead of the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance, this short historical commentary traces how modern Japan's aggression against China unfolded. Zang opens with Xi Jinping's description of Japan's continuous aggression as the darkest page of modern Chinese history. Zang argues that the aggression lasted more than 70 years from the 1874 invasion of Taiwan, and was most intense in the half-century of the Sino-Japanese War of 1894–95 and the later war of aggression.

The article is a chronological survey in five stages: the twenty years before the 1894–95 war (1874–1893); the twenty years after it (1895–1914); the First World War and the years to 1930; and the period from partial to full-scale war (1931–1945). It follows Japanese actions towards Taiwan, the Ryukyu Islands, Korea, Shandong and north-east China, and closes with the Chinese resistance.

Zang's central claim is that the 1874 landing in Taiwan, Japan's first overseas military action, began a continuous line of aggression, even though the 1871 Sino-Japanese Treaty of Amity was an equal treaty. In this account, the annexation of Ryukyu, the 1890 "line of interest" doctrine centred on Korea, and the Treaty of Shimonoseki shaped a continental policy and reversed the relationship between the two countries. The Twenty-One Demands, the 1927 Tanaka-era policy of separating Manchuria and Mongolia, and the invasions of 1931 and 1937 are presented as stages of the same course.

Zang credits the Communist Party-led national united front and the rear-area resistance with a pivotal role, and describes China as the main Eastern theatre of the Second World War. The 14-year resistance is called the first complete victory against foreign aggression in modern times and a turning point towards national rejuvenation. Zang calls for renewed study of this history and its lessons. Read the original if you want a brief overview of the official Chinese periodisation of Japanese aggression, 1874–1945.
quoteEn: The barbaric aggression of Japanese militarism brought unprecedented and enormous disaster upon the Chinese people and provoked their tenacious resistance.
quoteZh: 日本军国主义的野蛮侵略给中国人民造成空前巨大的灾难，激起中国人民的顽强反抗。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese term for the war against Japan, which official Chinese history dates from 1931 (14 years) to 1945. It is described as the Eastern main theatre of the Second World War.
The wartime cooperation between the Communist Party and the Nationalist government against Japan, promoted by the Communist Party in the mid-1930s.
A central official theme: the recovery of China's strength and status after the modern period of weakness and foreign aggression.

t: The historical position of China's War of Resistance in the world anti-fascist war
zh: 中国抗战在世界反法西斯战争中的历史地位
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 7 July 2025
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary of July 2025, Wang Meiping asks what place China's War of Resistance against Japan holds in the Second World War. Wang argues that it was an important part of the world anti-fascist war and, after the Pacific War began, its main Eastern theatre. In Wang's account, Cold War structures led the international community to overlook this role for a long time.

The article follows three stages: the local resistance after the 18 September 1931 Incident, the full-scale resistance from 7 July 1937, and the period after Pearl Harbor in December 1941. For each stage Wang considers what China's fight cost Japan, how it constrained Japanese strategy, and how it affected the wider anti-fascist camp. Japanese official statistics on casualties and military spending are cited throughout.

Wang's central claim is that total war cannot be won by military superiority alone. It also requires exhausting an opponent's strategic resources and will to fight until it has "nothing to fight with" and "no one willing to fight". On this reading, China, though weak, used its vast territory, large population, mobilisation capacity and resistance spirit to wear Japan down. Wang says China opened the earliest anti-fascist front, was the only Eastern front until December 1941, and tied down over 80 per cent of Japan's army before the Pacific War and 50 to 60 per cent afterwards. Wang adds that this fighting also deterred a Japanese attack on the Soviet Union and prompted Britain and the United States to aid China.

Wang concludes that China's fourteen years of resistance, as the main Eastern theatre, made an indelible contribution to human morality and world peace, and to the postwar international order. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the current Chinese historiographical case for China's role in the Second World War, together with the Japanese statistics Wang uses.
quoteEn: The Chinese theatre, as the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war, made an indelible contribution to upholding human morality and world peace.
quoteZh: 中国战场作为世界反法西斯战争的东方主战场，为维护人类道义与世界和平作出了不可磨灭的贡献。

glossary.explanation: The Japanese Kwantung Army's staged attack at Shenyang in 1931, which began the occupation of Northeast China. Chinese historiography treats it as the start of the fourteen-year War of Resistance.
The phase of the war against Japan that began with the 7 July 1937 Marco Polo Bridge Incident, when Japan launched a full invasion of China.
The Chinese characterisation of China's battlefield as the principal Asian theatre of the world anti-fascist war, a status Chinese authors say was long underrecognised abroad.

t: The contribution of the Eastern main battlefield deserves fair assessment
zh: 东方主战场的贡献应获公正评价
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 7 July 2025
paras: This short commentary is a Chinese translation of a piece by Nadia Helmy, an Egyptian political scientist and Asia specialist. Writing in the 80th anniversary year of victory in 2025, Helmy argues that China's role as the main battlefield of the East in the Second World War has received too little international recognition and should be assessed fairly.

Helmy opens with a visit to the Museum of the War of Chinese People's Resistance against Japanese Aggression at the Marco Polo Bridge in Beijing. The text then summarises the course of the war: the 1931 Mukden Incident, the puppet state of Manchukuo, the full-scale war from 1937, the Nanjing Massacre and Unit 731, the Lytton Report, the Potsdam Declaration and Japan's surrender in 1945.

The author's central claim is that China's contribution and sacrifice, put by the article at over 35 million military and civilian casualties over fourteen years, were in some respects greater than those of the United States and Britain. Helmy contends that Western states used the war's outcomes for their own interests and overlooked China's part, and that Japanese textbooks play down or delete the history of the invasion. Chinese scholars, and China specialists worldwide, are therefore urged to restore China's real contribution and step outside what Helmy calls a US and Western ideological narrative. Helmy cites Xi Jinping's May 2025 call in Russia to uphold a correct view of the history of the Second World War.

Helmy concludes that scholars should remind the world of China's sacrifices, that Global South countries have reason to take China as a model, and that the war's spirit still inspires efforts toward the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation. The author calls on all countries to learn from history and to cooperate in building a peaceful, mutually beneficial world. Read the original if you want an example of how a foreign scholar's commentary on the anti-fascist war is presented in Chinese academic media.
quoteEn: Chinese scholars bear an important responsibility: to restore China's true contribution in the Second World War and to step outside the ideological narrative framework of the United States and the West.
quoteZh: 中国学者肩负着重要责任，即还原中国在二战中的真实贡献，跳出美西方的意识形态叙事框架。

glossary.explanation: A term for developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America, widely used in Chinese foreign-policy discourse to describe China's partners.
A slogan popularised by Xi Jinping from 2012, centred on the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: a correct view of the history of the Second World War
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping and official media to stress China's role in the war and to oppose what they describe as distortions of its history.

t: Placing China's War of Resistance memory within global war history
zh: 构建全球战争史中的中国抗战记忆
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 7 July 2025
paras: This short commentary is a Chinese translation of a piece by the British historian Rana Mitter. It asks why China's War of Resistance against Japan remains one of the least understood parts of the Second World War in the West, and how that can change. Mitter argues that Western scholarship has improved markedly over the past decade, but that the war is not yet fully part of Western understanding of global conflict.

Mitter first gives reasons for the neglect: the war has received too little attention in Western countries, and the sources are mainly in Chinese or Japanese, languages that are little studied in Europe and North America. He then surveys scholarly progress since the 1990s, naming Ezra Vogel, Stephen MacKinnon and Hans van de Ven, and mentions his own 2013 book Forgotten Ally: China's World War II 1937–1945.

A central trend Mitter identifies is placing the war in a global-history frame, stressing its position in the world order and comparing China's experience with that of other countries. He sees two openings for future work. One is access to Chinese archive-based research, such as that in the journal Studies of the War of Resistance against Japan, which non-Chinese readers still struggle to use. The other is the post-war period: Asian reconstruction is far less studied than European, and Mitter points to growing interest in international institutions, above all the United Nations, in which Roosevelt's 'Four Policemen' idea gave China a key role.

Mitter concludes that comparative social history is a promising direction. He holds that research should bring out both what is distinctive about China's wartime experience and what it shares with other regions, and that this experience should be known globally. Read the original if you want a brief, author-sketched map of Western scholarship on the Sino-Japanese War and the research gaps a leading historian sees.
quoteEn: Understanding China's wartime experience of resistance matters not only to Chinese scholarship; it should also be known across the world.
quoteZh: 理解中国的抗战经验不仅对中国学术界具有重要意义，也应为全球所共知。

glossary.explanation: The standard Chinese name for the war with Japan, dated in China from 1937 (or, in recent official usage, from 1931) to 1945. It is treated as China's part of the Second World War.

t: The global significance of the main Eastern theatre
zh: 东方主战场的全球意义
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 7 July 2025
paras: This short commentary is a Chinese translation of a piece by Alpha Mohamed Jalloh of Sierra Leone, written for the 80th anniversary of victory in the World Anti-Fascist War (2025). Jalloh argues that the Eastern theatre, centred on China, was a decisive front of the Second World War, even though historical attention has focused mainly on Europe.

The piece first describes the Chinese theatre as the longest-running and largest in Asia, beginning with the 18 September 1931 incident. It then assesses the theatre's global significance from two angles and closes with remarks on historical memory and present-day peace.

Jalloh states that Chinese forces and civilians fought almost alone against Japan until the Pacific War began in 1941. In the article's account, Japan committed over half its troops in China and used up resources meant for other Asia-Pacific areas, which bought the Allies time to deploy, re-equip and counterattack. The two angles are a long-term buffer against fascism in Asia, which forced Japan into a war of attrition, and a catalyst for Allied cooperation. On the second point, Jalloh says China's resistance laid the basis for the alliance with the United States, Britain and the Soviet Union and led to China's role as a founding UN member and permanent Security Council member.

Jalloh concludes that remembering this history supports peace, mutual respect and multilateral cooperation, and calls on the international community to respect historical truth. In the article's view, belittling the contributions of China and other non-Western countries erodes collective memory and global solidarity. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a scholar from Africa frames China's wartime role for a Chinese audience in the anniversary year.
quoteEn: Attempts to distort or belittle the contributions of China and other non-Western countries to victory in the Second World War erode collective memory and undermine global solidarity.
quoteZh: 试图歪曲或贬低中国及其他非西方国家对二战胜利作出的贡献就是侵蚀集体记忆，破坏全球团结。

t: Building a historical narrative of the Eastern main theatre cannot wait
zh: 建立东方主战场历史叙事刻不容缓
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary on the eve of the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance and the world anti-fascist war (2025), Zhang Sheng argues that China urgently needs its own historical narrative of the Eastern main theatre. Zhang holds that Western narratives have long made China's war effort nearly invisible, and that this shapes how the war is remembered.

The piece opens with the Orientalist tradition traced to Herodotus and then turns to the Indian–Burmese–western Yunnan campaigns after Pearl Harbor. It recounts the Chinese Expeditionary Force in Burma in 1942, British mistrust of Chinese troops, the death of Dai Anlan and the later counter-offensive of 1943–44. It then contrasts Churchill's memoirs with Japanese military postwar accounts.

Zhang's central move is to show that Churchill's six-volume memoirs, begun in 1948, play down China. Zhang cites his remark about the loss of two Chinese divisions and his brief treatment of the Marco Polo Bridge Incident, Zhanggufeng and Nomonhan. Because Roosevelt had died and Stalin left no memoirs, Zhang says, Churchill controlled the narrative, and China was made to 'disappear'. Against this, Zhang cites the Japanese Defence Agency's history, which treats the Pacific and Burma campaigns as an extension of the war on China and records the strength of Chinese forces. Zhang also cites Hans van de Ven's criticism of Western-centrism.

Zhang concludes, citing Xi Jinping's statements on the Eastern main theatre and China's decisive role, that building an autonomous narrative is now pressing. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese historians argue against Western accounts of the Second World War.
quoteEn: What Churchill so rashly asserted was indeed a 'fiction', aimed at belittling the role and standing of the Chinese people's War of Resistance and of the Eastern main theatre.
quoteZh: 丘吉尔所妄言的确实是一种“虚构”——旨在矮化中国人民抗日战争和东方主战场的作用和地位。

glossary.explanation: Official Chinese term for China's theatre in the world anti-fascist war, used to stress its early start, long duration and role in tying down Japanese forces.

glossary.literal: Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japan
glossary.explanation: China's official name for the war against Japanese invasion, dated by the Party from 1931 or, in the full-nation sense, from 1937.

t: China's War of Resistance and its global contribution
zh: 中国抗战的世界性贡献
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression (2025), this newspaper commentary asks what China's war contributed to the world anti-fascist struggle. Gao argues that China opened the main Eastern theatre, tied down Japan's army and so made a major contribution to Allied victory.

The piece first sets out the military case for China's role as the main Eastern battlefield, using casualty figures and troop-deployment statistics. It then turns to assessments from abroad, citing Roosevelt, Marshal Chuikov, Russian and British scholars and the British press in 2005.

Gao contends that some Western scholars, shaped by "Western-centrism", deny the Chinese theatre's significance. Against this, the author reports that China fought the longest and began the world's first anti-fascist front. By the author's figures, Japan kept up to 94 per cent of its army in China before the Pacific War and still about 70 per cent afterwards, with over 2.8 million Japanese troops committed in China. Gao credits the protracted war led by the Communist Party with wrecking Japan's plans to strike north against the Soviet Union and south into Southeast Asia, and cites a 1943 Japanese North China Area Army report on Communist-led forces as enemy corroboration.

Gao concludes that China raised the banner of the world anti-fascist war first and gave strong support to the Allies. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Chinese narrative on the Eastern theatre and the foreign testimonies it marshals.
quoteEn: The Chinese people's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression opened the main Eastern battlefield and made a major contribution to victory in the world anti-fascist war.
quoteZh: 中国人民抗日战争开辟了东方主战场，为世界反法西斯战争的胜利作出了重大贡献。

t: China's War of Resistance holds an important place in the world anti-fascist war
zh: 中国抗战在世界反法西斯战争中具有重要地位
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of Japan's surrender in 1945, this newspaper commentary responds to claims that still circulate about the Second World War: a "Western-determinist" view, a "European main theatre" thesis, and the idea that the United States contributed most to victory. Zhu Chengshan argues that these views deliberately downplay the Eastern main theatre, and that China's War of Resistance against Japan held an indispensable strategic place in the world anti-fascist war.

The piece has three parts. It first presents China's resistance as the opening of the world anti-fascist war, beginning in north-east China in 1931. It then defines the Chinese theatre as the Eastern main theatre, and finally examines how China's war undermined the fascist powers' global strategy.

Zhu's central argument rests on duration, scale and strategic effect. He says China fought for 14 years, eight years before the European theatre and ten before the Pacific, with casualties of over 35 million. The article cites figures showing that the Chinese theatre tied down 54%–94% of Japan's army, including 32 of 34 divisions in 1938, and accounted for 70% of Japanese casualties. It argues that this pressure led Japan to abandon its northward advance against the Soviet Union, giving the USSR and the Allies strategic breathing space. Zhu supports this with statements from Mao Zedong, Stalin, Roosevelt, Marshal Chuikov and Japan's own official war history. He credits the Communist Party with a pivotal role through protracted and guerrilla warfare.

Zhu concludes that China's contribution gave the anti-fascist war "time, space and moral" support, and that it later allowed China to take part in global governance as a builder of world peace. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Chinese case for the Eastern main theatre, with the statistics and wartime testimonies it relies on.
quoteEn: The important role and strategic position of China's War of Resistance in the Second World War are beyond doubt, and the enormous national sacrifice and outstanding contribution of the Chinese nation on the Eastern main theatre cannot be erased.
quoteZh: 中国抗战在二战中的重要作用和战略地位毋庸置疑，中华民族在东方主战场上付出的巨大民族牺牲与作出的卓越贡献不容磨灭

glossary.explanation: The Chinese designation of the Asian theatre, centred on China's war against Japan, as one of the two principal theatres of the Second World War alongside the European one. It is used in official Chinese historiography to stress China's contribution.

t: The Communist Party's War of Resistance on the main Eastern battlefield, as seen in Japanese historical sources
zh: 日本史料所见东方主战场的中共抗战
source: China Social Sciences Net / Chinese Social Sciences Today, 7 July 2025
paras: Wu and Song ask what Japanese wartime documents reveal about the Chinese Communist Party's role in the War of Resistance against Japan. Their thesis is that these sources confirm the Party was the mainstay of China's resistance on the main Eastern battlefield of the world anti-fascist war. They also present the sources as an outside view that rebuts claims denying that battlefield's place and role.

This short newspaper commentary, published in July 2025, is organised in two parts. The first treats the Party as the core anti-Japanese force after the 1931 Mukden Incident and the 1937 Marco Polo Bridge Incident. The second treats敌后 (behind-the-lines) resistance and the Japanese forces it tied down. The authors draw on reports by the Toho Kokusaku Doshikai, Japanese army staff, the South Manchuria Railway Company and the Domei news agency.

The authors quote Japanese documents that, in their account, saw the Party's central aim as resistance and recognised its united front, political mobilisation and guerrilla warfare. A 1943 Domei survey, as cited, calls the linked North China base areas a 'red corridor' and a 'cancer' obstructing Japan's exploitation of the region. The authors read this as proof that Japan regarded the Party as its real opponent, and add that the 1940 Hundred Regiments Campaign tied down large forces and damaged transport lines.

Wu and Song conclude that the Party tied down and wore out large Japanese forces in North China and opened a rear battlefield through 19 base areas. They say these areas preserved resistance when the frontal battlefield suffered setbacks. They add that the Party gained military strength, political experience and mass support that proved decisive for postwar politics. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese scholars use Japanese sources to support the Party-centred account of the war.
quoteEn: The Chinese Communist Party played the role of mainstay on the main Eastern battlefield and was an indispensable component of the Chinese people's War of Resistance and the world anti-fascist war.
quoteZh: 中国共产党在东方主战场中发挥了中流砥柱的作用，是中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争中不可或缺的重要组成部分。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese designation of China's War of Resistance as the principal theatre of the world anti-fascist war in Asia. It stresses that China tied down most of Japan's army.
The Party's policy of cooperating with the Kuomintang and other forces against Japan, developed in the mid-1930s and formalised after 1937.
Territories behind Japanese lines, governed and defended by Communist-led forces, which served as bases for guerrilla warfare and mobilisation.
A large Eighth Route Army offensive in North China in 1940, aimed at Japanese rail lines and strongpoints.

t: China's theatre opens the main Eastern front of the world anti-fascist war
zh: 中国战场开辟世界反法西斯战争东方主战场
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 7 July 2025
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in 2025, this short commentary argues that the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression opened the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war. Zhang holds that it played a decisive part in defeating Japanese fascism and made a lasting contribution to the Allied victory.

The piece follows three themes. It first traces the war from the 18 September 1931 Incident through the 1937 Marco Polo Bridge Incident to Japan's surrender in 1945. It then considers how China's theatre tied down Japanese forces and supported other fronts. Finally it examines how the war affected China's international standing.

Zhang says the resistance began the world anti-fascist war and became the first large-scale anti-fascist front in the East. According to the article, 80 per cent of Japan's army divisions were in China between 1937 and 1941, and over a million Japanese troops remained there after the Pacific War began. It cites Chinese losses of 35 million military and civilian casualties. The author also points to the expeditionary force sent to Burma, to the air bases and strategic materials China supplied, and to the 1943 treaties ending British and American extraterritorial privileges. In Zhang's account, China's signing of the 1942 Declaration by United Nations and its seat as a permanent member of the Security Council confirmed its great-power status.

Zhang concludes that revisiting this history defends the outcomes of the anti-fascist war and international fairness and justice. The author adds that it also actively promotes a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a brief example of how the Chinese anniversary narrative presents China's role in the Second World War.
quoteEn: The Chinese theatre tied down and inflicted casualties on the most of Japan's main army force, annihilated the largest number of Japanese troops, lasted the longest and paid the highest price.
quoteZh: 中国战场牵制和毙伤日本陆军主力最多，歼灭日军人数最多，持续时间最长，付出代价最大。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the early 2010s. It calls for shared security, development and governance among nations.

t: Young people must remember the important role of China's War of Resistance in the world anti-fascist war
zh: 青年人要牢记中国抗战在世界反法西斯战争中的重要作用
source: China Social Sciences Net / Chinese Social Sciences Today, 7 July 2025
paras: This short commentary is a Chinese version of a piece by Olga Dubkova, a Russian associate professor in China. It asks how young people remember the Second World War and argues that they must keep a living memory of China's part in the world anti-fascist war. Dubkova presents the war as a shared human tragedy whose dead must not be reduced to statistics.

The author draws on family stories of the war and on annual classroom discussions with students. The main evidence is a written questionnaire given to third-year students at Xi'an International Studies University. It asked which countries played the most important role, which major events took place, and who the war heroes were.

According to Dubkova, 65% of respondents ranked China first, 28% the Soviet Union and 7% the United States. Students listed 46 battles and events, most of them in Europe, and few of those set on Chinese soil, which Dubkova calls a "memory gap". Of the 49 heroes named, from 12 countries, 18 were Chinese, 9 American and 7 Soviet. Dubkova reads this as a view of the war as a global catastrophe, but also as evidence of thin knowledge and little online material about wartime events and heroes in China.

Writing before the 80th anniversary commemorations of September 2025, Dubkova calls for preserving humanity's shared memory of the war. The author links this to common human values, the core values of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and intercultural ties among young people. Dubkova also urges using many kinds of resources to tell stories of the Chinese resistance and its heroes. Read the original if you want a small student survey on Chinese youth memory of the war, or a Russian scholar's view of Sino-Russian wartime remembrance.
quoteEn: Love for the past should become a basic emotion in our hearts; the tens of millions who died in the Second World War were individual people and should not be seen merely as statistics.
quoteZh: 对过往的热爱应该成为我们心中的一种基本情感,在二战中牺牲的几千万人是一个个具体的人,不能只将其看作统计数字。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism, in use since the 1980s. Party texts present it as Marxism adapted to China's conditions.

t: Strengthening research on the history of the War of Resistance is of great significance
zh: 加强抗战史研究意义重大
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 7 July 2025
paras: This short commentary is a Chinese-language text by the South Korean scholar Kim Jin-hwan, written for the 80th anniversary in 2025 of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War. Kim argues that the war was a major part of the global anti-fascist struggle and that deeper historical research on it is needed.
The piece first sets out what the victory meant, then recalls the sacrifices behind it, and finally turns to present-day problems of historical memory and to the need for archival research.

Kim describes the victory as having three meanings. For China, it was the first complete victory over foreign aggression in modern times and kindled hopes of independence; for Asia, it gave moral encouragement and reduced losses on other fronts; for the world, China joined the anti-fascist alliance with the United States, Britain and the Soviet Union. In Kim's account, by tying down the main Japanese forces in China, Chinese soldiers and civilians prevented the spread of the war to the Soviet Union and Southeast Asia and saved millions of lives, so that without their sacrifice there would have been no world victory.

Kim notes that the comfort women issue, the Nanjing Massacre and Unit 731 remain unresolved, and criticises Japanese right-wing forces and textbooks that play down war crimes, which Kim says threatens peace in East Asia. Kim calls for fuller use of archives, including Japanese-origin materials in Chinese archives that are still unpublished. Read the original if you want a brief view from a South Korean academic on how the anniversary is framed and why archival work is urged.
quoteEn: Without the enormous sacrifice of the Chinese people, there would have been no victory in the World Anti-Fascist War.
quoteZh: 如果没有中国人民的巨大牺牲，就没有世界反法西斯战争的胜利。

t: Carrying forward the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army and strengthening ideals and convictions
zh: 传承东北抗联精神 坚定理想信念
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how Party members and officials today can draw on the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army (Northeast Anti-Japanese Allied Army) to firm up their ideals and convictions. Zhong argues that the unit's fighters endured extreme hardship and torture because of an unshakeable loyalty to the Party. The piece takes its cue from Xi Jinping's remarks on revitalising the Northeast and on using red resources as teaching material.

The article is organised around three questions that Zhong treats as the logic of ideals and convictions: whether one believes, whether one acts, and for how long. Each is illustrated with episodes from the Northeast resistance, including the commanders Yang Jingyu and Zhou Baozhong, the political commissar Feng Zhongyun and the 'red capitalist' Zhu Shouyi. A short closing section links the three questions to present-day tasks.

On belief, Zhong says conviction begins with grasping the dialectic of ideal and reality: ideals arise from reality but must stand above it and lead change. Yang Jingyu's final days, when he predicted that others would carry on the cause, are offered as proof that lofty ideals are a spur and not an escape. On action, Zhong holds that fighters who gave up comfortable lives showed knowledge and practice united, and warns against empty talk. On endurance, Zhong recounts Zhou Baozhong's offer in 1939 to let starving soldiers leave, after which 120 stayed, and describes tests of power in peacetime as the same test of persistence.

Zhong concludes that promoting the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army spirit means first building belief, then strengthening practical commitment, and finally sustaining perseverance. Only by turning conviction into long-term struggle, the author says, can new prospects open for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want an example of how official Party-education writing uses regional revolutionary history to frame ideological discipline for cadres.
quoteEn: Lofty ideals are by no means an escape from real-world difficulties, but the spiritual driving force for breaking through historical limitations.
quoteZh: 崇高理想绝非对现实困境的逃避，而是突破历史局限性的精神原动力。

glossary.explanation: Anti-Japanese armed forces founded and led by the Chinese Communist Party in Northeast China in the 1930s–40s, made up of people of many ethnic groups. It fought Japanese occupation after the 1931 Mukden Incident.
A standard Party term for cadres' commitment to communism and socialism with Chinese characteristics, treated as their spiritual pillar.

t: Organisation and mobilisation in building the anti-Japanese democratic political power
zh: 抗日民主政权建设中的组织动员
paras: Written for the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japan (2025), this short commentary asks how the Communist Party organised and mobilised the people while building democratic political power in the anti-Japanese base areas. The author argues that democracy was the primary means of mobilising the nation, and that the base areas, above all the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region, drew mass support because they practised it.

The piece moves in three steps. It first sets out the wartime logic linking the united front to state-building, citing Mao Zedong's 1937 formulation and the Party's ten-point programme for resisting Japan. It then describes how democratic institutions were built in practice: the "three-thirds system" and the electoral campaigns. Finally it examines the consequences of this democracy, using Xie Juezai's 1940 remarks and the testimony of visitors to Yan'an.

In Hu's account, the base areas faced severe political, economic and military difficulties, especially in 1941–1942, and overcame them by mobilising the masses and relying on self-reliance. The author presents the three-thirds system (one-third Communists, one-third non-Party progressives, one-third centrists) as a way of widening participation without weakening Party leadership, which depends on exemplary conduct and persuasion. To overcome low literacy and weak democratic habits, the Party used spoken, written and artistic propaganda, and devised voting methods such as the bean ballot. The author lists four results of "the border region has democracy": wider political participation, a transformed social outlook (the "ten absences"), an influx of talent, and the winning of popular support in contrast to Guomindang-ruled areas.

The author concludes that strong mass mobilisation is a distinctive strength of the Party and an important reason for the revolution's victory. In this reading, the Party turned a national crisis into an opening for national rejuvenation and earned its place as the mainstay of united resistance. The author also says that drawing out these experiences helps promote the wartime spirit and build a strong country. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned overview of how Party scholarship presents democracy and mass mobilisation in the Yan'an-era base areas.
quoteEn: Democracy was the primary means of mobilising the whole population to join the War of Resistance.
quoteZh: 民主是动员全国民众投身抗战的首要方式。

glossary.explanation: A principle for allocating seats in base-area governments, proposed by Mao Zedong in 1940 and written into the 1941 Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region platform. It gave Communists, non-Party leftist progressives and centrists one-third each.
The main Communist-led base area during the war, covering parts of Shaanxi, Gansu and Ningxia, with its capital at Yan'an.
A voting method for illiterate voters, in which each candidate had a bowl and voters dropped a bean into the bowl of their choice.

t: The spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army as an important embodiment of the great founding spirit of the Party
zh: 东北抗联精神是伟大建党精神的重要体现
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in July 2025, asks how the spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army (Dongbei Kanglian) relates to the great founding spirit of the Party. Liu Xinjun argues that the former is a concrete unfolding and vivid embodiment of the latter, and a key component of the genealogy of Chinese Communists' spirit.

The article first summarises the founding spirit as stated by Xi Jinping in 2021: upholding truth and ideals, staying true to the original aspiration and mission, fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely, and being loyal to the Party and the people. It then sets out three features of the Northeast spirit and closes by tracing how each corresponds to the founding spirit.

Liu identifies the three features as firm belief and loyalty to the Party, the national righteousness of going to the rescue of the nation, and the heroism of fighting to the death. Examples include Yang Jingyu's two westward expeditions to regain contact with the Central Committee, Zhao Shangzhi's loyalty despite two expulsions from the Party, and Zhao Yiman's conduct under torture. Liu then maps these features onto the founding spirit. Loyalty reflects upholding truth and ideals and loyalty to the Party and the people; defending the nation reflects the original aspiration and mission; and the long guerrilla struggle under harsh conditions reflects fearlessness and bravery.

Liu concludes that the two spirits are in the same line of descent and that the Northeast spirit shows the depth of the founding spirit. Inheriting it is said to matter for strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence, for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party historians link a regional wartime spirit to the official genealogy of Communist spirit.
quoteEn: The spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army is a concentrated embodiment and deep unfolding of the great founding spirit of the Party on the enemy-rear battlefield in the Northeast.
quoteZh: 东北抗联精神是伟大建党精神在东北敌后战场的集中体现和深度展开。

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation set out by Xi Jinping in 2021 at the Party's centenary: upholding truth and ideals, staying true to the original aspiration and mission, fearing no sacrifice and fighting bravely, and being loyal to the Party and the people. It is presented as the source of the Party's spiritual lineage.

glossary.en: spirit of the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army
glossary.explanation: The revolutionary spirit attributed to the Communist-led anti-Japanese guerrilla forces in Northeast China after 1931. It is officially counted within the genealogy of Chinese Communists' spirit.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: An official term for the series of named spirits (for example the Jinggangshan spirit and the Yan'an spirit) drawn from episodes of Party history. It starts from the founding spirit.
Official slogan calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy line promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing discipline and anti-corruption within the Party.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's official long-term national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream.

t: Why the September 18 Incident was the beginning of the Second World War
zh: 九一八事变何以是第二次世界大战的开端
paras: Lu Xiaona asks why the September 18 Incident of 1931, Japan's seizure of north-east China, should be treated as the start of both China's War of Resistance and the Second World War. The author argues that the debate is not only about a date: it bears on the global standing of China's resistance and on China's international voice in writing the history of the war.

This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in June 2025, is organised under four headings. They cover the collapse of the old order, the continuity of aggression and the universality of resistance, the responsibility of the great powers, and the historical agency of the world's peoples.

Lu rejects the common distinction between the "world anti-fascist war" and the Second World War as having different starting points, calling them two sides of one war. In the author's account, Japan's aggression was the first fascist challenge to the Versailles–Washington system, and Western appeasement and the League of Nations' inaction let the order collapse. Lu also holds that Japan gave Germany and Italy a model and helped lay the basis of the Axis, and that anti-fascist resistance by many peoples began after 1931, not only when Britain and France entered the war. Lu blames the great powers' self-interested calculations for the League's failure.

Lu concludes that dating the war from 1931 warns that no state can stand aside from aggression and that major powers should impose firm sanctions instead of appeasing. It would also acknowledge China's role as the main eastern anti-fascist theatre and challenge a "Western-centred" narrative that, in the author's view, marginalises China, Africa and Oceania. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the Chinese academic case for 1931 as the start of the Second World War.
quoteEn: The Second World War was a war of external aggression by fascist states and of uprising resistance by anti-fascist states.
quoteZh: 二战是一场法西斯国家对外侵略与反法西斯国家奋起抵抗的战争。

t: Inheriting and promoting the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression in the new era
zh: 在新时代继承和弘扬伟大抗战精神
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 27 June 2025, ahead of the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, this commentary asks how the "great spirit of resistance" should be inherited and promoted today. Liu Guangming argues that this spirit, forged in the war, remains a precious moral resource for the new journey of building a strong country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Facing foreseeable and unforeseeable risks, the author holds, the country must keep advancing precisely where things are hardest and most dangerous.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the spirit's content, following Xi Jinping's four-part formulation: patriotism of shared responsibility for the nation's fate, national integrity of preferring death to surrender, heroism of fighting to the end without fear of violence, and a firm belief in victory. The second explains its value for the present. The third sets out how to turn it into practice on the new journey. Each element is traced back to figures from Chinese history, such as Fan Zhongyan, Wen Tianxiang, Zheng Chenggong and Yu Gong, and then to wartime examples, including the Battle of Shanghai, Pingxingguan, Taierzhuang and the Hundred Regiments Offensive.

Liu's central claim is that the spirit was forged under the leadership of the Communist Party, which Liu calls the "mainstay" of the national resistance and its chief cultivator. The author attributes to the Party the united front, the line of all-out resistance, the protracted-war strategy and guerrilla warfare. Liu also argues that the spirit turned a latent trait of courage and self-strengthening in the national character into an active one, so that the nation was spiritually reborn after repeated defeats in the modern period.

For the new journey, Liu calls for converting the spirit into strategic initiative, extraordinary courage and strong strategic resolve. In practice this means studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, relying on one's own strength, pressing ahead with deepened reform, law-based governance and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, including a zero-tolerance anti-corruption campaign. It also means holding steady against pressure and containment from hostile forces while advancing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want to see how Party-state discourse links the memory of the anti-Japanese war to present-day political mobilisation and to the 2025 commemorations.
quoteEn: The great spirit of resistance is a towering spiritual monument that our Party forged through leadership in an arduous struggle.
quoteZh: 伟大抗战精神是我们党在艰苦卓绝斗争中领导铸就的巍巍精神丰碑。

glossary.literal: great spirit of resisting the war
glossary.explanation: A formulation used by Xi Jinping for the values said to have emerged in the War of Resistance against Japan. It comprises patriotism, national integrity, heroism and conviction of victory.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream. It envisages China restored to strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation".
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy slogan of the Xi Jinping era that stresses strict Party discipline and a sustained anti-corruption campaign.

t: Memories of the War of Resistance in the archives of the Hundred Regiments Offensive
zh: 百团大战档案中的抗战记忆
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), this short piece in Study Times reads a set of documents held in the Central Archives to recall the Hundred Regiments Offensive. Gui Tengfei presents the campaign, fought by the Eighth Route Army in North China from August 1940 to January 1941, as the largest and longest strategic offensive the Communist-led army launched in the war.

The article draws on orders and telegrams signed by Zhu De, Peng Dehuai and Zuo Quan, including the preparatory order of 22 July 1940 and the campaign deployment of 8 August on breaking the Zhengtai railway. It also cites later directives on naming the campaign, the second-stage plan, anti-'mopping-up' planning, and a 1940 statistical report on mobilisation in central Shanxi. It is organised under four headings: taking the initiative, flexible adaptation, hard struggle, and unity of army and people.

Gui argues that in summer 1940 Japan's 'cage policy' in North China, setbacks on the Nationalist front and talk of peace had left the country pessimistic, so a victory was needed. According to the article, the original plan of 22 regiments grew to 105 regiments and about 200,000 troops as units joined on their own initiative. The author describes three phases with shifting tactics, improvised methods of sabotage and 'home-made' weapons against fortified lines, and says the fighters endured heavily armed opponents through sheer persistence. Civilians, militia and local organisations supplied intelligence, transport and labour; Gui cites a Japanese staff officer's recollections to show Japanese forces facing a 'sea' of people's war.

Gui concludes that the offensive struck the cage policy, tied down Japanese troops, raised the prestige of the Party and the Eighth Route Army, and reversed low morale nationwide, further proving the Communist-led forces' role as the 'mainstay' of resistance. The article says its patriotic spirit offers lasting inspiration for staying true to the Party's founding mission. Read the original if you want a brief, officially framed account of the Hundred Regiments Offensive that shows which archival documents are being highlighted in the 2025 anniversary commemorations.
quoteEn: The Hundred Regiments Offensive produced an epic of war in which army and people were of one mind and shared a common hatred of the enemy.
quoteZh: 百团大战，打出了军民一心、同仇敌忾的战争史诗。

glossary.literal: Great Battle of the Hundred Regiments
glossary.explanation: A large Eighth Route Army campaign in North China from August 1940, aimed at railways, mines and Japanese strongpoints. It is commemorated in Chinese official history as a major Communist-led operation.
The name given to the main Communist-led force in North China during the War of Resistance against Japan, nominally within the Nationalist command in the united front.
The term used in Chinese accounts for Japanese efforts in North China to enclose the Communist base areas with blockade lines, railways, roads and fortified posts.

glossary.en: staying true to the Party's founding mission
glossary.literal: never forget the original aspiration, keep the mission firmly in mind
glossary.explanation: A slogan from the Xi Jinping era urging Party members to keep faith with the Party's founding aims; it was also the name of a 2019 Party-wide education campaign.

t: Resolutely defending the historical contribution of the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression to victory in the world anti-fascist war
zh: 坚定捍卫中国人民抗日战争对世界反法西斯战争胜利的历史贡献
paras: Published in Qiushi in 2025, this commentary by the PLA National Defence University takes up the place of the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression in the Second World War. Following Xi Jinping's repeated statements, it argues that the Chinese theatre was the main Eastern theatre of the world anti-fascist war and that China made a major contribution to the victory. It also holds that this contribution must be remembered and defended today.

The text has three parts. The first sets out the Chinese theatre's military and strategic contribution. The second presents that contribution as a collective achievement of the whole nation and draws lessons from it for the "new journey". The third turns to present-day tasks: countering distortions of China's wartime role, preventing the revival of Japanese militarism, and upholding Taiwan's status as part of China. It closes with a call on the armed forces to carry forward the spirit of resistance.

In the first part, the article argues that China began resisting fascism earliest, fought longest and paid the highest price. It cites 1.5 million or more Japanese troops eliminated, over 70 per cent of Japan's Second World War casualties, and more than 35 million Chinese military and civilian casualties. It says China's resistance tied down Japan, ruled out a Japanese "northward advance" against the Soviet Union, delayed the "southward advance", and supported the Allies' "Europe first" strategy. It also points to the expeditionary force sent to Burma, and to support for anti-Japanese forces in Korea and Vietnam. The second part draws on Mao Zedong's On Protracted War and attributes the victory to the Chinese people's love of peace, courage, global outlook and unity under the anti-Japanese national united front. From each of these it derives a task for the present: military preparedness, fighting spirit, the concept of a community with a shared future for mankind, and unity around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core.

In the third part the authors say some forces portray China as a passive victim, credit the Allied victory to Britain and the United States alone, or promote a narrative of Japanese victimhood. They hold that the post-war trials of Japanese militarism were incomplete, and that China will never permit militarism to return. They cite the Cairo Declaration and the Potsdam Proclamation as confirming Chinese sovereignty over Taiwan, and call for opposing "Taiwan independence" and upholding the one-China principle and the "1992 Consensus".
