Read the original if you want an example of the official Chinese military-academic account of the war's international significance, and of how it is tied to current positions on Japan, Taiwan and national security.
quoteEn: History tells us that only by being able to fight can one stop war, that one may avoid fighting only by preparing to fight, and that the less able one is to fight the more likely one is to be attacked; this is the dialectic of war and peace.
quoteZh: 历史告诉我们，能战方能止战，准备打才可能不必打，越不能打越可能挨打，这就是战争与和平的辩证法。

glossary.explanation: Official Chinese designation of the Chinese theatre as the principal Asian front of the world anti-fascist war. Xi Jinping has repeatedly used it to stress China's role in the Allied victory.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since around 2012. It calls for shared development, security and values among states.
The wartime alliance between the Communist Party and the Kuomintang, together with other groups, formed in the late 1930s against Japanese invasion. It was based on Kuomintang–Communist cooperation.

Term used by Beijing for a 1992 understanding between mainland and Taiwan representatives that both sides adhere to one China. Its content and existence are interpreted differently across the Taiwan Strait.

t: Cadre education in the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army during the War of Resistance
zh: 抗战时期东北抗日联军的干部教育
paras: This short historical article, published in a newspaper in June 2025, asks how the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army trained its cadres and what distinguished that training. Wu and Bai note that from 1933 the Party-led forces absorbed volunteer armies and other local groups, and that rapid expansion left the army short of capable cadres. They argue that cadre education became essential for carrying the Party line into the army and that it produced a stronger, more cohesive force.

The article first sets out four methods: short-term training classes and training schools attached to units; training teams that moved with the army; a political-military school for senior cadres, opened in 1936 under Zhao Shangzhi; and selection of cadres for study in the Soviet Union. It then describes the content, which fell into military skills, political theory and basic literacy.

Wu and Bai identify three features. The methods were flexible, for example by turning an entire company into a training team when activists could not be spared, or by training a unit on skis. Education stressed the exemplary role of cadres, shown in disciplinary rules issued in 1939 and in the conduct of those trained in the teams. It also linked theory to practice, using recent battles in tactical teaching and asking students to compare their own hardships with lessons on capitalism.

The authors conclude that the army valued cadre education from its founding and that it raised the cadres' overall quality and resolve. In their view these cadres passed instructions up and down and set an example, which strengthened cohesion and advanced the northeastern resistance. Read the original if you want a concise overview of how a guerrilla force organised training under wartime conditions.
quoteEn: From its founding the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army attached great importance to cadre education, and this work achieved marked results: the cadres' overall quality improved and their resolve grew firmer.
quoteZh: 东北抗日联军自成立伊始就高度重视干部教育，其干部教育工作也取得了显著成效，干部整体素质得到了提高，意志更为坚定。

t: Learning from history: upholding the correct view of the Second World War
zh: 以史为鉴 坚持正确二战史观
paras: This short commentary, written after Xi Jinping's May 2025 state visit to Russia for the 80th anniversary of the Soviet Union's victory in the Great Patriotic War, asks what it means to uphold a "correct view of the Second World War". Li argues that doing so, and resisting incorrect views, helps to criticise historical nihilism and to draw lessons from history.

The piece opens with Xi's pledge that China and Russia will jointly defend the outcomes of the war's victory. It then sets out three requirements: adopting a grand historical outlook, adhering to historical materialism, and criticising historical nihilism. Li uses casualty figures, battlefield episodes and examples of foreign aid to China.

Li first holds that a grand historical outlook means judging the war in the span of human civilisation. On this basis the author cites over 100 million casualties worldwide, 35 million Chinese casualties and 300,000 deaths in the Nanjing Massacre, and presents China as committed to peaceful development and to building a community with a shared future for mankind. Second, historical materialism requires recognising the people as the principal force of the anti-fascist victory. Li points to the Northeast Anti-Japanese United Army, Yang Jingyu and the Five Heroes of Langya Mountain, as well as the Hump air route and Norman Bethune. Third, Li says historical nihilism, rooted in "Western-centrism" and the political right, spreads a "Japan as victim" narrative. It denies the contributions of China and the USSR and the Communist Party's leading role.

Li concludes that the correct view of the war must be upheld and nihilist distortions rejected, so that the results of China's War of Resistance are defended. The author stresses the Communist Party's role as the "mainstay" of national resistance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academic commentary frames the Second World War and historical nihilism after Xi's 2025 Moscow visit.
quoteEn: To uphold the correct view of the Second World War, one must criticise historical nihilism and clearly eliminate its negative effects of confusing the public and dissolving historical understanding.
quoteZh: 坚持正确二战史观，必须批判历史虚无主义，旗帜鲜明地消除历史虚无主义混淆视听、消解历史认知的负面影响

glossary.explanation: In Party discourse, a label for views seen as distorting or denying the established official account of history, especially of the Party and the revolution. Here it is applied to denial of China's and the USSR's wartime roles.
A concept stressed by Xi Jinping: understanding events through a broad historical, international and knowledge-based perspective and long-term development patterns.
The Marxist theory of history. In this article it is used to affirm the people as creators of history and the main force in the war.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations based on cooperation, mutual respect and shared interests.

t: The logical evolution of the core meaning of the Chinese Communist Party's original aspiration and mission
zh: 中国共产党初心使命核心意蕴的逻辑演进
source: Journal of Northeast Normal University (Philosophy and Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 3
paras: The article asks what the Chinese Communist Party's founding aspiration and mission (chuxin shiming) – to seek happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation – actually contain, and how that content has developed. Li Jing and Yue Ziqi argue that its core meaning is best grasped through three connected logics: theoretical, historical and practical. In their account, the aspiration and mission unite theory with practice, history with the present, and knowing with doing.

The piece is organised in three sections. The first sets out the theoretical meaning by answering three questions: what the mission is, why the Party adopted it, and how it is to be carried out, drawing on Marx and Engels's Communist Manifesto, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping. The second traces the historical meaning through four periods: new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. The third turns to practice since the 20th Party Congress (2022), covering Chinese modernization, common prosperity, the building of a modern socialist country and a new cultural mission.

The authors' central claim is that the mission expresses the proletarian vanguard character of the Party in specifically Chinese form. They hold that the Chinese working class, oppressed by imperialism, the bourgeoisie and feudal forces, was especially resolute, and that the Party therefore joined class mission, national destiny and popular wellbeing. Historically, they say, the Party has always linked its maximum programme (communism) with the common ideals of each period, so that the mission rose to new levels at each stage. In the new era, they list achievements in Party building, whole-process people's democracy, the new development philosophy, the elimination of absolute poverty and ecological civilization, which they present as giving the mission firmer institutional, material and spiritual support.

The authors conclude that pursuing the mission today means upholding Party leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics, putting the people at the centre of development, and pursuing common prosperity through a coordinated system of primary, secondary and third distribution. They also call for accelerating new quality productive forces, and for adapting Marxism to Chinese culture through the Two Integrations, with the aim of creating a new form of human civilisation. Read the original if you want a systematic statement of how current Party-theory scholarship frames the Party's founding mission across its history and into the present.
quoteEn: The Party's original aspiration and mission determine the advanced and correct character of China's leading force, theoretical choices and path exploration, and serve as a powerful guide for pursuing the people's happiness and national rejuvenation on the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 党的初心使命决定了中国领导力量、理论选择、道路探索等方面的先进性和正确性，成为在中国特色社会主义道路上坚持实现人民幸福和民族复兴的有力遵循。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Its listed features include a huge population, common prosperity, harmony with nature and peaceful development.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, given fresh emphasis under Xi Jinping. It is presented as a long-term undertaking, not an immediate equalisation.
The official description of China's democratic system, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019. It holds that democracy covers every stage of governance, not just elections.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological innovation and industrial upgrading.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture. It was formalised under Xi Jinping.
An official framework of five principles: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. It was set out in 2015.

t: The Bandung spirit today and China's contribution
zh: 万隆精神的时代回响与中国贡献
paras: Marking the 70th anniversary of the 1955 Bandung Conference, Ren Hongyan asks what the "Bandung spirit" of solidarity, friendship and cooperation means for a turbulent present. The article argues that the spirit remains vital, and that the Global South should carry it forward and give it new content through the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. Ren presents China as an indispensable contributor both in 1955 and since.

The piece, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in 2025, has three parts. The first assesses the conference's historical impact. The second explains why the Bandung spirit is still relevant, covering the rise of the Global South, the growth of South-South cooperation, cooperation mechanisms, and China's role. The third sets out four areas in which the spirit matters under current conditions.

In the first part, Ren credits Bandung with accelerating decolonisation, citing a rise in independent Asian and African states from 29 to 73 between 1955 and 1969. Ren also calls it the formal start of South-South cooperation, a declaration for peace and justice whose ten principles were absorbed into UN documents, and a milestone for the new China, whose Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence fed into those principles. For the present, Ren cites figures that the Global South accounts for over two-thirds of the world's countries and population, over 40% of world output and about 80% of growth. Ren credits the Belt and Road Initiative, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, the New Development Bank, BRICS and the Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives with advancing cooperation, and treats Xi Jinping's 2015 call to give the spirit new content as the guide.

Ren sees unilateralism, protectionism and great-power bullying, with no state named in the argument beyond "certain major powers", as threatening the world. The article calls on the Global South to defend international fairness and the UN-centred order, keep economic cooperation open, resist bloc confrontation in the name of peace, and promote civilizational diversity. It ends by citing Zhou Enlai's 1955 "seek common ground" statement and Xi's pledge that China will remain a reliable friend of developing countries. Read the original if you want an official Chinese account of how Bandung is being invoked in current Global South diplomacy.
quoteEn: The Global South is experiencing another politically awakening that shakes the world, playing an ever greater role in promoting world peace, upholding justice and meeting global challenges together, and is a force for stability, good and progress in today's world.
quoteZh: 全球南方正迎来又一次震撼全球的政治觉醒，在促进世界和平、维护公道正义、合作应对全球性挑战方面发挥着越来越重要的作用，是当今世界的稳定、向善、进步力量。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13 as the aim of China's foreign policy, stressing shared interests, cooperation and a more just international order.
A collective term for emerging-market and developing countries, which Chinese official discourse uses to describe a growing bloc in world affairs.
The ideals of solidarity, friendship and cooperation associated with the 1955 Asian-African Conference in Bandung, Indonesia, as the article presents them.

glossary.en: the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence
glossary.explanation: Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence, first put forward by China and India in 1954.
A global infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: Accelerating the formation of source-material, discourse and theoretical systems for the community of the Chinese nation
zh: 加快形成中华民族共同体史料体系、话语体系和理论体系
source: Renmin Luntan·Xueshu Qianyan (People's Tribune·Academic Frontiers), 2025 no. 5
paras: Mao Huabing takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the ninth collective study session of the 20th Politburo, to speed up a self-reliant Chinese system of historical sources, discourse and theory on the community of the Chinese nation. Mao argues that these "three systems" are an innovation in ethnic theory that applies the basic principles of Marxist ethnic theory to China's conditions and fine traditional culture. In this reading they support one another and form the scholarly and practical basis for forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation.

The article begins with current ethnic work. It cites uneven development in some regions and the rise abroad of separatism and religious extremism as threats to unity. It then devotes one section to each system: the source-material system, the discourse system and the theoretical system. A short conclusion describes how the three fit together.

On sources, Mao calls for wider and better-organised collection: a thematic database that combines documents, archaeology, inscriptions and oral tradition, uses digital and AI tools, and verifies authenticity. Research should move from elite to popular perspectives, use cross-cultural and interdisciplinary methods, and follow historical materialism by reading fragments within the whole. On discourse, Mao says Western ethnic theory has dominated, so the concept of "nation" (minzu) has been stressed more than that of the "Chinese nation" (Zhonghua minzu). The proposed remedy is original concepts, plain-language communication, and the Party's leadership of discourse, with political, academic, everyday and international registers converting into one another. On theory, Mao advocates "de-familiarisation" and "re-problematisation" of existing concepts under Marxist guidance, a people-centred principle and unity of theory and practice. Mao also calls for more research on basic and practical problems, and for stronger disciplines and training of specialists.

Mao concludes that the sources are the foundation, discourse is the bridge and theory is the soul of one organic whole. This whole is said to develop the Party's ethnic theory and policy, add substance to China's self-reliant knowledge system, and strengthen ethnic identity and cultural confidence. Mao also suggests that it can offer a Chinese approach to ethnic problems and civilisational conflict worldwide. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-aligned account of how Chinese scholars are expected to build the research agenda behind the "community of the Chinese nation" concept.
quoteEn: The source-material system is the cornerstone, giving solid historical support to building the discourse and theoretical systems; the discourse system is the bridge, linking past and future; the theoretical system is the soul of the whole structure.
quoteZh: 史料体系作为基石，为话语体系与理论体系的构建提供了坚实的历史支撑；话语体系是桥梁，连接着过去与未来，阐释着中华民族共同体的深刻内涵与时代价值；理论体系则是整个架构的灵魂

glossary.explanation: A concept in official ethnic policy that treats the 56 recognised ethnic groups as parts of one Chinese nation. It is closely tied to the Party's call to forge a strong sense of this community, which emphasises shared identity over group differences.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: to cast firm the consciousness of the Chinese national community
glossary.explanation: The guiding aim of the Party's ethnic work since the 19th Party Congress (2017). It stresses a shared national identity, culture and homeland across all ethnic groups.

t: "The enemy advances, we advance": how the Eighth Route Army prevailed in North China
zh: “敌进我进”：八路军在华北的制胜之道
paras: Deng Zhengyun examines how the Eighth Route Army answered Japanese "cage" policies and "three-all" sweeps in North China during the War of Resistance against Japan. The short commentary argues that the strategy of "the enemy advances, we advance", which Deng presents as a creative stroke of Mao Zedong's military thought, was no passive evasion. In Deng's account it turned the Japanese rear into the front line.

The piece rests on Mao's guerrilla concepts: turning defence into offence, fighting quick battles within a protracted war, and making enemy bases into guerrilla bases. Deng then works through three cases: the "three-three system" combat groups, the armed work teams (wugongdui), and the "red and black accounts" system.

On the combat groups, Deng describes small units that cut telephone lines, blew up railway bridges and ambushed supply columns, which allegedly forced Japan to commit over 70 per cent of its troops to rear-area defence. The work teams, proposed by Nie Rongzhen in 1942, infiltrated occupied areas. Deng cites figures such as a 40 per cent monthly disruption of rail transport and the Ranzhuang tunnel defence. The red and black accounts recorded the conduct of collaborators and tied their survival to it. Deng cites a 400 per cent rise in puppet-troop desertion in 1943.

Deng concludes that the approach traded space for time and built small victories into large ones. In this reading, strategic success depends on breaking conventional thinking. Read the original if you want a brief, celebratory account of Eighth Route Army guerrilla tactics, and of how they are presented in current Chinese popular historiography.
quoteEn: "The enemy advances, we advance" was a strategic innovation in Mao Zedong's military thought; it was in no way passive avoidance of battle, but a model of breaking deadlock through wisdom.
quoteZh: “敌进我进”是毛泽东军事思想的战略创举，绝非消极避战，而是以智慧破局的典范。

glossary.explanation: A slogan describing the Eighth Route Army's practice of sending forces into enemy-held areas when Japanese and puppet troops attacked its bases. It plays on the better-known guerrilla maxim of retreating when the enemy advances.
Small units combining military action, political work and mobilisation of villagers behind Japanese lines. The article credits Nie Rongzhen with proposing them in 1942.
A way of organising small combat groups in which veterans, trained soldiers and recruits or militia share roles. The article uses it for the groups' internal structure.
A system of keeping records on puppet officials, awarding red or black points for their conduct. The article describes it as a tool of psychological and political pressure.

t: Japanese archives corroborate the Communist Party of China's role as the mainstay of the War of Resistance against Japan
zh: 日方档案佐证中国共产党在抗日战争中的中流砥柱作用
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in 2025, Wu Xiangping asks what Japanese wartime records reveal about the Communist Party of China's (CPC) part in the War of Resistance against Japan. Wu argues that these records, seen from the enemy's side, confirm the Party's role as the mainstay (zhongliu dizhu) of the resistance. In Wu's view they also refute claims that glorify the Kuomintang's war effort while denying the CPC's position and role.

The article draws on documents produced by Japanese bodies from 1929 to 1944. These include South Manchuria Railway (Mantetsu) survey reports, Foreign Ministry intelligence compilations, army staff papers, and publications by Japanese policy and foreign-affairs associations. It also cites remarks by Prime Ministers Konoe Fumimaro and Abe Nobuyuki and by Prince Mikasa. It is organised in three parts: how Japanese observers rated the CPC as a political force, how the Japanese army made the CPC its main military target, and how Japanese sources judged the strength of CPC forces.

Wu's core argument rests on quoted Japanese assessments. Before and after the Mukden Incident (1931), Japanese reports called the CPC the most potential political force in China and the centre of an emerging anti-Japanese united front. After the Marco Polo Bridge Incident of 1937, Japanese army documents, in Wu's account, named the Communists as the key target of military 'suppression'. They record that the Eighth Route Army and local guerrillas filled the 'vacuum' left in North China when most Kuomintang main forces withdrew, and set up base areas. Japanese officials described the CPC-led bases as a 'cancer' and the Party as the real enemy of Japan's 'new order'. Wu also cites Prince Mikasa's 1944 remark that the Japanese army could not match the Communist forces.

Wu concludes that the Japanese records show the CPC organising resistance immediately after 1931 and promoting the anti-Japanese national united front and Kuomintang–Communist cooperation. They also show it leading resistance behind enemy lines, building 19 base areas, and tying down Japanese forces. In Wu's reading, this changed the balance of forces and laid the foundation for final victory. Read the original if you want to see which Japanese-side documents are cited in support of the CPC's wartime role as presented in current Chinese historiography.
quoteEn: The Japanese side realised that the anti-Japanese armed forces led by the Communist Party of China were a huge potential threat, and regarded the Party as Japan's true enemy.
quoteZh: 日本方面意识到中国共产党领导的抗日武装力量是潜在的巨大威胁，认为中国共产党是日本的真正敌人

glossary.explanation: An idiom for a steadfast force that holds firm amid turmoil. Official Chinese historiography uses it to describe the CPC's role in the War of Resistance against Japan.
The broad alliance of parties and social groups against Japan, formed around the second Kuomintang–Communist cooperation in 1937.
Territories behind Japanese lines that the CPC administered and used as bases for guerrilla and mass mobilisation.
The clash of 7 July 1937 near Beijing that began full-scale war between China and Japan.

t: From "civilization through technology" to "technology through civilization"
st: New China's path to modernization and the character of its civilization in the long durée
zh: “由技术而文明”到“由文明而技术”
zhSub: 从长时间段看新中国现代化径路及其文明的特质
paras: Hu Tianjiao asks how to understand what is distinctive about the path of Chinese modernization and about the new form of human civilization built on it. The article argues that Western modernity operates on a logic of "civilization through technology", under which technological and productive power decides who counts as civilized. New China, in Hu's account, first worked within this logic and then moved beyond it towards "technology through civilization".

Taking a long historical view and a China–West comparison, the article begins with the nineteenth-century Western "intrusion" into China and the civilized/barbarous/savage hierarchy that legitimised colonialism. It then examines two strands of New China's technological effort: building an independent and complete industrial system, and pursuing cutting-edge science alongside mass mobilisation of local knowledge. A third part sets out how China is said to have transcended the logic through three steps.

Hu contends that late-Qing and later Chinese thinkers followed the same sequence from technology to civilization, and that New China needed a modernization that was both self-directed and progressive. Examples include the 1956 long-range science plan, the Chinese malaria drug artemisinin and hybrid rice. Yet the article holds that China did not simply assimilate this logic. It recognised it "negatively" as a historical reality, for example in the Sino-Soviet dispute over whether Western "position of strength" policy had ended. It then separated civilization from technology by defining civilization relationally, by a state's commitment to equal international order and respect for other nations' paths. Finally it re-anchored technology in the people: developed for the people and relying on them.

Hu points to the 1950s combination of advanced weaponry and the "mass line", with its flat project teams and cooperation among cadres, experts and workers. The author says this model influenced Toyotism and post-Fordist practice and avoided the deskilling of workers under capitalism. The conclusion is that China's path corrects the defects of modern civilization rather than overturning it, and that it remains unfinished and open to the future. Read the original if you want a Chinese-language argument linking technology, civilizational discourse and Chinese modernization, with historical cases from the 1950s onward.
quoteEn: Civilization's guidance of technology means that, while pursuing technological development, one must also consider the prior questions of how technology is to be developed and what it is developed for.
quoteZh: 文明对技术的引领，意味着在追求技术发展的同时，还需要思考以怎样的方式发展技术、为了什么而发展技术的先决性问题。

glossary.explanation: Official Party term for China's own path to modernity, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
Official phrase for the civilizational outcome claimed for Chinese modernization, set against the Western-led model.
Party method of work, associated with Mao Zedong, of drawing on the experience of ordinary people and returning to them with policy.

t: The historical creation and practical achievements of "combining education with productive labour"
zh: “教育与生产劳动相结合”的历史创建和实践成就
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2025 no. 2
paras: Xu Xiyuan and Liang Yanbing take up the Marxist principle of combining education with productive labour, which they describe as both part of Marxist educational theory and a long-standing tradition of the Chinese Communist Party. They note that artificial intelligence has prompted worries about labour education being outdated, the deskilling of labour and technological unemployment. The article argues that the Party's practice, from the revolutionary years to the present, shows the principle to be historically necessary and productive, and that it remains a guide for education in the new era.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the principle arose and developed, under four headings: the needs of economic production, the need to overcome the separation of knowledge from practice, the need to overcome the split between mental and manual labour, and the aim of all-round human development. The second reviews achievements in three fields: transforming society, promoting production, and cultivating people. The third draws lessons for the present and uses Xi Jinping's 2024 speech at the National Education Conference as its reference point.

Xu and Liang tie each historical stage to a distinct need. In the base areas of the Yan'an period, schools and students took part in the production campaigns in order to survive the blockade. After 1949, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping presented the principle as a remedy for schooling cut off from society and for the gap between mental and manual workers. The authors credit the Party's practice with giving working people access to education, with bringing intellectuals and workers and peasants together, with raising the status of women, with supporting economic growth and innovation, and with producing people developed in moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour terms. They distinguish this from capitalist combinations of education and labour, which they say serve the extraction of surplus value and short-term employment.

The authors conclude that the history confirms the classical Marxist view of the principle as the fundamental route to transforming society, raising labour productivity and forming well-rounded people. They propose upholding Party leadership, adopting a people-centred approach, and innovating in practice: compulsory labour education at every school level, family–school–society cooperation, and vocational education that integrates industry and education. They present this as a distinctive contribution of socialism with Chinese characteristics to global education. Read the original if you want a Party-historical account of how the education–labour principle has been justified and applied from the revolutionary bases to current labour education policy.
quoteEn: The essence of "combining education with productive labour" is the combination of knowledge and practice.
quoteZh: “教育与生产劳动相结合”的本质上是认识与实践相结合

glossary.zh: 教育与生产劳动相结合
glossary.pinyin: jiàoyù yǔ shēngchǎn láodòng xiāng jiéhé
glossary.explanation: A principle derived from Marx and Engels that Chinese Party documents adopted as an educational policy. It has been applied in forms ranging from work-study schemes to present-day labour education.

t: Mao Zedong on the Zunyi Conference
zh: 毛泽东论遵义会议
source: Mao Zedong Deng Xiaoping Theory Research (Mao Zedong Deng Xiaoping lilun yanjiu), 2025 no. 1
paras: The Zunyi Conference, an enlarged Politburo meeting held during the Long March in January 1935, is widely treated as a historic turning point for the Chinese Communist Party and for Mao Zedong's own career. Lin Xuwu observes that existing scholarship has paid little attention to what Mao himself wrote and said about it. The article sets out to identify Mao's relevant texts, his core views and the historical value of those views.

Lin first counts the sources. Searching Mao's Selected Works, Collected Works and selected letters, the author finds 20 writings that mention the conference 40 times in all, 36 before 1949 and four after. The first is from December 1936 and the last from September 1963. The main part then sets out four strands in Mao's assessment, and a final section assesses their value.

In Lin's reading, Mao consistently held that Zunyi corrected the serious "Left" errors of 1931–34, which he variously called opportunist, dogmatist and subjectivist. Mao also credited the conference with promoting unity in the Party and the Red Army. Lin points to Mao's decision to confine the meeting mainly to military questions and to avoid labelling the earlier line a full line error, and to his insistence on thanking those comrades who had erred. The third strand is independence and self-reliance. Lin argues that the Party corrected its course without Comintern direction and criticised a Comintern adviser in a Central document for the first time. Mao is quoted as saying that real understanding of independence began at Zunyi. The fourth strand treats Zunyi as a turning point in line and in ideological work.

Lin concludes that Mao's views shaped the 1945 Resolution on Certain Questions in Party History and fed into the later historical resolutions, including the 2021 resolution on the Party's century of struggle. Lin also holds that Mao's insistence on analysing both sides of the earlier period, rather than rejecting everything, exemplifies dialectical and historical materialism. Independence and self-reliance, in the author's account, runs from Zunyi through Mao, Deng Xiaoping and later leaders to the Party's ten historical lessons. Read the original if you want a source-based account of how Mao characterised Zunyi and how that characterisation entered official Party historiography.
quoteEn: Real understanding of independence and self-reliance began with the Zunyi Conference.
quoteZh: 真正懂得独立自主是从遵义会议开始的

glossary.explanation: An enlarged Politburo meeting held in Zunyi, Guizhou, in January 1935 during the Long March. Party histories treat it as the point at which the "Left" military leadership was set aside and Mao Zedong's leading role began to be established.

glossary.zh: 关于若干历史问题的决议
glossary.pinyin: Guānyú ruògān lìshǐ wèntí de juéyì
glossary.en: Resolution on Certain Questions in Party History
glossary.explanation: The first historical resolution of the CCP, adopted in April 1945 under Mao's direction. It assessed the Party's earlier leadership lines and is treated as the first of three such resolutions.

A principle in CCP discourse that China's affairs must be decided by the Chinese people according to Chinese conditions rather than on foreign instructions. It is listed among the ten historical lessons in the 2021 resolution.

t: Economic practice and theoretical exploration in the period of socialist revolution and construction
st: Reflections on compiling "Economic History of the People's Republic of China (1949–1978)"
zh: 社会主义革命和建设时期的经济实践与理论探索
zhSub: 《中华人民共和国经济史（1949—1978年）》编写有感
paras: He Yaomin, who led the team of authors, introduces a new national textbook, Economic History of the People's Republic of China (1949–1978), published by Renmin University of China Press. He describes it as the first systematic, centrally compiled textbook on the economic history from 1949 to the start of reform and opening up, and a core course text for university economics. The article, a reflective commentary from Guangming Daily (17 June 2025), argues that studying this period's economic practice and theory will help build an autonomous knowledge system for Chinese economics.

He first sets out the contemporary value of this research. He then defines the object of study at three levels and names the key themes of the period. The last part deals with method. He lists concrete topics that he says deserve further study, including the general line for the transition period, land reform and agricultural cooperation, the planned economy, heavy-industry priority and the Angang Constitution.

He argues that the period of less than thirty years, despite serious setbacks, established the socialist economic system and an independent, relatively complete industrial and national economic system. In his account it also formed the path of socialist economic construction, which laid the political, institutional and material foundations for later development. Some experiences can be distilled into core concepts of Chinese economics, such as self-reliance, concentrating resources on major undertakings and respecting objective economic laws. On method, He calls for dialectical and historical materialism, guidance from Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and the political economy of socialism with Chinese characteristics. He also calls for a correct view of Party history, which neither hides mistakes because of achievements nor denies achievements because of mistakes. He insists that the periods before and after reform and opening up must not be used to negate each other.

He concludes that the theme of the period is the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, its main thread is exploring the path of economic construction and modernization, and its essence is achievement and valuable experience. He presents this as a basis for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a leading Chinese economic historian frames the official approach to the 1949–1978 period and the principles behind a state-sanctioned textbook.
quoteEn: One historical period cannot be used to negate another.
quoteZh: 不能用一个历史时期否定另一个历史时期。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing. It is often linked to the Chinese Dream and is used to frame the whole history since 1949.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. Official historiography treats it as the dividing line from the preceding period.
The official name for China's current model of socialism, developed since reform and opening up.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions. It is presented as the current stage of adapting Marxism to China.
A management model associated with the Anshan Iron and Steel Company, promoted in the 1960s. It stressed worker participation in management and cadre participation in labour.

t: Leading high-quality development with high-quality planning
st: Experience and lessons from drafting and implementing the "Xiamen Economic and Social Development Strategy, 1985–2000"
zh: 以高质量规划引领高质量发展
zhSub: 《1985年—2000年厦门经济社会发展战略》编制实施的经验与启示
paras: Jin Min asks what a 1985 local plan can teach those now drafting the 15th Five-Year Plan (the "15th Five-Year Plan" for 2026–2030). The commentary takes up the "Xiamen Economic and Social Development Strategy, 1985–2000", drawn up under Xi Jinping, then Xiamen's executive vice-mayor. Jin presents it as the earliest development plan among China's special economic zones and the first 15-year local strategy. The author argues that its methods remain a practical model for planning in an era of high-quality development.

The article has two parts. The first draws five lessons from the Xiamen strategy: a people-centred orientation, foresight, a systemic approach, a practical work style and historical patience. The second turns each lesson into a recommendation for the current planning cycle. The author closes by linking the lessons to Chinese modernization and to the 2035 long-range goals.

In Jin's account, the Xiamen strategy set income targets for workers and farmers, covered social and ecological goals, and consulted citizens. It proposed a "harbour city" and a three-step plan for a free port, and it had a three-tier structure of overall concept, 21 special studies and priority projects. Jin adds that Xi led research trips to Beijing and Singapore, and that the plan was built to outlast changes in personnel and terms of office. Jin presents these features as proof that systematic, practical planning drives high-quality development.

Jin proposes that the 15th Five-Year Plan should track people's needs through a dynamic mechanism, plan early in fields such as artificial intelligence, quantum technology and green transition, and build multi-level policy frameworks and regional cooperation. It should also set measurable, auditable targets and give long-term, graduated goals in key areas. The author concludes that Chinese modernization depends on combining respect for the people's primary role, systemic coordination, foresight, effectiveness and strategic stability. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-state commentary uses Xi Jinping's early local work as a template for current national planning.
quoteEn: Scientific planning is the greatest benefit, planning errors the greatest waste, and constant upheaval in plans the greatest taboo.
quoteZh: 规划科学是最大的效益，规划失误是最大的浪费，规划折腾是最大的忌讳

glossary.explanation: An official concept promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022) describing China's own path to modernization, set against Western models.
An official formulation since about 2017 that stresses quality, innovation and sustainability over raw growth rates.
China's national development plan for 2026–2030, being drafted in 2025.

t: Promoting the great spirit of resistance against Japanese aggression and advancing the cause of building a strong country and national rejuvenation
zh: 弘扬伟大抗战精神 奋进强国建设民族复兴伟业
paras: Marking the 80th anniversary of victory in the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War (2025), Yan Xiaofeng asks how the war's legacy can serve present national goals. The article argues that understanding the war as a moment of national awakening, and promoting the great spirit of resistance, supplies the unity and self-strengthening drive needed to advance the building of a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization.

The piece is organised in five parts. It treats the Communist Party's role as the mainstay of the war, the truths the war revealed, the content of the resistance spirit, the creativity the war called forth, and China's contribution to the world anti-fascist war and to modernization in the Global South. Each part links a historical point to a present-day task, drawing heavily on Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping.

Yan's central move is a parallel between the war and the current project. Under the Party's leadership, the author says, the united front, the strategy of protracted war and people's war, and the Rectification Movement from 1942 produced victory. Likewise, adherence to Party leadership, Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds is presented as the guarantee for the second centenary goal. The article reads Xi's formula "justice, peace and the people will prevail" as guidance for today: the cause is just, it pursues peace by building a strong military and a community with a shared future for mankind, and it relies on the people. Yan also states that peaceful reunification with Taiwan will be sought with utmost sincerity but without renouncing the use of force. The resistance spirit is broken down into patriotism and a strengthened sense of community of the Chinese nation, unyielding integrity, self-reliance, and unshakeable confidence in victory, each tied to present struggles.

Yan concludes that the Chinese path to modernization has no ready template, so it needs historical initiative, a readiness to struggle and innovation. It must also keep to Party leadership, socialism with Chinese characteristics, high-quality development, whole-process people's democracy and common prosperity. The author describes China as neither urging others to copy a "Western model" nor exporting a "Chinese model", but as offering the Global South new options. Read the original if you want an example of how Party theorists in 2025 link the war memory to Chinese modernization and Party leadership.
quoteEn: In human history, no nation or country has achieved strength and revitalisation by relying on external forces, copying foreign models, or trailing step by step behind others.
quoteZh: 人类历史上没有一个民族、一个国家可以通过依赖外部力量、照搬外国模式、跟在他人后面亦步亦趋实现强大和振兴。

glossary.explanation: Official Party term for China's own path to modernization, stressing a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development. It has been central to Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A 2021–22 Party formula affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold the core status of the General Secretary and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
The target of building China into a great modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, promoted since 2012–13, of a world of shared interests and common development.
Term for developing countries, which Chinese official discourse uses to describe China as one of them.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all of the people, presented as a defining feature of socialism.

t: Guiding the building of people's cities with the people's city concept
zh: 以人民城市理念引领人民城市建设
paras: This commentary, first published in People's Daily in June 2025, takes up how cities should be built and developed in the course of Chinese modernization. Lin and Li argue that the "people's city" concept, summed up in Xi Jinping's formula "people's cities built by the people and for the people", is the essence of a Chinese path of urban development. In their reading, it answers the basic question of for whom and by whom cities are built.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's statements on urban work, drawing on the first volume of his selected economic writings. It then sets out urbanisation data: global urban population shares from a 2023 UN-Habitat report, and China's rise from a 10.64% urbanisation rate in 1949 to 66.16% at the end of 2023. The middle section presents four features of people's cities, each with a city example. The final section lists four relationships that must be handled.

The authors contend that the concept follows from the principle of putting the people first and from the Party's leadership, which they call the fundamental guarantee of urban work. The four features are a people-centred approach (illustrated by Shanghai and Xiamen), serious protection of historical and cultural heritage (Beijing), urban modernization that supports new quality productive forces (Hangzhou), and protection of the urban ecological environment (Fuzhou, Chengdu). They stress that modernization means the modernization of people, not just industrial expansion or population concentration, and that it must not come at the countryside's expense.

To advance people's city construction, the authors call for balance between top-level design and grassroots exploration, between modernization and cultural preservation, between concentrated and dispersed development, and between urban high-quality development and rural revitalization. They hold that cities and countryside should become mutually dependent, with two-way flows of resources. The goal is cities that are liveable, resilient and smart, and that give residents a sense of belonging. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official urban-policy line in 2025, with its statistics and city examples.
quoteEn: The people's city concept gives a profound answer to the fundamental question of for whom and by whom cities are built and developed, and is the essence of the Chinese path of urban development.
quoteZh: 人民城市理念深刻回答了城市建设发展为了谁、依靠谁的根本问题，是中国特色城市发展道路的精髓要义。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula "people's cities built by the people and for the people", set out during his 2019 inspection of Shanghai. It frames urban planning and governance around residents' needs and participation.
The official term for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models. It was foregrounded at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to productivity driven by technological innovation, digital technology and green development.

t: Firmly establishing a correct view of the history of the Chinese nation
zh: 牢固树立正确的中华民族历史观
paras: Wang Dong and Wang Yonggui take up the question of what a correct view of the history of the Chinese nation is and why it should be firmly established. Their starting point is Xi Jinping's speech of September 2024 at the national conference commending ethnic unity and progress. In it, Xi said that all ethnic groups jointly opened up the country's vast territory, founded a unified multiethnic state, wrote its history, created its culture and fostered its national spirit (the "five commons"). The authors treat this as the theoretical statement of the correct view, and argue that holding it is required both by Xi's thinking on ethnic work and by building the Chinese national community in order to advance Chinese modernization.

The article is a short commentary in Red Flag Manuscript, organised in three parts. The first sets out the meaning and significance of a history view based on the "five commons". The second sets out the principles and methods for establishing it. The third proposes practical routes for doing so, covering research, education and cultural identity, and storytelling at home and abroad.

In the first part, the authors argue that this history view enriches the adaptation of Marxist ethnic theory to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They present it as an application of the Two Integrations, especially the second, since it draws on ideas such as "all under heaven as one family" and "harmony and coexistence". They also say it strengthens the ideological basis for forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation and deepens understanding of how nations develop. On method, they call for historical materialism, a long-range view linking past, present and future, and defence of the Chinese nation's cultural subjectivity. They also call for firm criticism of mistaken views of history that, in their account, dismember, distort or fabricate history under the cover of scholarship.

For practice, the authors propose three things. The first is to strengthen historical research, through the project to trace the origins of Chinese civilization and studies of the history of exchange and integration among ethnic groups. The second is to build a shared spiritual home. They list ethnic-unity education within national and social education, promotion of the standard national language and nationally compiled textbooks, and shared cultural symbols. The third is to tell the story of the Chinese nation effectively at home and to the world. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese scholarship links Xi Jinping's ethnic-policy formulations to history education, cultural identity and external communication.
quoteEn: The correct view of the history of the Chinese nation shows how the ethnic groups merged into the pluralistic and unified Chinese nation. It explains the formation of the Chinese national community as an inevitable result of historical development, and it also fully confirms the possibility and feasibility of building a community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteZh: 正确的中华民族历史观，展现了各民族交融汇聚成多元一体中华民族的历史，不仅说明了中华民族共同体的形成是中华民族历史发展的必然结果，也充分印证了构建人类命运共同体的可能性与可行性。

glossary.explanation: A formulation in Xi Jinping's speeches that all ethnic groups jointly opened up the territory, founded the unified multiethnic state, wrote the history, created the culture and fostered the national spirit of China. The article treats it as the basis of the correct view of the history of the Chinese nation.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: forging a firm consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: The guiding line of the Party's ethnic work since the 2010s, emphasising a shared national identity above ethnic identities. It is commonly rendered in official English as forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism with China's concrete realities (the first) and with its fine traditional culture (the second).
The official concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: British archives and the historical writing of the Eighth Route Army's War of Resistance
zh: 英国档案与八路军抗战的历史书写
paras: Xiao Ruping asks what the holdings of the British National Archives can add to the study and writing of the Eighth Route Army's resistance behind Japanese lines during the War of Resistance against Japan. Xiao argues that Foreign Office and War Office files contain extensive material on the Chinese Communist Party and the Eighth Route Army. In the author's view, these records give an outside, Allied view that supports the army's significance and offers new reference points for historians. The piece is a short commentary in a national newspaper.

The article sorts the British sources into three groups. The first is the reports of the British embassy in China, sent to the Foreign Office. The second is military intelligence from attachés and intelligence officers, held by the War Office. The third is the accounts of British journalists and resident expatriates who visited or lived in the North China base areas. Xiao draws on ambassadors Archibald Clark Kerr and Horace Seymour, as well as Bertram, Günther Stein, Michael Lindsay and William Band.

Xiao reads the embassy reports as showing a growing British appreciation of the Communist-led forces, especially after the Pacific War began. Military intelligence is presented as praising guerrilla warfare for tying down large numbers of Japanese troops. It is also said to record the army's growth, its shortages of weapons and medicine, and the hardships of anti-'mopping-up' campaigns. The author cites a 1944 report that at least 22 divisions, 64 per cent of Japanese forces in China, were engaged by the Eighth Route Army. The same report is said to describe Nationalist troops behind the lines as heavily defeated. The journalists' and expatriates' accounts are used to illustrate tunnel and mine warfare, peasant support, and the part played by militia and self-defence units. Xiao treats these as showing why the army succeeded, summed up as 'people's war'.

Xiao concludes that the archives cannot show the whole picture of the Eighth Route Army's war. Even so, the author holds that they show its historical position, its basic forms and characteristics, and part of the reason for its victory. Xiao acknowledges that British collectors had varied motives, but argues that the materials still confirm the army's significance from another's point of view. Read the original if you want a short overview of what British diplomatic, military and press sources say about the Eighth Route Army, and how a Chinese historian uses them.
quoteEn: Although these archives cannot show the whole picture of the Eighth Route Army's resistance, they vividly and truthfully reflect the historical position and role of its resistance behind enemy lines in the Chinese people's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression and the world anti-fascist war.
quoteZh: 这些档案虽然不能反映八路军抗战的全貌，但生动真实地体现了八路军敌后抗战在中国人民抗日战争暨世界反法西斯战争中的历史地位和作用

t: The Zhaojin spirit: the spiritual driving force behind the existence and growth of the Northwest revolutionary base area
zh: 照金精神：西北革命根据地存在和发展的精神动力
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times in June 2025, asks what sustained the Northwest revolutionary base area, the one that Ding Deke calls the only complete base area to survive late in the Agrarian Revolutionary War. Ding argues that the Zhaojin spirit, formed in the struggles of the early Northwest and especially in the Shaanxi–Gansu border base centred on Zhaojin, was the spiritual driving force behind that survival. The article presents it as a precious cultural resource for the Party's revolution, construction and reform.

The article opens with Xi Jinping's 2015 remarks in Shaanxi on the mass base at Zhaojin. It then sketches the armed struggle from the Qingjian Uprising (1927) and Weihua Uprising (1928) through Liu Zhidan's guerrilla forces to the Zhaojin base of 1933 and the Nanliang-centred base that followed. Ding then sets out the spirit's three-part content as part of the Chinese Communists' spiritual genealogy.

Ding defines the spirit as "firm belief in loyalty to the Party, heroic courage in tenacious struggle, and a work style rooted in the masses." For each element the article gives examples. Liu Zhidan, Xie Zichang and Xi Zhongxun kept faith despite failed uprisings, imprisonment and the damage done by a "Left" line. Heroism and revolutionary optimism appear in Wang Taiji's last poem, Zhou Enlai's remark that the Chenjiapo decisions were "Marxism of northern Shaanxi", and the defence of Xuejiazhai, where women fighters died. Mass-rooted work meant village-by-village mobilisation and a united front with local militias, one of whom sheltered sick soldiers in 1933.

Ding concludes that these three qualities embody the Communists' original aspiration and mission and the character they sought to show. Read the original if you want a brief, officially aligned account of how the Zhaojin spirit is defined and illustrated, for example in Party-history education.
quoteEn: The content of the Zhaojin spirit is: "firm belief in loyalty to the Party, heroic courage in tenacious struggle, and a work style rooted in the masses."
quoteZh: 照金精神的内涵是：“忠诚于党的坚定信念，顽强斗争的英雄气概，扎根群众的工作作风。”

glossary.explanation: A Party-history term for the ideals and work style attributed to Communists in the Zhaojin base area in Shaanxi in the early 1930s. It is counted within the Party's wider "spiritual genealogy" of revolutionary spirits.

glossary.zh: 中国共产党人精神谱系
glossary.explanation: An official framework that groups revolutionary spirits, such as the Jinggangshan, Long March and Yan'an spirits, into one lineage of Party values.
The Party's term for the period of about 1927–1937, when the Communists fought the Nationalist government and built rural base areas.

t: Secret communications in the Hubei–Henan–Anhui Soviet area during the Agrarian Revolutionary War and their historical role
zh: 土地革命战争时期鄂豫皖苏区的秘密交通与历史作用
paras: Chen Dongfang, writing in Guangming Daily (4 June 2025), takes up the clandestine front of the Chinese Communist Party's struggle in the New Democratic revolution, a subject the author says has drawn growing scholarly attention. The article asks how the secret communications network of the Hubei–Henan–Anhui Soviet area was built and what it contributed. Chen argues that, under Guomindang blockade, building this network was an urgent task, and that it played a positive role in the founding, development and growth of the base area.

The piece is a short historical commentary in two parts. The first describes how the network was set up, with reference to the Party Central Committee's early statements on the importance of secret communications and the instructions of the 7 August Conference (1927). The second sets out the network's historical significance. The evidence consists mainly of memoirs, Party history compilations and local histories, with examples of named couriers, stations and operations.

In the first part Chen distinguishes two types of line. One was established by the Central Committee and ran from outside into the base area: an eastern line from Shanghai, centred on a central station at Dianbu town in Hefei with four sub-stations, and a western line through Wuhan or, later, Zhengzhou, Xinyang, Luoshan and Guangshui. The other was built by the base area's own Party organisations and ran outwards, as in Liu'an, Xinyang and northwest Anhui. The second part credits the network with three functions. It secured the Centre's political leadership by carrying documents and escorting cadres such as Xu Xiangqian and Shen Zemin. It broke the economic blockade by smuggling medicine, salt, arms and cloth through shops, inns and clinics used as cover, and by passing on intelligence, including a tip that led to the capture of Zhengyangguan. It also drove social mobilisation, by helping to organise grain distribution, recruit soldiers and rebuild Party organisations.

Chen concludes that the secret lines and their couriers were also an efficient "seeding machine" that scattered revolutionary seeds across the base area and its surroundings, forming an important part of the Party's social mobilisation. The article presents secret communications as a key but little-noticed support for the Soviet area's survival. Read the original if you want a concise, source-based account of Party underground logistics in the Hubei–Henan–Anhui base area, with named routes, stations and couriers.
quoteEn: The secret communication lines and the many couriers were also an efficient "seeding machine", scattering many revolutionary seeds in the Soviet area and its surroundings and becoming an important force in the Party's social mobilisation.
quoteZh: 秘密交通线和广大交通员同时也是富有效率的“播种机”，他们在苏区及其周边地区散布了许多革命的种子，成为党的社会动员的一支重要力量。

glossary.explanation: A Communist-held revolutionary base area on the borders of Hubei, Henan and Anhui in the late 1920s and early 1930s. The article calls it the second largest Soviet area after the Central Soviet Area.
The Party's clandestine network of couriers, liaison stations and routes. It carried documents, intelligence, supplies and personnel between the Party Centre, white-area organisations and base areas.
An emergency meeting of the Chinese Communist Party held in August 1927 after the collapse of the First United Front. It shifted the Party toward armed struggle.
The Party's work of rallying peasants and other groups to join peasant associations, the army and revolutionary campaigns.

t: The Communist Party of China's historical exploration of its cultural mission in the New Democratic Revolution and its contemporary implications
zh: 新民主主义革命时期中国共产党对文化使命的历史探索与当代启示
paras: Li Qunqun asks how the Communist Party of China understood and carried out its cultural mission during the New Democratic Revolution, and what that experience offers for taking on a new cultural mission today. The article argues that the Party saw itself as a 'mission-driven party' guided by a logic of responsibility. In Li's account, its clear grasp of the cultural mission and its willingness to act on it greatly promoted the flourishing of New Democratic culture.

The article has three parts. The first treats the modern crisis of traditional Chinese culture. It covers the disputes over 'substance and function' among wholesale Westernizers, restorationist Confucian conservatives and New Confucians, and then the Party's growing cultural self-awareness. The second part examines how the Party understood and practised its cultural mission, under four headings: the leading force, the tasks, the development path and the guiding principle. The third part draws four lessons for the present, with frequent reference to Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping.

Li holds that the Party's rise as a cultural subject came with its correction of dogmatism towards Marxism and of blanket rejection of tradition. Mao's call for a 'national, scientific and mass' new culture of the Chinese nation expressed this. Li presents the wartime cultural path as combining Marxism with fine traditional culture. This meant defining culture through historical materialism, inheriting it critically ('discarding the dross, absorbing the essence') and serving the revolution. The Party's cultural leadership, its orientation towards the people after the Yan'an Forum, and its mass cultural campaigns are said to have won popular support and identification.

From this, Li draws four principles for the present. They are upholding the Party's cultural leadership while innovating (including digital cultural transformation and online cultural governance), promoting fine traditional culture to strengthen cultural confidence, respecting the people's principal position, and keeping a Chinese cultural standpoint while drawing on the best of other civilizations. Li links these to Xi Jinping's formulations and to the Two Integrations. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar reads Yan'an-era cultural policy as a precedent for current cultural leadership and cultural confidence.
quoteEn: The people are both the practical subject and the value subject of cultural construction.
quoteZh: 人民群众是文化建设的实践主体与价值主体

glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's term for the stage of the Chinese revolution (roughly 1919–1949) led by the proletariat and the Communist Party against imperialism and feudalism, as a step towards socialism.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture.
The Party's authority over ideology and culture, tied in official discourse to its control of ideological work. It echoes the Marxist concept of hegemony.
An official concept, prominent under Xi Jinping, of confidence in the value and vitality of China's own culture and in the Party's cultural path.

t: Mao Zedong's thinking and practice on "never becoming a Li Zicheng", and its lessons
zh: 毛泽东对“决不当李自成”的思考、实践及其启示
source: Journal of Hunan University of Science and Technology (Social Sciences Edition), 2025 no. 2
paras: Mao Zedong repeatedly warned the Communist Party to learn from the failure of Li Zicheng, the peasant rebel leader who took Beijing in 1644 but whose regime collapsed within a short time. As the Party prepared to take power nationwide, Mao stressed that it was going to Beijing to take an examination and must "never become a Li Zicheng". Liu and Chen argue that earlier scholarship mostly introduced Mao's thinking on the subject, while his concrete practice after 1949 and the deeper lessons drawn from it have received less attention. Their article tries to fill that gap.

The article has three parts. The first traces Mao's attention to Li Zicheng from his youth through the revolutionary period: the Great Revolution and land revolution years, the War of Resistance against Japan, and the late civil war. The second sets out six areas of practice after the Party entered Beijing. The third draws six lessons for the present, linking them to Xi Jinping's statements on the Mao-era warning.

In the authors' account, Mao located Li's failure in the lack of a leading class or party, the absence of a secure base, arrogance and underestimation of the enemy, corruption within the leadership, and the lack of institutions representing the majority. The wartime reading of Guo Moruo's essay on the 300th anniversary of the 1644 events and the 1945 "cave dialogue" with Huang Yanpei fed into the "Two Musts" and the rules adopted at the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee (1949). The six areas of practice are Mao's personal self-discipline; eliminating threats, including the decision to intervene in Korea; the united front; ties with the masses and opposition to bureaucracy; the Three-Antis campaign and the execution of Liu Qingshan and Zhang Zishan; and institutional safeguards such as people's democratic dictatorship, public ownership and the handling of letters from the public.

Liu and Chen conclude that Mao's reflections are a political legacy whose inheritance bears on long-term Party rule. Their six lessons are drawing wisdom from history, staying alert to danger in times of peace, upholding the Party's glorious traditions, keeping up work on Party conduct and discipline, treating anti-corruption as a permanent task, and using two answers together to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall. These two answers are supervision by the people and the Party's self-reform. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-historical account of how the Li Zicheng analogy has been used in Chinese Communist Party thinking on governance and discipline, from Mao to Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: Self-reform and democratic supervision are like the two wings of one body in the Chinese Communist Party's escape from the historical cycle, working together inside and out and driving jointly, which reflects adherence to dialectics.
quoteZh: 自我革命和民主监督如同中共跳出历史周期率的一体两翼，二者内外协同、内外结合、双轮驱动，这就是坚持辩证法的体现。

glossary.explanation: Mao's 1949 call at the Second Plenum of the 7th Central Committee for Party members to remain modest, prudent and free of arrogance, and to keep up hard struggle.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: The pattern of dynasties flourishing quickly and collapsing suddenly, raised by Huang Yanpei in 1945. Chinese Party discourse treats escaping it as a central test of lasting rule.
The Party's policy of building alliances with non-Party groups such as democratic parties and the national bourgeoisie.
A campaign launched in 1951 against corruption, waste and bureaucracy within Party and state organs.
Xi Jinping's term for the Party's capacity to correct itself, presented as the second answer to the historical cycle. The official rendering is the Party's self-reform.

t: Upholding the correct view of the history of the Second World War
zh: 坚持正确二战史观
paras: Writing eighty years after the end of the Second World War, Liu argues that unilateralism and geopolitical conflict are eroding the international consensus on the war, so a "correct view of the history of the Second World War" must be upheld. The short commentary holds that this requires respect for historical fact, opposition to historical nihilism, defence of the order built on the UN Charter, and a complete collective memory of the war.

The piece is organised in five steps: respect for facts as the premise, opposition to historical nihilism as an urgent task, defence of the postwar order as a practical requirement, shaping and spreading collective memory as a strategic path, and drawing on history to shape the future as the aim.

On facts, Liu cites foreign scholars to support three claims: the 18 September 1931 Incident opened the world anti-fascist war, China and the Soviet Union were the main Asian and European theatres, and the war was also a revolutionary and independence struggle. Liu says current nihilism works through selective memory rather than outright denial. Its Western forms, in the author's account, are Eurocentrism, marginalisation of the Eastern theatre, and a "liberator narrative" that downplays Soviet and Chinese contributions. Liu also claims that some Western powers are diluting the Nuremberg and Tokyo verdicts in order to reshape rules in their own favour.

Liu calls for defending the Cairo Declaration, the Potsdam Proclamation and the "enemy state clauses" of Article 107 of the UN Charter. Liu also calls for stronger history education for young people and for building China's own discourse on the war, so that its contribution is better understood abroad. The author closes by citing Xi Jinping on jointly safeguarding the victory and international fairness and justice. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholarship frames the war's history and its present-day uses.
quoteEn: Upholding the correct view of the history of the Second World War means taking respect for historical fact as the fundamental premise, opposing every form of historical nihilism, firmly defending the international order based on the UN Charter, shaping and spreading a complete collective memory of the war, and drawing on history to create the future together.
quoteZh: 坚持正确二战史观就是要将尊重历史事实作为根本前提，反对任何形式的历史虚无主义，坚定维护以《联合国宪章》为基础的国际秩序，塑造并传播关于二战的完整集体记忆，以史为鉴共创未来。

glossary.explanation: A term in official Chinese discourse for views that are said to deny or distort established history. Here the author applies it to Western narratives of the Second World War.
The 1931 Japanese seizure of Shenyang and then Northeast China, usually called the Mukden Incident in English. Chinese official historiography treats it as the start of the anti-fascist war.

t: The contemporary significance of defending the victory in the Second World War and the post-war international order
zh: 深刻理解维护二战胜利成果和战后国际秩序的时代意义
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 21 May 2025, in the 80th anniversary year of the end of the Second World War and the founding of the United Nations, Zhao Long asks why defending the war's outcomes and the post-war order matters now. The commentary takes its cue from Xi Jinping's visit to Russia on 7–10 May and the China–Russia joint statement issued there. Zhao argues that this defence is not abstract commemoration but a dynamic practice that depends on three things: great powers sharing responsibility, adapting to multipolarity, and answering the demands of the Global South.

The piece has three sections, one for each requirement. The first deals with the UN-centred international system as the core product of the 1945 victory and with the challenges to its authority. The second treats the post-war order as something historically changing, and sets out China's position on multipolarity. The third turns to the rise of the Global South and the question of fairness and justice in global governance.

In the first section Zhao says unilateralism and bullying are weakening the system. Zhao's examples are 'country first' policies, unilateral and secondary sanctions imposed under domestic law, and Cold War 'small circles' and 'value alliances'. Zhao presents China as a founding UN member that supports the Security Council and contributes to peacekeeping, and presents China and Russia as models of non-aligned, non-confrontational cooperation. In the second section, from a historical-materialist standpoint, Zhao holds that the Yalta system and bipolarity have long since ended. Zhao criticises 'rules-based international order' rhetoric, NATO expansion and tariff, trade and technology wars, and endorses 'equal and orderly world multipolarity', in which states of every size take part equally and new mechanisms supplement rather than replace the existing order. In the third section Zhao cites IMF figures: the Global South accounted for over 40% of the world economy in 2024 and contributed 80% of growth. Zhao argues that governance structures have not caught up with this shift, and that powers who label BRICS or the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation 'anti-Western' are the main source of instability.

Zhao concludes that states should reform and improve the post-war order and its multilateral mechanisms on the basis of genuine multilateralism, so that Global South countries can join global industrial and supply chains and develop through industrialisation and modernisation. Stability of institutions, Zhao says, rests on shared values, and justice in the order rests on historical awareness. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese international-affairs scholar presents the UN system, multipolarity and the Global South in the 2025 anniversary context, in a People's Daily commentary.
quoteEn: The stability of institutions stems from consensus on values; the justice of an order rests on historical consciousness.
quoteZh: 制度之稳定源于价值之共识，秩序之正义基于历史之自觉。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Chinese official discourse for developing countries and emerging economies, often contrasted with the Western powers. China presents itself as a natural member of this group.

glossary.zh: 平等有序的世界多极化
glossary.explanation: A formula endorsed by the Central Conference on Work Relating to Foreign Affairs in 2023. It calls for a multipolar world in which states take part as equals and the process is orderly and constructive.

t: Upholding the correct view of the Second World War and resolutely defending historical justice
zh: 坚持正确二战史观 坚定捍卫历史正义
paras: This commentary, originally published in People's Daily on 21 May 2025, was written for the 80th anniversary of victory in the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, the Soviet Great Patriotic War and the World Anti-Fascist War. It takes as its occasion Xi Jinping's state visit to Russia and his attendance at the Victory Day commemoration. Liu Jun argues that defending "historical justice" requires protecting the results of victory in the Second World War, holding to a correct view of that war, and upholding the United Nations and international fairness.

The piece is organised under three headings. The first defines historical justice and lists what China and the Soviet Union gained from the war. The second sets out the elements of the "correct view of the Second World War" and describes Chinese-Russian cooperation on it. The third links this view to the authority of the UN and the postwar international order. Liu draws heavily on Xi Jinping's statements and on the Sino-Russian Joint Statement signed during the visit.

Liu begins from a Marxist conception in which history is the foundation of justice and a correct view of history guides a just history. On this basis the author lists the war's results for China and the USSR: defeat of Japanese militarism and German fascism, the return of Taiwan and the Penghu Islands to China, a key role in founding the UN with permanent Security Council seats, and the collapse of the colonial system. The correct view, in Liu's account, holds that China and the USSR were the main Asian and European theatres and made decisive contributions. It also holds that China's war began earliest and lasted longest, that the Chinese Communist Party led the resistance, and that the Nuremberg and Tokyo tribunals are beyond challenge. Liu accuses some Western countries of using historical nihilism, double standards and discursive reconstruction to downplay the two countries' contributions and shake the postwar order in order to preserve hegemony. The author also criticises those who deny or glorify aggression.

Liu concludes that China and Russia, by making the correct view a matter of institutionalised bilateral cooperation, are taking a stand for international justice. The Joint Statement commits them to joint education and commemorations, research into Nazi and Japanese war crimes, and cooperation on searching for the remains of the fallen. The author expresses confidence that peoples worldwide will side with historical correctness and fairness. Read the original if you want an example of how official Chinese commentary framed the 80th anniversary, Sino-Russian historical memory politics and the postwar order in 2025.
quoteEn: History must not be profaned, the truth must not be distorted, and memory must not be erased.
quoteZh: 历史不能亵渎，真相不能歪曲，记忆不能抹杀。

glossary.explanation: A concept used in Chinese official discourse for upholding accurate historical facts and narratives, here applied to the Second World War and its outcomes.

glossary.en: correct view of the Second World War
glossary.literal: correct view of the history of the Second World War
