The article first describes the late-1950s pressure in three "voices": the United States (embargo, bases, obstruction of UN membership, the "two Chinas" issue), India (the Tibet revolt and the border dispute) and the Soviet Union (disputes over control, withdrawal of technical aid, differences with Khrushchev). It then examines Mao's separate approaches to each, his dialectical reading of the chorus itself, and his emphasis on domestic construction. It closes with lessons for the present, citing Xi Jinping on the "great struggle" and the "great changes unseen in a century".

Hu presents Mao's approach as differentiated. Towards the US he combined struggle and diplomacy, using the 1958 shelling of Quemoy and his "noose" image of American overextension. Towards India and the Soviet Union he combined firm principle with efforts to preserve unity, for example the proposed 20-kilometre demilitarised zone on the border and the suggestion that the two parties keep their own views and await the facts. Mao also judged the chorus to be "great support for China, small opposition", with only perhaps five to ten per cent of humanity truly hostile. In Hu's reading he held that hostility exposed the reactionaries, stirred the Chinese people and sharpened awareness of imperialism's two faces. Hu reports that Mao's fundamental remedy was an independent, complete national economic system, rejection of a "slave mentality" and dogmatic copying, and vigilance against "peaceful evolution".

Hu concludes with three lessons for the present. China should analyse principal and secondary contradictions, answer firmly and keep seeking unity. It should make many friends and unite most countries, as in the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind. It should rely on independent construction: the Four-sphere Confidence, Chinese modernization, technological self-reliance, and guarding against "peaceful evolution" through the Party's self-reform. Read the original if you want a Party School scholar's account of how Mao's Cold War foreign-policy reasoning is being used to frame China's current strategic outlook.
quoteEn: Mao pointed out that the fundamental way to reduce the arrogance of anti-China forces at its source lies in China's own unity, doing domestic work well and speeding up socialist construction, so that internal causes drive the transformation of external ones.
quoteZh: 毛泽东指出，从源头上消减反华势力的嚣张气焰，根本方法在于中国自身团结一致，做好国内工作，加快社会主义建设，以内因推动外因的转化。

glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's phrase for the simultaneous hostility towards China from the US, India, the Soviet Union and others around 1959–1962.

A term associated in Chinese discourse with John Foster Dulles's idea of undermining communist states by non-military means. Chinese writers use it for perceived Western efforts at ideological and political subversion.
The official concept of China's own path to modernity under Party leadership, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of shared global interests and joint development, promoted since about 2012.
Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, stressed since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
China's infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: Raising the quality of people's lives in building Chinese modernization: inherent requirements and practical dimensions
zh: 在中国式现代化建设中提高人民生活品质：内在要求与实践向度
source: Academic Frontiers (Xueshu qianyan) WeChat account, 8 November 2024
paras: Ding Yuanzhu takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) report's call to "promote people's wellbeing and raise the quality of their lives" and asks what "quality of life" (shenghuo pinzhi) means and why it is central to Chinese modernization. The article argues that the features of Chinese modernization named in the report, including common prosperity, coordinated material and cultural-ethical progress and harmony between humanity and nature, all find concentrated expression in the quality of people's lives. Understanding the concept, Ding contends, is therefore important for grasping the essential requirements of Chinese modernization.

The article opens with a conceptual section defining life quality as a composite of economic, social, cultural and spiritual elements, with objective and subjective dimensions and individual and group levels. It then draws on Marx and Engels's theory of all-round human development, Walt Rostow's stages of growth, and Amartya Sen. Later sections discuss how to combine objective measurement with subjective assessment, including happiness, and then turn to policy priorities in the new development stage: social resilience, ageing, employment, artificial intelligence, education, incomes and consumption, with Japan's consumption experience as a cautionary case.

Ding's core argument is that life quality is the necessary outcome of development at a certain stage. Following Rostow's added stage of "the pursuit of quality of life", Ding holds that economic growth should be judged by what it brings to all the people. Objective conditions and subjective satisfaction are each necessary but not sufficient, so the two must be assessed together. Placing "the all-round enrichment of material things and all-round human development" side by side is presented as a continuation of Marx's theory of human development, with free time and free choice as markers. Ding adds that government should look beyond individual happiness to the long-term wellbeing of society as a whole, because market-driven individual desires can foster greed.

On policy, Ding calls for attention to the effects of epidemics, ageing, digitalisation and climate on wellbeing. Ding also calls for the employment-first strategy, education reform in response to AI, attention to young people and avoidance of "involution", and a rise in incomes, with a more balanced distribution, to support consumption. The conclusion invokes the 20th Party Congress's five major principles, including Party leadership and a people-centred approach, as guiding the effort to raise life quality. Read the original if you want a Party-affiliated scholar's account of how "quality of life" is conceptualised in the discourse of Chinese modernization and linked to employment, ageing and consumption policy.
quoteEn: Only by organically combining the assessment of the two can one reflect whether the quality of life is good or bad.
quoteZh: 只有把二者的评价有机结合起来，才能反映生活品质的好坏情况。

glossary.explanation: The official framework for China's development path, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is characterised by a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical coordination, harmony with nature and peaceful development.
A goal of shared affluence for all the people, which Party documents present as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.
A principle associated with Xi Jinping that holds that development should serve the people's interests and the people's wellbeing.

t: Providing legal safeguards for implementing the Global Development Initiative
zh: 为落实全球发展倡议提供法治保障
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks how law can support the Global Development Initiative that Xi Jinping first proposed at the UN General Assembly in September 2021. Cao Junjin argues that the rule of law is an important safeguard for the Initiative's implementation, and that China's legal framework for it is still incomplete.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out what law contributes, then proposes how to build a legal system for the Initiative, and finally outlines supporting institutional measures. Cao notes that Article 18 of the Foreign Relations Law mentions the Initiative but, in Cao's reading, remains declaratory and principled. Two trial working documents from the International Development Cooperation Agency, on a fund pool and a project pool, also exist.

Cao says law makes implementation forceful, orderly and effective by pooling scattered resources, regulating project approval, procurement, monitoring and evaluation, and creating financing and cooperation rules. Cao proposes either a unified "Global Development Promotion Law" or separate laws on international development cooperation or foreign aid, linked to sectoral laws. Cao adds that regulations should cover private-sector participation, and that treaties and tripartite projects with developed countries and international organisations could create "contractual international law".

Cao calls for more legal research on the Initiative, a clearly designated lead agency, stronger funding and training of international development law specialists. On funding, Cao notes the 2022 upgrade of the South-South cooperation fund to the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund, with an extra US$1 billion on top of US$3 billion. Cao suggests further capital increases and sector funds, such as a global education fund. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese legal-policy view of how the Initiative might be institutionalised.
quoteEn: Implementing the Initiative has a dual character, as both development and diplomacy.
quoteZh: 落实倡议具有发展和外交双重属性

glossary.explanation: A framework Xi Jinping announced at the UN General Assembly in September 2021, promoting development cooperation, especially with developing countries. It is one of three global initiatives alongside those on security and civilisation.
A Chinese law adopted in 2023 that sets out principles and institutions for the country's foreign affairs. Cao treats it as a framework law with mainly declaratory provisions.
The Chinese state agency, established in 2018, that manages foreign aid and development cooperation.

glossary.zh: 全球发展和南南合作基金
glossary.pinyin: Quánqiú fāzhǎn hé Nán-Nán hézuò jījīn
glossary.en: Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund
glossary.explanation: A fund that China upgraded in 2022 from the South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund set up in 2015. It is used to support cooperation under the Global Development Initiative.

t: Grasping the people-centred character of further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 深刻把握进一步全面深化改革的人民性品格
paras: This short commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks what gives the drive to further deepen reform comprehensively its people-centred character (renminxing). Deng argues that this character is the essential attribute of Marxism and a distinguishing feature of the reform agenda adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). In the author's reading, it expresses the Party's founding mission and underpins innovation in Chinese modernization.

The article takes the Plenum's principle of 'putting the people first' and breaks it into four aspects. These are the value orientation of the people above all, respect for the people's principal role and creativity, the goal of bringing benefit to the people, and people's livelihood as the basic thread running through reform. It draws on Party documents and a 2024 remark by Xi Jinping in Chongqing.

Deng contends that reform starts from the people's overall, fundamental and long-term interests, and that it has moved from solving the problem of 'having enough' to solving that of 'being good enough'. The people are presented as the practical agents and the source of strength of reform, and their satisfaction as the final test of its results, so that reform becomes a way of pursuing the Party's mass line. The author describes human development as the end of social development, treats modernization as at bottom the modernization of people, and calls for both making the 'cake' bigger and dividing it fairly.

On livelihood, Deng lists remaining weaknesses: uneven urban–rural development, income gaps, unequal educational resources, scarce quality healthcare, employment pressure and incomplete social security. The author calls for reforms in income distribution, employment, social security, housing, medical care and childcare and elderly care, so that people's sense of gain, happiness and security grows. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars present the people-centred principle of the Third Plenum reform agenda.
quoteEn: Further deepening reform comprehensively is the cause of hundreds of millions of people themselves.
quoteZh: 进一步全面深化改革，是亿万人民自己的事业。

glossary.explanation: A Party concept, developed under Xi Jinping, describing China's own path of modernization, which stresses common prosperity and harmony between humans and nature.
A Party working method, associated with Mao Zedong, of gathering the views of the people and returning them as policy, and of relying on the masses.

t: Consolidating the scientific foundations of building a leading country in science and technology
zh: 夯实科技强国建设的科学根基
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2025, after the national science and technology work conference of 13 January stressed "organised basic research", Wan Jinbo argues that basic research is the source of the whole scientific system. The commentary holds that China needs to strengthen organised basic research and technological science to achieve high-level scientific and technological self-reliance.

Wan first reviews recent progress, citing the rise in basic research spending from 49.88 billion yuan in 2012 to 249.7 billion yuan in 2024, and the building of national laboratories and key laboratories. The author then cites international rankings, including the Global Innovation Index, the Nature Index and a list of top scientists, as evidence of growing strength. The final sections set out measures for the coming decade.

Wan's central claim is that strong international influence in basic research marks a leading science and technology country and shapes the shifting of global centres of science, talent and education. The author describes China's innovation as moving from "tracking and learning" to "original leadership", while acknowledging weak original innovation, dependence on foreign key technologies and a shortage of top talent. Wan proposes three linked types of research: strategy-oriented systematic, frontier-oriented exploratory and market-oriented applied basic research, supplying new quality productive forces at source.

Wan calls for coordinating major tasks, institutions, platforms, funding and international cooperation, combining competitive and stable funding, and deepening enterprise-led links between industry, universities and research. The author also urges an innovation-friendly culture with property protection, so that the goal of a leading science and technology country, ten years away, can be met. Read the original if you want a short official-style overview of how a Chinese Academy of Sciences researcher frames basic research policy and its statistical case.
quoteEn: Basic research sits at the starting end of the research chain running from research to application and then to production; it is the cornerstone and source of scientific and technological innovation, and the foundation and staying power of innovation-driven development.
quoteZh: 基础研究处于从研究到应用、再到生产的科研链条起始端，是科技创新的基石和源头，是创新发展的底蕴和后劲。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging industries.
A policy phrase for basic research planned and coordinated around national strategic needs, rather than left to individual researchers' free exploration.

t: Further unleashing the private economy's role in driving high-quality development
zh: 进一步发挥民营经济对高质量发展的推动力
paras: This newspaper commentary in Guangming Daily (27 February 2025) asks how the private economy can contribute more to high-quality development. Guo Chunli argues that the private economy is an important achievement of the socialist market economy and a key foundation of high-quality development in the new era. The author calls for a better environment for its healthy growth.

The piece first reviews private firms' contribution under five headings of the new development philosophy: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. It then turns to four sets of measures on finance, market institutions, property rights and public opinion.

Guo cites figures to show the sector's weight. Private firms are said to contribute 70% of technological innovation outputs, over 50% of tax revenue and 80% of urban jobs. They are also said to account for over 50% of foreign trade and almost 80% of charitable donations. The author presents these as evidence that private enterprises already drive high-quality development in each area, and that the new round of technological revolution and industrial change opens new space for them.

Guo proposes easing financing difficulties, tackling late payments to private firms, and opening major research infrastructure and national technology projects to them. The author also calls for stronger basic market institutions covering property rights, market access and fair competition, along with action against arbitrary fees, fines and inspections. Finally, Guo urges a supportive social climate that promotes entrepreneurship and rebuts slander against private entrepreneurs. Read the original if you want a concise, statistics-backed statement of the official case for supporting the private economy in early 2025.
quoteEn: Private enterprises are an important force in driving innovative development.
quoteZh: 民营企业是推动创新发展的重要力量。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
The guideline of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward by the Party leadership in 2015.
The official name for China's economic system, adopted in the 1990s. It combines market mechanisms with public ownership as the main body and state macro-control.

t: Fully and accurately grasping the principles of further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 全面准确领会和把握进一步全面深化改革的原则
paras: This article, published in Qizhi (Banner) in early 2025, is an interpretive study of the "six adherences" that the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) set out as principles for further deepening reform comprehensively. Qu argues that these principles condense Xi Jinping's new thinking on comprehensive reform, and that they must be understood fully and accurately and upheld unwaveringly in practice.

The text has three parts. The first explains the significance of the six principles from four angles: historical, practical, theoretical and methodological. The second sets out the content of each principle and the question it answers. The third turns to practical requirements for regions, departments and Party organisations implementing the Plenum's decisions.

Qu presents the six principles as one organic whole, each answering a distinct question about reform. Party leadership answers who leads; a people-centred approach answers for whom; upholding fundamental principles while innovating answers the question of stance and direction; institution-building as the main thread answers the question of goals; law-based governance answers the question of path; and a systems approach answers the question of method. On "upholding fundamental principles", Qu states that Party leadership, Marxism, the socialist path with Chinese characteristics and the people's democratic dictatorship cannot be shaken, or reform would be led onto "the wrong path". Qu also stresses the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and calls for balancing relationships such as government and market, efficiency and fairness, and development and security.

In conclusion, Qu asks that each principle be turned into a working requirement. These include safeguarding the authority of the Party Centre, starting from the people's fundamental interests, building institutions that are practical and effective, using law to consolidate reform results, and coordinating measures through clear task lists, timetables and priorities. The article closes by calling for unity around the Party Centre with Xi Jinping at its core and for pressing on with reform. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line exposition of the six principles of the Third Plenum's reform agenda, as presented by a senior Party theorist.
quoteEn: Upholding fundamental principles while innovating answers the question of the stance and direction of reform.
quoteZh: 坚持守正创新回答的是改革的立场和方向问题。

glossary.explanation: A formula from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. It is used in official texts to stress Party unity.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Centre and the Party Centre's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.literal: guarding what is correct and innovating
glossary.explanation: An official formula that couples adherence to core political principles with innovation in theory, practice and institutions.

t: Leading the development of new quality productive forces through scientific and technological innovation
zh: 以科技创新引领新质生产力发展
paras: Zhao Zhenhua takes up the instruction of the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference to "lead the development of new quality productive forces through scientific and technological innovation" and asks what these forces are, how innovation produces them and what path should be followed. The article, published in Qiushi's Red Flag Manuscript in 2025, argues that innovation is the leading factor in new quality productive forces. In Zhao's account this makes it central to building a modern industrial system, winning strategic initiative in international competition and meeting people's aspirations for a better life.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the features of new quality productive forces in the present era. The second explains the internal logic by which technological innovation drives their development, drawing on Marx, Engels and Xi Jinping's statements. The third proposes a path in four steps: reform of production relations, original innovation, the conversion of research results into output, and development adapted to local conditions.

Zhao's core argument is that productive forces advance through science and technology, now at an accelerating pace and across ever wider fields, with converging disciplines and globalised innovation. Innovation raises industries to higher levels and lifts the three elements of productive forces (labourers, means of labour and objects of labour) and the way they combine. Technological innovation also induces managerial, institutional and cultural innovation. Citing Engels's "parallelogram of forces", Zhao presents these as a joint resultant that is mutually conditioning. Because production relations must adapt to productive forces, the author says, further comprehensive deepening of reform is needed.

Zhao calls for a better division of roles between market and government. Enterprises should be the main actors in innovation, state capital should move toward forward-looking strategic emerging industries, and private firms should be able to lead major technological projects. The author also urges stronger basic research and a new national system for pooling resources on key technologies, along with markets for trading research results. Eastern regions should lead original innovation and western regions should focus on application, without abandoning traditional industries, and the "Internet Plus" and "AI Plus" initiatives should be accelerated. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy reasoning that links innovation, reform of production relations and regional industrial strategy.
quoteEn: Scientific and technological achievements are not in themselves real productive forces; only when they are applied to industry in good time, steadily raising technological levels and the quality of industrial development, promoting industrial upgrading and continually extending, completing and strengthening industrial chains, can they become real productive forces.
quoteZh: 科技成果本身不是现实生产力，只有及时运用到产业上，不断提升技术水平和产业发展质量，促进产业升级，持续延链、补链、强链，才能转化为现实生产力。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation and marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality. It is now a central slogan of Chinese economic policy.
An official term for mobilising state, market and social resources on a national scale to achieve breakthroughs in key technologies.

t: Upholding the five "must coordinate" principles in economic work
zh: 坚持以五个“必须统筹”做好经济工作
paras: This article, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao) in early 2025, interprets the five "must coordinate" principles set out at the Central Economic Work Conference of December 2024. Li and Gu argue that these pairs of relationships are regularities distilled from China's economic practice, apply dialectical and historical materialism to current economic contradictions, and further enrich Xi Jinping's economic thought. They present the principles both as rules for economic work and as a scientific methodology for high-quality development and Chinese modernization.

The article devotes one section to each of the five relationships: an effective market and a capable government; aggregate supply and aggregate demand; fostering new drivers of growth and updating old ones; improving the incremental and reviving the stock; and raising quality and expanding total quantity. Each section follows a similar pattern. It cites Xi Jinping and recent Party documents, including the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), gives illustrative data, and then lists the measures announced at the 2024 conference.

The central claim is that each pair is a unity of opposites that must be handled dialectically rather than by choosing one side. On market and government, the authors say the market allocates resources most efficiently but cannot do everything, so the state must correct market failure, under Party leadership and the socialist system. On supply and demand, they say policy emphasis should follow shifts in the principal contradiction and its main aspect. They cite the stimulus package of September 2024 as a response to weak domestic demand. On new and old drivers, they reject treating new quality productive forces as a replacement for traditional industry. For quality and quantity, they invoke the law of the transformation of quantity into quality. They cite figures such as 18.9 million registered business entities in 2024 and new-energy vehicle output rising from 18,000 in 2013 to over 13 million in 2024.

The authors conclude that the five relationships reveal the basic law of using a systems approach in economic work. They also supply tools for what they call a well-sung "economic chorus", offer guidance for macroeconomic governance, and form an innovation in contemporary Chinese Marxist political economy. They call for long-term adherence to the principles and stress the Party's overall leadership, especially the centralised and unified leadership of the Central Committee, amid greater external pressure and domestic difficulty. Read the original if you want a close view of how official commentary explains and justifies the economic policy framework adopted at the end of 2024.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces does not mean neglecting or abandoning traditional industries. Nor does fostering new drivers of growth mean rejecting or eliminating the old ones.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力，不是忽视、放弃传统产业。培育新动能，也不是排斥、消灭旧动能。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, such as digital technology, AI and green industries.
The official economic goal since about 2017, which prioritises efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An annual meeting held in December where the Party leadership sets the economic priorities and policy tone for the coming year.
The official body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping, treated as part of Xi Jinping Thought and as guidance for economic work.

t: Major institutional achievements of comprehensively deepening reform in the new era
zh: 新时代全面深化改革的重大制度成果
paras: Chen Jinlong and Wu Zhinan ask what institutional results the Party's drive to comprehensively deepen reform has produced since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and what these results suggest for the next stage. Their thesis is that the main outcome is institutional: a more mature and settled system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, whose advantages should now be converted into governance effectiveness. The article first appeared in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao), 2025, no. 1.

The article opens with Xi Jinping's remark that institution-building now carries greater weight in reform. It then sets out four headings: the steady improvement of the institutional system, the full display of institutional advantages, the rising authority of institutions, and the accumulated experience of institution-building. The first section follows the three tiers of the system: fundamental, basic and important institutions.

The authors argue that reform has consolidated the fundamental institutions, such as the Party's overall leadership and the people's congress system. It has also improved the basic institutions, including multiparty cooperation, regional ethnic autonomy, public ownership as the mainstay and the socialist market economy. Finally, it has innovated in the important institutions, including the legal system, administration, social security, ecological protection and supervision. They identify three advantages: Party leadership, the primacy of the people and centralised unity. They also say institutional authority has risen through stronger institutional awareness, supervision of implementation and better governance results. As evidence they cite the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform, recurring Party education campaigns, the supervision regulations, poverty alleviation and the response to COVID-19. Whole-process people's democracy is presented as the channel for popular participation.

The authors draw four lessons for further reform. These are to keep institution-building as the main thread, to unite upholding fundamental principles with innovation, to combine top-level design with grassroots exploration, and to treat breaking down and building up as a dialectical unity, building first and breaking afterwards. They call for reform to proceed steadily and firmly toward the goals set by the Party Central Committee. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party scholars classify China's institutional system and describe the lessons of a decade of reform.
quoteEn: The vitality of institutions lies in their implementation.
quoteZh: 制度的生命力在于执行。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2019. It holds that democracy covers every stage of political life, including elections, consultation, decision-making, management and supervision.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's guiding model since the reform era, combining Party leadership, a socialist market economy and the people's congress system.
The reform agenda launched at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013). It covers the economy, politics, culture, society, ecology and Party-building.

glossary.zh: 根本制度、基本制度、重要制度
glossary.pinyin: gēnběn zhìdù, jīběn zhìdù, zhòngyào zhìdù
glossary.explanation: The official three-tier classification of China's socialist institutional system. The fundamental tier covers the Party's leadership and the people's congress system. The basic tier covers economic and political arrangements such as public ownership and ethnic regional autonomy. The important tier covers more specific systems derived from the first two.

t: Implementing reform with a nail-driving spirit
zh: 以钉钉子精神抓好改革落实
paras: Written in the wake of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and the Central Economic Work Conference of December 2024, this commentary asks how the Party's plan for further deepening reform can be turned into results. Wu answers that the "nail-driving spirit" (钉钉子精神), a style of work stressing hard-nosed, persistent implementation, must guide every stage of carrying out reform. The piece first appeared in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao), 2024, no. 24.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the spirit is needed: it is presented as a fine Party tradition, a key to the achievements of the new era, and a practical necessity for the current round of reform. The second sets out its core meaning under three headings: a correct view of political achievements, a correct methodology, and the handling of several major relationships. The third turns to practice and names three requirements: serving the people wholeheartedly, being truth-seeking and pragmatic, and having the courage to take responsibility.

Wu leans heavily on Xi Jinping's image of hammering a nail: one or two blows leave it loose, and only seven or eight make it firm. On this basis Wu argues that implementation matters as much as design, citing the saying "one part planning, nine parts implementation". The Plenum set more than 300 major reform measures, to be completed by 2029, and the article treats this tight schedule as grounds for stronger follow-through. Wu calls for a correct view of political achievements, in which benefiting the people counts for most, and for guarding against formalism and vanity projects. Wu also calls for responsibility chains with accountability, field investigation, and balance between reform and the rule of law, breaking down and building up, reform and opening up, and deployment and implementation.

Wu concludes that cadres, above all leading ones as the "key minority", must carry reform through step by step, test it by tangible results and public satisfaction, and reject "lying-flat" attitudes. Wu presents this as essential to advancing Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a representative statement of how Party-aligned writers frame cadre responsibility and implementation after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee.
quoteEn: To carry out reform it is necessary to drive the nail in deep and fast, not by brute force or random hammering, but by implementing in light of actual conditions and local circumstances.
quoteZh: 抓好改革要“钉进钉深钉牢固”,不能只凭蛮力、胡打乱敲,而是要结合实际、因地制宜地抓落实

glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping uses for patient, repeated and thorough implementation of policy, likening it to hammering a nail until it holds. It is often invoked in campaigns against formalism.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
Official phrase for leading cadres, whose conduct is held to shape how policy is carried out and what example is set.
In Party discourse, going through the motions with slogans, meetings and paperwork, or staging showcase projects, instead of achieving real results.

t: Coordinating aggregate supply and aggregate demand to further unblock the circulation of the national economy
zh: 统筹好总供给和总需求关系 进一步畅通国民经济循环
paras: Xie Di's commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscripts, takes up the instruction of the Central Economic Work Conference of December 2024 to "coordinate the relationship between aggregate supply and aggregate demand and keep the national economy's circulation unobstructed". Xie presents this as Xi Jinping's summary of the laws of China's economic development in the new era. The article argues that planning supply and demand together is more than top-level design for one year's economic work: it also marks a refinement of the concept of macroeconomic governance, and matters for high-quality development.

The piece has four numbered sections. The first sets out the theory of aggregate supply and demand, covering aggregate and structural balance, the dialectic of supply and demand, and Xi's theories since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second deals with short-term and long-term macroeconomic regulation. The third discusses expanding domestic demand and unblocking the economic cycle, with consumption and investment data for 2023 and 2024. The fourth sets out the demand-side and supply-side policy tools, tying them to the 2024 Conference's measures.

Xie argues that under the socialist market economy the contradiction between private and social labour persists, so balance between aggregate supply and demand is occasional and temporary, while imbalance is normal. Citing Xi, Xie holds that China has cyclical and aggregate problems but that structural problems are the most prominent, so supply-side structural reform remains the main line. Xie also insists there is no way to "bypass the short term and go straight to the long term". Supply-side reform and the strategy of expanding domestic demand are therefore complementary, not substitutes, and should reach a higher-level dynamic equilibrium in which demand pulls supply and supply creates demand. Xie classes fiscal and monetary measures as demand-quantity management, income distribution as demand-structure management, and supply-side structural reform as supply-structure management.

Xie cites figures to show that room for expanding consumption and investment remains large. They include retail sales of consumer goods of over 47 trillion yuan in 2023, and a 16.1 per cent rise in equipment purchase investment in the first ten months of 2024. Xie concludes that a more proactive fiscal policy, moderately loose monetary policy, consumption-boosting measures and the supply-quality tasks set by the Conference together serve stable growth, employment and prices, and income growth in step with the economy. Read the original if you want an official-line economist's account of how Chinese policy framing links Marxist supply-demand balance with the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference agenda.
quoteEn: To discuss the supply side while abandoning the demand side, or the demand side while abandoning the supply side, is one-sided; the two are not an either-or relationship of substitution, but must work together and advance one another.
quoteZh: 放弃需求侧谈供给侧或放弃供给侧谈需求侧都是片面的，二者不是非此即彼、一去一存的替代关系，而是要相互配合、相互推进。

glossary.explanation: An economic policy line announced by Xi Jinping in 2015 that aims to improve the quality and efficiency of supply through structural adjustment, cutting excess capacity and deepening reform. It is described officially as the main line of economic work.
A long-standing policy line that stresses consumption and investment within China as the main driver of growth. It is treated as the strategic foundation of the "new development pattern".
An annual meeting, usually in December, of Party and state leaders that reviews the year's economy and sets the main economic tasks and policy direction for the next year.
The official goal of shifting from speed-driven growth towards growth emphasising quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability.

t: Digital technology as a booster of common prosperity in spiritual life
zh: 数字技术助推精神生活共同富裕
paras: This short commentary from Beijing Daily asks how digital technology can help realise common prosperity in spiritual life, which the authors treat as an integral part of Chinese modernization. Starting from Xi Jinping's statement that common prosperity means abundance in both material and spiritual life, Tang and Shi argue that generative AI and related technologies are accelerating this goal. They also acknowledge that the same technologies carry risks that could widen spiritual inequality.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why digital technology has an inherent capacity to enrich spiritual life. The second traces the Chinese Communist Party's commitment to spiritual abundance from the revolutionary base areas through the People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the new era. The third lists challenges and offers five policy recommendations.

On the first point, the authors take the practical logic of spiritual common prosperity to be "spiritual need, spiritual production, spiritual enjoyment", drawing on Marxist views of spiritual life and on Maslow's hierarchy of needs. They contend that digital technology is efficient, interconnected and decentralised, breaks down household-registration, regional and work-unit boundaries, and gives different groups more equal access to knowledge. Immersive technologies, in their account, extend the human body and mind ("the extension of humans" and "extended humans") and bring new spiritual satisfaction. They also name risks: imbalance between supply and demand of spiritual products, widening divisions, information overload, algorithmic bias and privacy leaks.

The authors propose that governments should: expand digital infrastructure and digital literacy training in less developed areas; set legal and ethical rules for algorithms, privacy and automated decisions; build occupational safety nets and retraining for workers displaced by automation; regulate recommendation algorithms to curb information overload and homogenised content; and strengthen safeguards in critical sectors such as health, finance and transport. They present this as a way to raise people's sense of fulfilment, happiness and security and support free and all-round human development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link AI and digital technology to the discourse of common prosperity and spiritual life, and a list of their policy suggestions.
quoteEn: "Spiritual need, spiritual production, spiritual enjoyment" is the practical logic of common prosperity in spiritual life, while "need, satisfaction, new need, renewed satisfaction" is the driving force of its development.
quoteZh: “精神需要—精神生产—精神享受”是精神生活共同富裕的实践逻辑，而“需要—满足—新需要—再满足”是精神生活发展的动力。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal that the Party leadership has stressed since the early 2020s, referring to prosperity shared by all people rather than a few. Official texts define it as covering both material and spiritual life.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out prominently in the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and presented as distinct from Western models.

The idea that cultural, intellectual and moral enrichment should be broadly shared among all people, as a counterpart to material common prosperity. The article notes that it has no settled definition.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Turning the long-term positive fundamentals into high-quality development outcomes
zh: 将长期向好基本面化为高质量发展成果
source: Jiefang Daily, 11 February 2024 (as stated in the source metadata)
paras: Hu Zhihao's newspaper commentary asks how China can convert the economy's long-term positive fundamentals into concrete high-quality development, given entrenched problems and short-term shocks. Hu argues that the underlying conditions have not changed, and that policymakers should set priorities, treat symptoms and causes together, and guide expectations sensibly.

The piece is organised under three headings: attention to nominal growth, effective use of policy tools, and reviving consumption as the lead driver. It draws on the 14th Five-Year Plan and the 2035 goals, official policy language on fiscal and monetary stance, and data on consumption shares and household wealth.

Hu contends that sustained nominal growth, meaning real growth plus mild inflation, steadies expectations and supports the renminbi exchange rate. Cost-push or runaway inflation would not be sustainable, so demand stimulus must go with high-quality supply and new quality productive forces. Hu says loose monetary policy alone cannot lift weak aggregate demand, so fiscal spending must create demand directly, with the financial sector helping through bond issuance and central bank purchases of government bonds.

On consumption, Hu notes that household consumption is close to 40% of GDP, well below the US, Japan and South Korea. Hu calls for stable income expectations, better income distribution, a fuller social security net, steadier asset prices (given household wealth of 482 trillion yuan net) and a larger household share of national income. Read the original if you want a brief, official-leaning economist's reading of China's 2025 macroeconomic policy mix and its consumption rationale.
quoteEn: Grasping consumption to drive aggregate demand is, it should be said, taking hold of the ox by the nose.
quoteZh: 抓住消费来拉动总需求，应该说是牵住了牛鼻子。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 that stresses innovation-driven, technology-led productivity as the basis of high-quality development.

t: Coordinating the advance of new urbanization and comprehensive rural revitalization
zh: 统筹推进新型城镇化和乡村全面振兴
paras: This newspaper commentary from Guangming Daily asks what it means in practice to "coordinate the advance" of new urbanization and comprehensive rural revitalization. Gao Fan argues that urban-rural integration is an inherent requirement of Chinese modernization, and that the pace of change in urban-rural structure determines how far modernization as a whole advances. The article takes its cue from the Central Economic Work Conference of 2024 and the No. 1 Central Document of 2025.

Gao sets out six dimensions of coordination: industrial layout, factor allocation, spatial planning, the provision of public goods, the way development is evaluated, and the reform of institutions and mechanisms. Each is presented as a separate task, with specific policy measures attached.

On industry, Gao argues that the old split, with farming in the countryside and manufacturing and services in cities, must give way to joint planning. Agriculture should draw in urban factors and technology, and rural resources should become new industries and markets. On factors, land, labour and capital should move in both directions through market-oriented reform, including the "three rights separation" of rural land, and through digital tools. On space, Gao calls for a shift from a sharp urban-rural divide to a blended pattern, with county seats and central towns as the "continuum" linking city and village.

For public goods, Gao urges more fiscal support for rural education, healthcare and old-age care, and faster citizenship for migrants from the countryside. Evaluation should give more weight to rural and integration indicators in local government appraisal, and the article ties this to protecting farmland and grain farmers. Gao concludes that single reforms have limited effect and that household registration, land and social security reforms must work together. Read the original if you want a concise outline of the policy agenda behind urban-rural integration as presented by an economist writing in the Party press.
quoteEn: Coordinating the advance of new urbanization and comprehensive rural revitalization is a systematic undertaking.
quoteZh: 统筹推进新型城镇化和乡村全面振兴是一项系统工程

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official policy line on urbanization that stresses people-centred development, including granting urban residency and services to rural migrants, rather than simple expansion of cities.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to develop rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards.
A rural land reform that separates ownership by the collective, contracting rights of households and operating rights, so that operating rights can be transferred.

t: Leading with innovation to promote high-quality development of the private economy
zh: 以创新为引领促进民营经济高质量发展
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's call at the symposium on private enterprises for private firms to pursue high-quality development, focus on their main business and strengthen independent innovation. Zhang Jin argues that the private economy has been an important innovative force since reform and opening up. The author holds that improved policy, market and talent conditions, together with further policy implementation, will let it contribute more to new quality productive forces.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews private enterprises' achievements in innovation. The second sets out the favourable conditions for their innovative development. The third lists the policy measures that Zhang says should be carried out.

On achievements, Zhang cites private firms becoming China's largest foreign-trade players from 2019, with exports of electric vehicles, 3D printers and industrial robots rising 13.1%, 32.8% and 45.2% year on year. The author also says these firms are moving China from innovation "follower" to "leader" and are a key force in artificial intelligence, big data, new energy and biomedicine. As favourable conditions, Zhang names policy support since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the 2023 Central Committee and State Council opinion on private-economy growth. Further conditions are a domestic market with over 400 million middle-income people, a talent pool in which the "demographic dividend" is turning into a "talent dividend", and entrepreneurial spirit.

Zhang calls for removing barriers to market access and factor use, and for supporting private firms in taking on major national science and technology projects. The author also urges easing financing difficulties through market-based risk-sharing and credit systems, and strengthening the application of results and intellectual property protection. Zhang presents these steps as helping private enterprises contribute to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise official-line statement of how Party-aligned economists frame private-sector innovation policy in early 2025.
quoteEn: The "demographic dividend" is accelerating its conversion into a "talent dividend".
quoteZh: “人口红利”正在加快向“人才红利”转化。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productivity growth driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging industries rather than traditional resource-heavy growth.
An official goal since about 2017 that emphasises efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
The Party's official formula for China's path to modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world begun in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, within which the private sector re-emerged.

t: Combining the boosting of consumption with higher investment returns
zh: 实现提振消费与提高投资效益的有效结合
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2025, Huang Kainan takes up the first task set by the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference: vigorously boosting consumption, improving investment returns and expanding domestic demand across the board. Huang argues that insufficient domestic demand is the main current difficulty of the economy, and that consumption and investment should be pursued together. Doing so would, in this account, create a virtuous circle and a high-level dynamic balance between supply and demand.

The short commentary begins with a technical clarification of how consumption and investment are credited with contributing to GDP. It then has two main sections: how consumption depends on investment returns, and how investment returns should be guided by consumption. It closes on the roles of market and government.

Huang notes that the expenditure method, behind the 'three engines' of growth, overstates the contribution of consumption and investment and understates that of exports. Imported goods are deducted only under net exports, and exports now carry more domestic value added, with general trade above 64%. Hence Huang calls for both stronger exports and greater efforts on domestic demand. Boosting consumption, whether by raising income or by borrowing, needs investment returns as its support; in Huang's phrase, consumption is past investment and investment is future consumption. Raising wage income means raising the 'cooperative surplus' of labour and capital and the labour share in primary distribution. In turn, investment should avoid blind, duplicated and low-efficiency projects, which Huang links to curbing 'involutionary' competition. It should target infrastructure, upgrading consumption and equipment renewal, with reforms to investment evaluation and fiscal-financial coordination.

Huang concludes that the market should play the decisive role in allocating resources while an 'effective government' uses fiscal and monetary policy. Fiscal, monetary, industrial and competition policies should work together to expand demand and improve the supply structure. Read the original if you want a concise official-economist account of the 2025 domestic demand agenda and its reasoning on the consumption–investment link.
quoteEn: Seen from this angle, consumption is past investment, and investment is future consumption.
quoteZh: 从这个角度讲，消费是过去的投资，投资是未来的消费。

glossary.explanation: An annual meeting of Party and state leaders, held at the end of the year, that sets economic priorities for the coming year.
A phrase used in Chinese economic discourse for an active state that works alongside the market, often paired with 'an efficient market'.
Describes intense, low-return competition, such as price wars and duplicated capacity, that consumes resources without raising overall output or quality.

t: The idea of "harmony and union" (hehe) in the Book of Changes as part of China's fine traditional culture
zh: 中华优秀传统文化中的《周易》“和合”思想
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (26 February 2025), Shi Shaobo argues that the Zhouyi (Book of Changes), first of the Confucian Five Classics, takes "harmony and union" (hehe) as its core value. Shi holds that the idea, especially in the themes of heaven–earth union and water–fire complementarity, has shaped Chinese thought for millennia and deserves deeper study.

The short commentary opens with the terminology of the Yijing and Yizhuan, then traces the characters he and he and the compound hehe through early texts such as the Guoyu, Mozi and Shiji. It then follows the Zhouyi's treatment of harmony at four levels: humans and nature, between people (extended to society and states), and within the self.

Shi reads the hexagram structure as a model of hehe: the 64 hexagrams contain 192 yang and 192 yin lines, whose mutual opposition and interdependence drive constant change. On this basis the author finds in the text a call to cherish nature while using human initiative in accord with natural law. Harmony between people rests on benevolence, righteousness and good faith, as in the Tongren and Zhongfu hexagrams, and personal harmony on yin–yang balance, moral cultivation, prudent speech and the mean. Change, Shi stresses, leads to flourishing only when it is orderly and upright.

Shi concludes that if every person and country develops uprightly, the Zhouyi's ideal of \"preserving supreme harmony\" and peace for all states can be reached. The piece presents the text as a resource for harmony with nature, society and oneself. Read the original if you want a brief introduction to how a contemporary Chinese scholar presents the Book of Changes' hehe idea as a traditional cultural value.
quoteEn: The Zhouyi highlights harmony between humans and nature.
quoteZh: 《周易》凸显了人与自然之间的和谐。

glossary.explanation: A traditional Chinese concept of different or opposed things coexisting, coordinating and developing together. Contemporary writers often cite it as a core value of Chinese culture.
An ancient divination and philosophical classic, comprising the Yijing text and the Yizhuan commentaries. It is traditionally ranked first among the Confucian classics.
The five core texts of the Confucian canon: the Book of Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites and Spring and Autumn Annals.

t: Forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation as the guide to high-quality development in ethnic minority areas
zh: 中华民族共同体意识引领民族地区高质量发展
paras: Li Junjie, writing in the China Social Sciences Today on 26 February 2025, asks how high-quality development can be achieved in ethnic minority areas. The answer given is that development there should be guided by forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, oriented towards increasing commonalities, and driven by new quality productive forces. Li presents this as both a necessary road to building a modern socialist country and an important task of building the Chinese national community.

The article has four parts. It first sets out why forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation is the main line of ethnic work. It then explains why high-quality development in ethnic areas needs new quality productive forces. Next it examines how the two innovations relate in theory and logic. Finally it proposes four paths for promoting development in ethnic areas.

Li's central move is to treat the two concepts as complementary. In Li's account, new quality productive forces are the material base and basic support for forging the community consciousness, while that consciousness supplies the spiritual impetus and value orientation for those forces. Li frames this as a relationship between matter and consciousness and between economic base and superstructure. Technological, organisational, industrial and cultural innovation are said to narrow regional gaps, widen channels of exchange and strengthen identification with the Chinese nation. Li lists problems in ethnic areas, including narrow industrial structures, weak innovation capacity and uneven development, and argues that new quality productive forces can serve as a new engine for addressing them. The two are also said to share the aim of national rejuvenation and the realisation of Chinese modernization in ethnic areas.

Li proposes four paths: upholding Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee; pursuing common prosperity as the goal, through rural revitalisation, infrastructure, fiscal transfers and targeted programmes; promoting exchanges, interaction and integration among ethnic groups, including mixed residential and community structures; and making Chinese modernization the central task. Li calls for linking improvements in people's livelihoods with building cohesion. Read the original if you want an official-line statement of how ethnic policy and economic development goals are being tied together, including the list of specific policy programmes.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces is the material foundation and basic support for forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation, while forging that sense is the spiritual impetus and value orientation of new quality productive forces.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力是铸牢中华民族共同体意识的物质基础和基本支撑，铸牢中华民族共同体意识是新质生产力的精神动力和价值导向。

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: forge firm consciousness of the Chinese national community
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the main line of Party ethnic work since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing a shared national identity across all ethnic groups. It was written into Party documents in 2017.

A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading, with higher total factor productivity as its hallmark.
An official goal of shared wealth for all, described as an essential requirement of socialism and a feature of Chinese modernization.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernity, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022), with features such as huge population scale, common prosperity and peaceful development.

glossary.en: exchanges, interaction and integration among ethnic groups
glossary.explanation: An official formula for the processes by which ethnic groups are meant to come closer together, used as a policy aim in ethnic work.

keywords: community consciousness of the Chinese nation

t: Leveraging the advantages of a super-large market to strengthen industrial and supply chain resilience
zh: 发挥超大规模市场优势 提升产业链供应链韧性
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 25 February 2025
paras: Yang and Li take up how China can use the scale of its domestic market to make its industrial and supply chains more resilient. They note that, despite growing competitiveness, China still faces anti-globalisation sentiment, geopolitical conflict and technology blockades, and that dependence on others for key technologies has not fundamentally changed. Their answer is that the super-large market is a structural advantage that can be turned into resilience through targeted policy.

The short commentary first sets out three channels through which market scale supports resilience, then offers three sets of policy measures. It opens with a statement by Xi Jinping on China's complete industrial system and its large domestic demand, and it closes with a note that the work is part of a National Social Science Fund project.

On the mechanisms, the authors argue that scale raises the expected returns of innovation, widens application scenarios and spreads R&D costs, which helps fill gaps in chains. Scale economies lower costs and encourage industrial clusters, which strengthens chains. A large market can also sustain a full industrial system; the authors say China is the only country with every industrial category in the UN classification, which they describe as an internal stabiliser in emergencies. To exploit these effects they call for expanding domestic demand through income distribution reform, a larger middle-income group and better investment quality. They also urge a modern circulation system of logistics and rural delivery networks, and a unified national market with fewer regional barriers, market-based factor allocation, stronger property rights and a better business environment.

The authors conclude that the super-large market already plays a prominent supporting role but needs these further measures to be fully effective. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the policy logic linking domestic market scale, innovation and supply chain security in Chinese economic discourse in early 2025.
quoteEn: A super-large market helps make full use of scale economies to raise productive efficiency, cut production costs and strengthen the core competitiveness of industrial and supply chains.
quoteZh: 超大规模市场有助于充分利用规模经济效应以提升生产效率、降低生产成本，强化产业链供应链核心竞争力。

glossary.explanation: A policy aim to remove regional protectionism and barriers so that goods, capital and labour move freely across China.

t: Accelerating the construction of China's industrial chain policy system
zh: 加快构建我国产业链政策体系
paras: Yu Rongjian and Cen Jie take up a gap in Chinese economic policy: policies exist for industries and for individual firms, but there is no policy category aimed specifically at the industrial chain. Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (25 February 2025), they argue that building the new development pattern, securing industrial and supply chains and gaining new advantages in international competition all require a complete, forward-looking and precisely implemented industrial chain policy system. They propose building it around five aims: safeguarding security, promoting innovation, raising efficiency, expanding openness and improving governance.

The commentary first sets out two background conditions, then the five focal points, then three supporting mechanisms. The background covers weaknesses in China's own chains and the measures taken by developed countries. The five focal points each receive a short list of concrete tasks. The closing section turns to institutional safeguards for the policy system itself.

On the background, the authors say China's chains show bottleneck ("chokehold") technologies, weak lead firms, poor upstream–downstream links and no backups for key links, while existing policies are fragmented across departments ("nine dragons controlling the water"). They point to US measures such as Section 301, Section 337, the 2018 export control law and the Wassenaar Arrangement, and to US and Japanese reshoring subsidies from 2020. Their five-part programme includes security measures (strengthening strengths, filling gaps, firming links, building resilience and barriers), innovation policy aimed at domestic demand, self-reliance in technology and digital-intelligent upgrading, and efficiency, openness and governance measures. On governance, they call for a three-tier "chain leader system" (链长制) under national, regional and grassroots leaders, extended to cover innovation chains, and for AI-based platforms for chain management.

For implementation the authors call for a national industrial chain leading group and pilot programmes in sectors such as chips and high-end equipment. They also want wider participation by firms, associations and think tanks in policy-making, performance management with dynamic adjustment, and a monitoring centre producing security, innovation, credit and governance indices. Their stated aim is an autonomous, controllable and secure industrial chain and the modernization of China's industrial chains. Read the original if you want a compact checklist of the policy measures that two Chinese business-school scholars propose for industrial chain security, innovation and governance.
quoteEn: It is necessary to speed up building China's industrial chain policy system along five dimensions — safeguarding security, promoting innovation, raising efficiency, expanding openness and improving governance — so as to build an autonomous, controllable, secure and reliable industrial chain and advance its modernization.
quoteZh: 有必要从“保安全，促创新，提效率，扩开放，优治理”五个方面加快构建我国产业链政策体系，构建自主可控、安全可靠的产业链，推动我国产业链现代化发展。

glossary.explanation: A strategy announced in 2020 that centres on the domestic market ("dual circulation") while remaining open to international trade and investment.
A governance arrangement in which a named official or leader coordinates a specific industrial chain, solving problems across firms and localities. It has been tried in several Chinese provinces.
Common Chinese expression for key technologies, components or resources that China depends on foreign suppliers for and that can be cut off.
A policy goal of upgrading industrial chains to be more advanced, secure and controllable, widely used in official economic discourse.

t: Cultural prosperity as an important hallmark of Chinese modernization
zh: 文化繁荣是中国式现代化的重要标识
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper in February 2025, Luo Sihai takes up the Party's 2024 decision on further deepening reform, which names the building of a strong socialist culture and the promotion of cultural prosperity as key reform goals. Luo argues that cultural prosperity is an important hallmark of Chinese modernization. In Luo's view, achieving it requires guidance from Xi Jinping's thought on culture, and it must keep to the distinctively 'Chinese' line of modernization.

The commentary is organised in four parts. The first sets out the guiding role of Xi Jinping's thought on culture. The remaining three discuss practical tasks: strengthening cultural confidence, strengthening cultural innovation and expanding cultural influence. Luo draws on the Decision and on Xi Jinping's remarks throughout, and cites Marx's 1845 notion of 'mental production' from The Holy Family.

Luo argues that Chinese modernization pursues material and cultural-ethical advancement together, so that without socialist cultural prosperity there can be no socialist modernization. Cultural confidence, in Luo's account, calls for embedding core socialist values in law, institutions and everyday moral norms, and for building an independent Chinese system of philosophy and social science under Party leadership. Cultural innovation rests on cultivating innovative talent and on meeting the public's varied spiritual and cultural needs, which Luo describes as lagging behind material development. Expanding influence means raising national soft power by summarising 'Chinese experience' with 'Chinese reasoning', and strengthening international discourse power through vivid storytelling and digital and intelligent communication. Luo cites TikTok travel content as an example of how overseas audiences form images of China.

Luo concludes that the Chinese modernization process should fuse modernization with socialist culture with Chinese characteristics, through these combined efforts. Culture is presented as the spiritual support for national rejuvenation and for a world facing great changes. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated academics link cultural policy, ideology and international communication to the post-2024 reform agenda.
quoteEn: Cultural prosperity and flourishing is an important hallmark of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 文化繁荣兴盛是中国式现代化的重要标识。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of development, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses coordinated material and cultural-ethical progress, among other features.

The cultural component of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, formally presented in 2023. It addresses cultural work and the building of a strong socialist culture.
A Party slogan for confidence in China's traditional, revolutionary and socialist culture. It is treated as a basis for the Four-sphere Confidence.
A set of 24 characters in 12 values at the national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
The capacity to shape narratives and be heard in global communication. The term is common in Chinese policy writing on external publicity.

t: The "historical consciousness" of the Chinese nation
zh: 中华民族的“历史意识”
paras: Lin Guobiao asks what historical consciousness is, what distinguishes the one found in the Chinese nation, and what practical use it has. The article, a newspaper essay in Guangming Daily (February 2025), argues that Chinese historical consciousness stresses continuity and the transmission of historical culture, and that cultivating it can strengthen several modes of thinking used in present-day governance. Lin presents understanding it as important for the continuation and renewal of Chinese civilisation.

The essay has three parts. The first defines historical consciousness as people's memory, reflection and evaluation of their own development, drawing on Nietzsche, Jörn Rüsen, the Japanese scholar Kawakatsu Yoshio and the Australian historian Greg Dening. The second sets out the features of the Chinese variant, citing Xi Jinping's remark that valuing, studying and drawing on history is a fine tradition of the Chinese nation. The third lists eight kinds of thinking capacity that historical consciousness is said to improve.

In Lin's account, historical consciousness always has a contemporary orientation: it interprets the past from present concerns and gives actions meaning and direction. Chinese historical consciousness is described as deep, connecting past, present and future, and practical. Lin finds three distinguishing commitments: combining "historical reason" with historical experience (including the tradition of taking the ancient kings as models); a seek-truth-from-facts view that presents history as it was; and an "organic" view that stresses the interconnection and continuity of events. These traits are then said to turn into methods of thought.

Lin links the traits to strategic, historical, dialectical, systems, innovative, rule-of-law and bottom-line thinking. For example, the organic view is tied to systems thinking, the tradition of "learning from Yin's downfall" (yinjian) to bottom-line thinking, and the pursuit of "the way of governance" to rule-of-law thinking. Lin concludes that cultivating historical consciousness helps people judge things within the continuity of history and solve current problems. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar ties a nation-specific concept of historical consciousness to official discourse on thinking methods.
quoteEn: The contemporary character of historical consciousness determines that its meaning and function point towards contemporary practice.
quoteZh: 历史意识的当代性决定了历史意识的意义和功能是指向当代实践的。

t: Strengthening expectation management to raise the overall effectiveness of policy
zh: 加强预期管理 提高政策整体效能
paras: This newspaper commentary takes up the instruction of the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference to strengthen expectation management and to advance policy implementation and expectation guidance together. Lin and Wang argue that managing expectations, mainly through information dissemination that acts on the psychology of economic actors, reduces expectation bias and turns favourable social expectations into orderly, rational economic behaviour. In their view this is important for improving the macroeconomic governance system and raising its capacity.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why expectation management matters more and more. The second describes its main content and requirements. The third proposes how to improve the mechanisms for expectation management, a task the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) named when it called for improving macroeconomic governance.

On importance, the authors give three reasons. Expectation management helps to create policy synergy for high-quality development, because broader goals and a wider range of policy tools risk what they call fallacies of composition or decomposition. It is a precondition for deepening reform, since reform adjusts interests and needs guidance of public opinion. It is also a key measure against the difficulties the economy faces, and the authors trace how successive Central Economic Work Conferences from 2021 to 2024 put stabilising expectations first. On content, they stress government credibility, stable consumption and investment expectations, and better expectations among firms, especially private and small and micro enterprises, alongside deepening state-owned enterprise reform. On mechanisms, they propose four improvements. These are a policy system linked to development plans, with a richer toolbox and better coordination between departments. They also want more quantified and composite indicators, such as confidence indices. They add regular tracking and communication, with transparent policy explanation and use of mainstream media, and early-warning and risk-identification mechanisms covering inflation and deflation expectations and financial markets.

The authors conclude that building these mechanisms is the central task if expectations are to move towards policy goals and if macroeconomic policy is to support high-quality development. They treat expectation management as part of the modernisation of national governance. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Chinese economists frame expectation management as a macroeconomic governance tool and what institutional measures they propose.
quoteEn: Expectation management works mainly through the spread of information on the psychological level of economic actors. It can effectively reduce expectation bias, turn favourable social expectations into orderly and rational economic behaviour, and so build strong confidence and momentum for high-quality development.
quoteZh: 预期管理主要通过信息传播作用于经济主体的心理层面，能够有效减少预期偏差，使良好的社会预期转化为有序、理性的经济行为，进而形成推动高质量发展的强大信心和动力。

glossary.explanation: Government efforts to guide and stabilise public and market expectations through policy explanation, information disclosure and press briefings. It is treated as part of macroeconomic governance.
An official goal, prominent since 2017, that stresses the quality, efficiency and sustainability of growth rather than speed alone.
An annual meeting of the Party and state leadership, usually in December, that reviews the economy and sets economic policy priorities for the coming year.
The official term for the state's overall management of the macroeconomy. It goes beyond conventional macroeconomic regulation to include development, coordination and fairness goals.

t: Playing a "quartet" to continue the historical cultural lineage and spread Chinese culture
zh: 弹好赓续历史文脉传播中华文化的“四重奏”
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the 17th collective study session of the Political Bureau (28 October 2024) on building a cultural powerhouse. Zhang and Zhu argue that two tasks must be pursued together: protecting and passing on cultural heritage so that the historical cultural lineage continues, and using that heritage as a vehicle for communicating Chinese culture abroad. They present the work as a four-part "quartet".

The piece is organised into four sections, each with a musical metaphor: a "song blending past and present" on integrating heritage into daily life, research and management; a "digital empowerment" section on protection, exhibition and storytelling; a "link between China and abroad" section on translation and self-presentation; and an "external communication symphony" on inclusiveness and integration. Examples include the Great Wall village of Shixia, the digital Dunhuang, Palace Museum, Great Wall and Sanxingdui projects, and a China–France exhibition on the Forbidden City and Versailles.

On the domestic side, the authors call for linking tradition to everyday life and tourism, for coordinated research on archaeology, intangible heritage and minority histories (in order to strengthen a sense of community of the Chinese nation), and for a management system built on censuses, a national database and a "protection first" principle. They argue that digital tools can restore damaged texts, create immersive virtual exhibitions that also reduce visitor damage, and renew narrative by combining grand and individual stories. On the international side, they propose a national translation capacity, key shared concepts and expressions that carry a Chinese style, and communication that starts from shared historical memory with other countries.

Zhang and Zhu also call for a multi-channel communication pattern: inviting foreign journalists to sites such as Liangzhu, Erlitou and Yinxu, dialogue with Western media and scholars, a focus on social media platforms, and tailored strategies for each country. They state that this should present Chinese modernization, the Chinese path and Chinese ideas, and promote understanding of them abroad.
