Read the original if you want an example of how Party-aligned academics translate the cultural-powerhouse agenda into concrete policies on heritage, digital technology and international communication.
quoteEn: We must grasp the trend towards mobile, social and visual international communication, make new media the focus of building external discourse carriers, and combine "building our own ships to go to sea" with "borrowing ships to go to sea".
quoteZh: 要把握国际传播领域移动化、社交化、可视化的趋势，把新兴媒体作为对外话语载体建设的重点，将“造船出海”“借船出海”相结合。

glossary.explanation: A strategic goal, set out in Party documents, of building China into a country with strong cultural influence by 2035.

glossary.en: a sense of community of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: A Party concept stressing that all ethnic groups belong to one Chinese national community; it is used in policy on ethnic minorities.
The official name for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Opening a new realm of contemporary Chinese development
zh: 开辟中国当代发展新境界
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 February 2025
paras: This commentary is a Chinese translation of a piece by Gohi Bi Foua Claude Alain, an Ivorian associate professor at Panzhihua University, published in Chinese Social Sciences Today in February 2025. Writing as a foreign observer who has visited China several times, the author argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012), under Xi Jinping's leadership, China has opened a new realm of development. The author presents this as a record of achievement that is also a source of lessons for other developing countries, Africa in particular.

The article is organised under five headings. It first surveys China's changes in the new era in social, economic, cultural and diplomatic fields, drawing on the author's own impressions. It then takes up whole-process people's democracy, Chinese modernization, the relevance of China's model for African states, and Xi's global ideas, notably a community with a shared future for mankind. It closes with the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and the further deepening of reform.

Alain argues that no democratic model is universally valid and that whole-process people's democracy, rooted in Chinese conditions, produces social cohesion that the author contrasts with polarisation in Western societies. The author cites criticism of Francis Fukuyama's end-of-history thesis to claim that Western democracy is far from the best option. Chinese modernization is described as led by the Communist Party, people-centred, ecologically minded and peaceful, in contrast with Western expansionism and the policy shifts the author attributes to multiparty systems. For Africa, the author contends that China offers a feasible path, respects independence, and gives aid without political conditions, whereas US policy is said to focus on economic and military interests; Kenya is cited as a case of Belt and Road investment benefiting infrastructure and manufacturing.

The author concludes that China supports genuine multilateralism, contributes to tackling climate change and other global problems, and that its opening to the world will widen after the Third Plenum. Alain predicts that more partner countries will benefit and that Western attempts to contain China's rise will fail. Read the original if you want an example of how an African academic's favourable view of China is presented in Chinese official academic media, or if you are interested in the China–Africa comparisons it draws with US policy.
quoteEn: There is no absolutely universal model of democracy in the world.
quoteZh: 世界上没有绝对普适的民主模式。

glossary.explanation: A concept advanced by Xi Jinping from 2019 describing China's socialist democracy as covering every stage of political life, not only elections. Official sources present it as an alternative to Western electoral democracy.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, formally set out in 2022. Official sources stress that it differs from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13, calling for shared responses to global challenges and cooperation among states.

t: Improving the price mechanism for green and low-carbon development
zh: 完善绿色低碳发展价格机制
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 February 2025
paras: Writing in a newspaper commentary in February 2025, Liu Yaobin asks how prices can be made to carry the costs and value of green and low-carbon development. Liu defines green and low-carbon development pricing as a market mechanism through which prices reflect supply and demand, resource scarcity and the cost of green and low-carbon development. The author argues that it has two main components, ecological product prices and carbon pricing, and that improving it is a basic requirement of high-quality development and of building a modernization in which humanity and nature coexist in harmony.

The article first traces the policy lineage of the idea, from the resource and environmental price formation language of the 17th Party Congress (2007), through the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee and the 2018 and 2023 national ecological and environmental protection conferences, to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It then gives three reasons for the mechanism, sets out five measures for improving it, and closes with four relationships that must be handled correctly.

Liu argues that the mechanism deepens ecological civilization reform, is a key route for putting into practice the idea that “lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets”, and fits the building of a community with a shared future for mankind. Pricing ecological products is presented as a way to make their non-monetary value explicit, while the national carbon market is described as sending price signals and steering funds towards high-potential emitters. The proposed measures include market-based allocation of resource and environmental factors, clearer carbon asset property rights, a unified green certificate system, government-guided prices for ecological products affecting people's livelihood, multi-party price supervision, and revised price laws and monitoring systems.

The four relationships Liu names are: high-quality development and high-level protection; an efficient market and an effective government; unified openness and orderly competition; and external constraints and endogenous motivation. Liu concludes that handling each of these in a complementary, dialectical way is the practical premise, cognitive core, governing principle and objective requirement of a sound pricing mechanism. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese policy scholarship links carbon markets, ecological product value realisation and price reform.
quoteEn: Implementing a green and low-carbon development price mechanism is a key path for putting into practice the idea that “lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets”.
quoteZh: 实施绿色低碳发展价格机制是落实“绿水青山就是金山银山”理念的关键路径。

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A formulation associated with Xi Jinping from 2005, holding that ecological protection and economic prosperity are mutually reinforcing. It is a core idea of ecological civilization policy.
Policy concept referring to converting ecosystem services such as clean air, water and carbon sinks into economic value through pricing, trading or compensation.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's framework for international relations, stressing shared interests and joint global governance, here applied to climate action.
Official concept, written into Party and state documents, that places environmental protection within China's overall development strategy.

t: How Northeast China can accelerate the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 东北地区如何加快发展新质生产力
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, asks how China's northeast can speed up the development of new quality productive forces. Chang Qinglin argues that doing so is a necessary step in carrying out the strategy of comprehensively revitalising the northeast in the new era and in advancing Chinese modernization. The piece opens by citing Xi Jinping's 2023 and 2025 remarks in Harbin, Liaoning and Jilin, which it treats as a guide to action.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the region's foundations: Liaoning, Jilin, Heilongjiang and five eastern Inner Mongolia league-level cities, with about 110 million people. The second lists the obstacles. The third proposes five sets of measures.

On foundations, Chang points to the digital and intelligent upgrading of traditional industry and agriculture, growth in new energy, biomedicine and artificial intelligence, and strong universities and research bodies. On challenges, the author cites figures: the three provinces' 2023 R&D spending of 111.59 billion yuan equals 26.5 per cent of Jiangsu's, and R&D intensity of about 1.74 per cent is 65 per cent of the national average. Other problems named are a university patent conversion rate of around 10 per cent in Liaoning, local sourcing of only about 40 per cent of parts by central-government automotive firms, under 5 per cent of national high-tech enterprises, talent loss, and weak coordination. The proposed responses are to build innovation platforms and technology-transfer and science-finance systems, to offer special talent policies, and to reform ownership of職務 scientific results by giving researchers partial or full rights. They also include strengthening the "chain leader" role of central state-owned enterprises such as FAW and Harbin Electric, and building a regional investment coordination system. That system would rest on a Harbin–Changchun–Shenyang–Dalian axis, with a specialised role for each city.

Chang concludes that, by integrating technological and industrial innovation and improving policy supply, the northeast can turn scientific innovation from a "key variable" into a "strong increment" for revitalisation. The aim is a shift from scientific strength to industrial and economic strength. Read the original if you want a concise, policy-oriented account of how a Party-school scholar translates the new quality productive forces agenda into regional measures, with the author's statistics on northeastern R&D.
quoteEn: The northeast should pilot reforms that grant researchers ownership or long-term use rights over职务 scientific results, giving them partial or even full rights, so that results move down from institutions to individuals.
quoteZh: 应在东北地区先行先试推动科研人员职务科技成果所有权或长期使用权赋权改革，向科研人员“部分赋权”甚至“全部赋权”，实现科技成果从单位向个人下沉转移。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging and future industries.
The official name for the Party's model of national development, set out especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A leading firm, often a central state-owned enterprise, tasked with organising and coordinating the upstream and downstream firms in an industrial chain.

t: Accelerating a complete domestic demand system and expanding domestic demand in all respects
zh: 加快培育完整内需体系 全方位扩大国内需求
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how China should put into practice the strategic requirement, set out at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), to "accelerate the cultivation of a complete domestic demand system". Huang and Xue argue that expanding domestic demand in all respects is the necessary choice for sustaining the economic recovery. They point to the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference, which placed boosting consumption, raising investment returns and expanding domestic demand first among its nine tasks for 2025.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why expanding domestic demand matters. The second argues that there is wide room for it, drawing on 2024 statistics for GDP, retail sales, consumer spending and fixed-asset investment. The third lists policy measures centred on consumption and people's livelihood.

On the reasons, the authors contend that expanding demand underpins the new development pattern by smoothing the domestic economic cycle and reducing dependence on external markets. They also describe it as a long-term means of changing the development model, from factor-driven to innovation-driven, from investment-led to coordinated consumption and investment, and from reliance on external demand to domestic-demand leadership. It would also speed industrial upgrading. On room for growth, they cite four sources: a very large market (GDP of 134.9 trillion yuan in 2024, up 5%), a complete industrial system, a population of over 1.4 billion including more than 400 million middle-income earners, and coordinated urban–rural and regional development.

The proposed measures are to widen the "two news" policies (large-scale equipment renewal and trade-in of consumer goods) and expand service consumption. The authors also call for investment in priority areas with stronger assessment of returns, high-quality supply that creates new demand, coordinated fiscal and monetary policy, and higher household incomes backed by a stronger social security system. They present these as the way to turn the strategy into practice and promote high-quality development. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of the rationale and policy toolkit for boosting domestic demand in China's 2025 economic agenda.
quoteEn: Expanding domestic demand in all respects is in essence an active adjustment of the economic development model and a long-term measure for promoting high-quality economic development.
quoteZh: 全方位扩大国内需求实质上是对经济发展方式的主动调整，是推动经济高质量发展的长远之策。

glossary.explanation: A concept from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), covering upgraded consumption, optimised investment and a dynamic balance between supply and demand.
A strategy that treats the domestic cycle as the mainstay of the economy, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other. It was put forward by Xi Jinping in 2020.
The official goal for China's economy since 2017, stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
Policies promoting large-scale equipment renewal and trade-ins of consumer goods, backed by government funding to stimulate demand.

t: Technological and institutional innovation as twin drivers of the shift from old to new growth drivers
zh: 科技创新和制度创新双轮驱动新旧动能转换
paras: Writing in People's Daily in February 2025, Wang Yiming takes up a line from the Central Economic Work Conference: that China must coordinate the cultivation of new growth drivers with the renewal of old ones, and develop new quality productive forces in light of local conditions. Wang argues that the transition from old to new drivers can be made smooth and sequential only if technological innovation and institutional innovation work together as 'two wheels' turning at once. The piece presents this as guidance for high-quality development.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out how new and old drivers relate, using the property sector, the 'new three' exports (new-energy vehicles, lithium batteries, photovoltaics), heavy industry and shipbuilding as examples. The second argues that technological innovation is the key to the transition. The third argues that institutional innovation is the fundamental condition, covering the innovation ecosystem, science-and-technology finance and further reforms.

Wang contends that new and old drivers are dialectically linked and change over time, so old industries can be upgraded into new ones. The author cites figures: traditional industries account for about 80 per cent of industrial value added above designated size, while strategic emerging industries make up only about 13 per cent of GDP. The principle is therefore to build the new before breaking the old. On technology, Wang stresses original and disruptive innovation and the full chain from basic research to large-scale industrialisation, and names weak original capacity and poor commercialisation as shortcomings. On institutions, Wang says government should act selectively, shifting from direct allocation of resources to supplying rules and services. Strict intellectual property protection, fair competition and the decisive role of the market are described as the core of a good ecosystem. The author also criticises finance geared to short-term, collateral-based lending that does not suit technology firms.

Wang calls for patient and long-term capital, venture and angel funds, and a science-and-technology finance system. Wang also proposes reforms to the ownership of职务 research results, data and technology markets, research funding, enterprise-led innovation and talent evaluation. The overall aim is to let traditional industries, emerging industries and future industries each open new room for growth under high-quality development. Read the original if you want an official-economist view, published in the Party's main newspaper, of how the Central Economic Work Conference line on new and old growth drivers is being turned into policy priorities.
quoteEn: Practice has proved that the innovation ecosystem matters more than innovation resources.
quoteZh: 实践证明，创新生态比创新资源更重要。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and innovation rather than traditional resource-heavy growth.
The official economic goal since about 2017, which stresses efficiency, innovation and sustainability over growth speed alone.
The annual meeting of Party and state leaders, held at the end of the year, that sets the economic agenda for the following year.

t: China's economy leads the world to rethink the essence of development
st: Interview with Carles Brasó Broggi, professor of arts and humanities at the Open University of Catalonia, Spain
zh: 中国经济引导世界反思发展要义
zhSub: 访西班牙加泰罗尼亚开放大学艺术与人文系教授卡洛斯·布拉索·布洛基
paras: This is an interview, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, in which a reporter questions Carles Brasó Broggi, a professor in the Department of Arts and Humanities at the Open University of Catalonia in Spain. The topic is China's economic history, from antiquity to reform and opening up. Brasó Broggi argues that China has contributed to world development and continues to prompt others to reconsider how development should proceed.

The interview has three questions. The first asks when China's economy stood out globally. The second asks how ancient China's development model, and the link between its political system and its economy, compares with the West's. The third asks about the main factors behind growth since reform and opening up.

On history, Brasó Broggi, citing Angus Maddison, holds that China ranked among the leading economies in most periods, the exception being 1840 to the 1970s. He urges looking beyond the Four Great Inventions to a wider global history of technology. As an example, he notes that Wang Zhen's Nongshu described a spinning machine about 500 years before Britain's Industrial Revolution, and that Wang warned of mechanization's social and natural costs. In comparing models, he says both China and Europe were agrarian. In his account, China invested heavily in canals and irrigation and was mostly unified, unlike Europe. He sees market laws, state intervention and class relations as broadly similar in both. On the reform era, he lists open-minded borrowing from many schools of economists, pragmatic and gradual experimentation (such as special economic zones) unlike the Soviet Union's radical reform, and a favourable demographic structure. He says no comprehensive theory of China's development yet exists.

Brasó Broggi concludes that China combined internal and external drivers to sustain decades of growth while raising living standards, which he describes as unprecedented in world economic history. Read the original if you want a short, accessible view from a Spanish scholar on how China's long-run economic history and reform-era success are presented in Chinese media.
quoteEn: China has not only made important contributions to world economic development but has guided, and continues to guide, us in reflecting on how we should develop.
quoteZh: 中国不仅对世界经济发展作出了重要贡献，而且引导了（还在继续引导）我们反思应该如何发展。

glossary.explanation: The policy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented economic reforms and opening China to foreign trade and investment.

t: The distinctive qualities of the Party's leadership in further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 进一步全面深化改革的鲜明特质
paras: Writing in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, Liu Sifang asks why and how the Communist Party of China can guarantee the success of reform. The commentary argues that the Party's comprehensive leadership is the fundamental guarantee for further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization, as set out at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Liu holds that this guarantee rests on six capacities, which the article calls the Party's "six distinctive qualities".

The piece first sets out the framing: leadership by the Party is described as the key lesson of reform and opening up and of the reform work of the new era. It then takes the six capacities in turn: political leadership, ideological guidance, strategic planning, mass organisation, social appeal and spiritual drive. Each is defined, and each is linked to concrete requirements for the current round of reform. A final section turns to the Party's self-reform.

Liu defines political leadership as the ability to grasp direction and the overall situation. In Liu's account it keeps reform on course, secures the Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership through the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, and keeps reform tied to Chinese modernization. Ideological guidance rests on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the Two Integrations. Strategic planning combines top-level design with local experimentation, pairs breakthroughs in key areas with overall advance, and builds systems of goals, policies, work and evaluation. Mass organisation means relying on the people and the mass line. Social appeal means uniting different groups around a shared vision of national rejuvenation. Spiritual drive means drawing on the Party's lineage of spirit, encouraging bold innovation and protecting reformers.

Liu concludes that further reform is a profound change in theory, organisation, institutions and popular participation. To keep it on course, the Party must keep up the Party's self-reform to lead social revolution, and the author says the harder the social revolution, the more thorough the self-reform must be. The author calls for full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and for stronger institutional norms for self-reform. Read the original if you want a concise statement, in official Party-theory language, of how Chinese scholars frame Party leadership as the guarantee of reform after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: The more complex and arduous the tasks of social revolution, the more thorough self-reform must be.
quoteZh: 社会革命任务越复杂艰巨，自我革命就越要彻底。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's development path, used prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
A 2022 Party formula affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of his thought.
A Party formula requiring members to uphold the authority of the General Secretary as core and the centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
An official concept for the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and renew itself, often linked to anti-corruption work and strict Party governance.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official slogan, in use since 2014, for strict discipline, anti-corruption and institution-building within the Party.

t: Advancing with the times: raising governance capacity in the cultural sphere
zh: 与时俱进提升文化领域治理能力
paras: This short commentary, written after a Politburo collective study session, asks how governance capacity in the cultural sphere can be raised under conditions of informatization. Wen and Lu argue that this capacity is a necessary requirement for building a socialist cultural powerhouse by the 2035 target set by Xi Jinping, and an important guarantee of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article proceeds through five principles, each introduced by a heading: upholding Party leadership, keeping to fundamental principles while innovating, integrating culture with technology, maintaining cultural confidence, and fostering the core socialist values. It draws throughout on Xi's statements and on the Third Plenum decision (2024) on deepening reform.

The authors argue that Party leadership gives cultural governance a consistent direction, protects ideological security and shields cultural work from market uncertainty. They hold that Marxism's guiding role, Xi Jinping's cultural thought and the Two Integrations underpin the Party's cultural leadership and the Chinese nation's cultural subjectivity. They call for big data, cloud computing and artificial intelligence, described as new quality productive forces, to make governance more intelligent and precise, and for better governance of cyberspace. They add that cultural reform, scholarly and artistic democracy and a larger body of cultural talent would release creativity.

Wen and Lu present the core socialist values as the basis for guarding cultural sovereignty and security against what they call foreign cultural infiltration. They conclude that a healthy, open and dynamic governance ecosystem would deepen Chinese modernization and offer Chinese wisdom to global cultural diversity. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official discourse links cultural governance, ideological security and digital technology.
quoteEn: Raising governance capacity in the cultural sphere is a necessary requirement for building a socialist cultural powerhouse in the new era, and an important guarantee for realising the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 提升文化领域治理能力是新时代建设社会主义文化强国的必然要求，是实现中华民族伟大复兴的重要保障。

glossary.explanation: An official goal of building a country with strong cultural influence and soft power, with 2035 set as the target year for its achievement.
Formula for combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture.
A term promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to technology-driven productive forces such as digital technology and artificial intelligence.
The official name for China's path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of restoring China's national strength and standing, tied to the Chinese Dream.
A set of twenty-four characters of official values at national, social and individual levels, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Giving full play to the leading role of higher education in supporting high-level scientific and technological self-reliance
zh: 发挥高等教育龙头作用 支撑高水平科技自立自强
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2025, Gong Qihuang, president of Peking University, takes up how universities can serve high-level scientific and technological self-reliance. Drawing on the Outline of the Plan for Building a Strong Education Country (2024–2035), Gong argues that high-level research universities, as part of the national strategic science and technology force, should act as the vanguard in the battle over key core technologies.

The commentary is organised around four tasks. These are adjusting the disciplinary structure to national needs, assembling strategic talent, producing frontier science and technology, and working with other strategic science and technology forces. Gong supports each with passages from Xi Jinping and with the Outline's call to integrate education, science and technology, and talent.

On disciplines and talent, Gong calls for rapid, even extraordinary, placement of urgently needed fields and for unconventional selection of strong students in basic disciplines, with integrated undergraduate-to-doctoral training. Universities should recruit globally through fast-track channels, develop strategic scientists and young talent, and use trust-based evaluation with long, stable support for basic fields. On research, Gong urges combining goal-oriented and free exploration, strengthening organised research and the "open competition" mechanism (jiebang guashuai). Universities should also link with national laboratories, leading firms and local governments, drawing on the whole-nation system for concentrating resources.

Gong concludes that universities should reform research paradigms and organisational models and build the whole chain from basic research to industrial application. The author presents this as a way for universities to act as a vanguard in developing new quality productive forces. Read the original if you want a concise statement, from a leading university president, of how Chinese higher education is expected to support the national science and technology strategy.
quoteEn: High-level research universities must play their leading role well and advance education, science and technology, and talent as one integrated whole.
quoteZh: 高水平研究型大学要发挥好龙头作用，坚持教育、科技、人才一体推进

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and emerging industries.
An approach of mobilising state, institutional and market resources nationwide for major strategic goals, here applied to science and technology.
A research funding mechanism in which major technical problems are publicly posted and capable teams compete to take charge of solving them.

glossary.zh: 教育强国建设规划纲要（2024—2035年）
glossary.en: Outline of the Plan for Building a Strong Education Country (2024–2035)
glossary.explanation: A national planning document issued in early 2025 setting goals and measures for building China into a leading education power by 2035.

t: Building a higher-standard new system for an open economy through institutional opening-up
zh: 以制度型开放建设更高水平开放型经济新体制
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily (February 2025) asks how China can build a higher-level open economy now that tariff-based "border opening" is largely settled. Yang Jijun argues that the answer is institutional opening-up: moving from the cross-border flow of goods and factors to alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules.

Yang first traces the shift, noting that the 2018 Central Economic Work Conference first called for moving from opening based on flows of goods and factors to opening based on rules and other institutions. The article then defines four components of institutional opening-up: rules, regulation, management and standards. It closes with the challenges China faces and a set of responses.

Yang describes rules opening as the foundation, covering both compliance with WTO and regional trade agreement rules and participation in writing new ones. Regulatory opening is illustrated by the removal of foreign-ownership caps in finance and the "zeroing out" of foreign-access restrictions in manufacturing. Management opening means streamlining administration, and standards opening means aligning with ISO and other standards. Yang says developed countries are competing to control the next generation of trade rules. In response, the author proposes learning from RCEP and DEPA provisions, shifting industrial policy from selective to functional, and offering Chinese proposals in areas without unified rules, such as digital and green trade, through the Belt and Road Initiative.

Yang also calls for using pilot free trade zones as stress-test sites for high-standard rules, and for coordinating institutional opening-up with deeper reform so that each supports the other. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic outline of what "institutional opening-up" is taken to include and which policy steps are proposed.
quoteEn: Institutional opening-up includes both full alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules, namely \"institutional learning\", and active participation in global governance by offering institutional solutions to the world, namely \"institutional innovation\".
quoteZh: 制度型开放既包括全面对接高标准国际经贸规则，即“制度学习”，也包括主动参与全球治理，向国际上提供制度方案，即“制度创新”。

glossary.explanation: A policy concept first put forward in 2018 that shifts emphasis from cross-border flows of goods and factors to aligning domestic rules, regulations, management and standards with international ones.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure, trade and investment links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
Designated areas in China where new trade, investment and regulatory policies are tried out before possible wider adoption.
A reform approach in which measures are first tested in selected localities or zones before being extended nationally.

t: Vigorously promoting high-quality development of China's new energy
zh: 大力推动我国新能源高质量发展
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 19 February 2025, Cheng Zhiqiang, a cooperation director at the Global Energy Interconnection Development and Cooperation Organization, takes up how China can sustain high-quality development of its new energy sector. Cheng argues that the sector's rapid progress since 2012 reflects four advantages that Xi Jinping has named for the Chinese economy: institutional, demand-side, supply-side and talent. Further progress, in this account, requires using these advantages to carry out Xi's new energy security strategy of "four revolutions and one partnership".

The commentary has three parts. It first lists achievements, using figures for the end of 2023: wind and solar capacity ten times that of a decade earlier and about 40% of the world total, clean energy at 26.4% of consumption, and a 77.6% rise in new-energy vehicle exports. It then links each achievement to one of the four advantages. Finally it sets out five policy directions that correspond to the strategy.

In Cheng's reading, the socialist market economy and the system's ability to concentrate resources on major undertakings are the fundamental guarantee, helping to cultivate new quality productive forces. A market of more than 1.4 billion people let firms refine products through domestic competition before competing abroad. China's complete industrial system, the only one covering all UN industrial categories according to the author, supports a full new-energy chain. By 2024, new energy capacity of 1.45 billion kilowatts had overtaken thermal power. Talent figures include 7.4 million renewable-energy jobs, 46% of the global total, and over two million related firms.

Cheng proposes five measures: strengthening industrial and supply chains and curbing disruptive market behaviour; improving electricity markets and pricing; opening market access and expanding green certificates and green power trading; expanding new-energy university programmes and talent funds while digitalising the sector; and deepening international cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative and Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives. The aim is to supply secure energy for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise official-style summary of how Chinese policy commentary ties new-energy statistics to the leadership's economic-advantage framework and to its energy security strategy.
quoteEn: The primary driving force of new energy development is innovation; innovation-driven development is in essence talent-driven, and the strong talent dividend provides important support for the sustained and rapid development of China's new energy.
quoteZh: 新能源发展的第一驱动力是创新，创新驱动本质上是人才驱动，强大的人才红利为我国新能源的持续快速发展提供了重要支撑。

glossary.pinyin: sì gè gémìng, yí gè hézuò
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's energy security strategy, first put forward in 2014. It calls for revolutions in energy consumption, supply, technology and institutions, plus comprehensive international cooperation.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgrading of industries.
The official term for the Party's path of national development, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
China's infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Asia, Europe, Africa and beyond.

t: The people's creative practice runs through the whole process of Chinese modernization
zh: 人民的创造性实践贯穿中国式现代化进程始终
paras: This short commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks how the people relate to Chinese modernization. Zhao and Huang argue that the people's creative practice runs through the entire process and is its source of dynamism. They start from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which stressed respect for the people's principal position and pioneering spirit.

The piece first stresses Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee and primary principle of Chinese modernization. It then sets out four ways in which creative practice matters: it provides the practical foundation, forges the main force of modernization, expresses its fundamental direction, and determines the choice of path. The authors rely heavily on Xi Jinping, Marx, Engels and the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022).

In the authors' account, history is ultimately human practice, so the people create both material and spiritual wealth. Through practice, they say, the people meet their own needs, take part in running the state, develop science and technology, and raise perceptual knowledge into rational knowledge. The authors hold that the Party represents the people's fundamental interests and that the path rests on a people-centred approach, with common prosperity and whole-process people's democracy among its practical requirements.

Zhao and Huang conclude that whether the path proves viable depends on keeping the people at the centre and putting the people first, so that the fruits of modernization reach everyone more fairly. They present the free and all-round development of the human being as its ultimate goal. They add that the path suits China's conditions and offers a useful reference for other countries. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the Party-people relationship and the people's role in history are framed in official-academic discourse on Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The people's creative practice runs through the whole process of Chinese modernization and is its source of dynamism.
quoteZh: 人民的创造性实践贯穿于中国式现代化进程始终，是中国式现代化的动力源泉。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out by the Party especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official concept introduced by Xi Jinping to describe China's socialist democracy. It is said to cover every stage of decision-making, not only elections.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all of the population. It has been a prominent policy theme in the Xi Jinping era.
A principle in Party discourse that the people's interests rank above all else. It is closely linked to the 'people-centred' approach.

t: Accelerating the development of green productive forces
zh: 加快发展绿色生产力
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 18 February 2025
paras: This commentary takes up Xi Jinping's statement of 31 January 2024, at a Politburo study session, that green development is the foundation of high-quality development and that new quality productive forces are themselves green productive forces. He Weijun argues that the formulation goes beyond conventional understandings of productive forces and is a theoretical innovation by Marxist productive-forces theory in the setting of Chinese modernization. The author contends that regions should seek footholds in this field early and build competitive advantage.

The article is organised in three parts: the meaning and requirements of green productive forces, why developing them is necessary and important, and how institutional and technological innovation can advance them. It links the concept to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which put building a beautiful China and a comprehensive green transition among its stated reform priorities. It also ties the concept to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, to Xi's thought on ecological civilization and to his economic thought.

On meaning, He identifies three implications: ecological, resource and environmental factors enter the productive-force category and change the traditional production function; growth shifts from resource consumption to green innovation, with growth decoupled from pollution; and barriers to realising the value of ecological products are removed. On necessity, the author says green productive forces are a basic requirement of Chinese modernization, in which humanity and nature coexist in harmony, and of high-quality development. They are also needed for China's contribution to global green development, moving from learner to demonstrator and leader. On means, He proposes clear property rights over natural resources, carbon and pollution rights, a national carbon market and ecological compensation. He also proposes EOD mechanisms, environmental disclosure, performance evaluations that treat ecological protection as a hard constraint, and green technology alliances and laboratories.

He concludes that regions should use their own advantages, including less developed, resource-rich and ecologically important areas, to take the green and low-carbon track. Zero-carbon cities, parks and factories and demonstration projects would build a pattern of benchmarks that other regions follow. The author calls for using the national "two new" and "two major" policies and joining global green supply chains, so that China moves from "green constraint" to "green breakthrough". Read the original if you want an example of how a university Party leader presents green productive forces as policy within official discourse on high-quality development and ecological civilization.
quoteEn: Green productive forces bring ecological, resource and environmental factors into the category of productive forces.
quoteZh: 绿色生产力将生态、资源、环境等要素纳入生产力范畴之中

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023–24 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industries. Official texts stress that they are green by nature.
The official aim of economic development since about 2017, which prioritises quality, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization. Its stated features include harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature.

A term in official discourse for productive forces built on green innovation and environmental protection, treating ecology and resources as elements of production. It follows Xi's remark that new quality productive forces are themselves green productive forces.

t: Cultivating high-level talent independently to help develop new quality productive forces
zh: 自主培养高层次人才 助力发展新质生产力
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (17 February 2025), Han Qingsong asks how China's postgraduate education can supply the high-level talent needed for new quality productive forces. The commentary argues that raising the quality of independent talent cultivation is both a precondition for, and an aim served by, the growth of such forces.

Han first defines the link between the two. New quality productive forces are said to be innovation-led and marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality, while high-level talent is characterised by advanced degrees, high capability and high all-round character. The remainder sets out six areas for action, citing the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

Han's proposals centre on training and institutional design. Postgraduate education should follow the 'four serves', the 'three-all' education policy and the 'five-education' principle, and build a distinctively Chinese knowledge system of disciplines, scholarship and discourse. Han also calls for adjusting disciplines towards basic, emerging, interdisciplinary and strategic fields, and for joint training with enterprises and research institutes under the new-type whole-nation system to integrate the innovation, talent, funding and industrial chains. Supervisors should be strengthened in ethics, ability and working conditions, and Han proposes a 'multi-dimensional, high-precision' value-added evaluation model that rejects the 'five onlys' (scores, further study, diplomas, papers, titles).

Han concludes that core technologies cannot be begged or bought, so China must secure control over its talent supply through these reforms. Han presents the measures as a way to link doctoral training seamlessly to high-level technological innovation. Read the original if you want a concise outline of current Chinese policy thinking on postgraduate training and talent strategy.
quoteEn: The premise of independently cultivating high-level talent is to build a Chinese autonomous knowledge system for postgraduate education, comprising three systems: disciplines, academic scholarship and discourse.
quoteZh: 高层次人才自主培养的前提是建构中国自主的研究生教育知识体系，构建学科体系、学术体系、话语体系三大体系。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for innovation-driven, technology-intensive productive forces. It is central to current official economic and development policy.
An official approach that mobilises state, institutional and market resources nationwide for major science and technology goals.

glossary.literal: education by all personnel, throughout the whole process, in all respects
glossary.explanation: An official policy requirement that all staff, at every stage and in every aspect, take part in educating students.
The principle of developing moral, intellectual, physical, aesthetic and labour education together.

The official educational guideline that education should serve the people, the Party's governance of China, consolidating and developing the socialist system, and reform, opening up and socialist modernization.
An evaluation reform campaign against judging people solely by scores, further study, diplomas, papers and titles.

t: Cultivating talent for new quality productive forces is the key to sustainable development
zh: 培养新质生产力人才是实现可持续发展的关键
paras: This commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, argues that training large numbers of people with innovative thinking, interdisciplinary knowledge and practical ability is the key to sustainable development. Zhai starts from the 20th Party Congress (2022) formula that science and technology are the primary productive force, talent the primary resource and innovation the primary driving force. On this basis Zhai holds that innovation-driven growth is in essence talent-driven, and that new quality productive forces depend on talent.

The piece sets out three areas of reform. They are the education and training system, the cultivation of practical skills through links between industry and education, and a wider ecosystem for talent covering selection, evaluation, use and incentives.

On education, Zhai calls for restructuring university disciplines around national strategic needs, including new engineering, medical, agricultural and liberal arts fields and stronger basic disciplines. Zhai also calls for integrating teaching with research and industry, and for better teacher evaluation. Zhai says Chinese training still stresses theory over practice, and proposes more internships, joint university–enterprise laboratories, industry colleges and "dual-qualified" teachers. On the talent ecosystem, Zhai says evaluation systems are incomplete. The commentary proposes overcoming the fixation on papers, titles and degrees, and adopting peer review and classified evaluation. It also proposes giving researchers more control over funds and technical routes, easing entry for overseas talent, and improving the sharing of income from technology transfer.

Zhai concludes that China needs a full-chain system running from training and recruitment to use and incentives, with national strategic plans for key fields. It should aim to produce leading scientists, outstanding engineers and highly skilled workers, and to keep them in China. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the talent-policy measures commonly linked to new quality productive forces in Chinese higher education.
quoteEn: Training large numbers of new-quality-productive-force talents with innovative thinking, interdisciplinary knowledge and practical ability is the key to achieving sustainable development.
quoteZh: 培养大批具有创新思维、跨学科知识和实践能力的新质生产力人才，是实现可持续发展的关键所在。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, as opposed to traditional resource-heavy growth.

t: The "Two Roads" spirit injects driving force into building a strong country
zh: “两路”精神为强国建设注入奋进力量
paras: This commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, takes up the "Two Roads" spirit, which grew out of building and maintaining the Sichuan–Tibet and Qinghai–Tibet highways. Gong Hui starts from Xi Jinping's 2014 instruction marking the highways' 60th anniversary. It summarised the spirit as fearing neither hardship nor death, tenacious struggle and willingness to serve as a paving stone, and unity between army and people and among ethnic groups. Gong argues that the spirit belongs to the Chinese Communist Party's spiritual lineage, continues the great founding spirit of the Party, and should be built into national projects such as becoming a country strong in transport.

The article has three sections: how the spirit was formed, what it contains, and how to carry it forward. The first traces its sources in traditional Chinese culture and revolutionary culture, the road-building and maintenance record, and its link to later achievements in transport. The second sets out the spirit's content. The third gives practical proposals for communication, education and the conversion of the spirit into practice.

On sources, Gong links the spirit to traditional ideas such as benevolence, self-strengthening and responsibility for the nation. Gong also ties it to the Red heritage of the People's Liberation Army units that advanced into Tibet while building the roads. Its content is read as revolutionary heroism and revolutionary optimism, a fighting spirit of tenacity, and a scientific rigour expressed in the "four nevers" of surveying and drawing. Gong adds the unity of army and people, which is said to rest on a people-centred stance. In this account the roads improved living standards in Tibet, strengthened the sense of a Chinese national community and allowed ethnic groups to share in national development.

Gong calls for a fuller all-media communication system, with immersive AR, VR and MR reconstructions and public activities such as retracing the roads. The spirit should be integrated into ideological and political education from primary school to university. It should also be turned into practice in public services, in cultural industries and tourism along the roads, and in building a modern socialist new Tibet, so that it supports the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an example of how the Party-state frames a regional infrastructure legacy as spiritual heritage, education content and cultural policy.
quoteEn: The "Two Roads" spirit is an important component of the spiritual lineage of Chinese Communists and a continuation of the great founding spirit of the Party.
quoteZh: “两路”精神是中国共产党人精神谱系的重要组成部分，是伟大建党精神的传承。

glossary.explanation: A Party-endorsed spirit drawn from building and maintaining the Sichuan–Tibet and Qinghai–Tibet highways. Xi Jinping defined it in a 2014 instruction.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: sense of a Chinese national community
glossary.literal: forging a firm consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: An official ethnic-policy formulation stressing a shared national identity across China's ethnic groups.

t: Vigorously promoting the mutual fit and interaction of new quality productive forces and new industrialization
zh: 大力推动新质生产力与新型工业化契合互动
paras: Writing in Study Times in February 2025, Qu Yongyi asks how new quality productive forces and new industrialization can be made to fit and reinforce each other. Qu argues that this interaction is a necessary requirement of high-quality development, the fundamental route to building a modern industrial system by strengthening strong points and filling gaps, and a firm guarantee of further breakthroughs in Chinese modernization. The piece is a short commentary that opens by citing Xi Jinping's definition of new quality productive forces and his description of new industrialization as a key task.

The article has three parts. The first sets out the underlying logic and practical dimensions of the interaction, against the domestic and international situation. The second argues that scientific and technological innovation should lead, and lists areas for action. The third identifies current points of leverage, framed by the 20th Party Congress (2022) goal of basically achieving new industrialization by 2035.

In Qu's account, new quality productive forces are a revolutionary force that reshapes producers, tools, objects and methods of production, improves resource allocation and so speeds up new industrialization; new industrialization in turn drives their growth through frontier breakthroughs, new production factors such as data, the upgrading of traditional industries and the rise of emerging and future industries. Qu holds that the 'new quality' is a comprehensive leap in labourers, means and objects of labour, not gradual change, and that innovation drives it. Qu therefore proposes a systematic push on core technologies through the new whole-nation system, cultivation of future industries such as generative AI, humanoid robots, 6G, the metaverse and quantum information, and support for strategic emerging industries such as new energy and new materials.

For present priorities Qu calls for a better policy environment, with competition policy and industrial security policy given precedence over general industrial policy. Qu also calls for a more focused central whole-nation system, with evaluation emphasised over process supervision, and for local governments' innovation performance to be assessed so as to avoid duplicated introduction and overcapacity. Finally, Qu urges rapid industrialization of fields with high technological maturity and market readiness, to boost confidence, investment and consumption. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how industrial-policy researchers link new quality productive forces to the 2035 industrialization target.
quoteEn: The mutual fit and interaction of new quality productive forces and new industrialization is a necessary requirement for high-quality economic development, the fundamental route to building a modern industrial system by strengthening strong points and filling gaps, and a solid guarantee of new breakthroughs and results in Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 新质生产力与新型工业化契合互动，是推动经济高质量发展的必然要求，是推进产业锻长板、补短板建设现代化产业体系的根本途径，是中国式现代化建设不断取得新突破新成效的坚实保障。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation and high technology, as opposed to traditional growth models.
An official term for industrial development built on digital, networked and intelligent technologies and innovation. The 20th Party Congress set the aim of basically achieving it by 2035.
An official term for mobilising national resources under central coordination, combined with market mechanisms, to achieve key scientific and technological breakthroughs.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth based on efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Modernizing the system and capacity for border governance is an integral part of Chinese modernization
zh: 推进边疆治理体系和治理能力现代化，是中国式现代化的应有之义
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 14 February 2025, explains and elaborates a statement by Xi Jinping at the 18th group study session of the Political Bureau of the 20th Central Committee: that modernizing the border governance system and capacity is an integral part of Chinese modernization. Yang Ziqiang argues that the statement sums up historical experience, marks a new level of understanding of border governance, and gives direction for high-quality development in border regions.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out the practical, theoretical and historical logic behind the statement. It then identifies four pairs of relationships that must be handled in implementation: whole and part, diversity and unity, development and security, and theory and practice. Finally it turns to how the statement should be put into practice through Party leadership and four modes of governance.

On practical logic, Yang cites achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the unprecedented risks and tasks now facing border areas. On theoretical logic, Yang argues that Chinese modernization requires that no border area be left behind, citing census figures: the nine land-border provinces and regions hold 284.5 million people, about one fifth of the total; more than half of over 140 border counties were formerly national-level poor counties; and nearly 60 per cent of ethnic minority people live in border areas. On historical logic, Yang points to dynastic practices from the Qin to the Qing and to ideas such as great unity and governing according to local customs. The four relationships are then tied to concrete tasks: integrating border development into national strategy and developing new quality productive forces; building a Chinese national community as the main thread, including promoting the common national language and embedded social structures; upholding the holistic approach to national security and strengthening border defence; and building an autonomous Chinese knowledge system of border studies.

Yang concludes that the full leadership of the Party must be implemented across border governance. Governance should be systematic, law-based, comprehensive and source-oriented, drawing on the Fengqiao experience, so that institutional strengths become governance effectiveness. Border governance is presented as a matter that cannot be relaxed for a moment. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative statement of how Party theorists frame border governance within Chinese modernization, including its policy vocabulary on ethnic affairs, security and academic discipline-building.
quoteEn: To achieve this kind of modernization, not a single border area can be left behind.
quoteZh: 要实现这样的现代化，边疆地区一个都不能少。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's path to modernization, stressing a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical balance, harmony with nature and peaceful development. It was elaborated especially from the 20th Party Congress (2022).

An official ethnic-affairs line that treats all of China's ethnic groups as parts of one Chinese nation and aims to strengthen a shared national identity. It is promoted as the main thread of ethnic work.
A term introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological innovation and upgraded industries.
Xi Jinping's 2014 concept of national security covering a broad range of fields, from political and territorial to economic, cultural and ecological security.
The official goal of economic development that prioritises quality, innovation and balance over speed of growth, advanced since around 2017.

A model of grassroots conflict resolution originating in Zhejiang in the 1960s, in which disputes are handled locally through mobilising the masses. It is now promoted as a method of social governance.

t: The socialist road as the inevitable choice of modern Chinese history
zh: 社会主义道路是中国近代历史的必然选择
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, responds to historical nihilism. Wang argues that the claim that modern China's turn to socialism was a 'historical misunderstanding' or 'accident' aims to push socialist China towards capitalism. Wang contends that history and reality both refute it, and that socialism was the inevitable choice of modern Chinese history.

The piece moves in three steps. It first describes imperialist aggression after the Opium War, then reviews the failed movements from the Taiping Rebellion to the 1911 Revolution, and finally explains why socialism and the Communist Party succeeded.

Wang's central claims run as follows. Foreign powers, the article says, imposed nearly 1,000 unequal treaties between 1842 and 1919 and extracted huge indemnities, so they would not let China grow strong and attempts to learn from the West failed. Each earlier movement, in Wang's account, lacked advanced guiding thought and mass support, and none ended China's semi-colonial, semi-feudal condition. The article credits the Communist Party's success to two things: guidance by Marxism, adapted to Chinese conditions, and a consistent people-centred stance.

Wang concludes that socialism in China is the historical choice of the people, not a misunderstanding, and cites Xi Jinping on the unique features of China's history and conditions. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese official scholarship answers historical nihilism with an argument for the inevitability of the socialist road.
quoteEn: The Taiping Movement, the Hundred Days' Reform, the 1911 Revolution and the others failed for many reasons, but these come down to two: they lacked the guidance of advanced thought, and they lacked the support of the broad masses.
quoteZh: 太平天国运动、戊戌变法、辛亥革命等的最终失败，原因是多方面的，但归结起来不外乎两条：一是没有先进思想的指导，二是没有广大人民群众的支持。

glossary.explanation: In official Chinese usage, a label for views that deny or disparage the Communist Party's revolutionary history and the legitimacy of the socialist path.

t: A good ecological environment is the most inclusive public benefit for people's well-being
zh: 良好生态环境是最普惠的民生福祉
paras: Hu Jun, writing in Study Times in February 2025, takes up the thesis that a good ecological environment is the most inclusive public benefit for people's well-being. The author presents it as a major theoretical innovation that clarifies how environment and livelihood relate and what ecological civilization is for. Hu argues that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core has acted on this principle, producing what the article calls historic, turning-point and overall changes in environmental protection.

The commentary has two main parts. The first sets out the theoretical meaning of the formula in three respects: the relation of environment to livelihood, the people-centred character of Xi Jinping's ecological thought, and the distinctive features it gives Chinese modernization. The second part reports practical results and then sets out tasks for the new journey, covering Party leadership, equitable sharing of benefits, and public participation. The results section uses figures on inspections, air quality, water quality and green finance.

Hu's central claim is that Marxism's view that humans live from nature is extended by Xi's statements that the environment is livelihood and that a sound ecology is the fairest public good. On this reading the traditional concept of livelihood is widened, and ecological civilization is answered in terms of for whom, by whom and with benefits shared by whom. Hu also contends that, with the principal contradiction now defined as that between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development, a modernization in harmony with nature surpasses a Western modernization centred on capital, polarisation and materialism. As evidence, Hu cites 3,294 tasks in the first round of central environmental inspection with a 98% completion rate, over 320,000 petitions handled, PM2.5 at 29.3 micrograms per cubic metre in 2024, and good-quality surface water sections rising from 64.5% in 2015 to 90.4% in 2024.

Hu concedes that improvement is still at a low level and well short of the goal of a Beautiful China. The author calls for strengthening the Party's overall leadership over ecological work, treating a good environment as a basic public service and a priority livelihood area, deepening ecological reform and modernizing governance. Hu also calls for the "from the masses, to the masses" method and a society-wide ecological culture, so that building a Beautiful China becomes conscious public action. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official line on ecological civilization is justified and presented, with the statistics it cites, in a Party-school newspaper.
quoteEn: A good ecological environment is not only natural wealth but also economic wealth and social wealth.
quoteZh: 良好生态环境不只是自然财富，也是经济财富、社会财富。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models. Its listed features include harmony between humanity and nature.
An official goal, set out since the 18th Party Congress (2012), of building a China with a good ecological environment as part of national rejuvenation.

keywords: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization

t: Identifying the key levers for high-level scientific and technological self-reliance
zh: 找准高水平科技自立自强关键抓手
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in Economic Daily in February 2025, asks how China can achieve high-level scientific and technological self-reliance. Sheng opens with DeepSeek and ChatGPT as signs that technological competition has become the central arena of great-power rivalry. Citing Xi Jinping's call to build a leading scientific and technological power by 2035, Sheng argues that the task needs clear key levers, an overall approach and defined priorities.

The article first sets out why self-reliance matters, pointing to a new round of scientific and technological revolution and sharper international competition. It then reviews progress since the 18th Party Congress (2012) in four areas: breakthroughs in core technologies, original innovations, international scientific cooperation and the innovation ecosystem. Finally it lists five priority tasks.

Sheng contends that self-reliance helps break through key core technologies, keep domestic industrial and supply chains running smoothly and raise total factor productivity. As evidence, the article cites R&D spending rising from 1.03 trillion to 3.61 trillion yuan between 2012 and 2024, with R&D intensity up from 1.91% to 2.68%. It also cites a 2024 South Korean assessment ranking China fourth in the world in technology level. The proposed tasks are key breakthroughs through the new-type whole-nation system, deeper reform of the science and technology system, stronger enterprise innovation, a firmer talent base and continued open innovation.

Sheng concludes that China should build an industrial innovation system linking basic research, technology development, commercialisation and application. Proposals include scientist-led research institutes with greater autonomy, enterprises as the main innovators, better evaluation of top talent and wider access to major scientific facilities for foreign teams. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of China's science and technology policy priorities in early 2025, with the statistics the author cites.
quoteEn: The key to achieving high-level scientific and technological self-reliance is to form institutions and mechanisms that enable key core technologies and major original technologies to emerge continuously, and to deepen reform of the science and technology system around stimulating people's initiative, enthusiasm and creativity.
quoteZh: 实现高水平科技自立自强的重点是形成有利于关键核心技术和重大原创技术源源不断产生的体制机制，围绕激发人的积极性主动性创造性深化科技体制改革。

glossary.literal: high-level science and technology self-standing and self-strengthening
glossary.explanation: A Party policy goal of mastering key technologies domestically and reducing dependence on foreign sources. It is closely associated with Xi Jinping's emphasis on innovation as the core of national development.

An approach that mobilises state, market and institutional resources nationwide to reach major scientific and technological goals. It updates the earlier whole-nation system with a larger role for markets and enterprises.
A strategic goal, which the article dates to 2035, of making China a world leader in science and technology.

t: Upholding a Chinese modernization of harmony between humanity and nature
zh: 坚持人与自然和谐共生的中国式现代化
paras: This commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, takes up the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) and its claim that Chinese modernization is a modernization of harmony between humanity and nature. Zhao and Chen argue that the idea rests on the Marxist dialectic of nature and on traditional Chinese ecological thought such as "the unity of heaven and humanity". They contend that, guided by Xi Jinping's thought on ecological civilization, China must grasp the idea's core meaning, principles and practical requirements in order to follow this path firmly.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first sets out the core meaning of harmonious coexistence from three vantage points: the lasting development of the Chinese nation, the laws of civilizational development, and a community with a shared future for mankind. The second sets out three principles: putting the people first, green development, and coordinated planning. The third turns to practice: improving the basic institutions of ecological civilization, the environmental governance system, and the mechanisms for green and low-carbon development.

The authors argue that Western modernization consumed resources and damaged the environment in pursuit of unlimited profit. In their account, China's large population, relatively scarce resources and weak environmental carrying capacity mean it must take a different route. They cite the maxim "when the ecology thrives, civilization thrives" and say ecological problems cut across class, state and ideology, so that China's approach contributes to global ecological security. On principles, they present a good environment as a basic livelihood issue, treat "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets" as a statement of the dialectic between development and protection, and call for treating mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert as one system.

On practice, Zhao and Chen call for removing institutional obstacles inherited from the old development model and building new mechanisms. They list measures from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), including differentiated zoning controls, property-rights systems for natural resources, and an ecological-environment code. They also cite the pollution permit system, joint river-basin and regional governance, and market allocation of environmental factors. They describe pollution control as at a critical stage, with carbon intensity a particular concern, and urge broad participation in building a Beautiful China. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official framing of ecological civilization within Chinese modernization, as of early 2025.]
quoteEn: A green economy cannot emerge spontaneously under traditional institutions and mechanisms; it needs new thinking, new concepts and new institutions and mechanisms to bring it into being.
quoteZh: 绿色经济不可能在传统体制机制下自发出现，需要新的思想、新的理念、新的体制机制来催生

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is said to include harmony between humanity and nature among its defining features.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations, stressing interdependence and shared global challenges.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan attributed to Xi Jinping (2005) holding that ecological protection and economic prosperity are mutually reinforcing.
An official goal of building a country with a good ecological environment, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
An official concept that makes ecological protection a core part of national development and institution-building, alongside economic, political, cultural and social construction.

t: The relationship between raising quality and expanding total output must be well coordinated
zh: 必须统筹好提升质量和做大总量的关系
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in February 2025, interprets one of the "five must-coordinate" relationships set out at the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference: the relationship between raising quality and expanding total output. Lai Desheng argues that coordinating the two is required to consolidate the material foundation of Chinese modernization. The author presents it as a deepening of the Party's understanding of how economic work operates and as guidance for high-quality development.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first explains why coordination is an inherent requirement of Chinese modernization. The second assesses the conditions already in place, and the third sets out four practical directions under a "systems perspective".

In the first part, Lai links the coordination to high-quality development, to improving people's wellbeing and to national security. Early in development, the author says, enlarging the total is more urgent, and stressing quality too soon is unrealistic. Now that China is the world's second-largest economy, Lai holds that quantity still matters, since the 20th Party Congress (2022) set a goal of reaching the per capita GDP of a moderately developed country by 2035. Quality must also rise, through a shift from factor inputs to innovation. Lai adds that people's concerns have moved from whether they have enough to whether it is good enough, and that economic security depends on both a larger total and better quality. The second part cites China's share of the global economy (over 18%), a contribution to world growth above 30% for several years, and progress on each element of the new development philosophy.

Lai proposes accelerating the new development pattern by expanding domestic demand and deepening supply-side structural reform. The author also calls for developing new quality productive forces adapted to each region, and for invigorating business entities by implementing the Two Unwaverings. The final proposal is to make full use of human capital by improving training, reforming talent evaluation and promoting the flow of talent. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Central Party School scholar explains and elaborates the 2024 economic work conference line for a general readership.
quoteEn: In the early stage of economic development, per capita income is low and the national economy is still small, so finding ways to enlarge the total within a short time is comparatively the more urgent task.
quoteZh: 在经济发展早期阶段，人均收入水平比较低，国家的经济总量还比较小，想办法在较短时间里把总量做大，相对而言是更加紧迫的事情。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The official economic goal since 2017. It stresses innovation, efficiency and balance over speed of growth alone.
A framework introduced in 2015 built on five principles: innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
A concept promoted since 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging industries.
The official policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A strategy that takes the domestic economic cycle as the mainstay, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other. It was put forward in 2020.

t: The unity of Chinese civilisation and the Chinese nation's pursuit of national unification
zh: 从中华文明统一性看中华民族对国家统一的追求
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks how the unity of Chinese civilisation explains the Chinese nation's persistent pursuit of national unification. Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development, which set out the "five prominent characteristics" of Chinese civilisation, Wang argues that the tradition of "great unification" has been a main thread of China's political order and thought and culture throughout its history.

The article moves chronologically from the Western Zhou to the Republic of China.
