It draws on early texts and inscriptions, the Han Confucian synthesis, the Sixteen Kingdoms and Northern Dynasties, the Tang, Yuan, Ming and Qing, and Sun Yat-sen's idea of a republic of five peoples, and ends with the Confucian ideal of family, state and all under heaven.

Wang's central claims are that ideas of a unified realm, a central "China" and shared Yan and Huang ancestry developed early, and that cultural identification came to outweigh blood descent. In this account the idea of "Hua and Yi as one family" gradually became the mainstream. Wang cites rulers of non-Han origin who adopted Han culture, the Yuan dynasty's choice of its name from the Classic of Changes, and Qing emperors' statements on ethnic unity. The author also presents the Qing's differentiated administrative systems for different regions as a successful handling of ethnic relations. The Confucian outlook of "family-state-all under heaven", with the family as the base of the state, is described as a cornerstone of national cohesion.

Wang concludes that the cultural identity formed through ethnic integration shaped a national spirit of seeking unity, and that this firm commitment to national unity, carried in the blood of more than 1.4 billion Chinese, is a source of cultural confidence. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese scholarship links classical sources and dynastic history to present-day claims about national unity.
quoteEn: In the course of ethnic integration, the various peoples formed a powerful cultural identity and forged a national spirit that pursues solidarity and unity.
quoteZh: 各民族在民族融合中形成了强大的文化认同，铸就了追求团结统一的民族精神。

glossary.explanation: A concept from the Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, later taken to mean a politically and culturally unified realm under one central authority. Chinese scholarship often treats it as a continuous thread in Chinese history.
A concept in Party discourse, stressed since the 2010s, meaning confidence in China's own cultural tradition and in socialist culture.

glossary.en: Hua and Yi as one family
glossary.explanation: A traditional idea that Han (Huaxia) and non-Han peoples belong to one community under the ruler. The article presents it as a mainstream view across dynasties.

glossary.literal: descendants of the Yan and Yellow Emperors
glossary.explanation: The belief that Chinese people descend from the legendary Yan Emperor and Yellow Emperor, used as a symbol of shared origin.

t: We must keep in mind that high-quality development is the hard truth of the new era
zh: 必须牢记高质量发展是新时代的硬道理
paras: Fan Peng's commentary in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (11 February 2025) takes up Xi Jinping's statement that high-quality development is the "hard truth" (硬道理) of the new era. Fan argues that the statement is a new development of Xi Jinping's economic thought and a fresh expression of Marxist philosophy, political economy and scientific socialism in contemporary China.

The article sets the formula in a historical sequence of "hard truths", each tied to the principal contradiction and mission of its period. It then turns to three practical requirements for putting high-quality development into effect.

Fan holds that Marxism's common essence, "to seek the liberation of mankind", takes different forms in different eras. Around 1939 the hard truth was revolution against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism; in 1992 Deng Xiaoping's "development is the hard truth" answered the contradiction between material needs and backward production. The present formula answers the new principal contradiction and the shift from high-speed growth to high-quality development. Fan presents it as continuing Deng Xiaoping Theory while adding new demands.

For implementation Fan calls for understanding the Two Establishes, strengthening the Four-sphere Confidence as the subjective force behind development, and fully applying the new development philosophy in practice. Innovation, coordination, green development and security are to produce new quality productive forces and results that ordinary people share. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party theorists place the high-quality development slogan within a genealogy of Marxist "hard truths".
quoteEn: The key to applying the new development philosophy fully, accurately and comprehensively is to firmly grasp high-quality development as the "hard truth of the new era".
quoteZh: 完整、准确、全面贯彻新发展理念最关键的是要牢牢把握高质量发展这个“新时代的硬道理”。

glossary.explanation: A phrase popularised by Deng Xiaoping's 1992 Southern Tour remarks ("development is the hard truth"), meaning a principle that is non-negotiable. Xi Jinping applies it to high-quality development.
Official economic goal since the 19th Party Congress (2017), stressing quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
Xi Jinping's framework of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, set out in 2015.
A 2022 Party formulation affirming Xi Jinping's status as the core of the Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for innovation-driven, technology-intensive productive forces seen as the basis of high-quality development.

t: The modern civilizational value of excellent traditional Chinese family culture
zh: 中华优秀传统家文化的现代文明价值
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 7 February 2025
paras: This newspaper commentary asks what contemporary value excellent traditional Chinese family culture holds. Li Ping'an argues that it is the soil in which the spiritual strength of Chinese culture is cultivated, and so a cultural foundation for Chinese modernization. Li reads the word for tradition as combining vertical transmission through history with the horizontal gathering of cultural essence, and says family culture matters on both counts.

The piece has three sections. The first treats family culture as a marker and essence of Chinese civilization. The second looks at its contribution to well-being and social civility in modern society. The third considers how it enriches the content and forms of human civilization.

Li contends that family elements such as surnames and genealogies pass on collective memory and identity. Family transmission of crafts and classic texts, for example paper-cutting, embroidery and ceramics, is said to have preserved intangible heritage. Virtues such as respect for elders, love for the young and filial piety are presented as the roots of the national spirit, leading to "loving the country as one loves the family". In modern life, Li says, the family gives emotional support against the pressures of a fast-paced society and is the first classroom of social responsibility. Internationally, Li points to the Spring Festival's recognition by the United Nations in 2023 and by UNESCO in 2024. Li also cites the ideal of "a harmonious family prospers" as a model of harmony and inclusiveness for dialogue between cultures.

Li concludes that this heritage should be explored and promoted in the new era so that it plays a greater role in society. It is described as sustaining social stability, adding diversity to human civilization and supporting a shared future. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academic commentary links family ethics to cultural confidence and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Excellent traditional Chinese family culture manifests the cultural values of harmony and inclusiveness, condensed in the plain expression \"a harmonious family prospers\".
quoteZh: 中华优秀传统家文化彰显和谐、包容的文化价值，凝聚在“家和万事兴”的朴素表达中

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization, promoted by the Party since the early 2020s. It is presented as distinct from Western models and as rooted in Chinese conditions and culture.

t: Upholding and applying the systems view to promote high-quality employment
zh: 坚持和运用系统观促进高质量就业
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks how universities should handle graduate employment. Han Wei argues that it is a complex systems undertaking, to be approached with systems thinking, which Xi Jinping has made a guiding method for Party and state work since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Han ties the argument to the Third Plenum decision (2024) on mechanisms for high-quality and full employment and on support for key groups such as graduates.

The piece is organised as a list of subsystems that universities should build, preceded by a call for top-level design. These are: an employment-oriented ideological and political education pattern, a course system, a team of guidance teachers, a reward system, a key-group assistance system and an institutional system for evaluation.

Han's central claim is that graduate employment serves national strategic and livelihood needs, so it must be planned under a broad view of employment and linked to the fundamental task of fostering virtue through education. Academic disciplines and majors are treated as the foundation, to be set up in line with national needs and with employment outcomes feeding back into resource allocation. Han also criticises current evaluation for focusing mainly on employment rates. The commentary proposes tracking graduates' careers for one year and for three to five years, and giving earlier, more personal support to students, including those who delay employment.

Han concludes that systems, holistic and overall-picture thinking must run through all employment work, so that universities supply a steady flow of high-quality talent for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a university leader applies Party-endorsed systems thinking to graduate employment policy.
quoteEn: Graduate employment work, as an important part of universities' task of training builders and successors of socialism, is a complex systemic undertaking, and systems, overall and holistic thinking must be built into the employment work system.
quoteZh: 高校毕业生就业工作作为高校培养社会主义建设者和接班人的重要一环，是一项复杂的系统工作，必须将系统理念、全局观念、整体观念融入就业工作体系之中。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official formulation of the fundamental task of education: moral and ideological cultivation alongside knowledge and skills.
A policy idea that ideological and political education should be spread across all courses, staff and settings, not confined to dedicated courses.
A method stressed in Xi Jinping's speeches that calls for treating tasks as interlinked wholes with top-level design and overall coordination.

t: Cultural identity: Huayan studies from the perspective of the Chinese national community
zh: 文化认同：中华民族共同体视野下的华严学
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in February 2025, asks how Huayan (Avatamsaka) Buddhist learning helped bind China's peoples together over a thousand years. Wang Jing argues that Huayan thought, moving from the western frontier to the interior and then to the northern frontier, became a spiritual resource for fostering a sense of the Chinese national community and for the integrated historical process of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised in three parts. The first traces the westward origins of the Huayan Sutra, from translations by Central Asian and Dunhuang-born translators in the Han to Jin periods to the full sutras obtained from Khotan. The second follows the spread of Huayan northwards under the Liao, Western Xia, Jin and Yuan. The third examines Huayan's philosophy of perfect interfusion and its influence on later Chinese thought.

Wang's central claim is that Huayan served as a cultural bond between the interior and the frontiers. The author notes that the sixty-fascicle translation of 418 and the eighty-fascicle version of 699, produced under Empress Wu Zetian with the Khotanese monk Siksananda, linked Khotan and the Central Plains and moved Huayan from sutra study to a formal school. In the Liao, Western Xia, Jin and Yuan, rulers and monks adopted and translated Huayan texts, which Wang reads as direct inheritance of interior Huayan during periods of division. Philosophically, the doctrine of the 'four dharma realms', the 'six characteristics' and the 'ten mysteries', summed up in 'one is all, all is one', is said to dissolve oppositions and justify the coexistence of different peoples. Wang adds that Cheng Hao, Zhu Xi, Lu Jiuyuan and Wang Yangming drew on Huayan ideas.

Wang concludes that Huayan's perfect interfusion promoted exchange and blending among peoples, contributed to the pattern of diversity within unity of the Chinese nation, and underpinned a Neo-Confucian cultural system that supported the Chinese national community in the Song to Qing periods. The piece calls Huayan an important intellectual resource for forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Buddhist history is being linked to the contemporary discourse on national unity and ethnic integration.
quoteEn: Tracing it to its roots, the Huayan philosophy of perfect interfusion can be called an important intellectual resource for forging a strong sense of community of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 追根溯源，华严学的圆融思想堪称铸牢中华民族共同体意识的一种重要思想资源。

glossary.en: sense of the Chinese national community
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A Party-state concept stressing that China's ethnic groups form one national community; since the late 2010s, 'forging a firm sense' of it has been a leading policy theme in ethnic affairs.
A Chinese Buddhist school based on the Avatamsaka (Huayan) Sutra, formalised in the Tang dynasty and known for its doctrine of mutual interpenetration of all phenomena.
A key Huayan idea that all things interpenetrate without obstruction. The author treats it as a basis for harmony among differing peoples and teachings.
Huayan's fourfold scheme of the realm of principle, the realm of phenomena, the unobstructed interpenetration of principle and phenomena, and of phenomena with phenomena.
A formulation associated with the anthropologist Fei Xiaotong, describing the Chinese nation as a unified whole made up of many ethnic groups.

t: Common prosperity: China's "solution" for realising fairness and justice
zh: 共同富裕：实现公平正义的“中国方案”
paras: Wang Li asks how China's experience of fairness and justice should be understood and theorised. The commentary argues that common prosperity is both a practice of fairness and justice and the "signature concept" and core category of a Chinese theory of it, and so offers a "Chinese solution" to the world.

The piece has two parts. The first presents common prosperity as a great practice of socialist fairness and justice. The second turns to its theoretical elevation, arguing that this practice needs its own theory of justice.

In the first part, Wang describes four steps: eliminating absolute poverty through the poverty-alleviation campaign; giving common prosperity broader content, covering material abundance, cultural and spiritual wealth, democracy, rule of law and the environment; relying on the advantages of the socialist system, including multi-level distribution through primary distribution, redistribution and third distribution; and following a two-stage road map from 2020 to 2035 and then to the middle of the century. Wang contends that only socialism can realise common prosperity, and that capitalist approaches to justice can amount only to reform and patching under private ownership. In the second part, Wang holds that China's achievements cannot be explained by any Western school of political philosophy or theory of justice. Common prosperity, in this account, draws on elements of Chinese philosophy and supplies the concepts for a systematic Chinese theory.

Wang concludes that practice, achievements and theoretical summary together give common prosperity a solid scholarly basis as China's contribution on fairness and justice. Read the original if you want a short example of how Chinese academics present common prosperity as a theoretical category that stands apart from Western theories of justice.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is absolutely incompatible with capitalist inequality and polarisation.
quoteZh: 共同富裕与资本主义的不平等和两极分化绝不相容。

glossary.explanation: A goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, in which all people share the fruits of development. It was given fresh emphasis under Xi Jinping from 2021 and is tied to narrowing income and regional gaps.
Distribution through voluntary donations and charity, following primary distribution (market) and redistribution (state taxes and transfers).

t: Vigorously enhancing national cultural soft power and the influence of Chinese culture
zh: 大力提升国家文化软实力和中华文化影响力
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how China should raise its national cultural soft power and the influence of Chinese culture. Liu argues that this task, set out in Xi Jinping's October 2023 instruction and in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), is a basis for building a socialist cultural power and for Chinese modernization.

The piece is organised around five requirements, each introduced with the word "must" and supported by statements from Xi Jinping from 2013, 2018, 2023 and 2024. They concern ideological guidance, traditional culture, international communication, China's image and civilisational exchange.

Liu first holds that the work must be guided by Xi Jinping's thought on culture and must draw on fine traditional culture, whose spiritual markers and creative energy should be distilled and renewed. Second, the author calls for rebuilding the international communication landscape. This means constructing Chinese discourse and narratives, using 5G, artificial intelligence and VR/AR, and building media clusters and an all-media matrix. Messages would be tailored to regions and audiences, with the Belt and Road Initiative as one setting. Third, China should promote its proposals and present itself as a credible, lovable and respectable country. In Liu's account, Xi's statements abroad already portray China as a civilised, Eastern, responsible and socialist major country.

Liu concludes that China should deepen exchange and mutual learning among civilisations. Examples include translating foreign classics, hosting academic conferences and holding international film festivals. The aim is new cultural achievements that join past and present and link China and the West, adding value to Chinese modernization and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the current official framework for cultural soft power and international communication.
quoteEn: Communication capacity determines influence, and discourse power determines the initiative.
quoteZh: 传播力决定影响力，话语权决定主动权。

glossary.explanation: The official Party framing of China's development path, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), which presents it as distinct from Western models.
A body of Xi Jinping's statements on culture, formally put forward in October 2023, which the Party presents as guidance for cultural and ideological work.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's slogan for China's vision of international relations, which stresses shared interests and joint development.
The attractiveness and influence of a country's culture and values, an idea adapted from Joseph Nye's concept and a stated policy goal in China.

t: Grasping the ecological-civilisation value and logic of Chinese modernization
zh: 准确把握中国式现代化的生态文明价值意蕴及逻辑理路
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (February 2025), Wang Qing takes up the 20th Party Congress (2022) formula that Chinese modernization is "a modernization of harmonious coexistence between humanity and nature". Wang argues that this makes ecological civilisation a defining feature of Chinese modernization. In the article's account, it is neither the traditional industrial model of "civilisation without ecology" nor a copy of the Western path of "pollute first, clean up later", and it therefore has values and comparative advantages the Western model cannot match.

The commentary is organised in four sections. The first deals with "lucid waters and lush mountains" and green productive forces; the second with institutions and mechanisms as the basic guarantee of green development; the third with the people-centred stance expressed in the pairing of ecology and livelihood; and the fourth with the joint development of digitalisation and ecologisation. Wang draws throughout on Xi Jinping's statements on ecological civilisation.

Wang's central move is to treat the ecological environment as an internal element of productive forces, so that protecting it is protecting productive forces. On this basis Wang identifies green productive forces with new quality productive forces, driven by green, low-carbon and circular technologies. Wang proposes intensive, innovation-led growth in place of extensive growth, a unified national market for carbon, water, energy and emission rights, regulated capital, and green skills among workers. A second move concerns institutions: the strictest rules and enforcement, clearly defined natural-resource property rights, and mechanisms for realising the value of ecological products. Wang further argues that ecological goods belong within livelihood and social justice, to be expanded through green productive forces and shared through the "three distributions". Finally, digital technologies such as AI, big data and digital twins are said to make ecological governance more precise, systematic and open.

Wang concludes that Chinese modernization, by combining green productive forces, suitable production relations, ecological livelihood and digital-ecological transformation, offers a distinctive and superior model of human–nature harmony. The piece is a short programmatic commentary that sets out the current official line rather than engaging in debate. Read the original if you want a compact view of how Chinese scholars link green development, new quality productive forces, common prosperity and digitalisation within the discourse of ecological civilisation.
quoteEn: Protecting the ecological environment is protecting productive forces, and improving the ecological environment is developing productive forces.
quoteZh: 保护生态环境就是保护生产力、改善生态环境就是发展生产力

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernisation, set out at the 20th Party Congress in 2022 and presented as distinct from Western models. Its listed features include a huge population, common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than by heavy factor inputs.
A stated goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics: prosperity shared by all rather than by a minority, strongly emphasised under Xi Jinping.
A framework in which the market allocates income first, the government redistributes through taxes and transfers second, and voluntary charitable giving and social contributions form the third.

t: Firmly holding the main front of online ideology
zh: 牢牢守住网络意识形态主阵地
paras: Zhao Yuanyuan and Ye Benqian take up how China should secure ideological work in cyberspace, which they call the main battlefield, main front and forefront of ideological struggle in the new era. Drawing on Xi Jinping's statements that there is no national security without cybersecurity and that control of online ideological leadership means safeguarding state sovereignty and political power, they argue that the Party must keep firm leadership, identify core problems, and build up mainstream ideas, culture, values, opinion and technology platforms.

The piece is a short commentary first published by China Theory Net (Zhongguo lilun wang). After an opening on the strategic importance of online ideology, it is organised around seven imperatives, each beginning with the phrase 'must': steady the core of leadership, pinpoint the main problems, sing the main theme, cultivate mainstream culture, promote mainstream values, strengthen mainstream opinion, and build main platforms. A short closing section calls for study of Xi Jinping's thought on cultural work and on building a strong cyber power.

The authors present online ideology as an extension of ideology into cyberspace, marked by virtuality, anonymity, hard-to-control spread, fragmentation and pan-entertainment. For them this calls for the principle of 'the Party manages the internet', with the Party coordinating government, enterprises, society and netizens, resisting capital's manipulation of technological innovation, and upholding the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. They credit campaigns such as 'Qinglang' with improving the online environment but say the ideological struggle has not been decisively won. They warn of Western capitalist infiltration, information cocoons and opinion storms. Marxism, Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and the core socialist values are to lead online content, using party media and popular formats. Mainstream culture is to draw on traditional and revolutionary heritage and oppose historical nihilism. Authoritative information should crowd out rumours, and breakthroughs in core technologies such as chips, operating systems and quantum communication are needed, since the authors hold that whoever controls advanced network technology controls ideological leadership.

The authors conclude that online ideological work is a 'war without gunsmoke' and that, in a line they quote, failing the internet test means failing the test of long-term rule. They propose persistent study of Xi Jinping Thought, firm Party leadership, Marxism's guiding position, and a technologically advanced security barrier, which they say will supply ideological backing for building a strong country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese theoretical discourse frames internet governance as ideological security.
quoteEn: The contest of ideologies is also a contest of platforms, and the main front and main platforms must be strengthened.
quoteZh: 意识形态的较量也是平台的较量，必须加强主阵地、主平台建设。

glossary.explanation: A formulation from the Party's 2021 resolution on history, affirming Xi Jinping's position as the 'core' of the Party and the guiding role of his thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the Central Committee's authority and centralised, unified leadership.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A principle of Party leadership over internet governance, listed first among the 'ten adherences' for cyberspace and informatisation work set out in 2023.
In official usage, a label for views that question or negate the Party's revolutionary history and the path of socialism.
A set of twelve values at national, social and individual levels, promoted by the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

t: Telling the story of the peaceful character of Chinese modernization well
zh: 讲好中国式现代化的和平性故事
paras: Wei Junquan takes up the claim, set out in the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), that Chinese modernization is a modernization that follows the path of peaceful development. The article links this to Xi Jinping's description of peacefulness as one of the "outstanding characteristics" of Chinese civilization. Wei argues that this peaceful quality is a core cultural marker and a key point of support for building China's national image in international communication.

The article has three parts. The first traces the intellectual sources of peacefulness in Confucian, Mohist and Daoist thought and in the history of China's external exchanges. The second looks at how peacefulness is enacted in communication practice, covering relations between humans and nature and relations between people and between states. The third sets out its contemporary value through a comparison between Chinese and Western civilizations. Wei draws on the Chinese-language literature on communication studies and Chinese modernization.

Wei argues that the idea of harmony (he) runs through Chinese thought, from "harmonizing all nations" and the ideal of great harmony to the Tang, Ming and Qing formulations of ethnic and international relations. Examples such as Zhang Qian, Jianzhen and Zheng He are presented as reciprocal, peaceful exchange. In the second part, Wei contrasts a Western capitalist logic that treats nature as a resource to be dominated and so produces alienation with a Chinese view of nature as a medium and a subject, expressed in "harmony between humanity and nature". In international relations, Wei sets peaceful development against the "clash of civilizations" thesis, the law of the jungle, zero-sum games and hegemonism, and contrasts Western atomistic individualism with a Chinese holistic way of thinking. Wei cites other scholars to argue that Western capital accumulation involved colonial plunder and a hegemonic logic.

Wei concludes that peacefulness draws on China's own historical development and on traditional culture, and also responds to survival and communication problems common to humankind. The article presents the Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives, a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative as practices that show China's concern for world peace and offer a model different from Western modernization. Wei suggests that stressing peacefulness can strengthen the reach of Chinese civilization and help build a cooperative international environment. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese communication scholars link traditional ideas of harmony to current foreign-policy discourse and national-image building.
quoteEn: Peace is both an important spiritual marker and cultural essence of the modern strength of Chinese civilization, a key vector for strengthening its communicative power and influence, and an important fulcrum for constructing national image in the field of international communication.
quoteZh: 和平既是中华文明现代力量的重要精神标识和文化精髓，又是增强中华文明传播力影响力的关键矢量，是国际传播场域中国家形象建构的重要支点。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), of China's own path to modernization. It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping. It calls for shared development, security and cooperation among states.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries in Asia, Africa and Europe.

glossary.zh: 全球发展倡议、全球安全倡议、全球文明倡议
glossary.pinyin: Quánqiú Fāzhǎn Chàngyì, Quánqiú Ānquán Chàngyì, Quánqiú Wénmíng Chàngyì
glossary.en: the Global Development, Security and Civilization Initiatives
glossary.explanation: Three initiatives proposed by Xi Jinping (2021, 2022 and 2023) as China's contributions to global governance and to dialogue among civilizations.
Five features named by Xi Jinping in 2023: continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness. They are used in official discourse to describe Chinese civilization.

t: Raising urban safety and resilience through new-type urban infrastructure construction
zh: 以新型城市基础设施建设提升城市安全韧性
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 7 February 2025, Li Zhao asks how cities can become safer and more resilient as the risks they face grow more complex. The commentary argues that building new-type urban infrastructure, which combines new-generation information technology with urban construction and governance, is the route to resilient cities. It takes as its basis the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and a November 2024 central opinion that sets a goal of notable results by 2030.

The piece first explains what new-type urban infrastructure does: it makes city operations safer, more orderly, smarter and more efficient, and it supports new quality productive forces and high-quality development. It then sets out four areas of work: government guidance, institutional mechanisms, scientific and technological innovation, and social participation. Party leadership is to run through all of them.

On government guidance, Li calls for top-level design, integrated use of infrastructure to avoid duplicated construction, a standards and evaluation system, and risk-prevention and data-security mechanisms. On institutions, Li proposes breaking down data barriers, a diversified financing system with government investment as guide and enterprises as the main body, and life-cycle management that moves from one-way regulation toward collaborative governance. On innovation, Li urges breakthroughs in key technologies and multidisciplinary talent training. On participation, state-owned enterprises should lead, private firms should get fairer market access, and experts and residents should take part.

Li concludes that these actors should each contribute their strengths so as to form a strong joint force for building resilient cities. The article is a policy-oriented explanation of official guidance, not an empirical study. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy agenda for urban digital infrastructure and resilience in early 2025.
quoteEn: The key to scientific and technological innovation lies in talent; building new-type urban infrastructure must rely on data-driven and talent-driven development.
quoteZh: 科技创新的关键在人才，新型城市基础设施建设要靠数据驱动和人才驱动。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation.
Official term for growth that stresses quality, innovation and efficiency over scale. It has been the Party's central economic goal since 2017.

glossary.zh: 新型城市基础设施建设
glossary.explanation: Urban infrastructure that fuses new-generation information technology with urban construction and governance, such as data platforms, sensing networks and building information models.
Cities able to withstand, adapt to and recover from disasters, accidents and other shocks. The term appears in recent central policy documents on urban safety.

t: Building an open environment for scientific and technological innovation with global competitiveness
zh: 打造具有全球竞争力的科技创新开放环境
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily, Wu argues that Chinese modernization depends on the modernization of science and technology, and that high-quality development needs innovation to create new momentum. Citing the Central Commission for Deepening Overall Reform (June 2024) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), the commentary holds that building an open innovation environment with global competitiveness is essential to self-reliant innovation and is an inherent requirement of developing new quality productive forces.

The short piece sets out three areas of work: deepening reform of the science and technology system, gathering innovation talent, and integrating into global innovation networks. Each is presented as a list of policy measures.

On institutional reform, Wu treats major technological innovation as the core of new quality productive forces. The author calls for better planning and management of science and technology programmes, more investment in basic research, and a stronger position for enterprises as the main innovators. On talent, Wu calls the workforce of researchers the first resource of innovation and proposes training domestic talent through closer links between education, industry and research, while recruiting top overseas talent under more open policies. On openness, Wu cites Xi Jinping on taking the initiative to join global innovation networks. The author proposes wider institutional opening, cross-border innovation programmes, joint science and technology cooperation zones under the Belt and Road Initiative, and stronger intellectual property management and technology security.

Wu concludes that these measures together would build a more coordinated, open and efficient innovation system that supports high-quality development. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary links science and technology policy, talent policy and international openness to new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: Talent is the first resource of innovation. Without a talent advantage, there can be no innovation advantage, no scientific and technological advantage, and no industrial advantage.
quoteZh: 人才是创新的第一资源。没有人才优势，就不可能有创新优势、科技优势、产业优势。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than by traditional resource-heavy growth.
The official name for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, set out since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
An official goal that replaces speed-focused growth with growth based on innovation, efficiency and sustainability.
China's international infrastructure and cooperation initiative, launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.

t: Empowering the study of Chinese civilization with digital-intelligence methods
zh: 以数智方法赋能中华文明研究
paras: Writing in People's Daily, Chen Yunsong asks how big data and artificial intelligence can be used to deepen research on Chinese civilization and the fine traditional culture it carries. Citing Xi Jinping's calls for deeper study of Chinese civilization and for the creative transformation of traditional culture, Chen argues that 'digital-intelligence' methods should complement, not replace, traditional humanistic scholarship. The piece is a short commentary, not a research article.

The article is organised in four parts: scientific measurement of culture and civilization; revealing the deep structure of civilizational texts; capturing the beauty of cultural heritage; and strengthening civilization studies through the principle of upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground. Chen's examples include book-corpus word frequencies, topic modelling of Tang and Qing poetry, joint image–text analysis of literati painting, and Nanjing University's digital atlas of Chinese ancient cities.

Chen's central claim is that soft indicators such as cultural influence and renown are hard to measure with questionnaires because of researcher bias, whereas large-scale book, internet, media and academic data allow multidimensional indices of cultural symbols. Topic models and deep learning can survey corpora no individual scholar could read, for example the roughly 50,000 surviving Tang poems, and make deep structures visible. For heritage, historical satellite images, lidar, drones and GIS can rebuild old city fabric and move protection from static records to dynamic monitoring. Chen calls this approach 'distant reading of culture' and likens its relation to traditional scholarship to that of telescope and microscope.

Chen concludes that the method can help correct bias in Western databases and large language models, speed the building of China's independent knowledge system in philosophy and social sciences, and raise the discourse power of Chinese civilization globally. The author also notes limits, namely high technical thresholds and dependence on massive data and complex algorithms, so it must be combined with traditional methods. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic statement of how computational humanities is being framed within China's cultural-confidence and cultural-subjectivity agenda.
quoteEn: Empowering the study of Chinese civilization with digital-intelligence methods is precisely a vivid practice of strengthening cultural construction by upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground.
quoteZh: 以数智方法赋能中华文明研究，正是守正创新加强文化建设的生动实践。

glossary.explanation: A computational approach to culture that analyses very large text and image corpora statistically rather than reading individual works closely. It echoes the 'distant reading' idea in digital humanities.
A compound of 'digital' and 'intelligent' technologies, referring to big data and artificial intelligence used together.

glossary.en: upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground
glossary.explanation: A principle in Xi Jinping's cultural policy that calls for keeping to Marxism and core traditions while innovating.

t: The world significance of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的世界意义
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily in February 2025, asks what Chinese modernization means beyond China. Yang Guangbin argues that it has changed China itself, rewritten the paradigm of world modernization and created a new form of human civilization.

The piece has three sections. The first compares Chinese modernization with Western modernization and traces China's own 'relay race' from the founding of the People's Republic through reform and opening up to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second discusses benefits to the Global South. The third turns to civilizational questions.

Yang characterises Western modernization as monopoly-based: it spread the capitalist 'modern world system' through force and industrialization, and, citing Thomas Piketty, channelled large flows of income from the Global South to wealthy countries. In Yang's reading, US containment of Chinese technology reflects an effort to keep a monopoly on advanced productive forces. By contrast, the article credits China's market, industrial base and independent R&D with breaking such monopolies. It cites low-cost smartphones and photovoltaics, Chinese firms' role in mobile broadband (Mexican internet use rising from 44% to 75%, 2014–2023) and aid projects that it says strengthen governance in recipient states.

Yang concludes that Chinese modernization, rooted in traditional culture and the essence of scientific socialism, offers a model of shared development, common security and mutual learning among civilizations rather than conflict. It is presented as an example for Global South countries seeking independent modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official People's Daily framing of Chinese modernization as an alternative to the Western path.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has rewritten the traditional liberal narrative of globalization and is a major transcendence of Western modernization in theory and practice.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化改写了传统的自由主义全球化叙事，是对西方式现代化理论和实践的重大超越。

glossary.explanation: A concept formally set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022) to describe China's own path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.
A term for developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America, which Chinese official discourse uses to frame China's partnerships and solidarity.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: An official phrase describing Chinese modernization as a civilizational alternative to the Western model, introduced in Party documents around 2021.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: China explores a new model of global development
zh: 中国探索全球发展新模式
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily, asks what path of development can replace the Western model, which the authors say has lost its capacity to guide sustainable global development. Li and Xu argue that Chinese modernization breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization and offers the world a new development model and path.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's statement that no single modernization model or standard exists. It then moves through three sections: the three global initiatives and the Belt and Road Initiative as practical expressions of a plural development model; a critique of the Western model's single, one-dimensional modernity; and an account of how Chinese modernization surpasses it, with the China–Africa partnership as the main example.

The authors trace the Western model to the age of exploration and describe it as producing North–South domination, dependence, widening inequality and ecological damage. Against this, they present Chinese modernization as marked by strong leadership and long-term planning, common prosperity, balanced material and cultural progress, harmony between humanity and nature, peaceful development and strategic resolve. They cite the China–Laos railway, Central Asian energy cooperation, and wind and solar equipment exports as evidence. They also point to the basic socialist economic system, in which public ownership underpins fairness and the non-public sector drives vitality.

Li and Xu conclude that Chinese modernization is leading Global South countries toward a fairer, more sustainable and more inclusive path, and that it supports a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary contrasts Chinese modernization with the Western model for an international development audience.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that "modernization equals Westernization" and presents a different picture of what modernization can be.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，展现了现代化的另一幅图景

glossary.explanation: The Communist Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models. It has been prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A term for developing countries, mostly in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Chinese official discourse uses it to stress solidarity among these countries.
A global infrastructure and investment programme launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China to countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
An official goal of shared affluence for all citizens, stressed by Xi Jinping as a defining feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of international relations, calling for joint global governance and shared development.

t: Building a higher-level rule-of-law China
zh: 建设更高水平的法治中国
paras: Zhang Wenxian, a senior jurist, asks what is meant by the call to build a "higher-level rule-of-law China". The phrase first appeared as a task in the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and was restated by Xi Jinping in August 2024. Zhang argues that it amounts to building a higher-level socialist rule-of-law state, and that its aim is a modernized "country strong through law". The piece was published in Beijing Daily in January 2025.

Zhang says the "higher level" has three progressive aspects: making all areas of state work subject to law, building a China of "good law and good governance", and implementing a strategy of becoming a country strong through law (fazhi qiangguo). The article then describes six features of such a country and ends with an assessment of China's present position.

On the first aspect, Zhang lists four tasks: placing national work, state governance, specialised legal work and domestic and foreign-related rule of law all on a legal track. On the second, Zhang contrasts instrumentalist legal culture in ancient China and formalist Western legal culture with a model of "good law and good governance". Good law is scientific, embodies good values, is well drafted and is well implemented. Zhang presents China's shift from "legal system" to "rule of law" as a move from formal rule of law to a combination of formal and substantive rule of law. On the third aspect, Zhang traces the idea to the Legalist thinker Han Feizi and the "strengthening the state by upholding law" tradition, which Xi has cited. Zhang adds that the Central Committee has not yet formally proposed "strong through law", though Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law already contains it. The six features include law as a core social value, the authority of the Constitution, protection of rights and restraint of power, strong voice in global governance, and integration of law with digital technology.

Zhang concludes that China is already a "big country in law", having built a legal system in 45 years from the "seven laws in one day" of 1979, but is not yet strong through law. The shift from the first to the second is described as a historic strategic transformation that demands great effort. Only then, Zhang argues, can the "rule-of-law dream" and the "strong-country dream" flourish together. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a leading Chinese legal theorist interprets the official goal of a higher-level rule-of-law China.
quoteEn: But, speaking realistically, China is not yet a "country strong through law".
quoteZh: 但是，实事求是地说，我国还不是一个“法治强国”。

glossary.explanation: A goal of making law a source of national strength, placed by the author alongside other "strong country" strategies such as those for industry, technology and education. The author notes it has not yet been formally proposed by the Central Committee.

A model of rule of law in which laws are themselves good in content and in drafting, and are well implemented. The author presents it as a Party Central Committee formulation that draws on Chinese and foreign legal traditions.

glossary.en: Xi Jinping's thought on the rule of law
glossary.explanation: The body of Xi Jinping's statements on law and governance, formally adopted as the Party's guiding thinking on rule of law in 2020.

keywords: Xi Jinping thought on the rule of law

t: Promoting new results in the Party's discipline building
zh: 推动党的纪律建设不断取得新成效
paras: This commentary, published in the PLA Daily on 27 January 2025, responds to Xi Jinping's speech at the Fourth Plenary Session of the 20th Central Commission for Discipline Inspection. Deng, Zhang and Zhang argue that discipline building must occupy a prominent place within full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and must be pursued persistently, strictly and regularly in order to produce new results.

The piece is organised in three parts. The first explains why discipline building matters at present, the second sets out the main ideas Xi Jinping has put forward since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and the third lists practical measures for the new journey.

The authors give three reasons for the importance of discipline. It is, they say, necessary to solve the problems unique to a large party, such as keeping unity of thought and will and a healthy political ecology. It is also needed to preserve the Party's vanguard character and purity under long-term rule, and to let the Party's self-reform lead the social revolution of Chinese modernization. They then summarise Xi's ideas: discipline as the fundamental means of governing the Party, political discipline and political rules as the first priority, a strict tone with no leniency and no exemption for the many or the minor, and a balance of strict management with care and encouragement. Here they cite the Two Establishes, the Two Upholds and the "four forms" of supervision and discipline enforcement.

On practice, the authors call for continuous discipline education so that members know the Party constitution and regulations and respect boundaries. They also call for firm enforcement, so that rules become a rigid constraint, and for a chain of responsibility in which Party secretaries bear primary responsibility and leaders, the "key minority", set an example. They present discipline building as a long and arduous task, because full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is "always on the road". Read the original if you want a concise example of how military-affiliated Party writers present the official line on discipline building after the 2025 plenum.
quoteEn: Party discipline is the lifeblood of the Party; discipline building is a key link in Party building and also a key measure for solving these problems.
quoteZh: 党的纪律是党的生命，纪律建设是党的建设的关键环节，也是解决这些难题的关键举措。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping since 2014 that covers Party discipline, anti-corruption work and internal Party regulation.
The official name for China's path of development, set out by Xi Jinping at the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A formula adopted in 2021–22 affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the Party as a whole, and the guiding role of his thought.
The official requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Party Central Committee.

Official term for the Party's efforts to purify and renew itself from within. It is often presented as a second answer, alongside popular supervision, to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and decline.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: Advancing new quality productive forces faster through deep industrial transformation and upgrading
zh: 以产业深度转型升级推动新质生产力加快发展
paras: In this commentary for Guangming Daily (27 January 2025), Cao Wenhong argues that deep industrial transformation and upgrading is one of the key forms through which new quality productive forces develop. Cao holds that it must be the main direction of effort if new quality productive forces are to be developed faster.

The piece opens with a definition of deep transformation and upgrading and a statement of the problems facing China's industrial structure. It then has two numbered sections. The first covers how industry itself should change: upgrading traditional industries and promoting coordination among industries. The second treats the institutional and policy side, arguing that the task is also a reform question.

Cao notes that traditional industries remain the base of the economy but suffer from distorted factor prices, low-end lock-in in value chains and pollution. The author calls for applying artificial intelligence and big data, green and low-carbon transition, closer cooperation along industrial chains and stronger links between enterprises. Cao stresses, citing Xi Jinping, that developing new quality productive forces does not mean abandoning traditional industry, and that local conditions and one-size-fits-all models must be considered. On institutions, Cao distinguishes strategic emerging industries from future industries and proposes different policy support for each, including pilot zones for the latter. The article also calls for stronger top-level design.

Cao concludes that the Party's unified leadership, a new whole-nation system, a unified national market and stable, transparent, law-based policy should make deep industrial upgrading and new quality productive forces reinforce each other. Read the original if you want a short official-style statement of how industrial policy is linked to the new quality productive forces agenda in early 2025.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces does not refer to one or several specific fields of science and technology, but to social activity that raises the scientific and technological added value of each unit of product on the basis of technological progress.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力并非特指一个或几个特定的科技领域，而是指基于科技进步提高单位产品科技附加值的社会活动。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, high efficiency and high quality, as opposed to growth based on resource and capital inputs.
An official term for mobilising state, Party, market and research resources nationwide for major scientific and technological goals, adapted from the earlier 'whole-nation system'.
A policy goal of removing local barriers and applying uniform rules on property rights, market access and fair competition across China.
An official category for high-technology sectors, such as new energy, new materials and information technology, that the state designates as priorities for growth.

t: Deepening reform to promote the deep integration of the real and digital economies
zh: 持续深化改革促进“实数”深度融合发展
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2025, asks how institutional reform can promote the deep integration of the real (physical) economy and the digital economy, abbreviated in Chinese as "shi-shu" integration. Xiang Xiaomei argues that such integration should be the main line for developing new quality productive forces and will supply lasting momentum for Chinese modernization. The piece takes its cue from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which made high-quality development the first task of building a modern socialist country.

The article has three parts. It first explains what integration means and why it matters globally and domestically. It then sets out three ways integration serves new quality productive forces: breakthrough innovation, the upgrading of traditional industries, and cross-sector cooperation. It closes with four policy areas that need strengthening.

Xiang stresses that the real economy is the foundation of the national economy and that digital technology must strengthen it ("以数强实") rather than drift away from it. Integration is not blind or superficial digitisation, the author says, but the use of digital knowledge and information as key production factors, driven by cloud computing, AI, blockchain and the Internet of Things. Xiang holds that integration shortens R&D cycles and lowers uncertainty, helps traditional industries raise total factor productivity on both supply and demand sides, and gives rise to platform economy, smart agriculture, humanoid robots, quantum information and the low-altitude economy. The author acknowledges remaining weak points and says integration needs managerial and institutional change as well as technological innovation.

Xiang proposes four sets of policies. The first is a policy system for digital technology innovation, drawing on the new whole-nation system and integrated reform of education, science and talent. The second covers digital industrialisation and industrial digitalisation, including support for manufacturers and small firms and an "AI Plus" initiative. The third is the marketisation of data factors, through national computing infrastructure, data trading rules and solutions to problems of data ownership and sharing. The fourth is a supportive framework of financial reform, a unified national market, high-level opening up and data security, because new productive forces require matching new relations of production. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a provincial Chinese academic presents the policy agenda linking the digital economy to new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: Promoting deep integration of the real and digital economies depends on innovation in technology and business models, and calls even more for change in management and institutions.
quoteZh: 促进“实数”深度融合，既离不开技术和业态模式层面的创新，更呼唤管理和制度层面的变革。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and emerging industries, as opposed to resource-heavy growth.
The official name for China's path of modernisation, presented by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
An official economic goal, stressed since 2017, that favours innovation, efficiency and sustainability over pure growth in speed or scale.
An official term for mobilising state, market and research resources nationally to achieve breakthroughs in key technologies.

t: Using the deep integration of the digital and real economies to speed up new quality productive forces
zh: 以数实深度融合为抓手加快发展新质生产力
paras: This newspaper commentary asks how new quality productive forces can be developed faster. He and Chen answer that the deep integration of the digital economy and the real economy, which they call 'digital-real integration', should be the main lever. They describe it as a typical form of new quality productive forces, resting on digital technology and the use of data as a factor of production. They cite Xi Jinping's Politburo study session and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) as the policy basis.

The article is organised around four dimensions of integration: technology, factors of production, industry and institutions. Each section explains how integration drives new quality productive forces and then lists measures to advance it.

On technology, the authors say digital tools shorten R&D cycles and create a closed loop of research, production and feedback. They call for breakthroughs in core technologies through the new-type whole-nation system and for faster conversion of results into production. On factors, they argue that data-centred recombination of factors needs clear data property rights, a unified market, and the smart upgrading of labour, capital and land. On industry, they call for digital transformation of traditional sectors, cross-sector integration of business forms, and a modern industrial system. On institutions, they argue that new production relations must suit the new forces. They assign roles to government (standards and infrastructure), the market (supply and demand for digital goods) and enterprises (integrated business processes).

The authors conclude that integration across all four dimensions would produce a unified and efficient ecosystem for developing new quality productive forces. Read the original if you want a short, policy-oriented example of how Chinese economists link the digital economy to the official agenda of new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: To speed up the cultivation and development of new quality productive forces, deep digital-real integration must be the key lever, continuously advancing revolutionary technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors, and deep industrial transformation and upgrading.
quoteZh: 加快培育和发展新质生产力，必须以数实深度融合为重要抓手，持续推进技术革命性突破、生产要素创新性配置和产业深度转型升级。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and innovative factor allocation, rather than by traditional resource-intensive growth.
Shorthand for the deep integration of the digital economy with the real (physical, industrial) economy, as used in recent Party policy documents.
A state-coordinated approach that mobilises national resources for key technological breakthroughs, combining government planning with market mechanisms.
An official term for an advanced, integrated industrial structure that links the real economy with technology, finance and human resources.

t: Exploring a new path for coordinated urban–rural and regional development in Guangdong
zh: 探索广东城乡区域协调发展新路径
paras: Yue Sheng's commentary, first published in the People's Daily in January 2025, asks how Guangdong can tackle uneven urban–rural and regional development, which Xi Jinping has called the province's biggest obstacle to high-quality development. The author argues that the "Hundred-County, Thousand-Town, Ten-Thousand-Village High-Quality Development Project" (the "Hundred-Thousand-Ten Thousand Project") is a provincial-level innovation in Chinese modernization. In Yue's account, after several years of practice it has produced results and experience that can be drawn on elsewhere.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why the project matters, the second reports results under four headings, and the third sets out lessons. Yue presents the project as modelled on the earlier "Ten Million Project" and centred on the county as the point of leverage. The four headings are county economies, town renewal, village revitalisation and urban–rural integration.

In the first part, Yue describes the project as key to regional coordination, county vitality, rural revitalisation and grassroots governance. Guangdong is said to promote strong counties, which in turn lift towns and villages, under the Party's overall leadership. The results come mostly as figures the author reports. They include 32 counties growing faster than the provincial average in the first half of 2024, 15 industrial transfer platforms and 124 towns among China's top thousand. They also include 22 national modern agricultural industrial parks and a 11.4 billion yuan provincial special fund for 2024.

Yue distils five lessons. These are combining an effective market with an effective government under Party leadership, following the new development philosophy and building new urban–rural relations, and putting people first and mobilising society. The last two are using reform to remove the urban–rural dual structure, and persistence through the "one-three-five-ten" timetable of goals. Yue concludes that Guangdong will keep pursuing the project to offer its experience to Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want an official-style overview of Guangdong's county-centred rural strategy, with the provincial statistics and policy mechanisms it cites.
quoteEn: When counties are strong, the province is strong; when counties are vibrant, the whole province is vibrant.
quoteZh: 县域强则省域强，县域活则全省活。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept, elaborated since the 20th Party Congress (2022), of a distinctive path of modernization with features such as a huge population and common prosperity.

glossary.zh: 百县千镇万村高质量发展工程
glossary.pinyin: Bǎi xiàn qiān zhèn wàn cūn gāozhìliàng fāzhǎn gōngchéng
glossary.en: Hundred-County, Thousand-Town, Ten-Thousand-Village High-Quality Development Project
glossary.explanation: A Guangdong provincial programme, abbreviated as the "Hundred-Thousand-Ten Thousand Project", aimed at narrowing urban–rural and regional gaps by developing counties, towns and villages. It was modelled on Zhejiang's "Ten Million Project".
The guiding framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth that is more balanced, innovative and sustainable.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to develop rural industry, environment, governance and living standards.

t: The "state" perspective on building Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化建设的“国家”视角
paras: This short commentary in the Chinese Social Sciences Today (24 January 2025) asks what role the state plays in building Chinese modernization. Wang Jiangcheng argues that the state's capacity to set development goals, govern effectively and safeguard security is central to realising the Party's task of building a modern socialist country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised under three headings: national development goals, state governance effectiveness, and national security capacity. Each is tied to Party documents, including the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), the 20th Party Congress report (2022) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

On development, Wang says the "Five-sphere Integrated Plan" gives development a growing holistic character, with the countryside and ethnic border regions named as the two areas that must be broken through. Urban–rural integration is presented as the basic strategy for rural modernization. In border regions, the Party's line of forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation is said to give all reform and development its meaning. On governance, Wang describes a "developmental governance" model and argues that institutional strengths must be converted into governance effectiveness, with Party leadership as the fundamental political guarantee and the rule of law as the path. On security, Wang holds that without national security there can be no modernization, and singles out non-traditional threats such as information security, national identity in ethnic and religious fields, and international public opinion.

Wang concludes that the three capacities together underpin Chinese modernization, and that security work needs stronger core competitiveness in the fields mentioned. Read the original if you want a brief, official-line overview of how Party scholars frame the state's developmental, governance and security roles, including its emphasis on rural and ethnic border regions.
quoteEn: National security is the precondition and guarantee for the continued advance of national modernization; without national security there can be no national modernization.
quoteZh: 国家安全是国家现代化持续向前的前提和保障，没有国家安全，就没有国家现代化。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to a modern socialist country, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022).
The overall layout of socialism with Chinese characteristics, covering economic, political, cultural, social and ecological development, formalised at the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: forging a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding line for ethnic affairs, emphasising a shared national identity across ethnic groups.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's official long-term national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream.

t: The Belt and Road Initiative reconstructs international communication capacity
zh: “一带一路”重构国际传播力
paras: Wang Min, writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2025, asks how China can overcome its difficulty in making its voice heard internationally. The author argues that since the Second World War the international communication order has been dominated by Western developed states, leaving developing countries in economic dependence and what the article calls cultural colonisation. Wang contends that the Belt and Road Initiative offers China a new opening to rebuild its communication capacity and to change that order, in the context of building a community with a shared future for mankind.

This short commentary is organised around three headings: economic foundation, cultural guidance and media reinforcement. Each is presented as a source of a different strength in China's international communication.

On the economic side, Wang argues that infrastructure and investment projects reshape city structures and trade links, weaken existing dependency relations and give China concrete, visible achievements to point to. The author cites National Bureau of Statistics data on rising trade with partner countries and says these results undermine the Western "power expansion" reporting frame. On culture, Wang points to the digital Silk Road, the Sino-Saudi animated film Kong Xiaoxi and Hakim, and regular Belt and Road festivals and expos, arguing that communication shifts from government-led to multi-actor, so that storytellers become the world rather than China alone. On media, Wang calls for more multilingual reporting and says themes such as the green Belt and Road widen the content of Chinese media.

Wang concludes that the initiative is an international communication practice under the community with a shared future for mankind, expressing both hard and soft power. The author holds that it gives developing countries visibility as concrete economies and cultures rather than a vague group. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese scholars link the Belt and Road Initiative to discourse power and international communication.
quoteEn: Economic foundation, cultural guidance and media reinforcement are important opportunities for China, within the Belt and Road Initiative, to keep strengthening its international communication capacity and open up the international communication landscape.
quoteZh: 经济奠基、文化引路、媒体增力，是中国在“一带一路”倡议中不断增强国际传播力、打开国际传播格局的重要机遇。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2012–13, calling for shared development and cooperation among states. The article treats it as the value framework for the Belt and Road Initiative.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with partner countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
The capacity to set agendas and shape how issues are framed in international debate. Chinese authors often treat its unequal distribution as a feature of Western dominance.

t: Understanding and advancing the development of new quality productive forces through systems thinking
zh: 以系统思维理解和推进新质生产力发展
paras: Yan Guohua, writing in the China Social Sciences Today in January 2025, argues that new quality productive forces should be understood and promoted through systems thinking. In Yan's account, they are not a simple combination of advanced productive forces and industrial structure but a complex systematic undertaking. It depends on iterating new technologies and industries and on a coordinated leap in the related elements, so it calls for overall planning and a macro perspective.

The short commentary is organised in three parts. It first sets out the systemic features of new quality productive forces, then their systemic value and goals, and finally a path for advancing them. Throughout, it builds on Xi Jinping's statements on the subject and on the idea of the systems approach as a basic way of thinking and working.

Yan reads the concept through three lenses: its internal elements, its form of development and its conditions of formation. Internally, it follows an "elements–structure–function" logic built on labourers, means of labour, objects of labour and their optimised combination. In form, it is a deep transformation that couples economic, cultural, social and ecological dimensions rather than a local upgrade of traditional productive forces. On goals, Yan holds that its underlying logic is the new development philosophy, high-quality development, Chinese modernization and the people's needs for a better life. Productive forces are also described as the "key" to historical materialism. Yan presents five paths: renewing ideas, including avoiding a rush into the field and the creation of bubbles; reforming institutions and mechanisms to remove blockages; applying digital and intelligent technologies; raising the quality of talent; and improving the wider social atmosphere.

Yan concludes that the whole of society and many actors must act together, since a change in one element affects the whole. The social atmosphere should encourage innovation, openness and tolerance of failure, and should support sound evaluation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academic commentary on new quality productive forces is framed through Xi Jinping's statements and the systems approach.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are not merely an innovation in technological form; they are expressed above all as an innovation in the form of ideas.
quoteZh: 新质生产力不是单纯的技术形态创新，更体现为观念形态创新。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by innovation, high technology, high efficiency and high quality, in place of traditional growth models.
The official set of principles introduced in 2015: innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
The official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from speed-oriented growth to growth that is more efficient, innovative and sustainable.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

t: Public space as the fullest expression of the core meaning of the "people's city" concept
zh: 公共空间充分彰显人民城市理念的核心要义
paras: Li Jun asks how urban sociology can study the "people's city" concept through public space. The author argues that public space is its most direct and fullest expression, and that studying it can link practice to theory and build a Chinese-style urban sociology able to talk with Western urban space research.

The commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2025, first reviews Western work from the Chicago School to Lefebvre, Harvey and the "new urban sociology". It then turns to Chinese research on public space and to Shanghai's public-space system since Xi Jinping put forward the people's city idea in 2019. It ends with fieldwork-based problems and proposed reforms.

Li reads Western urban space as chiefly dominated by capital, with public space threatened by commodification and privatisation. Chinese studies, in Li's account, stress power and capital logics and call for more weight on "life logic". Li proposes that public space should embody four aspects of the people's character: publicness, diversity, participation and perceived experience. The author lists problems such as wasted space, excessive self-run provision and rigid functions. Li proposes supply-side reform in four areas: guiding public spirit, with Party-building leadership visible in more community spaces; stressing public governance and deliberation; finer planning around the 15-minute community life circle; and integrated, professional, socialised and "Internet Plus" operation.

Li concludes that public space should be run so that services, deliberation and community governance operate together, and so that people's sense of gain and belonging serves as the test of success. Li ties this to common prosperity and whole-process people's democracy. Read the original if you want a Shanghai sociologist's short account of how the people's city concept is turned into public-space policy and research agendas.
quoteEn: It can be said that public space is the most direct embodiment and fullest expression of the people's city.
quoteZh: 可以说，公共空间是人民城市最直观的体现和最充分的彰显。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward during an inspection of Shanghai in 2019 ("people's cities are built by the people and for the people"). It guides urban construction and governance in China.
A Chinese policy goal of prosperity shared by all, emphasised in Party discourse especially since the 2010s.
An official term for China's democratic model, which stresses popular participation at every stage of decision-making and not only at elections.

t: Attitudes and principles for promoting exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations
zh: 推动文明交流互鉴的态度和原则
paras: This commentary, published in Study Times in January 2025, takes up the recent publication of the Outline for Studying Xi Jinping Thought on Culture.
