Shao Sheng argues that Xi Jinping's three statements of 2014 on civilizations (that they are colourful, equal and inclusive) set out the correct attitude and principles for exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations, and that they help in addressing a complex international situation and global challenges.

The piece first summarises the Outline's account of the Party's position since the 18th Party Congress (2012), then takes the three principles in turn. Each is illustrated with historical cases: ancient river-valley civilizations and the spread of bronze metallurgy, the Arab synthesis of knowledge from several civilizations, the Silk Road and the monk Xuanzang, and the cultural meeting point of Dunhuang.

On diversity, Shao holds that civilizational variety arises from differences in natural environment and is a dialectical unity of diversity and identity, so progress lies in many civilizations flourishing and influencing one another rather than in one dominating. On equality, the author presents every civilization as a treasure of humanity and says that exchange requires discarding arrogance and prejudice, citing Xuanzang's two-way transmission of Buddhist and Chinese texts between China and India. On inclusiveness, Shao argues that closed civilizations decline and that Chinese civilization has endured because it has kept absorbing outside influences, as at Dunhuang.

Shao concludes that global problems such as environmental crisis, economic inequality and social unrest cannot be met by any single civilization. The author calls for respecting diversity, promoting equal dialogue and fostering inclusive development, and describes this as both a historical responsibility of the Chinese nation and a shared aspiration of the world's peoples. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party media present Xi Jinping's civilizational principles with historical illustrations.
quoteEn: A civilization that closes itself off will inevitably decline; only through openness and acceptance can a civilization renew itself and regain vitality.
quoteZh: 文明的自我封闭必然导致衰退，只有在开放与接纳中，文明才能实现自我更新，焕发活力。

glossary.explanation: A body of ideas on cultural work attributed to Xi Jinping and promoted in Party theory since 2023. The Outline for Studying it is a study guide published in late 2024.

glossary.en: exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations
glossary.explanation: A standard official formula for the idea that civilizations should learn from one another on an equal footing instead of clashing or ranking each other.

t: Building a sound policy and institutional system requires upholding "people's wellbeing comes first"
zh: 构建合理的政策制度体系要坚持“民生为大”
paras: This commentary, first published in Study Times in January 2025, takes up Xi Jinping's statement that under Chinese modernization "people's wellbeing comes first". Guan Xinping asks how a sound system of social policy can be built to deliver it. The author argues that economic growth must be matched by better social policy, and that the central task is a policy system organised around three types of livelihood provision: universal, foundational and safety-net.

The piece has four parts. It first explains why the principle matters for Chinese modernization, then defines the three types of provision. It then assesses current shortcomings and closes with four proposals for strengthening and optimising social policy. Guan writes as director of a Nankai University institute for social construction and management.

Guan gives four reasons why the principle matters. It is an inherent requirement of Chinese modernization and of common prosperity, because markets alone are said to be unable to handle income gaps, unemployment, illness or care needs. It also supports high-quality development by raising human capital and domestic consumption, and it creates stable social conditions. On the three types, universal provision covers all members of a group (social insurance, education, health). Foundational provision guarantees basic income and services, and is not low-level provision but is set "to the best of our ability" according to economic conditions. Safety-net provision targets groups in hardship through social assistance and welfare services. Guan finds universal and safety-net coverage still insufficient, basic public services uneven, and links between programmes weak, risking gaps or duplication.

Guan makes four proposals. These are stronger top-level design, including national standards for basic public services; a better funding mechanism; fairer distribution, with urban–rural integration, transfer payments and support for low-income groups; and better management and service delivery through professional social work and integrated grassroots services. The author cites budget spending on livelihood areas at close to 10% of GDP, or about 17% with social insurance, and calls this still inadequate. Guan wants a larger livelihood share under more proactive fiscal policy. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Chinese social-policy scholar frames welfare reform within Chinese modernization, common prosperity and high-quality development.
quoteEn: Foundational livelihood protection does not mean low-level protection; rather, a reasonable level is set according to the level of economic development, people's basic needs in various respects and the government's fiscal capacity, on the principle of doing one's best and acting within one's means.
quoteZh: 基础性民生保障并不意味着是低水平保障，而是根据经济发展水平、民众在各方面的基本需要以及政府财力情况，本着尽力而为、量力而行的原则确定合理的水平。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's own path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: people's livelihood is the greatest matter
glossary.explanation: A phrase from Xi Jinping stressing that livelihood protection is central to Chinese modernization. 'Minsheng' covers jobs, income, education, health, housing and social security.
A Party goal of prosperity shared by all, promoted under Xi Jinping. It is meant to balance growth with reduced inequality.
The official guiding concept for the economy since around 2017. It emphasises innovation, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth.

t: Forming a powerful joint force: the "twin-wheel drive" stressed by General Secretary Xi Jinping
zh: 形成协同发力共同推进的强大合力—习近平总书记强调的“双轮驱动”
paras: This commentary from Study Times reviews how Xi Jinping has used the image of a "twin-wheel drive" (shuanglun qudong): two wheels turning together to give strong momentum, meaning two aspects that are coordinated, pushed forward jointly and planned as a whole. Liu argues that studying these remarks supports dialectical thinking and a systems approach to building a strong country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised chronologically around six speeches given since the 18th Party Congress (2012). They cover cyber security and informatisation (2014), new-type urbanisation and rural development (2015), science-and-technology and institutional innovation (2018), practical cooperation and civilisational dialogue with Greece (2019), science and reform in agriculture (2023), and the carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals (2023).

Liu presents each pairing as a dialectical unity rather than a choice between opposites. Security safeguards development and development is the purpose of security. Technological innovation opens new fields while institutional innovation removes obstacles to it. Under the "dual carbon" goals, a "capable government" and an "effective market" are to work together through a new-type whole-nation system and through the market's decisive role in allocating resources. The article restates Xi's policy detail in each area, such as integrating urban and rural planning, equalising basic public services and strengthening agricultural science and technology.

Liu concludes that the twin-wheel approach expresses the "two-point theory" (liangdian lun) and the systems concept, and should guide coordinated action in the new era. Read the original if you want a compact survey of where Xi has used this formula and how Party media present its logic.
quoteEn: Innovation is a systematic undertaking, and scientific and technological innovation and institutional innovation must work together in coordination.
quoteZh: 创新是一个系统工程，科技创新、制度创新要协同发挥作用。

t: Education, science and technology, and talent as the foundational and strategic support for Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的基础性战略性支撑
paras: He Yiting explains a thesis from the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): that education, science and technology, and talent are the foundational and strategic support for Chinese modernization. In He's reading, education is the foundation, science and technology the key, and talent the root. Because innovation depends on talent and talent on education, He argues that advancing the three together is the key path to Chinese modernization.

This short commentary, published in the Party newspaper Study Times, has four sections. The first three take education, science and technology, and talent in turn, each combining a statement of its role with an account of achievements, remaining weaknesses and the reforms the Decision calls for. The fourth section deals with integrated reform of the systems and mechanisms governing all three. The goals it cites are a leading education system by 2035 and a leading science and technology power by 2035.

He argues that education is both a content of modernization and a driver of it, and that the shift from a large education country to a strong one requires deeper comprehensive reform. For science and technology, He sketches successive industrial revolutions to argue that each technological leap has raised productive forces and shaped national fortunes. He says China still has weak original innovation, key technologies controlled by others and too few top scientists. Talent is described as the most active production factor, so that innovation-driven development is in essence talent-driven. He lists structural contradictions in China's talent pool and calls for removing institutional barriers, ending the "four onlys" in evaluation and building evaluation based on innovation and contribution.

He concludes that the three must be planned, decided and deployed as one, with systems thinking and a problem-oriented approach. This means using the new whole-nation system to raise the overall efficiency of the national innovation system, and cultivating an innovation culture that tolerates failure. He presents this as the way to supply the talent, intellectual support and innovation momentum that Chinese modernization needs. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed statement of how Party theorists link education, science and talent policy to Chinese modernization after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: Education, science and technology, and talent are internally consistent and mutually supporting.
quoteZh: 教育、科技、人才三者内在一致、相互支撑。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formulation of China's own path to modernization, set out prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
An official term for mobilising state, market and social resources in a coordinated way to achieve major scientific and technological goals.
A critical shorthand for evaluating researchers only by papers, titles, academic degrees and awards. Official policy calls for eliminating this practice.

t: Unwaveringly advancing high-quality Belt and Road cooperation
zh: 坚定不移推进高质量共建“一带一路”
source: Economic Daily (Jingji Ribao), 23 January 2024 (as given in the source; reposted on marxism.cass.cn on 23 January 2025)
paras: This newspaper commentary argues that the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) has moved from a proposal to practice and has entered a stage of high-quality development, which China should pursue unwaveringly. Zhao Lei opens with the December 2024 Central Economic Work Conference, which called for making high-quality BRI cooperation "deeper and more solid" and for improving overseas comprehensive services. Zhao also cites Xi Jinping's view that opportunities for BRI development outweigh the challenges.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the global and strategic significance of high-quality BRI cooperation. The second weighs opportunities and challenges. The third turns to institutional mechanisms and overall planning. Zhao draws on figures, such as the number of Chinese overseas enterprises, and on projects including the Chancay port in Peru, the Jakarta–Bandung high-speed railway and the China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan railway.

Zhao presents high-quality BRI cooperation as the main route to high-level opening up, which supports Chinese modernization, and as a strategic support for major-country diplomacy and for building a community with a shared future for mankind. On risks, Zhao points to unilateralism, protectionism and geopolitical conflict. The author proposes early-warning platforms for overseas projects, compliance with local law and anti-corruption measures. The core of the argument is three kinds of coordination: "hard", "soft" and "heart" connectivity; major landmark projects alongside "small and beautiful" livelihood projects, such as the Luban Workshops for vocational training; and consolidating traditional fields while expanding digital, green, AI and health cooperation.

Zhao concludes that openness is a defining mark of Chinese modernization and that persistent high-quality BRI cooperation will create more development opportunities and momentum for Chinese modernization and for shared global development. Zhao also calls for better mechanisms, including for investment and financing, risk control and a "clean" Silk Road. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Central Party School researcher frames BRI priorities, risks and project examples in official terms.
quoteEn: Practice has proved that high-quality Belt and Road cooperation must not only "connect roads" but, above all, "connect hearts".
quoteZh: 实践证明，高质量共建“一带一路”不仅要“通路”，更要“通心”。

glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and economic cooperation initiative proposed by Xi Jinping in 2013, centred on infrastructure, trade and investment links between China and partner countries.
The official Party term for China's own path of modernization, prominent in Party discourse since the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A concept in Xi Jinping's foreign policy thinking, presented as a vision of shared security, development and global governance.

glossary.pinyin: yìng liántōng, ruǎn liántōng, xīn liántōng
glossary.explanation: Official shorthand for BRI cooperation in infrastructure, in rules and standards, and in people-to-people ties.
Small-scale BRI projects in areas such as health, education and training that aim at visible local benefits, as opposed to large landmark infrastructure.
An annual meeting of Party and state leaders, held in December, that sets economic priorities for the coming year.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Better realising the role of enterprises as the main body of innovation
zh: 更好发挥企业创新主体作用
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily (January 2025) asks how enterprises can better serve as the main body of innovation. Pan and Xiao argue that firms sit at the key point where science, technology and the economy meet. Strengthening their position, they contend, helps turn scientific results into real productive forces and cultivates new quality productive forces.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's call and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) decision to strengthen enterprises' status in scientific and technological innovation. It then has two parts: the mechanisms through which enterprises drive innovation, and practical paths for improving their role. Examples come from artificial intelligence, synthetic biology and brain science.

On mechanisms, the authors identify three. Scenario-driven demand and technological iteration advance together, with leading firms building technical foundations and small and medium-sized firms building applications. Enterprises link scientific discovery to commercial conversion, because they respond fastest to market demand. They also push technologies into patents and patents into standards, which the authors treat as a 'soft' source of competitiveness. For paths, they propose backing enterprises in major research projects, including private firms in national laboratories. They also propose enterprise-led innovation consortia supported by government funds and 'patient capital', and encouraging firms to lead in setting domestic and international standards.

The authors conclude that coordinating the innovation, industrial, capital and talent chains depends on strengthening enterprises' role. They call for greater basic research spending by firms, fault-tolerance and incentive mechanisms, and fuller incubation systems. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy reasoning on enterprise-led innovation in China in early 2025.
quoteEn: Enterprises are both the source of original technology and the driving force of industrial innovation.
quoteZh: 企业既是原创技术的策源地，也是产业创新的推动者。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than traditional resource-intensive growth.
Long-term investment funds willing to wait for returns, promoted in Chinese policy as support for early-stage technology firms.

t: Building the "greatest consensus" and balancing five relationships: striving to do economic work well
st: An interpretation of the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference
zh: 凝聚一个“最大共识” 把握五个“必须统筹” 奋发有为做好经济工作
paras: This article, published in the People's Daily on 23 January 2025, interprets the formula that Xi Jinping presented at the Central Economic Work Conference at the end of 2024: "one greatest consensus and five must-balance relationships". Zhong argues that the formula further enriches and develops Xi Jinping's economic thought and gives guidance for economic work in the coming period.

The "greatest consensus" is that the Party Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership is the fundamental guarantee of good economic work. The article devotes one section to each of five relationships that must be balanced in promoting high-quality development. These are: an efficient market and a capable government; aggregate supply and aggregate demand; nurturing new growth drivers and updating old ones; improving the incremental and revitalising the existing stock; and raising quality and expanding total volume.

Across the sections, Zhong repeatedly frames each pair as a dialectical unity rather than an either/or choice. On government and market, Zhong says that better use of government does not mean more government. It means avoiding both absence and overreach, building a unified national market and regulating enforcement. On supply and demand, the article calls expanding domestic demand a long-term strategy and not a short-term expedient, and it pairs this with deepening supply-side structural reform. On new and old drivers, it holds that new quality productive forces are a matter of "quality" rather than of which industry is involved. Traditional industries are described as the base of emerging ones and should be upgraded, not discarded, and each region should develop its own approach. On stock and increment, it urges reviving idle land, housing and other assets and exploring a national macro balance sheet. On quality and quantity, it says that high-quality development is the primary task of Chinese modernization, and that quality leads quantity while scale in turn gives quality room to grow.

Zhong concludes that Party members should arm themselves with this innovative theory and work energetically to build the economic foundation for Chinese modernization. The text is an authoritative Party-press reading of the conference, and it presents the policy line as it was officially framed in early 2025. Read the original if you want a detailed account of how official commentary explains the priorities of China's 2025 economic work and the conceptual vocabulary behind them.
quoteEn: Better use of the government's role does not mean more use of it; it means insisting on doing some things and not others, getting the boundary between action and restraint right, and doing well and fully what government should do.
quoteZh: 更好发挥政府作用不是更多发挥政府作用，而是要坚持有所为、有所不为，把握好有为和无为的边界，把政府该做的事情做好做到位。

glossary.explanation: The official goal for China's economy since the late 2010s, replacing a focus on rapid growth with an emphasis on quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It stresses a huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023. It refers to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation.
A policy line launched in 2015 to improve the quality and efficiency of supply, for example by cutting excess capacity, rather than relying only on stimulating demand.
The official body of ideas on economic work that the Party says has taken shape since 2012 and forms part of Xi Jinping Thought.

t: Seizing the opportunity to strengthen original and disruptive scientific and technological innovation
zh: 把握机遇加强原创性颠覆性科技创新
paras: Writing in the Economic Daily in January 2024, Xiong Hongru asks how China can move from following existing technologies to leading them. The article opens by saying that a country's ability to produce major original and disruptive scientific results is the first measure of world-leading strength. Xiong argues that, in a harsher external environment, China must shift from tracking and incremental innovation towards pioneering, leading innovation, in order to raise the overall performance of the national innovation system.

The piece is a short newspaper commentary in three parts. It first sets out the opportunity created by rapid technological and market iteration. It then lists China's favourable conditions, using figures on research input, output, talent, infrastructure, firms and scale. It ends with four policy directions for building new advantages in science, technology and industry.

Xiong's central claim is that major breakthroughs are usually discontinuous: transistors replacing vacuum tubes, digital communication replacing analogue, power batteries replacing combustion engines. Such innovation brings technological uncertainty and "creative destruction", and, in Xiong's view, matters especially for latecomer countries facing faster technical change and rising protectionism. It is needed to end dependence on foreign core technologies, build "asymmetric advantages" and safeguard economic and national security. Xiong cites figures to show that China is well placed: R&D intensity above the OECD average, 30.3% of papers in the most influential journals in 2022, rising basic research spending (from 49.88 billion to 225.91 billion yuan, 2012–2023), 77 national major science and technology facilities, and 679 firms among the global top 2,500 R&D investors. Xiong adds the advantage of scale, citing the most complete industrial system and a very large market that lowers the cost of trial and error.

Xiong concedes that original innovation remains weak, some key technologies are still controlled by others, and top talent is scarce. The proposals are to strengthen basic research and forward-looking planning, with reform of evaluation away from quantified metrics; to coordinate national strategic science and technology forces with market-based innovators, with firms as the main innovators; to build matching talent, long-term finance and industrial systems; and to raise China's global innovation position through institutional opening. Read the original if you want a concise, data-supported statement of the official policy case for original and disruptive innovation, written by a State Council research official.
quoteEn: For latecomer countries, under current conditions of accelerating technological progress and rising protectionism, discontinuous innovation is more important than ever before.
quoteZh: 对于后发国家而言，在当前技术进步加速和保护主义抬头的形势下，非连续性创新的重要性前所未有。

glossary.en: national strategic science and technology forces
glossary.explanation: A term for the core state-backed research bodies, such as national laboratories, national research institutes, leading research universities and leading technology firms.

t: Coordinating the cultivation of new growth drivers and the renewal of old ones
zh: 统筹好培育新动能和更新旧动能的关系
paras: Writing in Economic Daily in January 2024, Zhang Qizai takes up the instruction of the Central Economic Work Conference to coordinate the cultivation of new growth drivers with the renewal of old ones, and to develop new quality productive forces in line with local conditions. Zhang argues that China is at a critical stage of economic transformation and upgrading, and that handling the relationship between new and old drivers correctly is essential for both a real improvement in quality and a reasonable increase in quantity.

The commentary has two parts. The first clarifies what new and old drivers mean and why the two should be pursued together. The second sets out four priority tasks: innovation, market-based mechanisms, new types of production factors, and locally tailored development of new quality productive forces. Zhang illustrates the argument with policy measures on strategic emerging industries and with a steel-sector example of digital upgrading.

Zhang defines new drivers as innovation-led advanced productive forces and the production relations suited to them, and contends that growth driven by expanding factor inputs is weakening as demand, not supply, becomes the main constraint. Cultivating new drivers means building strategic emerging industries and future industries; renewing old ones means upgrading traditional industries, not simply eliminating them. Of three possible transition modes, namely keeping old drivers while growing new ones, replacing old with new, or doing both at once, Zhang holds that the first two leave the drivers unintegrated and risk large economic swings or a gap in drivers. The third needs a relatively complete industrial system, and since Chinese industries range from followers to leaders, leading industries should focus on new drivers and following industries on renewing old ones.

Zhang calls for AI-assisted innovation, stronger basic research and national innovation platforms; better investment and financing, a leading role for state capital, equal protection of private enterprises and a unified national market; digital and AI-enabled upgrading of traditional industries; and regional choices based on resource endowments, avoiding blind imitation. Zhang concludes that this two-wheel drive will build new advantages for economic development. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how an economist at a Chinese state think tank links the new/old driver transition to new quality productive forces and industrial policy.
quoteEn: Converting old and new drivers does not mean simply eliminating traditional industries; it means upgrading equipment, stepping up support for technological breakthroughs in "chokepoint" areas, raising quality and efficiency and the fit between supply and demand, and so bringing about the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries.
quoteZh: 推动新旧动能转换，不是要简单淘汰传统产业，而是要通过设备更新改造，加大对“卡脖子”领域技术攻关支持，提升质量和效益、提升供给与需求的适配性，推动传统产业实现转型升级。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for innovation-led advanced productive forces, linked to technology, strategic emerging industries and future industries.
Growth drivers based on innovation and emerging industries, contrasted with older drivers based on expanding capital and labour inputs.
An official category of industries seen as key to future growth, such as new-generation information technology, biotechnology, new energy and new materials.
The annual meeting, held at the end of the year, at which the Party and state leadership set economic priorities for the coming year.

t: The shifting spirit of the age and the changing image of China
zh: 时代精神的流转与中国形象的变迁
paras: Fang Weigui asks why Western images of China have swung between admiration and contempt. Opening with the German sinologist Wolfgang Franke's remark that these images reveal the observers' standpoints more than the object observed, the author argues that each image reflects the spirit of its age, Western needs of the moment and the values of its makers. The piece, published in Guangming Daily in January 2025, extends this claim to the present day.

The article surveys Western views of China from antiquity to the early twentieth century. It begins with the vague Roman 'Seres' and Marco Polo, then treats the Jesuit-driven enthusiasm of roughly 1250–1750 and the hostile image that followed the Jesuits' dissolution around 1775. It ends with the early twentieth-century 'Orient fever', stressing the shift from Confucian to Daoist texts and the place of Chinese poetry in Western literary reception.

Fang's central device is two 'cross-century blocs': a positive image running from the Jesuits through Leibniz, Wolff, Voltaire and Diderot, and a negative one from Anson, the Macartney mission, Montesquieu, Rousseau, Herder and Hegel. The author attributes the swing to Enlightenment needs, later Eurocentrism, Christian and imperialist missionary consciousness, and ignorance of Chinese history, noting that Western knowledge relied on Jesuit works. Fang adds that popular and elite images of China differ. After the First World War, the author says, a Western spiritual crisis and Nietzschean cultural pessimism fed a Daoist craze, seen in Klabund's call to 'become Chinese Europeans', in Li Bai's rise as the emblem of Chinese culture, and in Mahler's Das Lied von der Erde.

Fang concludes that European affirmation or denial of China since the eighteenth century has come from Europe's own needs. The author contends that contemporary Western views remain largely the same, expressing Western positions on a changed situation and sometimes carrying Cold War thinking. Recent Western reception of Chinese literature is described as utilitarian, with selection driven by critical content or topical interest more than literary quality. Read the original if you want a concise Chinese scholarly account of how Western images of China have been historically constructed, especially in literary reception.
quoteEn: Since the eighteenth century, Europe's affirmation or negation of China has always arisen from Europe's own needs, depending on the age and intellectual background in which a particular image was formed and developed.
quoteZh: 18世纪以降，欧洲对中国的肯定或否定均出于欧洲自身的需求，取决于特定形象之生成和发展的时代与思想背景。

t: Centralized and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee is the fundamental guarantee for doing economic work well
zh: 党中央集中统一领导是做好经济工作的根本保证
paras: Writing in People's Daily after the Central Economic Work Conference of late 2024, Liu Wei takes up the claim that centralized and unified leadership by the Party Central Committee is the fundamental guarantee for doing economic work well. Liu presents this as a regular pattern drawn from China's economic practice and as an important part of Xi Jinping's economic thought. The commentary argues that the pattern is confirmed by experience and should be understood through the demands of high-quality development.

The piece has three parts. The first cites two cases from the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012): the response to Covid-19 in 2020 and the policy turn of September 2024. It also traces how Central Economic Work Conferences in 2019, 2020 and 2023 stated the same conclusion. The second part explains the claim in terms of high-quality development. The third sets out practical requirements for implementation.

Liu's core argument rests on three links between Party leadership and high-quality development. First, leadership sustains and improves the basic socialist economic system. Liu grounds this in the dialectic of productive forces and relations of production and of economic base and superstructure, which calls for the superstructure's active role. Second, leadership makes scientific governance and overall coordination possible, bringing consistent policy orientation in macroeconomic governance and balance in urban–rural and regional development. Third, leadership is said to enable the correct handling of the government–market relationship, with the digital economy and new quality productive forces as examples. In the evidence, Liu notes that China's GDP grew 2.2% in 2020, which the article calls the only positive growth among major economies, and that the September 2024 package of incremental policies lifted confidence and brought a clear recovery.

Liu calls for action under the principle of 'putting work first' so that Central Committee decisions are carried out. Leaders should build their capacity for economic work and judge economic questions with political insight. They should also use rule-of-law thinking, treating the socialist market economy as essentially a law-based economy, and speed up building a high-level socialist market economic system, following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Read the original if you want an authoritative People's Daily statement of how Chinese economic discourse links Party leadership to high-quality development and the socialist market economy.
quoteEn: The socialist market economy is in essence a law-based economy; we must adhere to rule-of-law thinking, strengthen awareness of the rule of law, and regulate and govern the economy in accordance with the law.
quoteZh: 社会主义市场经济本质上是法治经济，必须坚持法治思维、增强法治观念，依法调控和治理经济。

glossary.explanation: An annual meeting, held in late year, at which the Party and state leadership review the year's economic work and set the priorities and tone for the next year's economic policy.
The official guiding concept for China's economy since around 2017. It shifts the emphasis from speed of growth to quality, efficiency, innovation and balance.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and innovation.

glossary.zh: 社会主义基本经济制度
glossary.explanation: The official term for China's core economic institutions. They comprise public ownership as the mainstay alongside diverse forms of ownership, distribution according to work as the mainstay, and the socialist market economy.

t: Developing agricultural new quality productive forces in line with local conditions
zh: 因地制宜发展农业新质生产力
paras: This newspaper commentary in Guangming Daily (21 January 2025) takes up the call of the 2024 Central Rural Work Conference to develop agricultural new quality productive forces in line with local conditions. Zhang Haipeng and Zhang Yanlong argue that building China into a strong agricultural country, a precondition for a modern socialist great power, requires such forces. They hold that the work should proceed steadily and not be rushed, and that it needs \"one bottom line, two relationships and three goals\".

The authors define agricultural new quality productive forces as advanced productive forces generated in agriculture by revolutionary technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and deep industrial upgrading. Their defining features are said to be high technology, high efficiency and high quality. The piece is organised in three sections matching the formula: the bottom line, the two relationships and the three goals. They describe Chinese agricultural productivity as being at a critical stage of shifting from quantity to quality.

The bottom line is food security: the authors say new technologies must not loosen grain production, and should be embedded in it through big data, artificial intelligence and similar tools. They cite protective tillage in the Northeast and integrated rice-fish farming in the South as examples. The two relationships are between nurturing new and renewing old growth drivers, with paths varying by local resources, and between protecting smallholders and developing modern agriculture. Here the authors treat smallholder family farming as the main form for a long time to come, and propose organising smallholders through industrial consortia with cooperatives, leading enterprises and family farms.

The three goals are stronger coordinated agricultural science and technology research, wider application of results, and a comprehensive green, low-carbon transition. For the first, the authors invoke the new-type whole-nation system and call for breakthroughs in crop breeding, livestock breeds and high-end farm machinery. For the second, they call for a better extension system, digital tools and \"science and technology courtyards\" to bridge the \"last mile\". For the third, they call for fertiliser and pesticide reduction, efficient water use and national green development pilot zones. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy framework for agricultural new quality productive forces and its stress on food security and smallholders.
quoteEn: In developing agricultural new quality productive forces, we must hold to the bottom line of safeguarding food security.
quoteZh: 发展农业新质生产力，必须守住保障粮食安全这个底线。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new factor allocation and industrial upgrading. It is presented as central to high-quality development.

glossary.literal: new-type system of mobilising the whole nation
glossary.explanation: An official formula for concentrating state, market and research resources on major technological goals, adapted from the earlier whole-nation system.

t: Forming an economic order that is both "lively" and "well-regulated"
zh: 形成既“放得活”又“管得住”的经济秩序
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2025, Liu Wei comments on the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference, which listed "five must-balance relationships". First among them is the relationship between an effective market and a capable government, with the aim of an order that is both "lively" (fangde huo) and "well-regulated" (guande zhu). Liu treats this as guidance on the government–market relationship, which the article calls the core question of economic reform. The thesis is that the two are complementary, and that each needs its own institutional foundation.

The article has four parts. It first traces how the Party's understanding of the government–market relationship deepened, from the 1992 goal of a socialist market economy through the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). It then sets out the institutions an effective market requires and those a capable government requires. It closes with two principles for combining the two.

Liu's core argument is that an effective market rests on a high-level socialist market economy system. That system has two layers. Competition institutions cover market-entity rules, meaning modern enterprise institutions and the Two Unwaverings, and transaction rules, meaning market-determined prices, anti-monopoly rules and a unified national market. Basic institutions cover the rule of law and a credit system. A capable government, in Liu's account, mainly means active and systematic macroeconomic governance by the central government, which also corrects market failure. Liu says China's governance system rests on the socialist system and has five features: reform measures are part of governance; policy covers structural and development policy as well as monetary and fiscal policy; it uses both counter-cyclical and cross-cycle adjustment; state-owned enterprises give macro governance a micro-level base; and regulation can shift between demand-side and supply-side approaches.

Liu concludes that government and market are not opposed but mutually reinforcing, since more competition strengthens the micro-foundations of macro governance. Their functions should be defined by the problems they address, not by a mechanical division of fields. The market works directly through competition among micro-level actors where property rights are clear and rules fair. Government works indirectly, guiding actors from the macro level where markets fail. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned economist's reading of the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference formula and of how it fits the Party's evolving doctrine on the state and the market.
quoteEn: In resource allocation, government and market are not opposed but complement and reinforce each other, and both aim to raise the efficiency of resource allocation.
quoteZh: 在资源配置上，政府与市场不是对立的，而是相辅相成、相互促进的关系，目标都是提高资源配置效率。

glossary.explanation: A Party formula calling for unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official goal of economic reform adopted at the 14th Party Congress (1992), combining market allocation of resources with state macro-control and a leading role for public ownership.

glossary.en: an effective market and a capable government
glossary.explanation: A formula for the government–market relationship in which both sides are expected to work well together. The Chinese for the government side literally means "government that achieves something".
A policy goal of removing local protectionism and barriers so that goods, services and factors of production move freely across China.

t: Accelerating the development of the new rural collective economy
zh: 加快发展新型农村集体经济
paras: This short commentary by Kang Jiaojiao and Wu Fangwei takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) call to develop a new rural collective economy. The authors argue that speeding up its growth is an important means of building a strong agricultural country, a beautiful countryside and prosperous farmers, and that it supplies the material basis for rural revitalisation.

The piece first defines rural collective economic organisations and the "new" collective economy, which it describes as an upgrade of the traditional form under a socialist market economy using modern technology and management. It then explains why development matters, and sets out proposals in three areas: Party building, industrial upgrading, and institutional reform. Provincial and village examples illustrate each area.

The authors link the new collective economy to three goals. It strengthens the "unified" side of the two-tier management system, helping to meet food security and technology needs. It raises public services, social security and the rural living environment. It also raises incomes and cuts the risk of individual farming, which they present as a main lever for common prosperity. They say development remains insufficient and propose that Party leadership, described as the "compass", underpin it through stronger grassroots organisations, better personnel and professional managers.

Further proposals include developing distinctive industries, leasing property, taking shares in assets, and building digital platforms. On institutions, the authors call for clearer property rights, fairer distribution, and supervision under the rural collective economic organisation law. Read the original if you want a concise statement of official policy thinking on collective economy, with Chinese local examples.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's leadership is the "anchor" and the "compass" for promoting high-quality development of the new rural collective economy.
quoteZh: 坚持党的领导，是推动新型农村集体经济高质量发展的“定盘星”和“指南针”。

glossary.explanation: A policy term for rural collective ownership renewed through modern technology, management and diverse business forms under the socialist market economy. It builds on the older village and township collective economy.
A long-term goal of the Party under which all people share in wealth, stressed in recent official discourse as part of socialism.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to develop rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards together.

glossary.zh: 统分结合双层经营体制
glossary.pinyin: tǒng fēn jiéhé shuāng céng jīngyíng tǐzhì
glossary.literal: dual-layer system combining unified and separate management
glossary.explanation: The rural arrangement in which households contract land for family farming while the collective handles unified functions such as infrastructure and services.

t: Improving the support system for strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching farmers
zh: 完善强农惠农富农支持制度
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2025, Zhou Qisen takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee's (2024) call to improve the support system for strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching farmers. Zhou argues that, since institutions bear on what is fundamental, stable and long-term, building a strong agricultural country through agricultural and rural modernization depends above all on rural institutional construction. The commentary says deepening rural reform must be people-centred and treat institution-building as its main thread.

The piece has three parts. It first explains why the system is urgently needed, setting the case against the history of rural reform from the household contract responsibility system to rural tax-and-fee reform, the building of a new socialist countryside and rural revitalisation. It then argues that farmers must be the main actors in designing and running the system. Finally it identifies three practical focal points, corresponding to the three verbs in the formula: strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching farmers.

Zhou's central claim is that the system is a systematic project covering agriculture, the countryside and farmers, and that it serves the vision of strong agriculture, prosperous farmers and a beautiful countryside. Farmers, the author says, should be treated as the main beneficiaries of reform, as the main actors in rural development and as the main actors in rural governance. This means stable incomes, guaranteed grain-growers' interests, links between smallholders and modern agriculture, and a governance model that combines self-governance, rule of law and moral guidance. The author lists remaining difficulties, including consolidating poverty-alleviation achievements, supporting low-income rural people, and weaknesses in modernization.

On the three focal points, Zhou calls for policy support and cultural-ethical measures to activate rural vitality, as well as for coordinated systems for building, using, managing and maintaining rural infrastructure and for equalising public services through institutional and legal means. Zhou also calls for county-level industries that raise incomes, new rural business forms and a stronger collective economy, with market tools and policy incentives used together. The commentary presents these steps as the institutional base for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how rural policy priorities were framed after the Third Plenum, in the language of Party documents.
quoteEn: For China to be strong, agriculture must be strong; for China to be beautiful, the countryside must be beautiful; for China to be prosperous, farmers must be prosperous.
quoteZh: 中国要强，农业必须强；中国要美，农村必须美；中国要富，农民必须富。

glossary.pinyin: qiáng nóng huì nóng fù nóng
glossary.en: strengthening agriculture, benefiting farmers and enriching farmers
glossary.literal: strengthen agriculture, benefit farmers, enrich farmers
glossary.explanation: A formula for rural support policy: building a strong agricultural sector, delivering benefits to farmers and raising their incomes. The Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) called for improving the supporting system.
A national strategy launched in 2017 to develop rural industry, ecology, culture, governance and living standards, replacing the earlier new socialist countryside drive.
The shorthand 'three rural issues' (agriculture, rural areas, farmers), used in Party documents for rural policy as a whole.
The official term for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
The rural reform from the late 1970s that let households farm contracted collective land and keep surplus output; it is treated as the start of reform and opening up.

t: Empowering the modernization of rural governance with digital-intelligence technology
zh: 数智技术赋能乡村治理现代化
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily asks how digital-intelligence (shuzhi) technologies can advance the modernization of rural governance, which Zhang Yunping treats as part of modernizing the national governance system and as a requirement of building a modern socialist country. Citing Xi Jinping's call to use modern information technology to improve rural governance, Zhang argues that better infrastructure, smoother information channels and refined digital governance paths can make rural governance more forward-looking, precise and intelligent.

The article is organised under three headings: strengthening rural digital-intelligence infrastructure, raising the digital-intelligence skills of rural talent, and increasing the effectiveness of digital-intelligence governance in the countryside.

On infrastructure, Zhang calls for more fiscal support and diversified financing, with priority for less-connected areas, together with digital upgrading of water, transport, power, logistics and weather facilities and integrated governance platforms covering Party building, public affairs and health services. On skills, Zhang proposes training for farmers and especially for village cadres, plus incentives to attract information-technology talent. On effectiveness, Zhang calls for more precise public services, such as 'internet plus' grassroots governance, simple apps and elderly-friendly services. Zhang also urges reducing digital burdens by avoiding digital formalism and idle platforms, and securing data through legal rules, tiered protection and risk assessment.

Zhang concludes that the aim is good rural governance that maximises public interest, so that technology 'empowers' rather than burdens villages. Read the original if you want a concise statement of official-style policy priorities for digital rural governance in China at the start of 2025.
quoteEn: Priority should be given to raising the digital-intelligence skills of village cadres.
quoteZh: 应重点提高乡村干部的数智技能

glossary.explanation: A policy goal of upgrading how villages are administered, as part of modernizing the national governance system and capacity. It is linked to the rural revitalization strategy.
An official ideal of effective, orderly rural governance that serves the public interest and involves villagers.
A term for officials adopting digital tools or platforms for show, which adds work for grassroots staff without real benefit. Official campaigns have criticised it.

t: Computing power as the new infrastructure for high-quality economic development
zh: 算力是经济高质量发展的新基建
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 17 January 2025
paras: This short commentary, published in Chinese Social Sciences Today in January 2025, argues that computing power (suanli) is the foundation of the digital economy and a new form of infrastructure for high-quality development. Wei Jieyu and Cai Yuezhou open with the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for building and operating national data infrastructure and promoting data sharing. They present faster construction of computing infrastructure as necessary for releasing the value of data as a production factor and for integrating the real and digital economies.

The article has three parts. It first explains why computing power underpins the digital economy, then reviews progress and remaining problems in China's computing infrastructure, and finally sets out four groups of policy recommendations. The authors draw on official policy documents, national statistics up to mid-2024 and an international computing power index report.

Wei and Cai argue that computing power is both the base for applying digital technologies and a constraint on industrial change, since the digital transformation of traditional industries depends on supply of computing power. They cite the 2022–2023 Global Computing Power Index report: each one-point rise in the index is said to raise digital-economy value added by 3.6‰ and GDP by 1.7‰. On progress, they report total capacity of 246 EFLOPS by June 2024, second in the world, with annual growth near 30% and intelligent computing growing over 70% in 2023. They also describe the eight national hubs under the East Data, West Computing project, with eastern hubs serving latency-sensitive work and western hubs handling back-end processing. They name three problems: dependence on imported high-end chips, electricity supply and cost, and incomplete technical standards.

The authors recommend concentrating research on chip technology through the new-type whole-nation system (xin xing juguo tizhi), with diversified funding. They also call for top-level design and moderately advance deployment of capacity, and for siting computing centres where green power is plentiful and cheap, with joint scheduling of electricity and computing. They further urge application scenarios in industrial internet, intelligent transport and digital government, and a coordinated hardware and software ecosystem. Read the original if you want a concise official-line overview of China's computing infrastructure policy, its stated problems and its proposed remedies.
quoteEn: Computing power is the foundation for releasing the value of data as a production factor and activating its potential, and the cornerstone for ensuring the healthy development of the digital economy.
quoteZh: 算力是释放数据要素价值、激活数据潜能的底座，是保障数字经济健康发展的基石。

glossary.explanation: A national project launched in 2022 to move computing demand and data processing from the data-heavy east to western regions with cheaper energy and land, through eight national computing hubs.

glossary.literal: new-type system of mobilising the whole nation
glossary.explanation: A policy term for coordinating state, institutional and market resources behind major science and technology goals, especially key technology bottlenecks.
The official goal since around 2017 of shifting from speed of growth to quality, efficiency and innovation in the economy.

t: Digital finance empowering the development of new quality productive forces
zh: 数字金融赋能新质生产力发展
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), January 2025
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper in January 2025, Tian Kan asks how digital finance can support the development of new quality productive forces. The author starts from the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference, which stressed technological innovation as the lead for new quality productive forces and the building of a modern industrial system. Tian argues that digital finance, by combining digital technology with traditional financial services, can optimise factor allocation, drive technological innovation and promote industrial upgrading.

The short commentary sets out five mechanisms through which digital finance is said to work. They are a full-process service mechanism, an ecosystem-chain integration mechanism, a data-value release mechanism, a financing credit-enhancement mechanism and an inclusive service mechanism. Each is illustrated with practical measures for finance institutions, enterprises, universities and government.

In the full-process mechanism, Tian says big data and AI models can help firms identify promising research directions, while seed funding, venture capital and credit support carry projects through early research. Pledging data assets and intangible assets such as patents, together with digital matching platforms, is presented as a way to ease commercialisation and market entry. The ecosystem mechanism uses blockchain and cloud computing to break up 'information silos', steer capital toward fields such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing, and link firms, universities and research institutes in joint technical work. The remaining mechanisms rely on integrated data to improve technology, production, talent and market factors, on multidimensional credit profiles, risk-sharing tools and regulatory technology to improve the financing climate, and on mobile services, rural outlets and tailored products to draw small firms and individual entrepreneurs into the effort.

Tian concludes that digital finance, by activating market participants in all these ways, gives new quality productive forces strong momentum. The article also calls for government, finance institutions and firms to build risk-sharing and policy-support arrangements, with feedback channels to adjust services, while holding the line against systemic risk. Read the original if you want a concise, policy-oriented Chinese account of how digital finance is expected to serve the new quality productive forces agenda, including the specific instruments proposed.
quoteEn: Digital finance promotes the development of new quality productive forces by optimising factor allocation, driving technological innovation and advancing industrial upgrading.
quoteZh: 数字金融通过优化要素配置、驱动科技创新、推动产业升级，进而促进新质生产力发展。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industries, such as AI and new energy.
An annual meeting held at the end of each year at which Party and state leaders review the economy and set priorities for the coming year.

t: Leading the accelerated formation of new quality productive forces with the new development philosophy
zh: 以新发展理念引领新质生产力加快形成
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报)
paras: This short commentary from the Chinese Social Sciences Today argues that the new development philosophy should guide the accelerated formation of new quality productive forces. Su Yubo takes Xi Jinping's statement that these forces are an inherent requirement and key focus of high-quality development as the starting point. Su contends that the approach matters for economic quality, international competitiveness and the initiative in building a modernized country.

The article is organised around the five components of the new development philosophy: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. Each section names the problem the component addresses and links it to the formation of new quality productive forces.

Su argues that innovation supplies the driving force, citing high-speed rail, 5G and space exploration, while also listing weak points such as low basic-research spending, a low rate of converting research results, and dependence on foreign core technologies. Coordination is tied to regional balance, with Xi's launch of the concept during an inspection of the Northeast offered as significant. Green development is presented as the ecological form of these productive forces, linked to the carbon peak and carbon neutrality pledges. Openness draws on Marx's remark about world-historical inventions to argue that technology is global. Sharing is framed as the "make the cake bigger" and "divide the cake well" contradiction, which new quality productive forces are said to ease by converting into improved livelihoods.

Su concludes that matching an advanced supply side to people's growing and diversified needs is required if the fruits of modernization are to reach all people more fairly. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-school-style commentary maps the five elements of the new development philosophy onto new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces provide an ample source of power for "making the cake bigger", and the continued accumulation and full development of productive forces help realise "sharing the cake" at a higher level.
quoteZh: 新质生产力提供了“做大蛋糕”的充足动力源，生产力的不断积累和充分发展有利于在更高层面上实现“蛋糕共享”。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, as opposed to traditional growth reliant on resources and heavy inputs.
A framework announced in 2015 comprising innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, intended to guide China's economic and social policy.
An official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth emphasising efficiency, innovation and sustainability, prominent since 2017.

t: Further comprehensively deepening reform must always uphold the people's principal position
zh: 进一步全面深化改革要始终坚持人民主体地位
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), 17 January 2025
paras: This short commentary in China Social Sciences Today takes up one of the "six adherences" set out by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): putting the people first in further comprehensively deepening reform. Ren Pengcheng argues that upholding the people's principal position gives scientific guidance and a value orientation for advancing Chinese modernization and creating a higher-quality, happier life.

The article moves from theory to practice and then to tasks. It first grounds the principle in the Marxist view of the people as makers of history and in the Party's fundamental political stance. It then reviews achievements since reform and opening up and since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and ends with measures for the current round of reform.

Ren's central claim is that the people are both the beneficiaries and the source of strength of reform. The article presents the Party's century of struggle, the elimination of absolute poverty and the build-out of education, social security and health systems as proof that reform aims at the people's wellbeing. It also treats the Party's theoretical innovations as products of the people's wisdom, and cites Xi Jinping: reform is meaningful when done for the people and has momentum when it relies on them.

For the next stage, Ren calls for strengthening Party leadership through the Party's self-reform, and for sustaining ideals and convictions through the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds. Ren also calls for testing reform by actual results and public satisfaction, drawing on investigation and research, the mass line and whole-process people's democracy. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's official discourse links the people's principal position to the Third Plenum's reform agenda.
quoteEn: We must respect the people's principal position and pioneering spirit, so that reform is for the people, relies on the people, and its fruits are shared by the people.
quoteZh: 要尊重人民主体地位和首创精神，做到改革为了人民、改革依靠人民、改革成果由人民共享。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's development path, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western modernization models.
A formula from the Party's 2021 historical resolution. It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The Party's requirement that members uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
The official description of China's democratic system, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019. It stresses popular participation across all stages of governance, not only elections.
An official concept for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, often tied to anti-corruption work and Party-building.
A Party method of work from the Mao era. It requires officials to gather the views of ordinary people, turn them into policy and take it back to them.

t: Advancing the great practice of common prosperity with a spirit of historical initiative
zh: 以历史主动精神推进共同富裕伟大实践
source: China Social Sciences Network / Chinese Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), posted 17 January 2025
paras: This commentary from a Party-theory research base asks how the Communist Party's "spirit of historical initiative" can guide the work of advancing common prosperity as China moves from building a moderately prosperous society to building a modern socialist country. Pan Xuefeng argues that this spirit, which the article ties to theoretical innovation, putting the people first, responsibility for development and the Party's self-reform, is a source of strength for the task. On this basis, the author says, common prosperity can be pursued steadily.

The article is organised in three parts. The first examines the theoretical basis of common prosperity in Marx and Engels and in the Party's own record from Mao Zedong to Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. The second treats the theoretical and practical questions that the Party must answer. The third places common prosperity within the current stage of Chinese modernization and the changed principal contradiction in society.

Pan reads Marx and Engels as holding that common prosperity does not mean equal distribution of means of production. In this reading it means that all members of society have equal rights to manage, use and distribute them under public ownership. The author traces the term to a Mao-drafted resolution on agricultural cooperatives and to Deng's definition of the essence of socialism. Pan then cites Xi's formula that common prosperity is for all the people, covers both material and cultural life, and is not egalitarianism. For practice, the author calls for consolidating poverty-alleviation gains and preventing relapse into poverty, and for stable employment and rising incomes. Pan also calls for equalised public services, a multi-tiered social security system, and work on rules for wealth creation, distribution and redistribution and on the "third distribution".

Pan concludes that common prosperity is an essential requirement of socialism and a defining feature of Chinese modernization, and that it must be guided by Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. The author calls for the path to be adjusted in good time to national and international conditions, and for the Party to keep its historical consciousness and sense of responsibility. Pan claims that this will offer "Chinese wisdom" and a Chinese approach to the shared cause of peace and development. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars link common prosperity to Marxist classics and official doctrine.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is not an abstract theoretical slogan but has rich conceptual content, which must be understood in depth from the perspective of the basic principles of Marxism and the great practice of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 共同富裕并非抽象的理论口号，而是有其丰富的概念内涵，需要从马克思主义基本原理和中国特色社会主义伟大实践的视角加以深入理解。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in Party discourse, prominent since the Party's 2021 resolution on its history. It describes the Party as consciously and actively shaping historical development, rather than reacting to events.
A goal of socialism in Chinese official usage, in which prosperity is shared by all the people and is not egalitarian. It was stressed again under Xi Jinping from 2021 onward.
The official term for China's path to modernization, which the Party presents as distinct from Western models. Common prosperity is named as one of its defining features.
Voluntary redistribution of wealth through charity and donations, treated in official discourse as a supplement to market distribution (first) and government redistribution (second).

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for combining Marxism with China's conditions and with contemporary developments. It is also used to describe the Party's theoretical innovation.

The Party's formula for the main tension driving social development. Since the 19th Party Congress (2017) it has been defined as that between people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development.

t: Using new quality productive forces to drive the building of a modern industrial system
zh: 以新质生产力牵引现代化产业体系建设
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), January 2025
paras: This commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2025, asks how new quality productive forces can drive the construction of a modern industrial system. Starting from Xi Jinping's definition of new quality productive forces as an advanced form of productive forces led by innovation, Tao and Xu argue that these forces are the most dynamic and driving part of the industrial system. They present them as a key engine of high-quality development and call for institutional arrangements that support them.

The piece has three parts. The first explains why developing new quality productive forces is an inherent requirement for building a modern industrial system. The second sets out five main directions of effort. The third proposes institutional and policy safeguards, drawing on the call to reform science, education and talent systems and to supply new production relations suited to the new productive forces.

On the first part, the authors argue that disruptive technologies reshape the industrial structure, raise the share of emerging industries, create new factors such as data, and give traditional industries a new growth curve. They add that in fields such as artificial intelligence and aerospace the technology gap with developed countries is smaller, which they see as helping China catch up and ease 'bottleneck' dependence on foreign key technologies. The five directions are upgrading traditional industries, developing strategic emerging and future industries, integrating modern services with advanced manufacturing, integrating agriculture with manufacturing and services, and coordinating traditional and new infrastructure. Each is illustrated with cases from Guangdong, such as digital upgrading of textile firms, a low-altitude economy cluster in Huangpu, a Xinhui tangerine-peel data platform and Shenzhen's digital twin of Nanshan.

For safeguards, the authors call for using the new-type whole-nation system to link industrial and innovation chains and end the split between research and industry. They also urge breaking barriers to cross-sector integration, giving competition policy a foundational role, and shifting from selective to functional industrial policy. A further proposal is to complete a unified national market and change local-government incentives that encourage homogeneous competition. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Chinese economists link new quality productive forces to industrial policy, with regional case examples.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces is the key engine for China's current construction of a modern industrial system.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力是当前我国建设现代化产业体系的关键引擎。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of factors and industrial upgrading. It is used in official discourse to guide economic policy.
An official term for an industrial structure that is complete, advanced, secure and self-reliant. It combines manufacturing, modern services and agriculture with digital and green technology.
The official economic goal since 2017, stressing innovation, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth.
A model that mobilises state, market and social resources for major scientific and technological goals. It is presented as an updated form of the earlier centrally coordinated approach.

t: Creating a relaxed policy environment for developing new quality productive forces
zh: 为发展新质生产力营造宽松政策环境
source: China Social Sciences Today (中国社会科学报), via China Social Science Network
paras: Writing after the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference, Zhang Chengsi asks how macroeconomic policy can best support new quality productive forces in 2025. The commentary argues that fiscal and monetary policy, the two core tools of macroeconomic regulation, must work in coordination at a higher level. In Zhang's view, such a policy mix can make new quality productive forces a core driver of a new economic leap for China.

The piece, published in China Social Sciences Today, is organised in three parts: a more proactive fiscal policy, a moderately loose monetary policy, and the coordination of the two. It opens from the Conference's call to keep stability while pursuing progress, to adopt more active macro policy and to promote industrial upgrading through technological innovation. It closes with an outlook on high-quality development.

Zhang assigns fiscal policy the task of strengthening basic support and resource allocation. Higher deficit ratios, special treasury bonds and local government special bonds are said to fund basic research, break through "chokepoint" technologies, support digital and green transformation of industry, and lift consumption through pensions, medical insurance and incomes. Monetary policy, by contrast, is to improve the financial ecosystem. Zhang stresses that "moderately loose" does not mean aimless liquidity injection. Reserve-requirement and interest-rate cuts, relending, rediscounting and targeted loan quotas are meant to channel low-cost funds to innovative and specialised small firms, while macroprudential management keeps money out of inefficient projects and speculation. The two are to be sequenced: fiscal spending first builds infrastructure and public platforms and supports early-stage research, then credit supports expansion and market rollout across a firm's life cycle. Their combination is also said to aid urban–rural integration and regional coordination.

Zhang concludes that China is at a critical period of changing its development model, and that coordinated macro policy acts as a catalyst linking industrial upgrading with consumption upgrading, employment and better livelihoods. Looking ahead, Zhang expects technological change to raise total factor productivity and macro policy to help the economy absorb external shocks. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how a Chinese economist links fiscal and monetary policy to new quality productive forces after the December 2024 policy conference.
quoteEn: Fiscal policy and monetary policy cannot each fight their own battles; they should complement each other and exert force in concert.
quoteZh: 财政政策与货币政策不能各自为战，而应相互补位、协同发力。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023. It refers to growth driven by technological breakthroughs, digital, green and intelligent upgrading, and new industries.
An annual meeting of the Party and state leadership, usually held in December, that sets the main economic tasks and policy direction for the coming year.
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth based on innovation, efficiency and sustainability.

glossary.literal: specialised, refined, distinctive and innovative enterprises
glossary.explanation: Small and medium-sized enterprises officially designated for specialisation and innovation in niche fields. Policy supports them as part of industrial upgrading.

t: Providing legal safeguards for ecological civilization in the new era
zh: 为新时代生态文明建设提供法律保障
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), via Chinese Social Sciences Net
paras: This short commentary asks what the drafting of an Ecological Environment Code signifies for China's new era. Zhang argues that the political, practical and theoretical conditions for codification are now ripe, and that the code consolidates the results of ecological civilization construction in systematic, codified form under Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization.

The article lists the aspects of the code that Zhang says it embodies. They include sustainable development, the strategic status of ecological civilization, the modernization of environmental rule of law, the goal of a "Beautiful China", environmental rights, green and low-carbon development, global environmental governance, and a Chinese environmental-law knowledge system.

Zhang describes the code as organised in five parts: general provisions, pollution control, natural ecological protection, green and low-carbon development, and ecological and environmental liability. In Zhang's account, it would integrate a body of more than 30 laws, over 100 administrative regulations and over 1,000 local regulations. The author says these now overlap, and that codification can remove conflicts, fill gaps and improve enforceability. Zhang also cites the 2018 constitutional amendment and the 2022 UN General Assembly resolution on a clean, healthy and sustainable environment as supports for writing environmental rights into the code.

Zhang concludes that codification is more than a consolidation of existing rules. In the author's view, it reflects a change in the idea of rule of law in the new era and public consensus on environmental protection. Zhang expects it to coordinate economic development with ecological protection and to offer Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to global environmental governance. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of the rationale for China's environmental code and the policy documents behind it.
quoteEn: Compiling the Ecological Environment Code can systematically integrate existing environmental protection laws and regulations, eliminate legal conflicts, fill legal gaps, and form a unified and coordinated legal system.
quoteZh: 生态环境法典的编纂可以系统整合现有的环境保护法律法规，消除法律冲突，填补法律空白，形成统一、协调的法律体系。

glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization
glossary.explanation: The body of ideas on environmental protection and development associated with Xi Jinping, treated in Party doctrine as a component of Xi Jinping Thought. It is the official guiding framework for China's environmental policy.

An official goal, placed in the Party's overall plan from the 18th Party Congress (2012), of integrating environmental protection into economic, political, cultural and social development. It was written into the Constitution in 2018.
An official slogan and goal for a cleaner, ecologically sound country. It features in Party documents including those of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

An official development approach that seeks to cut pollution and carbon emissions while sustaining economic growth. It is linked to China's "dual carbon" targets for peaking emissions and reaching carbon neutrality.

t: How legal research can serve the building of a higher-level socialist country under the rule of law
zh: 法学研究如何服务建设更高水平的社会主义法治国家
