The article takes its framework from Xi Jinping's speech at the national conference commending ethnic unity and progress, which set out five areas of work. Chu goes through them in turn, each with a short account of what it requires.

On the political side, Chu holds that Party leadership gives the community its leadership, organisational strength and common ideological and political base. On culture, the author calls for continuing the Chinese cultural lineage, strengthening the Chinese nation's cultural subjectivity, and educating people in patriotism, collectivism and socialism. On the economy, Chu notes that ethnic areas lag behind and links their high-quality development to common prosperity, which the author calls the essential feature of Chinese modernization. Proposed measures include infrastructure, advantageous industries and new quality productive forces suited to local conditions.

On society, Chu proposes interlocking social structures and communities, so that peoples cling together like pomegranate seeds, together with better public services and orderly population movement. On law, the author calls for governing ethnic affairs by law, keeping regional ethnic autonomy and grassroots self-government, and promoting legal education. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official framework for ethnic-affairs work as presented in the Party press in early 2025.
quoteEn: To accelerate high-quality development in ethnic areas and steadily advance common prosperity for all ethnic groups, the new development philosophy must be applied completely, accurately and comprehensively.
quoteZh: 加快民族地区高质量发展，扎实推进各民族共同富裕，就要完整准确全面贯彻新发展理念

glossary.zh: 铸牢中华民族共同体意识
glossary.en: a strong sense of community for the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: forging a firm consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: The slogan designating the main thread of Party ethnic policy since the 2010s, stressing a common national identity shared by all ethnic groups.
The official term for China's development path under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western modernization.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all of the population, described in Party discourse as an essential feature of socialism.
A concept promoted from 2023–24 that stresses innovation-driven, technology-intensive productive forces as a basis for high-quality development.
The official goal for China's economy since 2017, emphasising quality, efficiency and balance over speed of growth.

t: Opening up broader prospects for Chinese modernization through reform and opening up
zh: 在改革开放中开辟中国式现代化更加广阔的前景
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 10 January 2025, takes its cue from Xi Jinping's 2025 New Year address. Yan Lianfu asks how further comprehensively deepening reform can keep opening broader prospects for Chinese modernization in the final year of the 14th Five-Year Plan. Yan's answer is that this requires strong leadership, unified effort, stronger development momentum and wider space for development.

The piece is organised under four headings, each tied to quotations from the New Year address and to the decisions of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). They cover mobilising Party members and cadres, making the people the protagonists of reform, concentrating on high-quality development, and improving the institutions and mechanisms of high-standard opening up.

On leadership, Yan argues that reform has overcome hard problems because it has stayed under the Party's centralised and unified leadership. Yan calls for better incentive and disciplinary mechanisms, a proper orientation in selecting cadres, and strict application of the "three distinctions" so that officials willing to take responsibility are backed. On the people, Yan cites per capita disposable income of 39,218 yuan in 2023, a real rise of 94.4% over 2012, as evidence that reform serves people's wellbeing. On development, Yan urges adapting new quality productive forces to regional strengths, advancing green development, and coordinating macroeconomic policies. Opening up is to deepen through institutional opening, pilot free trade zones and "true multilateralism", and to widen through new competitive advantages and a more proactive opening strategy.

Yan concludes that Chinese modernization will find broader prospects only if reform and opening up continue under Party leadership, with the people at the centre. The author describes China as the main trading partner of more than 150 countries and regions, and presents its opening up as win-win cooperation that offers the world new opportunities and contributes to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in early 2025 links the New Year address and the Third Plenum to cadre incentives, regional development, green growth and institutional opening up.
quoteEn: Only by making the Party stronger, with Party members and cadres all charging at the front, can Chinese modernization be ensured to break through the waves and travel steadily and far.
quoteZh: 只有把党建设得更加坚强有力，党员干部都冲锋在前，才能确保中国式现代化劈波斩浪、行稳致远。

glossary.explanation: The official concept of China's own path to modernization, elaborated by the Party since the early 2020s. It is presented as distinct from Western models.

A principle promoted by Xi Jinping for handling cadres' mistakes. It distinguishes errors made in exploratory reform from those made against explicit rules, unintended errors from deliberate ones, and personal gain from public-interest motives.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industries rather than traditional factor inputs.

The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth emphasising innovation, efficiency, environmental sustainability and balance. It has been described as the primary task of building a modern socialist country.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formulation of China's vision for international relations, stressing cooperation and shared interests.

t: Correctly handling the "five major relationships" to build China into a leading country in education
zh: 正确处理“五个重大关系”，扎实推进教育强国建设
paras: This short commentary takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference in September 2024, which set out a systematic plan for building a leading country in education. Zou argues that, although China's education system is now the largest in the world and its level of modernization is in the world's upper-middle ranks, further progress requires correctly handling five major relationships.

The article is organised as five sections, one per relationship, followed by a brief conclusion. The pairs are: supporting national strategy and meeting people's livelihood needs; knowledge learning and all-round development; training talent and meeting social needs; orderliness and vitality; and taking root in China while drawing on international experience.

In Zou's account, each pair is complementary rather than opposed. Education must supply talent for national strategy while giving people fairer access to quality schooling. Knowledge learning should not be narrowed to exam scores but integrated with moral, physical, aesthetic and labour education. Orderliness corresponds to "upholding fundamental principles" and vitality to innovation. Education should serve high-quality development and new quality productive forces, and combine Chinese cultural roots with selective foreign learning.

Zou concludes that building a leading country in education is a long-term, systematic undertaking centred on the fundamental task of fostering virtue and cultivating talent. Handling the five relationships, the author holds, will produce a high-quality education system that supplies talent and intellectual support for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Xi's 2024 education speech is being interpreted in Party-school and provincial commentary.
quoteEn: Orderliness means "upholding fundamental principles": it requires that education work strictly abide by the major policies of the Party and the state and by laws and regulations.
quoteZh: 规范有序就是“守正”，就是要求教育工作的开展严格遵守党和国家的大政方针以及法律法规

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological innovation, as a basis for high-quality development.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth emphasising quality, innovation and efficiency.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China's strength and international standing by mid-century.
The official fundamental task of education, stressing moral character alongside knowledge and skills.

t: Promoting the development of new quality productive forces through high-quality work on young talent
zh: 以高质量青年人才工作推动新质生产力发展
paras: This commentary, first published on People's Forum Network (Renmin Luntan Wang), asks how work on young talent can support the development of new quality productive forces. Wei and Ding argue that young people are a major force behind scientific progress and industrial upgrading, and that high-quality youth talent work can turn a talent advantage into an innovation and development advantage.

The piece opens with Xi Jinping's call to keep up innovation and with a January 2024 measure from the Ministry of Natural Resources on training and using young science and technology talent. It then has two main parts: the policy framework linking education, science and technology, and talent, and practical guidance for building a youth work system.

On policy, the authors cite the 20th Party Congress (2022) and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which treat education, science and technology, and talent as foundational support for Chinese modernization. They argue that China's talent pool is large but still falls short of what new quality productive forces require. Their proposals are to encourage innovation through projects and competitions and by grounding it in practice; to promote cross-disciplinary cooperation and industry–university–research platforms; to give ideological and political education; and to allow orderly talent flows while guarding against talent loss and waste.

Wei and Ding conclude that policy for cultivating strategic talent should centre on young science and technology talent, backed by top-level design, greater trust and stronger incentives so that young people can "take the lead". Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese policy writing links youth work, talent strategy and new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: The core of new quality productive forces lies in innovation, and young talent is precisely the main force of innovation.
quoteZh: 新质生产力的核心在于创新，而青年人才正是创新的主力军。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023–24 for productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, especially in advanced technology and emerging industries.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out by the Party from the 20th Party Congress (2022) onwards and presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Chinese modernization: a new paradigm and new opportunities for modernization in the Global South
zh: 中国式现代化：“全球南方”现代化的新范式与新机遇
paras: This short commentary asks how Chinese modernization can serve countries of the Global South as they pursue their own modernization. Ye and Fu argue that Chinese modernization, through its distinctive path, practical results and international influence, offers these countries a new path and a model to learn from. They open with Xi Jinping's statement that the collective rise of the Global South is a defining mark of great global change.

The article has three parts. The first describes the mixed situation of the Global South, in which opportunities and difficulties exist side by side. The second sets out what Chinese modernization demonstrates to other developing countries. The third turns to practical channels through which China is said to assist the modernization of these states.

On opportunities, the authors cite a rise in the Global South's share of world GDP from 24% to over 40%, deeper South–South cooperation and a more favourable multilateral setting. On difficulties, they list dependence on primary-product exports, weak industry and technology, poor infrastructure, unequal education and health provision, and wide wealth gaps. They then draw five lessons from China's experience: independent exploration of a path suited to national conditions rather than copying the West; a people-centred approach, illustrated by poverty alleviation, education and medical insurance; gradual and coordinated reform; and reliance on scientific and technological innovation backed by talent training. In practice, they point to the Belt and Road Initiative (the China–Laos and China–Thailand railways, the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor), trade and investment that move industrial links to partner countries, and technology transfer such as agricultural projects in Tanzania and the China–Belarus industrial park.

The authors conclude that China remains a member of the Global South and a reliable long-term partner for developing countries. In their view, deeper cooperation will give Global South modernization lasting momentum and help build a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academic commentary presents Chinese modernization as a reference point for the Global South.
quoteEn: This course clearly shows that Global South countries can fully escape excessive dependence on external models and truly take the initiative in development only by proceeding from their own realities, drawing deeply on their own strengths and resolutely exploring a path of modernization suited to their national conditions.
quoteZh: 这一历程清晰地表明，“全球南方”国家唯有立足本国实际，深度挖掘自身优势，坚定地探索符合自身国情的现代化路径，才能彻底摆脱对外部模式的过度依赖，真正掌握发展的主动权。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of a distinctively Chinese path to modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as an alternative to Western models.

A collective term for developing and emerging countries, mostly in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Chinese official discourse uses it to stress solidarity among these states and China's place among them.
A Chinese initiative launched in 2013 to build infrastructure and expand trade and investment links across Asia, Africa and Europe.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping. It calls for shared development and security and a more equitable international order.

t: New quality productive forces unleash powerful momentum for economic growth
zh: 新质生产力激发经济增长澎湃动力
paras: Liu Ying asks how China can move off its traditional growth path at a time when global industrial and supply chains are being reshaped. The commentary argues that accelerating the development of new quality productive forces, with innovation in the leading role, is the way to drive high-quality development. It links this to Xi Jinping's strategic plan, the 2024 Government Work Report and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

The piece is organised in three parts. The first treats a large rise in total factor productivity as the core marker of new quality productive forces. The second looks at the carriers of these forces: upgrading traditional industries and developing strategic emerging and future industries. The third covers deepening reform in the economic, science and technology, talent, financial and fiscal systems.

Liu defines total factor productivity as the residual in growth after labour and capital inputs are removed, and says it can rise through technological progress or better resource allocation. On this basis the author describes new quality productive forces as advanced and green productive forces that cannot form spontaneously. They require technology-led industrial innovation, new ideas, and management and institutional change. The author cites data as a core factor, giving a digital economy of 50.2 trillion yuan in 2022. The author also cites China's leading position in solar and wind power and new-energy vehicles, and Beijing's plans for 20 future industries.

Liu holds that reform is the necessary path. The author calls for a unified national market and factor-market reform, and for science and technology reform that turns patents into productivity, backed by R&D spending of 2.64% of GDP in 2023. Further proposals are talent reform to turn the demographic dividend into a talent dividend, financial reform that raises direct financing and supports innovation, and fiscal reform that realigns central and local powers and uses 1 trillion yuan in ultra-long-term bonds to draw in patient capital. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official policy case linking new quality productive forces to total factor productivity and structural reform.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces take a substantial rise in total factor productivity as their core marker.
quoteZh: 新质生产力以全要素生产率大幅提升为核心标志。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 for productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, especially in high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality sectors.
The official goal, set out since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth that stresses quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
An economic measure of the part of output growth not explained by labour and capital inputs, taken to reflect technology, management and institutions.

t: Promoting high-quality development requires guarding against "old wine in new bottles"
zh: 推动高质量发展要防止“新瓶装旧酒”
paras: This short commentary, published in Study Times in January 2025, takes up a warning Xi Jinping gave in January 2024: some officials, while claiming to promote high-quality development, are in practice pouring "old wine into new bottles". Wang argues that real high-quality development requires "new wine in new bottles", meaning new content as well as new forms.

The piece first explains the metaphor and the practices it describes. It then sets out what high-quality development means, drawing on its positioning, mode, goals and results. It goes on to discuss new quality productive forces and the deepening of reform, and closes with a call for fresh thinking, methods and practice.

Wang says the "old wine" problem appears when localities announce new policies, projects, technologies or models while keeping the traditional development mode, habitual thinking and outdated management. In Wang's view this is contrary to materialist dialectics, to the nature of high-quality development and to China's actual conditions. Developing new quality productive forces is presented as the "new wine", since they are marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality and so guard against innovation for its own sake. Wang also stresses building production relations suited to the productive forces. The commentary applies the same logic to reform: renamed measures with unchanged substance fail to build the needed institutions. As an example, it cites localities that set up large government-guided funds to build "patient capital" without grasping its dual policy and market character, which wastes resources.

Wang concludes that the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) shows the leadership's resolve to remove institutional obstacles, and that economic reform is the "ox's nose" leading further comprehensive deepening of reform. Officials are urged to read changing conditions accurately, adapt scientifically and seek change actively. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-press commentary turns a leader's metaphor into guidance for officials on high-quality development.
quoteEn: "Old wine in new bottles" fits neither the requirements of Marxist materialist dialectics, nor the essential features of high-quality development, still less China's actual conditions of development.
quoteZh: “新瓶装旧酒”既不符合马克思主义唯物辩证法的要求，也不符合高质量发展的本质特征，更不符合我国的发展实际。

glossary.explanation: A policy goal that has been prominent since the late 2010s. It shifts emphasis from fast, extensive growth to efficiency, innovation, balance and sustainability.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It refers to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, characterised as high-technology, high-efficiency and high-quality.
Long-term investment capital that accepts slow returns, discussed in Chinese policy circles as support for innovation and emerging industries.

glossary.en: the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A Party meeting held in July 2024 that adopted a decision on further comprehensively deepening reform.

t: Understanding the buzzwords of China's economic development
zh: 读懂中国经济发展热词
source: China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News (posted on marxism.cass.cn, 8 January 2025)
paras: This short explanatory piece, first published in the Party discipline newspaper China Discipline Inspection and Supervision News, sets out to help readers understand the key terms in current discussion of China's economy. Writing at the start of 2025, Xu presents 2024 as a year in which the economy, despite greater external pressure and domestic difficulties, remained generally stable while making progress, and shows the new terms as expressions of that development.

After an opening overview of 2024, the article defines seven terms in turn: new quality productive forces, patient capital, future industries, the package of incremental policies, the silver economy, the debut economy and the low-altitude economy. Each entry follows a similar pattern of definition, characteristics, significance and prospects. The author's overview credits ultra-long special government bonds and the policy package with expanding domestic demand and lifting consumption.

Xu defines new quality productive forces as an advanced form of productivity led by innovation, marked by a major rise in total factor productivity and described as an inherent requirement of high-quality development. Patient capital, which comes mainly from government funds, pension funds and insurance capital, is presented as a necessary condition for developing these forces. Future industries are described as frontier-technology sectors still at an early stage, needing sustained investment and cooperation among government, firms and universities. The incremental policy package is portrayed as comprehensive and coordinated, covering fiscal, monetary, employment, industrial and consumption policy, with the aim of long-term high-quality development. The silver economy, debut economy and low-altitude economy are treated as growth areas in which Xu notes opportunities and, for the last, obstacles such as weak airspace management, thin infrastructure and low technical standardisation.

Xu concludes that these concepts show an economy displaying resilience and potential, which the article calls an important engine of world economic growth. For the newer sectors, the author calls for better policy frameworks, infrastructure, technology research and safety supervision, with government, firms and society working together. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned glossary of the economic vocabulary used in Chinese policy discourse at the end of 2024.
quoteEn: Developing new quality productive forces is an inherent requirement and an important focal point for promoting high-quality development.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力是推动高质量发展的内在要求和重要着力点。

glossary.explanation: A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than traditional growth paths. It is now central to official economic policy.
The official economic goal since about 2017, stressing efficiency, innovation and sustainability over the speed of growth.
Long-term investment funds that tolerate risk and do not seek quick returns. Official discourse treats them as supporting technological and industrial innovation.
The set of additional economic support measures announced in late 2024 to stabilise growth, the property market and capital markets and to boost domestic demand.
Economic activity serving retirees and older people, such as elder care, health services and age-friendly products.
Economic activity based on low-altitude flight by crewed and uncrewed aircraft, including drones and eVTOL vehicles.

t: Advancing high-quality development of the Yangtze River Economic Belt through regional coordination and integration
zh: 以区域协同融通推进长江经济带高质量发展
paras: Li Xuesong asks how the Yangtze River Economic Belt can move from cost-driven, scale-based expansion to innovation-driven high-quality development. The article argues that the Belt is one interdependent system whose public problems cannot be handled by any single administrative unit. In Li's view, regional coordination and integration must therefore be the main lever, replacing a mindset of competition with one of cooperation and shared benefit.

The article opens by quoting Xi Jinping's call for provinces along the river to deliberate jointly, govern the ecology together, build jointly and share development. It then diagnoses four shortfalls in coordination: industry, cities, the ecological environment, and scientific and technological innovation. Each shortfall is matched with a set of remedies, and the article closes with proposals on innovation networks and 'innovation enclaves'.

On the diagnosis, Li describes a clear east–west gradient. The Yangtze River Delta leads in output, city coordination and innovation, while the middle and upper reaches suffer from weak industrial foundations, 'core–periphery' city structures and fragmented innovation. Li also points to administrative barriers, local protectionism and weak cross-boundary governance. For industry, Li proposes orderly gradient transfer: Jiangsu and Zhejiang as a 'dual core' for labour-intensive manufacturing, Jiangsu as the anchor for capital-intensive sectors, and technology transfer from the lower reaches to Anhui, Hubei, Sichuan and others. For cities, Li calls for integrated markets, fiscal and tax revenue-sharing for cross-regional projects and enclaves, and the Chengdu–Chongqing urban agglomeration as a breakthrough linking the three major agglomerations. Li also proposes linking the Belt with the Belt and Road Initiative.

For ecology, Li urges legally backed ecological red lines, a law on ecological compensation, vertical and horizontal compensation, and unified monitoring networks. For innovation, Li recommends corridors modelled on the G60 Science and Technology Innovation Corridor, shared major scientific facilities, university alliances and two-way enclaves, with the aim of world-class advanced manufacturing clusters. Li concludes that these measures would build ecological and interest communities along the river. Read the original if you want a detailed, policy-oriented regional economics account of Yangtze coordination, with sector-by-sector and province-by-province proposals.
quoteEn: The Yangtze River Economic Belt faces the dual constraints of high institutional transaction costs and local protectionism, resulting in a fragmented innovation ecosystem, obstacles to innovation cooperation and blocked circulation of innovation resources.
quoteZh: 长江经济带区域面临制度性交易成本偏高与地方保护主义的双重约束，存在创新生态系统呈现碎片化，创新合作面临障碍，创新资源流通受阻等问题。

glossary.explanation: A national development strategy covering provinces and cities along the Yangtze, from Shanghai to Yunnan and Sichuan, elevated to a national strategy in the mid-2010s.
The official goal, set out since 2017, of shifting from rapid scale-based growth to growth driven by innovation, efficiency and sustainability.
China's international infrastructure and trade cooperation initiative, launched in 2013.

t: Empowering the development of new quality productive forces in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area through digital transformation
zh: 以数字化转型赋能粤港澳大湾区新质生产力发展
source: China Theory Network (中国理论网), reposted 2025-01-08
paras: Taking up the call of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) to develop new quality productive forces in line with local conditions and to integrate the real and digital economies, Liu and Chen ask how digital transformation can drive such development in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area. They argue that digital transformation is becoming the key path for the region's high-quality development.

This short commentary is organised in three parts: achievements, challenges and measures. It draws on regional statistics and examples from Guangdong, including industrial, service-sector and governance initiatives.

On achievements, the authors cite the China Digital Economy Development Index Report (2024): Guangdong's digital economy reached 6.9 trillion yuan in 2023, first in the country for eight years, with Shenzhen's core digital industries adding over 1 trillion yuan. They also report that 29,000 large industrial enterprises had been digitalised and over 650,000 small and medium-sized firms connected to cloud services. They identify four challenges: uneven infrastructure across cities, weak digital innovation in chips, operating systems and key AI algorithms, inadequate regulation of cross-border data flows and privacy, and the difficulties small and medium-sized enterprises face with funding, technology and talent.

The authors propose four responses: strengthen infrastructure and use regional support schemes to narrow gaps, raise innovation capacity through closer ties among government, industry, universities and research, improve regulation and cross-border data governance, and support small firms through training, funding and leadership from large enterprises. Read the original if you want a concise, policy-oriented overview of Guangdong's digital economy data and the official agenda for linking digitalisation with new quality productive forces.
quoteEn: Using digital transformation to empower the development of new quality productive forces in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area is a systematic undertaking.
quoteZh: 以数字化转型赋能粤港澳大湾区新质生产力发展是一项系统工程。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological innovation, digital technology and new industries.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from speed-oriented growth to growth based on innovation, efficiency and sustainability.
A national regional development strategy linking Hong Kong, Macao and nine cities in Guangdong province, including Guangzhou and Shenzhen.

t: Scientific methods for developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions
zh: 因地制宜发展新质生产力的科学方法
source: China Theory Network (中国理论网), posted 8 January 2025
paras: Liu Qirui and Luan Yongyu take up a methodological question: how should new quality productive forces be developed in line with local conditions? Starting from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which made this a measure for improving the institutions of high-quality development, they argue that the approach gathers the methodological wisdom of Xi Jinping's economic thought. In their view it must be grasped fully, accurately and comprehensively if further reform is to advance Chinese modernization.

The article is organised around seven modes of thinking, each presented as a method drawn from Xi Jinping's statements: strategic, historical, dialectical, systems, innovation, rule-of-law and bottom-line thinking. Each section pairs the method with a concrete task, ranging from national coordination and the Party's historical role to regional differentiation, education and talent, the legal environment, and economic security. Most claims are supported by quotations from Xi's speeches and Party documents.

Three moves carry the argument. First, the authors read the 'new' and the 'quality' of new quality productive forces as a dialectical pair: 'new' means technological, industrial and other innovation, and 'quality' means high-quality development under the new development philosophy. They contend that, with resource and environmental constraints and a shift from factor inputs to total factor productivity, technology-led industrial innovation is the only new path. Second, they argue that localities should build on their own resource endowments, industrial base and research conditions, while staying within one national plan and a unified national market. The authors stress that there is more than one model, and that finance must serve the real economy. Third, they claim that education, science and talent must be advanced together, and that the rule of law protects innovation, intellectual property and both leading and specialised small firms. They also hold that high-quality development and high-level security reinforce each other.

The authors conclude that new quality productive forces can form faster, and new production relations be shaped faster, only under the Party's comprehensive leadership and the centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. They present the seven methods as a practical toolkit for local officials and policymakers. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned account of how Party theorists frame local-conditions-based development of new quality productive forces and the methods they link to it.
quoteEn: There is not just one model for developing new quality productive forces; one must hold a nationwide-coordination mindset, find one's own strengths within the overall picture of Chinese modernization, play to strengths and avoid weaknesses, and consolidate the foundation while fostering the new.
quoteZh: 发展新质生产力不只有一种模式，要树立一盘棋思想，在中国式现代化大局中找准自身优长，扬长避短、固本兴新。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since 2023, referring to advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovation and upgraded industries rather than by factor inputs alone.
The official goal of the current stage of China's economic development, stressing innovation, efficiency, green growth and balance over speed of growth.
The official name for China's path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
Xi Jinping's framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, introduced in 2015.

t: Upholding the path of integrated development of education, science and technology, and talent with Chinese characteristics
zh: 坚持中国特色教育科技人才一体化发展道路
paras: Guo Hailong asks what historical experience the Communist Party has accumulated in promoting education, science and technology, and talent as one integrated undertaking, and how that work should be coordinated going forward. The article's answer is that over a century of exploration the Party has produced a distinctive path of coordinated development, which it says combines Marxist views of education, science and talent with China's concrete conditions and with traditional Chinese culture. Guo describes this path as the result of the Party's hard exploration and as showing the strengths of China's state system and governance.

The article treats the path as comprising the education development path, the independent innovation path and the path of self-reliant talent training, all with Chinese characteristics. It organises the path around "eight upholds": Party leadership, the "four orientations", a development orientation, goal guidance, reform and innovation, institution building, rule-of-law thinking, and openness and cooperation. Each section gives a short historical sketch, from the Party's early period through Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and then sets out three requirements for the present.

Guo's central claim is that Party leadership is the most essential feature, and that errors on this point would have catastrophic consequences. Guo requires centralised and unified leadership, carried through every field and stage, while the Party sets direction, plans and policy rather than managing every detail. Other sections tie the path to Xi Jinping's concepts: the new development philosophy, high-quality development and new quality productive forces. They also tie it to the goal of building a strong education, science and technology, and talent nation by 2035, and to a reform that Guo describes as neither closed and rigid nor a change of banner. Guo also stresses systematic institution building, lawmaking that is precise and timely, and global innovation cooperation under a community with a shared future for mankind.

Guo concludes that these eight features answer both why and how education, science and technology, and talent should be coordinated. The article presents them as guidance for the "new journey" of building a modern socialist country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It is a statement of official interpretation, not a critical or empirical study.

Read the original if you want a compact account of how Party-state discourse frames the integration of education, science and technology, and talent policy, including its main slogans and their historical lineage.
quoteEn: Upholding the Party's leadership is the most essential feature of the path of coordinated development of education, science and technology, and talent with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 坚持党的领导。这是中国特色统筹教育科技人才发展道路的最本质特征。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023 to describe growth driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation rather than by traditional resource-heavy inputs.
An official formula, prominent since 2017, that emphasises quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
Xi Jinping's formulation of five principles: innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
A guideline for science and technology work: facing the world's scientific frontiers, the main economic battlefield, major national needs, and people's lives and health.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world of shared interests and cooperation, used by Chinese official sources since 2012.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely linked with the Chinese Dream.

t: How to make capital more patient
zh: 怎样让资本更有耐心
paras: This short commentary asks what "patient capital" is, why capital can be patient and why China needs more of it now. Meng defines it as capital focused on long-term investment, with high risk tolerance and endurance of short-term market swings. The article argues that patience is compatible with capital's profit-seeking nature and is essential to technological innovation.

The piece begins with the term's recent prominence in Party and economic-work meetings. It then distinguishes patient capital from merely long-term capital, explains where patience comes from, and links it to innovation and to new quality productive forces. It closes with four policy directions.

Meng rejects the view that capital's drive for quick profit rules out patience. In the author's account, patience arises from understanding the lengthy, risky path from scientific discovery to industrial change, and from building a "community" between investors and innovative firms. Because innovation must cross a "valley of death" between research and market, Meng argues that patient capital matches its internal rhythm and is needed to address the lack of long-term funding for new quality productive forces.

Meng proposes a predictable, law-based investment environment; high-quality investment targets and ways to connect venture capital to innovators; a virtuous cycle of science and technology, industry and finance; and a leading role for state capital. State capital and government funds should serve as the "ballast" of patient capital, with assessment over the full life cycle and reasonable tolerance of failure. Read the original if you want a concise, official-register account of why Chinese policy circles promote patient capital and what measures they link to it.
quoteEn: The investment philosophy of patient capital fits closely with the inherent laws of scientific and technological innovation.
quoteZh: 耐心资本的投资理念与科技创新的内在规律高度契合。

glossary.explanation: Capital that commits to long-term investment, tolerates high risk and short-term volatility. It was highlighted at a Politburo meeting in April 2024 and at the Central Economic Work Conference.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven mainly by technological innovation rather than by factor inputs.

t: Intellectual threads and two-way interpretation in the "dispute between ancient and modern, China and the West"
zh: “古今中西之争”的思想线索和双向阐释
paras: Yang Huilin, a professor at Renmin University of China, asks how the long-running "dispute between ancient and modern, China and the West" can be resolved. Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2025, Yang takes up Xi Jinping's remark that the present era is better placed than any before it to resolve this dispute. Yang's thesis is that the world's texts should be read as "intertexts" and that scholarship should take the form of dialogue. Such dialogue can recover the distinct texture of Chinese civilisation and also give access to Western systems of knowledge.

The piece has three parts. The first looks at Chinese resources in Western reflection on metaphysics, drawing on Graham, Kristeva, Heidegger, Levinas, Badiou and Western theologians. The second traces a dialogical tradition in modern Chinese scholarship: Lü Simian, Qian Mu, Zhang Guangzhi, Liang Shuming, Feng Youlan, Zhang Dongsun and Zhou Zuoren. The third sets out the method of "mutual reference" and "mutual interpretation" between China and the West. Yang is a chief expert on a major National Social Science Fund project on conceptual tools for dialogue between Chinese and Western civilisations.

Yang's central contrast is linguistic. In Indo-European subject–predicate syntax, Being is explained through the predicate "is". Yang says classical Chinese lacked this use, so that A. C. Graham found the small word "is" vital to Western philosophy but meaningless in Chinese. Chinese thought instead rests on polar relations, yin and yang. Yang links this to Western concepts of relationality and "correlation", and to the "correlative thinking" described by Sinologists. Yang's case study is Zhang Dongsun's 1938 essay on thought, language and culture. It was translated in 1939 and summarised by Mazumdar in 1956, but entered the core of Western debate only when Kristeva read it. Effective conceptual tools, Yang argues, are "productive" rather than merely "descriptive", and translation works in both directions. Yang's examples are Heidegger's "Es gibt" and Derrida's Donner la mort.

Yang concludes that mutual reference and interpretation seek neither agreed conclusions nor a single governing logic. They reactivate the resources of both sides and bring new self-understanding along with understanding of others. Such deep dialogue, Yang says, can counter talk of civilisational superiority and conflict, and should lead to exchange over estrangement, mutual learning over conflict and inclusiveness over superiority. Yang proposes tracing back and restoring each side's theoretical tools and sources of problems as the basic task. Read the original if you are interested in comparative philosophy, translation and Chinese–Western intellectual exchange, or in how a Chinese scholar frames this project.
quoteEn: The essence of "mutual reference" and "mutual interpretation" lies in sharing together and moving towards each other; it does not presuppose given conceptual tools and discourse systems, nor seek "common ground" on the basis of any single logic.
quoteZh: “互参”和“互释”的实质在于“相与而共”“相向而行”，却不是默认既定的概念工具和话语系统，不是依据任何单一的逻辑而“求同”。

glossary.en: dispute between ancient and modern, China and the West
glossary.explanation: A long-standing debate in modern Chinese thought over how to relate tradition to modernity and Chinese culture to Western learning. Xi Jinping has referred to it when calling for cultural work that fuses past and present and bridges China and the West.
Yang's term for using Chinese and Western ideas as reference points for each other in dialogue, so that each is illuminated by difference.
Yang's term for two-way explanation, in which each tradition is read in the other's terms and gains new self-understanding.

t: Cultivating high-calibre talent suited to green and low-carbon development
zh: 培育与绿色低碳发展相适应的高素质人才
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2025, Xu Huajun asks how China can train the large body of skilled people needed to meet its carbon peak and carbon neutrality commitments. Xu argues that green and low-carbon development depends on mobilising universities, enterprises and society as a whole to produce talent that practises, adapts to and leads low-carbon change. The article is a short newspaper commentary that takes its policy cue from the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024).

The piece is organised around three actors: universities, enterprises and the wider public. Each section gives a short list of practical measures. Xu refers to the Ministry of Education's implementation plan for building a national education system for green and low-carbon development, and cites Xi Jinping's call for a simple, moderate, green and low-carbon way of life.

For universities, Xu proposes faster building of disciplines and majors such as energy storage, hydrogen, carbon capture and carbon trading, together with interdisciplinary training and new textbooks. Xu also proposes innovation and entrepreneurship education, competitions, and integrating the Party's carbon decisions into ideological and political education and campus culture. Enterprises, Xu says, must first green their own operations, then act as a bridge by co-training students with universities, co-building research platforms and developing professional evaluation standards. For society, Xu calls for family, community and social-organisation campaigns, continuing education for working people, and online courses and new-media outreach.

Xu concludes that combining these channels would create a multi-level learning system that raises public awareness and produces innovative people with practical ability. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese official commentary links carbon-neutrality goals to education, workforce training and ideological work.
quoteEn: Enterprises are the main actors in developing green and low-carbon industry and bear important responsibility for advancing green and low-carbon education, and achieving their own green and low-carbon development is the precondition for fulfilling that responsibility.
quoteZh: 企业是绿色低碳产业发展的主体，在推进绿色低碳教育方面肩负重要责任，而实现自身绿色低碳发展是履行这一责任的前提。

glossary.explanation: China's pledge, announced in 2020, to peak carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and reach carbon neutrality before 2060.
Compulsory courses in Chinese universities teaching Marxism and official Party theory. The article proposes adding green and low-carbon content to them.

t: Modernization is not an ideology but a development experience
st: Lecture by Professor Zheng Yongnian at Shanghai Jiao Tong University's "Wenzhi Lecture Hall"
zh: 现代化不是意识形态而是发展经验
zhSub: 郑永年教授在上海交通大学“文治大讲堂”的演讲
paras: This is the text of a lecture given by Zheng Yongnian at Shanghai Jiao Tong University and posted in January 2025. Zheng asks where China's opening up should go next and what China can contribute to a more open world. The answer is that China should deepen high-level opening, including unilateral opening to less developed countries, and treat Chinese modernization as a development experience for the Global South rather than as an ideology.

Zheng begins with his years working in the United States and Britain during the Thatcher and Reagan revolutions. He then compares three historical modernization models: the Latin American, the US-allied and the isolated. Next he reads China's two waves of opening, the forced opening after the Opium Wars and the opening after 1978. He then assesses the current international situation, covering Western decline, multipolarity and the Global South. The final part turns to development, artificial intelligence, regulation and unilateral opening.

In Zheng's account, Chinese modernization is unusual because it has achieved both development and independence, whereas the other models bring dependence or isolation. He says the second wave of opening depended on specific conditions, including Cold War geopolitics, Western capital seeking a "new frontier" and Western hopes that China would become more like the West. Those conditions have changed, because the United States now favours protectionism and economic nationalism. Zheng argues that great-power competition is mainly a contest of development models. He notes that the US leads in AI, that Europe over-regulates, and that China produces strong research but weak application, with talent leaving for Silicon Valley. He argues that regulation should follow development, as in Singapore. Zheng also holds that unilateral opening, which he says Britain and the US practised, would reshape trade patterns and reduce confrontational thinking.

Zheng concludes that China should keep a peaceful, win-win mindset, avoid pessimism about the "great changes unseen in a century", and avoid big mistakes. He asks whether China can sum up its experience of developing while staying independent and offer it to the Global South as a reference. He also says Chinese modernization needs strategic thinking beyond economics, for example by opening to foreign-owned hospitals and building mutual interdependence. Read the original if you want to see how a prominent Chinese scholar links openness, the Global South, US–China technology competition and Chinese modernization in a single public lecture.
quoteEn: Modernization is not an ideology but a development experience.
quoteZh: 现代化不是一种意识形态，而是发展经验。

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, promoted prominently since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from the Western model.
A term for developing and emerging countries, often used to stress their shared interests and their relative weakness in the existing international order. Chinese official discourse uses it widely.

t: Strengthening the ability to grasp and apply laws
zh: 增强把握运用规律能力
source: Jiefang Daily, 7 January 2024 (as given in the source; the posting date suggests 2025)
paras: This short newspaper commentary interprets the Central Economic Work Conference's call for five relationships to be "properly coordinated". Zhang Xu starts from the view that external conditions are worsening and the economy faces difficulties. Zhang also holds that China's economic foundation is sound, and that the basic trend of long-term improvement is unchanged. The article argues that handling these five relationships well is how positive factors become real development results.

The piece takes the five pairs in turn: an effective market and an enterprising government; aggregate supply and aggregate demand; fostering new growth drivers and updating old ones; improving the increment and revitalising the stock; and raising quality and expanding total volume. Each gets a brief explanation tied to the Conference's policy language. The piece ends with a point about Party leadership and the capabilities required of officials.

Zhang presents the market–government pairing as a law that a high-level socialist market economy must follow. It combines the general law that the market plays the decisive role in allocating resources with the avoidance of the defects of capitalist market economies, through a stronger role for the Party and government. On supply and demand, Zhang names weak investment, insufficient consumption and sluggish exports as demand-side problems, and capacity surplus as a supply-side one. Zhang reads the Conference's priority on boosting consumption as a way to raise total demand. The remaining pairs are linked to high-quality development, new quality productive forces driven by technological and institutional innovation, better resource allocation, and the material basis of Chinese modernization.

Zhang concludes that whether China can manage the world's second-largest economy depends fundamentally on how well the Party plays its leading role. Leaders at all levels are urged to study, investigate and gain practical experience. The aim is to strengthen their ability to grasp and apply the laws of the market economy, of social development and of nature. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Party-affiliated economist presents the Central Economic Work Conference's priorities in official terms.
quoteEn: In the final analysis, whether China can manage the world's second-largest economy and sustain healthy economic and social development depends fundamentally on how well the Party plays its core leadership role in that development.
quoteZh: 归根结底，能不能驾驭好世界第二大经济体，能不能保持经济社会持续健康发展，从根本上讲取决于党在经济社会发展中的领导核心作用发挥得好不好。

glossary.explanation: An annual closed-door meeting of the Party and state leadership, usually held in December, that sets the economic agenda and priorities for the coming year.
The official name for the Party's model of national development, presented as distinct from Western modernization paths.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation.
The official goal of shifting growth from scale and speed towards efficiency, innovation and sustainability.

glossary.zh: 社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.explanation: The official description of China's economic system, which combines market mechanisms with public ownership and Party leadership.

t: Expanding development advantages through capability building
zh: 以能力提升扩大发展优势
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in Jiefang Daily in January 2024, asks what abilities Shanghai's officials need if the city is to play a leading and exemplary role in advancing Chinese modernization. Cao Dongbo argues that Shanghai must build three capabilities: strategic agility and initiative, focusing on critical junctures and overcoming difficulties, and grasping laws of development while allocating resources scientifically.

The piece follows these three capabilities in turn. Each is defined conceptually, tied to remarks by Xi Jinping, and then applied to Shanghai's industrial and urban agenda. Cao draws on the book Xi Jinping in Shanghai, on Xi's 2007 visit to Baoshan District, and on the Central Economic Work Conference's call for major economic provinces to "shoulder the main burden".

Cao presents strategic agility (flexible adjustment) and strategic initiative (seizing opportunities) as complementary. As examples he cites Xi's earlier push for balanced development of the three industrial sectors, with manufacturing not neglected, and Shanghai's aim of becoming a national AI hub. On critical junctures, he reads the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and of the 18th Central Committee (2013) as epoch-making turning points. He describes tackling "hard bones" and "choke-point" problems as concentrating resources on bottlenecks. On laws of development, he invokes Marxist philosophy and calls for tailored policies for producer services, knowledge-intensive services and consumer services.

Cao concludes that these three capabilities are the core of urban development and the foundation of high-quality development. He calls for a consistent, persistent style of work, likened to hammering in a nail with repeated blows. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-school-style leadership discourse is applied to Shanghai's industrial policy.
quoteEn: Strategic agility and strategic initiative are the key abilities to adapt to change, seize the initiative and lead development in a complex and changeable environment, and they are a dialectical unity of flexibility and adaptability with foresight and initiative.
quoteZh: 战略敏捷和战略主动是在复杂多变的环境中适应变化、抢占先机、引领发展的关键能力，是灵活性、变通性与前瞻性、主动性的辩证统一。

glossary.explanation: The official Party framing of China's development path, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022), which stresses a large population, common prosperity and peaceful development.
An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to development driven by innovation, efficiency and better quality.

t: Opening up broader prospects for Chinese modernization
zh: 开辟中国式现代化更加广阔的前景
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in Jiefang Daily in January 2025 and reposted on the Academy of Marxism site, takes up Xi Jinping's New Year message that the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) sounded the call for further comprehensive deepening of reform. Feng Jun argues that Chinese modernization will open up still broader prospects through reform and opening up, and that further reform must be organised around it as its central theme.

The piece is organised under three headings: the historical shift from "modernization in China" to "Chinese modernization"; the rejection of the equation of modernization with Westernization; and the status of Chinese modernization theory within Marxist theory.

On the first point, Feng traces the path from the Opium War and the Self-Strengthening Movement through the founding of the People's Republic to reform and opening up. The author insists that the periods before and after 1978 are stages of one exploration and must not be set against each other. On the second, Feng argues that no single modernization model or universal standard exists, that the Western process coincided with capitalism but this does not make modernization Westernization, and that China's experience widens the options open to developing countries.

Feng concludes that the theory of Chinese modernization, with its defining features, essential requirements and major principles, is a major achievement of scientific socialism and part of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official narrative links Chinese modernization to reform and opening up, to civilisational claims and to Party theory.
quoteEn: Modernization does not equal Westernization. Modernization has both universality and particularity.
quoteZh: 现代化不等于西方化。现代化既有普遍性，又有特殊性。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of socialist modernization under Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models and has five stated features, such as a huge population and common prosperity.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: Doing a good job of assessing the consistency of macro-policy orientation
zh: 做好宏观政策取向一致性评估
source: Economic Daily, 7 January 2024 (as dated on the site)
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily, takes up the call of the Central Economic Work Conference held at the end of 2024 to bring economic and non-economic policies together in a single assessment of macro-policy orientation consistency. Jiang argues that such assessment is the precondition for making policies work as a coordinated 'combination of punches' and for raising their overall effectiveness in support of high-quality development.

The piece first explains why non-economic policies such as environmental protection and education belong in the assessment, then sets out three practical measures. It is a compact policy argument rather than a survey of literature or cases.

Jiang contends that non-economic policies shape resource allocation, market expectations and social wellbeing. Environmental policy, for example, restrains high-emission industries while fostering green industries; education raises human capital and innovative capacity. Joint assessment, the author says, avoids a 'fallacy of composition' in which policy goals cancel or contradict one another, and balances short-term, local gains against long-term, overall goals. The proposed measures are a cross-departmental coordination mechanism with regular meetings and shared data; digital-intelligent assessment using big data, artificial intelligence and digital-twin simulation; and greater disclosure of assessment standards and results.

Jiang concludes that consistency assessment, backed by cross-department cooperation and feedback, would improve policy transparency and public trust, stabilise market expectations and encourage corporate investment and innovation. Read the original if you want a brief example of how a Chinese economist interprets the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference's emphasis on policy coordination.
quoteEn: Bringing both economic and non-economic policies into the assessment of macro-policy orientation consistency can optimise resource allocation, make policy goals complementary, avoid the 'fallacy of composition' caused by goals that offset or contradict each other, and safeguard coordinated economic and social development.
quoteZh: 把经济政策与非经济性政策都纳入宏观政策取向一致性评估，可以实现资源优化配置和政策目标互补，避免政策目标相互抵消或矛盾冲突带来的“合成谬误”，保障经济社会协调发展。

glossary.explanation: An official goal, prominent since the 19th Party Congress (2017), of shifting from speed-driven growth to growth emphasising quality, efficiency and sustainability.
An annual meeting of top Party and state leaders, usually held in December, that reviews the year's economy and sets the next year's economic priorities.

glossary.zh: 宏观政策取向一致性评估
glossary.explanation: A review mechanism intended to check that economic and non-economic policies point in the same direction and do not work against one another. The Central Economic Work Conference stressed it at the end of 2024.

t: Adhering to a problem-oriented approach and coordinating integrated reform of the education, science and technology, and talent systems and mechanisms
zh: 坚持问题导向，统筹推进教育科技人才体制机制一体改革
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2025, asks how the integrated reform of the education, science and technology, and talent systems and mechanisms should be advanced. Sun Xiaolei argues that it is a global, holistic and forward-looking strategic arrangement, and the practical path for implementing the strategies of invigorating China through science and education, strengthening the country through talent, and innovation-driven development. Sun holds that it must rest on three principles: a problem-oriented approach, a people-centred stance and systems thinking.
The piece is organised in three sections, one for each principle. The first deals with identifying the main line of reform, the second with its direction, and the third with how it is carried out.

Under the first principle, Sun argues that closer links between research and application, shorter conversion cycles and industries built on innovation make traditional mechanisms ill-suited to high-quality development. Sun calls for breakthroughs in management and service, resource allocation, talent evaluation and income distribution, including distribution by contribution of factors such as knowledge, technology and data. Under the second, Sun says reform must serve the all-round development of the person, with high-calibre talent as its core. Under the third, Sun calls for foresight, overall planning and holistic implementation, citing a remaining gap with developed countries in key technologies and global top talent.

Sun concludes that reform should move from local experiments to systems integration, supported by Party leadership, national coordination mechanisms, supporting legislation, and assessment and accountability. Read the original if you want a short example of how Party-affiliated academics present this reform agenda in official language.
quoteEn: To discuss reform without the people, or to pursue reform divorced from people's livelihood, would be like water without a source or a tree without roots, and would struggle to build popular consensus and common strength.
quoteZh: 抛开人民谈改革、脱离民生搞改革，那便是无源之水、无本之木，难以形成群体共识和普遍合力。

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: An official principle holding that development and reform should serve the people's interests and rely on them. It is prominent in Xi Jinping-era discourse.
An official economic goal, stressed since 2017, that favours innovation and efficiency over growth driven by investment and input expansion.

glossary.en: invigorating China through science and education
glossary.literal: strategy of rejuvenating the country through science and education
glossary.explanation: A national strategy adopted in 1995 that makes science, technology and education the basis of national development.

t: The "AI Plus" initiative and the cultivation of future industries
zh: “人工智能+”行动引领未来产业培育
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in January 2025, Jiao Hao asks how the "AI Plus" initiative can lead the cultivation of future industries. The initiative was announced at the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference. Jiao argues that, by integrating AI with sector-specific knowledge and technical resources, it speeds up technological breakthroughs and helps identify and nurture high-potential future industries.

The commentary takes the six future-industry fields named in the official implementation opinions: future manufacturing, information, materials, energy, space and health. It then examines four channels through which the initiative works: building a technological base, reshaping business models, empowering industrial and supply chains, and promoting a digital innovation ecosystem. Each channel is illustrated with examples such as quantum information, humanoid robots, brain-computer interfaces, the metaverse, biomanufacturing and new energy storage.

Jiao holds that AI supplies core technologies (machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision) and, combined with other frontier technologies such as quantum computing, speeds up iteration. In business models, the author describes a shift towards platform-based operation, precise response to individual user needs, and a logic of integrating the digital and the real economy. For supply chains, AI is said to make them more open, predictable and traceable and to deepen human–machine collaboration. In the innovation ecosystem, AI helps stakeholders (firms, laboratories, universities, government) predict technology trajectories and combine innovation factors. It also supports innovation consortia in the Yangtze River Delta biomedical sector and lets the public help correct industries that stray from a proper path.

Jiao notes that future industries are still at a gestation stage and lack mature risk-identification and regulatory systems. The author calls for risk assessment systems for AI applications, a review system for technology ethics, and faster AI legislation, so that innovation and social and economic benefits interact well and future industries move towards high-quality development. Read the original if you want a short, example-led official-style account of how AI policy is linked to future-industry planning in China.
quoteEn: The "AI Plus" initiative is a bridge linking the digital world and the real economy; it breaks the traditional value-chain structure and drives innovation in the modes of capturing, delivering and creating value.
quoteZh: “人工智能+”行动是连接数字世界和实体经济的桥梁，打破了传统的价值链结构，推动价值获取、传递和创造的模式创新

glossary.explanation: A policy initiative put forward at the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference to integrate AI into all sectors of the economy. It follows the earlier "Internet Plus" model.
Emerging industries based on frontier technologies that are still at an early stage. Official documents list six fields: manufacturing, information, materials, energy, space and health.
An official economic goal that stresses innovation, efficiency and sustainability over speed of growth alone.
An annual meeting of Party and state leaders, held at the end of the year, that sets economic policy priorities for the next year.

t: Three relationships to get right in building a high-standard socialist market economy
zh: 构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制需要把握好几个关系
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2025, asks how the goal of a high-standard socialist market economy should be pursued. Li Chungen takes as his starting point the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called such a system an important safeguard of Chinese modernization and set the aim of building it fully by 2035. Li argues that the task depends on handling three pairs of relationships correctly: government and market, top-level design and practical exploration, and high-quality development and high-standard security.

The piece is organised in three numbered sections, one for each relationship, after a short introduction. It places the 2024 Plenum decision in the line of the 14th Five-Year Plan and the 20th Party Congress (2022) report, and cites Xi Jinping on the establishment of a socialist market economy as a major theoretical and practical innovation of the Party. Li then turns to the current stage of reform, which he describes as a period of tackling hard problems in uncharted territory.

On government and market, Li holds that the market's decisive role in resource allocation is a general law of market economies, but that unrestrained markets produce insufficient demand, unfair distribution and widening gaps. Government must therefore regulate, correct market failures and protect fair competition, while avoiding excessive intervention and fixing clear boundaries between the two so that the combined effect exceeds the sum of its parts. On top-level design and exploration, Li calls for upholding the Party's overall leadership, reforming state-owned enterprises, directing capital to emerging industries and developing new quality productive forces, while respecting popular initiative, opening more to private firms and following a sequence of experiment, summing up and then wider rollout. On development and security, Li treats them as two wheels of one cart, calling for a unified national market, the Two Unwaverings, equal property protection, compliance, risk prevention and curbs on local protectionism and involutionary competition.

Li concludes that integrating these relationships will lay a solid foundation for a modern socialist country by the middle of the century. Li's proposals are framed as tasks for the reform period ahead rather than as an assessment of past results. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of how the 2024 Plenum's market-economy reform agenda is explained to a general Chinese readership.
quoteEn: Only by reasonably defining the boundary of responsibility between government and market, and reasonably dividing their respective duties, and by giving full play to the strengths of each, can a "1+1>2" effect be achieved.
quoteZh: 只有合理界定政府与市场的责任边界、合理划分二者的职责范围，充分发挥政府和市场各自的优势和长处，才能达到“1+1＞2”的效果。

glossary.zh: 高水平社会主义市场经济体制
glossary.pinyin: gāo shuǐpíng shèhuì zhǔyì shìchǎng jīngjì tǐzhì
glossary.explanation: A goal set in the 14th Five-Year Plan and the 20th Party Congress report and elaborated at the 2024 Third Plenum, which aims to complete it by 2035. It refers to a more complete system of market-based institutions under Party leadership.
The official term for China's path of modernization, set out by Xi Jinping and the Party from the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological innovation, advanced industries such as AI and big data, and higher productivity.
The official guiding aim for the economy since 2017, shifting emphasis from speed of growth to innovation, coordination, green, open and shared development.
The Party's formula of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.

t: Cultivating new quality productive forces and shaping new drivers and new advantages
zh: 培育新质生产力 塑造新动能新优势
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily in January 2025, asks how new quality productive forces can be cultivated so as to generate new drivers and advantages of growth. Shao and Zhang argue that, in the age of the internet and what they call intelligent interconnection, high-quality development requires productive forces marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality.

The article is organised around four sources of a 'leap' in productive forces: breakthrough technological innovation, structural industrial upgrading, open business-model innovation, and a well-developed supply of institutions. It illustrates the middle two with examples from Changle district in Fuzhou, Fujian, and a national modern agriculture park in Yongqiao district, Suzhou, Anhui.

On technology, the authors hold that intelligent interconnection breaks down technical barriers, links innovation resources and spreads into production networks, so digital technology should be used to integrate resources and promote cross-sector innovation. On industry, they cite nearly a thousand lace factories in Changle that used digital technology from design to delivery, and call for linking upstream and downstream firms and lengthening the industrial chain. On models, they point to 5G, internet-of-things and AI applications in agriculture, and urge shared-economy, customised and flexible management models that suit new relations of production.

On institutions, Shao and Zhang call for upholding the Party's overall leadership over productive-force development, local policies adapted to local conditions, and rules that bring relations of production into line with new quality productive forces and raise total factor productivity. They conclude that deeper reform in key areas will provide the institutional guarantee for the leap. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Chinese academic commentary links digital technology, industrial policy and Party leadership under the new quality productive forces framework.
quoteEn: Intelligent interconnection breaks down 'information silos' and, through an open, shared and collaborative industrial ecosystem, achieves value linkages between industries and promotes the transformation and upgrading of traditional industries.
quoteZh: 智能互联打破“信息孤岛”，以开放、共享、协同的产业生态系统，实现产业间价值联动，促进传统产业转型升级。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023 for advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, innovative factor allocation and industrial upgrading, in place of growth reliant on traditional methods.
The official goal, stressed since the 19th Party Congress (2017), of shifting from rapid growth to growth that is efficient, innovative and sustainable.
A Marxist category for the social relations, especially of ownership, within which production takes place. Chinese policy texts call for adjusting them to fit new productive forces.

t: Using economic system reform as the lead in further deepening reform comprehensively
zh: 经济体制改革为牵引进一步全面深化改革
paras: This article, published in the Party journal Red Flag Manuscripts in late 2024, explains why economic system reform should "lead" the further comprehensive deepening of reform set out by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Jiang Chuanhai argues that deepening economic reform remains the focus of reform as a whole and that it drives and conditions reform in other fields. The piece is an interpretive commentary on Xi Jinping's statements at the study seminar for provincial and ministerial leaders on the Plenum.

The article has three parts. The first sets out why the lead role matters; the second lists four "inherent requirements" for carrying it out; the third sets out concrete tasks for economic reform. These tasks are the mechanisms for high-quality development, new drivers and advantages of development, the Two Unwaverings, a unified national market, and the basic institutions of the market economy.

Jiang's reasoning begins from the Marxist premise that the economic base determines the superstructure. On this view the pace of major economic reforms sets the pace of many others, so economic reform is the "ox's nose" that moves the whole. The author gives three grounds: the internal logic of comprehensive reform, the need for high-quality development, and the modernization of the system and capacity of national governance. Jiang says the market system is still incomplete and that government–market relations are not fully settled. The four requirements are to be both "lively" and "well-regulated" in handling government and market; to combine key breakthroughs with systematic planning; to build up (li) and break down (po) together, building first; and to rely on national conditions while drawing on the best of other civilizations.

On tasks, Jiang calls for institutions favouring innovation, coordinated regional development, green development, opening up and shared development. The article also urges building production relations suited to new quality productive forces, together with deeper integration of the real and digital economies. It calls for consolidating public ownership while supporting the non-public sector, removing local protectionism to form a unified national market, and strengthening property protection, fair competition, anti-monopoly enforcement and the social credit system. Jiang concludes that this approach reflects the Party's grasp of the laws of reform and that officials must act as implementers and doers. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary justifies the primacy of economic reform within the post-2024 reform agenda.
quoteEn: Grasping the \"ox's nose\" of economic system reform can powerfully help resolve deep-seated contradictions in other fields, creating conditions and providing momentum for comprehensively deepening reform.
quoteZh: 牵住经济体制改革这个“牛鼻子”，可以有力促进其他领域深层次矛盾的化解，为全面深化改革创造条件、提供动力。

glossary.explanation: A policy formula: unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector, and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2023, referring to advanced productivity driven by technological breakthroughs, new industries and innovative allocation of production factors.
Official term for a stage of economic development that stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth alone.
