t: The "great changes unseen in a century" from the perspective of long economic waves
zh: 经济长波视角下的“百年变局”
paras: Huang Wenyi and Hu Leming ask how the official judgement that the world is undergoing "great changes unseen in a century" can be understood in economic terms. Drawing on Xi Jinping's call to study economic conditions through long cycles, they argue that long-wave theory (Kondratieff cycles) gives an effective tool for locating the present moment and for reading the paradigm of global economic development. Their thesis is that the world is in a turbulent restructuring phase that will give way around 2030 to a new upswing, and that China is positioned to benefit if it responds correctly.

The article has three main parts. The first builds a framework of long waves and industrial revolutions, tracing three industrial revolutions from the 1760s to the present, each made up of two Kondratieff waves. The second examines trends in the current "techno-economic paradigm" in three areas: energy and technology, institutions and organisation, and the global economic order. The third considers China's opportunities and challenges and sets out a Chinese response, followed by a short conclusion.

The authors divide each industrial revolution into four stages (introduction, expansion, synergy, maturity), and place the present in the synergy stage of the third revolution and the downswing of the sixth Kondratieff wave, which began with the 2008 financial crisis. They expect a maturity stage and upswing from about 2030. In their reading, connectivity, renewable-energy and intelligent-manufacturing technologies will favour flatter, networked, cooperative organisation, while the "rise of the East and decline of the West" and the stronger weight of emerging economies reshape the global order. For China they see opportunities in multi-point technological breakthroughs and an institutional "soil" suited to the new revolution. They also see risks: Western pressure and technology controls, weak standard-setting, structural unemployment and a worsening external environment.

The authors propose three national strategies: a precisely implemented innovation-driven development strategy, modernisation of state governance and its capacity, and a new pattern of comprehensive opening up with active participation in global governance. They conclude that China is on the "right track" and prepared for the coming upswing, and that, if the first-step goal for 2035 is met, the second step of building a modern socialist country will fall within the upswing. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese economic journal uses long-wave theory to give the official "great changes" thesis an economic-historical basis and a policy agenda.
quoteEn: The "century" in "changes in a century" is more a general reference to time: it denotes the enormous historical shift, determined by the economic base, in the balance of power between Eastern and Western civilisations that is "under way" or "about to occur" across the long course of several past century-scale upheavals.
quoteZh: 所谓百年变局的“百年”更多是一种时间上的泛指，即在过去几个百年变局的漫长历史进程中，由经济基础所决定的东西方文明在力量对比上展现出来的“正在”或“即将”发生的巨大历史性变迁。

glossary.pinyin: bǎinián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.literal: great changes not seen in a hundred years
glossary.explanation: A formula used by Xi Jinping from around 2017–2018 to describe a shift in the global balance of power and order. Chinese scholarship debates its timing, features and implications.
A concept from Carlota Perez for the best-practice model through which a technological revolution is put to use. The article applies it to energy, technology, organisation and institutions.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernisation of state governance and its capacity
glossary.literal: modernisation of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal set out at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and elaborated in a 2019 Party decision. It covers improving institutions and their effective operation.
A national strategy that makes scientific and technological innovation the main engine of economic growth, promoted in Party documents since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

keywords: great changes unseen in a century

t: Coordinating high-quality development and high-standard protection
zh: 统筹推进高质量发展和高水平保护
paras: Wang Congxia takes up the first of five relationships that Xi Jinping named at the National Conference on Eco-environmental Protection: that between high-quality development and high-standard protection. The article argues that ecological protection and economic growth are not an either/or choice. In Wang's account, the two are mutually reinforcing and must be advanced together on the basis of the idea that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out how high-quality development and high-standard protection relate to each other. The second presents their joint pursuit as an inherent requirement of Chinese modernization, under three headings: harmony between humanity and nature, the logic of building ecological civilization, and the development of new quality productive forces. The third turns to practical measures, drawing on the July 2024 Third Plenum Decision on further deepening reform.

On the relationship itself, Wang argues that high-quality development is the precondition of protection because it supplies the financial, technological and market support for it. High-standard protection, in turn, underpins development: it sets bottom lines through eco-environmental zoning and spatial planning, drives industrial and energy restructuring, and supplies ecological products. Wang quotes Xi's view that protecting the environment is protecting productive forces, and that green development is the 'underlying colour' of high-quality development. On this basis the article presents Western modernization, with its 'pollute first, clean up later' path, as the contrast to a Chinese modernization of harmony between humanity and nature.

For policy, Wang calls for three things. The first is to establish the new development philosophy firmly and plan modernization with foresight, at the level of the whole and at the strategic level. The second is to shift the development model towards green and low-carbon forms, through a protection system, a governance system based on source prevention and precise pollution control, and a system of market incentives and technology. The third is to build a green, low-carbon, circular economy by greening industry, converting green technologies into products, and encouraging green lifestyles. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated writing presents ecological policy as part of Chinese modernization and new quality productive forces after the 2024 Third Plenum.
quoteEn: High-quality development is the precondition of high-standard protection, and high-standard protection is an important support for high-quality development, able to raise its quality.
quoteZh: 高质量发展是高水平保护的前提，高水平保护是高质量发展的重要支撑，能够提升高质量发展的品质。

glossary.explanation: An official goal, prominent since 2017, of shifting from rapid quantitative growth to growth stressing quality, efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, described as distinct from Western models. It includes harmony between humanity and nature among its features.
A concept Xi Jinping introduced in 2023. It refers to productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, including green and digital technologies.
A framework announced in 2015 that calls for innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and verdant mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan Xi Jinping put forward in 2005. It holds that ecological protection and economic benefit are compatible, and it is a core idea of Xi's ecological thought.
A Party policy goal, written into the Party and state constitutions, of integrating environmental protection into economic, political and cultural development.

t: The foremost characteristic of a education powerhouse with Chinese characteristics: ideological and political guiding force
zh: 中国特色社会主义教育强国的首要特质
source: Research on Ideological Education (思想教育研究), 3 December 2024
paras: Li Hui takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the National Education Conference (9–10 September 2024), which listed six capacities that a socialist education powerhouse with Chinese characteristics should have and placed "ideological and political guiding force" (sizheng yinlingli) first. The article argues that this ordering is a new contribution both to Xi's discourse on education and to the theory and practice of ideological and political education. Its thesis is that this guiding force is what gives the education powerhouse its Chinese character.

The article has three parts. The first explains why the guiding force is the distinctive Chinese feature of an education powerhouse, tracing Xi's statements from 2014 to 2024. The second defines the guiding force and breaks it into components. The third sets out practical routes for strengthening it.

In the first part, Li follows Xi's remarks from the 2014 Peking University symposium through the 2016 and 2018 conferences to 2024. In Li's reading they move from "Chinese characteristics" to socialist universities with Chinese characteristics and then to an education powerhouse with Chinese characteristics. Li treats the guiding force as the same thing as the guiding power of socialist ideology, with university ideological work as a part of it. The second part says the force is made up of three elements: the guidance of Marxist thought, the value guidance of core socialist values, and the goal guidance of fostering virtue and cultivating talent (lide shuren). Li argues they produce a combined force only when they act in the same direction. The third part names four routes: goal, discipline, curriculum and evaluation. Li lists the Marxist theory research and construction project (launched 2004), the first-level discipline of Marxist theory (2005), and the pairing of ideological and political theory courses with "curriculum ideology and politics". Li also lists the 2020 Overall Plan for Deepening Education Evaluation Reform in the New Era, aimed at the "five onlys" (scores, further study, diplomas, papers, titles).

Li concludes that the guiding force expresses the Chinese character of the education powerhouse. Li adds that strengthening it in turn shows the superiority of socialism with Chinese characteristics in theory and institutions. Both rest on the basic task of education: whom to train, how to train them and for whom. Li says that how to improve the supporting systems and mechanisms, and how Marxist theory can lead other social science disciplines, still need study. Read the original if you want a concise account of how Party-line scholarship interprets the first of the "six capacities" in Xi's 2024 education speech and the policy instruments linked to it.
quoteEn: The ideological and political guiding force, on the one hand, embodies the Chinese characteristics of an education powerhouse, and on the other, strengthening it in turn demonstrates the superiority of the theory and institutions of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 思政引领力一方面体现了教育强国的中国特色，另一方面通过增强思政引领力反过来彰显中国特色社会主义的理论、制度的优越性。

glossary.explanation: The capacity of ideological and political education and work to steer teaching, management and services in schools. In Xi Jinping's 2024 list of six capacities for an education powerhouse it comes first.
A slogan, prominent in official policy since the 18th Party Congress (2012), naming moral education as the fundamental task of education.
A campaign against evaluating students and teachers solely by scores, further study, diplomas, papers and titles. It is a central aim of the 2020 education evaluation reform plan.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义理论研究和建设工程
glossary.pinyin: Mǎkèsī zhǔyì lǐlùn yánjiū hé jiànshè gōngchéng
glossary.en: Marxist theory research and construction project
glossary.explanation: A national project launched by the Party Central Committee in 2004 to compile standard textbooks and promote theoretical innovation in Marxism and the humanities and social sciences.

t: Cultural confidence and the logical dimensions of Chinese modernization
zh: 文化自信与中国式现代化的逻辑向度
paras: Liu Jianhua and Li Tingyan take up the relationship between cultural confidence and Chinese modernization, which they say scholars have not yet treated systematically. They argue that the two have developed together over a century of Party history and that each supplies something the other lacks. In their formula, cultural confidence gives Chinese modernization spiritual strength, while Chinese modernization gives cultural confidence modern strength.

The article has three parts. The first traces a historical logic in which cultural confidence moves through cultural awakening, independence, innovation and rejuvenation, while the path of modernization moves through choice, exploration, practice and definition. The second sets out how the two are theoretically embedded in each other. The third turns to practice, covering how cultural confidence supports modernization and how modernization shapes cultural confidence.

In the historical section, the authors run from the reformers and Sun Yat-sen after the Opium War, through the New Culture Movement, Mao Zedong's insistence on independence, the cultural theories of Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao, to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Their theoretical section argues that traditional culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture each feed Chinese modernization. Traditional ideas such as grand unification, common wealth and the unity of heaven and humanity are said to underpin its features: a huge population, common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature. In the other direction, the authors say modernization updates cultural confidence through digital media, wider horizons and a modern civilization of the Chinese nation. This, they write, moves cultural confidence towards civilizational confidence and a new form of human civilization.

On practice, the authors call for persistence on the path of socialist cultural development with Chinese characteristics and for the promotion of core socialist values. They also call for firm Party leadership in ideological work, a people-first cultural outlook, and cultural exchange and mutual learning that keeps cultural independence. They further propose using technology to bring cultural resources into everyday life. They conclude that the Party's pursuit of modernization reflects deep cultural self-awareness and a commitment to a modernization with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a compact example of how current Chinese scholarship links cultural confidence, Party history and Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Cultural confidence gives Chinese modernization spiritual strength, and Chinese modernization gives cultural confidence modern strength, helping cultural confidence achieve innovative development.
quoteZh: 文化自信赋予中国式现代化以精神力量，中国式现代化赋予文化自信以现代力量，助力文化自信实现创新性发展。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path to modernization under Communist Party leadership, promoted since the 20th Party Congress (2022). Official texts present it as distinct from Western models.
Confidence in the value and vitality of China's own culture. Official discourse treats it as a basis for the other 'confidences' in the Four-sphere Confidence.
The official goal of prosperity shared by all the people. Official texts treat it as a defining feature of Chinese modernization.
A set of official values promoted since the 18th Party Congress. They are presented as the core of the ideological and cultural order.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping used in 2021 for the civilizational form that Chinese modernization is said to create, in contrast to Western modernization.

t: Understanding and following the laws of building socialist culture with Chinese characteristics
zh: 论对中国特色社会主义文化建设规律的认识与遵循
paras: Jiang Yingchun reads the cultural provisions of the Decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) as a deepening of the Party's understanding of the laws governing cultural work. The article asks what these laws are and what they demand in practice. Its answer is that Marxist guidance, a holistic view of socialist culture and the strengthening of national cultural soft power are the three core requirements, and that together they enrich Xi Jinping's thought on culture.

The article has three main parts. The first deals with Marxist guidance: the system of Marxism's guiding position in the ideological field, resistance to liberalism, and mastery of Marxist theory. The second treats socialist culture with Chinese characteristics as an organic whole of fine traditional Chinese culture, revolutionary culture and advanced socialist culture, and sets out the continuity, contemporaneity and global dimension of cultural development. The third concerns soft power: culture's social functions, institutional culture, a culture of "peaceful development", and the cultural industries. A short conclusion follows.

Jiang argues that Marxism is the soul and the defining mark of socialist culture, and that without it culture would lose direction. Liberalism is presented as the most persistent and widespread challenge, backed by the political and economic systems of capitalist states. Jiang draws on Deng Xiaoping's criticism of abstract humanism and of the theory of alienation under socialism, and on Althusser's warning, to link such tendencies to the Soviet collapse. Traditional culture must be transformed creatively, with no cultural restorationism, and revolutionary culture must be defended against historical nihilism that rejects revolution in favour of reform. Culture is also said to act back on the economic base, so historical materialism is not economic determinism. In the soft-power section Jiang calls for communicating China's institutional culture, above all whole-process people's democracy, against Western "constitutional democracy", and for countering what the article calls Western cultural hegemony with a culture of peaceful development linked to a community with a shared future for mankind.

Jiang concludes that culture's role in national rejuvenation is prominent but that problems remain: the Party's leadership and discourse power in culture have weakened in some respects, Marxism is still marginalised in some fields, and the international reach of Chinese cultural products is weak. Citing Lenin, Jiang says cultural tasks need long, persistent effort. The article calls for implementing Xi Jinping's thought on culture to build cultural strength for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned reading of the Third Plenum's cultural agenda, including its ideological argument against liberalism and historical nihilism.
quoteEn: Adherence to Marxism as the guiding ideology is the fundamental mark that distinguishes socialist culture with Chinese characteristics from other cultures.
quoteZh: 坚持以马克思主义为指导，是中国特色社会主义文化区别于其他文化的根本标志。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation of China's development path, stressed since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is said to include the coordinated development of material and cultural-ethical civilization.
Borrowed from Joseph Nye's concept of soft power. In Party discourse it refers to the attractiveness and international influence of Chinese culture and values.
The official term for China's democratic model, put forward by Xi Jinping in 2019. It stresses people's participation in all stages of political life, not only elections.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, promoted since 2013, calling for cooperation and shared development in international relations.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views that are seen as negating the Party's revolutionary history and socialist achievements.

t: Improving people's quality of life in building Chinese modernization: inherent requirements and practical dimensions
zh: 在中国式现代化建设中提高人民生活品质：内在要求与实践向度
paras: Ding Yuanzhu takes up the phrase "improving people's quality of life" (生活品质), which the report to the 20th Party Congress (2022) placed alongside "promoting the people's wellbeing". The article asks what the concept means and why it is an inherent requirement of Chinese modernization. Ding argues that the Congress's stress on common prosperity, the coordination of material and cultural-ethical advancement, and harmony between humanity and nature all converge in quality of life, and that grasping the concept deepens understanding of what Chinese modernization requires.

The article is organised in three parts. The first defines quality of life as a composite of economic, social, cultural and spiritual elements, with objective and subjective sides, individual and group levels, and a link to all-round human development. The second discusses how to combine objective measurement with subjective evaluation, including happiness as an indicator. The third turns to practical priorities in the new development stage: social resilience, quality employment, incomes and consumption. Ding draws on Amartya Sen, W. W. Rostow, the Finnish sociologist Erik Allardt, and Japanese experience with weak consumption.

In Ding's reading, the Congress's pairing of the "all-round enrichment of material things" with "all-round human development" continues Marxist theory, which Ding divides into three levels: bodily and mental development, the capacity for activity, and free development, including free time and free choice of occupation. Citing Rostow's later addition of a stage of \"pursuing quality of life\", Ding presents the concept as a natural product of economic maturity. Ding adds that wealth growth does not automatically raise wellbeing, so a government representing society as a whole should look beyond individual satisfaction and the market. This is said to explain why Chinese modernization must follow the five-sphere integrated plan.

On practice, Ding calls for strengthening resilience to epidemics, ageing, digital change and climate; the employment-first strategy, with attention to the effects of artificial intelligence, education reform and young people, including avoiding \"involution\"; and rising incomes, better distribution and stronger consumption. Ding concludes that the Party's five major principles from the 20th Congress show the way to raising quality of life. Read the original if you want a Chinese policy scholar's account of how \"quality of life\" is being conceptualised within Party discourse on people's wellbeing.
quoteEn: At the individual level, quality of life mainly includes income, physical health, family relations, neighbourly relations, work situation, recreation and leisure, and so on.
quoteZh: 个人层面的生活品质，主要包括经济收入、身体健康、家庭关系、邻居关系、工作状况、娱乐休闲，等等。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for China's path to modernization, set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It lists five features, including a huge population, common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, not only some. Under Xi Jinping it is presented as a defining requirement of socialism.

t: Reform requires a "nationwide chessboard" mindset
st: People's Daily "Thought and Perspective" commentary, 6 January 2025
zh: 改革要树立全国一盘棋思想（思想纵横）
paras: This short commentary in the People's Daily takes up a directive from Xi Jinping at the second plenary session of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): all regions and departments should adopt a "nationwide chessboard" mindset when carrying out reform. Wang Yunsong argues that further comprehensively deepening reform cannot be confined to one's own "plot of land" and must be planned within the overall interests of the Party and the country.

The piece moves in four steps. It first grounds the principle in the Marxist dialectic of whole and part, then points to practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012), then presents the principle as a method of thinking and working, and finally addresses how local conditions fit within it.

Wang argues that the whole governs the parts and the parts serve the whole, citing Mao Zedong's 1936 remark that grasping the overall situation makes it easier to use its parts. Because reform is large in scale, wide in scope and touches deep interests, the author says it needs coordination to avoid going it alone or each acting separately. As an example, Wang cites the building of a unified national market, which is said to have removed local protectionism and market segmentation. Leading cadres, in Wang's account, should calculate "big accounts", reject watered-down implementation, and coordinate across departments and regions, especially in education, healthcare, elderly care and housing.

Wang concludes that the principle does not ignore local realities. Regions should locate their role in national strategy and develop distinctive strengths and comparative advantages, so that reform proceeds steadily. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary links Marxist dialectics, Xi Jinping's directives and the practical coordination of reform.
quoteEn: Establishing a nationwide-chessboard mindset reflects a deeper grasp of the Marxist dialectical relationship between whole and part.
quoteZh: 树立全国一盘棋思想，是对马克思主义关于整体与部分的辩证关系的深入把握。

glossary.literal: the whole country as one game of chess
glossary.explanation: A long-standing Chinese political expression meaning that all regions and departments should act in coordination under central planning and the overall national interest.
The reform agenda adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee in July 2024, which set out a broad package of reform measures through 2029 and beyond.
A policy goal of removing local protectionism and administrative barriers so that goods, capital and other factors flow freely across China.

glossary.literal: what is of greatest importance to the country
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping urging officials to keep the country's most important interests in view; the commentary invokes it alongside the idea of calculating "big accounts" rather than "small accounts".

t: The key to building a modern socialist country in all respects lies in the Communist Party of China
st: An important perspective for understanding the spirit of the 20th Party Congress
zh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家关键在中国共产党
zhSub: 理解中共二十大精神的一个重要视角
paras: This text is an edited version of Zhang Hefu's remarks at the Red Hall Forum seminar on understanding the 20th Party Congress (2022). Zhang takes up Xi Jinping's statement in the congress report that building a modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation 'depend on the Party'. Zhang presents this as a key to the congress's spirit and reads it in three ways.

The remarks are short and organised around those three points: the achievements of the previous decade, the pursuit of the modernization goals, and the need for a strong Party built through strict self-governance. Zhang then lists the seven arrangements the congress report makes for Party building.

On the first point, Zhang attributes the decade's achievements, including the poverty-alleviation campaign and the building of a moderately prosperous society, to the Party's leadership, to Xi Jinping as the 'core', and to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. On the second, Zhang argues that Chinese modernization is by definition modernization led by the Party. In this account the Party has no special interests of its own and represents no interest group, which is why it can rally the people. Third, Zhang summarises the report's seven tasks: centralised leadership, theoretical study, institutional rules for the Party's self-reform, a capable cadre corps, stronger Party organisations, stricter discipline and conduct, and a long-term anti-corruption struggle.

Zhang concludes that these arrangements respond to problems within the Party and are essential if it is to keep its vanguard character, purity and governing capacity while leading modernization. Read the original if you want a brief official-affiliated summary of how the 20th Party Congress's emphasis on Party leadership is explained.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party of China.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化，是中国共产党领导的社会主义现代化

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's path of modernization, set out prominently at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as led by the Party and distinct from Western models.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017.
An official concept that the Party must continually correct itself and remove its own problems without external pressure.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central official national goal, associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream and linked to the second centenary goal of 2049.

t: Solidly advancing common prosperity through integrated urban–rural development
zh: 在城乡融合发展中扎实推进共同富裕
paras: This commentary in Guangming Daily asks how integrated urban–rural development can serve the goal of common prosperity. Zheng Huixia starts from the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which lists improving the institutions and mechanisms for urban–rural integration as a major reform task and calls it a necessary requirement of Chinese modernization. Zheng argues that this gives direction and a path for realising common prosperity.

The article is organised around five dimensions of integration: space, industry, factors of production, ecology and institutions. Each section is presented as a way of building a particular aspect of common prosperity, and each lists practical measures. Zheng treats the ideal urban–rural relationship as one of equal status, mutual dependence, complementary functions and mutual promotion.

On spatial integration, Zheng calls for unified multi-plan urban–rural planning, better rural infrastructure including 5G and gigabit fibre networks, and a new type of urbanisation centred on county towns. On industry, the author proposes that cities specialise in technology- and capital-intensive sectors while the countryside develops specialised agriculture, deep processing and rural tourism, with science and technology, e-commerce and fiscal, tax and financial policy as supports. On factors of production, Zheng urges freer two-way flows of land, talent, capital and technology, including orderly transfer of land management rights and a technology-information sharing platform.

The last two sections cover ecology and institutions. Zheng proposes green development, ecological compensation, green finance and wider public environmental participation. Institutional integration would mean household registration reform, reform of rural homestead and collective construction land, a further 30-year extension of land contracts in pilot areas, greater fiscal support for agriculture, rural areas and farmers, and equalised basic public services in education, health care, culture and community governance. Zheng concludes that these combined measures would build an equitable, inclusive and sustainable urban–rural system and generate the joint force needed for common prosperity. Read the original if you want a compact, policy-oriented overview of how official discourse links urban–rural integration to common prosperity after the 2024 plenum.
quoteEn: Urban–rural industrial integration requires building on the respective strengths of city and countryside and promoting complementarity and mutual reinforcement between their industries; this is the material foundation for seeking common prosperity for both.
quoteZh: 城乡产业融合要求立足城乡各自优势，推动城乡产业互补互促，这是谋求城乡共同富裕的物质基础。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal of shared wealth, given renewed policy emphasis under Xi Jinping. It is presented officially as a defining feature of Chinese modernization.
The official name for China's path to modernization, set out by Xi Jinping and the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is described as distinct from Western models.
A policy aim of removing the divide between city and countryside through two-way flows of people, resources and services. It builds on earlier 'urban–rural integrated development' (城乡一体化) language.

The hukou system ties access to public services to a person's registered place of residence and has long separated rural from urban status. Reform aims to let migrants settle in cities with equal services.
Shorthand for agriculture, the countryside and farmers, treated as a priority area of Party policy.

t: Improving the basic institutions of ecological civilization and strengthening the eco-environmental governance system
zh: 完善生态文明基础体制 健全生态环境治理体系
paras: This short commentary, first published in Jiefang Daily, responds to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). The plenum described Chinese modernization as modernization in harmony between humanity and nature and called for speeding up the institutions that put into practice the idea that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets. Wang argues that doing so means improving the basic institutions of ecological civilization and the eco-environmental governance system, not merely adding green space.

The piece has two parts. The first deals with national institutional design around the "three lines and one list". The second applies the regional-governance logic to the Yangtze River Delta, with concrete proposals for cooperation zones.

Wang presents the "three lines and one list" (ecological protection red lines, environmental quality bottom lines, resource utilisation ceilings and a negative list for environmental access) as a foundational tool. It should integrate ecological protection, environmental management, spatial planning and environmental assessment. It should also build spatial controls on environmental management units and set differentiated entry requirements. For the Yangtze River Delta, Wang calls for joint construction, governance and sharing of the environment. Proposals include demonstration zones around the Yangtze estuary and Hangzhou Bay, a Shanghai–Xuancheng–Huangshan carbon-trading cooperation zone, and a cross-regional compensation scheme for freshwater supply along the Taipu River and surrounding areas. Wang also proposes shared urban parks with equal access across cities.

Wang concludes that systematic, differentiated and precise environmental management, backed by ecological compensation and cross-boundary cooperation, can ease the structural pressures that still weigh on environmental protection. The commentary suggests that the delta can serve as a model of regional coordination. Read the original if you want concrete, place-specific policy proposals for Yangtze River Delta ecological cooperation, set within the 2024 plenum's language on ecological civilization.
quoteEn: Under the new circumstances, speeding up institutions that put into practice the idea that lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets is not limited to enlarging the area of flowers and grass; it also requires improving the basic institutions of ecological civilization and strengthening the eco-environmental governance system.
quoteZh: 新形势下，加快完善落实绿水青山就是金山银山理念的体制机制，不仅限于增加“繁花绿草”面积，而且要注重完善生态文明基础体制、健全生态环境治理体系

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's development path, set out since 2021 and stressed at the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is defined by features such as common prosperity and harmony between humanity and nature.

glossary.zh: 绿水青山就是金山银山
glossary.en: lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets
glossary.literal: green waters and green mountains are mountains of gold and silver
glossary.explanation: A slogan associated with Xi Jinping from 2005, holding that environmental protection and economic development are mutually reinforcing. It is a core idea of official ecological civilization policy.
An official goal of Chinese development, written into Party and state documents since the 2000s. It seeks to integrate environmental protection into economic, political and social development.

A zoning-based environmental management framework made up of ecological protection red lines, environmental quality bottom lines, resource utilisation ceilings and an environmental access negative list. Localities are directed to build it.
The economically developed region around Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Anhui, treated in national policy as a priority area for integrated development.

t: Empowering gains in production quality and efficiency with the new development philosophy
zh: 以新发展理念赋能生产质效提升
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily asks how the new development philosophy should guide the formation of new quality productive forces and high-quality development. Shen argues that innovative practice needs guiding ideas as well as material conditions, so the new development philosophy must run through any understanding of how the two are related.

The piece first sets out the theoretical link between the philosophy and new quality productive forces. It then offers three practical requirements: breakthroughs in core technologies, steady progress, and region-specific development.

Shen contends that scientific theory is an important condition for productive forces to develop. Under capitalism, in the author's account, production stays disorderly and spontaneous, whereas only socialism can produce theory serving large-scale socialised production and people's all-round development. New quality productive forces are presented as advanced productive forces that conform to the new development philosophy. They are said to arise from technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and industrial upgrading, not from a mere partial optimisation of traditional productive forces. Shen treats their formation as confirming the philosophy's scientific validity.

On practice, Shen calls for winning the battle over key core technologies, since innovation is the first necessary condition. The author also calls for maintaining stability while seeking progress, protecting industrial and supply-chain security, and avoiding bubbles and neglect of traditional industries. Finally, regions should act according to local conditions, with Beijing supporting other regions through its role as an international science and technology innovation centre. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-school commentary links new quality productive forces to the new development philosophy.
quoteEn: New quality productive forces are an advanced form of productive forces that accords with the new development philosophy.
quoteZh: 新质生产力是符合新发展理念的先进生产力质态。

glossary.explanation: A concept associated with Xi Jinping from 2023, describing advanced productive forces driven by technological breakthroughs, new factor allocation and industrial upgrading.
A Party framework put forward in 2015 comprising innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, intended to guide economic development.
An official goal that shifts emphasis from fast growth to quality, efficiency and sustainability in the economy.

t: A global source of AI innovation: Shanghai's path to empowering the building of a cyber power
zh: 全球AI创新策源地 赋能网络强国建设的上海路径
paras: Writing in Jiefang Daily on 30 December 2024, Song Haitao, who heads the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Research Institute, presents the institute as a model of how artificial intelligence can serve the building of a cyber power (wangluo qiangguo). Song argues that AI is central to breaking technological blockades and strengthening network security. The institute, jointly established by the Shanghai municipality and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, is described as the first municipal-level new-type R&D body in AI.

The piece is organised under three headings: consolidating the core technology base, cultivating an innovation ecosystem, and strengthening the talent pillar. It reports the institute's research areas, including humanoid robots, virtual power plants, DNA storage and AIGC network governance. It also covers its start-up incubation record, its partnerships with companies such as Huawei and SenseTime, and its international links.

Song's central claim is that the institute links the talent chain, innovation chain and industrial chain, so that universities and firms reinforce each other. As evidence, the article cites a 2024 World Internet Conference award for a social-governance visual-understanding project and more than 20 incubated firms. Of these firms, 70% have received fund backing and 15% are unicorns or near-unicorns, with a combined valuation above 200 billion yuan. Song also points to a UNIDO global AI centre of excellence hosted by the institute, to an AI-focused MBA, and to cooperation with universities abroad.

Song concludes that new quality productive forces are taking shape at the institute through the integration of frontier AI, computing power and network infrastructure. The article presents this as a distinctive Shanghai path for AI-enabled cyber power building. Read the original if you want an institutional insider's account of how a Chinese AI research body describes its role in national technology policy.
quoteEn: The institute positions itself precisely as a key hub for turning technological results into practice, deeply integrating the talent, innovation and industrial chains to build a full-chain, high-efficiency industrial ecosystem.
quoteZh: 研究院精准定位为技术成果转化的关键枢纽，深度融合人才链、创新链与产业链，匠心打造全链条、高效能的产业生态。

glossary.explanation: A strategic goal promoted under Xi Jinping since 2014 to make China strong in internet technology, cybersecurity and the digital economy.
A concept introduced by Xi Jinping in 2023 for growth driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, particularly in advanced technology sectors.

t: Viewing the world through the distinctive worldview embedded in Chinese modernization
zh: 以中国式现代化蕴含的独特世界观看天下
paras: Tian Pengying, writing at the end of 2024, asks how Chinese modernization can answer what the author calls the "questions of world modernization". These include polarisation versus common prosperity, zero-sum games versus win-win cooperation, and copying foreign models versus independent development. Tian argues that the distinctive worldview embedded in Chinese modernization offers a methodological option for developing countries and an innovation in modernization theory and practice.

The short commentary draws on a major National Social Science Fund project on the worldview contained in Chinese modernization. It looks at that worldview through three relationships: China and the world, China and the South, and China and a new form of human civilisation. It opens by describing a world of intertwined crises, a widening development gap and environmental deterioration.

Tian contends that this worldview combines the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation with concern for all humanity, and treats building a community with a shared future for mankind as an essential requirement of Chinese modernization. Tian describes China as a natural member of the Global South, supporting other developing countries in choosing their own paths and helping latecomers avoid the "paradox of modernization" and the "afflictions of modernity". On civilisation, Tian says the twenty-first century has three basic blocs: Chinese, Western and developing-country modernization. The author holds that Chinese modernization dissolves the discursive hegemony of Western modernization and breaks the equation of modernization with Westernization.

Tian concludes that Chinese modernization widens the paths open to developing countries and offers a Chinese approach to protecting and passing on human civilisation. Read the original if you want a brief statement of how a Chinese scholar leading a national research project frames the worldview of Chinese modernization in relation to the world, the Global South and civilisation.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has broken the myth that "modernization equals Westernization", shown another picture of modernization, and widened the paths open to developing countries on the road to modernization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化，打破了“现代化=西方化”的迷思，展现了现代化的另一幅图景，拓展了发展中国家走向现代化的路径选择

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation for China's own path of modernization, prominent since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
A term for developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Chinese official discourse describes China as a member of this group.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept associated with Xi Jinping since 2012–13. It calls for shared responsibility and cooperation among states on common global problems.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in official Party discourse, referring to restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

glossary.en: a new form of human civilisation
glossary.explanation: An official phrase, used since 2021, describing Chinese modernization as an alternative to the Western model of modernity.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: From digital "fission" to global "symbiosis": a new philosophical situation and economic outlook in cyberspace
zh: 从数字“裂变”到全球“共生”：网络空间下的哲学新局与经济展望
paras: This short commentary, published on Guangming Online in late 2024, asks how rapid digital technological change and the difficulties of global digital governance can be reconciled. Gao Ying argues that the rapid "fission" of digital technology makes a global "symbiosis" urgent, and that building a community with a shared future in cyberspace is the way to balance the international digital order and protect fairness and justice.

The piece has three parts. It first surveys advances in artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain, 5G and edge computing and their effect on industry. It then turns to the idea of a community with a shared future in cyberspace, citing Xi Jinping's statements, the 2024 World Internet Conference in Wuzhen and China's assistance to African countries. A final part offers a dialectical reading and an economic outlook.

Gao describes the world's cyberspace as marked by cyberattacks, data leaks and what the author calls hegemonic states wielding a "digital big stick", while less developed regions face a digital divide. The community concept, in the author's account, rests on equality, mutual trust and win-win cooperation, and promises multilateral rule-making, resource sharing and joint security. Gao also reads the relationship between technology and governance through the Marxist principle that productive forces determine relations of production: digital productive forces call for new governance rules and new international relations.

For the economy, Gao calls for more basic research, closer ties between universities and enterprises, work on \"chokepoint\" technologies, and the export of digital payment, e-commerce, 5G and cloud technologies through the Belt and Road Initiative. The author concludes that countries can develop sustainably only through joint consultation and mutual learning. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official discourse links digital technology, Marxist theory and the cyberspace community idea.
quoteEn: The "fission" of digital technological innovation is a direct manifestation of a leap in productive forces, and follows the principle that productive forces determine relations of production.
quoteZh: 数字技术创新的“裂变”是生产力飞跃的直观体现，遵循生产力决定生产关系原理

glossary.en: a community with a shared future in cyberspace
glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping since the mid-2010s, extending the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind to internet governance. It stresses cyber sovereignty, multilateral rule-making and shared security.
A Chinese international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013. It includes a digital dimension such as e-commerce and network infrastructure.
The gap between those with and without access to digital technology and skills. The article applies it mainly to less developed countries.

t: How new quality productive forces grow in practice
zh: 新质生产力，如何在实践中成长
paras: In this commentary in the People's Daily, Wang Yiming asks what new quality productive forces are, why China should develop them and how. Wang argues that they should be understood against the current wave of scientific and technological revolution and China's shift to high-quality development. In this account they are innovation-led, high-tech, high-efficiency and high-quality, and in essence advanced productive forces.

The piece first sets out the technological and economic background, then names three sources of new quality productive forces: breakthroughs in technology, innovative allocation of production factors, and deep industrial transformation and upgrading. It then lists six relationships to be handled, and ends by placing the concept within Xi Jinping's theoretical contribution since 2023.

Wang contends that the old growth model of factor inputs cannot continue and that China must rely on innovation and total factor productivity. The author's examples include artificial intelligence replacing mental as well as manual labour, data as a new production factor, and China's new-energy vehicle output passing 10 million in 2024. The six relationships are: innovation and the commercialisation of results; emerging and traditional industries (the latter said to exceed 80 per cent of manufacturing); government guidance and market mechanisms; finance and innovation; productive forces and relations of production; and top innovative talent and the wider quality of workers. Wang warns against rushing in, bubbles and one-size-fits-all approaches, and says the government should cultivate an innovation ecosystem rather than allocate resources administratively.

Wang concludes that new quality productive forces are an internal requirement of high-quality development. The author presents Xi Jinping's concept as a major development of Marxist productivity theory and calls for study of it and for putting it into practice. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of the practical policy balances behind the new quality productive forces agenda.
quoteEn: An innovation ecosystem is more important than innovation resources.
quoteZh: 创新生态比创新资源更重要。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward by Xi Jinping in 2023. It refers to innovation-driven, technology-intensive productive forces seen as a break from traditional growth paths.
An official goal since about 2017 that stresses efficiency, innovation and sustainability over rapid growth driven by input expansion.
An economic measure of output growth not explained by increases in labour and capital inputs, often used as a proxy for technology and efficiency.

t: Understanding the distinctive features of comprehensively deepening reform through the "seven focuses"
zh: 从“七个聚焦”洞悉全面深化改革的鲜明特质
paras: Liu Zongling and Jiang Ruibing take up the "seven focuses" set out in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively to advance Chinese modernization. They argue that the formulation reveals distinctive features of the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core in the current stage of reform and opening up. In their account, these features are upholding the leadership core, firming up the development path, grasping the value orientation, staying problem-oriented and applying systems thinking.

The commentary is organised as five sections, each treating one feature and tying it to the seven focuses, including the one on raising the Party's leadership level and long-term governing capacity. The authors draw on Xi Jinping's statements, on the Marxist theory of proletarian leadership, and on a historical survey of reform since 1978. They also refer to the fifteen areas of reform the plenum addressed, from the market economy and the innovation system to ecological civilization.

On leadership, the authors say that the Party's guidance supplies the theoretical framework and the strategic deployment for reform, and that improved governing capacity in turn supports reform. On the path, they hold that the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, rooted in the Two Integrations, has delivered economic liberalisation of productive forces, fuller opening and a more developed legal system, and must be followed without deviation. On values, they write that reform is carried out for the people and relies on them, and that people should judge its results. On method, they describe reform as forced by problems and deepened by solving them. They add that reform has moved step by step from points to lines to whole areas and now needs coordination across fields, levels and regions.

The authors conclude that further reform should keep the Party's leadership, strengthen confidence in the chosen path, respond to new domestic and international conditions and new technological revolutions, and be planned within the \"five-sphere integrated plan\" and the \"four-pronged comprehensive strategy\". They call for greater systemic, integrated and coordinated reform. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese academic commentary presents the plenum's reform agenda and its underlying principles.
quoteEn: Comprehensive deepening of reform must always adhere to systems thinking, which is determined by the complexity of the cause of reform and opening up.
quoteZh: 全面深化改革要始终坚持系统观念,这是由改革开放事业的复杂性所决定的。

glossary.explanation: A formulation in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) naming seven priority areas for further reform, such as the economic system, democracy, culture, people's livelihood, ecological civilization, national security and Party building.
The official concept of China's path to modernization, promoted by the Party since the 20th Party Congress (2022) as distinct from Western models.
Xi Jinping's formula for combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with China's fine traditional culture.
The Party's overall plan for coordinated development of the economy, politics, culture, society and the ecological environment.
Xi Jinping's strategic layout from 2014: building a modern socialist country, deepening reform, advancing law-based governance and strengthening Party discipline.

t: Empowering the development of new quality productive forces through an innovation culture
zh: 以创新文化赋能新质生产力发展
paras: Taking up Xi Jinping's call, in a June 2024 Qiushi article, to "do a good job on the big article of innovation", Zhang argues that the formation of new quality productive forces is a process of cultural reshaping as well as an economic and technological one. The author defines an innovation culture as a whole cultural ecosystem made up of innovative values, institutional arrangements and practical norms, and contends that it empowers new quality productive forces on all fronts.

The short commentary is organised around three components, each given a metaphor. Traditional Chinese culture's innovative genes are the "golden key"; a basic system of comprehensive innovation is the "booster"; and original, disruptive breakthroughs are the "navigation instrument". It draws on the 20th Party Congress (2022) report, speeches by Xi, and classical sources such as the Book of Changes, Records of the Grand Historian and Han Yu.

On values, Zhang finds three features in traditional culture that suit the new quality productive forces: active reform, dialectical "upholding fundamental principles while innovating", and open, integrative borrowing. On institutions, the author draws on Marxist political economy, in which institutional and technological innovation are two sides of one process. Zhang lists obstacles such as uneven allocation of research resources and weak coordination, and proposes measures on investment, research platforms linking industry, universities and institutes, market rules and top-level design. On practice, Zhang says Chinese firms rely mostly on integrated and imitative innovation. The author calls for stronger basic research, tolerance of failure, and attention to turning results into products, not only to going "from zero to one".

Zhang concludes that cultivating an innovation culture is a key lever for advancing innovation and new quality productive forces. A social climate in which innovation becomes the norm would, in the author's view, generate internal momentum for high-quality development and the goal of building a strong country. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-aligned scholarship links traditional culture, institutional reform and technology policy to the new quality productive forces agenda.
quoteEn: The formation of new quality productive forces is not merely an economic or technological process, but above all a process of cultural reshaping.
quoteZh: 新质生产力的形成不仅仅是一个经济过程、技术过程，更是一个文化重塑的过程。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping put forward in 2023 for productivity driven by technological breakthroughs and innovation, as opposed to traditional resource- and investment-heavy growth.
An official goal of the economy since about 2017, stressing efficiency, innovation and sustainability over speed of growth.
A term used in Party documents, including the 20th Party Congress report, for the values, norms and atmosphere that encourage scientific and technological innovation.

glossary.literal: preserving what is correct and innovating
glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse calling for innovation that stays faithful to core principles and the Party's course.

t: Scientific legislation as a key link in handling the relationship between reform and the rule of law
zh: 科学立法是处理改革和法治关系的重要环节
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 27 December 2024, asks how legislation can keep pace with deepening reform. Zhou Longjie argues that, of all the dimensions of rule-of-law building, scientific legislation is the key link in handling the relationship between reform and the rule of law.

The piece opens by citing Xi Jinping on earlier reform eras in Chinese history and on the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for deepening reform "on the track of the rule of law" and for advancing Chinese modernization. It then sets out five practical requirements, followed by a note on institutional obstacles.

Zhou's central claim is that reform stresses change while law stresses stability, so law tends to lag behind practice. The rule of law is therefore both a guarantee of reform and an object of reform. The five requirements are: consider legislation while designing reform measures; elevate proven experience into law, as with the 2018 Supervision Law and the Foreign Investment Law; grant authorisation under legal procedure for pilot reforms where legislation is premature, such as the rural land pilots authorised by the NPC Standing Committee; and amend or repeal laws that no longer fit reform, citing the 2023 State Council order revising 14 administrative regulations. Zhou rejects both "beneficial law-breaking reform" and the use of missing legal basis as a reason to hold reform back.

Zhou concludes that overcoming local and departmental interests, and improving the quality and efficiency of legislation, is also necessary. The author calls for clearer limits on legislative power and institutional safeguards against the legalisation of departmental interests and local protectionism. Read the original if you want a brief, official-style statement of how Chinese legal scholars link legislation to the reform agenda set out in 2024.
quoteEn: Comprehensively advancing the rule of law does not permit arbitrarily crossing legal red lines in so-called "beneficial law-breaking reform"; comprehensively deepening reform likewise does not permit the lack of a basis in existing law to be used simply as a reason to bind or delay reform.
quoteZh: 全面依法治国不允许随意突破法律红线，搞所谓“良性违法改革”；全面深化改革也不允许简单以没有现行法依据为由，束缚改革或迟滞改革。

glossary.explanation: The official Party formulation for China's path of development, promoted especially since the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernisation.
An official principle holding that lawmaking should respect objective laws of social development. It is usually listed with democratic legislation and legislation in accordance with law.

t: Safeguarding and improving people's wellbeing through development
zh: 在发展中保障和改善民生
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily on 27 December 2024, Lin Jinping takes up a line from the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): that safeguarding and improving people's wellbeing (minsheng) through development is a major task of Chinese modernization. Lin argues that the classical Marxist texts contain a rich body of thought on this subject, and that rereading it clarifies why wellbeing is "of the greatest importance" and what principles should guide the work in the new stage.

The short commentary has three sections. The first treats wellbeing as a matter of the people's welfare. The second presents Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee of work on wellbeing. The third stresses institution-building. Lin draws on Marx, Engels and Lenin, and ends with the record of the People's Republic.

Lin argues that Marxist thinking on wellbeing rests on three elements: material production, human needs and the distribution of interests. Production is the foundation, meeting needs and all-round human development is the goal, and fair distribution is the key. Development alone is not enough, since Marx and Engels' analysis of capitalism shows that a people-centred social system is also required. Lin contends that a Communist Party representing the fundamental interests of the broadest masses must lead, drawing on Engels's account of authority in large-scale industry. Lin also holds that people should not be seen only as workers, so social security and other institutional means must accompany productive development.

Lin concludes that the Chinese Communist Party has moved the people's material and cultural life from scarcity to sufficiency and is now working on the shift from sufficiency to quality. Lin calls for better income distribution, employment-first policies, social security, healthcare reform and population support, to advance common prosperity. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-aligned commentary ties classical Marxist texts to current policy on livelihoods.
quoteEn: Improving and raising people's wellbeing depends on development and also cannot do without institutional guarantees.
quoteZh: 民生的改善与提升既要靠发展，也离不开制度保障。

glossary.explanation: A traditional Chinese term covering the material conditions of ordinary life, such as employment, income, education, healthcare and social security. It is now a standard category in Party policy discourse.
The official name for China's development path, set out by Xi Jinping and the Party from the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models of modernization.
An official goal of shared wealth for all the people, given new prominence under Xi Jinping. It is presented as a defining feature of socialism.

glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de èrshí jiè sān zhōngquánhuì
glossary.en: Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee
glossary.explanation: A plenary meeting of the Party's Central Committee held in July 2024. It adopted a decision on further comprehensively deepening reform.

t: Strengthening the consistency of macro-policy orientation to release the combined effect of multiple overlapping strategies
zh: 增强宏观政策取向一致性 释放多重战略叠加效能
paras: This short commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 27 December 2024, takes up a question raised by the 2024 Central Economic Work Conference: how to make the overlapping regional strategies work together. Hao and Ni argue that strengthening the consistency of macro-policy orientation is the key means of releasing the advantages of such overlap and improving regional governance.

The authors begin from the fact that regional strategies now routinely overlap. They give Shaanxi, Gansu, Henan and Shanxi as examples, and Anhui as the only province covered by three strategies at once. They list problems in local practice, including market segmentation and administrative barriers, poor fit between planning goals and policy tools, and weak coordination of fiscal, financial and industrial policy with national strategy. The rest of the piece sets out three goals, each paired with a mechanism.

In the authors' account, consistency has three dimensions. The first is overall layout, which calls for a deep-integration mechanism. Anhui, for example, should treat its three strategies as one whole, led by Yangtze River Delta integration. The second is the institutional system, which calls for a coordination mechanism. Here the authors stress balancing the whole and its parts, unity and difference, and long-term and phased policies, and they propose assessing economic and non-economic policies together. The third is implementation, which calls for a linking mechanism. It would join up institutions across fields, levels and time, and link special, regional, spatial and local plans to national planning.

The authors conclude that policies should undergo a consistency assessment before release and be checked continuously during implementation. After they take effect, policies that diverge from governance goals should be adjusted or suspended. They present this as a way to bring out the distinctive strengths of socialism with Chinese characteristics and to modernise national governance. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-school researchers frame policy coordination across regional strategies after the Third Plenum.
quoteEn: Strengthening the consistency of macro-policy orientation and releasing the advantages of overlapping regional strategies have become an important lever for improving regional governance.
quoteZh: 增强宏观政策取向一致性，释放多重区域战略叠加优势，成为提升区域治理效能的重要抓手

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's governing doctrine and system since the reform period. It is presented as Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions.

glossary.zh: 增强宏观政策取向一致性
glossary.literal: strengthen the consistency of macro-policy orientation
glossary.explanation: A requirement repeated in central documents since late 2023. It means that fiscal, monetary, industrial and other policies should point in the same direction and be assessed together.

t: Stimulating powerful momentum for high-quality development
zh: 激发高质量发展的强大动力
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 15 November 2022, shortly after the 20th Party Congress, this commentary asks how the Congress's priority of high-quality development can be achieved. Han argues that it requires applying the new development philosophy fully, accurately and comprehensively, accelerating the new development pattern, and mobilising society as a whole. High-quality development is presented as the essential requirement of Chinese modernization and as the primary task of building a modern socialist country.

The piece is organised in three parts, each anchored in the Congress report and in quotations from Xi Jinping. The first sets out what high-quality development means and how the new development philosophy should be built into social reproduction, the new development pattern and the modern economic system. The second, the longest, deals with the new development pattern. The third turns to the social forces needed to carry the effort through.

Han's core argument draws on Marxist political economy. Citing the theory of the realisation of the total social product, Han holds that quality ultimately depends on whether goods find buyers, so aggregate demand must validate aggregate supply. After more than 40 years of reform and opening up, the author says, China faces relative oversupply, and this makes expanding domestic demand the strategic basis. Han ties this to supply-side structural reform, with innovation, a strong manufacturing base, "long boards" strengthened and "short boards" repaired in industrial chains, agricultural modernization, and balanced development of finance, property and the real economy. The third lever is reform and opening up, which Han says should remove blockages in the economic cycle through a high-level socialist market economy and high-level opening.

Han concludes that the new development pattern can be built only by drawing on the creativity of the people, as historical materialism holds. The author proposes arming officials and the public with Xi Jinping's economic thought, deepening state-owned enterprise reform, protecting private and foreign-invested firms, and building a capable cadre corps with accountability and error-tolerance mechanisms. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how a prominent Party School economist links the 20th Congress economic goals to Marxist circulation and realisation theory.
quoteEn: Whether the quality of development is high ultimately depends on whether the products of social production can be realised.
quoteZh: 发展质量到底高不高，归根到底还是看社会生产的产品能否得到实现。

glossary.explanation: An official concept, prominent since 2017, that shifts the emphasis from growth speed to the quality, efficiency and sustainability of growth. The 20th Party Congress called it the primary task of building a modern socialist country.
The Party's guiding framework of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, put forward in 2015.
An economic strategy centred on the domestic cycle, with domestic and international cycles reinforcing each other. It was advanced by Xi Jinping in 2020.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out in detail at the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
A policy line launched in 2015 to improve the quality of supply, cut excess capacity and raise efficiency, rather than relying only on stimulating demand.

t: Raising traditional Chinese medicine to a level that contributes to the whole world
st: Mao Zedong's role in reviving traditional Chinese medicine in the early People's Republic
zh: 把中医提到对全世界有贡献的高度
source: China Journal of Traditional Chinese Medicine (Zhongguo Zhongyiyao Bao), 19 November 2014
paras: Han Honghong asks how Mao Zedong shaped the revival of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) after 1949. Writing in 2014, Han draws on the six-volume Chronology of Mao Zedong (1949–1976), published in December 2013, which for the first time disclosed several of his remarks on the subject. The article argues that Mao treated TCM as a cultural heritage to be critically inherited, unified with Western medicine and raised to the point of contributing to the world.

The article is organised in five parts. It begins with Mao's assessment of TCM's historical and practical value between 1949 and 1958, including his edits to a 1954 Central Committee directive. It then examines his campaign against contempt for TCM, his principle of combining Chinese and Western medicine, and the movement for mutual learning between the two. A final section draws three lessons for present-day TCM policy.

Han's central claim is that Mao combined respect for TCM with a demand that it be scientifically examined. Han reports that Mao described TCM as a product of agrarian and handicraft society, to be accepted critically, keeping what is rational and discarding the dross. Mao denounced disdain for TCM as a servile, pro-foreign attitude and blamed sectarianism among Western-trained doctors. Han shows how Mao's position developed into the principle of integrating traditional Chinese and Western medicine, with Western-trained doctors learning TCM and TCM practitioners learning modern science, aiming at a unified new Chinese medicine. Han cites concrete measures: the 1955 Central Committee approval of a report on improving TCM work, and the training courses that released Western-trained doctors to study TCM. According to the article, about 36,000 such doctors were studying TCM by 1960.

Han draws three lessons. TCM development should rest on national conditions and balance inheritance with innovation, in line with Xi Jinping's call for creative transformation and innovative development of traditional culture. Integration of Chinese and Western medicine should be maintained as mutually complementary, which the article says has influenced the rise of integrative medicine worldwide. TCM should also follow a healthy and sustainable path, supported by talent, industry and overseas outreach. Read the original if you want a Party-historian's account of Mao's recorded remarks on TCM and of how they are used to frame current policy.
quoteEn: Second, the development of TCM must handle its relationship with Western medicine dialectically, adhering to the principle of integrating Chinese and Western medicine, so that the two promote and complement each other.
quoteZh: 第二，发展中医药事业要辩证地处理好与西医的关系，坚持中西医结合的原则，互相促进，互为补充。

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A formula used by Xi Jinping for treating traditional culture: adapting its content and forms to the present and developing them further.

keywords: integration of Chinese and Western medicine

t: Four "defeats" in Mao Zedong's own account: Gaoxingxu, Nanxiong Shuikou, Tucheng and Luban Chang
zh: 《党史博采》：毛泽东眼中的四次“败仗”
source: Dangshi Bocai, 2023, no. 1 (first half of the month)
paras: This is a popular Party-history feature from the journal Dangshi Bocai (2023, first issue). It takes up a remark Mao Zedong made on 10 September 1956 at a preparatory meeting for the Eighth Party Congress. There he said openly that he had personally commanded battles that were lost: Gaoxingxu, Nanxiong, Tucheng and Maotai (Luban Chang). The text presents the four engagements as evidence that Mao, though celebrated as a brilliant strategist, never claimed to be undefeated.

The article is built as four short military narratives in chronological order. The first is the Gaoxingxu fighting of September 1931 during the Third Encirclement Campaign in the Central Soviet Area. The second is the Nanxiong–Shuikou campaign of July 1932 against Guangdong forces. The third is the battle of Tucheng in January 1935, the first fight after the Zunyi Conference. The fourth is the attack on Zhou Hunyuan's column at Luban Chang in March 1935. Each section gives troop movements, orders, casualties and what went wrong.

The article's central point is that each "defeat" had a specific cause. At Gaoxingxu, the Red Army's forces were not concentrated, it ran short of ammunition and lost heavily, though it wiped out an enemy brigade. At Nanxiong Shuikou, false reports that the enemy had withdrawn, and the mistaking of ten enemy regiments for four, produced a costly victory. The article quotes Mao's later remark that such battles, "usually counted as victories", were ones "we have never welcomed". At Tucheng, a one-character intelligence error (a brigade rendered as a regiment) meant the enemy was far stronger than expected. At Luban Chang, the enemy's fortifications, fierce fire and air support forced a withdrawal.

The article concludes that these setbacks did not end in failure overall. The Tucheng reverse pushed the Red Army to cross the Chishui River westward, which opened the Four Crossings of the Chishui, described as one of Mao's finest strokes. Luban Chang, in the article's view, rested on a correct decision and did not prevent that success. Read the original if you want a detailed, narrative-style account of these four engagements and the Chinese Party-history framing of Mao's admission of failure.
quoteEn: A victory won by mutual attrition like this was, in a sense, simply a defeat.
quoteZh: 这种互拼消耗的胜仗，在某种意义上简直是一次败仗。

t: An analysis of the content of intra-Party political culture in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期党内政治文化内涵探析
source: Journal of Beijing Normal University (Social Sciences Edition), 2022 no. 6
paras: Feng Liujian and Jiang Wei ask what constituted the political culture inside the Chinese Communist Party during the Yan'an period, which they date from October 1935, when the Central Committee reached Wuqi in northern Shaanxi, to March 1948, when its leaders crossed the Yellow River. They define this culture as the Party values and behaviour found among members and organisations, including political belief, cognition, style, norms and values. Their thesis is that it formed an organic unity of three layers: political ideas, political institutions and political conduct.

The article is organised around these three layers. Ideas are called the 'soul' of intra-Party political culture, institutions its 'guarantee' and conduct its outward 'manifestation'. Under ideas, the authors treat Marxism as guiding ideology, communism as fundamental political belief, and wholehearted service to the people. Under institutions, they cover the Party's leadership system, democratic centralism and cadre management. Under conduct, they cover the three work styles, the Party's political image and its clean, honest character. The evidence is drawn from Party resolutions, speeches by Mao Zedong and Liu Shaoqi, and accounts by visitors such as Edgar Snow, Anna Louise Strong and Huang Yanpei.

In the authors' account, the Sinification of Marxism, the idea of adapting Marxism to China's conditions, gave the Party a theoretical, ideological and practical self-awareness. They cite the 1942 decisions on unified leadership, the system of reporting to superiors, and the 1941 decision on strengthening Party spirit as institutional means of upholding the authority of the Central Committee. Democratic centralism is presented as balancing inner-Party democracy with centralised unity. The authors credit the cadre system, which they say rested on merit and virtue, study systems, screening, supervision and anti-corruption rules, with building a capable leadership.

Feng and Jiang present the three work styles of linking theory with practice, keeping close ties with the masses, and criticism and self-criticism as the visible form of this culture.
