glossary.explanation: In Mao's 1927 Report, one of the four 'authorities' (political, clan, divine, marital) binding the peasantry. It covers the whole hierarchy of gods, spirits and ghosts, seen as part of the feudal order.

The official Party characterisation of China's current developmental stage, in which socialism is established but productive forces remain underdeveloped. The article uses it to explain why belief in spirits persists.

t: Why Mao Zedong called the Rectification Documents a "classic"
zh: 毛泽东为何称《整风文献》为经书
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2022 no. 6
paras: In November 1942, speaking to a conference of senior cadres in north-west China, Mao Zedong called the documents of the rectification campaign "a classic" (jingshu). Hu Weixiong notes that scholars have rarely asked why, and that some, influenced by foreign scholarship, hold that the collection contains no Marxist classics. The article analyses the choice of items and the structure of the Rectification Documents (Zhengfeng wenxian) to explain in what sense Mao could call them a classic. Hu concludes that the collection is a classic of Party-building whose core is the union of Marxist-Leninist truth with Chinese revolutionary practice.

Hu first reconstructs the editions: 18 documents in April 1942, 22 after additions, then a revised edition rising to 27 items by 1943. Taking the 27-item version, the article sorts the contents into four groups: rectifying the Party's style of study, Party work and writing; Party members' self-cultivation and organisational building; leadership, cadre policy, inner-Party struggle, discipline and democracy; and the Party's mission, propaganda and leadership, including Bolshevization. It describes the main items in each group, then assesses the collection's place in the history of Chinese Marxism.

Hu's central claim is that the first group is the core. He singles out Mao's "Reform Our Study", "Rectify the Party's Style of Work" and "Oppose Stereotyped Party Writing" as foundational texts attacking subjectivism, dogmatism, sectarianism and formulaic writing, and urging investigation of Chinese conditions and history. The remaining items, by Liu Shaoqi, Chen Yun, Stalin, Dimitrov and Lenin, supply standards for Party members, discipline and self-criticism. Hu also stresses that Mao selected and reviewed every item, and that ten of the texts are his own. He places the collection beside two other study series for cadres, the "Party books" on Party history and the compilation of Marx, Engels, Lenin and Stalin on methods of thinking, and presents the whole as a Marxist study campaign in the form of rectification.

Hu argues that the campaign removed the dogmatism and sectarianism associated with Wang Ming's line, made the Party a tightly organised Bolshevik-style party, and prepared the successful Seventh Party Congress. He treats Mao's principles of uniting theory and practice and seeking truth from facts as holding universal significance for Marxist parties. Hu also reads Mao's 1943 letter, which called only some rectification documents "fragments" of his thought, as consistent with their central role. Read the original if you want a detailed, document-by-document account of what the rectification canon contained and how a Party School scholar justifies its status.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong called the Rectification Documents a "classic"; such high praise for a work he compiled himself was unprecedented, far exceeding his assessment of his own beloved poems.
quoteZh: 毛泽东把《整风文献》称之为“经书”，如此高度评价自己编的作品，这是“破天荒”，远远超越了他对自己创作而又心爱的诗词作品的评价。

glossary.explanation: The Yan'an-era campaign of 1941–45 led by Mao Zedong to correct styles of study, Party work and writing, and to consolidate his leadership and the Sinification of Marxism.
A compiled collection of study texts for Party cadres, first published in 1942 and later expanded, used as the standard reading in the rectification campaign.
In Mao's usage, a style of thinking that ignores objective conditions, covering both dogmatism and narrow empiricism.
In Party discourse, treating Marxist texts or Soviet experience as fixed formulas, a charge aimed in the campaign at Wang Ming and the returned students.
Mao's term for empty, formulaic and jargon-filled Party writing and speech, likened to the old imperial eight-legged examination essay.
The process of remodelling a Communist party on the Bolshevik model; Stalin's twelve conditions were a standard text on it in the Chinese Party.

t: A brief discussion of Mao Zedong's view of history and its practice
zh: 简论毛泽东的史学观及其实践
source: Journal of the Party School of the CPC Central Committee (National Academy of Governance), 2022 no. 5
paras: How did Mao Zedong's deep reading of history shape his views and decisions? Zhou Suyuan argues that Mao respected, studied and used history throughout his life, and that this gave him foresight, a grasp of historical regularities and a distinctive method of learning from the past. The article presents this as a coherent view of history that Mao applied at critical junctures of the revolution and in governing.

The article has four parts. It first sets out Mao's view of history and his stated aims and methods in studying it. It then looks at how Mao drew on history at key turning points: choosing Marxism-Leninism and the socialist road, the strategy of encircling the cities from the countryside, the protracted-war thesis, and carrying the revolution through to the end. A third part treats three famous exchanges, the "Jiashen dialogue", the "cave dialogue" and the "examination dialogue". The last part considers the historical wisdom in Mao Zedong Thought and in his education of cadres.

Zhou contends that Mao treated history as a heritage to be respected but critically sifted, rejecting both historical nihilism and uncritical revival of the past. He is said to have studied failure as well as success, reinterpreted old texts ("new readings of ancient books, using the past to serve the present") and separated essence from dross. In Zhou's account, the three living aspects of Mao Zedong Thought, seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence and self-reliance, each have roots in classical sources; "seeking truth from facts" was lifted from textual scholarship into a Marxist epistemology. Zhou reads the three dialogues as warnings, drawn from the fall of Li Zicheng's rebels and the historical cycle of rise and decline, against complacency after victory and as the basis for the answer that democracy lets the people supervise government.

Zhou concludes that Mao's use of history gave him far-sighted judgement, an optimism rooted in his understanding of social development, and a lasting method of drawing lessons from others' experience. After 1949, the article says, Mao's concern shifted to guarding against corruption and degeneration among cadres. Read the original if you want a Chinese scholar's account of how Mao's historical outlook is presented within official Party history, with many cited episodes and classical allusions.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong raised \"seeking truth from facts\" from a method of textual scholarship to a Marxist epistemology and developed it into the Chinese Communist Party's ideological line, enriching its content and widening its scope, a model of using the past to serve the present.
quoteZh: 毛泽东将“实事求是”从考据学的方法提升为马克思主义认识论，发展为中国共产党的思想路线，使其内涵得到丰富，外延得到拓展，是古为今用的典范。

glossary.explanation: An old phrase from the Han Shu that Mao redefined in 1941 as investigating objective things to find their inner regularities. It became the core of the Party's ideological line.
The Party's method of gathering the views of the masses, turning them into policy and returning to the masses to explain and implement it. Associated with Mao Zedong.
The Party's official term for the adaptation of Marxism-Leninism to Chinese conditions, credited to Mao and the collective leadership.
A 1945 conversation in Yan'an between Mao and Huang Yanpei about escaping the historical cycle of rise and decline. Mao's answer was democracy, with the people supervising government.
The label later given to Mao's 1944 exchange with Guo Moruo and his use of Guo's essay on the fall of Li Zicheng's regime in 1644, as a warning against complacency.
Mao's remark to Zhou Enlai in March 1949, as the leadership travelled to Beijing, that they were going to take an examination and must not be like Li Zicheng.

t: The "Yan'an Road" as a Third World path and a new world history
zh: 作为第三世界的“延安道路”与新的世界史
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 7
paras: Lü Xinyu asks how China's place in the world should be understood amid what the author calls a Western-imposed "new Cold War". The article argues that a Third World perspective, together with a return to the "Yan'an Road", is indispensable for answering where China comes from and where it is going. In Lü's reading, China's rise is the extension of a twentieth-century socialist and anti-colonial line, and its path belongs to more than China alone.

The article opens by contrasting two ideas of the "Third World": Mao Zedong's and Deng Xiaoping's 1974 Three Worlds theory, and Leften Stavrianos's Global Divide (1981), which describes Third World failure under neo-colonialism. It then compares China with the neoliberal West through David Harvey, before turning to Samir Amin's "delinking" and Immanuel Wallerstein's account of ecology. It ends with China's anti-poverty, green development, Belt and Road and pandemic-aid measures, and with questions about the Party's "self-reform".

Lü's core moves are as follows. First, drawing on Stavrianos, the author holds that China was the exception among Third World revolutions because the Yan'an "mass line" built a political subject on egalitarian participation, whereas other movements were bourgeois-nationalist. Second, drawing on Harvey, Lü argues that neoliberalism and right-wing populism are two sides of one coin, and that the Western left's failure ceded the state to the right. China's patriotism should therefore not be equated with Western nationalism. Third, Lü reads Amin's call for sovereignty-based "delinking" and internal change as describing the Chinese road, and treats Chinese measures on poverty, state-owned enterprises, ecology and aid as evidence that it is not "state capitalism".

Lü concludes that the Party's historic task is now to prove that "only China can save socialism", as it earlier showed that only socialism could save China. The Yan'an Road is described as the starting point of the "China road", and the Party's self-reform as a new test. Lü also raises open questions, including whether China can resist great-power chauvinism and keep supplying infrastructure to the Third World. Read the original if you want a Chinese left-wing scholar's argument linking Yan'an, Third World theory (Amin, Wallerstein, Harvey) and current geopolitics.
quoteEn: The "Yan'an Road" is the starting point of the "China road".
quoteZh: “延安道路”是“中国道路”的起点。

glossary.explanation: The revolutionary practice of the Chinese Communist Party in its Yan'an base area (1930s–40s), including the mass line and rectification campaigns. Lü treats it as the origin of the later "China road".
A Party method of drawing on and mobilising the masses, associated with Mao Zedong and the Yan'an period. It means leaders learn from the people and then lead them.
Mao Zedong's 1974 division of the world into the superpowers (the US and USSR), other developed countries, and the Third World. It placed China within the Third World.
An official term for the Party's efforts to correct itself and maintain discipline. Lü presents it as a new test linked to the Yan'an tradition.

t: The structure, main themes and influence of Mao Zedong's annotations on A System of Ethics
zh: 毛泽东《〈伦理学原理〉批注》的结构、主旨和影响
paras: Han Qi and Tian Linian examine the more than 12,000 characters of marginal notes that the young Mao Zedong wrote in 1917–1918 on Cai Yuanpei's Chinese translation of Friedrich Paulsen's System of Ethics. They ask what moral philosophy Mao developed there and how it shaped his later practical character. They argue that the notes contain a distinctive moral ontology and two ethical positions, individualism and realism, which together unify value and truth.

The article has three parts. The first reconstructs Mao's chain of eight paired concepts, from good and evil down to "mind and principle" (xinli), and the two positions drawn from it. The second analyses how these positions relate to value, truth and the "force of mind" as moral foundation. The third traces two chains of thought and their later Marxist transformation into On Practice and On Contradiction. The authors engage Kondo Kuniyasu, Zhang Hao, Wakeman, Li Zehou, Xiao Yanzhong, Tian Chenshan and Schwartz, and draw on Yang Changji's teaching.

The authors read Mao's "spiritual individualism" as a subjective moral law, and his realism as the historical and concrete condition for realising it. Mao's notes thereby overcome the flaws they find in the British Hegelian self-realisation ethics that Yang Changji had introduced, and in moral theology. The central principle is sincerity (cheng), through which value governs truth. From it come two chains: mind, individualism, value and subjective initiative; and principle, realism, truth and objective regularity. The authors situate these in the thought of change (tongbian) in the Book of Changes, in Rousseau and Kant, and in May Fourth individualism and social reform.

The authors conclude that after Mao's turn to Marxism, "seeking truth from facts" replaced sincerity, and practice replaced force of mind. The individual was then understood as a member of a class within social relations. They argue that Mao's late thought on socialist construction should be read within this lifelong trajectory, and not reduced to "philosophy of struggle", moralism or populism. Read the original if you study the early Mao, the roots of his practical philosophy, or the Sinicisation of Marxist philosophy.
quoteEn: Unifying value and truth by letting value govern truth in fact brings people no greater freedom of action; on the contrary, people bear their own responsibility to know reality and to practise morality.
quoteZh: 由价值统摄真理而使二者实现统一，实际上并没有给人带来更大的行动自由，恰恰相反，人担负着认识现实和实践道德的本己责任

glossary.explanation: A principle taken from classical Chinese texts and made central to Mao Zedong's thought. It stresses basing judgement and action on actual conditions.
The Party's term for adapting Marxism to Chinese conditions and culture. It is often associated with Mao Zedong's theoretical works.
A concept from the Confucian Doctrine of the Mean, meaning sincerity or authenticity. The article treats it as the central principle of Mao's early ethics.
A term for willpower or mental energy, used in the title of Mao's 1917 essay "The Power of the Mind". The article treats it as his moral ontology.
A mode of thinking rooted in the Book of Changes, in which opposite pairs such as yin and yang generate change through interaction. Tian Chenshan treats it as the base of "Chinese dialectics".

t: Why Mao Zedong called the Rectification Documents a "classic text"
zh: 毛泽东为何称《整风文献》为经书
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2022 no. 6
paras: In November 1942 Mao Zedong told a meeting of senior cadres in the Northwest that the documents for rectifying the Party's "three work styles" were "a classic text" (jingshu). Hu Weixiong notes that scholars have paid little attention to why Mao said this. Some foreign scholars hold that the collection contains no Marxist classics. Hu argues, from the selection and structure of the Rectification Documents, that the collection deserves the label because it is a coherent programme for building the Party, grounded in the union of Marxist-Leninist theory with Chinese revolutionary practice.

The article first traces the editions: 18 documents in the April 1942 version, 22 after the Propaganda Department's additions, and 27 in the revised 1943 edition, which Hu takes as the object of study. It sorts the 27 texts into four groups: rectifying the Party, study and writing styles; Party members' self-cultivation and organisational building; leadership, cadre policy, inner-Party criticism and struggle, discipline and democracy; and the Party's mission, propaganda, leadership methods and Bolshevisation. Hu summarises the main texts in each group, from Mao's own reports to pieces by Liu Shaoqi, Chen Yun, Stalin, Dimitrov and Lenin.

Hu's central claim is that Mao's writings supply the core and the guiding spirit. Reform Our Study, Rectify the Party's Style of Work and Oppose Stereotyped Party Writing attack subjectivism, dogmatism and sectarianism, and ask that Marxism-Leninism be used as an \"arrow\" aimed at the \"target\" of the Chinese revolution. The Bolshevisation texts, the Stalin and Dimitrov selections and the Liu and Chen pieces then supply norms for members, discipline, self-criticism and cadre selection. Hu also places the collection beside two other study series, the \"Party books\" and Marx, Engels, Lenin and Stalin on Methods of Thought, and treats it as the only one containing original works. Hu reads the campaign as a Marxist study movement against the dogmatism of Wang Ming, and cites Mao's remark that he did not wish his thought presented as a system.

Hu concludes that the Rectification Documents hold a landmark place in the history of Chinese Marxism. They answered the question that had troubled the Party for nearly twenty years, namely how to combine universal truth with Chinese practice. They helped turn the Party into a cohesive, Bolshevik-style body able to lead the War of Resistance and the New Democratic revolution, and its seventh congress marked its transformation into a modern party. Hu adds that the principles of linking theory with practice and seeking truth from facts apply to Marxist parties worldwide. Read the original if you want a document-by-document account of what the 1942–43 rectification texts contained and how a Party School scholar reads their role in Mao's thought.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong called the Rectification Documents a "classic text"; such high praise for a work he had compiled was unprecedented, far exceeding his appraisal of his own beloved poems.
quoteZh: 毛泽东把《整风文献》称之为“经书”，如此高度评价自己编的作品，这是“破天荒”，远远超越了他对自己创作而又心爱的诗词作品的评价。

glossary.explanation: The Party-wide campaign launched in Yan'an in 1942 to correct ideological and organisational faults. It targeted subjectivism, sectarianism and stereotyped Party writing.
A compilation of documents that cadres had to study during the Yan'an rectification campaign. The first edition appeared in 1942 and the revised edition in 1943.
Mao's term for formulaic, empty and dogmatic writing and speech in the Party, likened to the stiff imperial examination essay.
In Mao's usage, treating Marxist texts as fixed formulas detached from Chinese conditions. The campaign associated it with Wang Ming and the Soviet-trained group.
The process of remaking a communist party on the Leninist model. Stalin's twelve conditions for it were among the texts studied in the campaign.
A principle central to Mao's thought that Marxist theory must be applied to concrete Chinese conditions. It is closely tied to seeking truth from facts.

t: Advancing social development with a people-centred approach
zh: 以人民为中心推进社会建设
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 7 October 2022, this short commentary reviews a decade of "social development" (shehui jianshe) since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Yu Jianxing and Wu Jiebing argue that Xi Jinping's new ideas have answered why and how social development should be pursued in the new era. In their account, these ideas raised the Party's understanding of the subject and drove theoretical and practical innovation.

The article has two parts. The first summarises practice and experience since 2012 under four headings: a people-centred concept of social development, the joint advance of social and economic development, the balance between order and vitality, and the interaction of government and society. The second part identifies remaining problems and sets out five areas for reform of the institutions and mechanisms of social development.

The authors say that before 2012 social development was understood mainly as improving people's livelihoods. They hold that the 18th Party Congress report added the innovation of social governance, so that social development became a large system spanning resource allocation, social interests, livelihoods, social organisations and social undertakings. They cite GDP above 100 trillion yuan, per capita GDP above US$10,000, an olive-shaped income distribution, and legal and organisational reforms such as the Civil Code and the Charity Law. They also note the Fengqiao experience and the decoupling of trade associations from administrative organs. They then name three imbalances in some regions: economy over society, livelihood services over social governance, and stability over vitality. They add that local governments treat social development as a weak incentive because results are slow to appear.

The authors propose strengthening Party leadership, for instance through Party committee social work or social development commissions. They also call for treating social development like economic development, narrowing the urban–rural, regional and income gaps, and building community resilience and emergency capacity. Further proposals are classified, dynamically empowered management of social organisations, funded by project subsidies rather than service outsourcing, and digital and intelligent reform that reshapes power structures and cooperation. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned summary of how Chinese scholars framed social development and its reform agenda in 2022.
quoteEn: The process of social development in China is a process of continually adjusting the relationship between government and society.
quoteZh: 我国社会建设的进程,就是不断调整政府与社会之间关系的过程

glossary.explanation: A Party-state term for building the social sphere: livelihoods, public services, social governance and social organisations. It stands alongside economic, political and cultural development.
The management of social affairs through Party, government, social organisations and citizens. It replaced the older term 'social management' in official usage after 2012.
A model of resolving disputes at the grassroots, originating in Fengqiao, Zhejiang, in the 1960s. It is promoted in the 'new era' as a method of local conflict prevention and mediation.

t: The essential attributes and contemporary concerns of the path of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化道路的本质属性和当代关切
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in September 2022, this commentary asks what defines the path of Chinese modernization and what concerns it addresses today. Xu Ping and Yu Miao argue that its essential attributes are Party leadership and socialism, and that it differs from Western modernization in three practical features: independence, rootedness in Chinese soil and a people-centred orientation. The authors present it as a path that creates a new form of human civilisation and offers developing countries a new option.

The piece opens by citing the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's centenary achievements and historical experience. It then has three sections: the essential attributes of the path, its distinctive practical features compared with Western modernization, and its contemporary content. The contemporary content is organised around Xi Jinping's account of the five features of Chinese modernization and the new development philosophy. The argument rests largely on quotations from Xi Jinping, Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping.

In the authors' account, Party leadership is the decisive element and the fundamental political advantage of the path. Socialism is its institutional basis and fundamental direction, and the path aims to unite a high level of modernization with socialism and so go beyond capitalist modernization. The authors say this rejects the old Western routes of capital-centred, polarising, materialist and expansionist modernization. Independence, they argue, follows from a history of subordination to the West and from the lesson that no nation can prosper by depending on others. Rootedness means gradual, endogenous evolution from Chinese civilisation. The people-centred character draws on Marxism, with development for the people, by the people and shared by the people.

The authors conclude that the path must be advanced by acting on the new development stage, the new development philosophy and the new development pattern. They call for coordinating the "five-sphere" overall plan and the "four-pronged" strategy. They say innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing steer modernization toward higher quality, efficiency, fairness and harmony. A framework centred on whole-process people's democracy and common prosperity is said to be taking shape. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary in 2022 presented Chinese modernization's defining attributes and its contrast with Western models.
quoteEn: The essential attributes of the path of Chinese modernization are Party leadership and socialism: that is, the path is continually advanced and extended on the basis of the socialist system framework that the Communist Party of China created in leading the Chinese people.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化道路的本质属性是党的领导和社会主义，即在中国共产党领导中国人民开创的社会主义制度框架的基础上，不断推进和拓展中国式现代化道路。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's model of modernization, presented by the Party as combining universal features of modernization with Chinese conditions and socialism. It was elaborated especially after the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A set of five principles announced in 2015: innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing. It is the official guide for China's development policy.
A socialist goal of prosperity shared by all the people, which the Party has emphasised under Xi Jinping as a defining feature of Chinese modernization.
The official term for China's claimed democratic model, which stresses people's participation at every stage of governance, not only in elections.

t: The key to building a modern socialist country in all respects lies in the Party
zh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家关键在党
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 18 October 2022, during the 20th Party Congress, this commentary takes up Xi Jinping's statement in the Congress report that the key to building a modern socialist country in all respects and advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation lies in the Party. Wang and Liu argue that Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party, and that the Party's overall leadership must therefore be upheld and strengthened.

The piece has three parts. It first traces how the Party led the people onto the path of Chinese modernization across four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era from the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then explains why Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of the project, and finally turns to the role of full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

On the second point, the authors give three reasons. Party leadership keeps Chinese modernization on the right direction and in line with the essential requirements of socialism. It keeps modernization people-centred. It also gathers great strength, because the Party is said to share the people's interests and fate. The authors credit this leadership with letting China complete in decades an industrialization that took developed countries centuries, and with two miracles of rapid growth and long-term social stability.

The authors conclude that upholding leadership requires improving it, and call for the Party's self-reform to lead social revolution. Their agenda covers political, ideological, organizational, conduct and discipline building, institutional improvement, and an integrated approach to fighting corruption. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed statement of how Party commentary linked Party leadership to Chinese modernization on the eve of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Building a modern socialist country in all respects depends on the Party, and above all on upholding the principle that the Party must supervise itself and exercising full and rigorous self-governance.
quoteZh: 全面建设社会主义现代化国家，关键在党，关键在坚持党要管党、全面从严治党。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path of modernization, described in the 20th Party Congress report by five features, including huge population size and common prosperity.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A Party-building policy emphasised since 2012, covering ideological, organizational, conduct and discipline building and anti-corruption work.

A formulation in Xi Jinping-era discourse for the Party's continual internal correction and purification, presented as the second answer to the question of how to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall.

t: Stand firm in historical confidence and strengthen historical initiative
zh: 坚定历史自信 增强历史主动
paras: Written on the eve of the 20th Party Congress (2022) and first published in Guangming Daily, this commentary takes up Xi Jinping's call, made during a visit to the exhibition "Forging Ahead in the New Era", for the whole Party and people to stand firm in historical confidence and strengthen historical initiative. Li Hua argues that historical confidence rests on understanding history: the more fully the historical process is grasped, the more initiative the Party has over the future.

The article is organised around three sources of the Party's historical confidence, each tied to one Chinese character: Marxism "works" (xing), the Communist Party "can" (neng), and socialism with Chinese characteristics is "good" (hao). It moves from the modern failure of Western doctrines in China, through a periodised account of the Party's record, to the achievements of the new era.

Li's first claim is that Marxism is the source of this confidence. After the Opium War, reformism, liberalism, social Darwinism, anarchism, pragmatism and other imported doctrines were tried and failed; the October Revolution brought Marxism-Leninism, and the Party's adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times has led China from "standing up" through "becoming rich" to "becoming strong". Second, Li reviews four periods: new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. The article credits each with historic breakthroughs, including national independence, the basic socialist system, the rise to the world's second-largest economy, and the first centenary goal. Third, Li presents socialism with Chinese characteristics as the practical expression of that confidence, citing industrialisation completed in decades, the elimination of absolute poverty, and Chinese modernization as a path that, in the author's account, rejects capital-centred, polarising and expansionist Western models.

Li concludes that the Party's confidence rests on its achievements, its capacities and its fighting and self-reforming spirit, and ultimately on a commitment to the people's wellbeing, national rejuvenation and human progress. The piece cites Xi's statement that the Party, state and nation have the most reason to be confident. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the 2022 official discourse on historical confidence was framed for a general newspaper readership on the eve of the Congress.
quoteEn: The Party's historical confidence is confidence in the great achievements the Party has won through struggle, and in the Party's outstanding capacities and fighting spirit.
quoteZh: 我们党的历史自信，就是对党取得的伟大奋斗成就的自信，是对党的卓越能力、奋斗精神的自信。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in Party discourse around the 20th Party Congress, meaning confidence in the Party's historical path and record, grounded in its reading of history.
A term in Party discourse meaning acting proactively and consciously, on the basis of grasping historical laws, to shape the future.
The official name for China's path of modernization, presented by the Party as distinct from Western models.
The official designation of the Party's theory, path and system since the reform era.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: Always at the forefront of the cause of the Party and the people
st: Commemorating the 120th anniversary of the birth of Peng Zhen
zh: 永远站在党和人民事业的最前线
zhSub: 纪念彭真同志诞辰120周年
authors: Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 12 October 2022, the 120th anniversary of Peng Zhen's birth, this commemorative article from the Party's central history and documentation institute presents Peng (1902–1997) as a proletarian revolutionary, a staunch Marxist and the chief founder of socialist legality in New China. Its thesis is that he spent his whole life at the forefront of the Party's and the people's cause, and that his career offers lasting lessons for Party members today.

The article is organised chronologically in four sections. The first follows Peng from a poor peasant family in Shanxi through Party organising in Taiyuan and Tianjin, imprisonment, work in the north during the War of Resistance, the Jin-Cha-Ji base area, the Yan'an rectification movement and the Northeast. The second covers the early People's Republic, when Peng sat on the Secretariat and led Beijing for 17 years. The third covers the period after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), when he headed the legal and legislative work of the National People's Congress Standing Committee. The fourth draws lessons.

In the article's account, Peng's most important contributions were in Party building, in Beijing's development and above all in law. It credits him with ideas on keeping the Party free from corruption, on collective leadership and democratic centralism, and on the people's congress system. It reports that between 1979 and 1988 he oversaw 88 laws and 35 legal decisions, drafted the preface to the 1982 constitution revision, and promoted standing committees of local people's congresses, competitive elections and direct elections to county level. It also credits him with directing the trial of the Lin Biao and Jiang Qing cliques, and notes that he suffered persecution during the Cultural Revolution.

The closing section draws four lessons, each tied to a statement by Xi Jinping: firm conviction and fidelity to the original aspiration, a people-first public-servant outlook, seeking truth from facts, and an enterprising spirit. The article calls on readers to rally around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core and to greet the 20th Party Congress (2022) with practical action. Read the original if you want an official Party-history portrait of Peng Zhen and an example of how the Party's central history institute presents a revolutionary leader's legacy for current political purposes.
quoteEn: His revolutionary spirit and lofty example have set up a spiritual monument for the whole Party and for the people of all ethnic groups across the country.
quoteZh: 他的革命精神和崇高风范，为全党和全国各族人民树立起一座精神丰碑。

glossary.explanation: The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining discussion and election with binding obedience to higher bodies and majority decisions. The article cites Peng as stressing it alongside collective leadership.
China's basic political system, in which congresses at each level elect or appoint state organs and the National People's Congress is the highest organ of state power.

t: Liu Shaoqi's reflections on socialist construction in China
st: Centred on his speeches at the study and discussion meetings on the Soviet Political Economy textbook
zh: 刘少奇对我国社会主义建设的思考
zhSub: 以《在苏联〈政治经济学教科书〉学习讨论会上的发言》为中心
source: Documents of the Party (Dang de wenxian), 2022 no. 4
paras: Ma Huiyi examines what Liu Shaoqi said about socialism in the study and discussion meetings on the Soviet Political Economy textbook (third edition), which he organised in November 1959. Mao Zedong had urged officials to read the textbook from late 1958 in order to correct the 'Leftist' errors of the Great Leap Forward and the people's commune movement. Ma argues that Liu, reading the textbook critically against Chinese realities, deepened the Party's understanding of 'what socialism is and how to build it'.

The article is organised in three parts, followed by a short conclusion. It first sets out Liu's account of the basic features of socialist society, then his view of the essence and purpose of socialist construction, and finally the methodological principles he advanced for exploring a distinctively Chinese path. Ma draws mainly on Liu's speeches, later published in a volume on China's economic construction, and places them against the experience after the Eighth Party Congress (1956).

On socialist society, Ma reports that Liu defined it as a lower stage of communism that still bears marks of the old society. Its four features are planned, proportionate development, in which speed and proportion are a unity of opposites; public ownership as the main body, retaining forms such as money and commodities to be used and eventually discarded; distribution according to labour, combined with political and ideological work rather than reliance on 'material incentives'; and attention to relations among working people, especially between leaders and led. On the essence of construction, Liu is said to have treated it as the continual handling of contradictions between productive forces and relations of production, with relations adjusted consciously, and as aiming at the free all-round development of people in step with social development. On method, Ma highlights three points: Soviet and Chinese experience each have both universal and particular aspects; errors are possible and must be corrected promptly; and principle must be combined with flexibility.

Ma concludes that these ideas deepened the Party's understanding of the laws of socialist construction and laid an intellectual basis for later exploration of the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article stresses Liu's method of linking theory with practice. Read the original if you want a detailed, Party-history account of Liu Shaoqi's critical reading of the Soviet textbook, with extensive quotations from his speeches.
quoteEn: Liu Shaoqi held that, in improving relations among working people, "capitalism cannot solve these problems, whereas we can take the initiative to solve them, and this is precisely the superiority of socialism".
quoteZh: 刘少奇认为，改善劳动者之间的相互关系，“资本主义不能解决这些问题，我们能主动地解决这些问题，这正是社会主义的优越性”。

glossary.explanation: The 1958 campaign for rapid industrial and agricultural growth, which the Party later acknowledged produced serious Leftist errors and economic imbalance.
The 1958 drive to merge agricultural cooperatives into large rural communes combining economic and administrative functions.
The socialist principle that individuals receive income in proportion to the labour they contribute, in contrast to distribution by need under communism.

The 1956 congress of the Communist Party of China, which judged that the main domestic contradiction was no longer between the working class and the bourgeoisie and set an economic line of steady advance.
The official name for China's socialist path since reform and opening up, presented as socialism adapted to Chinese conditions.

keywords: productive forces and relations of production

t: Chinese modernization offers important lessons for the world
zh: 中国式现代化具有重要启示意义
paras: This short commentary, first published in People's Daily on 10 October 2022, argues that Chinese modernization carries significant lessons for other countries. Opening with Xi Jinping's list of its five features, Wen and Wang present it as supplying a Chinese theory and a Chinese approach that other countries can draw on.

The piece is organised as a series of claims, each beginning with a feature of Chinese modernization and ending with the lesson the authors draw from it. They address modernization theory, the pace of development, the relation between growth and distribution, international relations, and the relation between traditional and modern civilization.

On theory, the authors contend that the West has long held discursive dominance and that many scholars equate modernization with Westernization. In their account, Chinese modernization shows that modernization is not a single-choice question, and that its theory fully surpasses capital-centred Western theory. They also say that, unlike the Western 'serial' sequence, China pursued industrialization, informatization, urbanization and agricultural modernization in parallel. On distribution, they say it first makes the 'cake' bigger and then divides it through institutional arrangements, in pursuit of common prosperity.

The authors conclude that Chinese modernization breaks the myth that modernization means Westernization. They hold that it gives developing countries a new perspective, path and model, and that it creates a new form of human civilization under Marxist guidance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party press presented Chinese modernization's international significance just before the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Modernization is not a single-choice question: the diversity of historical conditions determines the diversity of the development paths countries choose, and that diversity in turn determines the diversity of modernization theories.
quoteZh: 现代化不是单选题，历史条件的多样性决定了各国选择发展道路的多样性，各国选择发展道路的多样性又决定了现代化理论的多样性。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's development path, which Party texts present as distinct from Western models. It is described by five features: huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony with nature, and peaceful development.
A goal of shared affluence for all the people, described in Party texts as an essential requirement of socialism. It has been given renewed emphasis in policy since the early 2020s.

keywords: a community with a shared future for mankind

t: Persisting in advancing the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization
zh: 坚持以中国式现代化推进中华民族伟大复兴
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 11 October 2022, this commentary by Chen Shuo and Guo Guangyin takes up Xi Jinping's instruction, given at a study session for provincial and ministerial leaders, that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation must be advanced through Chinese modernization. The authors argue that Chinese modernization is socialist modernization led by the Communist Party. In their account, the Party's leadership, the socialist direction and the goal of national rejuvenation are what make the path both distinctive and sustainable.

The piece is built in three parts, each opening with a statement by Xi Jinping. The first treats Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee of Chinese modernization. The second treats socialism as its fundamental direction. The third presents national rejuvenation as its goal. The authors frame the discussion by the achievements of the decade since the 18th Party Congress (2012), which they describe as historic and as making rejuvenation an irreversible process.

On leadership, Chen and Guo argue that the Party gives modernization a firm leading core, keeps it on the correct course and sustains its vitality. For the last point they cite full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform. On socialism, they set Chinese modernization against Western modernization, which they describe as capital-centred, polarising, materialistic and expansionist. They credit Chinese modernization with a people-centred approach, common prosperity, all-round human development and a path of peaceful development, and they cite poverty alleviation and a moderately prosperous society as evidence.

On national rejuvenation, the authors say China was drawn passively into a Western-led modernization after the modern era began. They conclude that the search for a modern path has always carried a double meaning, modernization and rejuvenation. They describe the Party as holding to this mission through successive theoretical and practical innovations, and they cite the two-step plan to build a modern socialist country by mid-century. They also point to the spiritual drive that the mission provides. They conclude that continuing on the chosen path will build China into a great modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary linked Chinese modernization, socialism and national rejuvenation just before the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: China's exploration of a path to modernization has, from the very beginning, carried the dual meaning of achieving modernization and achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 我国对现代化道路的探索，从一开始就具有实现现代化和实现中华民族伟大复兴的双重内涵。

glossary.explanation: A Party concept presenting China's path to modernization as distinct from Western models. It was elaborated especially after the 18th Party Congress and formally set out at the 20th Party Congress (2022).

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal. It refers to restoring China's strength and international standing after the historical humiliations of the modern era.
A goal of shared wealth for all, presented as an essential requirement of socialism. It has been stressed in Party policy under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's drive since 2012 to tighten discipline, fight corruption and strengthen internal oversight.
An official phrase for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems and renew itself. It is presented as the means by which the Party leads wider social change.

t: A typology and stage theory of modernization, and Chinese modernization
st: Also on how Chinese modernization responds to the predicaments of Western modern civilization
zh: 现代化类型学、阶段论与中国式现代化
zhSub: 兼论中国式现代化对西方现代文明困境的回应
paras: Yang Dian takes up two questions in this short piece, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in August 2022: whether modernization is the same as Westernization, and whether it is a one-off state or an evolving process. Taking a global-sociology perspective, Yang proposes a typology and a stage theory of modernization. The article argues that modernization is not Westernization and that Western leadership is not permanent.

The piece first sets out two roads and five types of modernization, then three historical stages. It next applies this framework to the origins, distinctive features and eight characteristics of Chinese modernization. It closes by listing predicaments of Western modern civilization and seven ways in which China's path is said to respond to them.

Yang divides capitalist modernization into market-led, state-led and coordinated types, and socialist modernization into the Chinese and Soviet types. Yang contends that socialist modernization suits latecomer countries better, because it eases the tension in capital's dual nature and supplies a strong government able to pursue catch-up. In the stage theory, industrialization and urbanization (led by Britain) gave way to informatization, globalization and financialization (led by the United States). A third stage, built on artificial intelligence, is in Yang's account now contested by China and the United States, so non-Western countries may lead later stages.

Yang concludes that Chinese modernization is theoretically and practically viable and offers "Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach" for going beyond Western-centred, one-model views of modernity. The proposed responses include whole-process people's democracy, curbing the disorderly expansion of capital, common prosperity, green development and a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how a Chinese sociologist frames modernization theory to support the case for Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Modernization is not a static, once-and-for-all state, but a constantly evolving, dynamic process.
quoteZh: 现代化并不是一个一劳永逸的静止状态，而是一个不断演化的动态过程。

glossary.explanation: A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019, describing China's political system as democratic across every stage of governance, not only at elections. Official sources contrast it with Western electoral democracy.
A long-standing socialist goal that Xi Jinping has stressed since 2021, referring to prosperity shared by all and a narrower wealth gap.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, promoted since 2012–13, calling for cooperation and shared development among nations.
The official description of China's path to modernization under Communist Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse from 2021–22 and presented as an alternative to Western models.

t: What is new about the Chinese path to modernization
zh: 中国式现代化道路新在哪里
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 10 October 2022, just before the 20th Party Congress, Huang Qunhui asks what is new about the path of Chinese modernization. Huang argues that it fits China's realities, reflects the laws of socialist construction and of human social development, and comprehensively surpasses Western modernization theory.

The short commentary opens with Xi Jinping's formulation of a new path and a new form of human civilization. It then proceeds through four themes: the people-centred development philosophy, the use of national conditions to shape modernization's driving mechanism and strategy, exchange and mutual learning among civilizations, and the path of peaceful development.

Huang contends that Chinese modernization follows the general laws of industrialization, marketization and globalization but rejects the Western logic of subordinating productive forces to capital, which the author associates with polarization, materialism and external plunder. Instead, it pursues common prosperity and the coordinated development of five civilizations. Huang credits the socialist market economy, which combines an effective market with an effective government and curbs the "reckless expansion" of capital, along with phased strategic planning. The author also contrasts Western views of a "clash of civilizations" and a "strong countries seek hegemony" logic with China's promotion of civilizational mutual learning and its pledge never to seek hegemony.

Huang concludes that China's experience shows a late-developing country can achieve leapfrog development by independently exploring a path suited to its own conditions. Against a backdrop of what the article calls great changes unseen in a century, it presents China's initiatives as offering the world "Chinese wisdom" and solutions. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Chinese modernization was contrasted with the Western model on the eve of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Chinese modernization has abandoned the logic, followed by Western modernization, in which the development of productive forces simply serves capital.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化摒弃了西方现代化所遵循的生产力发展单纯服从于资本的逻辑

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept of China's own path to modernization, stressed from the 20th Party Congress (2022) onwards and presented as distinct from the Western model.
A goal of shared affluence for all, presented officially as an essential requirement of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

t: The Seventh Party Congress and the great victory of the New Democratic Revolution
zh: 党的七大与新民主主义革命的伟大胜利
source: Ideological and Theoretical Education Guide (思想理论教育导刊), 2022 no. 9
paras: Writing in 2022, Yang Fengcheng asks how the Seventh National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party, held in Yan'an in 1945, contributed to the final victory of the New Democratic Revolution. The article argues that the Congress secured that victory in three ways: it drew on the Party's historical experience, it established Mao Zedong's leadership and Mao Zedong Thought as the guiding ideology, and it set out a sound strategy for post-war China.

The article has three main parts. The first places the Congress in the whole history of the New Democratic Revolution. It traces the repeated postponements from 1937 onwards and the way the Party reviewed its past errors, through the rectification movement and the 1945 Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party. The second part examines the Congress's endorsement of Mao as leader and of Mao Zedong Thought. The third turns to the political line, the peasantry, Party leadership, cadres, and the 'two transformations'. Yang draws on speeches by Liu Shaoqi, Zhang Wentian, Zhou Enlai, Ren Bishi, Zhu De, Chen Yun, Peng Zhen and others.

Yang argues that the long delay had an unintended benefit: the Party had by then gathered experience from the War of Resistance and could set the lessons of its earlier detours against the way to victory. By moving the review of Party history to the Sixth Central Committee's Seventh Plenum, the leadership kept the Congress focused on present tasks and avoided prolonged settling of old scores. Yang reads the delegates' endorsement of Mao as resting on comparisons of correct and mistaken lines. Liu Shaoqi's report defined Mao Zedong Thought as the unity of Marxism-Leninism with Chinese revolutionary practice. On strategy, Yang stresses the peasantry as the main force, the independence of the Party within the united front, cadre unity and self-criticism, and the shift of work from countryside to city and from guerrilla to mobile warfare. Yang treats the last as the key military and political plan for victory, and describes Party maturity as both 'soft power' and 'hard power'.

Yang concludes that the Seventh Congress ensured the victory of the New Democratic Revolution by summing up historical lessons, establishing Mao's position and Mao Zedong Thought, and making correct decisions on Party building and strategic transitions. The article closes with the hope that Party congresses in the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics will, like the Seventh, become new milestones. Read the original if you want a detailed, document-based account of the Seventh Congress as presented in Chinese Party-history scholarship, with many quotations from delegates' speeches.
quoteEn: The Seventh Congress's most important contribution to the victory of the New Democratic Revolution was to establish Mao Zedong as leader of the whole Party and the core of the Central Committee, and Mao Zedong Thought as the Party's guiding ideology, laying the foundation for that great victory.
quoteZh: 党的七大对于新民主主义革命的胜利，最重要的贡献在于确立毛泽东的全党领袖、党中央核心地位，确立毛泽东思想作为党的指导思想，为新民主主义革命的伟大胜利奠定了根基。

glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's term for the Chinese revolution of roughly 1919–1949, led by the proletariat and the Communist Party against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism, as a stage before socialism.
The Party's term for the adaptation of Marxism-Leninism to Chinese conditions, written into the Party constitution as its guiding ideology at the Seventh Congress in 1945.

glossary.literal: correcting the style of work campaign
glossary.explanation: A Party-wide campaign from 1941–45 centred in Yan'an, aimed at overcoming dogmatism and sectarianism and unifying ideas under Mao's leadership.

glossary.zh: 关于若干历史问题的决议
glossary.pinyin: guānyú ruògān lìshǐ wèntí de juéyì
glossary.en: Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party
glossary.explanation: A resolution approved in principle at the Seventh Plenum in 1945 and formally adopted in 1945. It assessed the Party's past line struggles, especially the 'Left' errors of the early 1930s.
The strategic ideas discussed at the Seventh Congress: shifting from dispersed guerrilla warfare to mobile warfare, and moving the Party's centre of work from countryside to cities.

t: The Yan'an Rectification Movement and strengthening the Party's centralized and unified leadership
zh: 延安整风与加强党的集中统一领导
paras: This article, originally published in Guangming Daily on 12 October 2022, asks how the Yan'an Rectification Movement (1941–1945) was linked to the strengthening of the Chinese Communist Party's centralized and unified leadership during the War of Resistance against Japan. Tan argues that this strengthening was a historical necessity and a core outcome of the movement. In Tan's account, it laid an ideological and political foundation for victory in the War of Resistance and in the democratic revolution.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out why strengthening unified leadership reached the historical agenda. The second traces the central decisions of 1941–1943. The third examines how the policy was applied in the Northwest Bureau and the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region. Tan draws on Party directives, speeches by Mao Zedong, Ren Bishi, Wang Jiaxiang and Chen Yun, and regional documents.

Tan names four reasons for the policy. These were the surviving subjectivism and sectarianism, including the mountain-top mentality (shantouzhuyi) Mao criticised in 1944. They were also the harsher conditions behind enemy lines, the mistaken view that the "three-thirds" system made Party presence unimportant, and the weak coordination among Party, government, army and mass organizations. The key documents are the 1941 decision on strengthening Party spirit and the 1 September 1942 decision on unifying Party leadership in the base areas. The latter holds that the Party should lead all other organizations, that lower levels must obey higher ones, and that Party leadership should be a matter of principle and policy, not interference in every detail. Tan adds that leadership cores were set up at military-region level, and that the 1943 reorganization made Mao chairman of the Politburo and the Secretariat.

In the Northwest Bureau, Tan reports, the policy was applied to mass organizations, Party broadcasting, relations with the army and the salt industry. By the end of 1943 the border region had achieved positive results. Tan notes that Party control of the army and financial departments was still weak, and that some government bodies still stressed government-system unity. The bureau responded with continued education, tighter organizational control and a stronger Party grip on overall affairs. Read the original if you want a documented account of how the Party's centralized leadership system was built in Yan'an and applied in the Border Region.
quoteEn: Strengthening the Party's centralized and unified leadership became an inevitable choice for Party building and development.
quoteZh: 加强党的集中统一领导成为党的建设与发展的必然选择

glossary.explanation: An ideological and organizational campaign within the Chinese Communist Party, launched in 1941–1942 and lasting to about 1945. It targeted subjectivism, sectarianism and "Party formalism" (stereotyped Party writing) and consolidated Mao Zedong's leadership.

A principle for the anti-Japanese base-area governments from 1940. Communists were to hold no more than one third of seats, with the rest going to non-Party progressives and middle-of-the-road figures.
The 1942–1943 principle that a single Party committee leads all work in a base area, including government, army and mass organizations. It is also rendered as "monistic leadership".
A term for factionalism rooted in the separate revolutionary base areas, where groups put local or group loyalties above Party unity.
The Central Committee decision on unifying Party leadership in the anti-Japanese base areas and adjusting relations among organizations. It was adopted on 29 August and issued on 1 September 1942.

t: The essential attributes of the path of Chinese modernization and its contemporary concerns
zh: 中国式现代化道路的本质属性和当代关切
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 27 September 2022, this commentary asks what defines the path of Chinese modernization and what concerns it addresses today. Xu Ping and Yu Miao argue that the path shares general features of modernization but is distinguished by Chinese attributes. Its essential attributes, they hold, are Party leadership and socialism.

The article has three parts. The first defines modernization as the historical shift from traditional to modern society and sets out the two essential attributes. The second identifies three practical features that set the Chinese path apart from Western modernization: independence, rootedness in local history and culture, and a people-centred character. The third turns to the contemporary meaning of the path, drawing on Xi Jinping's account of its distinctive features and on the new development philosophy.

The authors present Communist Party leadership as the decisive factor in the path and as its fundamental political advantage. Socialism, in their account, is its institutional basis and basic direction, so that Chinese modernization seeks to unite a high level of modernization with socialism. They say this surpasses capitalist modernization and discards the older Western routes of capital-centred, polarising, materialist and expansionist modernization. On the three features, they argue that independence follows from the historical choice between dependence on the West and self-reliance, citing Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. They say local roots come from Chinese civilization and the path's own evolution, and that the people-centred character follows from Marxist theory and the Party's founding mission.

The authors conclude that the path, defined by Xi Jinping as modernization of a huge population, of common prosperity, of material and cultural-ethical advancement, of harmony between humans and nature, and of peaceful development, is a logical framework for coordinated progress. They claim it has widened the routes open to developing countries and offers a new choice to states that want faster development while keeping their independence. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official Chinese discourse in 2022 framed the Party's leadership, socialism and the new development philosophy as the core of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: The essential attributes of the path of Chinese modernization are Party leadership and socialism.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化道路的本质属性是党的领导和社会主义

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Communist Party leadership, which Party documents present as distinct from Western models. It was elaborated especially from the 20th Party Congress (2022).
A policy framework put forward by Xi Jinping in 2015 and centred on innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, presented as a defining feature of socialism and given new emphasis under Xi Jinping.

t: The rich connotations and significance of the path of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化道路的丰富内涵与意义
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in September 2022, asks what the path of Chinese modernization contains and why it matters. He Degui argues that the path, explored by the Party from "industrialization" and the "four modernizations" to Chinese modernization, shares features with other countries' modernization but carries distinct Chinese characteristics. In He's account it has produced a "new form of human civilization" that goes beyond Western modernization.

The piece has three parts. The first describes the path's nature and its link to the Party's century of struggle. The second sets out the characteristics of the new form of human civilization. The third assesses the practical, historical and theoretical significance of the path.

He contends that the path rests on the Party's leadership, mobilises the state, the market, society and the people, and aims at developing the productive forces, common prosperity and all-round human development. The new form of civilization is said to stress shared development, openness and inclusiveness, and a shared human destiny. He presents it as having overcome ills attributed to Western capitalist modernization, such as wealth polarisation and class conflict, and as having broken the idea that modernization means Westernization.

He concludes that the path widens the routes to modernization open to developing countries and shows socialism with Chinese characteristics to be a successful road. In He's view it also ends the "end of history" thesis and the "failure of socialism" thesis, and advances the adaptation of Marxism to Chinese conditions. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official 2022 narrative links Chinese modernization to the idea of a new form of human civilization.
quoteEn: The path of Chinese modernization has overcome the various ills of the developed Western capitalist countries, broken the myth that modernization equals Westernization, and created a new form of human civilization that goes beyond Western modernization.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化道路克服了西方发达资本主义国家的种种弊病，打破了现代化就是西方化的神话，创造了超越西方现代化的人类文明新形态。

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernization, stressed from the 20th Party Congress (2022) onwards. It is presented as distinct from the Western model.

A phrase used in official discourse, notably in Xi Jinping's 2021 speech on the Party's centenary. It describes the civilization said to arise from Chinese modernization, in contrast to the Western model.
A goal of socialism in Party discourse, meaning prosperity shared by all. It has been given new emphasis under Xi Jinping.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism since the reform era.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Why Mao Zedong called the Rectification Documents a "classic"
zh: 毛泽东为何称《整风文献》为经书
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theory, 2022 no. 6
paras: In November 1942, speaking to a conference of senior cadres in north-west China, Mao Zedong described the documents used to rectify the Party's "three work styles" as "a classic" (jingshu). Hu Weixiong notes that scholars have paid little attention to why he said so. Existing studies discuss editions and contents, and some, influenced by foreign scholars, hold that the collection contains no Marxist classics. Hu argues that the choice and arrangement of the texts show the collection to be a classic of Party-building, and that it marks a milestone in the development of Marxism in China.

The article first traces the editions: an 18-document version issued in April 1942, a revised edition of 22 documents in 1943, and a final set of 27 documents, which Hu takes as its object of study. It then sorts the 27 texts into four groups. These are rectification of the Party's style of work, of study and of writing; the training of Communists and Party organisation; Party leadership, cadre policy, inner-Party criticism and struggle, discipline and democracy; and the Party's mission, propaganda, leadership methods and Bolshevisation. Hu summarises the main texts in each group, including works by Mao, Liu Shaoqi, Chen Yun, Stalin, Dimitrov and Lenin.

Hu's central claim is that the collection's core is Mao's own work, above all \"Reform Our Study\", \"Rectify the Party's Style of Work\" and \"Oppose Stereotyped Party Writing\", with the preface to Rural Surveys. In Hu's reading, these texts demand that Marxism-Leninism be combined with the concrete practice of the Chinese revolution, and they attack subjectivism, dogmatism and sectarianism. Hu also argues that the whole is a coherent programme. Mao supplied the original theory, while the Soviet and Comintern texts and the Party's own decisions supplied standards for discipline, self-criticism and cadre selection. Hu places the collection beside two other reading sets used in rectification, and presents it as a Marxist study campaign aimed at the dogmatism associated with Wang Ming.

Hu concludes that rectification matured the Party and prepared its transformation into a modern party at the Seventh Congress (1945). He also holds that the principle of uniting theory with practice and seeking truth from facts applies to Marxist parties generally. Hu cites a 1943 letter in which Mao said that only some of the rectification documents, not his thought as a system, should be promoted. Read the original if you want a detailed, text-by-text account of what the Rectification Documents contained and how Party historians present their role in the Yan'an rectification campaign.
quoteEn: Rectification aimed to eliminate the Party's own bad styles of work and strengthen Party building, so that the Party could become a great party truly armed with Marxist-Leninist theory.
quoteZh: 整风是为了整掉党自身的不良作风，加强党的建设，使我们党能成为一个真正用马克思列宁主义理论武装起来的大党

glossary.explanation: The Party-wide campaign launched in Yan'an in 1942 to correct dogmatism, sectarianism and formulaic writing, and to unify the Party under Mao Zedong's leadership.
Mao's term, drawn from the rigid imperial examination essay, for empty, formulaic and jargon-laden Party writing and speech.
The Comintern-era idea of remodelling communist parties on the Bolshevik party, stressing discipline, theory and ties to the masses. Stalin's twelve conditions for it were studied in the campaign.
In Mao's usage, a way of thinking that ignores objective conditions. It covers both dogmatism (applying book formulas) and empiricism (relying on narrow experience).
The three targets of the 1942 campaign: subjectivism in study, sectarianism in Party work, and stereotyped Party writing.

t: Strengthening Party-building leadership to empower rural construction
zh: 强化党建引领 赋能乡村建设
paras: This commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2022, asks how rural construction can be carried through to the modernization of the countryside. Wu and Peng argue that Party building must run through the whole effort. In their view, ensuring that the Party "takes overall charge and coordinates all sides" in rural work is the key to success, and they set out three forms of leadership: ideological, organisational (through personnel) and capacity-based.

The piece is organised under these three headings. The first covers how Party members, cadres and villagers should understand rural construction. The second covers four groups: township cadres, the village two committees, resident work teams and local talented people. The third covers three capacities that the authors say grassroots Party organisations need.

On ideological leadership, the authors say cadres should study Xi Jinping's statements on agriculture, rural areas and farmers. They should see rural construction as important, arduous and long-term, and should mobilise villagers into a mechanism of Party leadership, self-governance and peasant participation. On personnel, they call for wider recruitment of township cadres, training for the village Party branch and village committee, and stronger Party membership among returning entrepreneurs, young people and graduates. They also want resident teams to coordinate with village leaders and local talents to be drawn in and cultivated. On capacity, they propose better mobilisation, including digital tools, farmers' participation in decisions, consultative village governance, and emergency response that prevents risks early.

Wu and Peng conclude that these measures would give rural construction a firm political guarantee and activate its endogenous drive. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-building language is applied to rural governance and cadre training in 2022.
quoteEn: Ensuring that the Party always takes overall charge and coordinates all sides in rural work, and provides a strong political guarantee for rural construction, is the key to its success.
quoteZh: 确保党在乡村工作中始终总揽全局、协调各方，为乡村建设提供坚强有力的政治保障，是乡村建设成功的关键。

glossary.explanation: The village Party branch committee and the villagers' committee, the self-governing body elected by villagers. Their relationship is a recurring concern in rural governance.
Teams of cadres sent by higher-level organisations to live and work in villages, used in poverty alleviation and rural revitalisation.
Shorthand for agriculture, the countryside and farmers, treated in official discourse as a core policy field.
A national programme, with an Implementation Plan issued in 2022, to improve rural infrastructure, public services and living conditions.

t: "Harnessing capital" and the path of Chinese modernization
zh: “驾驭资本”与中国式现代化道路
paras: Xi Ge, in a short commentary first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2022, asks how the path of Chinese modernization should treat capital. The author argues that its distinctive character lies in sublating and going beyond the Western, capital-centred road to modernization. The key issue, in Xi's account, is understanding capital's characteristics and laws of behaviour and learning to "harness" it.

The piece presents itself as a call to Marxist theory and the philosophy and social sciences to study these questions in connection with General Secretary Xi Jinping's speech of 17 May. It has two main parts. The first sets out what Marxist theory must clarify about capital; the second takes up the rational harnessing of capital as a frontier issue and a practical task.

Xi argues that going beyond capital-centred modernization does not mean abandoning capital. It means using and controlling capital to serve socialist modernization, developing its positive role while restraining its negative effects. Capital has a dual character as a relation of production and as means of production. Its "logic" brings contradictions: valorization dominating the labour process, social polarization, commodity fetishism and expansionist hegemony. Harnessing it therefore means following capital's laws of motion and using the superiority of the socialist system, so that socialist relations of production direct capital towards socialized productive forces and all-round human development.

Xi concludes that Chinese modernization can create a new form of human civilization because it consciously applies and develops Marxist principles, especially the theory of capital. Through this the path is said to be rooted in China's particularities while offering universal demonstration value and world-historical significance. Read the original if you want a compact statement of how Chinese theorists frame the "harnessing capital" formula within Marxist theory.
quoteEn: Going beyond capital-centred modernization does not mean completely negating or abandoning capital, but making rational use of and controlling capital so that it serves the development of socialist modernization.
quoteZh: 超越以资本为中心的现代化，并不是要彻底否定或抛弃资本，而是要合理地利用和控制资本为发展社会主义现代化服务。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from the Western model. It was elaborated especially after the 20th Party Congress in 2022.
The Chinese rendering of Hegel's and Marx's Aufhebung: overcoming something while retaining some of its elements in a higher form.

t: Mao Zedong's firm resolve in upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee during the revolutionary war years, and his major contribution
zh: 毛泽东在革命战争年代维护党中央权威的坚定意志及其重要贡献
source: Studies on Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping Theories, 2022 no. 5
paras: Zheng Zhiqiang takes up a question the author says earlier scholarship handled mostly in broad narrative: how Mao Zedong upheld the authority of the Party Central Committee during the democratic revolution. The article argues that the turn from danger to victory in the Chinese revolution cannot be separated from Mao's defence of that authority. In Zheng's account, Mao showed firm resolve from the early years and became an outstanding example of loyalty to centralised, unified Party leadership.

The article follows Mao through three periods. The first runs from Jinggangshan to Ruijin, the second from the founding of the Soviet-area Central Bureau to the early Long March, and the third from the Zunyi Conference to the eve of the People's Republic. A final section distils lessons. Zheng frames the study as relevant to the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds.

In the first period, Zheng contends, Mao carried out the Central Committee's general line of armed struggle and land revolution. Where he disagreed, he did so through democratic centralism, discussion and voting, and through formal reports to the Centre. In the second period, when the Provisional Central Committee criticised his line and stripped him of military posts, Zheng argues that Mao kept to his views but accepted each reassignment for the sake of unity. The author sets this against Luo Zhanglong, Zhang Guotao and others who opposed the centre or split the Party. After Zunyi, Zheng says, Mao's core position was consolidated through the Sixth Plenum, the Seventh Congress and ideological work, including the Yan'an rectification, the stress on Party spirit and new Party regulations.

Zheng draws three lessons: a revolutionary party needs strict discipline and a Central Committee with authority; it must follow the mass line and carry out investigation so that its line is correct and can be transmitted downwards; and it must practise criticism and self-criticism. The article closes by linking these lessons to the Party's centenary, the new stage of development and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and calls for stronger Party history education. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of Mao's conduct toward the Central Committee from the Jinggangshan base through the Seventh Congress, including the specific conferences and personnel decisions Zheng cites.
quoteEn: Mao Zedong did not stick to convention; he combined scientific theory with concrete practice and boldly worked out the correct methods of upholding the authority of the Party Central Committee, making an important contribution to the victory of the New Democratic Revolution.
quoteZh: 毛泽东不是墨守成规，而将科学理论与具体实践相结合，大胆探索出维护党中央权威的正确方法，为新民主主义革命走向胜利作出重要贡献。

glossary.explanation: A formulation from the Party's 2021 historical resolution and the 20th Party Congress (2022). It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the Party's core and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
A Party requirement to uphold Xi Jinping's core position in the Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party: free discussion followed by binding unity of action, with lower bodies subordinate to higher ones.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term national goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping since 2012, of restoring China's national strength and international standing.
A Party-wide campaign of study and criticism in 1941–45, aimed at dogmatism and sectarianism, which consolidated Mao Zedong's ideological leadership.

t: The image of the hero in Mao Zedong's poetry
