The official formula, adopted in 2017, for a shift from fast growth to growth stressing quality, structure and balance.
The Party's official judgement that China is in an early, long-lasting phase of socialism, used to justify a mixed ownership economy and gradual goals.
The policy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented reforms and opening China to foreign trade and investment.

t: Era characteristics of the Party's leadership in building a modern economic system
zh: 党领导建设现代化经济体系的时代特征
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 27 January 2022
paras: This short commentary, published in January 2022, asks how the Communist Party of China has led the building of a modern economic system and what distinguishes that leadership in the current era. Fu and Zhao argue that the Party has combined long-term strategic design with responses to immediate conditions. In their account, it first set the framework through supply-side structural reform and the new development philosophy, then added new content and a yardstick by linking the project to the new development paradigm.

The article is organised in two parts. The first examines the top-level design set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017): high-quality development as the theme, supply-side structural reform as the main line, and the new development philosophy as the theoretical base. The second turns to the new development stage and the new development paradigm of "dual circulation", drawing on the 14th Five-Year Plan and the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee. The authors lean throughout on the 2021 Party resolution on history, the 19th Congress report and statements by Xi Jinping.

In the first part, Fu and Zhao list five features of the Party's leadership: long-term planning paired with short-term breakthroughs, theoretical innovation guiding practice, comprehensive and coordinated advance, solid and effective concrete policies, and drawing on foreign experience while keeping Chinese characteristics. In the second part, they argue that the new development paradigm serves as the macro-level guide and objective standard for the modern economic system. They say it makes expanding domestic demand the strategic anchor, makes smooth domestic circulation an urgent requirement, calls for better investment structure, and requires balancing development with security. They describe the relationship as "upholding fundamentals and innovating": the Party keeps its core line while extending the practical standards and overall layout as conditions change.

The authors conclude that the modern economic system is a long process within the broader goal of a modern socialist country. They say the Party's centralised, unified leadership over economic work lets it plan ahead while grasping the principal contradiction of the day. They present this leadership as a core element of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era's economic thought and as the precondition for national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a compact statement of the official rationale linking the modern economic system, supply-side reform and dual circulation.
quoteEn: The new development paradigm is the macro-level guide and objective standard for building a modern economic system.
quoteZh: 新发展格局是现代化经济体系建设的宏观指引和客观标准。

glossary.explanation: A concept put forward at the 19th Party Congress (2017) for an integrated economy of high-quality development, innovation, coordination and openness. It is presented as a strategic goal of the shift from rapid growth to high-quality development.

An economic policy line launched around 2015 that aims to improve the quality of supply and fix structural imbalances in the real economy. It includes the "three cuts, one reduction, one improvement" measures.
The five principles of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, set out in the 13th Five-Year Plan period and used as guidance for economic policy.

A strategy with domestic circulation as the mainstay and domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other ("dual circulation"). It stresses expanding domestic demand and was written into the 14th Five-Year Plan.
The official theme of China's economic development since the 19th Party Congress, emphasising quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.

t: Grasping the value implications and practical significance of putting the people at the centre
zh: 深刻把握以人民为中心的价值意蕴和现实意义
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in June 2022, starts from a line in the Party's 2021 historical resolution. The line says the Party has sought happiness for the Chinese people, rejuvenation for the Chinese nation, progress for humanity and "great harmony" for the world. Zheng argues that this formulation expresses the Marxist people's standpoint and the principle of putting the people at the centre. The author says it should be studied through its value implications and practical significance.

The article takes the four aims in turn: the people, the nation, humanity and the world. For each it names a corresponding goal and cites Xi Jinping's statements and Party history. It then discusses how the four relate to one another and ends with China's international role.

Zheng links the aims to concrete programmes. Seeking happiness for the people means pursuing common prosperity. Seeking rejuvenation for the nation means building a modern socialist country, with Chinese modernization traced from the Seventh Party Congress (1945) through Deng Xiaoping's three-step strategy to the present. Seeking progress for humanity means building a community with a shared future for mankind, and seeking great harmony means the Global Development Initiative and shared values of humanity. The author stresses that the four are an organic unity, so that serving humanity and the world also serves the people and the nation. Zheng presents this as drawing on Chinese tradition and on Marx and Engels's "association of free individuals".

Zheng concludes that China will take on more international responsibilities as its strength grows. The author says Chinese modernization has created a new form of human civilization and offers developing countries a fresh option. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party commentary ties domestic goals to its global vision in 2022.
quoteEn: Seeking progress for humanity and great harmony for the world also helps better secure happiness for the people and rejuvenation for the nation.
quoteZh: 为人类谋进步、为世界谋大同，也能更好为人民谋幸福、为民族谋复兴。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal that Xi Jinping has given new prominence since the 18th Party Congress. It stresses prosperity shared by all, with narrower regional and income gaps.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, set out in Party documents under Xi Jinping. It is presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, introduced around 2012–13. It calls for shared responses to global problems and has been written into several UN documents.
A proposal Xi Jinping put forward in 2021 for international cooperation on development, especially in support of the UN 2030 Agenda.
A classical Confucian ideal of a harmonious world in which "the world is shared by all". Party writing uses it to describe a world of common good.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: The sources of strength behind the Communist Party of China's centenary of achievement
zh: 中国共产党铸就百年辉煌的力量源泉
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in June 2022, Zhao Xiaohu and Mao Junji ask what explains the Communist Party of China's achievements over its hundred-year history. They argue that four forces, acting together, kept the Party at the forefront of its era: the power of belief, of theoretical innovation, of bold practice and of self-reform.

This is a short commentary with one section for each force, followed by a brief forward-looking passage. It draws on Xi Jinping's speech at the centenary of the Party's founding, the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, and statements by Mao Zedong.

On belief, the authors hold that the Party's ideals rest on Marxism, on the patriotic traditions of Chinese culture and on the aim of national independence and liberation; they link these to the spirit of the Party's founding. On theoretical innovation, they point to historical, political and theoretical self-awareness, a practical, reality-based style of thought, and the unity of innovation with theoretical education within the Party. On practice, they describe an unprecedented firmness, spirit of sacrifice and thoroughness, running from revolution through construction to reform and opening up. On self-reform, they follow the resolution in calling it what distinguishes the Party from others, rooted in its having no interests of its own. They add that Mao's answer, supervision by the people, and Xi Jinping's answer, self-reform, now combine internal and external discipline.

The authors conclude that, as the Party begins its journey toward the second centenary goal amid great changes unseen in a century, preserving these four forces will let it succeed in governing, building and strengthening itself under long-term rule. Read the original if you want a compact, officially aligned account of how Party writers explain the sources of its historical success.
quoteEn: An advanced Marxist party is not born that way; it is tempered through continual self-reform.
quoteZh: 先进的马克思主义政党不是天生的，而是在不断自我革命中淬炼而成的。

glossary.explanation: A term in Party discourse for the Party's capacity to correct its own errors and discipline itself. It has been stressed in official texts since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.en: the spirit of the Party's founding
glossary.explanation: A formulation first summarised by Xi Jinping on 1 July 2021. It names the founders' commitment to truth, ideals, original mission, sacrifice and loyalty to the Party and people.
The official aim of building China into a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

t: Injecting new impetus into the innovative development of excellent traditional Chinese culture
zh: 为中华优秀传统文化创新发展注入新动力
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily on 6 June 2022, asks how excellent traditional Chinese culture can be given fresh momentum. Wang Zhenzhong builds on Xi Jinping's remarks at the 39th collective study session of the Political Bureau, where Xi called traditional culture the "root and soul" of the Chinese nation. Wang argues that its creative transformation and innovative development should proceed by upholding fundamental principles while innovating, and by fusing tradition with scientific culture.

The piece has three parts. It first lists the values Wang finds in traditional culture, from harmony between humans and nature to ethics, self-improvement, people-based governance, national unity and peaceful international relations. It then treats transformation and development as a systematic project that needs top-level design and workable methods. It ends with a call to remain guided by Marxism.

Wang's central claim is that traditional culture is open, inclusive and developing rather than fixed. In Wang's account, it evolves with its society and grows by absorbing and exchanging with other cultures. Wang names integration with scientific culture as an important route, citing the 14th Five-Year Plan's emphasis on science and technology. Concretely, Wang proposes carrying forward the tradition's esteem for innovation, bringing scientific spirit (seeking truth from facts, respect for laws of nature) and modes of thinking (dialectical, empirical, deductive) into its renewal. The two are described as mutually reinforcing, since scientific culture can in turn draw wisdom from tradition.

Wang concludes that, under Marxist guidance and Xi's directives, traditional culture will show greater vitality. It will offer insight for understanding and changing the world, for state and social governance and for moral development, and will help build Chinese spirit, Chinese values and Chinese strength. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 framed tradition, science and Party guidance together.
quoteEn: It should be recognised that excellent traditional Chinese culture, formed through sedimentation over the long course of history, is not unchanging but open, inclusive and developing, and its content is always enriched as the times advance.
quoteZh: 应当认识到，在历史长河中积淀形成的中华优秀传统文化并非一成不变，而是开放的、包容的、发展的，其内涵总是随着时代的发展而丰富发展

glossary.zh: 创造性转化和创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A formula in official discourse for reworking traditional culture so that it fits contemporary society. It has been widely used in Party documents since the mid-2010s.

glossary.literal: preserve what is correct and innovate
glossary.explanation: An official principle holding that innovation must proceed while maintaining the Party's basic orientation and principles.

t: The Communist Party of China and the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 中国共产党与中华民族伟大复兴
paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 29 June 2022, Ren Lixuan asks why the Communist Party of China (CPC) alone could take on the task of national rejuvenation, and what that task has meant across the Party's history. Ren answers by citing Xi Jinping's statement that without the Party there would be no new China and no rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article argues that the Party has fundamentally reversed the fate of the Chinese people since the modern era and is moving irreversibly towards rejuvenation along the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The commentary has three parts. The first sets out four reasons why only the CPC can carry the historic mission: scientific theory, an unchanging founding mission, reliance on the people, and self-reform. The second presents rejuvenation as the single theme of all the Party's struggles, sacrifices and creations over a century. The third looks ahead and tells the Party to take charge of the "four greats": great struggle, great project, great cause and great dream. It closes by linking the Chinese Dream to a community with a shared future for mankind.

Ren holds that earlier political forces and ideologies failed because they lacked scientific theory and did not understand the strength of the people. By contrast, Ren credits the Party's adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, culminating in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Ren also credits its refusal to pursue any special interest. Ren answers the question of how the Party escapes the historical cycle of rise and fall with self-reform, presented as a second answer after Mao Zedong's appeal to supervision by the people. Ren also points to Party leadership, full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and the Two Establishes as guarantees. Sacrifice is illustrated by the figure of more than 3.7 million named martyrs between 1921 and 1949.

Ren concludes that China is closer than ever to rejuvenation, but must expect harder struggles, including the pressures of trade friction with the United States and the pandemic, which Ren says will last until the second centenary goal. The article calls for the Two Upholds, the Four-sphere Confidence, high-quality development and common prosperity, and presents rejuvenation as a boost to human progress. Read the original if you want an authoritative example of how the Party's leadership framed its historical mission and its tasks in mid-2022.
quoteEn: The fundamental reason the Party emerged from repeated contests among political forces in modern times, won the people's trust and achieved major successes is that it held to its original aspiration as firmly as a rock and pursued its mission without wavering.
quoteZh: 我们党之所以能够在近代以后各种政治力量反复较量中脱颖而出，赢得人民信任、取得重大成就，根本原因就在于党秉持初心坚定如磐、履行使命矢志不渝。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, often called the Chinese Dream. It means restoring China's wealth, power and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.

A formulation from the 6th Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). It affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and the Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement that Party members firmly uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The post-2012 Party-building policy of strict discipline, including the anti-corruption campaign.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of shared interests and joint global governance.
A stated goal of prosperity shared by all, which the Party presents as a defining feature of socialism.

t: The distinctive regional features of the anti-Japanese war behind enemy lines in South China
zh: 华南敌后抗战呈现鲜明地域特色
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in June 2022, asks what set the anti-Japanese war behind enemy lines in South China apart from that in North and Central China. Guo Lu argues that the region's rivers, coast, overseas-Chinese ties and border position gave it clearly regional characteristics.

The article first notes that after Japan occupied Guangzhou in October 1938, soldiers and civilians led by the Communist Party built several bases, including Dongjiang, Qiongya and Wuguishan, known together as the South China anti-Japanese base areas. It treats these as one of the three main fronts behind enemy lines. It then examines three features in turn: maritime guerrilla warfare, mobilisation of overseas Chinese and Hong Kong and Macao compatriots, and support for Allied operations.

On the first, Guo says South China forces used mountain and plain guerrilla tactics common elsewhere, and also developed maritime guerrilla warfare, citing Mao Zedong's 1938 remarks on rivers and coasts. Examples include the Dongjiang Column's sea units near Daya Bay and Dapeng Bay, which attacked Japanese transport with wooden sailing boats and home-made explosives, and the 'Sea Eagle' unit at the Pearl River estuary. On the second, the author lists returnees joining guerrilla units, more than thirty home-service groups and donations of money and supplies. On the third, Guo reports the rescue of 89 foreign friends from Hong Kong, the rescue of nearly 40 American and British airmen in 1944–45, and a joint intelligence station with US forces.

Guo concludes that South China's forces achieved good results in all three areas and strongly supported the worldwide anti-fascist war. Read the original if you want a brief, example-based overview of how geography shaped the Communist-led resistance in Guangdong and its links to Hong Kong and the Allies.
quoteEn: Shaped by these regional factors, the war behind enemy lines in South China showed some distinct regional characteristics.
quoteZh: 受这些地域因素的影响,华南敌后抗战呈现出一些鲜明的地域特色。

t: The threefold identity of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化的三重身份特质
paras: Chen Fulong asks what shapes the path of Chinese modernization and why it differs from Western modernization. The article, a short commentary first published in China Social Sciences Today in June 2022, answers that three identities together form its basic character: socialist country, developing country and emerging country. Chen argues that these identities determine the model and path of Chinese modernization, which is therefore planned within both "China in the world" and "China's world".

The commentary is organised in three sections, one for each identity, with a short closing summary. It draws on Marx's remarks on the world market and the modern history of capital, on passages from Xi Jinping and the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017), and on examples from Latin America, West Asia and North Africa. It also looks at the two world wars as episodes of shifting power among rising and established states.

On the first identity, Chen contends that modernization began in the West on a capitalist basis, but that this historical priority gives capitalism no moral priority and no exclusive claim to the means of realising modernization. Chinese modernization, in this reading, goes beyond capital-centred logic, puts the people first, joins efficiency with fairness and aims at common prosperity. On the second, the author cites the "two unchanged" judgments (China remains in the primary stage of socialism and is the largest developing country) and argues that "modernization equals Westernization" is a prejudice. Countries that copied Western models, such as Argentina, Brazil, Peru and Chile, are said to have met similar internal contradictions. Developed countries modernised in "serial" fashion, while developing ones must compress industrialisation, informatisation, urbanisation and agricultural modernization into a "parallel" process. On the third, Chen argues that China has risen through interaction and cooperation, not through expansion or colonialism. As part of a collective rise of emerging and developing countries, it is said to push toward a more multipolar and equitable order.

Chen concludes that the three identities show Chinese modernization to be a distinctive socialist "Chinese version" that dissolves the "modernization equals Westernization" narrative. The author presents it as offering Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach to problems facing humanity, and as helping to build a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese official scholarship frames the international and developmental identity of Chinese modernization in 2022.
quoteEn: Socialist country, developing country and emerging country form the underlying identity of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 社会主义国家、发展中国家、新兴国家构成了中国式现代化的身份底色

glossary.explanation: The official Party concept for China's own path to modernization, elaborated especially after the 20th Party Congress (2022). It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The Party's official judgment, since 1987, that China is still in an early stage of socialist development. It is used to justify market reforms and a long-term developmental focus.
A long-standing socialist goal, revived in recent Party discourse, of prosperity shared by all rather than widening wealth gaps.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept, promoted since 2012–13, calling for joint global governance and shared development.
A formula from the 19th Party Congress report (2017) stating that China's stage of socialism and its status as the largest developing country remain unchanged.

t: Unswervingly following the path of Chinese modernization
zh: 坚定不移走中国式现代化道路
paras: This commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today on 26 May 2022, asks what it takes to keep to the path of Chinese modernization. Qin Qiang argues that the path must be pursued by linking the overall strategy for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation with the "great changes unseen in a century". It rests on four elements: the new development stage, the new development philosophy, the new development pattern and high-quality development.

The piece follows the sections headed historical position, source of momentum, key link and essential requirement. It draws on the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), which stated that the Party has opened a Chinese modernization path and created a new form of human civilisation.

Qin reads the new development stage as the move from \"standing up\" and \"becoming prosperous\" to \"becoming strong\". The stage is also one in which the principal contradiction is between people's growing needs for a better life and unbalanced, inadequate development. The new development philosophy of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing is presented as the source of momentum. Qin says it has shifted the economy from asking whether something exists to asking whether it is good. The new development pattern is called the key link. It is described as a proactive move, not a stopgap: open dual circulation, built on a unified national market, with domestic demand as the basic driver.

Qin concludes that the four elements form one logical whole. The stage defines the historical position, the philosophy gives direction, the pattern sets strategic priorities, and high-quality development is the fundamental purpose. Together they are said to guide the building of a modern socialist country and a new form of human civilisation. Read the original if you want a short, official-style account of how Party discourse in 2022 linked these four concepts.
quoteEn: Building the new development pattern is a proactive opening move, not a forced expedient; it is open dual circulation at home and abroad, not closed single domestic circulation.
quoteZh: 构建新发展格局是主动调整的先手棋，不是被迫的权宜之计；是开放的国内国际双循环，不是封闭的国内单循环

glossary.explanation: The Party's official term for China's own path to modernity, which it presents as distinct from Western models. It is used in Party documents and became a central slogan in 2021–22.

The official label for the period after the completion of a moderately prosperous society, aimed at basically achieving socialist modernization by 2035 and building a modern socialist country by mid-century.
The five concepts of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, first put forward at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2015).
The official strategy that takes the domestic economic cycle as the mainstay, with domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other ("dual circulation").
The official goal of shifting from fast growth to growth that stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A Party slogan for restoring China's national strength and international standing, linked to the Chinese Dream.

t: Paths for advancing the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
zh: 推进马克思主义中国化时代化的路径选择
paras: This short commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in April 2022, asks how the Party should continue adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Jiang takes as a starting point Xi Jinping's remark that Marxism is why the Party and socialism with Chinese characteristics succeed. Jiang presents theoretical innovation as one of the key lessons of the Party's century of struggle, drawn up at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021).

The piece briefly traces the sequence from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. It then sets out six requirements, each framed as a four-character maxim.

Jiang argues that adaptation must not abandon the Marxist "forefathers", meaning its stance, viewpoint and method. It must also draw on foreign achievements without wholesale Westernization, and read the major trends of the age. In addition, it must address China's actual conditions and practice, and draw on fine traditional Chinese culture through creative transformation. Jiang cites concepts such as a moderately prosperous society, a harmonious society and a community with a shared future for mankind as rooted in Chinese civilization. The last requirement is to distil the practical wisdom of the people, citing Deng Xiaoping on reform ideas originating with the masses.

Jiang concludes that the Party should keep to emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts and keeping pace with the times, and should answer the questions of the era and the people. The aim is to open new horizons for contemporary Marxism in China and twenty-first-century Marxism. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official 2022 account of how Marxism is to be "sinicized" and kept current.
quoteEn: The adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context must be grounded in China's national conditions and oriented to Chinese practice; otherwise one cannot speak of "Sinicization" at all.
quoteZh: 马克思主义中国化，必须立足中国国情、面向中国实践，否则就谈不上“中国化”。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The Party's formula for applying Marxist principles to Chinese conditions and updating them for the present era. The addition of "时代化" gained prominence in the Party's 2021 history resolution.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept, adopted in the early 2000s, stressing people-centred, coordinated and sustainable development.
Jiang Zemin's theory, which holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the interests of the overwhelming majority.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world order based on shared interests and cooperation.
A goal rooted in the classical Confucian term xiaokang, adopted by Deng Xiaoping as a target for China's development.

t: The Chinese Communist Party's exploration of governing the Party through institutions
zh: 中国共产党制度治党的探索历程
paras: This newspaper commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in May 2022, traces how the Chinese Communist Party has developed "governing the Party through institutions". Chi defines this as a system of intra-Party regulations that adjusts relations within the Party and between the Party, the state and society. The author argues that understanding of this approach deepened over more than a century of struggle, and that it has become an important support for preserving the Party's vanguard character.

The article follows four periods. It begins with the New Democratic Revolution, then moves to socialist revolution and construction, the era of reform and opening up, and finally the new era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). For each period Chi cites key documents, Party congresses and statements by leaders from Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping to Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping.

In Chi's account, the early Party built rules to unite revolutionary forces: the concept of intra-Party regulations was articulated, the Party constitution was refined, and the 7th Congress (1945) systematised democratic centralism. After 1949 the Party tried to combine ideological education with discipline, and the 8th Congress (1956) advanced institutional rules, though the author concedes that broad consensus and lasting mechanisms did not form. Reform-era leaders, Chi says, raised institution-building to a central place. Since 2012 the Party has set the goal of a fairly complete system of intra-Party regulations, and the author reports more than 3,600 such regulations in force by July 2021. Chi also lists the "seven focuses" guiding further improvement, including full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

Chi concludes that ideological and organisational Party-building must be combined with institutional governance, and that political discipline should be strengthened as the foundation. The author calls institutional governance the Party's "unique code", an expression of why Marxism and socialism with Chinese characteristics work, and claims it offers a useful reference for party governance worldwide. Read the original if you want a concise official-style historical outline of how Party regulations are framed in Chinese Party-building discourse as of 2022.
quoteEn: Governing the Party through institutions is the Chinese Communist Party's unique code, reflecting the self-confidence, self-reflection and self-reliance of a responsible major party that has lasted a hundred years.
quoteZh: 制度治党是中国共产党的独特密码，体现出一个负责任大党延续百年的自信、自省与自力

glossary.explanation: A term in Party-building discourse for managing the Party through formal intra-Party regulations and systems, alongside ideological and organisational Party-building.
Formal rules issued by the Party, including the Party constitution, guidelines, regulations and measures, that govern Party organisations and members.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining discussion and collective decision with centralised, unified discipline.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party-building programme promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012), stressing strict discipline and anti-corruption work.

t: The world-historical contribution of the "new form of human civilization"
zh: “人类文明新形态”的世界历史贡献
paras: Wu Hongzheng takes up the Party's claim, made in Xi Jinping's speech at the centenary of the Communist Party (2021) and in the Party's 2021 historical resolution, that socialism with Chinese characteristics has created a "new form of human civilization". The article asks what world-historical contribution this form makes. Its thesis is that it makes four: it develops Marx and Engels's theory of world history, it holds the commanding height in the "great changes unseen in a century", it leads the trend toward a community with a shared future for mankind, and it advances the world-historical course of scientific socialism.

The article opens with a conceptual account of the new civilization form, built from five spheres (material, political, spiritual, social and ecological) and five defining attributes. It then devotes one section to each of the four contributions, drawing on Marx and Engels's writings on world history, on Hegel's philosophy of history, on Huntington's "clash of civilizations" and on Wolfgang Streeck's diagnosis of capitalism. The closing section places the concept within a periodisation of scientific socialism as "three 70-year periods" and ties it to the essential features of Chinese modernization.

Wu argues that the new form is socialist and therefore different from the capitalist civilization Marx called the most "barbarous". The author holds that it rests on the creative transformation of traditional Chinese culture and is a transitional form, since it arose while two systems coexist and has not reached communist civilization. Its outlook of "exchange and mutual learning" is set against Western-centrism, "universal values" and the clash-of-civilizations thesis. Wu reads this as extending Marx and Engels, who offered no concrete theory of how to build a new civilization, by showing that socialism can create one within a single country and before capitalism disappears. In the author's account, the capitalist order is in historical difficulty and an "East rising, West declining" trend is under way, so that this form gives a basis for a community with a shared future for mankind that capitalism's zero-sum logic cannot supply.

Wu concludes that the new form is not only "Chinese" but "human", adding new elements to the family of civilizations and carrying forward scientific socialism's aim of human freedom and liberation in the "third 70 years", when the author says the centre of world socialism lies in China. The article is a Party-theoretical interpretation that follows official documents closely. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist scholar links the official concept of a new form of human civilization to the Marxist theory of world history, the community with a shared future for mankind and the history of world socialism.
quoteEn: The new form of human civilization is a transitional civilization form that advances toward communist civilization under conditions in which two systems coexist.
quoteZh: 人类文明新形态是在两种制度并存条件下向共产主义文明形态前进的过渡性文明形态。

glossary.explanation: A formula used in Xi Jinping's speech at the Party's centenary in 2021 to describe the civilizational achievements of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It is presented as comprising material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing interdependence, cooperation and common interests. It has been promoted in Chinese diplomacy since the early 2010s.

glossary.pinyin: bǎi nián wèi yǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping has used since around 2017–18 to characterise the current shifts in the global balance of power and the international order.

Official term for China's path of modernization, whose stated features include a huge population, common prosperity, balanced material and spiritual civilization, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's theory, path and system since the reform era. It is presented as Marxism adapted to Chinese conditions.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Interpreting the Chinese path, stimulating discursive innovation
zh: 阐释中国道路 激发话语创新
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today in April 2022, Wang argues that China's growing place on the world stage requires close study of the relationship between the "Chinese path", "Chinese theory" and "Chinese discourse". Building theory and discourse on the basis of the path is described as an epoch-making, comprehensive theoretical undertaking, with significance for the Chinese nation and for world history.

The commentary has three sections. The first presents the Chinese path as a contribution to world civilization and cites growth figures from reform and opening up. The second takes up Chinese theory and its link to Marxism. The third addresses Chinese discourse and its place in international communication.

Wang contends that the path is the premise of theory: practice drives theoretical innovation, and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation needs its own theory. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is presented as a theory of national strength and as an original contribution to discourse. Chinese discourse is defined as the theoretical expression of the path. It should combine Chinese and foreign elements, drawing on Chinese tradition while learning from the West. The author says Chinese modernization has broken the West's monopoly over the terms "modernization" and "civilization".

Wang calls on Marxist scholars to build disciplinary, academic and discourse systems with Chinese characteristics, and to offer solutions for a community with a shared future for mankind. Wang expects Chinese theory and discourse to reshape international communication and to support countries that want development while keeping their independence. Read the original if you want a short example of how official scholarship links Chinese modernization to the project of building Chinese discourse.
quoteEn: Chinese discourse is in essence the theoretical expression of the Chinese path.
quoteZh: 中国话语本质上是中国道路的理论表达

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own route to modernization, stressed in Party documents since the early 2020s as distinct from Western models.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world of shared interests and joint governance.

t: The ideological foundations of the spirit of self-reform
zh: 自我革命精神的思想底蕴
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 April 2022
paras: This short commentary asks what intellectual resources lie behind the Chinese Communist Party's insistence on self-reform, which the 2021 resolution on the Party's century of struggle lists as one of ten historical experiences. Wen argues that the Party's persistence in self-reform draws on the deep substance of Marxism, and that this can be seen in three of Marxism's features: its scientific and truthful character, its popular and practical character, and its openness and timeliness.

The article opens with the claim that courage in self-reform is the Party's most distinctive trait and greatest strength. It credits the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) with strengthened capacities for self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-elevation, a reversal of laxity in Party governance, and an overwhelming victory in the anti-corruption struggle. Three sections then take each of the Marxist features in turn, ending with a look at the present international setting.

On the first feature, Wen cites Marx and Engels's 1850 Address of the Central Authority to the League and Lenin's endorsement of self-criticism as foundations for a proletarian party's self-reform, and presents Xi Jinping's systematic remarks on its meaning and methods as continuing them. On the second, Wen argues that self-reform must target the problems the masses complain of most, and that the people's interests are its standard. The author links this to Marxism's practical orientation towards changing the world, and describes the post-1949 move from campaign-style governance to institutional thinking, together with the successive Party education campaigns since 2012. On the third, Wen holds that self-reform is an open, developing system, and that it has enabled the Party to escape the historical cycle of rise and fall.

Wen concludes that on the new "road to the examination" of building a modern socialist country, the Party must treat itself as a special object of revolution, which the author calls the hardest and highest-level kind. Doing so, the article says, is the key to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and to meeting the risks of the pandemic, international conflict and the "great changes unseen in a century". Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 grounded the Party's self-reform in Marxist classics and the discourse of Xi Jinping.
quoteEn: The key to realising the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation lies in building the Party itself well.
quoteZh: 实现中华民族的伟大复兴，关键在于把党自身建设好。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping, in which the Party identifies and corrects its own errors and impurities. It is presented as the Party's distinctive strength and a core historical experience.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal, closely tied to the Chinese Dream and to building a modern socialist country by mid-century.

glossary.en: historical cycle of rise and fall
glossary.explanation: A phrase associated with a 1945 exchange between Mao Zedong and Huang Yanpei about how regimes rise and decline. Party writers say the Party avoids it through self-reform and popular supervision.

t: Deepening the "Two Integrations" on the new road of the examination
zh: 深化“两个结合” 走好赶考之路
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2022, Dong Yanfang takes up the resolution on the Party's century of struggle adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). The resolution calls for combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. Dong argues that these Two Integrations must be deepened as the Party leads the people towards the second centenary goal, which the article calls a new "road of the examination".

This short commentary is organised around four areas in which the Two Integrations are to continue: putting the people first, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, achieving common prosperity, and promoting human progress. Each section pairs a Marxist source, such as the Communist Manifesto, Marx's 1857–58 manuscripts or Engels, with classical Chinese texts including the Book of Documents, the Book of Songs and the Book of Rites.

Dong's central move is to present Marxist principles and Chinese tradition as pointing the same way in each area. Min-ben (people-as-foundation) thought is set beside the Manifesto's "movement of the immense majority". The Chinese ideals of renewal, shared wealth and "all under heaven belongs to all" are set beside Marx on production aimed at the wealth of all. Dong credits this approach for the Party's success and for Chinese modernization. The article also holds that absolute poverty has been resolved, which it says lays the base for common prosperity.

Dong calls for policy to rest on the people's approval, for continued innovation alongside established achievements, for narrowing regional, urban–rural and income gaps, and for peaceful, mutually beneficial development that builds a community with a shared future for mankind. The aim is to write a new chapter of twenty-first-century Marxist theory of international relations. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the Two Integrations are presented in official-academic commentary on the Party's historical resolution.
quoteEn: The code to the success of the Communist Party of China's century of struggle lies in upholding Marxist standpoint, viewpoint and method while, in response to our "specific problems", forging the path of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 中国共产党百年奋斗成功的密码就在于既坚持马克思主义的立场、观点、方法，又针对我们的“具体问题”，走出了中国式现代化道路。

glossary.explanation: The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities and with its fine traditional culture. The second element was added in the Party's 2021 historical resolution.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, described by the Party as distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given new emphasis in Party policy from 2021.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing cooperation and shared interests among countries.
A metaphor associated with Mao Zedong in 1949, who likened the Party's task of governing to sitting an examination. It is now used for each new stage of the Party's mission.

glossary.literal: the people are the foundation of the state
glossary.explanation: A classical Chinese political idea, from the Book of Documents, that the people are the root of the state. The Party cites it as a traditional source for its people-centred stance.

t: The essentials and advantages of the new path of Chinese modernization
zh: 中国式现代化新道路的要义与优势
paras: Writing in the China Social Sciences Today in December 2021, Wang Heng asks what is "new" and what is "good" about the path of Chinese modernization, a path Xi Jinping presented at the Party's centenary celebration. Wang argues that it can be grasped by comparing it with Western modernization, and that it differs from that model in four ways.

The short commentary is organised as four numbered claims, each pairing a defining feature of Chinese modernization with a shortcoming Wang attributes to the Western path. It closes with a brief statement of the path's significance for China and for developing countries.

First, Wang calls it socialist modernization. Capitalist modernization, driven by surplus-value extraction, is said to produce alienation, polarisation and social atomisation, while the socialist path is people-centred, aims at common prosperity and can concentrate resources on major undertakings. Second, it is scientific development: comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable, in contrast with Western materialism, consumerism and the "pollute first, clean up later" route. Third, it is peaceful development. Wang contends that Western powers built modernity on colonial plunder, whereas China pursues win-win openness and a community with a shared future for mankind, rejecting the logic that a strong state must seek hegemony. Fourth, it is independent: no single universal model exists, so each country must find a path suited to its own conditions.

Wang concludes that the path belongs to China and to the world. It is described as the necessary road to national rejuvenation and as offering developing countries a wider range of routes, a "Chinese approach" to modernization. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned statement of how Chinese modernization was contrasted with Western models in late 2021.
quoteEn: But there is more than one road to modernization, and there is no single correct universal model or standard answer.
quoteZh: 但现代化的道路不止一条，不存在唯一正确的普遍模式或标准答案。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization under Party leadership. It is presented as distinct from Western models, and Xi Jinping applied it to the Party's centenary narrative in 2021.
A long-standing socialist goal, stressed under Xi Jinping, of prosperity shared by all rather than concentrated in a few hands.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for China's vision of international relations based on cooperation and shared interests.
Drawn from the Scientific Outlook on Development, a Party guideline that stresses comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable growth.

glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, usually rendered as the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

t: Establishing a correct view of Party history through systems thinking
zh: 以系统思维树立正确党史观
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2021, ahead of the Party's centenary, Shi Shiyue takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the mobilisation meeting for Party history study and education, to "establish a correct view of Party history". Shi argues that this requires systems thinking, and that Party history is a systematic, innovative and practical history. The article treats such thinking as a way to raise Party members' ability to understand what that history means.

The short commentary is organised around four attributes of systems thinking: wholeness, dynamism, hierarchy and openness. Each gets its own section, covering the value of Party history as a whole, its four periods, its record of governance across several fields, and its orientation towards the future.

On wholeness, Shi presents the century as a history of struggle and sacrifice, citing revolutionary martyrs such as Li Dazhao and later figures such as Wang Jinxi and Jiao Yulu. In the author's account, this history carries traditional virtues and also the values of the Party's self-reform, innovation and putting the people first. On dynamism, Shi divides the century into four periods: New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article describes these as moves from standing up, to growing rich, to growing strong. On hierarchy, it surveys achievements in politics, the economy, culture and ecological civilization.

On openness, Shi points to the elimination of absolute poverty as the first centenary goal. The article says the Party will now pursue the second centenary goal of building a modern socialist country, guided by the experience and spirit contained in Party history. Shi concludes that learning from history should shape the daily practice of every member and citizen. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-school commentary frames the 2021 Party history study campaign through a four-part systems schema.
quoteEn: The history of the Communist Party of China is a developmental history rich in systematicness, innovativeness and practicality.
quoteZh: 中国共产党党史是一部富有系统性、创新性和实践性的发展史。

glossary.en: a correct view of Party history
glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping first used at the Party history study and education mobilisation meeting in February 2021. It calls on Party members to interpret Party history in line with official assessments.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

glossary.pinyin: liǎng gè yìbǎi nián fèndòu mùbiāo
glossary.explanation: Two official targets: a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021, and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.
An official term for the Party's capacity to correct itself and maintain discipline from within.

t: Tracing and reflecting on Chinese modernization from a century-long perspective
st: A scientific understanding of the Sixth Plenum's judgement on the historical significance of the Party's century of struggle
zh: 百年视野下中国式现代化的溯源与思考
zhSub: 科学理解十九届六中全会关于百年奋斗历史意义的科学论断
paras: Writing in 2022, Hou Weimin asks how the Communist Party's century of struggle should be understood through the lens of Chinese modernization, taking as its guide the resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). Hou argues from historical materialism that Chinese modernization is the outcome of accumulated historical energy, confirms the objective laws of social development, and demonstrates the necessity and practical truth of the socialist road.

The article has five sections. It begins with the accumulated conditions behind Chinese modernization's starting point, then turns to its convergence with national rejuvenation, to its unity with the Marxist theory of practice, to its fit with a new form of human civilization, and finally to its link with Party leadership. Hou draws on the Resolution, Marx, Engels, Mao Zedong and Xi Jinping, and on Western figures such as Huntington, Weber, Marcuse and Macron. Hou also cites GDP, poverty-reduction and trade figures.

Hou's central claim is that Chinese modernization departs from the Western model, which the author characterises as marked by war, plunder and instability. Four features are said to follow: peaceful rise, long-term stability alongside rapid growth (which Hou presents as refuting Huntington), active opening up, and a changed international position. Hou holds that public ownership as the main body of the economy and the socialist market economy explain this success, and that earlier non-Marxist modernization schemes in China failed. Chinese modernization is described as the third landmark shift in world history favourable to socialism, after the October Revolution and the 1949 revolution. Hou says it also creates a new form of human civilization that rebuts Weber's claim that modern capitalism belongs to the West.

Hou concludes that Party leadership is the decisive condition of this path. The argument is that socialism, unlike earlier social formations, begins with scientific theory and so needs a vanguard party with no interests separate from the people's. Hou contrasts India's slower modernization as the result of lacking such a party. Hou also credits Party leadership with keeping the socialist market economy under public ownership, supporting common prosperity and reducing poverty. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese economist reads the 2021 Resolution to present Chinese modernization as an alternative to capitalist modernization and as a stage in world socialism's history.
quoteEn: The key reason China has been able to surpass the Western model of modernization is that it has upheld the socialist principle of public ownership as the main body of the economy.
quoteZh: 中国之所以能够超越西方现代化模式，关键在于坚持了公有制为主体的社会主义原则。

glossary.explanation: Official term for China's own path to modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from the Western model. It became a central slogan in Party discourse from 2021–22 onward.
Official goal of shared prosperity for all, stressed by the Party especially since 2021.

t: Raising philosophical thinking and grasping the direction of development
st: A study of General Secretary Xi Jinping's philosophical wisdom and major practice
zh: 提高哲学思维 把握发展方向
zhSub: 关于习近平总书记的哲学智慧和重大实践的学习研究
paras: This commentary, first published in the China Social Sciences Today in March 2022, starts from the Party's tradition of studying and applying philosophy. Zhou and Huang note that General Secretary Xi Jinping has repeatedly urged leading cadres to study Marxist philosophy, so as to improve their strategic thinking, ability to make comprehensive decisions and ability to manage the overall situation. The authors argue that Xi's work in Fujian Province offers concrete examples of a series of philosophical modes of thinking applied to practice.

The piece is organised under nine headings, each naming a mode of thinking: strategic, historical, dialectical, innovative, rule-of-law, bottom-line, systems and precision thinking. Each section opens with a definition and a quotation from Xi, and then lists, usually in three or four numbered points, examples from his years in Fujian. These cover posts in Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningde and at provincial level, with cases such as the Digital Fujian and Ecological Fujian initiatives, the Jinjiang experience, collective forest tenure reform and poverty reduction in eastern Fujian.

The authors' central move is to read each local initiative as the application of a specific philosophical method. Under dialectical thinking, they cite Xi's use of the image of water dripping through stone to explain the law of the transformation of quantity into quality, and his use of the 'two-sided' and 'key-point' approaches in planning eastern Fujian's development. Under systems thinking, they describe the 'six constant principles' of the Jinjiang experience as six subsystems forming a whole, and the 'one-building office' as an example of the whole being greater than the sum of its parts. Under rule-of-law thinking, they point to integrity regulations for officials in Ningde and the innovation of forest-rights mortgage loans. Under precision thinking, they describe fieldwork in Junying village and the 'Three Heroic Islands', where Xi is said to have prescribed measures matched to local conditions.

The authors conclude that Xi's reform exploration and practice in Fujian left a deep impression on local cadres and the public in thought, courage and sentiment. In their account, this has become a valuable spiritual resource and a driving force for continuing reform and development. The text is a short, example-driven account in the official idiom, and it presents Xi's practice as a model of applied philosophy for cadres. Read the original if you want to see how Chinese official commentary links Xi Jinping's early local work to a catalogue of philosophical thinking methods promoted for cadre study.
quoteEn: During his time working in Fujian, General Secretary Xi Jinping attached great importance to investigation and research at the grassroots, stressing that real problems are found by 'sinking down' to the base, and that measures must be precise and treat both symptoms and root causes, so that problems are handled scientifically and efficiently and things are done well.
quoteZh: 习近平总书记在闽工作期间，十分重视对基层的调研考察，强调要在“沉下去”中发现真问题，措施要精准到位，标本兼治，从而科学高效地把问题处理好、把事情办好。

glossary.explanation: One of the modes of thinking the Party encourages cadres to cultivate: far-sighted, big-picture judgement of overall trends and direction. The article treats it as the first of nine philosophical methods.

A summary of the development path of Jinjiang, a county-level city in Fujian, which Xi Jinping distilled in the early 2000s. It stresses the market, local strengths, integrity and a service-oriented government.

t: Leading social revolution with the Party's self-reform
zh: 以党的自我革命引领社会革命
paras: This commentary, published in the China Social Sciences Today in March 2022, takes up the strategic idea in the Resolution on the Party's centenary achievements and historical experience, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). That idea is that a great self-revolution should lead a great social revolution. Lü and Shi argue that the Party's self-reform is the precondition and the key for carrying forward the social revolution of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era.

The piece has three parts. It first sets out the close link between the two "revolutions" in the history of Chinese revolution and construction, and in the present. It then explains how self-reform guides the social revolution. Finally it proposes ways to advance and deepen self-reform, drawing throughout on quotations from Xi Jinping and Party documents.

The central argument is that the two revolutions are mutually reinforcing. In the authors' account, the Party's achievements come from advancing both its own construction and social change in the economy, politics, law, ecology and culture. In the new era, the authors say, the complex and sharp struggles of socialist construction demand a stronger Party, able to meet what they call the "four tests" and "four dangers". Self-reform is said to guide the social revolution in three ways. It secures the leadership foundation, by keeping the Party's purpose of serving the people. It supplies ideological guidance, through campaigns of concentrated education from the Yan'an rectification movement to the recent Party history study. And it forges a leading force in the "critical minority" of leading cadres, through anti-corruption work and the "five qualities" and "eight abilities" required of them.

The authors conclude that self-reform must be pursued comprehensively. They call for guidance from Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, and for full implementation of the general requirements for Party building set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017). They also propose concrete measures: strengthening political discipline through the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds, building a culture of integrity, encouraging cadres to take responsibility, and improving supervision mechanisms. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in early 2022 presented the link between Party building and social transformation.
quoteEn: The Party's self-reform helps ensure the people-centred character of the Party's purpose and provides a solid leadership foundation for better advancing the social revolution.
quoteZh: 党的自我革命有助于确保党的宗旨的人民性，为更好地推动社会革命提供坚实领导基础。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed under Xi Jinping: the Communist Party's continuous efforts to correct its own problems, enforce discipline and fight corruption. It is presented as the Party's distinctive quality and the means of sustaining its long-term rule.
A formulation from the Sixth Plenum (2021) that affirms Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Party Central Committee and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought.
The requirement that Party members firmly uphold Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
Official term for leading cadres, especially senior officials, whose conduct is seen as decisive for Party governance and therefore the focus of discipline campaigns.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.

t: Upholding the practical logic of theoretical innovation
zh: 坚持理论创新的实践逻辑
paras: This short commentary, originally published in the China Social Sciences Today newspaper on 31 March 2022, takes up one of the "ten upholds" in the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). Hui Zhaoyang argues that upholding theoretical innovation is a key reason for the Party's success, because a nation at the forefront of its age cannot do without theoretical thinking and correct guidance. In Hui's account, theory must develop with practice rather than harden into dogma.

The article is organised in three sections. The first sets out the vitality of Marxist theory and the innovation that each era requires, citing Engels, Lenin and Xi Jinping. The second traces the Party's century of practice-driven theoretical exploration through revolution, construction and reform. The third discusses how innovative theory guides practice and what is required for the future.

Hui's central move is to present Chinese Marxism as a sequence of theoretical achievements, each answering the major questions of its period. These are Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The article describes each as the product of combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete conditions, and, under Xi, with fine traditional Chinese culture. It credits them with successive leaps in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Hui further holds that Xi Jinping Thought is open in character, will keep being enriched in the Party's governing practice, and is distinguished by its popular character, practicality, timeliness, creativity and scientific rigour.

Hui concludes that, on the path to a modern socialist country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the Party must keep using Marxism to observe, grasp and lead the times. The first task, Hui says, is to study and master the Party's innovative theory so that it can be applied flexibly in new practice. Research on Xi Jinping Thought should rest on solid scholarship, be practice-oriented and take an international view, uniting learning with application. Practice and theoretical innovation, the article says, have no end. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated commentary in 2022 presented the lineage of theoretical innovation after the Resolution.
quoteEn: There is no end to the development of practice, and no end to theoretical innovation either.
quoteZh: 实践发展永无止境，理论创新也永无止境。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions and to each historical period. The "times" element was added to the older phrase "Sinification of Marxism" in recent years.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. Official texts present it as the latest stage of Marxism adapted to China.
The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, emphasising people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development. It was written into the Party constitution in 2007.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents the advanced productive forces, the advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, especially emphasised since 2012.

t: The threefold meaning of "walking our own path"
zh: “走自己的路”的三重意涵
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 31 March 2022
paras: This short commentary, published in China Social Sciences Today in March 2022, takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the Party's centenary celebration (2021) that "walking our own path" is the historical conclusion of a century of struggle. Gao argues that the phrase has three layers of meaning: socialism with Chinese characteristics is the correct path, independence and self-confidence must guide its advance, and comprehensive deepening of reform is the way to sustained development.

The article proceeds in three sections that match these meanings. It first looks back at failed late-Qing and early Republican attempts at national salvation, then at the Party's revolutionary and socialist history. It then turns to the spirit of independence and the Four-sphere Confidence, and finally to reform and opening up since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Gao contends that earlier reformers such as those of the 1898 Reform Movement and the 1911 Revolution failed because they copied foreign models rather than adapting world experience to Chinese conditions. In the new era, the author says, Chinese modernization rests on the coordinated development of the economy, politics, culture, society and ecology, which avoids treating modernization as merely industrial and instrumental. Gao presents independence and the Four-sphere Confidence as the means of keeping China's destiny in its own hands, and lists four principles for deepening reform: Party leadership, a people-centred approach, development as the first priority, and opening up.

Gao concludes that a country should judge its path by whether it resolves the historic tasks it faces, and that China's development achievements show socialism with Chinese characteristics to be a successful path. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official 2022 narrative links the centenary "historical conclusion" to reform and the Four-sphere Confidence.
quoteEn: In choosing which path to take, what matters for a country is whether that path can truly resolve the historic tasks the country faces.
quoteZh: 一个国家选择什么样的道路，关键要看这条道路是否能够真正解决这个国家所面临的历史性课题。

glossary.explanation: Official formula calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. It was set out under Xi Jinping.
The official name for China's governing system and development path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a socialist system and market reforms.
The official term for China's own model of modernization, stressed in Party documents since the 2021 centenary. It is presented as distinct from Western models.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: Continuing to carry forward the spirit of historical initiative through fearless responsibility and great struggle
zh: 在无畏担当和伟大斗争中继续发扬历史主动精神
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily in March 2022, takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the opening of the spring 2022 training course for young and middle-aged cadres at the Central Party School. Xu argues that Party members, especially leaders, must carry forward a "spirit of historical initiative" by taking responsibility and being willing to struggle. In Xu's account, only this can realise the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece first defines historical initiative as the Party's conscious, Marxist-guided effort to transform society on the basis of historical laws. It then surveys the Party's century of history, then turns to present-day shortcomings and the international setting of the early 2020s.

Xu's central claim is that responsibility and struggle reinforce each other: taking responsibility tempers the courage to struggle, and struggle shows the capacity to bear responsibility. The article says this pairing runs through the Party's history and its "spiritual lineage", from the Jinggangshan spirit to the anti-epidemic spirit. Xu criticises a minority of cadres who lack both qualities, who avoid major tasks or shy from taking a stand on questions of principle, and says this weakens the Party's fighting capacity.

Xu concludes that the Party faces growing risks amid what it calls great changes unseen in a century, protectionism and the pandemic. Cadres are urged to keep "the nation's most important interests" in mind, take the initiative in struggle and pass the spirit on. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party media framed cadre conduct and struggle after Xi's 2022 Central Party School speech.
quoteEn: Taking responsibility and struggle are a spirit, a responsibility and a breadth of vision.
quoteZh: 担当和斗争是一种精神，一种责任，一种格局。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in Xi Jinping's discourse for the Party's conscious and proactive shaping of history, based on grasping historical laws. It was widely promoted around the Party's 2021 centenary.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's central national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream.
The official term for the series of named "spirits" (such as the Long March spirit) that the Party presents as its founding values and historical sources of strength.

glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping and Party media to describe the shifting global order and intensifying great-power rivalry.

t: Daring to advance theoretical innovation on the basis of practice
zh: 勇于推进实践基础上的理论创新
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in March 2022, takes \"adhering to theoretical innovation\" as one of the main lessons of the Communist Party of China's hundred-year struggle. Xin Ming argues that it explains both how the Party led the nation from \"standing up\" to \"becoming prosperous\" and then \"becoming strong\", and why Marxism keeps its vitality. Xin's thesis is that theory must be tied to Chinese realities, answer the questions of the age and grow out of practice, so that Marxism is continually adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The article has three sections. The first traces the leaps in the adaptation of Marxism to China, from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development, to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The second sets these theories against the changing character of each era: war and revolution, then peace and development, then the present period of \"changes unseen in a century\". The third gives examples of how practice since the 18th Party Congress (2012) has produced new theory.

Xin's central claim is that Marxism has been applied in China through the Two Integrations: combining its basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. Each stage of theory, in this account, answered the main questions of its time, and the \"Ten Clarifications\" of the new-era thought are presented as a further deepening. Xin then stresses that practice is the source of theory, with examples ranging from the Jinggangshan base area to reform and opening up. For the current era, Xin links the thought's claims on Party leadership, the principal contradiction, whole-process people's democracy, common prosperity and ecological civilization to specific achievements of the past decade. The article also describes Chinese modernization as having created a new form of human civilization and offering other countries a new option.

Xin concludes that over a century the Party has kept theoretical guidance and practical exploration in dialectical unity. In this account, the interaction tests Marxism's scientific character and truth, and shows its popular, practical, open and time-bound qualities. The piece is an official-line statement of how theoretical innovation is understood in Party discourse in 2022. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's narrative links the stages of Marxism's adaptation to China with the era-specific questions each is said to have answered.
quoteEn: Practice is the source of theory.
quoteZh: 实践是理论之源。

glossary.explanation: The formula of combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was added in official discourse under Xi Jinping.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology since 2017, written into the Party and state constitutions.
An official summary of ten core propositions of Xi Jinping Thought, covering Party leadership, the main contradiction, reform, rule of law, the military, diplomacy and Party building.
An official term for China's democratic model, which the Party presents as covering every stage of political and social decision-making.
A Party goal of prosperity shared by all the people, emphasised in the Xi era.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Walking the new "examination road" well requires always preserving the unity and solidarity of the Party
zh: 走好新的赶考之路必须始终保持党的团结统一
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in March 2022, Sun Cunliang takes up the 2021 Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee. Sun builds on its statement that "ensuring the unity and solidarity of the Party is the Party's lifeblood". The article argues that, as the Party starts a new "examination road" towards the second centenary goal, keeping its unity is both the key to past success and the basic guarantee of future success.

The piece has three parts. The first reviews the Party's history, from the first Party constitution at the Second Congress, through the Zunyi Conference (1935) and the Yan'an rectification campaign, to the Eighth Congress, the reform era and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second sets out why unity remains fundamental on the new road. The third lists concrete means of keeping it.

In Sun's account, unity guaranteed each stage of achievement: new-democratic revolution, socialist construction, reform and opening up, and the new era. Looking ahead, Sun gives three reasons why unity is the "fundamental guarantee".
