It rallies all ethnic groups, citing Deng Xiaoping that national unity begins with the unity of the Party and especially its leadership core. It enables the Party to withstand growing external and domestic risks, including what Sun calls ideological bias abroad and economic downward pressure at home. It also allows strategic decisions in the interest of the whole Chinese nation, because in Sun's view the Party has no interests of its own. Sun then names four means: shared ideals and convictions, a tight organisational system, a strong body of members, and iron discipline.

Sun calls for study of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, for democratic centralism, and for upholding the Party centre's authority and Xi Jinping's core position through the Two Upholds. Sun also calls for grassroots organisation, strict political vetting of new members, opposition to factions and double-dealing, and strict enforcement of political discipline. Read the original if you want a concise statement, in the official Party-building idiom of 2022, of how unity and centralised leadership were framed as the condition for the Party's next stage of work.
quoteEn: Preserving the Party's unity and solidarity cannot depend on empty slogans; it requires concrete measures and concrete action.
quoteZh: 保持党的团结统一，不能靠空喊口号，而是要靠采取具体的举措，付诸具体的行动。

glossary.explanation: A formula from 2018 requiring Party members to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position in the Party Central Committee and the whole Party, and to uphold the authority and centralised, unified leadership of the Central Committee.

glossary.literal: new road of going to sit the exam
glossary.explanation: A metaphor derived from Mao Zedong's 1949 remark that the Party was "going to Beijing to sit the exam". Xi Jinping revived it to describe the Party's continuing tests in governing and national rejuvenation.
The goal of building China into a great modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic. The first goal was a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining democratic discussion with centralised decision-making and subordination of lower bodies and individuals to higher ones.

t: Understanding the deep meaning of "drawing on history to open up the future"
zh: 深刻认识和把握“以史为鉴、开创未来”的深厚意蕴
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 22 March 2022, explains what Xi Jinping's call to "draw on history and open up the future" involves. Sang Jianquan writes in the wake of the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), which summed up the Party's major achievements and historical experience over its first century. The author argues that the call can be grasped through three tasks: understanding historical laws, strengthening historical confidence, and taking the historical initiative.

The piece is organised under three headings that follow these tasks. The first covers the Party's understanding of the laws governing Communist Party rule, socialist construction and human social development. The second goes through confidence in the path, theory, system and culture. The third turns to the present context of global change and the Covid-19 pandemic.

On historical laws, Sang holds that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee has deepened understanding in each of the three areas. It has done so through full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, a revised assessment of the principal contradiction in society, the Belt and Road Initiative, a community with a shared future for mankind and Chinese modernization. On historical confidence, the author asserts that socialism with Chinese characteristics is the only correct path, that Marxism adapted to the Chinese context and the needs of our times has produced the guiding theories, and that the institutional system has proved effective. Culture is described as the basis of the other three forms of confidence. On historical initiative, Sang calls for grasping the main trends of history, locating China's position in the new era and the primary stage of socialism, and seizing opportunities. The author describes the period as one of strategic opportunity in which crisis and opportunity coexist.

Sang concludes that studying the Plenum's spirit and Xi's speeches will help the Party and people build a modern socialist country and achieve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The piece is an authoritative-style interpretation of the Plenum rather than a historical study. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the 2021 history resolution was presented to a general readership in Party media.
quoteEn: Only this path, and no other, can lead China forward, improve the people's well-being and achieve national rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 只有这条道路而没有别的道路，能够引领中国进步、增进人民福祉、实现民族复兴。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era for strengthening Party discipline, political building and the anti-corruption campaign.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's vision of international relations, stressing common interests and shared development.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.
A global infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013.
The official judgement that China remains at an early, underdeveloped stage of socialism, which will last a long time; it underpins the Party's basic line.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and international standing by the mid-twenty-first century.

t: Overseas studies of the Chinese Communist Party's revolutionary history in Chinese translation since reform and opening up: a review
zh: 改革开放以来海外中国共产党革命史研究译著评介
paras: This is a review of foreign scholarship on the Chinese Communist Party's revolutionary history before 1949, as it has reached Chinese readers in translation since reform and opening up. Zhang notes that domestic scholars have paid some attention to overseas studies of Party history but have not systematically surveyed the translated works on the revolutionary period. The article sets out to map these translations, identify their research hotspots and discuss how to deepen engagement with them.

The first part surveys translated works by period and theme: the Party's founding (1921–27), the Jiangxi Soviet period and the Long March, the War of Resistance against Japan, and the civil war. It then covers the Party's foreign contacts, the role of the Comintern and Soviet advisers, and general studies of the revolution and of Marxist historiography. A long section treats biographies of Mao Zedong, including two series of translated overseas Mao studies, and studies of Li Dazhao, Qu Qiubai, Zhou Enlai, Deng Xiaoping and others. The second part draws out characteristics of this scholarship, and the third offers reflections and recommendations.

Zhang argues that overseas work offers models worth learning from. It draws on interdisciplinary methods, pays close attention to detail and comparison, and uses archives held abroad in Russia, Japan and elsewhere. Authors such as Schwartz, Meisner, Schram, Goodman, Selden and Pepper combine micro and macro perspectives, place events in wider contexts and study local cases. Zhang also reports their new arguments, such as Pepper's view that land reform mainly overthrew the rural elite. Zhang cautions that some works lack primary Chinese sources and are shaped by ideology, Western-centrism and Cold War thinking. Some, in Zhang's judgement, contain serious misreadings or deliberate vilification, and Zhang cites Wang Rongzu's typology of such errors.

Zhang identifies gaps in the translation effort: too many English-language titles, too few from other languages and regions, dated selections, uneven translation quality, and many representative works still untranslated. Zhang calls for specialised institutions and multilingual researchers, and for timely rebuttals of errors and of historical nihilism in foreign journals and conferences. Further proposals are to translate Chinese scholarship abroad, to buy more foreign books and journals, to revive a Party-history digest of overseas research and to create dedicated funding and a database. Read the original if you want a bibliographic guide to Chinese translations of foreign works on the CCP's pre-1949 history, or an example of how Party-history scholars assess overseas research and propose to respond to it.
quoteEn: Overseas researchers of the CCP's revolutionary history combine macro and micro perspectives and use new interpretive methods, showing the complexity and diversity of the Party's history.
quoteZh: 海外研究者的中国共产党革命史研究注重宏观与微观考察相结合，运用新的阐释方法来解释中国共产党革命史，展示了中国共产党历史的复杂多样性。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from 1978. The article uses it as the starting point for the period in which foreign works were translated.
In official Chinese usage, a label for views that deny or disparage the Party's revolutionary history and leaders. The article uses it to describe some overseas writing.

t: Mao Zedong's six assertions on what the Communist Party of China "lives on"
zh: 毛泽东关于中国共产党“靠什么吃饭”的六个论断
paras: Wang Jin takes up a set of colloquial formulas in which Mao Zedong explained what the Communist Party of China "eats by", that is, the basis of its success. The article identifies six assertions: the Party lives on the truth of Marxism-Leninism, on seeking truth from facts, on science, on solving problems correctly, on honesty, and on summing up experience. Wang argues that, read together, they point to a single theme: the Party advances by continuing its self-reform and strengthening its own building.

The article is written for the centenary of the Party's founding (2021) and is organised as six sections, one for each assertion. Each section ties the phrase to the occasion on which Mao used it, such as the 1942 talk "Oppose Stereotyped Party Writing", the 1954 remarks on the 1911 Revolution, and a 1965 conversation with Cheng Siyuan. Wang then illustrates it with episodes from the revolutionary, socialist-construction and reform periods, including the Xunwu investigation, the 1962 Seven Thousand Cadres Conference and "On the Ten Major Relationships".

Wang's main move is to give each phrase a concrete meaning. "Truth of Marxism-Leninism" means making Marxism the guiding ideology of the Party and the state. "Seeking truth from facts" is presented as the living soul of Mao Zedong Thought, and Wang says the Party's setbacks came from departing from it. "Science" is read as acting on objective laws through investigation and research. "Solving problems correctly" is linked to relying on the masses and the principle "from the masses, to the masses". "Honesty" covers modest conduct, truthful reporting, and admitting and correcting errors, with Mao's self-criticism in 1962 as the example. "Summing up experience" covers learning from Chinese history, the Soviet Union and the Party's own record.

Wang concludes that the six assertions share one essence: the Party relies on self-reform and on strengthening itself. This spirit of turning the blade inward is said to have driven the great social revolution and the Party's achievements in revolution, construction and reform. Revisiting them is meant to help build a Marxist party that is resolute, has the people's support and is ready for self-reform. Wang also ties this to carrying forward socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Read the original if you want to see how Party scholars turn Mao's colloquial sayings into a framework for Party building, with the historical episodes each saying is attached to.
quoteEn: In essence, the six important assertions by Mao Zedong on what the Communist Party of China \"lives on\" stress one common point: the Party lives on continually advancing self-reform and strengthening its own building.
quoteZh: 毛泽东关于中国共产党“靠什么吃饭”的上述六个重要论断，从本质上讲，强调的实际是一个共同的问题，即党靠不断推进自我革命、加强自身建设吃饭。

glossary.explanation: A phrase from classical Chinese thought that Mao Zedong adopted as the core of the Party's ideological line. It means starting from objective reality and testing theory in practice.
Mao's term, from his 1942 Yan'an Rectification talk, for formulaic, empty and intimidating writing among Party members. It is modelled on the rigid eight-legged essays of the imperial examinations.
A term now widely used in Party discourse for the Party's own rectification and self-improvement. It is often glossed in official English as the Party's self-reform.

t: Carry forward the spirit of historical initiative and walk well the new road of the "examination"
zh: 发扬历史主动精神 走好新的赶考之路
paras: Writing in Economic Daily on 24 February 2022, Wang Yibiao takes up a phrase from the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021) and from Xi Jinping's speech to the CPPCC: the Party should "carry forward the spirit of historical initiative" on the "new road of the examination" towards the second centenary goal. The article asks why this spirit is stressed, what it contains and how it can be strengthened. Wang's answer is that historical initiative is the "secret code" of the Party's century of achievements and the spiritual driver of national rejuvenation.

The piece has three parts. The first gives three reasons why the spirit matters: it is a conclusion drawn from a hundred years of history, it is part of grasping historical laws, and it is needed to meet risks and challenges. The second sets out its content through the Party's record from the revolutionary period to the new era. The third lists five sources from which the Party should draw strength on the new road. It ends with a call to unite around the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core ahead of the 20th Party Congress, due in the second half of 2022.

In the article's account, historical initiative has six elements: scientific planning that respects historical laws; a sense of mission that follows the course of history; innovation that draws on historical wisdom; great struggle informed by historical experience; self-reform grounded in historical self-confidence; and the Party's founding mission. Wang cites Marx's remark that people make their own history under inherited conditions, and Xi's statement that people are not wholly passive in history. Wang also cites episodes such as the Long March, the War to Resist U.S. Aggression and Aid Korea and reform and opening up. For the new era, the article lists regional strategies, poverty alleviation, anti-corruption work and the response to Covid-19. It presents the Party's self-reform as the second answer, after popular supervision, to Mao Zedong's "cave dialogue" question about escaping the historical cycle of rise and fall.

Wang concludes that the new road requires drawing initiative from five sources: the latest results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times; a people-first stance aimed at common prosperity; the spirit of the Party's founding and its ideological lineage; confidence in traditional Chinese culture; and a global outlook oriented to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the official 2022 narrative linked the Party's history, the third historical resolution and the run-up to the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Carrying forward the spirit of historical initiative is the buoyant state the Party's members have maintained throughout a century of struggle, and the secret to success by which the Party united and led the Chinese people in writing the grandest epic in the Chinese nation's thousands of years of history.
quoteZh: 发扬历史主动精神是中国共产党人在百年奋斗历史进程中始终保持的昂扬状态，是中国共产党团结带领中国人民书写中华民族几千年历史上最恢宏史诗的成功密码。

glossary.explanation: A phrase from the Party's 2021 historical resolution, used to describe the Party's claimed capacity to grasp historical trends and act on them rather than react to events.

glossary.en: the new road of the examination
glossary.literal: new road to sit an examination
glossary.explanation: A metaphor tracing back to Mao Zedong's 1949 remark that the Party was going to the capital "to sit the examination". Xi Jinping uses it for the task of building a modern socialist country.

The goal of building China into a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic. It follows the first goal of a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021.

An official term for the Party's efforts to discipline and renew itself, including the anti-corruption campaign and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party. It is presented as the Party's answer to the question of how to avoid the historical cycle of rise and decline.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for China's foreign policy and vision of international order, stressing cooperation, openness and win-win outcomes.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for the Party's ongoing project of combining Marxist principles with China's concrete conditions and traditional culture.

t: The Communist Party of China's century of philosophical exploration
zh: 中国共产党百年哲学探索
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 December 2021
paras: Wang Qingfeng takes up the question of what the Communist Party of China's hundred-year struggle has contributed to Marxist philosophy. Writing after the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), Wang argues that the Party's history is a process of philosophical exploration, combining Marxism's basic principles with China's concrete conditions and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The result, in the article's account, is a subjective and original Sinicized Marxist philosophy.

The short article is organised around the three main components of Marxist philosophy. Each section sets out how the Party is said to have transformed one component: the practical viewpoint became the line of seeking truth from facts; dialectical materialism became a dialectical thinking of practical wisdom; and historical materialism became the creation of Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilization. Wang draws on Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping throughout.

On practice, Wang presents seeking truth from facts as the most distinctive and original contribution of Sinicized Marxism. In Wang's reading it unites the "measure of man" with the "measure of things", and so turns a "philosophy of practice" into a genuine "practice of philosophy". On dialectics, Wang traces a line from Mao's dialectics of practical wisdom, aimed at solving concrete problems of the revolution, to the "systems thinking" and "strategic thinking" dialectics of the era after the 18th Party Congress (2012). On historical materialism, Wang contends that Marx's path "dismantles the logic of capital", whereas socialism with Chinese characteristics "harnesses" it. This is done by criticising private capital, building a public-ownership capital logic with common prosperity as its aim, and shaping "public-oriented capital", which is said to reflect the people's interests and to move beyond capitalist civilization.

Wang concludes that the Party's century of philosophical exploration is a continuing process of Sinicizing Marxist philosophy, and that its final theoretical result is a Marxist philosophy with Chinese subjectivity and originality. Wang says that reviewing this history matters for upholding the socialist path with Chinese characteristics at the meeting point of the "Two Centenary Goals". Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Party-aligned scholarship frames the Party's own philosophical contributions to Marxism.
quoteEn: If Marx's historical materialism is a path of \"dismantling the logic of capital\", then socialism with Chinese characteristics is a path of \"harnessing the logic of capital\".
quoteZh: 如果说马克思的历史唯物主义是一条“瓦解资本逻辑”的道路，那么中国特色社会主义则是一条“驾驭资本逻辑”的道路。

glossary.explanation: A slogan Mao Zedong used to summarise the Party's ideological line, later reaffirmed by Deng Xiaoping. It stresses starting from actual conditions rather than from dogma.
The official term for China's own path of modernization under Party leadership, prominent in Party discourse since 2021.
The official name for the Party's model of socialism since reform and opening up, combining public ownership as the mainstay with a socialist market economy.
An official goal of shared wealth for all, which the article presents as the value aim of public capital.
Official goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary (2049).

t: Making scientific and technological innovation a key support for promoting common prosperity
zh: 把科技创新作为促进共同富裕关键支撑
authors: Research group of the Macroeconomic Research Think Tank, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences
paras: This newspaper commentary, written by a research group of the CASS Macroeconomic Research Think Tank, asks how scientific and technological innovation can better serve high-quality development and common prosperity. The authors argue that innovation's current driving force is not yet strong enough. They name three problems: R&D that does not focus enough on industrial bottlenecks and demand, weak coordination between science and technology policy and economic and industrial policy, and a limited capacity to turn research results into products.

The article proposes concentrating innovation on three areas: the digital economy, green and low-carbon development, and industrial upgrading together with coordinated urban–rural and regional development. Each is treated in a separate section with specific measures.

On the digital economy, the authors call for breakthroughs in "choke-point" core technologies and more basic research. They also want small firms and individual businesses to share in digital opportunities, a fair mechanism for distributing the returns on data as a production factor, curbs on platform monopolies, and a larger skilled workforce to expand the middle-income group. On green development, they describe a good ecological environment as the most inclusive form of well-being and urge a market-oriented green technology system, green manufacturing and stronger pollution-control technology. On industry and regions, they propose innovation consortia, upgrading of traditional manufacturing, smart agriculture, and a strategy of science and technology for counties.

The authors conclude that the heaviest task of common prosperity still lies in the countryside. They call for consolidating the gains of poverty alleviation, advancing rural revitalization, training new professional farmers, and deepening the science and technology commissioner system so that rural residents can become prosperous through technology. Read the original if you want a concise example of how a Chinese think tank linked innovation policy to the common prosperity agenda in early 2022.
quoteEn: A good ecological environment is the most inclusive form of well-being for the people.
quoteZh: 良好生态环境是最普惠的民生福祉。

glossary.explanation: A goal of socialism that the Party leadership has emphasised, especially since 2021, meaning prosperity shared by all and a narrowing of gaps between regions, urban and rural areas, and income groups.
An official economic goal that prioritises innovation, efficiency, balance and sustainability over rapid growth alone.

glossary.literal: to be throttled by the neck
glossary.explanation: A colloquial term for key technologies in which China depends on foreign suppliers, so that access to them can be cut off.
A national strategy announced in 2017 to develop agriculture, rural industries, ecology and governance, following the poverty alleviation campaign.

t: The profound meaning of historical self-confidence and what the new era requires
zh: 历史自信的深刻内涵与时代要求
source: Chinese Social Sciences Today, 7 April 2022, p. A01
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in April 2022, Jin Minqing takes up the notion of "historical self-confidence" (lishi zixin), which the Party put forward when summarising its hundred years of struggle. The commentary argues that this confidence rests on the Party's political advancedness, its achievements and its experience, and that it also carries concrete requirements for the new era.

Jin first recalls Xi Jinping's statements on the subject since the 18th Party Congress (2012), including his remarks on the Party's 95th and 100th anniversaries and at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). The article then has two parts: the content of the Party's historical self-confidence, and four tasks through which it is to be strengthened. Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi are cited throughout, together with the 2021 Party resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience.

In the first part Jin defines historical self-confidence as the Party's firm confidence in its own history, extended to the history of the Chinese nation, and divides it into five aspects: confidence in the course of history, in historical achievements, in historical influence, in historical experience, and in the spirit of struggle. On this account, the Party's cause conforms to historical laws and the people's wishes, its achievements span four historical periods, and its experience is summed up in the "ten adherences". The fifth aspect, the spirit of struggle, is tied to the founding spirit of the Party and to the Party's self-reform. In the second part, Jin names four requirements: upholding the Party's overall leadership and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party; pursuing Chinese modernization and common prosperity; holding to historical materialism and a correct view of Party history; and the creative transformation of fine traditional Chinese culture.

Jin concludes that historical self-confidence is both an affirmation of past achievements and a firm confidence in future development. The four tasks are presented as laying the subjective, practical, cognitive and cultural foundations of that confidence. Read the original if you want a concise statement, from a senior CASS historian in 2022, of how official discourse defines historical self-confidence and links it to Party building and the study of Party history.
quoteEn: The Chinese Communist Party's historical self-confidence is both a full affirmation of historical achievements and, even more, a firm confidence in future development.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的历史自信，既是对历史成就的充分肯定，更是对未来发展的坚定信心。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed by Xi Jinping in the run-up to the Party's centenary and in the 2021 historical resolution. It denotes the Party's confidence in its own history and, by extension, in the history of the Chinese nation.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: The official slogan, used since around 2014, for the Party's campaign to tighten discipline and Party-building across all levels.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, which leaders present as distinct from Western models.
A long-standing socialist goal that Xi Jinping's leadership has made a central policy aim, meaning prosperity shared by all people.
The ten items of historical experience listed in the 2021 Party resolution, such as upholding Party leadership, putting the people first and persisting in self-reform.
Official term for the Party's efforts to cleanse and discipline itself, presented as the means by which it stays advanced and avoids decay.

t: Grasping and making good use of the Party's valuable experience of persisting in theoretical innovation
zh: 深刻把握并运用好我们党坚持理论创新的宝贵经验
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2022, Yang Yanqiu takes up one of the lessons set out in the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021). That lesson is "persisting in theoretical innovation". Yang argues that the Party's history is also a history of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and that continuing to develop contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism is necessary if the Party is to keep pace with its era.

This short commentary has three sections. The first traces how each stage of Party theory arose in response to the demands and themes of its time. The second discusses continuity and innovation across these stages. The third identifies the method of theoretical innovation as the Two Integrations.

In the first section Yang surveys the sequence from Mao Zedong Thought, described as the first historic leap in adapting Marxism to China, through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development, which together form the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and a new leap. The sequence ends with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, presented as a further leap. Yang holds that each body of theory is grounded in new practice, builds on its predecessors and answers the questions of its period. The article describes the Two Establishes as reflecting the shared wishes of the Party, the military and the people. On method, Yang says that combining Marxism's basic tenets with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture is the fundamental way to innovate. Marxism is not dogma, Yang writes, and it can revitalise traditional culture while that culture serves as a source of ideas for the Party's theory.

Yang concludes that developing twenty-first-century Marxism and contemporary Chinese Marxism is a historical responsibility of today's Communists, citing Xi Jinping. This means using Marxism to observe and lead the times, drawing on present-day practice and traditional culture, taking a historical and international view, and absorbing the achievements of other civilisations. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party theorists present the lineage of Party theory and the role of the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: The Chinese Communist Party's theoretical innovation includes both the inheritance and development of Marxist theory and the transmission and transformation of fine traditional Chinese culture.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的理论创新既包括对马克思主义理论的继承和发展，也包括对中华优秀传统文化的传承与转化。

glossary.explanation: The formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was added to the official formulation in recent years.

An official formulation affirming Xi Jinping's position as the core of the Central Committee and of the whole Party, and the guiding role of Xi Jinping Thought. It was formalised in the 2021 Resolution on the Party's history.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the process of applying Marxism to Chinese conditions and updating it for each era. Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory and later theories are officially presented as its successive results.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's current official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

The guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development. It is counted among the components of the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority of the people.

t: The people's principal role and the path of Chinese modernization
zh: 人民主体性与中国式现代化道路
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2022, Yang Xuedong and Huang Xiaofang ask what distinguishes successful paths to modernization from failed ones. Their answer is that the decisive yardstick is whether a path is people-centred: whether broad popular participation drives modernization and whether its fruits are widely shared. They present the people as the real agent of modernization and the source of the distinctive character of Chinese modernization.

The short commentary has three parts. It first sets out the people-centred criterion and contrasts China's path with Western and dependent models. It then lists five features that give Chinese modernization its "people-oriented" character. Finally it draws out four practical requirements for keeping the people at the centre. Historical examples include the post-1949 elections, literacy and public-health campaigns, and Deng Xiaoping's three-step strategy. The authors also cite figures on education, life expectancy and poverty reduction.

The authors argue that classifications of modernization by period, region, culture or institutions describe only surface phenomena. In their view the real cause of divergence is whether the people become the principal actors. Late-Qing and Republican-era attempts failed, they say, because the people were not organized. The Communist Party, described as coming from and representing the people, mobilized and empowered them and so avoided exclusion of the masses. The five features are: organizing the people, empowering them to be masters of the country, raising their capacities, meeting their aspirations for a better life, and sharing results. The authors contend that this produced a path of internally driven development. They say it avoids the ills of capital-centred Western modernization and of "growth without development" elsewhere, and that it reached in about seven decades what the West took centuries to build.

The authors call for adherence to a people-centred philosophy of development. They also call for judging success by whether people are happy, satisfied and approving rather than by statistics or buildings. They urge widening the reach of the results by narrowing urban–rural, regional and sectoral income gaps and regulating high incomes, and developing whole-process people's democracy so that more people take part. They link this to common prosperity. Read the original if you want a concise official-academic statement of how Party theorists framed the people's role in Chinese modernization on the eve of the 20th Party Congress.
quoteEn: Whether a path is people-centred is the fundamental yardstick by which to measure each country's road to modernization.
quoteZh: 是否以人民为中心是衡量各国现代化道路的根本尺度。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for China's own path of modernization, stressed as distinct from the Western model. It is used in official discourse with features such as a huge population, common prosperity and coordinated material and cultural-ethical progress.

A concept promoted by Xi Jinping from 2019, describing Chinese democracy as covering every stage from elections to consultation, decision-making, management and oversight. Official sources present it as an alternative to electoral-only Western democracy.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given new emphasis under Xi Jinping. It is linked to narrowing income, regional and urban–rural gaps.

t: The digital economy and common prosperity
zh: 数字经济与共同富裕
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 15 February 2022, asks whether the digital economy can advance common prosperity. Tan Hongbo notes that China has eliminated absolute poverty, that the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020) set substantial progress toward common prosperity as a long-range goal, and that the digital economy is growing fast alongside it. The article argues that, left unregulated, the digital economy tends to widen income and wealth gaps. Tan therefore calls for regulating its development and building a matching income distribution system.

The article has two parts. The first, on whether the digital economy can promote common prosperity, examines the general relationship between technological progress and inequality and then the specific features of digital technology. The second sets out two lines of effort: reasonable regulation of the digital economy, and a distribution system suited to it. Tan cites figures that the digital economy reached 39.2 trillion yuan in 2020, or 38.6% of GDP, growing at 9.7%.

Tan makes two main moves. In general terms, technological revolutions have historically coincided with widening gaps, which Tan supports with Thomas Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century and a study of housing-size Gini coefficients by Timothy Kohler and colleagues. Tan adds that innovation tends to produce monopoly power, reinforced by patents. Digital technology adds four features: unequal possession of data as a production factor, increasing returns to scale, network externalities and two-sided platform markets. In Tan's reading these make monopoly easier to form. Dominant platforms can then extract extra profit from merchants through ranking and advertising fees, practise near-perfect price discrimination against consumers using profiling, and stifle rivals.

Tan proposes that regulation include price controls such as average-cost pricing, supervision of data collection and the transparency of algorithms, lower entry and exit costs, and compensated interoperability between platforms. On distribution, Tan calls for clarifying data property rights that reflect the contributions of consumers, merchants and platforms while protecting security and privacy. Tan also calls for a tax system adapted to digital trade, including a digital regulatory tax, and for digital technology to be used to improve tax administration and equalise public services. Read the original if you want a concise, policy-oriented economic argument from 2022 on monopoly, data rights and taxation in the context of common prosperity.
quoteEn: Therefore, the digital economy will not ease but rather aggravate income distribution gaps.
quoteZh: 因此，数字经济不但不会缓解反而会加剧收入分配差距。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal of shared affluence for all, given new prominence in Party policy from 2020–21. It is used to frame policies on distribution and narrowing gaps.
Official policy language since 2019–20 that treats data as a factor of production alongside land, labour, capital and technology. It raises questions of ownership and income from data.

t: The essence of the times of Chinese culture and the Chinese spirit
zh: 中华文化和中国精神的时代精华
paras: This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 1 March 2022, takes up one phrase from the resolution on the Party's century of struggle adopted by the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is "the essence of the times of Chinese culture and the Chinese spirit". Sun argues that this formulation offers a new theoretical angle for understanding the Thought, which the resolution also describes as twenty-first-century Marxism and a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times.

The piece is organised under three headings. The first treats the Thought's roots in the Chinese cultural tradition and its role in guiding cultural development. The second treats the Chinese spiritual temperament, values and strength it is said to embody. The third treats its grasp of the features of the era, its answers to the questions of the times and the direction it indicates.

Sun's central claim is that the Thought fuses Marxism with fine traditional Chinese culture. Drawing on Xi's formula of making the past serve the present, Sun says Xi reactivates elements of tradition through a Marxist standpoint and method, and cites ideas such as putting the people first, a community with a shared future for mankind and harmony between humanity and nature. On the Chinese spirit, the author traces a line from ancient ideals such as "all under heaven as one" through the Party's founding spirit to the core socialist values, and argues that the Thought gathers spiritual strength for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. On the era, Sun maintains that the Thought answers questions about the nature and path of socialism, modernization and Party building, and about where the world is heading.

Sun concludes that the Thought gives Chinese culture a guiding direction under firm cultural confidence and a Marxist leadership in ideology. It is also presented as offering "Chinese wisdom" and "Chinese solutions" for humanity. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in 2022 linked Xi Jinping Thought to traditional Chinese culture and national spirit.
quoteEn: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is a model of the creative transformation and innovative development of fine traditional Chinese culture.
quoteZh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想是推动中华优秀传统文化创造性转化、创新性发展的典范。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2012–2013. It calls for cooperative, shared-benefit international relations.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official description of the Party's ongoing effort to fit Marxist theory to Chinese conditions and contemporary issues.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely tied to the Chinese Dream.
A slogan stressing confidence in China's cultural heritage and socialist culture. It was added to the earlier three confidences to form the Four-sphere Confidence.
A twelve-word official value set at national, social and individual levels, promoted since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Unwaveringly keeping economic development as the central task
zh: 坚持以经济建设为中心不动摇
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in February 2022, after the Central Economic Work Conference of late 2021, Shi Jianxun asks why the Party must keep economic development as its central task in the new development stage. Shi argues that the line is a basic experience of the People's Republic and is essential for achieving high-quality development.

The commentary is organised around three "logics": historical, theoretical and practical. The historical section traces the line from the Eighth Party Congress to the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and the 13th Party Congress (1987), which set out the basic line of "one centre, two basic points".

In the theoretical section, Shi holds that the changed principal contradiction of the new era does not alter China's position in the primary stage of socialism. Shi reasons that a better life for the people needs a material base and higher productive forces. Shi also presents economic development as the "key point" within the "five-sphere integrated plan", which does not conflict with coordinating the other four spheres.

In the practical section, Shi calls for the new development philosophy, supply-side structural reform and attention to demand management, and treats economic growth as the precondition for common prosperity. Making the "cake" bigger requires the basic socialist economic system, distribution according to work combined with distribution according to factors of production, and the Two Unwaverings. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official rationale for the economy-centred line in early 2022.
quoteEn: The great cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics does not consist only of economic development as the centre, but without economic development as the centre, common prosperity cannot be achieved.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义伟大事业不只是以经济建设为中心，但没有以经济建设为中心，就不可能实现共同富裕。

glossary.explanation: An official goal, stressed since 2017, of shifting from rapid growth to growth that is more efficient, balanced and innovative.

glossary.pinyin: yī gè zhōngxīn, liǎng gè jīběndiǎn
glossary.explanation: Shorthand for the Party's basic line from the 13th Party Congress (1987): economic development as the centre, with the Four Cardinal Principles and reform and opening up as the two basic points.
Xi Jinping's formula of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, announced in 2015.
A stated socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given prominence in official policy from 2021.
The official overall layout for advancing economic, political, cultural, social and ecological progress together.
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector and unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.

t: Strengthening the historical confidence of Chinese Communists
zh: 坚定中国共产党人的历史自信
paras: Yao Hongzhi and Nie Shengping take up the call in Xi Jinping's remarks to "firm up historical confidence" and ask where Chinese Communists' confidence in their own history comes from and how it is formed. The commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today in January 2022, defines historical confidence as a firm conviction in the spiritual value and vitality shown by the Party's own history. The authors argue that no party in the world has more reason to be confident, and that every Party member should take pride in the Party's century of struggle and draw strength from it for the "new road to the exam".

The piece has two parts. The first identifies four sources of historical confidence: the Party's major achievements, its contributions to the world, its fighting spirit, and its distinctive strengths. The second sets out a "logical path" linking study of Party history, historical understanding, historical consciousness and historical initiative.

In the first part, the authors list the achievements of the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. They hold that these changed the fate of the nation. They present Chinese modernization as a new form of human civilization that rejects capital-centred, polarising and expansionist Western modernization. They cite setbacks such as the failure of the Great Revolution and the "Left" errors of Wang Ming as proof of resilience, from which the Party's spiritual lineage grew. In the second part, they describe an ascending spiral. Study campaigns, from the Yan'an rectification to the 2021 Party history study and education drive, deepen understanding. Historical materialism and a "correct view of Party history" turn understanding into historical consciousness. That consciousness in turn produces historical initiative.

The authors conclude that Party history study is meant not to console but to raise awareness of historical experience and laws, so that the Party can take the initiative. Having met the first centenary goal, they say, the Party must keep drawing wisdom from its history to answer the "exam" of the second centenary goal and write a new chapter of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars in early 2022 framed historical confidence and the purpose of Party history education.
quoteEn: The Party's century of struggle is an important source of Chinese Communists' historical confidence.
quoteZh: 党的百年奋斗史，是中国共产党人历史自信的重要来源。

glossary.explanation: A concept stressed in Party discourse around the Party's centenary in 2021. It means firm confidence in the Party's own history and the values it is said to embody.
The official name for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

glossary.literal: new road of going to the examination
glossary.explanation: A metaphor from Mao Zedong's 1949 remark about "going to the capital for the exam". It is used by Xi Jinping for the Party's continuing tests in governing.

t: A new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
zh: 马克思主义中国化新的飞跃
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 February 2022
paras: Yang Xin takes up a formulation from the Party's 2021 historical resolution (adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee): that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is "twenty-first-century Marxism" and has achieved a new leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context. Writing in a Party-newspaper commentary, Yang argues that this leap shows itself in five "organic unities" that define the thought's theoretical innovation.

The article takes these five pairings in turn: theoretical consciousness and political confidence; theoretical logic and historical logic; the value of the times and practical value; inheriting and promoting tradition and drawing on other civilisations; and the Chinese path and its contribution to the world. Each section is a short exposition that places the thought within the longer history of Marxism's adaptation in China, from Mao Zedong Thought to the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics and then to the present.

Yang's central reasoning is that the Party has advanced Marxism by always joining theory to history. The theoretical logic is the combination of Marxism's basic tenets with China's concrete conditions and its fine traditional culture. The historical logic is the Party's founding mission of seeking happiness for the people and renewal for the nation. Yang presents the three theoretical stages as answers to successive demands: Mao Thought to make the nation "stand up", the Deng-era system to make it "prosper", and Xi's thought to make it "become strong". The thought is also said to answer the era's major questions through the "Ten Clarifications" and to rebut anti-Marxist and non-Marxist currents.

Yang concludes that the thought opens a new realm of Marxist development and enriches the path of Chinese modernization in both theory and practice. In the author's account, China's road, as a country of about 18 per cent of the world's population, offers developing countries experience and a new option for those seeking faster development while keeping their independence, and so contributes "Chinese wisdom and a Chinese approach" to human problems. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official 2022 narrative frames Xi Jinping Thought as a third historic leap of Sinicised Marxism.
quoteEn: The theoretical consciousness embodied in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is clearly shown in its accurate grasp of, and scientific answers to, the questions of the times.
quoteZh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想所蕴含的理论自觉，鲜明地体现在它对时代课题的准确把握和科学回答上。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage in the adaptation of Marxism to China.
The official name for China's path and system since reform and opening up, which combines Marxist principles with China's conditions as the Party defines them.
A ten-point summary of the core content of Xi Jinping Thought, set out in the Party's 2021 historical resolution.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.

t: Telling China's story well: focusing on the logic of modern narrative
zh: 讲好中国故事聚焦现代叙事逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 24 February 2022
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in 2022, asks how China's story can be told effectively in a period when, in the author's account, Western actors control much of the world's political, academic and news discourse. Ling argues that the task is both strategically urgent and theoretically unresolved, and that it can be met only by drawing on the historical and cultural roots of Chinese civilization. The proposed answer is a modern narrative paradigm built on the subjectivity, regularity and purposiveness of the China story.

The article opens by presenting storytelling as a source of cultural confidence, a way of rallying support for modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and a contribution to exchange among civilizations. It then proceeds under three headings: upholding China's standpoint, spreading Chinese wisdom and highlighting Chinese values. Ling draws on Xi Jinping's speeches and on the report to the 19th Party Congress (2017) as models and guidance.

Ling first contends that China must be the subject of its own narrative, and that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era supplies the guiding principle. Storytelling should explain Chinese practice with Chinese theory. Second, the author holds that a discourse system with Chinese cultural features is the practical entry point, and credits Xi with three methods: using distinctively Chinese cultural content (such as the Silk Road idea behind the Belt and Road Initiative), using classical Chinese phrasing, and carrying on the people-centred tradition of minben thought through the notion of putting the people first. Third, Ling argues that emotional narrative links past and present and young and old, and that the Party leadership has derived values from tradition, for example ecological civilization from the idea of harmony between heaven and humanity and a community with a shared future for mankind from the idea of benevolence.

Ling concludes that China has the confidence and strength to present its civilization's achievements and its contribution to humanity, so that the world better understands China, its history and its national spirit. Cultural identity, in this reading, is a basic source of national self-confidence and a spiritual force for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Chinese commentary frames international communication, cultural confidence and traditional culture in the Xi Jinping era.
quoteEn: Telling China's story well means using Chinese theory to explain Chinese practice and Chinese practice to elevate Chinese theory, presenting Chinese thought more distinctly and putting forward Chinese proposals more loudly.
quoteZh: 讲好中国故事，就是要用中国理论解释中国实践，用中国实践升华中国理论，更加鲜明地展示中国思想，更加响亮地提出中国主张。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution in 2017.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central official goal of national revival, associated with the Chinese Dream and used by the Party to frame its long-term mission.
An international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative proposed by Xi Jinping in 2013, drawing on the historical image of the Silk Road.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and global-governance concept promoted by Xi Jinping, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states.
A traditional Chinese political idea that the people are the foundation of the state; official discourse links it to the principle of putting the people first.

t: The theoretical logic and practical path of whole-process people's democracy
zh: 全过程人民民主的理论逻辑与实践路径
source: People's Forum (Renmin Luntan), 2021 no. 10 (second ten-day issue)
paras: Writing in People's Forum in 2021, Sun Yingshuai asks what whole-process people's democracy contributes to socialist democratic theory and to China's political development. The article argues that it is a major theoretical innovation, a new practice within the political path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and a form of democracy that, in the author's account, shows the superiority of Chinese-style democracy over Western bourgeois democracy.

The piece opens with the concept's recent history: Xi Jinping's first use of "whole-process democracy" in November 2019 at a grassroots legislative contact point in Shanghai, his October 2021 speech to the Central Conference on NPC work, and the March 2021 amendment to the NPC Organic Law that wrote the term into national law. Three sections follow, covering theory, practice and comparative advantage. They move from Marx and Engels, through Mao Zedong's 1949 writing on the people's democratic dictatorship, to the present.

Sun first places the concept in a line from the Communist Manifesto's call to "win the battle of democracy" and the Communist League's democratic statutes, through the Chinese Communist Party's people's democracy, to Xi's stress on the people-centred stance. Second, the article describes practice: the people's congress system, multiparty cooperation and political consultation, grassroots self-governance and regional ethnic autonomy, plus consultation mechanisms such as legislative contact points and hearings. It cites 187 draft laws opened to public comment since the 18th Party Congress (2012), and 10 rounds of consultation on the Civil Code that drew over 1.02 million suggestions. Third, Sun names three distinguishing features: Party leadership as the fundamental political guarantee, the people's congress system as the main institutional channel, and a full-chain, all-round, full-coverage design linking election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight in a closed loop. Sun contrasts this with the "one-off democracy" of the West.

Sun concludes that whole-process people's democracy enriches socialist democratic theory, supports the modernization of national governance, and contributes to a new form of human civilization. The author calls for pursuing high-quality development of Chinese-style democracy with greater confidence in the new development stage. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how the concept was introduced, institutionalised and justified in 2021, with the legislative-consultation figures it cites.
quoteEn: Whole-process people's democracy is a new practice of the political development path of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
quoteZh: 全过程人民民主是中国特色社会主义政治发展道路的新实践

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping first used in 2019 and which Party documents present as the defining feature of China's socialist democracy. It stresses people's participation across election, consultation, decision-making, management and oversight, not only at elections.
The official name for China's political and economic system since the reform era. It presents the system as Marxism adapted to China's conditions.
The official definition of the state system of the People's Republic, set out by Mao Zedong in 1949. It describes a state led by the working class and based on the worker–peasant alliance.
China's basic political institution, a system of congresses from local level to the National People's Congress that is formally the organ of state power.

t: The Chinese Communist Party's courage in self-reform: its historical record and underlying logic
zh: 中国共产党勇于自我革命的历史呈现与生成逻辑
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 25 November 2021
paras: Published in China Social Sciences Today in November 2021, shortly after the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee adopted the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century, this article asks why the Communist Party of China can claim that it has the courage for self-reform. Wang and Guo argue that this courage is a defining mark separating the Party from other parties. They present it as one of the main lessons of the Party's centenary and as a guide to future success.

The article has two main parts. The first surveys the Party's history in four periods: the New Democratic Revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. For each it identifies the specific campaigns and rules through which the Party reformed itself. The second part explains the sources of this drive and then sets out its wider significance.

The authors trace the drive to three logics. In theory, self-reform follows from the nature of a Marxist proletarian party that, in their account, has no interests of its own and serves the people wholeheartedly. In history, it is required by the Party's founding mission of seeking the happiness of the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. In practice, it is needed to meet present risks, including a world undergoing great changes unseen in a century and factors that weaken the Party's vanguard character and purity. They then argue that self-reform enriches the theory of Marxist party building, keeps the Party advanced and pure, and gives momentum to what they call the great social revolution. They also hold that it offers a reference for other governing parties.

Wang and Guo conclude that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party is never finished and that self-reform has no final note. They call for a scientific summing-up of the century's experience, so that the Party can carry on its new great project of Party building and lead the people through a new "examination". The article is a concise, officially aligned statement of the Party's own account of its history. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Chinese Party scholarship presents self-reform as the thread of the Party's century and as an export-ready governance model.
quoteEn: Courage in self-reform is the distinguishing mark that sets the Communist Party of China apart from other parties, and it is also one of the valuable pieces of historical experience the Party has accumulated in leading the people's great struggle.
quoteZh: 勇于自我革命，是中国共产党区别于其他政党的显著标志，也是党领导人民进行伟大奋斗积累的宝贵历史经验之一。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly governing the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line announced under Xi Jinping, covering Party discipline, conduct, political building and anti-corruption. It was made part of the "Four-Pronged" (Four Comprehensives) strategy.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Party discourse, associated with the Chinese Dream. It refers to restoring China's strength and international standing.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.
The official name for China's path and system since the reform era. The "new era" label dates from the 19th Party Congress (2017).

t: The Communist Party of China's historic contribution to the progress of human civilization
zh: 中国共产党对人类文明进步的历史性贡献
paras: Marking the Party's centenary, this commentary (originally in the Chinese Social Sciences Today, November 2021) asks how the Communist Party of China has contributed to the progress of human civilization. Li Baogeng argues that, over a hundred years, the Party has made three historic contributions: it liberated the Chinese people and pointed the way to the liberation of the world's peoples, it opened a path of modernization that goes beyond the logic of capital, and it shaped a new form of human civilization through the idea of a community with a shared future for mankind.

The piece follows these three headings in turn. It opens by tracing the Party's aspiration to contribute more to humanity from the First Congress's goal of communism, through Mao Zedong's 1956 remark, to Xi Jinping's formulation about seeking happiness for the people, rejuvenation for the nation and "great harmony" for the world. It then reviews the stages of Party history and of modernization, before turning to the contemporary international situation.

On liberation, Li contrasts failed utopian thinkers from Plato to Owen with Marxism as a theory of human emancipation, and presents the four "great leaps" (standing up, becoming prosperous, becoming strong) as proof of its truth. On modernization, Li runs from the first generation's revolution and industrial base through reform and opening up to the post-2012 campaigns for poverty alleviation and common prosperity, claiming that this confirms Marx's idea of bypassing the "Caudine Forks" of capitalism. On civilization, Li reads Marx's "two inevitables" and "two never wills" as implying a long coexistence of socialism and capitalism, and argues that the community with a shared future for mankind answers how the two can coexist: through "strong but not hegemonic" states, plural civilizations, just exchange and a human-centred rather than capital-centred logic. In Li's account this idea develops Marx's theory of world history and refutes the "Thucydides trap", the "clash of civilizations" and the "end of history".

Li concludes that the Party saved the Chinese nation and, through Chinese modernization, created a new form of human civilization. China, the author says, will remain a builder of world peace and will become a leader and builder of civilizational progress as it grows stronger. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the centenary-era Party narrative links Marxist theory, modernization and the community with a shared future for mankind.
quoteEn: The path of Chinese modernization that the Party has opened up over a hundred years proves the truth of Marx's idea of "bypassing the Caudine Forks of capitalism" and offers other countries a reference option for exploring independent paths of modernization.
quoteZh: 中国共产党百年来开创的中国式现代化发展道路，证明了马克思关于“跨越资本主义卡夫丁峡谷”设想的真理性，为世界其他国家探索独立自主的现代化发展道路提供了可资借鉴的选择。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy and theoretical concept advanced by Xi Jinping from 2012–13, calling for shared responsibility, consultation and mutually beneficial cooperation among states.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.
A goal of shared wealth for all, emphasised in Party policy especially from 2021.
The policy launched in 1978 that introduced market-oriented reforms and opened China to foreign trade and investment.
Chinese shorthand for the Communist Manifesto's judgement that the bourgeoisie's fall and the proletariat's victory are equally inevitable.

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Reform and opening up as a great awakening of the Party
zh: 改革开放是党的一次伟大觉醒
paras: Qu Qingshan takes up the judgement in the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience over the past century, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021), that "reform and opening up was a great awakening of the Party". The article, a commentary first published in the People's Daily, asks how this awakening came about and why the decision for reform and opening up was taken. Qu's answer is that it rested on several mutually reinforcing foundations: an understanding of the nation's fate, a summing-up of socialist practice, insight into the trend of the times, attention to the people's needs, the Party's nature and Marxist guidance.

The text is organised as a sequence of short sections, each naming one basis or feature of the awakening. It begins with the Cultural Revolution and the choices facing the Party in the late 1970s, then reviews the theoretical and strategic achievements of successive leaderships from Deng Xiaoping to Hu Jintao. It goes on to the international context, popular aspirations, the Party's purpose and ideals, the 1978 debate on truth, and the role of the masses. It closes with the results of reform and opening up.

Qu argues that the Cultural Revolution exposed serious defects in the system and policies of the time, and quotes Deng Xiaoping to the effect that without reform the cause of modernization and socialism would be lost. The Party, in this account, faced three roads: a closed and rigid old path, a "wrong path" of changing the Party's banner, and a new path of development. It chose the third. Qu holds that the Party could correct its own errors because it has no interests apart from those of the working class and the people. He presents the 1978 debate on "practice as the sole criterion of truth" as the start of the awakening, restoring the line of seeking truth from facts, and treats the masses as the real creators of reform.

Qu concludes that the awakening produced reform and opening up as a "new great revolution" that liberated productive forces and raised living standards. He cites China's rise to the world's second-largest economy and largest exporter, and the move from the nation having "stood up" to having "become prosperous". Reform and opening up is described as the key to the fate of contemporary China and to realising the Two Centenary Goals and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official People's Daily framing of the 1978 turning point and the Party's own account of why it chose reform.
quoteEn: Reform and opening up is the important magic weapon by which the Party and the people have strode forward to catch up with the times, the only way to uphold and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the key move that determines the fate of contemporary China.
quoteZh: 改革开放是党和人民大踏步赶上时代的重要法宝，是坚持和发展中国特色社会主义的必由之路，是决定当代中国前途命运的关键一招

glossary.explanation: The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in December 1978 under Deng Xiaoping, introducing market-oriented domestic reforms and opening to foreign trade and investment.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China to national strength and international standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
The goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021 and a modern socialist country by the centenary of the People's Republic in 2049.

t: Firmly establishing a correct view of development and of modernization
zh: 牢固树立正确的发展观现代化观
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 18 March 2022, this commentary takes up Xi Jinping's statement that only a people-centred approach to development yields a correct view of development and of modernization. Lou Qinjian argues that this approach answers basic questions about the concept, purpose and driving force of high-quality development and socialist modernization. The author calls for establishing these views firmly so as to create a higher quality of life for the people on the new journey.

The article has three parts. It first presents the people-centred approach as the expression of the Marxist people's standpoint and of the Party's founding mission. It then sets out the content of the approach: development for the people, development relying on the people, and development whose fruits are shared by the people. The last part applies the approach to five features of Chinese modernization: high-quality development, common prosperity, the all-round development of the person, green development and a community with a shared future for mankind.

Lou's central move is to read the Party's history as proof that the people-centred approach is the source of its victories. The author runs through the New Democratic Revolution, socialist construction, reform and opening up, and the new era, and distinguishes the Party's stance from the traditional Chinese idea of the people as the foundation of the state. In Lou's account, the Party has no interests apart from those of the working class and the broad masses. The author ties sharing to national conditions, holding that it must be universal, comprehensive and gradual, neither standing still nor aiming too high. Common prosperity, in this reading, is not simultaneous or equal enrichment, and requires making the cake bigger while also dividing it better by narrowing regional, urban–rural and income gaps.

Lou concludes that every area of modernization should follow the people-centred approach. The proposals include innovation-driven growth, a better market environment alongside a stronger role for government, coordination of development and security, cultural and ethical progress, the "dual carbon" goals, and high-standard opening up with high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-state officials presented the link between the people-centred approach and Chinese modernization in early 2022.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is an essential requirement of socialism and an important feature of Chinese modernization.
quoteZh: 共同富裕是社会主义的本质要求，是中国式现代化的重要特征。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for China's own path to modernization. It is usually characterised by a huge population, common prosperity, material and cultural-ethical advancement, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.
The official development goal since about 2017. It stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over speed of growth.
A socialist goal of prosperity for all, which the Party presents as a gradual process rather than equal enrichment. It was given new prominence under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world bound by common interests and cooperative global governance.

t: Adhering to the "Two Integrations"
zh: 坚持“两个结合”
paras: Tang Zhouyan and Wang Xueyuan take up the formula of the Two Integrations, which Xi Jinping set out at the Party's centenary celebration (2021): combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The authors argue that adding the second integration, with traditional culture, greatly enriches the content of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They present it as a new height and an original contribution to Sinicised Marxism, and say that adhering to it is an urgent need.

This short commentary in a Party theoretical journal is organised in four parts. The first three each name a source of urgency: launching the new journey of building a modern socialist country in all respects, passing on and renewing fine traditional culture, and advancing contemporary Chinese Marxism. The fourth reads the integration as an expression of theoretical and cultural confidence. The authors draw mainly on speeches by Xi, Mao Zedong's 1938 report to the Sixth Plenum of the Sixth Central Committee, and the 2021 Party resolution on history.

Tang and Wang argue first that Chinese modernization differs from Western modernization, which they describe as built on capital export, colonial expansion and imposed values. In their account, Chinese modernization draws on traditional culture, and further integration is needed so that China can promote exchange and mutual learning among civilizations. They then argue that Marxism develops only by joining national practice. They read Mao's On Practice and the principles of seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence as products of this integration with traditional culture. They also read the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind as bearing the imprint of that culture. Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era is called a model of the Two Integrations.

The authors conclude that the Party's integration of Marxism with China's realities and culture has moved from spontaneity to self-awareness and then to confidence. They cite Mao's New Democracy of 1940 as the start of conscious effort, and Xi's advocacy of civilizational exchange as a leap to theoretical and cultural confidence. They hold that Marxism can show its contemporary and global value only by engaging Chinese culture, and that traditional culture must be modernised through Marxist critical inheritance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party theorists in 2022 justified adding the cultural dimension to the Two Integrations.
quoteEn: Sinicised Marxism can further show its value for our times and for the world only in the course of combining with fine traditional Chinese culture, and on the basis of continually answering and resolving the questions facing Chinese culture and civilization as they increasingly go global.
quoteZh: 中国化的马克思主义只有在同中华优秀传统文化相结合的过程中，在不断回答和解决日益走向世界的中国文化、中华文明问题的基础上，才能进一步体现出自己的时代价值和世界价值。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula of combining the basic tenets of Marxism with China's specific realities and with fine traditional Chinese culture. The second element was stressed from 2021.

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official term for the Party's project of fitting Marxism to China's conditions. The article uses the shorter form 马克思主义中国化, "Sinicisation of Marxism".
The official name for China's development path, presented as distinct from Western modernization.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
China's international infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative, announced by Xi Jinping in 2013.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states.

t: Strengthening the economic foundation to ensure progress while maintaining stability
zh: 做强经济基础 确保稳中求进
