paras: Writing in Economic Daily in March 2022, Quan Heng takes up the "triple pressure" that the Central Economic Work Conference and the Government Work Report said China's economy faces: demand contraction, supply shocks and weakening expectations. The author argues that grasping the nature of these pressures and answering them precisely is essential for assessing the economic situation and for strengthening the economic foundation, in line with the guideline of putting stability first and seeking progress within stability.

The commentary has three parts. The first analyses the new features of the triple pressure. The second lists risks that must be guarded against in the coming period. The third sets out the strategic advantages the author sees for China and four directions for dealing with the pressures over the short and long term.

Quan notes that demand, supply and expectations rarely all come under strain at once, and that a change in expectations can reshape supply and demand over time. The author finds three features: a complex international background (global supply chain disruption, trade protectionism, rising global PPI); deep domestic causes (low final consumption as a share of GDP, new growth drivers not yet clearly formed); and overlap with older problems, namely the "three-phase superposition" and structural, institutional and cyclical problems. The three pressures can also feed one another through price, cost and inflation expectations. On this basis Quan calls for vigilance against weakening of both external and domestic demand, falling household consumption, a split between upstream and downstream firms and between large and small firms, transmission of PPI to CPI, rising debt and financial risks, and rushed or one-size-fits-all pursuit of the "dual carbon" goals.

Quan points to five strategic advantages named by Xi Jinping, including Party leadership and the institutional strengths of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and concludes that the long-term fundamentals are unchanged. The proposed response is to coordinate macro, micro, structural, technology and other policies in the short term. In the longer term, it rests on four tasks: building on the new development stage and high-quality development, deepening institutional reform, advancing technological innovation, and pursuing high-level opening up, including a shift to institutional opening. Read the original if you want an example of how official economic commentary in early 2022 framed the triple pressure and its policy responses.
quoteEn: The triple pressure of demand contraction, supply shocks and weakening expectations is an old contradiction accumulated over long-term development, a new difficulty under new domestic and international conditions, and above all a new bottleneck that must be faced and broken through with great effort on entering the new development stage.
quoteZh: 需求收缩、供给冲击、预期转弱三重压力既是过去长期发展过程中累积下来的旧矛盾，也是国内外新形势下面临的新困难，更是进入新发展阶段必须面对并需要花大力气去破解的新瓶颈。

glossary.zh: 需求收缩、供给冲击、预期转弱三重压力
glossary.pinyin: xūqiú shōusuō, gōngjǐ chōngjī, yùqī zhuǎnruò sānchóng yālì
glossary.literal: triple pressure of demand contraction, supply shock and weakening expectations
glossary.explanation: A formula from the Central Economic Work Conference (December 2021) naming demand contraction, supply shocks and weakening expectations as the main pressures on China's economy. It was repeated in the 2022 Government Work Report.

glossary.pinyin: wěn zì dāngtóu, wěn zhōng qiú jìn
glossary.en: putting stability first and seeking progress within stability
glossary.explanation: The general principle of China's economic work, which prioritises stability while pursuing progress. Official documents repeated it as the keynote for 2022.

An official term for the period of China's development after the 18th Party Congress (2012), and especially from the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021–25) onwards. It is used to justify a shift towards high-quality development.
An official goal that shifts emphasis from speed and scale of growth to efficiency, innovation and sustainability.
An official description of China's economy as being simultaneously in a period of slower growth, structural adjustment and digestion of earlier stimulus policies.
China's pledge to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and reach carbon neutrality before 2060.
Opening up through alignment of rules, regulations and standards with international ones, as distinct from opening limited to flows of goods and factors.

t: Common prosperity is an important feature of Chinese modernization
zh: 共同富裕是中国式现代化的重要特征
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily and written in 2022, takes up Xi Jinping's statement that common prosperity is an essential requirement of socialism and an important feature of Chinese modernization. Liu Wei argues that understanding this feature properly matters for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics and for achieving more visible, substantive progress toward common prosperity for all people.

The piece moves from the classical Marxist vision of production aimed at the prosperity of all, through the Communist Party's founding mission, to the present stage. It then contrasts Chinese modernization with the paths of earlier and later modernizing countries, and closes with principles and concrete measures for the new era.

Liu contends that common prosperity, like communism, is a long historical process and must fit the primary stage of socialism, rest on economic and social development and follow objective laws. In the author's account, modernization led by elites and capital in early-developing countries left unresolved polarisation between rich and poor, while some late developers that imitated them produced wider gaps, instability or interrupted modernization. Chinese modernization, by contrast, is described as one of common prosperity for all, whose fundamental task is resolving unbalanced and inadequate development.

Liu sets out three principles: encourage prosperity through hard work and innovation, first enlarging the "cake" and then dividing it well; act within means; and proceed step by step. Measures include enlarging the middle-income group toward an olive-shaped social structure, equalising basic public services, regulating high incomes while protecting lawful ones, promoting people's all-round development and cultural life, and rural revitalisation. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line academic statement of how common prosperity is framed within Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: Achieving common prosperity is likewise a long historical process, and both its historical content and its means of realisation must suit the basic national condition of the primary stage of socialism.
quoteZh: 实现共同富裕同样是一个漫长的历史过程，无论是历史内涵，还是实现方式，都必须与社会主义初级阶段的基本国情相适应

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given renewed policy prominence under Xi Jinping, especially from 2021.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.
An official thesis, formalised in the 1980s, that China remains in an early and long phase of socialist development.
The Party's official name for its socialist system and path since reform and opening up.

t: The strategic blueprint for building a modern socialist great power
zh: 建设社会主义现代化强国的战略擘画
paras: This short commentary, published in the People's Daily in March 2022, explains the "general task" of upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics as set out in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Gu argues that the task, which combines socialist modernization with the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, condenses the Party's answer to the major questions of the era.

The article is organised around three claims about the general task. It clarifies the direction of development in the new era, it sketches a blueprint for a modern socialist great power, and it expresses the Party's resolve to remain true to its founding mission.

Gu places the task in a historical line. After the Opium War, China faced two historical tasks: national independence and people's liberation, then national prosperity and the people's happiness. The author traces the Party's pursuit of modernization from industrialization and the "four modernizations" to the start of "Chinese-style modernization" under reform and opening up, and then to the path of Chinese modernization in the new era. In Gu's reading, socialist modernization and national rejuvenation are essentially one. The blueprint envisages basically realizing modernization by 2035 and building a prosperous, strong, democratic, culturally advanced, harmonious and beautiful country by mid-century. Gu lists the features Xi Jinping attributes to Chinese modernization, including its huge population, common prosperity and peaceful development.

Gu concludes that the Party's achievements show that the Party is capable, Marxism works and socialism with Chinese characteristics is good. The author holds that national rejuvenation has entered an irreversible historical process and that Chinese modernization will further display the strengths of the system. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned exposition of how Party theorists frame the general task and its historical lineage.
quoteEn: Socialist modernization is the core content of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and national rejuvenation is the vivid expression of socialist modernization; the two are essentially identical.
quoteZh: 社会主义现代化是中华民族伟大复兴的核心内容，中华民族伟大复兴是社会主义现代化的形象表达，两者在本质上是一致的

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Party's path of modernization with Chinese features. Xi Jinping stressed it prominently from the 20th Party Congress (2022) onward.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, closely linked to the Chinese Dream.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
The official name for the Party's system and path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, a socialist system and a market economy.
A goal of shared affluence for all the people, which the Party presents as a defining feature of socialism.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978.

t: Taking the correct path that suits China's national conditions
zh: 走符合中国国情的正确道路
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in December 2021, Leng Rong takes up one of the ten lessons of the Party's century of struggle listed in the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): "upholding the Chinese path". Leng argues that the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics has been proven in practice to suit China's national conditions. In this account it is the only route to a better life for the people and to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and Leng calls for stronger confidence in the path.

The commentary is a study-and-interpretation piece in three parts. The first traces how the Party explored and formed a path suited to China across the revolutionary period, the socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second places the path within Chinese civilisation and history. The third sets out how the path is to be followed in future.

Leng's central claim is that a correct path is hard to find and must be cherished. In the early years, the Party's failure to recognise the importance of its own path, including the leftist errors, is said to have brought heavy losses. Mao Zedong's strategy of encircling the cities from the countryside, and later Deng Xiaoping's call to "take our own path", are presented as the turning points. Leng then argues that the path did not "fall from the sky": it is rooted in over 5,000 years of continuous civilisation, so that confidence in the path, theory and system rests finally on cultural confidence. Leng points to China's rapid industrialisation, rapid economic growth and long-term social stability as evidence that the path is correct, workable and effective.

Leng concludes that China should neither return to the "closed and rigid old path" nor take the "evil path" of changing the Party's banner, and should hold unwaveringly to the Chinese path. Leng says this does not mean standing still: China should learn from the beneficial achievements of other civilisations and welcome well-meant criticism. It rejects lecturing from outsiders, insisting that socialism with Chinese characteristics is socialism and not some other "ism". Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official People's Daily framed the "Chinese path" and its link to civilisational continuity after the 2021 Resolution.
quoteEn: No country or nation in the world can achieve development and rejuvenation by cutting itself off from its own realities and slavishly following another's path, and no unchanging path can guide all countries and nations to development and rejuvenation.
quoteZh: 世界上没有哪一个国家和民族能够脱离本国实际，通过亦步亦趋、走别人的道路来实现自己的发展振兴，也没有一条一成不变的道路可以引导所有国家和民族实现发展振兴。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's current model and ideology, associated with Deng Xiaoping and the reform era. It combines Marxist-Leninist commitments with market reforms and Chinese conditions.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, associated with the Chinese Dream. It means restoring China to national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation".
The policy launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. It shifted the focus to economic development through domestic reform and opening to the outside world.
A concept stressed under Xi Jinping. It adds confidence in Chinese culture to confidence in the path, theory and system of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

glossary.zh: 党的十九届六中全会决议
glossary.pinyin: Dǎng de shíjiǔ jiè liù zhōng quánhuì juéyì
glossary.en: the Resolution on the Party's major achievements and historical experience
glossary.explanation: The Party's third "historical resolution", adopted in November 2021. It summarises a century of Party history and lists ten lessons of historical experience.

t: Socialism with Chinese characteristics and its multidimensional innovation of the form of human civilization
zh: 中国特色社会主义对人类文明形态的多维创新
paras: Responding to Xi Jinping's claim at the centenary of the Communist Party (2021) that socialism with Chinese characteristics has created "a new form of human civilization", Jin Fenglin asks in what sense it is "new". The article argues that the answer emerges only when the Party's achievement is set within the long history of traditional Chinese civilization and within a global comparison with Western capitalist civilization.

The article has three sections. The first takes the long historical view, sketching the traditional Chinese civilizational form, its Qin-Han and Sui-Tang peaks, and its dynastic cycles. The second compares socialism with Chinese characteristics with capitalist civilization, drawing on Marx, the Keynesian and neoliberal phases, Piketty and US wealth data. The third traces the line from utopian and scientific socialism through Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping to the present.

Jin's first move is that traditional China's agrarian economy, with stagnant productive forces, produced a recurring cycle of dynastic rise and collapse. In Jin's account the Party, through the people-centred stance and the democratic supervision Mao Zedong described to Huang Yanpei in 1945, has taken China out of that cycle and raised the old civilization to a new level. The second move holds that capitalism, whatever its policy adjustments over five centuries, remains defined by the supremacy of capital, the alienation of public power and the exploitation of labour. Jin cites shareholder primacy, the 2008 crisis, "one dollar, one vote" politics, and widening inequality as evidence of a crisis in Western civilization. Against this, Jin credits Chinese socialism with poverty reduction, social security coverage, institutional reform and a market economy that combines state and private capital. The third move is that the five-fold advance of material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization has created Chinese modernization.

Jin concludes that socialism with Chinese characteristics has renewed traditional Chinese civilization and broken the monopoly of the Western capitalist form. In Jin's reading it also refutes the "end of history" thesis and shows that each country must build socialism from its own conditions, so that different forms of civilization can coexist. A civilization's worth, Jin argues, should be judged by its contribution to resolving international disputes and shared human problems, not by victories over rivals. Read the original if you want an example of how a Central Party School scholar frames the "new form of human civilization" claim through history and comparison with capitalism.
quoteEn: The new form of civilization of socialism with Chinese characteristics goes beyond the narrow vision of contemporary capitalist civilization, which is centred on the logic of capital.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义文明新形态超越了当代资本主义文明形态以资本逻辑为中心的狭隘视野

glossary.en: a new form of human civilization
glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping used in his speech marking the Party's centenary in 2021. It presents China's path as a new civilizational form that goes beyond both traditional Chinese civilization and Western capitalist modernity.

The official name for China's own path to modernity, set against Western models. It is described by the Party as combining the five dimensions of material, political, spiritual, social and ecological civilization.
The official term for the Party's governing ideology and system since the reform era, usually dated to Deng Xiaoping. It combines Marxism with Chinese conditions and a socialist market economy.

t: Party-organisation-led cooperatives as an effective path for developing the new-type rural collective economy
st: Lessons from the "Yantai practice"
zh: 党组织领办合作社是发展新型农村集体经济的有效路径
zhSub: “烟台实践”的启示
paras: Writing in 2022, Jiang Yu takes up several questions on which, the author says, consensus is still lacking: what the new-type rural collective economy is, why it should be developed, whether it is a "return to the old road", and how it differs from the pre-reform collective economy and from farmer-initiated specialised cooperatives. The article argues that Party-branch-led cooperatives, pioneered in Yantai, Shandong, are an effective and feasible path for gradually strengthening the collective economy under market conditions.

The article first reviews the history of rural collectives, from agricultural cooperativisation and the people's communes through the household contract responsibility system to developments since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then proposes a definition of the new-type rural collective economy and distinguishes it from share-based cooperatives, companies and spontaneous specialised cooperatives. The final section describes the Yantai experience and draws general lessons from it.

Jiang concludes from the history that the collective economy is a product of revolution and socialist transformation, not a voluntary association of small private owners, and that household contracting changed only the mode of operation, not the collective ownership of land. The author defines the new-type economy as public ownership in which a group of labourers jointly hold the means of production, and rejects equating it with the unallocated assets of reformed "share-economy cooperatives". Quantifying shares to individuals, Jiang warns, is only a first step. If assets became divisible and transferable they would amount to private ownership. In the Yantai model, the Party branch registers a cooperative in which the village collective and villagers pool land, funds and labour. In Jiang's account, only Party leadership can organise dispersed farmers, keep the cooperatives "public rather than private", and negotiate with capital, as in the Beiluotang village orchard deal.

Jiang concludes that the new road of agricultural cooperation must put Party leadership at its core: ideological, political and organisational. The author presents this as a spiral upward from the people's communes rather than a retreat, and calls for institutionalising the Yantai approach and for higher-level governments to give cooperatives financial and policy support. Jiang also says the cooperative form is a workaround, given the absence of a full legal framework for collective economic organisations. Read the original if you want a Party-affiliated policy researcher's detailed case for rural collective ownership and for the Yantai model, including its legal and ownership arguments.
quoteEn: Only by upholding the Party's political leadership can cooperatives be ensured to be "public rather than private" and to truly serve the interests of the broadest mass of farmers.
quoteZh: 只有坚持党的政治领导，才能确保合作社“姓公不姓私”，真正为最广大农民利益服务。

glossary.explanation: A term used in Party documents for a renewed form of village collective ownership and operation, distinct from the people's commune era. Xi Jinping has called for developing it as part of rural revitalisation and common prosperity.

glossary.literal: cooperatives initiated and run by the Party branch
glossary.explanation: A model developed in Yantai, Shandong, from 2017, in which village Party branches register and lead farmers' cooperatives that pool land, funds and labour.
The post-1978 arrangement under which collectively owned land was contracted to individual households for farming, replacing collective production in the people's communes.

t: Keeping national strategic priorities in view while continuing to advance rural revitalization across the board
zh: 着眼国家重大战略接续全面推进乡村振兴
paras: Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in early 2022, Han Yang interprets the Central Committee and State Council's No. 1 Document for 2022 on key tasks in comprehensively advancing rural revitalization. The article argues that, in a period of global upheaval and the pandemic, agriculture, rural areas and farmers must serve as the "ballast stone" and stabiliser of the economy, so that work on them should be governed by the keynote of "stability".

The piece is organised around three questions drawn from the document: what to hold on to and how, what to push forward and how, and what to guarantee and how. It opens by placing 2022 within the Party's two centenary goals, the 14th Five-Year Plan and the 2035 targets, and stresses that rural revitalization, unlike poverty alleviation, is a protracted campaign rather than a decisive battle.

Han sets out two bottom lines: national grain security and no large-scale return to poverty. On grain, the author cites output above 650 million tonnes for seven consecutive years and calls for "storing grain in the land and in technology", covering farmland protection, seed-source research, machinery and soybean expansion. On poverty, the article calls for continued monitoring, support for industries and employment in lifted-out areas, and stable transition-period policies. Three tasks follow: industrial revitalization through integrating primary, secondary and tertiary sectors and county-level development; steady rural construction that respects farmers' wishes; and better rural governance, given population outflow and ageing. The article cites 292.51 million migrant workers in 2021.

For guarantees, Han lists people (talent, training of high-quality farmers), money (public budget priority, rural financial services, agricultural insurance) and land (extending second-round land contracts by 30 years, pilot reforms of homestead land, and cautious entry of collectively owned commercial construction land into the market). The article ends by insisting on full Party leadership over rural work, including the "five levels of secretaries" responsibility system, performance assessments of officials and a coordinating mechanism at central level. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of the 2022 No. 1 Document and its priorities in grain security, poverty-return prevention and rural governance.
quoteEn: Comprehensively advancing rural revitalization differs from poverty alleviation: it is a protracted war, not a decisive assault.
quoteZh: 全面推进乡村振兴不同于脱贫攻坚，是持久战而不是攻坚战。

glossary.explanation: A national strategy announced in 2017 and elaborated in a 2018 plan, aiming at modernising agriculture, rural industries, environment, governance and living standards. It succeeded poverty alleviation as the focus of rural policy from 2021.
A shorthand for agriculture, the countryside and peasants, used for the cluster of rural policy issues. The annual No. 1 Document of the Central Committee has addressed them since 2004.
The campaign to eliminate extreme rural poverty by 2020, which the Chinese government declared completed that year. The article treats it as the precondition for rural revitalization.

glossary.pinyin: cáng liáng yú dì, cáng liáng yú jì
glossary.en: storing grain in the land and in technology
glossary.literal: hide grain in land, hide grain in technology
glossary.explanation: A grain-security strategy that seeks to sustain production capacity through farmland protection and agricultural technology rather than stockpiles alone.

glossary.pinyin: wǔ jí shūji zhuā xiāngcūn zhènxīng
glossary.literal: five levels of secretaries take charge of revitalization
glossary.explanation: A responsibility system under which Party secretaries at provincial, city, county, township and village levels are all held accountable for rural revitalization.

t: Building a new pattern of economic work rooted in market entities
zh: 构筑扎根于市场主体的经济工作新格局
paras: In this short commentary, first published in Economic Daily and posted in March 2022, Gao Peiyong asks how economic work should be done amid unprecedented risks and challenges in the new development stage. His answer is that it should be rooted in market entities. He presents the Party Central Committee's new judgements, measures and formulations on this point as an innovation in adapting Marxist political economy to China and as part of Xi Jinping's economic thought.

The piece first explains the shift from the concept of the enterprise to that of the market entity. It then sets out the status that Xi Jinping assigns to market entities and closes with the tasks ahead under the Central Economic Work Conference's deployment.

Gao notes that, under the newly issued Regulations on the Registration and Administration of Market Entities, market entities cover enterprises, individual businesses and farmers' professional cooperatives, that is, every economic unit that creates GDP. In Gao's metaphor, large and medium-sized enterprises are the aorta of economic activity and small and micro units are its capillaries. Moving analysis from one to the other means that economic work and macro policy can reach all sources of GDP. Gao also cites Xi's description of market entities as the main participants in economic activity, the main providers of jobs and the main drivers of technological progress. On this basis Gao argues that, in extreme situations, keeping the economy running depends on preserving market entities, so risk prevention must begin with their risks.

Gao concludes that a pattern of economic work rooted in and organised around market entities is taking shape. Under the keynote of "seeking progress while maintaining stability", Gao calls for continued focus on market entities and for efforts to stimulate their vitality. Read the original if you want a brief, authoritative statement of why policy discourse in 2022 shifted from enterprises to market entities.
quoteEn: Moving macroeconomic analysis from the "aorta" to the "capillaries" clearly means that the starting point and destination of China's economic work and macro-policy allocation are increasingly shifting towards, and concentrating on, the micro-foundational level.
quoteZh: 宏观经济分析由“主动脉”深入“毛细血管”，显然意味着，我国经济工作和宏观政策配置的出发点和落脚点越来越向微观基础层面转移和集聚。

glossary.explanation: The body of economic ideas attributed to Xi Jinping and presented in official discourse as the guiding framework for China's economic work since the 2010s.
A legal and policy category covering enterprises, individual businesses and farmers' cooperatives, all of which are registered and take part in market activity.
An official term for the period after China's first centenary goal, in which the country is to build a modern socialist country.

glossary.pinyin: wěn zì dāngtóu, wěn zhōng qiú jìn
glossary.literal: put stability first, seek progress within stability
glossary.explanation: The official keynote of China's economic work, giving priority to stability while pursuing progress.
An annual meeting of Party and state leaders, usually held in December, that sets the economic agenda for the following year.

t: A historical examination of the Communist Party of China's strategic thinking and its present-day lessons
zh: 中国共产党战略思维的历史考察与现实启示
source: Journal of the China Executive Leadership Academy Jinggangshan, 2021 no. 6
paras: Du Min asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has treated and used strategic thinking over its first hundred years, and what lessons this holds for the present. The article, published in 2021, argues that the Party has consistently prized strategic thinking and applied it well in revolution, construction and reform. In Du's account this is what carried the country "from standing up to becoming prosperous and then strong".

The article has four parts. The first traces how successive leadership generations stressed strategy: Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, the Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao period, and Xi Jinping. The second surveys how the Party applied strategic thinking in three dimensions: the whole (accurate strategic judgements), the long term (goals and development strategies) and the fundamental (priorities and initiative). The third distils lessons, and the fourth sets out how leading cadres should raise their strategic capacity.

Du's central move is to treat strategic thinking as the practical application of Marxist materialist dialectics. It handles relations such as essence and appearance, whole and part, long-term and immediate, principal and secondary. Du holds that the Party's strategic thinking, as expressed in Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, has also enriched dialectics. The second lesson is a people-centred strategic standpoint: the people are the starting point and goal of strategic decisions and the source of their strength and wisdom, which Du illustrates with Mao's, Deng's and Xi's remarks on learning from the masses. Du also records that the 16th Party Congress (2002) was the first to write "strategic thinking" into a congress report. The article further notes that Xi introduced "strategic resolve" in 2012, and the 19th Party Congress (2017) listed strategic thinking first among the leaders' thinking capacities.

Du concludes that strategic thinking is "always the way of thinking Communists should establish" and proposes four pairs of balances for cadres. These are coordinating all aspects while stressing priorities, holding to principle while staying flexible, seizing opportunities while meeting challenges, and strengthening resolve while pursuing innovation. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Party discourse presents strategic thinking across successive leaderships, with many quotations from Mao, Deng, Jiang, Hu and Xi.
quoteEn: Strategic thinking is expressed above all in handling properly the relations between essence and appearance, whole and part, long term and present, principal and secondary, individual and general, and it stresses observing, thinking about, analysing and solving problems from the standpoint of the whole, the long term and the fundamental.
quoteZh: 战略思维，突出表现在妥善处理好本质与现象、全局与局部、长远与当前、主要与次要、个体与共性等的关系上，强调要从全局上、长远上、根本上观察、思考、分析与解决问题。

glossary.explanation: A concept Xi Jinping introduced in late 2012, meaning the capacity to hold to long-term strategic goals without being swayed by short-term shifts. It is usually paired with strategic confidence and strategic patience.
Hu Jintao's guiding concept, emphasising people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.

t: The historical-materialist narrative of the Great Founding Spirit of the Party and its dimensions for the new journey
zh: 伟大建党精神的唯物史观叙事及新征程向度
source: Journal of Tongji University (Social Sciences Edition), 2021 no. 6
paras: Liu Shun asks how the Great Founding Spirit of the Party, as formally put forward in 2021, should be understood. The article contends that its formation and formulation are not a formulaic ideological construction but follow a historical-materialist logic that explains ideas from material practice rather than the reverse. Liu argues that the Spirit arose from the Party's leadership of revolution, construction and reform, and that it should now guide the Party's second-centenary journey.

The article is organised into five parts. Four "narratives" – of value, of formation, of problems and of the subject – read the Spirit through historical materialism. A fifth part sets out its dimensions for the new journey. The formation narrative runs through four periods: the New Democratic revolution, the establishment of basic socialist institutions, reform and opening up, and the era since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Liu's core move is to link each element of the Spirit to a Marxist category. On value, the Spirit is said to match historical materialism's stress on actuality: it serves "real people" rather than abstract ones, rests on the practically confirmed path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, and charts the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The author contrasts the Party with Western parties, which are described as driven by interest groups and electoral competition. On problems, the Spirit is read as reflecting the Party's grasp of the basic contradiction between productive forces and relations of production, and of the principal contradiction of each stage, including its redefinition in the new era. On the subject, Liu holds that the people are the fundamental force creating history, and treats the Party's stress on the unity of the people and the "country" as its expression.

For the new journey Liu proposes four conversions of the Spirit: into a new upsurge of struggle for a better life, including common prosperity; into new momentum for modernization, through the new development stage, the new development philosophy and a new development pattern; into practice towards the lofty ideal of communism; and into conscious action to build a community with a shared future for mankind. Liu presents these as the Spirit's active role as part of the superstructure. Read the original if you want to see how a 2021 academic article ties the official Party-spirit discourse to historical-materialist categories and to the policy agenda of the second centenary goal.
quoteEn: The Great Founding Spirit has never been an empty idea that discusses spirit for its own sake; it is deeply embedded with insight into the basic contradictions of society.
quoteZh: 伟大建党精神从来都不是“就精神谈精神”的空洞理念，而是深嵌着对社会基本矛盾的洞悉。

glossary.en: Great Founding Spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation put forward by Xi Jinping in July 2021 at the Party's centenary. It names the spirit of the Party's founders as upholding truth and ideals, fulfilling the original aspiration and mission, fighting bravely, and being loyal to the Party and faithful to the people.
A goal of socialism in Chinese official discourse, stressing prosperity shared by all rather than a few. It was given renewed emphasis from 2021.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept of foreign policy and global governance, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states.
Official guideline calling for innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, introduced in 2015.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, presented as restoring China's strength and status after the modern period of decline.

The Party's official judgement of the central social contradiction at each stage. Since 2017 it has been defined as that between the people's growing need for a better life and unbalanced and inadequate development.

t: Marxism's people-centred and practical character fully carried out in China
zh: 马克思主义人民性和实践性在中国得到充分贯彻
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in Guangming Daily in March 2022, takes up a formulation from the Party's third historical resolution, adopted at the Sixth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2021): that the people-centred character (renmin xing) and the practical character (shijian xing) of Marxism have been fully carried out in China. Liu argues that both qualities have been demonstrated across a century of revolution, construction and reform, and that they will continue to drive the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece has three parts. The first treats the people-centred character of Marxism as it appears in the passage from oppression to a moderately prosperous society in all respects. The second treats its practical character, from semi-colonial, semi-feudal China to building a modern socialist country. The third turns to what must be done to uphold both qualities in future.

On the first quality, Liu holds that Marxism sees the people as the subject of history and that the Party has kept to this position since its founding. The article runs through the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era, and presents each as a stage in which the Party led the people from national independence to the leap from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" and then "becoming strong". On the second, Liu argues that practice is what distinguishes Marxism from other theories. The article presents successive Party leaders from Mao Zedong to Xi Jinping as having adapted Marxism's basic principles to Chinese conditions and traditional culture and tested them in practice, guided by seeking truth from facts.

Liu concludes that the Party has joined the two qualities in the whole process of revolution, construction and reform, opening up socialism with Chinese characteristics, Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilization. Looking ahead, the article calls for a people-centred approach to development, aimed at common prosperity and at the free and all-round development of the person. It also calls for theoretical innovation grounded in practice, and for continuing to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 2021 historical resolution's language on Marxism was explained to a general readership in the official press.
quoteEn: The practical character is Marxism's inherent theoretical quality and the essence of why it retains its vitality; knowledge can be continually tested, developed and perfected only in practice.
quoteZh: 实践性是马克思主义固有的理论品格，是马克思主义永葆强大生命力的要义所在，认识只有在实践中才能不断得到检验、发展和完善。

glossary.explanation: Official term for China's own path to modernization, promoted by the Party leadership especially since 2021 as distinct from Western models.
Official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, stressed in Party documents as an essential requirement of socialism.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: Central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing, often tied to the two centenary goals of 2021 and 2049.
Ideological line associated with Mao Zedong and revived by Deng Xiaoping; it requires policy and theory to proceed from actual conditions and be tested in practice.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: How the Communist Party of China led young people to Yan'an
zh: 中国共产党引领青年奔赴延安
paras: This short commentary, first published in China Social Sciences Today on 5 July 2021 during the Party History study and education campaign, asks why the Communist Party of China could draw so many young people to Yan'an during the War of Resistance against Japan. The authors note that by the end of 1938 more than 100,000 intellectuals, many of them young, had gone there despite hardship and danger. They argue that three factors explain this appeal.

The article first covers the Party's patriotic leadership of the anti-Japanese national united front. It then turns to its spread of Marxist theory, and finally to its governance of Yan'an as a revolutionary base. It closes with remarks on youth work today.

Luo and Zhou contend that the Party raised the banner of patriotism after the 1931 Mukden Incident, in contrast to the Nationalist government's concessions, and trained cadres at the Anti-Japanese Military and Political University. Second, by adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, works such as Mao Zedong's On Protracted War gave young people a convincing account of the nation's future. Popular works such as Mass Philosophy made theory accessible, and Yan'an grew into a city of study with many schools. Third, the authors describe Yan'an as youthful, song-filled and free of corruption, citing Ding Ling, He Qifang, Mao's 1940 list of Yan'an's virtues and Tan Kah Kee's remark that China's hope lay in Yan'an.

The authors conclude that winning over youth was an important reason for the Party's revolutionary victory. They call for equipping today's young people with Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, explained in language they can accept. They also want stronger youth policy and a deeper sense of national feeling. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party history presents Yan'an's attraction for young people and links it to current youth work.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China has served not only as the vanguard of the Chinese working class but also as the vanguard of the Chinese people and the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 中国共产党不仅担当了中国工人阶级的先锋队，也担当了中国人民和中华民族的先锋队。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context
glossary.explanation: The Party's term for applying Marxism to China's concrete conditions, associated especially with Mao Zedong's writings of the Yan'an period.
The alliance of Chinese political forces, including the Communists and Nationalists, against Japanese invasion, formed in the late 1930s.

t: Reform and opening up and the new path of Chinese modernization
zh: 改革开放与中国式现代化新道路
paras: Zhang Shengen and Huang Xiaowu ask how the Communist Party's four decades of reform and opening up produced what they call a new path of Chinese modernization and a new form of human civilization. Writing in early 2022, they argue that Deng Xiaoping's concept of 'Chinese-style modernization', introduced at the start of reform, set the direction. In their account, the Party then enriched the concept in stages, from the 1980s to the 19th Party Congress (2017) and the 19th Central Committee's Fifth Plenum (2020).

The article is a chronological survey in three parts. The first covers the launch of reform after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) and Deng's 1979 formulations. The second follows the stated goals from a 'highly civilized, highly democratic' socialist country with a moderately prosperous society, through the three-step strategy of the 13th Party Congress (1987) and the 15th Party Congress (1997), to the comprehensive building of a moderately prosperous society under the Scientific Outlook on Development. The third turns to the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

The authors give four reasons why Deng put forward Chinese-style modernization: the need for realistic goals, lessons from history, knowledge of other countries' modernization, and an assessment of China's conditions. On their reading, the target of the end of the century was lowered from the four modernizations to a 'moderately prosperous' household. They trace how the content widened beyond industry, agriculture, defence and science to democracy, spiritual civilization, social harmony and ecology, which gave the 'five-in-one' overall plan. They report that the 19th Congress brought forward the date for basically realizing modernization to 2035. They also set out Xi Jinping's five features: a huge population, common prosperity, coordination of material and cultural-ethical progress, harmony between humanity and nature, and peaceful development.

The authors conclude that the Party's understanding of modernization has deepened continuously, and that the new path and new form of civilization were created within socialism with Chinese characteristics. In their view, the path draws on China's long history, widens the options for developing countries that want independence, and shows the world-historical significance of the Chinese revolution. They urge strengthened confidence in the path, theory, system and culture. Read the original if you want a detailed, official-line chronology of how Party congress documents and Deng-era statements built up the concept of Chinese modernization.
quoteEn: By proposing Chinese-style modernization, Deng Xiaoping both set China's modernization goals in a realistic way and made clear the path modernization should follow, defining its direction.
quoteZh: 邓小平提出搞中国式现代化，既实事求是地确定了我国现代化的发展目标，又明确指出了现代化建设所应遵循的路径，规定了现代化发展的方向。

glossary.explanation: Term first used by Deng Xiaoping in 1979 for a modernization suited to China's conditions. Later developed by Xi Jinping as a core Party concept.
A Chinese term for a comfortable level of well-being. Deng used it in 1979 as a modest target for modernization, and later Party congresses made it a stage goal.
Guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, put forward after 2003 and written into Party documents at the 17th Party Congress (2007). It stresses balanced and sustainable development.
Goal of prosperity shared by all the people, which the Party describes as an essential requirement of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Continuing to promote the spirit of historical initiative through fearless responsibility and great struggle
zh: 在无畏担当和伟大斗争中继续发扬历史主动精神
paras: This short commentary in Guangming Daily (March 2022) takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the opening of a training course for young and middle-aged cadres at the Central Party School. Xu Xiaoming argues that Party members, and leading cadres in particular, must keep up the spirit of historical initiative by combining a willingness to take responsibility with a readiness to struggle, if the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is to be achieved.

The piece defines historical initiative as the Party's conscious, Marxist-guided effort to transform history on the basis of grasping its laws. It then looks back over the Party's century, lists the spirit lineage it has produced, and turns to the present international environment and to shortcomings among some cadres.

Xu's central move is to treat responsibility and struggle as mutually reinforcing: responsibility tempers the courage to struggle, and struggle shows the ability to bear responsibility. In the author's account, the Party's history is both a history of responsibility and of struggle, from the Jinggangshan and Long March spirits to the anti-epidemic spirit. Xu says that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) the Central Committee has led major struggles, which demand more of cadres. The article also criticises a minority of cadres who avoid major tasks or decline to take a position on questions of principle, saying this weakens the Party's fighting capacity.

Xu concludes that, amid what is described as great changes unseen in a century and the pandemic, risks will grow more complex. Cadres are urged to keep "the nation's greatest interests" in mind, root fearless responsibility in practice, and pass the spirit on. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party Schools framed the call for responsibility and struggle among cadres in early 2022.
quoteEn: Struggle and responsibility are precious historical qualities of the Communist Party of China; they promote and complement each other.
quoteZh: 斗争与担当是中国共产党宝贵的历史品格，二者相互促进、相辅相成。

glossary.explanation: A phrase in Party discourse for consciously and actively shaping history on the basis of understanding its laws. The article ties it to Xi Jinping's 2022 speech to cadres.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official goal of restoring China's national strength and standing, closely associated with Xi Jinping's leadership.
The Party's official list of named "spirits" from different historical periods, such as the Long March spirit and the Yan'an spirit, traced back to the founding spirit.
The 2012 congress at which Xi Jinping became General Secretary; Party writings use it to mark the start of the "new era".

t: Mao Zedong's theory of contradiction and its contribution to Marxist-Leninist dialectics
zh: 毛泽东矛盾论对马克思列宁辩证法的贡献
paras: Cheng Guangyun, in a short piece first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in October 2021, asks what readers should focus on when they revisit Mao Zedong's "On Contradiction". Cheng treats the theory of contradiction as Mao's main contribution to Marxist-Leninist dialectics and, with the theory of practice, one half of the "Two Essays". Cheng's thesis is that it works both as a worldview and as a methodology.

The article takes Alain Badiou's five propositions on the law of the unity of opposites as its starting point. Cheng groups the first two (all reality is process; every process reduces to a set of contradictions) as a "set theory of contradiction". The remaining three (the principal contradiction, the principal aspect, and antagonistic versus non-antagonistic contradictions) become an "algebra of contradiction". The piece then considers readings by Louis Althusser and Norman Levine, and ends with lessons for the present.

On the worldview side, Cheng notes that Mao revised the essay after 1949, replacing the heading "two views of development" with "two views of the universe". In Cheng's reading, this raised the theory from a view of development to a cosmology. Extending Engels's account of Hegel, who moved from a collection of things to a collection of processes, Mao treats the world as a collection of contradictions. Cheng presents this as a unity of ontology and epistemology. On the methodological side, Cheng traces the theory to Mao's military and political dialectics of whole and part, and reads it as a development of Lenin's definition of dialectics as the "algebra of revolution". Cheng also takes up Althusser's "overdetermination" and Badiou's elaboration of it, calling the latter possibly an over-interpretation. Cheng argues that the idea of a "cluster of contradictions" moves dialectics from linear to non-linear, complexity-oriented thinking, and describes the essay as a model work of complexity science.

Cheng places Mao closer to Lenin than to Marx, since Mao applied dialectical materialism to the political world, and notes Levine's description of the essay as "Hegelianized Leninism". Cheng attributes this to the era and to China's conditions, and says it should be viewed historically. Three lessons follow. Facing domestic and international contradictions requires strategic resolve, analysing problems with the set theory and resolving them with the algebra. Analysis of the roots of contradictions should add the historical-materialist perspective and treat each case concretely. Methods must respect complexity and avoid simplification. Read the original if you want a brief, Badiou- and Althusser-inflected reading of Mao's "On Contradiction" and its stated relevance today.
quoteEn: The theory of contradiction is not only a methodology but also a worldview, a unity of ontology (objective dialectics) and epistemology (subjective dialectics).
quoteZh: 矛盾论不仅是方法论，而且是世界观，是本体论（客观辩证法）和认识论（主观辩证法）的统一。

glossary.explanation: The collective name for Mao Zedong's philosophical works "On Practice" and "On Contradiction", written in Yan'an in 1937. They are treated in Chinese Marxism as the core of his philosophical thought.

Mao Zedong's account of dialectics, set out in "On Contradiction". It stresses the universality and particularity of contradiction, the principal contradiction and its principal aspect, and antagonistic versus non-antagonistic contradictions.
In Mao's theory, the contradiction that plays the leading and decisive role in a given process among its many contradictions.
Mao Zedong's account of knowledge as arising from and tested in practice, set out in "On Practice". It is the epistemological counterpart to the theory of contradiction.

t: Learning from history to open up the future: studying Xi Jinping's speech at the commemoration of the 110th anniversary of the Xinhai Revolution
zh: 以史为鉴、开创未来——学习贯彻习近平总书记在纪念辛亥革命110周年大会上重要讲话
paras: Writing in October 2021 for the Chinese Social Sciences Today, Bao Dawei offers a study commentary on General Secretary Xi Jinping's speech marking the 110th anniversary of the Xinhai Revolution. The article asks what the revolution's failure and its legacy teach about achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Bao's answer is that the revolution's patriotic aims were realised only under the leadership of the Communist Party, and that five lessons from the past 110 years apply to the present.

The piece moves in two stages. It first assesses the 1911 Revolution and its limits, drawing on Sun Yat-sen's own writings and speeches from 1894 to 1924, together with remarks by Chen Duxiu. It then turns to five lessons, each introduced with a sentence from Xi's speech: Party leadership, the Chinese path, struggle, the consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community, and a community with a shared future for mankind.

In Bao's analysis, the revolution failed for three reasons: its guiding ideas were abstract, its values reflected a class standpoint, and its attitude was not thoroughgoing. It borrowed from Western bourgeois thought, including Rousseau and Montesquieu, in a semi-colonial, semi-feudal country that lacked the conditions for such ideas to work. Bao reads the ensuing warlord period as showing that the real contradiction lay between the productive forces and the relations of production. Bao also stresses Sun's self-reflection after 1912. Sun turned towards socialism, praised the October Revolution, and in the new Three Principles of the People equated the principle of people's livelihood with socialism. On this account, Communists were Sun's most loyal heirs, and the Kuomintang's reorganisation took place with Communist help and Soviet assistance. Bao then ties each of the five lessons to Sun's statements, so that the history appears to support current Party positions.

Bao concludes that the dream of the revolution's pioneers is being realised under the Party. In the new journey towards a modern socialist country, amid what the article calls great changes unseen in a century and an 'East rising, West declining' trend, the five lessons are presented as guidance. Bao calls for gathering more closely around the Party Central Committee with Xi at its core. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-line commentary of 2021 draws on Sun Yat-sen's statements to link the 1911 Revolution to current Party themes.
quoteEn: The Xinhai Revolution could not find the correct path to national rejuvenation because its guiding ideas were abstract in theory, its values were class-bound in standpoint, and its revolutionary attitude was not thoroughgoing.
quoteZh: 辛亥革命之所以无法找到实现中华民族伟大复兴的正确道路，理论上是由于其指导思想的抽象性，立场上是由于其价值取向的阶级性，革命态度上是由于其不彻底性。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central goal of Party discourse since the early 2010s, presenting national strength and prosperity as the overcoming of the 'century of humiliation' that began with the Opium War.

glossary.en: the consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.literal: consciousness of the Chinese nation community
glossary.explanation: A Party concept, stressed under Xi Jinping, that all ethnic groups in China form one national community with shared interests and identity.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula for international relations, promoted since 2012–13, stressing peaceful development and shared global interests.

glossary.en: the Three Principles of the People
glossary.explanation: Sun Yat-sen's political doctrine of nationalism, democracy and people's livelihood. Its 1924 'new' version was reworked in cooperation with the Communists.

t: The 1911 Revolution: a milestone on the road to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 辛亥革命：中华民族伟大复兴征程上的里程碑
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 28 October 2021
paras: Kang Peizhu and Shang Nana, writing in a newspaper commentary after Xi Jinping's speech marking the 110th anniversary of the 1911 Revolution, ask what the revolution contributed to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. They argue that, although the bourgeois republic it created ultimately failed, the revolution was a milestone on that road. In their account it supplied the historical conditions on which the Communist Party later built.

The article is organised around five contributions, each introduced by a statement from Xi Jinping. They are: conditions for the founding of the Chinese Communist Party; a push to early modernization; a foundation for the consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community; a spur to the nation's intellectual awakening; and an impetus to national liberation movements elsewhere in Asia. A short closing section sets the revolution's limits and the Party's role as its heir.

The authors argue that the revolution ended the monarchy, and that the Provisional Constitution of the Republic of China gave citizens rights of assembly and association. They say this allowed hundreds of parties to form and opened the way for new currents of thought, including Marxism. They cite an incomplete count that about a third of the earliest Party members had direct or indirect experience of the revolution. They also credit it with early economic, political and social modernization, citing a 1933 industrial survey and the abolition of customs such as kneeling and foot-binding. On national identity, they argue that the modern concept of the Chinese nation took shape in this period, from the 'five-race republic' idea to Sun Yat-sen's 1919 call to fuse all peoples into one Chinese nation. They also argue that the shift from 'subject' to 'citizen' awakened popular political participation, citing the mass meetings against the Twenty-One Demands in 1915.

The authors conclude that the weakness and compromising nature of the national bourgeoisie made a bourgeois republic unworkable in semi-colonial, semi-feudal China. In their reading, this failure showed that the revolution needed new leadership. The Party, founded ten years later, completed the democratic tasks Sun Yat-sen left unfinished, won the New Democratic Revolution and founded the People's Republic. They present the Party as the revolution's most steadfast supporter and the leader of national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 1911 Revolution is framed in Party historiography of 2021 as a precursor to the Communist Party's role.
quoteEn: The 1911 Revolution provided a powerful impetus for the intellectual self-awareness of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 辛亥革命为中华民族思想自觉提供了强大动力

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation' that began in 1840. It is closely associated with Xi Jinping's slogan of the Chinese Dream.

Mao Zedong's term for the revolution led by the Communist Party from about 1919 to 1949, distinguished from the earlier bourgeois-led 'old democratic' revolution, of which the 1911 Revolution is the main example.
An early Republican slogan that the state was shared by the Han, Manchu, Mongol, Hui (Muslim) and Tibetan peoples. Sun Yat-sen later replaced it with the idea of a single Chinese nation.

glossary.en: consciousness of the Chinese nation as a community
glossary.explanation: A Party concept, prominent under Xi Jinping, stressing a shared national identity that unites all ethnic groups in China.

t: A milestone step: building a moderately prosperous society in all respects
zh: 具有里程碑意义的关键一步
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 10 September 2021, this commentary follows Xi Jinping's announcement at the Party's centenary celebration that the first centenary goal had been achieved. Li and Wei argue that building a moderately prosperous society in all respects is a milestone in the history of the Communist Party, of the People's Republic and of Chinese civilization. In their account it is also a key step towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three sections. The first traces how the goal of a "moderately prosperous society" developed from the start of reform and opening up through the 12th, 13th, 14th, 16th, 18th and 19th Party Congresses. The second places the achievement within national rejuvenation, citing economic, poverty-reduction and social-security figures. The third turns to its significance for developing countries and for Chinese modernization.

Li and Wei first read the goal as a promise kept to the people and to history, one that successive Party generations carried forward. They present it as the Party acting on its original aspiration and founding mission, with a people-centred standard: the result must be recognised by the people and withstand the test of history. Second, they treat it as material and political groundwork for rejuvenation. They cite 2020 GDP above 100 trillion yuan, per capita GDP above US$10,000, a middle-income group of over 400 million, and the end of absolute poverty for 98.99 million rural people. They credit Party leadership and the socialist system's capacity to concentrate resources, citing the central-provincial-local work mechanism and targeted poverty alleviation. Third, they argue that success in a country of over 1.4 billion shows the "new path" of Chinese modernization is viable. They describe it as distinct from the Western model and as an option for countries that want faster development while keeping their independence.

The authors conclude that developing countries are not confined to a single Western path, that each country's own exploration should be respected, and that China's experience offers a "Chinese approach" and "Chinese wisdom". They stress that the achievement is a starting point rather than an end, and they call for keeping to the original aspiration while working towards the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a compact example of the official People's Daily framing of the 2021 poverty-eradication and moderate-prosperity milestone, including its list of statistics and its claims about international significance.
quoteEn: Building a moderately prosperous society in all respects is not an end point, but the starting point of a new life and new struggles.
quoteZh: 全面建成小康社会不是终点，而是新生活、新奋斗的起点。

glossary.en: a moderately prosperous society in all respects
glossary.explanation: The Party's first centenary goal, drawn from the classical notion of xiaokang (modest comfort). It was proclaimed achieved in 2021 and is defined by the Party as covering the balance and sustainability of development, not just income.
The target of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021. The second centenary goal is a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official overarching aim of the Party, associated with the Chinese Dream, of restoring China to national strength and prosperity.
The official name for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models.
The policy of economic reform and engagement with the world launched in 1978.
A Party slogan, stressed under Xi Jinping, for its stated purpose of seeking the happiness of the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the nation.

t: Understanding and grasping "applying history study in practice" accurately
zh: 准确认识和把握“学史力行”
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 2 September 2021, takes up the slogan "applying history study in practice" (xue shi li xing) from the Party history study and education campaign of that year. Huang opens with Xi Jinping's statement that this is the campaign's "end point": the results of studying history to understand principle, strengthen belief and uphold virtue must become action that changes both the subjective and the objective world. The article argues that Party members should aim to make their practice forceful, effective and productive.

The piece is organised under three headings, each beginning "apply in practice": honing Party spirit, serving the people, and promoting development. Each heading is subdivided into several short exhortations. Huang draws throughout on Xi Jinping's formulations and on the Party's hundred-year history as the source of lessons, and does not discuss particular historical episodes in detail.

On Party spirit, Huang holds that it is not innate and must be built through continuous education. The author calls for upholding the Party's overall leadership, strengthening the Four Consciousnesses and the Two Upholds, drawing on the great founding spirit of the Party, and practising strict self-discipline. On serving the people, the commentary treats the Party's history as a record of putting the people first. It links the mass line to the Marxist view of the masses as makers of history, and to whole-process people's democracy and common prosperity. On development, Huang asks cadres to connect history study with their work, by grasping the new development stage, applying the new development philosophy fully, speeding up the new development pattern of dual circulation, and balancing development with security.

Huang concludes that Party members should turn history study into concrete results, so as to open up new prospects for the cause of the Party and the state on what the text calls a new "road to the examination", the path towards the second centenary goal. The article is a programmatic statement of how the Party presents the practical purpose of history education. Read the original if you want a compact example of official 2021 language on Party-building, people-centred governance and economic strategy as joined in one campaign slogan.
quoteEn: The Party's hundred-year history is a history of putting its original aspiration and mission into practice, and a history of constantly seeking happiness for the people.

glossary.explanation: One of four aims of the 2021 Party history study and education campaign, alongside learning history to understand principle, strengthen belief and uphold virtue. It stresses turning study into practical action.

t: An epoch-making event: the founding of the Communist Party of China
zh: 开天辟地的大事变
paras: This commentary, published in the People's Daily in September 2021, takes as its starting point Xi Jinping's statement at the ceremony marking the Party's centenary that the emergence of the Communist Party in China was an "epoch-making event". Ni Bangwen argues that the founding of the Party changed the direction and course of the Chinese nation's modern development, the fate of the Chinese people, and the trends and configuration of world development. The author calls for understanding this significance from a broad spatial and temporal perspective.

The piece is organised in three parts that follow the three clauses of Xi's formulation. The first treats the nation's direction and course after the Opium War; the second, the future and destiny of the Chinese people and nation, running from the founding of the People's Republic to the reform era and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012); the third, the Party's effect on the world. Each part opens with a quotation from Xi and then offers a historical account.

In Ni's account, the failure of earlier salvation schemes after the Opium War arose above all from the lack of an advanced party as a leading core. The Party, by adopting Marxism and integrating it with Chinese realities and fine traditional culture, is said to have shifted the Chinese people from a passive to an active spiritual state and, through its wars, to have won national independence. Ni then cites achievements: the First Five-Year Plan, the world's second-largest economy, GDP above 100 trillion yuan, per capita GDP above 10,000 US dollars, and the elimination of absolute poverty. Internationally, Ni argues, the founding of the People's Republic broke the colonial system, and Chinese modernization offers developing countries a path that preserves independence. The article describes the community with a shared future for mankind and the common values of humanity as Chinese contributions to global governance.

Ni concludes that under Party leadership the nation has moved from standing up, to becoming prosperous, to becoming strong, and that national rejuvenation is now an irreversible process. The author urges keeping the country's fate in its own hands and advancing towards the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a compact example of the official People's Daily narrative on the Party's centenary and its claimed national and global significance.
quoteEn: The success of the new path of Chinese modernization shows that there is no fixed model of modernization, and that what suits a country is best.
quoteZh: 中国式现代化新道路的成功表明，现代化道路并没有固定模式，适合自己的才是最好的。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's own path to modernization, presented as distinct from Western models; it became a prominent slogan under Xi Jinping.

glossary.explanation: The goals of building a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary (2021) and a modern socialist great power by the centenary of the People's Republic (2049).

t: Understanding the great historical significance of building a moderately prosperous society in all respects
zh: 深刻理解全面建成小康社会的伟大历史意义
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 9 September 2021, this commentary by Chen Jin follows Xi Jinping's announcement at the Party's centenary celebration (2021) that the first centenary goal had been met and a moderately prosperous society had been built in all respects. Chen asks what this achievement means historically and argues that it has three kinds of significance: for the path of modernization, for the strengths of China's institutions, and for the next stage of national rejuvenation.

The article is organised in three sections after a brief opening. The first traces how the goal of modernization was defined from Mao Zedong's 1945 slogan on industrialization, through the 1978 target of the four modernizations, to Deng Xiaoping's idea of a 'xiaokang' household. The second concerns poverty alleviation and what it shows about the national system and governance. The third looks ahead to the second centenary goal of a modern socialist country.

Chen's central claim is that the goal changed in content as understanding deepened. Deng's xiaokang was first measured by per capita output, with a target of 800 US dollars by the end of the twentieth century. The 18th Party Congress (2012) then set five dimensions, and Xi's 2015 formula treated moderate prosperity as all-round progress across five domains. Chen also treats the elimination of poverty as an essential requirement of socialism. He cites 98.99 million rural poor lifted out of poverty, 832 counties removed from the poverty list and 128,000 villages, and reads this as showing three institutional strengths: centralised, unified Party leadership; a people-centred approach aimed at common prosperity; and the ability to concentrate resources on major undertakings.

Chen concludes that the achievement lays a solid base for the second centenary goal and is a key step in the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, one that he calls irreversible. He cites figures including GDP above 100 trillion yuan, per capita GDP above 10,000 US dollars and more than 400 million people in the middle-income group. He also holds that it strengthens the Four-sphere Confidence and offers other countries a Chinese option for developing while keeping their independence. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how Party media framed the meaning of the moderately prosperous society in 2021.
quoteEn: Building a moderately prosperous society in all respects is a stage-specific goal that the Party, uniting and leading the people, gradually clarified and set in the course of socialist modernization.
quoteZh: 全面建成小康社会，是我们党团结带领人民在进行社会主义现代化建设过程中逐步明确和设立的一个阶段性目标。

glossary.explanation: A Confucian-derived term for a comfortable standard of living, adopted by Deng Xiaoping in 1979 as a modernization target. 'Building a moderately prosperous society in all respects' was the first centenary goal.

t: The rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is irreversible
zh: 中华民族伟大复兴不可逆转
paras: This commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 8 September 2021, interprets a central claim in Xi Jinping's speech marking the centenary of the Communist Party of China (CPC): that the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation has entered an irreversible historical process. Shuang argues that the claim rests on historical necessity. It also rests on the Party's leadership and on continued struggle.

The piece has three parts. The first sets out the historical foundations of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The second explains why the CPC is the "core of leadership". The third lists what the Party and the people must do in what the author calls the critical period of the rejuvenation. Throughout, Shuang quotes Xi Jinping's speech and presents the Party's hundred-year history as a single narrative.

On history, Shuang points to three sources of confidence. One is the long continuity of Chinese civilisation, which Marxism is said to have reactivated in a time of crisis. Another is successive generations' struggle for national revival. The author says each stage created a condition for the rejuvenation: new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. The third is Xi's formula that "time and momentum are on our side". On leadership, Shuang attributes the Party's capacity to its guidance by Marxism, which was adapted through Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The author also credits the Party's qualities and its focus on a single theme of national rejuvenation over a century.

Shuang concludes that the rejuvenation requires three things. These are an enduring spirit of struggle against risks to Party leadership, sovereignty, security, development and core interests; sober awareness of the "examination" the era sets, through the Party's self-reform and a great new project of Party building; and strategic resolve to stay on the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The author rejects both a "closed and rigid old path" and an "evil path of changing banners". quoteEn: To get China's affairs done well, the key lies in the Party.
