t: The great achievements and profound lessons of economic and social construction in new China
zh: 新中国经济社会建设的伟大成就与深刻启示
authors: Policy Research Office of the National Development and Reform Commission
paras: This commentary, written by the Policy Research Office of the National Development and Reform Commission and published in the People's Daily in September 2021, reviews 72 years of economic and social construction in the People's Republic. It argues that under the Party's leadership the country has created the "two miracles" of rapid economic growth and long-term social stability, built a moderately prosperous society in all respects, and entered an irreversible historical process towards the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The text has two parts. The first lists achievements in seven areas: economic strength and structural change, poverty elimination and living standards, scientific and technological self-reliance, ecological protection, reform and opening up, and national security. The second draws six lessons from this record. Most of the evidence is statistical, and the figures are the author's own.

On the record, the article reports that GDP rose from 67.91 billion yuan in 1952 to 101.6 trillion yuan in 2020, and that China moved from a backward agricultural country to the world's largest industrial one. It cites the removal of 98.99 million rural people from poverty under the current standard over eight years, forest cover rising from 8.6% to 23.04%, and a pledge of carbon peaking before 2030 and carbon neutrality before 2060. It credits the Party Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, since the 18th Party Congress (2012), with historic change in each area.

The six lessons are: uphold the Party's overall leadership; keep to a people-centred development philosophy; arm the mind with the Party's innovative theory, namely Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era; keep to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, described as the only correct one; improve and develop its institutions; and apply correct methods, including seeking truth from facts and systems thinking. For the "new journey" the author calls for the Two Upholds and for implementing the new development philosophy, building a new development pattern and pursuing high-quality development. Read the original if you want a compact example of the official narrative of seven decades of development, with its headline statistics and standard formulations, as presented for the Party's centenary year.
quoteEn: Leadership by the Communist Party of China is the most essential feature of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the greatest strength of its system; it is the foundation and lifeblood of the Party and the state, and bound up with the interests and destiny of the people of all ethnic groups.

t: The world-historical significance of the Communist Party of China's century of struggle
zh: 中国共产党百年奋斗的世界历史意义
paras: Written for the centenary of the Communist Party of China (2021), this commentary asks what the Party's hundred years of struggle have contributed beyond China. Taking its cue from Xi Jinping's statement that the Party's path, cause and achievements will enter the annals of both the Chinese nation and human civilization, Tang argues that the century has world-historical significance in four respects: modernization, Marxist party-building, world socialism and global peace and development.

The article is organised as four numbered sections, each opening with a statement by Xi Jinping and then setting out the author's reading. They deal in turn with a new path to modernization, a new stage in the development of Marxist parties, a new phase of world socialism and a new contribution to peaceful development. Tang draws on the Party's record from the revolutions before 1949 through reform and opening up to the new era, and on the figures reported for poverty reduction.

Tang's central claim is that Chinese modernization differs from the Western model, which the author characterises as based on colonial plunder, benefiting few, pursuing growth one-sidedly and tending to hegemony. In Tang's account it relies on self-reliant development, is people-centred, seeks harmony between humans and nature and aims at peace. The author cites 770 million rural people lifted out of poverty since reform and opening up, over 70 per cent of global poverty reduction, as evidence. On party-building, Tang holds that some older socialist ruling parties collapsed because they failed to pair social revolution with the Party's self-reform, whereas the Communist Party of China has used full and rigorous self-governance of the Party to keep its vanguard character. Tang also contrasts it with Western electoral parties, which the author describes as marked by factional strife and money politics.

Tang concludes that Chinese socialism has been the mainstay of world socialism since the Soviet and East European upheavals, refuting what the author calls the theories of socialism's failure, China's collapse and the end of history. The Party is said to offer China's wisdom and proposals on global governance through a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative, and to promise continued contributions in a turbulent international environment. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official Party narrative presented the centenary's international significance in 2021.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China has not only found a path of social revolution suited to China's conditions, but with firm political consciousness and tenacious will has also found a path of self-reform marked by self-improvement, self-purification, self-renewal and self-advancement.
quoteZh: 中国共产党不仅成功走出了一条适合中国国情和特点的社会革命之路，而且以坚定政治自觉、顽强意志品质走出了一条自我完善、自我净化、自我革新、自我提高的自我革命之路

t: A towering milestone on the journey to great rejuvenation
zh: 伟大复兴征程上一座巍然屹立的里程碑
paras: Marking the 110th anniversary of the 1911 Revolution, this commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 21 October 2021, takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the commemoration meeting. Wang Jianlang argues that the revolution, in Xi's words, 'will forever be a towering milestone on the journey toward the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation', because it opened the way for later struggles even though it did not achieve national independence.

The article has three parts. The first traces the Chinese people's search for national salvation after 1840, from Lin Zexu and Wei Yuan through the Taiping movement, the Self-Strengthening Movement, the Hundred Days' Reform and the late-Qing New Policies, to Sun Yat-sen's revolutionaries. The second assesses what the revolution achieved and failed to achieve. The third draws five historical lessons from Xi's speech.

In Wang's account, the revolution was the inevitable result of sharpening social contradictions in a semi-colonial, semi-feudal China. It ended millennia of monarchical autocracy rather than merely changing a dynasty, and two attempted restorations of the monarchy failed. Wang says the idea of democratic republicanism took hold and freed thought. Yet the revolution lacked a correct path and leading force, so it did not change China's semi-colonial, semi-feudal character. Wang links the October Revolution, the spread of Marxism-Leninism and the founding of the Communist Party, ten years after 1911, to this opening. The Party then became Sun Yat-sen's most loyal successor and carried the task forward.

Wang lists five lessons: rejuvenation must be achieved under the leadership of the Communist Party; through upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics, described as the only correct path; through the Chinese people's own heroic struggle; through solidarity and the broadest patriotic united front; and through building a community with a shared future for mankind. Wang concludes that commemoration should mean carrying forward the pioneers' spirit towards the goal of rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official narrative links the 1911 Revolution to the Communist Party's mission and to current slogans.

t: Upholding seeking truth from facts and continuing to advance the great social revolution
zh: 坚持实事求是 不断推进伟大社会革命
paras: This short commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 14 October 2021, takes its cue from Xi Jinping's speech at the Party's centenary celebration. Li argues that seeking truth from facts is the fundamental viewpoint of Marxism and the Party's basic way of thinking, working and leading. In Li's account, practice has repeatedly shown that adhering to it strengthens the Party and the country, while departing from it harms both.

The article is organised around four requirements for continuing the great social revolution: starting from China's actual conditions, discerning the general trend of the times, seizing historical initiative, and relying on the people in arduous exploration. Each section pairs seeking truth from facts with a distinct unity, such as scientific and value dimensions, or generality and specificity.

Li first stresses that one must proceed both from objective reality and from the needs of the people. Without the scientific dimension, seeking truth from facts loses its objective basis; without the value dimension, it loses popular support. Li then presents the Party's century of experience as a record of reading trends and acting on them, and argues that people are not passive in history. Seeking truth from facts, Li says, offers a methodological guide to finding truth rather than an absolute truth. The author ties the principle to the restoration of the ideological line more than forty years ago, which began a new revolution.

Li concludes that today this means recognising that China remains in the primary stage of socialism and addressing the principal contradiction through deepened reform. It also means preparing for a complex international environment, adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and upholding a people-centred stance. Party members are urged to speak, act and be honest. Read the original if you want a brief example of how the 2021 centenary discourse presented seeking truth from facts as a method for the Party's future tasks.
quoteEn: The essence of seeking truth from facts lies not in supplying an absolute truth, but in giving people a scientific choice and methodological guide for discovering truth in concrete terms.
quoteZh: 实事求是的本质不在于提供一个绝对真理，而在于为人们具体地发现真理提供科学性选择和方法论指南。

glossary.explanation: A principle central to Chinese Communist thought, associated especially with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. It calls for policy to be based on actual conditions rather than dogma.

t: We must uphold the strong leadership of the Communist Party of China
zh: 必须坚持中国共产党坚强领导
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2021, Liu Jingbei takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the Party's centenary celebration that drawing on history to open up the future requires upholding the strong leadership of the Communist Party of China. Liu presents this as the most valuable historical lesson of the Party's century of struggle and as the foundation of the Party and the state.

The commentary is built around four requirements. They are to establish and defend a strong leadership core, to arm the whole Party with the latest results of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context, to improve the institutions that secure the Central Committee's centralised and unified leadership, and to hold to Party leadership at critical historical moments. Each is illustrated with episodes from Party history, from the Zunyi Meeting to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012).

Liu argues that the Party's early setbacks came from lacking a mature, stable leadership core, and that victory in the new-democratic revolution followed from Mao Zedong's leadership after Zunyi. Since 2012, Liu says, the core status of Xi Jinping has been the most fundamental reason for historic achievements. Ideological unity, citing Lenin, is the basis of organisational unity, and Liu traces a line from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Liu also lists institutional steps, including democratic centralism, reporting requirements, Party groups in government bodies and inner-Party regulations issued since 2012.

Liu concludes that, amid great changes unseen in a century and at a critical stage of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the country needs unified Central Committee leadership more than ever. Party organisations and cadres are called on to treat the Two Upholds as a political requirement and to keep in step with the Central Committee. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style statement of how Party-press commentary linked the leadership core, ideology and institutions in the centenary year.
quoteEn: The more critical and pivotal the historical moment, the more we must uphold the strong leadership of the Communist Party of China; this is the fundamental basis on which our Party overcomes all risks and challenges.
quoteZh: 越是在历史的关键时刻、转折关头，越要坚持中国共产党坚强领导，这是我们党战胜一切风险挑战的根本所在。

t: The 1911 Revolution and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 辛亥革命与中华民族伟大复兴
paras: Marking the 110th anniversary of the 1911 Revolution and the 100th anniversary of the Communist Party's founding, Jin Yilin asks how the revolution should be assessed and what it means for the present. Writing in Guangming Daily in October 2021, Jin argues that the revolution was both a success and a failure, and that it was an essential preparation for the Party's founding and for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article is organised in four parts: the historical background, from the Opium War and especially the 1894–95 Sino-Japanese War; the revolution's contributions and limitations; its link to the birth of the Communist Party; and the lessons Jin draws for today. It draws on Mao Zedong's 1942 remarks on studying Party history, on Xi Jinping's speech at the 110th anniversary commemoration, and on Sun Yat-sen's own statements.

Jin holds that defeat in 1894–95 turned "national salvation" into the central question for patriots, while the Qing court refused reform. In Jin's account the revolution's main achievement was ending millennia of monarchy and founding Asia's first republic, which liberated thought and spread ideas of democracy and republicanism. Its failure lay in leaving the semi-colonial, semi-feudal structure intact, with Yuan Shikai seizing the fruits of victory. Jin attributes this to the lack of a scientific theory, of mass mobilisation and of correct leadership. Drawing on Mao, Jin presents these limits as historical and not the result of individual failings. Many early Communists, including Wu Yuzhang, Lin Boqu, Dong Biwu and Zhu De, took part in the revolution before moving beyond it.

Jin links the revolution to the formation of the Chinese nation as a self-conscious community ("Zhonghua minzu"), citing Liang Qichao's 1902 usage and the "five-nation republic" slogan. Jin also presents Sun's support for unification, including on Taiwan, as part of the same tradition. Jin concludes that rejuvenation requires Party leadership and socialism with Chinese characteristics. Citing Sun's formula of the capable person, place and time, Jin calls for readers to carry the effort forward, take part in the Belt and Road Initiative and work towards a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want an example of how the official Party-history narrative of 2021 places the 1911 Revolution within the story of national rejuvenation.
quoteEn: However, the value of a revolution cannot be measured only by its short-term effects.
quoteZh: 但是，一次革命的价值不能仅从它的短期效果来衡量。

The Party's official name for its model of socialism since reform and opening up. It stresses adapting Marxism to China's conditions.
A Chinese foreign-policy and infrastructure initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013. It aims to build trade and investment links across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A slogan in Xi Jinping-era diplomacy that calls for cooperative global governance and shared development.
The collective term for all of China's ethnic groups, regarded in official discourse as a single national community. The term came into use around 1902.

t: Gathering cultural strength for the realisation of common prosperity
zh: 为实现共同富裕凝聚文化力量
paras: This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 30 September 2021, asks how culture can contribute to common prosperity. Niu and Zhang argue that common prosperity covers both material and spiritual life, and that culture is an important fulcrum for pursuing it within high-quality development.

The authors set out five mission tasks: raising the banner, rallying the people's hearts, nurturing new people, reviving culture and presenting the national image. They then work through five areas of practice: ideology, core socialist values, literature and art, public cultural services, and the cultural industry.

The authors hold that Marxism is the banner and soul of socialist ideology, so that Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era must guide practice. They also call for strengthening the core socialist values through education, practice and institutional safeguards, and for civic-morality and civilisation-building campaigns. For the arts and culture, they call for a people-centred orientation and works that reflect the people's aspirations. On the cultural industry, they argue that the key measure of quality is whether it supplies products that both meet cultural needs and strengthen the people's spiritual strength, so social benefits come before economic ones.

Niu and Zhang conclude that satisfying cultural needs and strengthening spiritual strength must go together. They propose building a cultural atmosphere for common prosperity as part of becoming a strong socialist cultural country, with better public cultural services, digital cultural industries and integrated culture and tourism. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party-media writing in 2021 linked culture, ideology and common prosperity.
quoteEn: The most important measure of the quality and level of cultural industry development is not economic returns, but whether it can supply more cultural products that both meet the people's cultural needs and strengthen their spiritual strength.
quoteZh: 衡量文化产业发展质量和水平,最重要的不是看经济效益,而是看能不能提供更多既能满足人民文化需求、又能增强人民精神力量的文化产品。

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal that was given new prominence in Party policy in 2021. The article treats it as covering both material and spiritual life.
The official economic strategy since 2017, which stresses quality, efficiency and innovation over growth speed.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
A set of twelve official values promoted since 2012 at national, social and individual levels, including prosperity, harmony, patriotism and integrity.

t: The epochal significance of the new road to the exam
zh: 新的赶考之路的时代意蕴
paras: Published in Economic Daily in October 2021, this commentary takes up Xi Jinping's remark at the Party's centenary celebration that the Communist Party has set out on a "new road to the exam" towards the second centenary goal. Shang explains that "sitting the exam" goes back to Mao Zedong's 1949 phrase for the move to Beijing. The author argues that the new exam has new content and new goals, and that studying it helps the Party meet fresh tests.

The article is organised as six statements about what the new road rests on: the achievements of the Party's first hundred years, the building of a moderately prosperous society as its starting point, the goal of a modern socialist great power, the "nine musts", the Party's founding spirit, and reliance on the whole people.

Shang's central claim is that the new exam continues an unbroken history of passing tests, from the new-democratic revolution through socialist construction and reform and opening up to the new era. The author describes the elimination of absolute poverty as the starting point. The 19th Party Congress (2017) split the thirty years to mid-century into two stages, with modernization basically achieved by 2035. The "nine musts", drawn from Xi's summary of Party history, are presented as the basic guide. Shang also stresses the founding spirit and the Party's self-reform alongside social revolution, and the Party's ties to the people.

Shang concludes that the road is hopeful but demanding. The author calls for confidence together with vigilance and readiness for a great struggle with many new historical features. Under Party leadership and with national unity, the author holds, the new exam can be passed with an excellent answer. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned reading of the "new exam" metaphor in the 2021 centenary discourse.
quoteEn: The new road to the exam has the great achievements of a hundred years of Party history as its deep foundation.
quoteZh: 新的赶考之路，以百年党史取得的丰功伟绩为深厚基础。

glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's 1949 image, on leaving Xibaipo for Beijing, of the Party going to take an exam. It has since become a standard Party metaphor for facing historical tests.
Nine requirements drawn from Xi Jinping's 2021 centenary speech as lessons of Party history, such as upholding Party leadership and advancing the Sinicization of Marxism.

glossary.literal: building a moderately prosperous society in all respects
glossary.explanation: The first centenary goal, declared achieved in 2021 and tied to the end of absolute poverty.
A formulation from Xi's 2021 speech for the values of the Party's founders, such as seeking truth, staying true to the original aspiration and loyalty to the Party and the people.
The Party's official term for continuous internal rectification, set beside social revolution.

t: The correct path to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 实现中华民族伟大复兴的正确道路
paras: Published in Economic Daily on 27 September 2021, this commentary follows Xi Jinping's speech at the celebration of the Party's centenary, which said that learning from history and creating the future requires upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics. Chen argues that this path is the correct road to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. In Chen's account, it is an inevitable choice of modern Chinese history and the fundamental direction of China's progress, and the Party and people should follow it with confidence.

The article is organised in four sections. The first presents following one's own path as the historical conclusion of the Party's hundred years of struggle. The second asserts that socialism with Chinese characteristics is socialism and not some other "ism". The third turns to results since reform and opening up. The fourth looks ahead to the path's future.

Chen first traces the line from Mao Zedong's integration of Marxism-Leninism with Chinese revolutionary practice, through the founding of the socialist system, to Deng Xiaoping's 1982 call to build socialism with Chinese characteristics, and on to the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012). The article then argues that the path keeps the basic principles of scientific socialism while carrying practical, national and contemporary characteristics. It holds that there is no universal development model and that the primary stage of socialism leaves many problems unresolved, so theory, practice and institutions must keep innovating. Chen presents China's industrialisation, its poverty reduction (over 70% of the world's total, by the article's figure) and its roughly 30% contribution to world growth as proof of success. These achievements, Chen contends, break the myths that "there is no alternative to capitalism" and that "modernization equals Westernization", and they open new options for developing countries.

Chen concludes that China must avoid both the "closed and rigid old path" and the "wrong path of changing banners", citing the lessons of the planned economy and of the Soviet and East European collapse. In this reading, the Party's theme in the new era remains upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics, and this is also what will secure the goals for 2035 and the middle of the century. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official narrative links Party history, the Four-sphere Confidence and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation around the 2021 centenary.
quoteEn: Socialism with Chinese characteristics is not a reissue of other countries' socialist practice, nor a socialism \"cloned\" from another country's model, but one grounded in China's unique cultural tradition, historical destiny and actual national conditions; this is its national character.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义，不是其他国家社会主义实践的再版，不是从他国模式“克隆”出来的社会主义，而是立足于我国独特的文化传统、历史命运和现实国情的社会主义，这是其民族特色。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central goal of Party discourse, especially since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It refers to restoring China to a position of national strength and prosperity, with milestones set for 2035 and the middle of the century.
The official name for China's path, theory and system since the reform era. It was articulated by Deng Xiaoping at the 12th Party Congress in 1982.
An official judgement that China is still at an early, underdeveloped stage of socialism. It is used to justify reform policies and a long period of development.
The policy of domestic economic reform and opening to the outside world, launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.
The Party's call for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

t: Guiding the new "exam road" with the great founding spirit of the Party
zh: 以伟大建党精神引领新的赶考之路
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 28 September 2021, this commentary takes up the "great founding spirit of the Party", which Xi Jinping first set out at the ceremony marking the Party's 100th anniversary (2021). Gong and Fu argue that this spirit must be inherited and promoted as the Party and the people set out on a "new road to the exam" towards the second centenary goal, so that the Party can again hand in an excellent answer sheet.

The piece takes the four components of the spirit in Xi's formulation in turn: upholding truth and ideals; staying true to the founding mission; being ready to sacrifice and fight bravely; and being loyal to the Party and never failing the people. Each is presented as a distinct "strength" (intellectual, political, spiritual and moral) and paired with a task for the new journey. The authors draw on Party history, from the Soviet areas and the Jinggangshan period to poverty alleviation, and on quotations from Xi.

The core argument is that the Party's past achievements flowed from these four strengths and that the same strengths are needed now. On the intellectual side, the authors hold that Marxism, adapted to Chinese conditions and traditional culture, underpinned the leap from "standing up" to "becoming rich" to "becoming strong". They say it must continue to guide Chinese modernization under the new development philosophy. On the political side, they stress the people-centred approach, citing the image of the times as examiner and the people as marker. They cite more than 3.7 million named revolutionary martyrs between 1921 and 1949 and over 1,800 deaths in the poverty campaign as evidence of the spirit of sacrifice.

The authors conclude that the second centenary goal is a harder test. It requires Party members and officials to keep up vigilance against risks and long-term struggle, and to guard against factors that weaken the Party's vanguard character or alienate it from the masses. They call for cultivating loyalty to the Party, public virtue in serving the people, and personal integrity. They argue that the Party's nature and the people's interests are identical, so loyalty to the Party means responsibility to the people. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary in 2021 turned the founding spirit into practical tasks for Party cadres.
quoteEn: Loyalty to the Party means being responsible to the people, and not failing the people is the greatest loyalty to the Party.
quoteZh: 对党忠诚就是对人民负责，不负人民就是对党最大的忠诚。

glossary.en: great founding spirit of the Party
glossary.explanation: A formulation first set out by Xi Jinping on 1 July 2021 to summarise the founding values of the Communist Party: upholding truth and ideals, staying true to the founding mission, fearless struggle, and loyalty to the Party and the people.

The official aim of building China into a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic. The first centenary goal was a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021.
The official term for China's own path of modernization, promoted by the Party leadership and presented as distinct from Western models.
A set of five concepts (innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development) put forward by the Party in 2015 to guide economic and social policy.

t: The historical perspective and contemporary significance of the "three profound changes"
zh: “三个深刻改变”的历史观照与现实意蕴
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 29 September 2021, takes up a passage from Xi Jinping's speech at the ceremony marking the Party's centenary. In it Xi says the founding of the Communist Party of China was an earth-shaking event that profoundly changed the direction of the Chinese nation, the fate of the Chinese people, and the trends and patterns of world development. Deng argues that these "three profound changes" express the Party's consistent views of history, of the people and of its own role, and give the idea of an "earth-shaking event" its historical and present meaning.

The article has three numbered sections, one for each change. The first looks at the Party's origins after the Opium War, the failure of earlier salvation schemes and the arrival of Marxism-Leninism. The second goes through the four historical periods of the Party's leadership, from the New Democratic Revolution to the new era. The third turns to the international effects of the Party's rule, from the founding of the People's Republic to the Belt and Road Initiative and the Party's role in the Covid-19 pandemic.

Deng's central claim is that the Party has distinctive sources of strength that earlier Chinese political forces lacked. These are the guidance of scientific Marxist theory, the support of the people, and firm goals backed by a disciplined vanguard organisation. Deng says the Party's class character depends on whose fundamental interests it represents, not on the social origins of its members. In each period the Party is said to have laid the political, institutional and material conditions for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, taking the people from "standing up" to "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong". Deng adds that socialism with Chinese characteristics has broken the assumption that modernization means Westernization, and so offers other countries a different path and "Chinese wisdom" and "Chinese solutions".

Deng concludes that the Party, which holds to Marxist truth and to communist ideals, has created achievements worthy of history and of the people. On the eve of the second centenary goal, Deng says, history has proved and will go on proving the "three profound changes". The piece restates the official reading of the Party's centenary and links the Party's mission to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the centenary speech's historical judgements were presented to a general readership in 2021.
quoteEn: The basic establishment of the socialist political and economic systems brought China, an Eastern giant with a quarter of the world's population, into socialist society and strengthened the forces of world peace, democracy and socialism.
quoteZh: 社会主义政治制度和经济制度的基本确立，使得中国这个占世界四分之一人口的东方大国进入了社会主义社会，壮大了世界和平民主和社会主义的力量。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping's Chinese Dream. It means restoring China's national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation".

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since about 2012. It calls for shared security, development and global governance.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation programme launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries in Asia, Africa and Europe.
The Party's official name for its system and path since reform and opening up, combining Marxism with China's conditions and a market-oriented economy under Party leadership.

t: Common prosperity: an important feature of Chinese modernization
zh: 共同富裕：中国式现代化的重要特征
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 27 September 2021, takes up Xi Jinping's statement at the tenth meeting of the Central Financial and Economic Affairs Commission (17 August 2021) that common prosperity is an essential requirement of socialism and an important feature of Chinese modernization. Lu Mingchuan argues that, over the Party's first hundred years, common prosperity and socialist modernization have been united in the practice of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, opening a new path that shows the advantages of socialism with Chinese characteristics.

The piece is organised in five numbered sections. Each presents common prosperity as embodying a different aspect of Chinese modernization: its essential requirement, its fundamental standpoint, its main content, its strategic method, and its place in a "new form of human civilization". It draws on Xi Jinping's speeches, Deng Xiaoping's remark on modernization and socialism, and official poverty-reduction figures.

Lu contends that capitalist modernization cannot deliver common prosperity because private ownership and exploitation prevent capitalists from sharing wealth with workers. Under the primary stage of socialism, by contrast, public ownership as the mainstay, together with the Two Unwaverings, provides the institutional guarantee, and continued development of the productive forces remains necessary. Common prosperity is described as covering both material and cultural-ethical life, and as neither egalitarianism nor simultaneous wealth: some may get rich first and then help others, by making the "cake" bigger and dividing it well through primary, secondary and tertiary distribution. Lu stresses that this is a long, gradual process, pursued through staged goals from the "two-step" plan to the new two-step plan (basic modernization by 2035, a modern socialist power by 2050). The article also credits the Party since the 18th Party Congress (2012) with lifting 98.99 million rural people out of poverty and eliminating absolute poverty.

Lu concludes that common prosperity separates socialist civilization from Western capitalist civilization, which the author describes as centred on capital and producing an accumulation of poverty alongside wealth, even where welfare states have been built. Chinese modernization is thus presented as a new form of human civilization and a contribution to world socialism. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the 2021 official line on common prosperity was explained to a general Chinese readership.
quoteEn: Common prosperity is not uniform egalitarianism, nor equal or simultaneous wealth, still less levelling rich and poor or robbing the rich to help the poor.
quoteZh: 共同富裕不是整齐划一的平均主义，也不是同等富裕、同步富裕，更不是均贫富、劫富济贫

glossary.explanation: A long-standing socialist goal in Chinese Party discourse, given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping from 2021. It is presented as prosperity shared by all, reached in stages rather than through equal outcomes.
The official term for China's path of modernization under Party leadership, presented as distinct from Western models.
The policy of unwaveringly consolidating and developing the public sector while unwaveringly encouraging, supporting and guiding the non-public sector.
The official assessment that China is at an early stage of socialism, lasting a long historical period, which justifies mixed ownership and market mechanisms.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, referring to restoring China's strength and international standing.
The official name for the Party's theory, path and system since reform and opening up.

t: Mao Zedong's approach to correcting and improving the style of meetings
zh: 毛泽东关于纠正和改进会风的思想方法
paras: Meetings are the Party's main means of making decisions and setting policy, and Deng and Yan argue that the style of meetings (huifeng) reflects the work style, morale and cohesion of Party members and cadres. The article contends that Mao Zedong, in both the New Democratic revolution and the period of socialist revolution and construction, treated bad meeting styles as a serious problem and developed a coherent set of methods for correcting them. These methods, the authors say, remain instructive today.

The article has three parts. The first sets out Mao's criticism of three kinds of poor meeting style: formalism, bureaucracy and liberalism. The second covers his methods for correcting them: institutional rules, investigation and research, democracy combined with centralism, and the summing up of experience. The third assesses the results. Evidence comes from Mao's speeches and drafts from the Gutian Resolution (1929) through the Yan'an period to the 1950s and early 1960s, plus anecdotes about his own conduct at meetings.

The authors argue that Mao read each bad style as a distortion of Party work. Formalism meant stereotyped agendas, reports read from scripts and a 'Party eight-legged essay' format. Bureaucratic style meant a commanding manner and distance from the masses, and liberalism meant aimless debate, extreme democracy and a lack of discipline. On remedies, Mao required meetings to be prepared in advance, short and infrequent, and focused on real problems. He held that 'no investigation, no right to speak', and that investigation should be done in person. He also tied meetings to democratic centralism and the mass line, for example by circulating draft reports for comment before the Seven Thousand Cadres Conference (1962).

The authors credit these efforts with three results: a democratic and efficient meeting style, a Marxist study style that links theory with practice (notably in the Yan'an rectification), and a practical, truth-seeking work style. They cite examples including the 7th Party Congress and the 8th Party Congress. They conclude that Mao's experience should guide efforts to improve meeting and work styles on the path towards the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want a detailed, source-based account of how Mao is presented in Party historiography as a model for reforming meeting practice and work style.
quoteEn: Meeting style is a microcosm of work style; meeting style is work style.
quoteZh: 会风是作风的缩影，会风就是作风。

glossary.explanation: The manner in which Party meetings are conducted, including preparation, speech, discussion and decision-making. In Party discourse it is treated as part of the broader 'work style' (zuofeng) of cadres.
In Party usage, a fault in which form, procedure and appearance take priority over substance and results, such as ritual meetings and stereotyped reports. It is distinct from formalism in art theory.
Mao's term, used in his 1942 Yan'an speeches, for stiff, formulaic and empty writing and speaking within the Party, modelled on the rigid imperial examination essay.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Communist Party, combining open discussion with unified decisions and discipline once a decision is made.
An ideological education campaign from 1942 to 1945 aimed at dogmatism, sectarianism and Party formalism, which strengthened Mao's line of linking theory with practice.
The Party's method of drawing ideas from the masses, concentrating them, and returning them as policy to be tested in practice.

t: Drawing boundless strength from the Yan'an Spirit
zh: 从延安精神中汲取无穷力量
paras: Marking the Party's centenary in 2021, Zhao Yaohong asks what the Yan'an Spirit consists of and why it still matters. The author argues that this spirit, formed during the Yan'an period, is a treasure of the Party's spiritual lineage. Zhao holds that studying its scientific content and present-day value helps Party members pass on the "red gene", take on new missions and open new prospects.

The article, first published in Red Flag Manuscripts, has three parts. The first describes how the Yan'an Spirit took shape, citing the period's achievements: the sinicization of Marxism, the writing of Mao Zedong Thought into the Party constitution, a mature central leadership and the experience of governing the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region. The second sets out its content. The third draws out its contemporary value, quoting Xi Jinping throughout.

Zhao characterises the Yan'an Spirit as thoroughly revolutionary, as a sublimated national spirit, as the spirit of an era devoted to national independence and people's liberation, and as a collective spirit with broad popular roots. Its content has four elements: a firm and correct political direction, the ideological line of emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts, the fundamental purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly, and the pioneering spirit of self-reliance and hard struggle. The author treats these as the spirit's soul, essence, nature and distinguishing feature. In Zhao's account, self-reliance showed in rejecting the dogmatising of Marxism and the sanctifying of Comintern instructions, in keeping independence within the united front, and in surviving blockade and the Japanese "three alls" policy.

Zhao concludes that each element should guide Party members and officials today. They should strengthen ideals and convictions, including by studying Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. They should practise seeking truth from facts, which includes Party self-reform and criticism and self-criticism. They should keep the people at the highest place in their hearts, oppose formalism and bureaucratism, and improve mass work. They should also keep up hard struggle in peacetime and oppose hedonism and listlessness. Read the original if you want to see how a Party-school scholar presents the Yan'an Spirit as a framework for Party-building education at the centenary.
quoteEn: The Yan'an Spirit is a treasury of the spirit whose main content is a firm and correct political direction, the ideological line of emancipating the mind and seeking truth from facts, the fundamental purpose of serving the people wholeheartedly, and the pioneering spirit of self-reliance and hard struggle.
quoteZh: 延安精神是以坚定正确的政治方向、解放思想实事求是的思想路线、全心全意为人民服务的根本宗旨、自力更生艰苦奋斗的创业精神为主要内容的精神宝库。

glossary.explanation: The set of values and work styles the Party attributes to its Yan'an period (1935–1948), such as self-reliance, serving the people and seeking truth from facts. It is one of the revolutionary "spirits" in the Party's official spiritual lineage.

An old Chinese phrase that Mao Zedong gave a Marxist meaning and made the Party's ideological line during the Yan'an rectification. It stresses starting from actual conditions and linking theory to practice.
The official term for a series of named revolutionary "spirits" (such as the Jinggangshan, Long March and Yan'an spirits) that the Party presents as its spiritual heritage.

t: The Long March: red flags fluttering in the west wind
zh: 长征，红旗漫卷西风
paras: Marking the 85th anniversary of the Red Army's Long March and the centenary of the Communist Party (2021), Shi Zhongquan sets out what the Long March was, how the Zunyi Meeting turned the Party's fortunes, and what the "Long March spirit" means for today. The article, first published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao), takes Xi Jinping's 2016 speech on the 80th anniversary as its guide. Shi argues that studying the Long March and its spirit is the best way to commemorate the Party's centenary and to "walk well the Long March of the new era".

The article has three parts. The first describes the march of 1934–1936: its scale, its changing routes and destinations, and the final meeting of the three main Red Army forces in October 1936. The second traces the Zunyi Meeting and the meetings before and after it. The third lists the components of the Long March spirit and draws lessons for the present, quoting Mao Zedong's poems and veterans' recollections as illustration.

On Zunyi, Shi contends that Mao Zedong's leadership was established gradually. The heavy losses at the Xiang River, which Shi attributes to mistaken leadership decisions, discredited the "Left" line. Meetings at Tongdao, Liping and Houchang then curbed the military authority of Bo Gu and Otto Braun (Li De). Zunyi ended "Left" dogmatism in practice, and later meetings at Goukan, Gougba and Huili consolidated Mao's position. Shi then presents the Long March spirit as five elements: revolutionary ideals, fearlessness of hardship and sacrifice, seeking truth from facts, putting the overall situation and discipline first, and reliance on the people. Shi holds that courage alone is not enough, and that only a correct line turns it into victory.

For the new era, Shi calls for upholding firm ideals and convictions, seeking truth from facts and opening new horizons for adapting Marxism to China, strengthening unity and discipline, and following the Party's mass line. The article ties these to the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, to common prosperity and to the risks of a world undergoing changes "unseen in a century". It closes by describing the Long March spirit as an inexhaustible source of strength for the "two centenary goals". Read the original if you want an official Party-historian account of the Long March, the Zunyi Meeting and the Long March spirit as used in the 2021 centenary commemorations.
quoteEn: Only under the guidance of a correct line, strategy and tactics can the Long March spirit bear rich fruit and lead the Chinese revolution to victory.
quoteZh: 只有在正确的路线和战略战术的指导下，长征精神才能结出丰硕之果，引导中国革命取得胜利。

glossary.explanation: The set of values the Party attributes to the Long March, defined in Xi Jinping's 2016 speech. They include faith in revolutionary ideals, readiness for sacrifice, independence and seeking truth from facts, discipline and unity, and reliance on the people.
An enlarged Politburo meeting held in Zunyi, Guizhou, in January 1935. Party history presents it as the point at which Mao Zedong's leadership was effectively established.
A principle of the Party's ideological line, associated with Mao Zedong and later with Deng Xiaoping. It calls for policy to be based on actual conditions rather than dogma.
The Party's method of work, which stresses drawing on the people and serving them ("from the masses, to the masses"). It is treated as a basis of the Party's legitimacy.
A goal of socialism with Chinese characteristics, stressed in recent years, that prosperity should be shared by all the people.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The central national goal in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse. It is linked to the two centenary goals of 2021 and 2049.

t: The Autumn Harvest Uprising: the great beginning of a new path for the Chinese revolution
zh: 秋收起义：中国革命新道路的伟大开端
paras: Marking the Party's centenary period, Tang Zhengmang revisits the Autumn Harvest Uprising of 9 September 1927, led by Mao Zedong on the Hunan–Jiangxi border. The article, published in Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao), argues that the uprising was the great beginning of the new revolutionary path of "encircling the cities from the countryside and seizing power by armed force". Tang follows Deng Xiaoping in treating the discovery of this path as Mao's greatest achievement.

The piece is organised around six themes, each with its own heading: raising the Party's red flag; correcting the direction of advance and opening a rural base; placing the Party branch at company level; introducing democracy in the army; creating the first army discipline; and persevering through setbacks. Tang draws on Mao's letter to the Central Committee, the Sanwan reorganisation of late September 1927, and accounts of the later reactions of Liu Bocheng, Zhu De and Peng Dehuai.

Tang contrasts the uprising with the Nanchang Uprising, which still flew the banner of the left Kuomintang. By abandoning that banner and adopting the hammer-and-sickle flag, the article says, the uprising began armed struggle independently led by the Communist Party. On strategy, Tang notes that the plan to take Changsha, in line with the "city-centred" model, failed, and that Mao's decision at Wenjiashi to turn toward the weakly defended countryside took the first step on the new path. Tang credits the Sanwan measures with building a new type of people's army: Party branches at company level, soldiers' committees and the abolition of officer abuse, and early rules that later became the "Three Main Rules of Discipline and Eight Points for Attention".

Tang stresses that the uprising was not a string of victories. The forces fell from over 5,000 to about 1,500 men, commander Lu Deming was killed, and Mao himself was briefly captured. Tang presents Mao's steadfastness, including the remark about a small stone breaking Chiang Kai-shek's great water jar, as the spirit that carried the red flag to the Jinggang Mountains. The article concludes that the uprising made important explorations on major questions of the revolution and of building the people's army, and that this path led to final victory in the New Democratic revolution. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-history writing in 2021 presents the Autumn Harvest Uprising and its legacy for army-building.
quoteEn: Placing the Party branch at company level was the fundamental organisational measure that made the Party organisation strong, and a powerful organisational guarantee that enabled the Red Army to \"carry out the political tasks of the revolution\" and to persist in extremely arduous struggle.
quoteZh: “支部建在连上”是使党组织坚强有力的根本组织措施，是红军能够“执行革命的政治任务”、坚持艰苦卓绝斗争的强大组织保障。

glossary.en: encircling the cities from the countryside
glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's strategy of building rural base areas and armed forces first, then taking the cities. It is presented in Party history as the distinctive path of the Chinese revolution, as opposed to the Soviet city-centred model.

The armed uprising of September 1927 on the Hunan–Jiangxi border, led by Mao Zedong after the collapse of the first Kuomintang–Communist cooperation. Its surviving forces went to the Jinggang Mountains.
The reorganisation of Mao's remaining troops at Sanwan village, Jiangxi, in late September 1927. Party histories credit it with establishing Party leadership over the army and internal democracy.
Mao Zedong's term for the stage of the Chinese revolution (roughly 1919–1949) led by the proletariat and its party against imperialism, feudalism and bureaucrat-capitalism, ahead of socialism.

glossary.pinyin: sān dà jìlǜ bā xiàng zhùyì
glossary.en: Three Main Rules of Discipline and Eight Points for Attention
glossary.explanation: The code of conduct for the Red Army and later the People's Liberation Army, governing treatment of civilians. Its early forms date to 1927–28 and it was later standardised.

keywords: encircling the cities from the countryside

t: Letting the Jinggangshan spirit shine with new light for our times
zh: 让井冈山精神放射出新的时代光芒
source: Red Flag Manuscripts (Hongqi Wengao), published on marxism.cass.cn 9 November 2021
paras: Writing in the centenary year of the Communist Party of China (2021), Kuang Sheng asks how the Jinggangshan spirit, formed in the revolutionary base of 1927–1930, should be carried forward under present conditions. Starting from Xi Jinping's 2016 remarks that Jinggangshan was the cradle of the Chinese revolution, Kuang argues that its core is firm conviction and hard struggle, seeking truth from facts and daring to open new paths, and relying on the masses to win victory. Each element, the article holds, must be given a contemporary form.

The commentary is organised around four injunctions: to be steadfast believers in the lofty communist ideal and the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics; to place innovation at the centre of national development; to keep up a tireless spirit and an unflinching fighting posture; and to remain the people's servants while meeting their new expectations of a better life. Each section opens with a Jinggangshan episode and then turns to present-day tasks. Kuang draws on Mao Zedong's Jinggangshan-era ideas and on Xi Jinping's formulations.

Kuang argues that belief in Marxism is the soul of the Jinggangshan spirit, since genuine communists did not waver after the 1927 defeat. The article says that some cadres' ideals wavered after reform and opening up, and it links firm conviction to confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. On innovation, Kuang notes that Mao combined Marxist universal truth with Chinese realities and found a rural-centred revolutionary path that "Marx and Lenin never mentioned". In the same way, the new development philosophy and reform are presented as answers to unprecedented problems. On hard struggle, Kuang stresses that China remains in the primary stage of socialism, and calls for strategic resolve and stronger governing capacity.

Kuang says the victory in the campaign against poverty is a new starting point and not an endpoint. Uneven development, urban–rural gaps and common prosperity remain demanding tasks. The article calls for a people-centred approach, for the people to be treated as the makers of history, and for consolidating the broadest united front, including harmony among parties, ethnic groups, religions and social strata, and mutual respect among civilisations. Read the original if you want an example of how Party-school commentary turns a revolutionary-era "spirit" into guidance for cadres at the start of the Fourteenth Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: Firm belief in Marxism and firm conviction in socialism and communism are the soul of the Jinggangshan spirit.
quoteZh: 对马克思主义的坚定信仰，对社会主义和共产主义的坚定信念，是井冈山精神的灵魂。

glossary.explanation: A Party-defined set of values attributed to the 1927–1930 revolutionary base in the Jinggang Mountains, where Mao Zedong established the first rural base area. It is counted within the Party's 'spiritual genealogy'.
The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's path of socialist development since reform and opening up.
Xi Jinping's framework, set out in 2015, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development, used as a guide for economic and social policy.
The official judgement that China is still at an early stage of socialist development, which is used to justify the Party's basic line and policies.
A long-standing official goal of prosperity shared by all the people, given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping.

t: Mao Zedong's struggle at Anyuan in keeping to the Party's original aspiration, and its lessons for today
zh: 毛泽东在安源的初心奋斗与现实启示
paras: Published in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2021, during the Party History Study and Education campaign, this commentary asks how Mao Zedong's work at Anyuan embodied the Communist Party's original aspiration and mission (chuxin shiming). Huang argues that Anyuan, where Mao and others led a ten-year workers' movement from 1921 to 1930, was a key place where Communists first put that mission into practice. The author draws practical lessons for Party members today.

The article has three parts. The first presents Anyuan as a model of building the Party among industrial workers and recounts its pioneering steps. The second follows Mao's visits to Anyuan from 1920 to 1930. The third turns to three lessons for the present, introduced with a quotation from Xi Jinping on political awareness and the Party's original aspiration.

Huang's central claim is that Anyuan answered basic questions of the Party's early years: how to rely on the working class, how to join Marxism to the workers' movement, how to organise the Party among industrial workers, and how to form a people's army of workers and peasants. The author lists early initiatives such as a Party organisation among workers (1922), a Party-led economic organisation (1922), anti-corruption work (1923) and a Party school (1924). In Huang's account, Mao went down the mines, lived among workers and learned that Communists must change their own attitudes before they could be accepted. Mao also set strategy at critical moments, including the "army of the aggrieved is bound to win" line before the strike and the 1927 Autumn Harvest Uprising planning at Anyuan.

Huang draws three lessons. Party members should treat the people as teachers and learn from them with sincerity and humility. They should earn the people's trust, admiration and respect through sacrifice, ability and integrity. Whether they keep the original aspiration is proved by real achievements in practice, not by words. The author ties these lessons to the 14th Five-Year Plan and the new journey of building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a Party-history commentary that uses Anyuan to support present-day arguments about Party conduct and mass work, written by a local specialist in Red culture.
quoteEn: Whether a Communist truly lives out the original aspiration and mission has never been tested by what he says himself, still less by what is written on paper, but is proved and tested by real actions and achievements in the struggle for the cause of the Party and the people.
quoteZh: 检验一个共产党员是否真正践行初心使命，从来就不是靠自己说出来的，更不是凭空写出来的，而是在为党和人民事业奋斗的进程中以切切实实的作为和成就证明检验的。

glossary.explanation: A slogan in Xi Jinping-era Party discourse for the Party's founding purpose of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the nation. It was the theme of the 2019 education campaign and recurs in the Party History Study and Education campaign of 2021.

glossary.en: Party History Study and Education campaign
glossary.explanation: A Party-wide campaign launched in early 2021 ahead of the Party's centenary. It called on members to study Party history and draw lessons from it.
China's national economic and social development plan for 2021–2025.

t: The Soviet revolution: an important historical stage in laying the Party's foundations
zh: 苏维埃革命：建基立业的重要历史阶段
paras: Written for the centenary of the Communist Party of China in 2021, this article asks what place the Chinese Soviet revolution (1927–1937), also called the Agrarian Revolution, holds in the Party's hundred-year history. He Youliang argues that it was a short but pivotal stage in which the Party, facing a threat to its survival, drew on the Soviet Russian model and Comintern support and then independently led the Chinese revolution. In the author's account, it laid the Party's foundations and solved the problems of survival, finding a way forward and building a base.

The article is a short commentary in Hongqi Wengao. It first defines the Soviet revolution as armed struggle, land revolution and the building of people's political power. It then sets out six contributions: institutional foundations, a path or model, ways of governing, theoretical results, spiritual character, and lessons from experience. Each is linked to later developments in the Party's history.

On institutions, He argues that the Soviet (workers', peasants' and soldiers') congress system, the principle that the Party commands the gun, and people's war set the basis for the Party's leading position. The author treats the people's congress system of the new China as an inheritance and development of the Soviet congresses. On the path, He says the Party found that the Soviet Russian city-centred model did not fit China and switched to encircling the cities from the countryside, with the peasantry as the main force. He cites a Nationalist official who compared the Party's relation to the peasants to fish in water and the Nationalists' to fish on sand. The base areas gave the Party its first experience of partial rule, and Mao Zedong's writings of the period set out the core of what later became Mao Zedong Thought: seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence.

He adds that the Jinggangshan, Soviet Area and Long March spirits became part of the Party's "red genes". The Party later treated the period's errors as lessons, sublating the Soviet model and developing the theory of New Democracy that led to the 1949 victory. The author concludes that the period's practice and legacy merit continued study. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned Chinese account of how Party historians present the 1927–1937 Soviet period as a foundation for later Party rule.
quoteEn: Its greatest and most important achievement was to open up the primal chaos, find the path, preserve strength and establish a foundation, that is, to essentially resolve the epochal problems and historical tasks of surviving, finding a way out and laying a base.
quoteZh: 最大也是最为重要的业绩,是开辟了鸿蒙,探明了道路,保存了力量,创立了基业,即基本解决了求生存、找出路、奠基业的时代难题与历史任务。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for its 1927–1937 revolutionary stage, when it built Soviet-style governments in rural base areas. It is also called the Agrarian (Land) Revolution.
The rural base areas, spread over more than ten provinces, where the Party set up Soviet governments. The best known are Jinggangshan and the Central Soviet Area.
Mao Zedong's theory of a revolution led by the proletariat through a broad class alliance. It was adopted as the Party's strategy in place of the Soviet-period model.
A Party principle that leaders should learn from the masses and work on their behalf. Party histories count it among the three living souls of Mao Zedong Thought.
The Party's official term for Mao's adaptation of Marxism-Leninism to Chinese conditions. It was written into the Party's guiding ideology.

t: The emotional meaning of the Communist Party of China's hundred-year history
zh: 中国共产党百年历史的情感意蕴
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in August 2021, in the run-up to the Party's centenary commentary season, Chen Jinlong asks what emotional values have been built up over the Communist Party of China's hundred years and what they show about the Party. Chen holds that emotion shapes not only individuals but also the value orientation and goals of states, nations and parties. The article argues that the Party's emotional character has five elements, and that it offers one way of explaining "why the Party is able" to succeed.

The short piece is organised under five headings: cherishing history, respect for the people, deep love for the country, pride in the nation, and dedication to the world. Under each, Chen draws on statements by Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping, along with commemorative practices and policy initiatives, as evidence of the sentiment in question.

On history, Chen argues that the Party judges the past by historical materialism and dialectical thinking, and shows its attachment through memorials, anniversaries and national commemoration days. On the people, the article holds that the Party's original aspiration and mission, its principle of serving the people wholeheartedly and its mass line express respect for the people's strength and interests, including the pursuit of common prosperity. Love of country is traced from Mao's hopes for a free, prosperous and civilised China through the Four Modernizations, the "three-step" strategy and the Two Centenary Goals. Chen reads pride in the nation in remarks on Chinese civilisation, national character and the Chinese Dream, and dedication to the world in internationalist commitments from the anti-fascist war to a community with a shared future for mankind and the Belt and Road Initiative.

Chen concludes that these five sentiments give the Party an emotional image and personal appeal. The Party's success, in this account, results from many factors working together, among which emotion is an important one. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official commentary in 2021 framed the Party's centenary through affect and sentiment rather than institutions or policy.
quoteEn: The Party's ability to succeed is the result of the combined effect of many factors, and "emotion" is an important one among them.
quoteZh: 中国共产党之所以“能”，是多方面因素综合作用的结果，而“情感”是其中的重要因素。

glossary.explanation: A Party slogan, prominent since 2017, on the founding purpose of the CPC: to seek happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation.
A working method developed under Mao Zedong in which Party cadres gather the views of ordinary people and turn them into policy, then take it back to them.
A goal of socialism in Party discourse, stressing shared prosperity for all; it has been given renewed emphasis under Xi Jinping.
A slogan Xi Jinping put forward in 2012 for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
Official targets: a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021, and a modern socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's concept for international relations, advanced since 2012–13, stressing shared interests and cooperation among states.
A Chinese infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched in 2013, linking China with Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

t: The Communist Party of China's historical experience in building a socialist state
zh: 中国共产党建设社会主义国家的历史经验
paras: Liu Fangliang asks what historical experience the Communist Party of China has accumulated in building and perfecting a socialist state system. Writing in a newspaper commentary in 2021, Liu argues that the Party has followed a path of "theory as guide, mechanisms in operation, governance as advance" in constructing and developing national institutions.

The piece moves through three stages. It first treats the adaptation of Marxist political theory to China, from the revolutionary period through the founding of the People's Republic to the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978). It then turns to institutional mechanisms, and finally to the modernization of the national governance system and governance capacity.

Liu argues that the classics left open how a backward Eastern country should build its institutions after crossing the "Caudine Forks", so the Party had to answer this through Chinese conditions. Liu holds that the core institutions stay fixed, namely Party leadership, a predominantly public-ownership economy and the people's democratic dictatorship. Mechanisms such as consultation, supervision and market regulation are adjusted flexibly, and foreign practice is borrowed only at the mechanism level. Since the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), Liu says, comprehensive deepening of reform has aimed at modernizing the national governance system and governance capacity, which Liu presents as the next stage of institutional development.

Liu concludes that treating governance as the concentrated expression of institutions and their execution criticises and goes beyond Western "society-centred" governance theories, which Liu says dissolve government and neglect authority. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official narrative on how the Party links theory, institutions and governance.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China takes mechanism-building, that is, the improvement of the institutions, regulations and policies that put the goals and principles of the system into practice, as an effective way to resolve the contradiction between the system's long-term stability and its dynamic operation.
quoteZh: 中国共产党以机制建构，即实际运行制度目标和原则的机构、法规、政策等的健全和完善，作为解决制度长期稳定性与动态运行性之间矛盾的有效方式。

glossary.explanation: The Chinese state form, presented in Party theory as the Chinese version of the dictatorship of the proletariat. It is enshrined in the Constitution as the basis of the state.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernization of the national governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal set by the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) as the overall aim of deepening reform. It refers to improving institutions and the ability to implement them.

t: The ethical functions of China's new type of party system
zh: 中国新型政党制度的伦理功能
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily (16 August 2021), Zhan Shiyou asks what political-ethical work China's new type of party system does. Zhan argues that the system, built on Communist Party leadership and multi-party cooperation, serves the public good of Chinese society. It does so through five functions: political participation, interest expression, social integration, democratic oversight and the maintenance of stability.

The short commentary takes each function in turn under its own heading. It describes the system as rooted in the pre-1949 cooperation between the Communist Party and the democratic parties, and it sets this against party systems of rotation in office and adversarial competition.

Zhan's central claim is that the democratic parties are participating parties, not opposition parties, and that consultation channels bring their views into major policy. In interest expression, Zhan holds that the parties should integrate the demands of particular strata into the fundamental interests of the people, turning "interest disputes" into "interest integration". Zhan presents integration as working through Party organisation at every level, grassroots Party building and shared ideals. Democratic oversight is said to help the Party govern scientifically, democratically and in accordance with law, and Zhan cites the 13th Five-Year Plan period as an example. Zhan also contends that the system avoids the social division produced by decisions made from party, class or regional standpoints.

Zhan concludes that the system puts into practice a political ethic of "using good to achieve good". Zhan sees it as producing considerable governance effectiveness and as a major contribution to human political civilisation. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how Chinese commentators frame the multi-party cooperation system in ethical terms.
quoteEn: China's new type of party system genuinely puts into practice the political value of using good to achieve good, performs a very important political-ethical function, can deliver great governance effectiveness, and is a major contribution to human political civilisation.
quoteZh: 中国新型政党制度真实地践行着以善致善的政治价值理念，具有十分重要的政治伦理功能，能够发挥出巨大治理效能，是对人类政治文明的重大贡献。

glossary.explanation: The official name for China's system of multi-party cooperation and political consultation under Communist Party leadership. It is presented in official discourse as distinct from Western multi-party competition.

The eight non-Communist parties that exist in China and take part in the political consultation system under Communist Party leadership. Official texts call them participating parties, not opposition parties.
The official designation of the democratic parties. It distinguishes them from both ruling and opposition parties.

t: Promoting a community with a shared future for mankind: the mission and responsibility of the Communist Party of China in the new era
zh: 推动构建人类命运共同体：新时代中国共产党的使命担当
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in July 2021, shortly after Xi Jinping's speech marking the Party's centenary, Liu Guizhen takes up one of the "nine musts" set out there: the need to keep promoting a community with a shared future for mankind. The article argues that this task expresses the Communist Party of China's concern for humanity's future and its responsibility to seek peace and development for all. Liu holds that the Party has the capacity and the duty to play a larger role in global affairs.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first sets out the Party's historical and cultural foundations, the second its practical basis, and the third its value orientation. It moves from classical Chinese texts and the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence to poverty reduction, the pandemic response, Chinese modernization and the Belt and Road Initiative, and finally to the notion of common values of humanity.

Liu first traces the idea to traditional Chinese thought on harmony, citing the Book of Documents and the Book of Rites. The author then follows a line of continuity from Zhou Enlai's Five Principles in 1953 and Deng Xiaoping's judgement that peace and development are the two major themes of the age, through to the 18th Party Congress (2012) and Xi's 2015 United Nations speech. In the practical section Liu cites figures: 98.99 million rural people lifted out of poverty, agreements with 140 countries and 32 international organisations under the Belt and Road Initiative, and over 350 million vaccine doses supplied abroad by 1 June 2021. Liu contrasts Chinese modernization, described as peaceful, with Western modernization achieved through plunder and war. The third part presents the Party's people-centred stance as the source of the idea. Liu says the common values of humanity (peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom) are the international reflection of that stance, and differ from "universal values" drawn along ideological lines.

Liu concludes that the pandemic shows humanity to be a community of shared destiny. In this view, abandoning Cold War thinking, upholding multilateralism and pursuing global governance through consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits is the right path. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's official narrative links the shared-future idea to tradition, foreign policy history, pandemic diplomacy and Belt and Road.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China's vision of building a community with a shared future for mankind has always aimed at promoting world peace and development, developing through inheritance and innovating through development.
quoteZh: 中国共产党倡导的构建人类命运共同体的构想始终以促进世界和平与发展为目标，从继承中发展，在发展中创新

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept written into the report of the 18th Party Congress in 2012 and elaborated by Xi Jinping. It calls for cooperation among states on the premise that nations' fates are interlinked.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries across Eurasia, Africa and beyond.
The official term for China's path to modernization. The article lists its features, including huge population size, common prosperity and peaceful development.

glossary.en: the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence
glossary.explanation: Principles of mutual respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. Zhou Enlai first put them forward in 1953.
Xi Jinping's 2015 formulation of peace, development, equity, justice, democracy and freedom as shared values. Official texts distinguish it from Western "universal values".

keywords: community with a shared future for mankind

t: Advancing steadily towards building a community with a shared future for mankind
zh: 朝着构建人类命运共同体方向不断迈进
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in November 2021, Qin Long and Liu Yushan take up Xi Jinping's statement at the centenary of the Communist Party (2021) that 'drawing on history to create the future' requires continuing to build a community with a shared future for mankind. The authors present the concept as part of Xi Jinping's diplomatic thought and as China's answer to the question of where human society should go. They argue that grasping its basic meaning and policy proposals is important for carrying the practice forward.

The short commentary has three parts. The first sets out the theoretical, cultural and practical roots of the concept. The second presents it as the Party's responsibility to seek happiness for the people and progress for humanity. The third turns to its policy content in the world economy, international relations and global governance.

On roots, the authors claim the concept inherits Marx's idea of the community. In their reading, Marx distinguished 'illusory' communities from the 'real community' in which individuals can be free, and the authors describe the community with a shared future as a transitional form towards the latter. They also trace it to traditional Chinese values of peace and harmony, and to the foreign policy experience from the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence through Deng Xiaoping's judgement that peace and development are the theme of the era. On responsibility, they say it reflects the Party's guidance on humanity's direction, its response to peoples' expectations, and its upholding of the common values of all humanity. On policy, they hold that it favours openness, with the Belt and Road Initiative as a practical platform. They also stress equality among states, rejection of power politics and non-interference, and global governance based on consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits.

The authors conclude that, facing great changes unseen in a century and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the Party will keep to an independent foreign policy of peace. It will also promote the common values of humanity and work with progressive forces towards the community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise statement, from the 2021 official-theory perspective, of how the concept is justified through Marxism, Chinese tradition and diplomatic history.
quoteEn: Building a community with a shared future for mankind advocates taking equality as the foundation and promoting a new type of international relations.
quoteZh: 构建人类命运共同体主张以平等为基础，推动建设新型国际关系。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept advanced by Xi Jinping after the 18th Party Congress (2012). It calls for states to treat their interests and futures as interlinked and to cooperate on development and global challenges.
An infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative proposed by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with countries in Asia, Africa and Europe.

glossary.en: the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence
