paras: Writing in the People's Daily on 7 July 2021, days after the centenary of the Communist Party of China, Liu Guangming takes up Xi Jinping's statement that, in drawing on history to open up the future, the Party "must continue to adapt Marxism to the Chinese context". Liu presents this as both a summary of a century of theoretical innovation and a pledge to keep enriching the latest results of that process. The commentary argues that the Party's history is one of continuous theoretical innovation and creation, and that Xi's 1 July speech is a programmatic document for the next stage.

The piece is a short commentary in four parts, each framed around remarks by Xi Jinping. The parts deal with upholding the principles of emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts, keeping pace with the times and being realistic and pragmatic; respecting the new creations of the people in practice; answering the new questions posed by the age; and drawing on new achievements of human civilisation. Liu moves between historical examples, from Mao Zedong to the Party's recent theoretical formulations, and forward-looking exhortations.

Liu's central claim is that Marxism stays vital because it is rooted in practice. Liu lists the sequence of theoretical results: Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Each, in this account, arose from answering a major problem of its period and from the people's own practice. Liu cites the household contract responsibility system, which Deng Xiaoping credited to the peasants, as an example of popular innovation later turned into theory. Liu also says that after the late 1970s the Party shifted its theoretical theme to building socialism with Chinese characteristics, reaching conclusions such as that socialism does not equal a planned economy. At the same time Liu stresses holding the ideological line and Marxism's guiding position.

Liu calls for freeing thinking from outdated ideas, from dogmatic readings of Marxism, and from subjectivism and metaphysics, so that the Party can deepen its understanding of the laws of Party rule, socialist construction and human social development. Theory should be problem-oriented and should absorb the best of human civilisation, including in the digital and intelligent fields, while starting from China's own conditions. The aim is to make contemporary Chinese Marxism, the Marxism of the twenty-first century, more powerful. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the official press framed the continuing adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context at the centenary of the Party in 2021.
quoteEn: Respecting the people's practice, drawing intellectual nourishment from their great creations and elevating it into theory is the inexhaustible source of the Party's theoretical innovation.
quoteZh: 尊重人民实践、从人民的伟大创造中汲取思想营养并上升为理论，是我们党进行理论创新的不竭源泉。

glossary.zh: 解放思想、实事求是、与时俱进、求真务实
glossary.pinyin: jiěfàng sīxiǎng, shíshì qiúshì, yǔshí jùjìn, qiúzhēn wùshí
glossary.en: emancipating the mind, seeking truth from facts, keeping pace with the times and being realistic and pragmatic
glossary.explanation: A four-part formula of ideological guidelines in Party discourse. It stresses breaking with outdated thinking while basing policy on practical reality.
Jiang Zemin's theory, introduced around 2000. It holds that the Party represents advanced productive forces, the advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the overwhelming majority.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept that stresses people-centred, comprehensive, balanced and sustainable development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
Rural reform of the late 1970s and 1980s that let farm households contract land and keep surplus output. It replaced collective farming in the people's communes.

t: Studying and understanding the Party's innovative theory of the new era
zh: 深刻学习领会新时代党的创新理论
paras: This short commentary, published in Chengdu Daily in June 2021, asks how Party members should study Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Wang and Qiu present it as the Marxism of contemporary China and of the twenty-first century, and as the latest result of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context. They argue that study should grasp its theoretical character and also its philosophical method, scientific spirit and political wisdom.

The article is organised in three sections: theory lives through innovation; innovative theory arises from innovative practice; and innovative theory guides innovative practice. It opens with a survey of the Party's century of theoretical innovation, running from Mao Zedong Thought through Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents and the Scientific Outlook on Development to Xi Jinping's thought.

The core argument is a two-way relation between theory and practice. The authors hold that the Party's theory has always begun where its practice begins, citing the new development philosophy, the green-mountains idea and targeted poverty alleviation as responses to problems after the 18th Party Congress (2012). They then claim that the thought guides practice, pointing to the victory over absolute poverty, the nearly completed moderately prosperous society, epidemic control and GDP above 100 trillion yuan as evidence of its power.

The authors conclude that theory stays vital only when it is tied to its era, to Chinese realities and to the people's needs. They call for studying the new theory thoroughly, using it to unify thinking and draw the widest "concentric circle" around the Party, and continuing theoretical innovation on the basis of practice. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party press presents the lineage of Sinicized Marxism and the theory–practice relationship in 2021.
quoteEn: Wherever the great practice of socialism with Chinese characteristics begins, there the Party's theory begins; whatever development and innovation occurs in practice, theory advances together with it.
quoteZh: 中国特色社会主义的伟大实践从哪里开始，党的理论就从哪里开始，有什么样的实践发展和创新，就有什么样的理论随之“俱进”。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official guiding ideology of the Communist Party of China, written into the Party constitution in 2017. It is presented as the latest stage of adapting Marxism to China.
A theory associated with Jiang Zemin, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority.
A guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive and sustainable development.
A framework introduced in 2015 stressing innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.

t: The great leap from standing up and growing rich to becoming strong
zh: 从站起来、富起来到强起来的伟大飞跃
paras: Published in the People's Daily on 24 June 2021, in the run-up to the Communist Party's centenary, this commentary presents a Party-history narrative. Chen Li argues that under the Party's leadership the Chinese nation has passed through a "great leap" from "standing up" to "growing rich" to "becoming strong". In the author's account, the dawn of the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation now lies ahead.

The article is organised in four numbered sections following the Party's history. The first covers the semi-colonial, semi-feudal China after the Opium War, the founding of the Party and the revolution under Mao Zedong. The second covers reform and opening up under Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao. The third deals with the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012) under Xi Jinping, including the response to Covid-19 and poverty alleviation. The fourth looks ahead to the goals for 2035 and the middle of the century.

Chen's central move is to assign each stage a distinct historical achievement, each tied to a theoretical innovation by successive Party leaderships. The founding of the People's Republic is said to have ended the old semi-colonial order and laid the political and institutional foundation, together with an independent industrial system, for national wealth. Reform and opening up, the author says, released productive forces: the article cites average annual real GDP growth of 9.8% in 1979–2012 against roughly 2.8% worldwide, and a rise in China's share of the world economy from 1.8% to 11.5%. For the Xi era, the article credits Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era with historic achievements, citing the pandemic response, GDP above 100 trillion yuan in 2020 and the end of absolute poverty.

Chen concludes that the first centenary goal, a moderately prosperous society, has been achieved, and that the 19th Party Congress (2017) set out goals of basic modernization by 2035 and a strong modern socialist country by mid-century. The author calls the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation a relay race and warns that it will not be easy. Chen urges the whole Party to unite around the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core, maintain the Four-sphere Confidence and carry out the Two Upholds. Read the original if you want a compact example of the official periodisation of Party history published at the 2021 centenary.
quoteEn: Realising the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation is a relay race.
quoteZh: 实现中华民族伟大复兴，是一场接力长跑。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, associated especially with Xi Jinping's "Chinese Dream", of restoring China to national strength and prosperity after what the Party calls a century of humiliation.
The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. It introduced market-oriented economic reform and opened China to foreign trade and investment.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology under Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018.
Official slogan calling for confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
A Party requirement to uphold the core position of Xi Jinping in the Central Committee and the Party's centralised, unified leadership.
A development goal dating from Deng Xiaoping's era. Its full realisation was declared in 2021 as the first of the "two centenary goals".

t: Laying a solid foundation for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
zh: 为实现中华民族伟大复兴奠定坚实基础
paras: Published in the People's Daily in June 2021, in the centenary year of the Communist Party of China, this commentary by Li Jie reviews the Party's hundred years. Li argues that since its founding the Party has made the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation its mission, and that through revolution, construction and reform it has carried the nation from "standing up" through "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong".

The piece has three parts. The first surveys the century in three stages: the revolution, the building of socialism after 1949, and reform and opening up. The second describes the situation after the 18th Party Congress (2012) and the prospects for national rejuvenation. The third draws four lessons from the hundred years, and quotes Xi Jinping on each.

Li frames modern Chinese history as the pursuit of two tasks: national independence and the people's liberation, and national prosperity and the people's wellbeing. In Li's account the Party achieved the first through 28 years of armed struggle and the founding of the People's Republic. It then laid the basic socialist system and an independent industrial system, and, after the Cultural Revolution, opened the way to socialism with Chinese characteristics through reform and opening up. For the recent period Li cites figures: the world's second-largest economy, GDP above 100 trillion yuan, urbanisation above 60%, a middle-income group above 400 million, and the elimination of absolute poverty. Li presents the new development stage, set out by the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020), as the start of a new journey to build a modern socialist country.

The four lessons are firm ideals and convictions, standing with the people, seeking truth from facts, and a problem-oriented approach. Li calls on Party members to hold to these on the new journey and to keep a sense of "matters of national importance". Li concludes that no force can stop the Chinese people's advance and that the Party will lead the people to new achievements. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official People's Daily account of the Party's centenary, with its periodisation and its four lessons.
quoteEn: Reform and opening up is an important magic weapon for the Party and the people to catch up with the times in great strides, the only way to uphold and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics, and the key move that decides the fate of contemporary China, as well as the key to achieving the "two centenary goals" and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.
quoteZh: 改革开放是党和人民大踏步赶上时代的重要法宝，是坚持和发展中国特色社会主义的必由之路，是决定当代中国命运的关键一招，也是决定实现“两个一百年”奋斗目标、实现中华民族伟大复兴的关键一招。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's long-term goal of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the "century of humiliation". It has been central to official discourse, especially since Xi Jinping's leadership began.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. It shifted the Party's focus to economic construction.
The official name for China's path, theory and system since reform and opening up. It combines a leading role for the Party with a market economy.
A principle associated with Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping that policy should start from actual conditions and be tested in practice.

t: A century of tempering forged the bearing of a great Party
zh: 百年淬炼铸就大党风范
paras: Published in Economic Daily on 21 June 2021, shortly before the centenary of the Communist Party of China, this commentary asks what the "bearing of a great Party" (dadang fengfan) consists of and how a hundred years of history produced it. Zhao Zhongyuan argues that this bearing is the spiritual distillation of the Party's size and stature, and that it was formed through a century of struggle and trial.

Zhao starts from Xi Jinping's 2017 remark that the world's largest party must have the appearance of a large one, and defines "bearing" as an inner quality made visible in conduct. It is built from four elements: conviction, sentiment, character and capability. The commentary devotes one section to each, describing them as tempered by the Party's history. It recommends studying Party history together with the history of the People's Republic, of reform and opening up, and of socialist development.

On conviction, Zhao holds that the Party has preserved its "advanced nature and purity" by keeping faith in Marxism, by developing Marxism in step with the times through its integration with Chinese conditions, and by tempering Party spirit in practice. On sentiment, the author says the Party puts the people first and follows the mass line, and that since the 18th Party Congress (2012) it has pursued a people-centred approach. Zhao adds that the Party takes responsibility internationally by promoting party exchanges, advancing a community with a shared future for mankind and opposing unilateralism.

On character, Zhao presents the Party's record of struggle, from the revolutionary period to the new era, and names self-reform as its most distinctive trait and greatest strength. On capability, the author cites the Party's achievements: broad people's democracy, rapid economic growth, the end of absolute poverty and the opening of a new drive to build a modern socialist country. Zhao traces these to the Party's roots in Marxism, traditional culture, the people and practice, and to its emphasis on learning. The commentary concludes that further drawing on historical experience will let the Party meet future risks and open new horizons for socialism with Chinese characteristics. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholars framed the centenary and the Party's self-image in 2021.
quoteEn: Daring to carry out self-reform is the Party's most distinctive character and also its greatest strength.
quoteZh: 勇于自我革命,是我们党最鲜明的品格,也是我们党最大的优势。

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: A foreign-policy concept promoted by Xi Jinping since around 2013, calling for shared development and cooperation among states.
Official term for the Party's efforts to discipline, purify and renew itself, presented as a defining trait of the CPC.
A working method associated with Mao Zedong in which Party cadres gather the views of the people, process them and return them as policy, while relying on the people.
The official name for China's path since reform and opening up, combining Party leadership, public ownership as the mainstay and a market economy.
Official qualities said to define a Marxist party: advanced nature refers to its guiding ideology and aims, purity to loyalty and integrity in thought, politics, organisation and conduct.

t: The Communist Party of China and China's modernization
zh: 中国共产党与中国现代化
paras: Written for the Party's centenary in 2021, the article asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) relates to China's modernization and what lies behind its success. Chen argues that building a modern country has been the most distinctive theme of the Party's hundred years of struggle. In Chen's account, success came mainly because the Party found a modernization path suited to China's own conditions.

The article first divides the century into two stages. Before 1949, the new-democratic revolution removed imperialism and feudalism and created the basic political conditions for modernization. The author recalls the failure of the Self-Strengthening Movement and of Sun Yat-sen's plans, and quotes Mao Zedong on industrialization. After 1949, Chen traces the path from the "four modernizations" through the "three-step" strategy and the "two centenary goals" to the post-2012 period under Xi Jinping.

The core of the article lists five features of Chinese modernization. It is led by the Party, which Chen calls the decisive factor, citing five-year plans and long-term blueprints pursued as "one blueprint to the end". It is based on China's actual conditions, above all the primary stage of socialism, a huge population and a poor starting point. It is people-centred, with development for, by and shared with the people. It is comprehensive, covering prosperity, democracy, culture, harmony and ecology, and common prosperity. Finally, it is independent: Chen insists that modernization is socialist, rejecting both the "closed and rigid old path" and the "wrong path of changing banners", and not a single Western model.

Chen concludes that the Party's institutional strengths, illustrated by the author's account of the response to the Covid-19 epidemic, justify confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The article claims this path widens the options for developing countries that want faster growth while keeping their independence, and offers "Chinese wisdom" and a "Chinese approach" to global problems. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of how Party theorists in 2021 narrated the link between the Party's history and modernization.
quoteEn: There are many reasons for the success of China's modernization, but in the final analysis the most important is that it is the result of the Communist Party of China's strong leadership.
quoteZh: 中国现代化成功的原因有很多条，但归根到底最重要的一条，是中国共产党坚强领导的结果。

glossary.explanation: Two long-term targets set out at the 15th Party Congress (1997): a moderately prosperous society by the Party's centenary in 2021, and a modernized socialist country by the People's Republic's centenary in 2049.

Deng Xiaoping-era development plan: meet basic needs by 1990, reach a xiaokang standard of living by the end of the century, and reach the level of a moderately developed country by the mid-21st century.
Official characterization of China's present historical stage, held to last a long time because productive forces remain underdeveloped.
The official name for the Party's reform-era path, theory and system of socialism adapted to China's conditions.
A goal of prosperity shared by all, presented in official discourse as an essential requirement of socialism.

t: Making efforts in studying Party history, grasping the Thought, doing practical things and opening new prospects
zh: 在学党史悟思想办实事开新局上下功夫
paras: This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 21 June 2021, takes up the Party History Study and Education campaign launched in the centenary year of the Communist Party. Tang argues that Party members and cadres should keep working along four lines: studying Party history, grasping the Thought, doing practical things for the people and opening new prospects. The aim is to deliver results in the new stage of development.

The piece is organised under four headings, each with its own required outcome: a new level in the compulsory course of Party history, a new consciousness of the power of ideas, new results in practical work for the people, and new breakthroughs in nurturing opportunities and opening new prospects. It draws repeatedly on remarks by Xi Jinping.

In Tang's account, a century of Party history offers experience that cadres can turn into ideological enlightenment and working skills. Cadres are urged to master the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, to study Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, to evaluate major events and figures correctly and to oppose historical nihilism. Tang says the purpose of study is application: employment, healthcare, education and housing projects, balanced regional development and substantive progress towards common prosperity, while avoiding vanity projects.

Tang concludes that, in a world undergoing great changes unseen in a century, history should help cadres respond to risks. Cadres are called on to implement the new development philosophy and the 14th Five-Year Plan, build the new development pattern of dual circulation, pursue high-quality development and strengthen bottom-line thinking. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party media framed the practical aims of the 2021 history-study campaign.
quoteEn: The whole purpose of study lies in application.
quoteZh: 学习的目的全在于运用。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
An official goal of prosperity shared by all, which Party leaders have emphasised in the Xi era.
Official concept, put forward in 2015, centred on innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development.
An official economic goal that stresses quality and efficiency rather than speed of growth.
In official usage, a label for views that are said to negate the Party's history and the path of socialism in China.

t: Heaven and earth overturned, with passion and resolve: a hundred years of the Communist Party of China
zh: 天翻地覆慨而慷：中国共产党的100年
paras: Written for the Party's centenary in 2021, this article by Shi Zhongquan offers a narrative overview of the Communist Party of China's first hundred years. Shi argues that the Party's history can be read as four successive struggles: saving the nation, founding the state, enriching the country and strengthening it. Each is tied to a slogan: the Chinese people have stood up, the basic socialist system has been set up, the people have begun to grow rich, and China has begun to grow strong.

The article follows the four periods that the Party itself uses: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Part one treats the founding, with Chen Duxiu as principal founder, and Mao Zedong's leadership to victory in 1949. Part two covers 1949–1978, including the Korean War, land reform, socialist transformation, the First Five-Year Plan, the Great Leap Forward and its correction, the Cultural Revolution and the 1976 arrest of the Gang of Four. Parts three and four review the leadership of Deng Xiaoping, Jiang Zemin, Hu Jintao and Xi Jinping. Shi supports the account with economic, poverty-reduction, military and diplomatic statistics.

Shi attributes the revolutionary victory to a new path (encircling the cities from the countryside) and three "magic weapons": Party building, armed struggle and the united front. Chen Duxiu is credited with founding the Party but is described as an immature leader who made right-opportunist errors in 1927, partly because of Comintern instructions. For the reform era, Shi stresses Deng's redefinition of socialism, the primary stage of socialism, and the socialist market economy. Jiang's Three Represents and Hu's Scientific Outlook on Development follow. For the Xi era, Shi lists achievements in the economy, innovation, poverty alleviation, military reform, diplomacy, the Belt and Road Initiative and a community with a shared future for mankind. He also credits full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, including the anti-corruption campaign, which he calls a decisive victory. Shi treats the Cultural Revolution as a disaster while describing Mao's original aims as defending the Party's purity and finding a Chinese road to socialism.

Shi concludes that the Party is both a century-old and a strong party, and that after meeting the first centenary goal of a moderately prosperous society in all respects it has begun building a modern socialist country towards the second centenary goal. The text is an official-style historical narrative, mainly of use for seeing how the Party's own periodisation and verdicts were presented in 2021. Read the original if you want a detailed example of the centenary account of Party history, with its statistics and its assessments of Chen Duxiu, Mao, Deng and later leaders.
quoteEn: The Communist Party of China is both a century-old major party and a century-old strong party.
quoteZh: 中国共产党既是百年大党，也是百年强党。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Slogan put forward by Xi Jinping in 2014 for strengthening Party discipline, anti-corruption work and internal regulation.
Official thesis that China, as an economically underdeveloped country, is at an early stage of socialism that will last a long time. It was formalised at the 13th Party Congress in 1987.
Guiding idea associated with Jiang Zemin, stating that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the majority.
Guiding concept associated with Hu Jintao, stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of shared interests and joint global governance.
Infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative announced by Xi Jinping in 2013.
Policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.

t: The Chinese Communist Party's historical experience of building a socialist state
zh: 中国共产党建设社会主义国家的历史经验
paras: This newspaper commentary, published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in June 2021, asks what experience the Chinese Communist Party has accumulated in building and improving the socialist state system. Liu Fangliang argues that the Party has developed a path of state-system construction that runs from theoretical guidance, through operating mechanisms, to governance.

The piece is organised in three parts that follow this sequence. It first treats the adaptation of Marxist political theory to Chinese conditions across the revolutionary period, the founding of the People's Republic and the post-1978 era. It then turns to mechanism innovation, and finally to the modernization of the state governance system and governance capacity.

On theory, Liu holds that the classic writers left no detailed plan for building socialism in a backward Eastern country, so the Party had to combine Marxist doctrine with national conditions. Examples include New Democracy, the people's democratic dictatorship, the people's congress system, multi-party cooperation and political consultation under Party leadership, regional ethnic autonomy, and the theory of the primary stage of socialism. On mechanisms, Liu distinguishes a stable state system from dynamic operating mechanisms: the leadership, public ownership and people's democratic dictatorship stay fixed, while institutions, regulations and policies are renewed. Grassroots practices such as the household contract responsibility system were written into the constitution, and foreign borrowing is confined to the mechanism level.

Liu concludes that, since the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), making governance capacity the concrete expression of the state system has refined it across political, economic, social, cultural and ecological fields. In Liu's view this also criticises and goes beyond Western "society-centred" governance theories that dissolve government and neglect authority. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line statement of how Chinese scholars frame the Party's institutional experience.
quoteEn: Foreign borrowing is limited to the level of mechanisms, while at the level of the state system the fundamental defining features of socialism with Chinese characteristics are always upheld without wavering.
quoteZh: 对外借鉴仅限于机制层面，国家制度上则始终坚守中国特色社会主义的根本规定性不动摇

glossary.explanation: A theory formalised in the 1980s holding that China is in an early, long-lasting phase of socialism with underdeveloped productive forces.
The constitutional definition of China's state nature, presented as the Chinese form of the dictatorship of the proletariat, led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance.

glossary.zh: 国家治理体系和治理能力现代化
glossary.pinyin: guójiā zhìlǐ tǐxì hé zhìlǐ nénglì xiàndàihuà
glossary.en: modernization of the state governance system and governance capacity
glossary.explanation: A goal set at the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) as the overall aim of comprehensively deepening reform.

t: Telling the Party's stories well and passing on the red gene
zh: 讲好党的故事 传承红色基因
paras: Published in People's Daily in June 2021, in the centenary year of the Communist Party, this commentary asks how the Party's history can be conveyed so that the 'red gene' is handed down. Long Xinmin argues that the Party's stories are a vivid interpretation of its history and a living teaching resource. The author builds on Xi Jinping's call to tell stories of the Party, the revolution, the base areas, heroes and martyrs, so that the 'red country' never changes colour.

The article has three parts. The first treats the Party's stories as carriers of its original aspiration and founding mission, its fine work style and its spirit of struggle. The second explains why these stories matter for Party members and officials, for young people and for society as a whole. The third sets out practical measures for telling the stories of the new era that began with the 18th Party Congress (2012). Examples range from the textbook tales of the 'half a quilt' and Zhu De's carrying pole to Xia Minghan, Jiang Jie, Wang Jinxi, Jiao Yulu and Lei Feng.

In Long's account, the stories show communists serving the people and sharing hardships with ordinary soldiers. They also show successive generations making sacrifices in revolution, construction and reform. For officials, the stories nourish the original aspiration and the faith in Marxism, as in the account of Chen Wangdao finding the taste of truth 'very sweet'. For young people, the stories explain where the red state and today's life came from. They are meant to lead young people to follow the Party. For society, models such as Lei Feng are said to raise moral standards and strengthen shared ideals as China pursues the second centenary goal.

Long concludes that stories of the new era are still under-represented in textbooks and in literary and artistic work. The author proposes campaigns to collect and create new stories, drawing on poverty alleviation and the fight against Covid-19. The author also wants such stories placed in textbooks, classrooms and students' minds, and calls for a large corps of storytellers made up of teachers, officials, veterans, volunteers and journalists. Read the original if you want a clear example of how official commentary frames Party history education and storytelling as tools for ideological transmission.
quoteEn: The Party's stories are a vivid interpretation of the Party's history.
quoteZh: 党的故事是对党的历史的生动诠释

glossary.explanation: A metaphor in Party discourse for the revolutionary ideals, traditions and spirit of the Communist Party, said to be inherited by each generation. Xi Jinping has repeatedly called for it to be passed on.
The Party's stated purpose of seeking happiness for the Chinese people and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. It was prominent in Party education campaigns from 2019.
The goal of building China into a modern socialist country by 2049, the centenary of the People's Republic. The first goal was to build a moderately prosperous society by 2021.

glossary.zh: 中国特色社会主义新时代
glossary.literal: new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics
glossary.explanation: The official name for the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012), marked by Xi Jinping's leadership and presented as a new historical stage.

t: Party self-knowledge: the secret of how a century-old Party keeps its advanced nature
zh: 政党自知：百年大党长期保持先进性的奥秘
source: Jianghan Forum (Jianghan Luntan), no. 6; the stated year of 2012 appears inconsistent with the 2021 content
paras: Writing around the centenary of the Communist Party of China in 2021, Yu Chongsheng asks why this Party has kept its advanced nature through a century of history and more than 70 years in power. Yu's answer is "Party self-knowledge": a Party's clear grasp of its own mission, strengths, shortcomings and historical moment. The article presents this as the main secret of the Party's long-term vitality.

The article has three parts. The first defines Party self-knowledge, drawing on the Daodejing's idea that knowing oneself is true insight and on Fei Xiaotong's notion of cultural self-awareness. The second explains why it matters, using Mao Zedong's remarks on self-knowledge and the Soviet collapse as a negative case. The third sets out ways to advance it. It opens by noting how few parties worldwide have lasted over a century or governed continuously.

Yu argues that Party self-knowledge goes beyond Party confidence because it unites four "selfs": confidence, awareness, introspection and discipline. Awareness comes first logically, since only rational awareness can ground firm confidence. Advanced nature is neither innate nor permanent, so a ruling party must keep checking itself. Yu reads the Soviet Communist Party's fall, citing Ryzhkov and a study of the Soviet system's end, as the result of distorted ideas about socialism and complacency. Yu calls Huntington's explanation of the Party's durability superficial because it ignores advanced nature. Four paths follow: use the Party's theoretical, political, organisational, institutional and mass-line strengths; face its limits and learn from mistakes; meet risks calmly, including by bottom-line thinking and a spirit of struggle; and keep the four "selfs" in proper relation.

Yu concludes that the Party's history is a history of the Party's self-reform, expressed as self-purification, self-improvement, self-renewal and self-elevation, each answering a specific weakness of long single-party rule. Yu holds that self-knowledge must be advanced continually, given the "four tests" and "four dangers" the Party faces, and that it is needed for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a Chinese Party-theory account that links Daoist and Confucian-era ideas of self-knowledge to arguments about Party building and the Soviet experience.
quoteEn: Party self-knowledge therefore becomes the combined expression of Party confidence, Party awareness, Party introspection and Party discipline.
quoteZh: 因此，政党自知就成为政党自信、政党自觉、政党自省、政党自律的综合体现。

glossary.explanation: A concept the author develops from the Daodejing's idea of self-knowledge. It covers a party's clear grasp of its mission, strengths, flaws and historical conditions, and it combines confidence, awareness, introspection and discipline.
In Party discourse, the quality of being the vanguard that leads society and the people. It is treated as a defining trait of a Marxist party that must be maintained continually.
An official formulation, prominent in Xi Jinping-era discourse, for the Party's efforts to correct its own errors and improve its conduct without outside checks.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The official long-term national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, central to Party discourse since the early 2010s.

t: The Communist Party of China's century of history and historical initiative
zh: 中国共产党百年历史与历史主动
paras: Published in Guangming Daily in June 2021, in the run-up to the Party's centenary, this article by Qu Qingshan asks how the Communist Party of China (CPC) has combined respect for objective historical laws with active, purposeful agency. Qu's answer is the concept of "historical initiative". The CPC, he argues, has followed the laws of historical development, conformed to the main historical trend and so seized the initiative at each stage. He frames this as an application of historical materialism, drawing on Xi Jinping's speech of 20 February 2021 launching Party history study and education.

The article opens with a theoretical premise. In Qu's account, history has objective laws, but humans have "conscious dynamism", and a Marxist party should unite conformity to law with conformity to purpose. It then moves through five periods, each introduced with the same formula: the founding of the Party, the founding of the People's Republic, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the entry of socialism with Chinese characteristics into a new era. A final section draws nine lessons from the century.

Qu argues that each turning point was an inevitable product or outcome of historical trends. The Party emerged from the failure of earlier attempts at national rejuvenation, the example of the October Revolution, the spread of Marxism-Leninism and the rise of the Chinese working class. The later stages are presented as correct readings of the era: the united front against Japan, victory in the civil war, socialist transformation, and the post-1978 turn to reform and opening up. Qu also reviews the theoretical achievements of successive leadership generations, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Each lesson, such as keeping to the original aspiration, grasping the principal contradiction, struggle, reform and innovation, unity and advancing human progress, is tied to a task for the "new journey".

Qu concludes that this grasp of trends carried China from "standing up" through "becoming prosperous" to "becoming strong". He treats the nine lessons as guidance for building a modern socialist country and meeting the "second centenary" goals, including the 2035 and 2050 strategic arrangements. The article is an authoritative statement of the official narrative of Party history in its centenary year. Read the original if you want to see how the Party's official historiography links historical materialism to the claim of a consistent historical initiative across the whole century.
quoteEn: The birth of the Communist Party of China was the inevitable product of following the laws of historical development, conforming to the main trend of history and seizing the historical initiative.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的诞生是遵循历史发展规律、顺应历史发展大势、掌握历史主动的必然产物。

glossary.literal: historical initiative / taking the lead in history
glossary.explanation: A concept in Party historiography. It describes the Party as acting purposefully by grasping the laws and main trends of history, instead of passively following events.

The policy launched at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping. It shifted the focus to economic development, market-oriented reform and opening to the outside world.
The official name for the Party's path of socialist development since the reform era. It combines Marxism with China's specific conditions.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: The Communist Party of China's century-long exploration and practice of people's democracy
zh: 中国共产党对人民民主的百年探索与实践
source: Journal of Northwest Normal University (Social Sciences), 2021 no. 4
paras: Written in the centenary year of the Party's founding (2021), this article asks how the Communist Party of China has pursued people's democracy since 1921. Wang Zongli argues that the Party's history is a history of struggle for people's democracy: a continuous effort to combine Marxist democratic theory with Chinese conditions, to build institutions of popular rule, to diversify democratic forms and to refine a distinctive path and theory. In Wang's account, this has produced a new road of democracy with Chinese characteristics.

The article has four parts. It first traces people's democracy as the Party's goal through the revolutionary periods, the Soviet Republic, the anti-Japanese base areas, the founding of the People's Republic, and the leadership eras from Deng Xiaoping to Xi Jinping. It then examines the meaning of 'the people as masters of the country' and how the scope of 'the people' has changed. The last two parts cover the institutional system of people's democracy and its forms: electoral, consultative and participatory democracy.

Wang's central claim is that most Western theorists treat democracy only as a question of political system, whereas Marxism treats it first as the relation between state power and the people, and so as a question of who owns power. Democracy therefore involves the state's class nature, the way organs of power are formed under democratic centralism, and the state's responsiveness to popular interests. Wang stresses that 'the people' is a historical category that has widened, from workers and peasants to include intellectuals, private entrepreneurs and patriots working for national rejuvenation. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012), Wang holds, the institutional system has been strengthened through Party leadership, the people's congress system, a new type of party system, regional ethnic autonomy and grassroots self-governance. Wang describes consultative democracy as a distinctively Chinese form and argues that Western participatory democracy cannot achieve direct popular management because of the limits of capitalist private ownership.

Wang concludes that people's democracy is the broadest, most genuine and most effective form of democracy, and a higher type than bourgeois democracy. Wang calls for upholding Party leadership while making democracy more institutionalised, law-based and procedural, perfecting the people's congress system, widening orderly political participation, and combining electoral and consultative democracy. Read the original if you want a Party-historical account of how Chinese scholarship in 2021 framed a century of democratic practice, with a detailed chronology of institutions and electoral laws.
quoteEn: Without a well-developed democratic system, the people being masters of the country is an empty phrase.
quoteZh: 没有完善的民主制度，人民当家作主就是一句空话。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for its own model of democracy, grounded in the idea that state power belongs to the people under the leadership of the working class and the Party. It is presented as the essence of socialist democracy.

glossary.en: the people as masters of the country
glossary.literal: the people act as masters of the house
glossary.explanation: A standard formula in Chinese political discourse for popular sovereignty, which the Party treats as the core of socialist democracy.

China's fundamental political institution, in which deputies elected at local levels choose higher congresses up to the National People's Congress. Official accounts describe it as the organ through which the people exercise power.

A form of democracy in which Party, democratic parties, the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference and other bodies consult on decisions. Official discourse treats it as a distinctive feature of Chinese democracy.
A basic political system under which areas with concentrated ethnic minority populations exercise autonomy within the unified state.

t: Mao Zedong and the opening of a new path for the Chinese revolution
st: A dialogue with Professor Sha Jiansun
zh: 毛泽东与中国革命新道路的开辟
zhSub: 与沙健孙教授的对谈
source: Journal of Ideological and Theoretical Education (思想理论教育导刊), 2021
paras: This is a dialogue, published for the centenary of the Communist Party of China in 2021, between Li Yuanpeng, an associate professor at Guizhou Normal University, and Sha Jiansun, a professor at Peking University's School of Marxism. It builds on Sha's 1983 essay and his 2016 book on Mao Zedong and the opening of the new revolutionary path in the Agrarian Revolutionary War period. Sha's central claim is that Mao was the chief representative of a collective effort that opened the road of encircling the cities from the countryside and seizing power by armed force, and that this road was the only correct one after 1927.

Li, who raised the questions while teaching the course Outline of Modern Chinese History, organises the exchange into six topics. They are the definition of the new path; the Party's exploration after the failure of the Great Revolution in 1927; Mao's role; his creative solutions to problems of sustaining rural base areas; the path's significance for the formation of Mao Zedong Thought; and its link to the revival and victory of the revolution through to 1949.

On definition, Sha holds that the path has two defining features: protracted revolutionary war as the main form of struggle, and the countryside first, cities later, as the main direction of attack. He therefore judges formulas such as "the road of red political power" or "armed independent regime of workers and peasants" imprecise. On Mao's role, Sha stresses that the path came from the collective wisdom of Party and people, not from one genius. He still credits Mao with early commitment to armed struggle and to the countryside, and with solving problems the classics could not answer. These included building a proletarian party with a peasant membership through ideological work (the Gutian Resolution), shaping a people's army, devising guerrilla strategy and tactics, and framing a land policy of relying on poor peasants and redistributing land by population.

Sha argues that this path, much of it contrary to Comintern instructions, shows Chinese communists learning to think independently and combine Marxism with Chinese practice, which makes it a marker of Mao Zedong Thought's formation. He ties this to Mao's essay Oppose Book Worship, which he reads as an early statement of seeking truth from facts, the mass line and independence. The dialogue closes by tracing the path through the War of Resistance and the civil war to the 1949 shift of emphasis to the cities. Read the original if you want a Party-historian's detailed account of how the "countryside encircling the cities" strategy is defined, periodised and credited to Mao within official historiography.
quoteEn: Using the armed, revolutionary countryside to encircle the cities held by the counter-revolution, so as finally to seize them, was the only feasible road after 1927 for reviving the Chinese revolution and winning victory.
quoteZh: 以武装革命的农村包围被反革命占领的城市以便最后夺取这些城市，是1927年以后复兴中国革命和争取中国革命胜利的唯一可行的道路。

glossary.en: encircling the cities from the countryside
glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's strategy after 1927 of building rural base areas and armed forces first, then taking the cities. Official historiography presents it as the distinctive path of the Chinese revolution.
A resolution drafted by Mao for the Fourth Red Army's Party congress in December 1929. It sets out the principles of the Party's command over the army and ideological work in the Party and army.

The official Party doctrine of the Marxism-Leninism adapted to Chinese conditions, credited to Mao and the collective experience of the Party. Official accounts say it took shape in the late 1920s and 1930s.
The Party's term for 1927–1937, when it fought the Kuomintang while building rural base areas and redistributing land.
A principle taken up by Mao as the core of the Party's ideological line, meaning to start from actual conditions rather than from books or dogma.

keywords: encircling the cities from the countryside

t: The Communist Party of China's source of strength and guarantee of victory
zh: 中国共产党的力量源泉与胜利保障
paras: Published in Red Flag Manuscripts and posted in June 2021, shortly before the Party's centenary, this commentary asks why the Communist Party of China won the whole country within 28 years and has since achieved what the author calls world-renowned successes over more than seven decades. Xue Guangzhou answers that the Party's strength and guarantee of victory rest on three things: holding to a lofty faith, forming a correct ideological line, and forging a strong ranks of members through strict Party discipline.

The article is organised in three sections matching these answers. It moves through the Party's history, from the 1921 first programme, the Long March and the Korean War to reform and opening up and the period after the 18th Party Congress (2012). It draws on statements by Mao Zedong, Li Dazhao and Xi Jinping, and on Marxist classics concerning the proletarian party.

On faith, Xue argues that the Party's fate is tied to that of the broad masses, and that, unlike bourgeois parties serving a minority, it serves the great majority. Conviction carried Party members through the defeat of the Great Revolution, the losses on the Long March and the Korean War, and Xue attributes the fall of some officials in the reform era to a failure of faith. On the ideological line, the author holds that integrating Marxism's universal principles with Chinese practice produced the line of seeking truth from facts, which Xue credits with the revolution, socialist transformation and reform, and sees continued in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. On Party building, Xue traces a tradition of strictness from the first programme through democratic centralism, rectification campaigns and the "two musts", to the eight-point regulations, anti-corruption drive and Party regulations of the Xi era.

Xue concludes that full and rigorous self-governance of the Party must continue, because the "four tests" and "four dangers" remain serious and impurities in thought, politics, organisation and style are not yet fundamentally solved. The author calls for strengthening the Four Consciousnesses, the Four-sphere Confidence and the Two Upholds, and for making officials neither dare, nor be able, nor want to be corrupt. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official Party commentary around the 2021 centenary framed the sources of the Party's success.
quoteEn: The fundamental source of the Communist Party of China's strength and guarantee of victory lies in holding to a lofty faith, forming a correct ideological line, and forging a strong ranks of members.
quoteZh: 中国共产党的力量源泉与胜利保障的根本在于，坚守了崇高的信仰，形成了正确的思想路线，锻造出了坚强的队伍。

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.literal: comprehensively and strictly govern the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan for the Party's disciplinary and anti-corruption drive, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012).

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party constitution at the 19th Party Congress in 2017.
A Party requirement to uphold General Secretary Xi Jinping's core position and the authority and centralised leadership of the Central Committee.
Confidence in the path, theory, system and culture of socialism with Chinese characteristics.
The Party's ideological line of basing policy on actual conditions, associated with Mao Zedong and restored under Deng Xiaoping after the Cultural Revolution.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, whereby decisions are made after discussion and then binding on all members, with lower levels obeying higher ones.

t: The Communist Party of China and Chinese modernization
zh: 中国共产党与中国式现代化
paras: Published in the People's Daily around the Party's centenary in 2021, this commentary asks how the Communist Party of China relates to the country's modernization. Qin Xuan argues that the Party opened China's modernization drive at a moment of national crisis, shaped Chinese modernization through generations of exploration, and must be upheld and strengthened in its overall leadership if the project of building a modern socialist country is to succeed.

The piece has three parts. It first reviews the failed attempts at national salvation before 1921, then traces the Party's exploration of a modernization path from Mao Zedong through Deng Xiaoping to the present, and finally turns to the tasks of the new journey set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017) and the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020).

Qin's central move is a historical argument by elimination. The Taiping movement, the Self-Strengthening Movement, the 1898 reforms, the 1911 Revolution and various copies of Western political models all failed, in the author's account, to complete the tasks of national salvation and anti-imperialism. Marxism-Leninism, brought by the October Revolution, supplied the direction, and the Party then founded the People's Republic. Qin presents Chinese modernization as a path rooted in China yet open to the world, which has moved China from lagging behind the times to catching up with and leading them. The author cites its status as the second-largest economy and the largest manufacturing country, and holds that it shows the Western route is not the only road to modernization.

Qin concludes that a modernization of enormous population, common prosperity, balanced material and cultural progress, harmony with nature and peaceful development needs a leading core, which in contemporary China can only be the Party. The author calls for strengthening the Party through the Party's self-reform and full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, for deriving theory from this experience to enrich Marxist modernization theory, and for realising the 2035 and mid-century goals. Read the original if you want a concise example of the official People's Daily narrative that links the Party's history, Chinese modernization and Party leadership.
quoteEn: To achieve such a modernization, there must be a "backbone" and a strong leadership core.
quoteZh: 实现这样的现代化，必须有“主心骨”，有坚强的领导核心。

glossary.explanation: The official term for China's own path to modernization under Party leadership, which Party theorists present as distinct from the Western model. Deng Xiaoping used the phrase in 1979, and it became a major slogan after 2021.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: Official slogan for the Party's drive to tighten discipline, supervision and anti-corruption work within its own ranks, prominent since the 18th Party Congress (2012).
Official phrase for the Party's claimed capacity to purify, improve and renew itself without outside pressure.
Official goal of prosperity shared by all of the people, presented as a defining feature of socialism and of Chinese modernization.

t: Summing up historical experience and strengthening historical resolve
zh: 总结历史经验 增强历史定力
paras: Published in Red Flag Manuscript around the centenary of the Communist Party of China in 2021, this commentary asks what lessons the Party's hundred years of revolution, construction and reform offer for the present. He Xinyuan argues that the Party's history is a "textbook" and "nutrient", and that studying it strengthens the resolve needed to build a modern socialist country and achieve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The piece is organised around five lessons, each introduced by a short heading: having faith and turning it into a spirit of struggle; being guided by scientific theory and innovating in theory; doing everything for the people and relying on them; correcting mistakes through self-reform; and being responsible as a major country. Each lesson is illustrated with episodes from the revolutionary, socialist-construction and reform periods, and tied to remarks by Xi Jinping at the Party history study and education mobilisation meeting.

He contends that faith in Marxism and communism has sustained the Party through defeats, the Long March, the "two bombs and one satellite" programme and reform, and has produced a "spiritual lineage" of revolutionary spirit. The author reads the Party's theory as a continuous process of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. On the people, He holds that popular support decides the Party's survival, and that its errors were errors of exploration, corrected in time because of a healthy force within the Party. On international responsibility, He lists the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence, Deng Xiaoping's judgement on peace and development, a community with a shared future for mankind, and the Belt and Road Initiative.

He concludes that the Party should keep Marxism as its guide, innovate in practice and theory, stay close to the people and pursue common prosperity. He also calls on Party members, including senior cadres, to keep a revolutionary drive and the Party's self-reform so that praise and success do not breed complacency. Read the original if you want a compact example of how the official narrative of the Party's centenary summarised its "historical experience" for a general Party readership.
quoteEn: In a hundred years, whether in favourable or adverse circumstances, the Communist Party of China has never wavered in its faith in Marxism, which is the spiritual pillar of how Communists conduct themselves, deal with the world and get things done.
quoteZh: 中国共产党百年来无论是处于顺境还是逆境，从未动摇对马克思主义的信仰，这是中国共产党人立身、处世、干事的精神支柱。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for developing Marxist theory in light of Chinese conditions. In 2021 the text uses the shorter 'Sinification of Marxism', which this rendering covers.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology associated with Xi Jinping, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.
An official term for the Party's claimed capacity to correct its own errors and discipline itself, emphasised in the Xi Jinping era.
A long-standing socialist goal of shared wealth, given renewed policy emphasis under Xi Jinping.

glossary.en: a community with a shared future for mankind
glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's foreign-policy concept of a world of shared interests and cooperation, promoted since 2012–2013.
A Chinese infrastructure and economic cooperation initiative launched by Xi Jinping in 2013, linking China with Eurasia, Africa and beyond.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal of restoring China's strength and international standing, often linked to the centenary goals.

keywords: centenary of the Communist Party of China

t: A century of the adaptation of Marxism to the Chinese context
zh: 马克思主义中国化的百年发展
source: Red Flag Manuscript (Hongqi Wengao), posted on marxism.cass.cn 29 June 2021
paras: Written for the centenary of the Communist Party in 2021, this article asks how the Sinification of Marxism ran through the Party's hundred years and what lessons it offers for the future. Shang Zhixiao opens with Xi Jinping's March 2021 remarks in Fujian on why the Party, Marxism and socialism with Chinese characteristics "work". The author argues that the Party's history is a history of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, and that this process runs through every stage of that history.

The piece has three parts. The first traces Marxism's adaptation across four periods: the new-democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the period since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The second surveys the theoretical results: Mao Zedong Thought, Deng Xiaoping Theory, the Three Represents, the Scientific Outlook on Development, and Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. The third sets out lessons for the next stage.

Shang presents the adaptation of Marxism as a response to the problem of applying a theory born in Western Europe to a semi-colonial, semi-feudal China. Earlier eighty-odd years of struggle had failed, in the author's account, for lack of both a lasting organisation and sound theory. The article quotes Mao's 1930 "Oppose Book Worship" and his 1938 formulation of "the Sinification of Marxism", and describes the "second integration" of Marxism-Leninism with Chinese reality after 1949. Each leadership generation, Shang says, summarised practice into a systematic theory, so that Marxism changed China and China enriched Marxism.

For the next stage, Shang calls for three things: a full and accurate grasp of Marxist standpoint and method, especially dialectical and historical materialism; an understanding of China's basic national conditions in light of the times; and firm struggle against dogmatism and empiricism, described as the great enemies of the process. The article closes by saying theory's vitality lies in continual innovation, and calls for developing contemporary Chinese Marxism and twenty-first-century Marxism. Read the original if you want a concise, Party-line periodisation of the Sinification of Marxism, written for the 2021 centenary.
quoteEn: Marxism has profoundly changed China, and China has greatly enriched Marxism.
quoteZh: 马克思主义深刻改变了中国，中国也极大丰富了马克思主义。

glossary.explanation: The Party's term for combining Marxism's basic principles with Chinese conditions to produce new theory. Mao Zedong put it forward as a formal task in 1938.
The Party's official designation for the theory that adapted Marxism-Leninism to Chinese revolution and construction. It is defined as the collective wisdom of the Party.
The theory underlying reform and opening up and the founding of socialism with Chinese characteristics, from the late 1970s.
Jiang Zemin's theory, formed around 2000, holding that the Party represents advanced productive forces, advanced culture and the fundamental interests of the people.
Hu Jintao-era guiding concept stressing people-centred, comprehensive, coordinated and sustainable development.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's guiding ideology since the 18th Party Congress (2012), written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018.

t: The Communist Party of China's century of experience in advancing national modernization
zh: 中国共产党推进国家现代化建设的百年历史经验
paras: Writing in the year of the Party's centenary (2021), Zhang Shihai asks what lessons can be drawn from the Communist Party of China's hundred years of work on national modernization. The author argues that the Party's history is, in a sense, a history of exploring and building modernization, and that this record has produced five basic lessons. These lessons are presented as the basis for continuing to build a modern socialist country.

The article is a short Red Flag Manuscripts essay organised around five headings. It first traces how the Party's modernization goals evolved across four periods: revolutionary war, the early People's Republic, reform and opening up, and the era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then takes up the people-centred standpoint, the political line, phased goal-setting and the Party's own modernization. A brief closing passage addresses the international significance of the Chinese path.

Zhang's central claim is that the Party's success rests on a few consistent practices. One is that it has treated modernization as a strategic task throughout, moving from industrialization to the "four modernizations", then to "Chinese modernization" in the reform era, and to a "modern socialist country" since 2012. Another is that it has held to a people-centred position, with the people as the "supreme judge" of results, and to a correct basic line described as the "lifeline" of Party and state. The author also stresses stepwise planning, from the two-step revolution and two-step construction plans to the three-step strategy and the 19th Party Congress (2017) timetable of basic modernization by 2035 and a fully built modern socialist country by mid-century. Finally, Zhang argues that the Party must modernize itself through self-reform, because a ruling party's capacity largely determines whether a country modernizes.

Zhang concludes that the Chinese path offers developing countries a new model, gives practical vitality to scientific socialism and contributes a Chinese approach to global governance. Facing complex domestic and international challenges, the author calls for adherence to these lessons and unwavering effort to build a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official Party-history narrative on modernization, as it was framed around the 2021 centenary.
quoteEn: The Party's own modernization is inherent in advancing national modernization and is the key to it, as well as its core driving force and fundamental organizational guarantee.
quoteZh: 政党自身现代化是推进国家现代化建设的题中之义和关键所在，也是推进国家现代化建设的核心驱动和根本组织保障。

glossary.explanation: The goal of modernizing agriculture, industry, national defence and science and technology, set out in the early People's Republic and later revived as a reform-era objective.
A formula used in Party discourse, first in the reform era, for a modernization path said to be specific to Chinese conditions. The article uses it for the reform-era path.
A Party term, stressed under Xi Jinping, for the Party's efforts to correct its own problems, including discipline and anti-corruption work.
The reform-era development plan: meet basic needs by 1990, reach a moderately prosperous standard of living by the end of the century, and basically achieve modernization by the mid-21st century.
The Party's overarching guideline for the primary stage of socialism, centred on economic development, with the Four Cardinal Principles and reform and opening up as the "two basic points".
A principle of Xi Jinping-era development thinking that places the people's interests and judgement at the core of policy.

t: The leadership of the Communist Party of China is the choice of history and the people
zh: 中国共产党的领导是历史和人民的选择
source: Red Flag Manuscript (Hongqi Wengao), 2021; posted on marxism.cass.cn 29 June 2021
paras: Published on the eve of the Party's centenary in 2021, this commentary argues that the leadership of the Communist Party of China is the choice of Chinese history and the Chinese people, not an accident. Yin Hanning holds that practice has already proved this and will continue to do so. The author presents deepening this understanding as a way to strengthen popular confidence in following the Party as the country begins a new journey toward building a modern socialist country and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

The article has three parts. The first reviews the political models China tried after the Opium War of 1840 and the 1911 Revolution. The second rebuts the view that the Nationalist government's 1927–1937 decade was a 'golden decade' that could have led to capitalist modernization. The third traces the Party's role from its founding in 1921 through the Northern Expedition, the land revolution, the War of Resistance against Japan and the civil war, drawing on Xi Jinping and Mao Zedong.

Yin argues that constitutional monarchy, imperial restorations, parliamentary government, a multiparty system and a presidential system each failed, citing the Qing constitutional documents, the assassination of Song Jiaoren and the 682 groups formed by the end of 1913. Against the 'golden decade' thesis, the author offers five points: history cannot be hypothesised, China remained semi-colonial and semi-feudal, the Nationalist regime faced warlord fragmentation and civil war, the national bourgeoisie was too weak to complete the old-democratic revolution, and Western political models had lost credibility. As evidence, Yin notes that 15 of 16 essays in a 1933 Shen Bao discussion favoured socialist or non-capitalist paths.

The author concludes that after these failures, history and the people chose the Party, which gave the struggle for national independence and liberation its 'backbone'. Yin credits it with leading the anti-Japanese united front and, after Chiang Kai-shek's regime lost popular support, founding the People's Republic. The article states that this choice was correct and must be upheld long-term and without wavering. Read the original if you want an example of how a senior Party theorist uses the history of the Republican period to justify the Party's leadership.
quoteEn: The choice of the Communist Party of China was not the chance result of some particular event, but a historical necessity.
quoteZh: 选择中国共产党，不是特殊事件发生后的偶然结果，而是历史的必然。

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: A central Party goal, popularised under Xi Jinping, of restoring China's national strength and international standing after the 'century of humiliation'.
A label some historians and commentators give to the Nationalist government's 1927–1937 period of relative stability and development; the author rejects it.

t: The Communist Party of China and China's fine traditional culture
zh: 中国共产党与中华优秀传统文化
paras: Writing in 2021, the centenary year of the Communist Party of China (CPC), Jiang Yihua asks how the Party has related to China's fine traditional culture over its hundred years. Jiang argues that the Party has combined the basic tenets of Marxism with China's concrete realities, with the development of the times and with that culture. By excavating, inheriting and promoting its essence, the Party is said to have unlocked the culture's inner dynamism and raised it to a new historical level.

The article is a Red Flag Manuscripts essay opening with Xi Jinping's call for 'creative transformation and innovative development' of traditional culture. It is organised around four features of the Party's century: putting the people first, seeking truth from facts, staying true to the original aspiration, and applying materialist dialectics. Each section pairs a traditional idea, often quoted from the Xunzi, the Book of Documents, the Laozi or Mencius, with episodes from Party history.

On the first point, Jiang argues that the classical ideas of benevolence and the people as the foundation of the state were carried through fully only by the CPC. The author contrasts the Party with the late Qing and Republican societies and parties, which are said to have failed to trust, mobilise and serve the people, and credits the liberation of hundreds of millions of peasants as the source of Party strength. On seeking truth from facts, Jiang points to two turning points, the shift to the countryside after 1927 and the post-Cultural Revolution reform and opening up. On staying true to the original aspiration, Jiang cites traditional awareness of hardship and danger, and describes Party membership screening, democratic centralism, cadre selection by 'virtue first' and anti-corruption mechanisms as an institutional system of self-correction. Materialist dialectics is presented as the method that gave traditional ideas such as the golden mean a scientific character.

Jiang concludes that the Party's successes rest on these four commitments, which let it lead the nation from standing up to becoming prosperous and then strong. The essay presents the Party as continuing to open a new era for traditional culture and describes its record as a victory for Marxism and materialist dialectics. Read the original if you want an example of how a Party-affiliated historian frames the centenary narrative through traditional Chinese culture.
quoteEn: Looking across past and present, it is the Communist Party of China that has truly achieved the creative transformation and innovative development of the fine traditional culture of benevolence and valuing the people as the root, and has put the people first without compromise.
quoteZh: 纵观古今，真正能够把讲仁爱、重民本的优秀传统文化创造性转化和创新性发展，并不折不扣做到人民至上的，是中国共产党。

glossary.zh: 创造性转化和创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A formula in Party discourse for how traditional culture should be treated: reinterpreted and adapted to present needs rather than simply preserved. It is associated with Xi Jinping's statements on traditional culture.

A principle of the Party's ideological line, drawn from a classical phrase and given prominence by Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping. It requires policy to start from actual conditions and be tested in practice.

glossary.en: staying true to the original aspiration
glossary.explanation: A slogan stressing fidelity to the Party's founding mission of seeking the people's well-being and national rejuvenation. It was emphasised under Xi Jinping, notably in the 2019–2020 'Remain true to the original aspiration' education campaign.
The Leninist organisational principle of the Party, combining discussion with binding unity of action under higher bodies.

t: The people are the country
zh: 人民就是江山
paras: Writing in the centenary year of the Communist Party of China (2021), Chen Xiangjian takes up Xi Jinping's formulation "the people are the country" (人民就是江山), which Xi stressed in speeches that year, including during a May 2021 inspection in Henan. Chen argues that the phrase is significant in two ways. It is a deep summation of the Marxist view of the masses, and it is a solemn declaration of the Party's mass line.

The article is a short commentary in two parts. The first part collects a long series of Xi's statements, from the Party's mass-line education campaign through the Long March anniversary, the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up, the fight against COVID-19 and poverty alleviation. Chen presents them as the new-era expression of the Marxist view of the masses and as the point of Xi's "people-centred" development thinking. The second part organises the argument around the three questions of the mass line: for whom, on whom to rely, and who we are.

On "for whom", Chen reads the Party's century of struggle as the pursuit of the people's happiness, from the Party's founding through the founding of New China to reform and opening up and the new era. On "on whom to rely", Chen sets the historical-materialist view that the people create history against the idealist view of heroes. The author lists the people's role in the Great Revolution, the Red Army years, the War of Resistance, the Huai-Hai and Yangtze crossing campaigns, and socialist construction. The conclusion is that the Party does not claim credit for itself but attributes every achievement to the people. On "who we are", Chen cites the Party constitution describing the Party as the vanguard of the working class, the Chinese people and the Chinese nation. Chen adds that China's socialist state, in which all power belongs to the people, is a "people's country" in essence and differs fundamentally from one founded on private ownership.

Chen concludes that the Party must never separate itself from the masses and must keep the people at the highest place in its heart. Quoting Xi, the article says this means making the fruits of development reach all more fairly, advancing common prosperity, and uniting 1.4 billion people for the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a compact example of how Party commentary in 2021 tied Xi's "people" language to the mass line and to Marxist historical materialism.
quoteEn: The essence of China's socialist country is that it is the people's country, which differs fundamentally from a country founded on private ownership.
quoteZh: 我国社会主义江山的本质就是人民的江山，这就与以私有制为基础的江山性质有根本区别。

glossary.explanation: A working method and principle of the Communist Party, developed under Mao Zedong, of drawing ideas from the people and returning to them. Party texts call it the Party's lifeline and fundamental line of work.

glossary.literal: taking the people as the centre
glossary.explanation: A development philosophy Xi Jinping put forward after the 18th Party Congress (2012). It holds that development should be for the people, rely on the people and have its results shared by them.
A long-standing socialist goal of prosperity shared by all, given fresh emphasis under Xi Jinping. Official usage links it to narrowing gaps in income and public services.
