glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.literal: great revival of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's overarching national goal, closely associated with Xi Jinping's idea of the Chinese Dream. It refers to restoring China's strength and international standing.
The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in 1978 under Deng Xiaoping.

t: A century of the Communist Party of China inheriting and promoting China's fine traditional culture
zh: 中国共产党继承与弘扬中华优秀传统文化的百年历史考察
source: Marxist Philosophy Studies (Makesi zhuyi zhexue luncong), 2020 no. 3
paras: Deng Haiying asks how the Communist Party of China has treated the nation's traditional culture over roughly a hundred years of revolution, construction and reform. The article, published in 2020, argues that Party members are Marxists rather than historical or cultural nihilists, and that the Party has consistently been a faithful inheritor and firm promoter of China's fine traditional culture.

The article is a chronological survey in four stages: the revolutionary war years; the early People's Republic; the period of reform and opening up; and the years since the 18th Party Congress (2012). For each stage Deng draws on leaders' statements, policy documents and regulations, institutional measures and concrete cases of protecting cultural relics, theatre, medicine, script and ethnic minority cultures.

For the revolutionary period, Deng stresses Mao Zedong's insistence that history must not be severed, and his principle of "taking the essence and discarding the dross", which Liu Shaoqi echoed at the Seventh Party Congress. Deng also cites wartime relic-protection rules and episodes such as the rescue of the Zhaocheng Jin Canon and the peaceful liberation of Beiping. After 1949 the Party kept the line of critical inheritance, expressed in the "Hundred Flowers, Hundred Schools" policy and the maxim "making the past serve the present". Deng describes reform of opera, support for traditional medicine and the simplification of Chinese characters, while acknowledging that the Anti-Rightist campaign, the Great Leap Forward and above all the Cultural Revolution's attack on the "Four Olds" broke this continuity.

Deng presents the reform era as a re-evaluation: the Party corrected "Leftist" errors, then linked traditional culture to socialist modernization, the primary stage of socialism and soft power. Since 2012, in Deng's account, the Party under Xi Jinping has taken unprecedented steps. These include Politburo study sessions, Xi's 2014 speech at the Confucius anniversary conference, large-scale cataloguing and heritage protection, wider public access to museums, new media formats and international dissemination. Deng also summarises Xi's ideas on the subject: traditional culture as the nation's "roots" and "soul", creative transformation and innovative development, and a call to study and implement them fully. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned account of how Party narratives portray continuity in cultural policy from the 1930s to 2020.
quoteEn: Throughout nearly a hundred years of leading the Chinese people in revolution, construction and reform, Chinese communists have always been faithful inheritors and resolute promoters of China's fine traditional culture.
quoteZh: 在带领中国人民近百年来进行革命、建设、改革的长期历史实践中，中国共产党人始终是中华优秀传统文化的忠实传承者、坚定弘扬者。

glossary.pinyin: qǔ qí jīnghuá, qù qí zāopò
glossary.en: taking the essence and discarding the dross
glossary.literal: take its essence, remove its dross
glossary.explanation: A formula associated with Mao Zedong for critically inheriting traditional culture: keeping its progressive, 'democratic' elements and rejecting its feudal ones.

glossary.literal: a hundred flowers bloom, a hundred schools contend
glossary.explanation: A cultural and scientific policy formulated by Mao Zedong in the 1950s, encouraging diversity in the arts and academic debate under Party leadership.

glossary.en: making the past serve the present
glossary.literal: let the ancient serve the present
glossary.explanation: A slogan of Mao Zedong's, paired with 'making foreign things serve China', calling for the selective use of cultural heritage for current purposes.

glossary.zh: 创造性转化、创新性发展
glossary.explanation: A formula promoted under Xi Jinping for handling traditional culture by adapting it to contemporary needs and developing it in new forms.
The official characterisation of China's current developmental stage, adopted in the 1980s and written into the Party's basic programme.

t: Building the "three major systems" of CPC history studies, seen through a century of Party history
zh: 从百年党史看中共党史学“三大体系”建设
paras: Writing in Guangming Daily in May 2021, in the centenary year of the Communist Party of China (CPC), Song Xueqin asks how the discipline of CPC history studies should build its disciplinary system, academic system and discourse system (the "three major systems"). The author argues that the experience accumulated across each stage of the discipline's hundred-year development is an essential foundation and resource for this task in the new era.

This short commentary proceeds chronologically through four stages. It covers the period from the Party's founding in 1921 to 1949, the early People's Republic, the period of reform and opening up, and the era since the 18th Party Congress (2012). For each stage Song identifies the main researchers, texts and characteristic features of Party history research.

Song's central claim is that the discipline has repeatedly developed by combining Marxist guidance with the Party's practical needs. Early Party leaders such as Cai Hesen, Qu Qiubai and Li Lisan wrote Party history to serve political struggle, and the Yan'an rectification movement, Mao Zedong's "How to Study the History of the CPC" and the 1945 resolution on historical questions gave the field its theoretical methods. After 1949 the Selected Works of Mao Zedong formed the core of the academic system, and after the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978) the field corrected the damage of the Cultural Revolution and merged political and academic attributes. For the new era, Song names two requirements: adherence to Marxist guidance, which the author says has repeatedly been shown to determine whether the field prospers or goes astray, and a problem-oriented approach.

Song concludes that Party history scholars should start from the practical problems facing contemporary China, respect the "Chinese case" and "Chinese experience", and put forward original theoretical views with distinctive concepts. The aim is a systematic discipline with Chinese characteristics, style and manner that distils regularities of the Party's long-term governance and guides new practice. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned periodisation of how Party history studies developed in China and what a leading scholar expects of the discipline in 2021.
quoteEn: History has repeatedly proved that whenever Marxist guidance is upheld, research in CPC history flourishes, and whenever it is abandoned, research in Party history departs from the correct track.
quoteZh: 历史反复证明，什么时候坚持马克思主义指导，中共党史学研究就会繁荣，什么时候背离马克思主义指导，党史学研究就会偏离正确轨道。

glossary.explanation: The policy of economic reform and opening to the outside world launched in China from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee in 1978.
A Party-wide campaign of study and criticism launched in the early 1940s in Yan'an, which consolidated Mao Zedong's leadership and ideological line.
The academic discipline devoted to the history of the Communist Party of China, closely tied to Party education and to the Party's official historical narrative.

t: The Party's political building since the founding of the PRC: development, features and lessons
zh: 新中国成立以来党的政治建设：发展历程、特点及其启示
source: Xin shidai Makesizhuyi luncong (New Era Marxism Series), 2020 no. 1
paras: Writing in the wake of the 2019 CPC Central Committee Opinions on Strengthening the Party's Political Building, Wang Shiyi and Zhou Nan ask how the Party's political building has developed since 1949, what marks it, and what it teaches. They argue that it has advanced with the times, moving from a tortuous course under socialist revolution and construction to a systematic, leading component of Party building in the new era. Taking a stand on politics, they say, is a basic requirement of a Marxist party.

The article is organised in three parts. The first gives a periodised history: 1949–1978; 1978–2012, divided into three stages (1978–1989, 1989–2002, 2002–2012); and the new era from 2012. It follows Party congresses, plenums, intra-Party regulations and the changing layout of Party building, from the four-part to the five-part arrangement. The second part identifies three features, and the third draws six lessons.

The authors read the early period as a good start (the 1951 rectification, the 1954 resolution on Party unity, the Eighth Congress) followed, from 1957, by a drift under "Leftist" thinking that reached its worst in the Cultural Revolution. After the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee (1978), they trace recovery through the 1980 guidelines on intra-Party political life, the creation of discipline inspection bodies and Deng Xiaoping's institution-based approach. Under Jiang Zemin and Hu Jintao they describe the "talk politics" campaigns and the Scientific Outlook on Development. Since the 18th Party Congress (2012) they credit Xi Jinping with the most systematic exposition, and with putting political building first and adding discipline building at the 19th Congress (2017). The three features are: upholding the Party's overall leadership; a problem-oriented mix of regular and concentrated education; and strict discipline, moving to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party.

The six lessons are: put political building first; hold high the banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics; innovate by freeing minds and seeking truth from facts; serve the Party's political line and long-term governing capacity; strengthen Marxist ideological and political education; and coordinate political building with ideological, organisational, conduct and discipline building. The authors hold that political building is the Party's "backbone" and that its theory and practice have made a historic leap. Read the original if you want a detailed, officially aligned chronology of how Party political building and its regulations developed from 1949 to 2019.
quoteEn: The Party's political building is the \"backbone\" of all aspects of Party building.
quoteZh: 党的政治建设是党的各方面建设的“主心骨”

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan that Xi Jinping put forward in 2014. It covers anti-corruption, discipline, regulation-based governance and ideological education within the Party, and was made part of the "Four Comprehensives" strategy.

A strand of Party building concerned with political direction, political leadership, political discipline and political ecology. The 19th Party Congress (2017) placed it first among the strands of Party building.
The norms and practices governing Party members' internal activity, such as democratic centralism, criticism and self-criticism, and discipline. The term was formally adopted in the 1980 guidelines.

keywords: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party

t: The great historical significance of our Party's creation of Chinese revolutionary theory
zh: 我们党开创中国革命理论的伟大历史意义
paras: Published in Guangming Daily on 26 May 2021, in the run-up to the Party's centenary, this commentary asks how a party founded in 1921 has lasted a hundred years, governed for more than seventy, and become the world's largest governing party. Zhang Haipeng answers by pointing to one feature of the Party's history. In Zhang's account, the Communist Party created a revolutionary theory suited to a semi-colonial, semi-feudal country, and this developed Marxism-Leninism.

The article follows the Party's theoretical path chronologically. It begins with the Marxist model of urban proletarian insurrection and with Lenin's 1920 ideas on colonial revolution. It then covers the first and second Party congresses, the uprisings after 1927, the Jinggangshan base area, the Zunyi Conference of 1935, the 1938 proposal to adapt Marxism to Chinese conditions, and Mao Zedong's 1949 shift of the Party's focus to the cities.

Zhang's central argument is that urban insurrection was one successful form of the general principle of seizing power by force, not the only one. Treating it as universal, as the "urban-centred" line did under Comintern influence and the Party's leftist leadership, confused a specific form with the theory itself. Zhang argues that Mao, drawing on peasant-movement experience, developed the strategy of encircling the cities from the countryside and set it out in his writings, including the 1930 essay against book worship. The leftist line, the author says, caused heavy losses until Zunyi confirmed the new path. Zhang reads this as the first leap in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times, which produced Mao Zedong Thought. Zhang also stresses that the countryside was only a means. Citing Mao's 1944 letter to Bo Gu and his 1949 speech, Zhang says the aim was industrialisation and a socialist economic base, and that looking only at the villages and small-peasant economy would be populism.

Zhang concludes that this revolutionary theory was a major contribution to the treasury of Marxism-Leninism and laid the foundation for the victory of the democratic revolution and the founding of the People's Republic. Zhang adds that the same method must guide socialist construction after taking power, producing socialism with Chinese characteristics that differs from the Soviet model while keeping Marxism's general principles. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how Party historiography presents the rural-revolution strategy as Marxism adapted to China, and how that account is tied to the centenary.
quoteEn: Only those who closely combined Marxist revolutionary theory with China's national conditions, creatively put forward the theory of the "sinification of Marxism" and explored the path of the Chinese revolution on that basis, could lead the Chinese revolution to victory.
quoteZh: 只有把马克思主义的革命理论与中国的国情紧密结合起来，创造性地提出“马克思主义中国化”理论并根据这一理论探索中国革命道路的人，才能领导中国革命取得胜利。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The Party's official formula for applying Marxism to Chinese conditions. Mao Zedong first put forward the idea of Marxism's "Sinification" at the Sixth Plenum of the Sixth Central Committee in 1938; the term was later extended to include adaptation to the times.
The official name of the Party's path and system since the reform era, presented as Marxism applied to Chinese conditions.
The Party's official term for the first major theoretical outcome of adapting Marxism-Leninism to China. It was adopted as the guiding ideology at the Seventh Party Congress in 1945.

glossary.en: encircling the cities from the countryside
glossary.explanation: Mao Zedong's revolutionary strategy of building rural base areas and armed forces, and seizing the cities last. The Party presents it as an alternative to the Soviet-style urban insurrection.
A Politburo meeting in January 1935, during the Long March. Party history treats it as the turning point at which the leftist military line was corrected and Mao Zedong's leadership was established.

keywords: encircling the cities from the countryside

t: The path of belief of a century-old Party
zh: 百年大党的信仰之路
source: China Social Sciences Today (Zhongguo shehui kexue bao), 29 April 2021
paras: Marking the Communist Party of China's centenary in 2021, this newspaper commentary asks where the Party's "power of belief" comes from and how it has been built up. Xiang argues that this power is the Party's distinguishing mark and unique strength, and that over a hundred years it has grown together with material force. In Xiang's account it has been consolidated through the most thoroughgoing theory, the loftiest ideals and the most vivid practice of serving the people, and it forms a distinctive driving mechanism of national governance.

The piece is organised in three parts: theory as the seed of belief, ideals as the banner that gathers belief, and service to the people as the practical theme of belief. A short closing passage sums up the internal logic of the Party's century of belief-building. The text draws on the history of the new-democratic revolution, socialist construction, reform and opening up, and the new era.

Xiang's first move reads Marxism through four lenses: epistemology (a scientific theory), value theory (a theory of the people), practice (a theory that turns belief into action) and intellectual history (an open, developing theory, from Mao Zedong Thought to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era). The second move holds that belief rests on two ideals. The lofty communist ideal gives long-term direction, while the common ideal of socialism with Chinese characteristics gives a present-day footing. Xiang adds that Party members unify personal and social ideals. The third move links belief to three practical themes: \"standing up\" in the revolutionary period, \"becoming prosperous\" in socialist construction and reform and opening up, and \"becoming strong\" in the new era. For the last of these, Xiang cites full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, theoretical innovation, and the new \"two-step\" strategy with the 14th Five-Year Plan and 2035 goals.

Xiang concludes that the Party's belief-building lies in studying and applying Marxism, in uniting members around the two ideals, and in leading the people from standing up to becoming prosperous and strong. Looking ahead, the author expects the Party to gather an even stronger power of belief in service of economic and social development and the people's well-being. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party-affiliated scholarship framed belief and ideals during the 2021 centenary.
quoteEn: The power of belief is the distinguishing mark and unique strength of the Communist Party of China as a century-old Party.
quoteZh: 信仰力量是中国共产党作为百年大党的显著标识与独特优势。

glossary.explanation: A term in Party discourse for the motivating force of members' commitment to Marxism and communist ideals. The article treats it as a source of the Party's cohesion and strength.
Official term for the shared goal of building socialism with Chinese characteristics, distinguished from the long-term communist ideal.
The Party's official name for its path, theory and system of socialism since reform and opening up.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A policy line of the Xi Jinping era stressing strict Party discipline, anti-corruption work and cadre conduct.

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into its constitution in 2017.

keywords: standing up, becoming prosperous, becoming strong

t: Research on modern Chinese history in 2020
st: An annual survey of scholarship from the Opium War to 1949
zh: 2020年的中国近代史研究
paras: This is an annual literature review, first published in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2021, of research on modern Chinese history in 2020. Wu defines the field as the 109 years from the Opium War (1840) to the founding of the People's Republic (1949). Citing Xi Jinping's January 2020 addition of the history of socialist development to the Party's three histories, Wu holds that the theme of this period is the Communist Party leading the people towards socialism. The review reports strong results in historiography, theory, institutional and economic history, wartime source collections and Party history.

The survey is organised by theme. It covers historiography and the building of the "three major systems" (disciplinary, academic and discourse systems), new angles in historical theory, the War of Resistance against Japan and Party history, institutional history and state governance, and source compilations and databases. Each section lists journal articles and books with a one-line summary of each author's finding. It names economic, foreign-relations, intellectual, conceptual and environmental history only briefly, citing limited space.

Wu stresses several clusters. In historiography, scholars on treaty relations, border studies and urban history link their work to building a Chinese discourse system. In theory, debates continue over whether the phrase "sinicisation of Marxist historiography" is valid, how to evaluate historical figures under historical materialism, and how hermeneutics and the "long durée" can correct fragmented cultural and social history. For the 75th anniversary of victory in 2020, wartime work stresses the Party's role as the "mainstay", along with Japanese war responsibility, Nanjing, the north-west rear area and global perspectives. Party-history work covers the First Congress delegates, rebuttals of claims about Yan'an, and revolutionary discourse and base-area finance. Governance studies address official selection, border governance, supervision systems and the Taiping aftermath.

Wu notes major source publications, including the eight-volume History of China's War of Resistance against Japan and a 100-volume military source collection. It also lists new databases, among them a platform on the war and modern Sino-Japanese relations and a fourth batch of modern newspapers. The review closes by hoping historians will study Xi Jinping's statements on modern history and Party history, strengthen basic theory and produce works that join history and theory. Read the original if you want a detailed map of 2020 Chinese-language publications, with journal citations, on modern Chinese history, wartime history and Party history.
quoteEn: The theme of the 109 years of modern Chinese history is the history of the Communist Party of China leading the people towards and realising socialism in China.
quoteZh: 109年的中国近代史，其主题就是中国共产党带领人民在中国走向并实现社会主义的历史。

glossary.explanation: A slogan from Xi Jinping's 2016 speech on philosophy and social sciences, calling for Chinese disciplinary, academic and discourse systems. Scholars invoke it when reviewing their fields.
A phrase the Party uses to describe its role in the War of Resistance against Japan. Some historians contest the claim.
Marx's materialist conception of history, which Chinese historians present as the required guide for evaluating historical figures.

t: Establishing a correct view of Party history through systems thinking
zh: 以系统思维树立正确党史观
paras: Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in March 2021, ahead of the Party's centenary, Shi Shiyue takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the mobilisation meeting for Party history study and education, to establish a correct view of Party history. Shi argues that Party members should study the history of the Communist Party of China with a systems mode of thinking that is holistic, dynamic, hierarchical and open.

The short commentary is organised around those four features. Each section links one feature to an aspect of Party history: its overall value, its phases of development, its record of governance, and its forward-looking character.

On wholeness, Shi presents the century as a history of struggle and sacrifice, citing revolutionary martyrs such as Li Dazhao and Cai Hesen and builders such as Wang Jinxi and Jiao Yulu, and says it educates members by example. On dynamism, Shi divides the century into four periods: New Democratic revolution, socialist revolution and construction, reform and opening up, and the new era under Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Shi describes these as the shift from standing up to becoming prosperous to becoming strong. On hierarchy, Shi surveys governance in politics, the economy, culture and ecological civilisation. On openness, Shi cites the elimination of absolute poverty as an achievement that prepares the next goal of building a modern socialist country.

Shi concludes that Party history offers practical experience and spiritual resources to guide every member and citizen. The author expects the Party to keep to a people-centred approach and to pursue modernization goals through systematic and creative work. Read the original if you want a brief example of how Party-affiliated commentary in 2021 presented the official framework for studying Party history.
quoteEn: Party members should adhere to a systems way of thinking that is holistic, dynamic, hierarchical and open, so as to raise their ability and level in studying and understanding the content of the Party's history.
quoteZh: 坚持以整体性、动态性、层次性和开放性的系统思维，提升广大党员学习理解中国共产党党史内涵的能力和水平。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017–2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.

glossary.en: a correct view of Party history
glossary.literal: establish a correct outlook on Party history
glossary.explanation: A formulation Xi Jinping introduced at the Party history study and education mobilisation meeting in February 2021. It stresses interpreting the Party's past in line with official assessments.
The policy launched in 1978 at the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee, introducing market-oriented reforms and engagement with the global economy.
An official concept for development that aims to balance economic growth with environmental protection. It is now part of the Party's overall national development framework.

t: The great leap from keeping up with the times to leading the times
zh: 从赶上时代到引领时代的伟大跨越
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in 2021, in the run-up to the Party's centenary, Yan Xiaofeng takes up a formulation from Xi Jinping: that under the Party's leadership China has moved from "keeping up with the times" to "leading the times". Yan presents this as the central achievement of the Party's first hundred years. In the author's account, it shows the Party's aims of securing happiness for the people, rejuvenation for the nation and world harmony.

The commentary is organised in three parts. The first traces how the Party found the correct road to national rejuvenation, from the New Democratic Revolution through socialist revolution and construction to reform and opening up. The second discusses the new era of socialism with Chinese characteristics as the marker of the leap to leading the times. The third sets out what it takes to remain at the forefront of the times.

Yan's core argument is that keeping up with the times meant bringing China's development into line with the growth of productive forces, the direction of historical progress and the interests of the people. In this reading, it required establishing the socialist system and then launching reform and opening up. Leading the times, by contrast, means coordinating the strategic overall situation of national rejuvenation with the "great changes unseen in a century" in the world, so that each shapes the other. Yan adds that the leap depends on the Party's self-reform, because long-term rule brings constant risks to the Party's advanced nature and purity, and the task of leading is harder than that of catching up.

Yan concludes that leadership of the times must be sustained. The author calls for unifying thought and action through Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese characteristics for a New Era, and for advancing towards the second centenary goal. This goal means building a modern socialist country by the middle of the century, with basic modernization by 2035. Yan describes Chinese modernization as socialist, as a developing country's path and as one of unprecedented scale. The author also stresses continually meeting the people's growing need for a better life. Read the original if you want a compact, official-style statement of how Party theorists framed China's historical trajectory on the eve of the centenary.
quoteEn: Leading the times is a continuing state.
quoteZh: 引领时代是一种持续的状态。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuì zhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The Party's official guiding ideology, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is presented as the latest stage in adapting Marxism to China.
The official term for China's own path to modernization, which official texts distinguish from Western capitalist models.
An official concept of the Party rigorously correcting its own faults and strengthening its discipline. It is said to underpin the Party's leadership of social change.

glossary.zh: 世界百年未有之大变局
glossary.pinyin: shìjiè bǎinián wèiyǒu zhī dà biànjú
glossary.en: great changes unseen in a century
glossary.explanation: A phrase used by Xi Jinping from about 2017 for the current shifts in the global order, especially the rise of emerging economies and the relative decline of the West.

t: Studying Party history and grasping the political big picture
zh: 学党史和把握政治大局
paras: Writing in the People's Daily in May 2021, during the Party-wide study campaign on Party history ahead of the Party's centenary, Jin Chongji asks how Party history can help officials meet Xi Jinping's call to "grasp the political big picture". Jin takes Xi's formulation of three capacities as the framework: political judgement, political comprehension and political execution. The main claim is that, at a new historical starting point and amid what the article calls great changes unseen in a century, the key to solving concrete problems is grasping the overall political situation, and that the Party's own history is the best textbook for learning how.

The article is a short commentary organised into an introduction and three sections, one for each capacity. Jin draws on episodes from the Party's history: Mao Zedong's wartime and civil-war analyses, the founding of the basic socialist system in the 1950s, Deng Xiaoping's reform-era decisions, Zhou Enlai at the 1955 Asian-African Conference, and the Party leadership under Xi Jinping. Jin cites Mao's essay "On Practice" to justify learning from indirect experience, meaning the experience of earlier generations.

On political judgement, Jin argues that a sound judgement must match reality and avoid partial views. Examples are Mao's "On Protracted War" against both defeatism and quick-victory theories, his 1947 assessment of a turning point in the civil war, and Deng's judgement that China is in the primary stage of socialism. On political comprehension, Jin stresses grasping the principal contradiction and what the article calls "matters of national importance": the peasant question in the revolution, the Shenzhen special zones, and common prosperity, which Jin presents as a political issue touching the Party's basis of rule. On political execution, Jin quotes Mao on "grasping firmly", describes Zhou Enlai as combining strategic vision with diligent implementation, and names formalism and bureaucracy as the main obstacles. The remedy Jin offers is investigation among the masses and doing practical work.

Jin concludes that studying Party history serves more than commemoration, because it supplies lessons that strengthen the three capacities. Officials can then open the new journey of building a modern socialist country in an all-round way and work towards the second centenary goal. Read the original if you want to see how a senior Party historian linked the 2021 history-study campaign to Xi Jinping's political requirements for cadres, using standard episodes from the Party's past.
quoteEn: Studying Party history can help people broaden their horizons, keep \"matters of national importance\" in mind, and raise their political comprehension.
quoteZh: 学党史可以帮助人们开阔眼界，胸怀“国之大者”，提高政治领悟力。

glossary.literal: the great matters of the nation
glossary.explanation: A phrase Xi Jinping used to urge officials to keep the country's most important priorities in view. The article uses it for the central tasks of the Party and state.
A goal of shared wealth for all the people, presented in Party discourse as an essential requirement of socialism. Xi Jinping has given it more prominence in recent years.
A thesis that China is at an early, underdeveloped stage of socialism. It underpins the Party's basic line and was affirmed at the 13th Party Congress in 1987.

t: Cultivating "civic morality" in the new era, as seen through the epidemic
zh: 透过疫情看新时代“公民道德”的培育
paras: Writing in early 2020 in People's Forum (Renmin Luntan, no. 4), Sun Yingshuai treats the COVID-19 epidemic as a test not only of national governance but also of civic morality and civic consciousness. The article argues that the behaviour the epidemic exposed, good and bad, shows why a healthy, modern cultivation of "civic morality" matters. Sun's answer is that this cultivation needs three foundations: an economic base, a sense of community, and a sound public space.

The piece begins with the Party's guiding documents on civic morality, including the 2001 Implementation Outline and the Outline for the New Era issued after the 18th Party Congress (2012). It then moves through three headed sections: the economic basis of civic morality; the three "spirits" (scientific, rule-based and equality) that sustain community consciousness; and the interaction of Party leadership, the rule of law and social organisations. Examples come from the epidemic's "social panorama".

In the first section, Sun applies the Marxist view that moral imbalance must be explained through economic relations, not ideas alone. Hoarding masks, profiteering and selling fake supplies are read as confirming Marx's remarks on capital and profit. Sun contends that China's public-ownership-based economy, in which state enterprises and public hospitals played a pillar role, allows collectivist values and the idea of the "public" to become mainstream. In the second section, Sun links panic-buying of herbal remedies and belief in conspiracy theories to a lack of scientific spirit. Defiance of quarantine rules is tied to a weak rule-based spirit, and spitting at medical staff, privilege-seeking and heavy-handed local enforcement are tied to a weak spirit of equality.

Sun concludes that cultivating civic morality requires strengthening the economic base, fostering community consciousness through the three spirits, and building a public space through Party leadership, the combination of rule by law and rule by virtue, and healthy social organisations. The goal is a spiritual civilisation grounded in legal rules and public order and good customs. Read the original if you want an example of how Chinese Party-affiliated scholarship in early 2020 tied pandemic behaviour to Marxist moral theory and to governance policy.
quoteEn: Only with an economic base in which public ownership is dominant can the idea of the "public" and the value of "collectivism" in civic morality become mainstream values.
quoteZh: 有公有制为主体的经济基础垫底，“公民道德”中“公”的观念和“集体主义”的价值诉求才有可能成为主流价值观

glossary.explanation: The moral norms expected of citizens in social life. The Party has issued implementation outlines on its construction, in 2001 and again for the new era.
The principle that collective interests take precedence over individual ones. Official documents name it the principle of socialist morality.

The awareness that individuals share responsibility for public affairs and common interests. The article draws on this idea, linked to official calls to forge a sense of community among the Chinese nation.
The sphere of social life outside the family and the market where public norms operate. The article treats it as the practical basis of social morality.

glossary.en: combination of rule by law and rule by virtue
glossary.explanation: A governance principle that pairs legal enforcement with moral education and persuasion.

t: Carrying forward the Xibaipo spirit and taking the new era's "examination" road well
zh: 弘扬西柏坡精神 走好新时代“赶考”路
paras: This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 19 August 2020, asks how the Communist Party of China should draw on the "Xibaipo spirit" in the new era. Xibaipo was the Party Central Committee's base before it moved to Beijing in 1949, when Mao Zedong spoke of going to the capital to "sit an examination". Yang and Sun argue that, as Xi Jinping said in 2013, the Party's "examination" is far from over. They hold that the Xibaipo spirit has gained new vitality in keeping the Party's style, its ties with the people and its purity.

The article is organised into four sections, each linking a Xibaipo-era principle to present tasks. These are modesty and hard struggle (the "Two Musts"), daring and being skilled at struggle, strict discipline and rigorous Party governance, and vigilance in times of peace together with continuous effort. Each section briefly recalls the Xibaipo period and the Party's record since 1949 before turning to the new era.

Yang and Sun argue that the Two Musts remain relevant against formalism and bureaucracy, and call for strict implementation of the Central Committee's eight-point regulation. On struggle, they cite a world undergoing "changes unseen in a century" and Xi's call for struggle across fields from Party governance to national security. On discipline, they credit the 18th Party Congress (2012) and later measures with building a supervision and discipline system that has found a way to escape the "historical cycle" of rise and decline. They connect these measures to the Party's political leadership.

The authors conclude that the Party must keep the spirit of "going to the capital for the examination", staying vigilant and working continuously. They call on it to face the "four tests" and overcome the "four dangers", and to pursue full and rigorous self-governance of the Party in order to achieve the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Party commentary in 2020 used Xibaipo history to frame the Party's current tasks of discipline, struggle and self-building.
quoteEn: In the new era, it is particularly important to uphold the Party's organisational and leadership principle of democratic centralism, to enforce Party discipline strictly, and to strengthen the Party's centralised and unified leadership.
quoteZh: 进入新时代，坚持党的民主集中制的组织原则和领导原则，严明党的纪律，加强党的集中统一领导，显得尤为重要。

glossary.explanation: A Party-promoted set of values associated with Xibaipo in Hebei, the Central Committee's headquarters in 1948–49 before the move to Beijing. It stresses modesty, hard struggle and discipline.
A statement by Mao Zedong in 1949 that comrades must remain modest and prudent and must keep up the style of hard struggle. It is widely cited in Party discipline campaigns.
Rules issued by the Central Committee in December 2012 to curb extravagance, formalism and bureaucracy among officials.

glossary.en: full and rigorous self-governance of the Party
glossary.explanation: A slogan of the Xi Jinping era for strengthening Party discipline, anti-corruption work and internal regulation.

glossary.en: the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation
glossary.explanation: The Party's central national goal, often called the Chinese Dream, of restoring China's strength and international standing.

t: What kind of internet innovation thinking does the new era need?
zh: 新时代需要何种互联网创新思维
paras: Writing in People's Forum (2020, no. 17), Zhang Jianyun asks why Xi Jinping stresses "innovation thinking" and what form it should take in the internet age. The article argues that big data, the internet, cloud computing, blockchain and intelligent machines mark a qualitative leap in the productive forces, so that thinking, production and social management must all be transformed accordingly.

The piece has three sections. The first explains, from a historical-materialist standpoint, why Xi emphasises innovation thinking, citing his speeches from 2015 onward. The second sets out what the new productive forces demand, centred on innovation in applied technology. The third identifies two defining features of internet-era innovation, which Zhang calls "subversive" and "popular", and draws out their significance.

Zhang begins from Marx's point that tools of production distinguish social epochs, and treats the internet toolset as comparable to the steam engine and electricity. Applied-technology innovation, meaning putting everything "online" as electrification once put everything on the grid, is described as the core, hardest and most practically meaningful kind. Examples include smart agriculture, automated manufacturing, online government and services, and the "Internet Plus" strategy launched in 2015. The article then argues that internet innovation is disruptive: it is said to merge production and consumption under consumer-led demand, make planned production achievable on the basis of big data, and replace pyramid-style command structures with flat, self-organising networks. It is also popular: cheap information, cloud services and maker spaces allow ordinary people, not only experts, to innovate.

Zhang concludes that big data and the internet will bring humanity into an "informatised socialist era", just as machinery and electricity ushered in industrial capitalism. Innovation must therefore be systemic, and the creativity of the masses should be encouraged, in line with Xi's call to respect the masses' pioneering spirit as a key to socialism's prosperity. Read the original if you want to see how a 2020 Party-theory commentary links Xi Jinping's statements on innovation to historical materialism and to optimistic claims about the internet economy.
quoteEn: Innovation in the internet age is mass innovation, innovation by everyone.
quoteZh: 互联网时代的创新是大众创新，是人人创新。

glossary.explanation: A national strategy launched in 2015 to integrate internet technologies with traditional sectors such as manufacturing, finance, agriculture and retail.

t: The significance and lessons of the Chinese path for modernization in developing countries
zh: 中国道路对发展中国家现代化建设的意义和启示
source: Observation and Thinking (Guancha yu sikao), 2020 no. 1
paras: Writing in 2020 after seventy years of the People's Republic, Sun Yingshuai asks what other developing countries can learn from the Chinese path to modernization. The article starts from the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) and Xi Jinping's report to the 19th Party Congress (2017). Both present socialism with Chinese characteristics as offering a new option to countries that want faster development while keeping their independence. Sun's thesis is that these countries can draw on China's development paths, but must also recognise how their own economic, strategic and leadership conditions differ from China's.

The article has two main parts. The first identifies three paths worth borrowing: independent development, leapfrog development and common development. The second asks latecomer countries to face three differences from China: the structure of the economy, the strategic position of the state, and the quality of political leadership. Sun draws on Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, Xi Jinping and Marx, and on Alexander Gerschenkron's theory of latecomer advantage. Comparisons are made with the Soviet Union, post-Soviet Russia, India, South Africa, the Philippines and Indonesia.

On the first part, Sun argues that China moved from imitating the Soviet model to seeking a path suited to its own conditions, and that other countries should likewise avoid dogmatism and copying. China's experience of using latecomer advantages, such as opening up, market-oriented reform and the new wave of information technology, is described as a way to avoid the pain of the "Caudine Forks" of capitalist development. Sun adds that in an age when peace and development are the main themes of the era, modernization can no longer rely on colonial plunder. In the second part, Sun contends that China's public-ownership-based economic system, its complete industrial system (39 major, 191 medium and 525 minor categories in the UN classification, according to the article) and its size as a large power give it advantages that few latecomers share. Sun also stresses the Communist Party's leadership core, arguing that China's success owes much to Mao Zedong and Deng Xiaoping, and contrasts Gorbachev and the leaders of other communist parties.

Sun concludes that other developing countries should not copy China. They should instead locate their own advantages in global industrial chains, ideally through close links with China's economy and market. They should also widen their strategic horizons and develop capable teams and leaders from their own social practice. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese scholar presents the "Chinese path" as a reference point for latecomer states, and how the argument ties development strategy to leadership and the Party.
quoteEn: Therefore, when latecomer countries seek a path to modernization, they should face squarely how their economic structure differs from China's, and, through close ties with China's economic system and vast market, find their own advantageous industries and distinctive place in global industrial chains and the division of labour.
quoteZh: 因此，后发国家寻求现代化发展路径时应当正视与中国经济格局的不同，并通过与中国经济体系和庞大市场的紧密联系，找到自身在全球产业链和分工格局中的优势产业和独特地位。

glossary.explanation: The official name for the Chinese Communist Party's model of socialism since the reform era, combining Marxism with China's specific conditions.

t: The world significance of institution-building on China's road to modernization
zh: 中国现代化道路上制度建设的世界意义
source: Theoretical Research Trends (Lilun yanjiu dongtai), 2020 no. 2
paras: Sun Yingshuai asks what China's institution-building on its road to modernization offers to other countries. Writing in 2020, after the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019) adopted its decision on upholding and improving the socialist system, Sun argues that the system, state governance and governance capacity built up under Communist Party leadership give developing countries a new path to modernization. The article presents this as relevant above all to countries that want faster development while keeping their independence.

The article begins with the search for a modernization path since the Opium War of 1840, and with what Sun calls the "two miracles" of rapid growth and long-term stability. It then criticises Western modernization theory for equating modernization with "Westernization" or "capitalization". The main body has three parts, which treat the economic foundation, the framework of institutions across all fields, and the political leadership of the Party. A short conclusion places the argument within Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era.

Sun's central contrast is with developing countries that adopted Western models wholesale: private ownership, free markets, separation of powers and a break with their own traditions. In Sun's account these countries met political disorder, economic decline and a loss of governing capacity. China is said to have avoided this by combining socialism with a market economy in its basic economic system, with public ownership as the mainstay, and by building coordinated political, cultural, social and ecological institutions rather than copying Western ones. These include the people's congress system, multiparty cooperation under Party leadership, and an ecological civilization system. Sun treats Party leadership as the decisive advantage. In this reading, the Party supplies the "political guidance" that keeps a country from the economic divisions and political polarization Sun attributes to some other states and to multiparty, decentralised systems in developed countries.

Sun concludes that China's institutional experience is a set of innovations that can serve as a reference system for developing countries, and that deeper reform will require more institution-building. The article closes by calling for China and other developing countries to exchange experience and learn from one another's institutions, so as to turn institutional strengths into effective governance. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese scholarship in 2020 framed the international relevance of China's governance model as an alternative to Western modernization.
quoteEn: This is the inevitable choice and the sole standard for all countries seeking to achieve modernization.
quoteZh: 这是所有国家实现现代化的必然选择和唯一标准。

glossary.zh: 习近平新时代中国特色社会主义思想
glossary.pinyin: Xí Jìnpíng xīn shídài Zhōngguó tèsè shèhuìzhǔyì sīxiǎng
glossary.en: Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
glossary.explanation: The official name for Xi Jinping's body of ideas, written into the Party and state constitutions in 2017 and 2018. It is treated as the current stage of Marxism adapted to China.
The official name for China's path and system since reform and opening up, which combines Party leadership, public ownership as the mainstay and a socialist market economy.

t: Marx and Engels on the historical direction of modern China
zh: 马克思恩格斯论近代中国的历史走向问题
paras: Si Shuyan asks how Marx and Engels, watching China from the First Opium War to the Sino-Japanese War of 1894–95, judged the country's future course. The article argues that they applied historical materialism to reach three linked conclusions: the monarchical autocracy would perish, China would move towards a European-style capitalist civilisation, and China would ultimately arrive at socialism. Si presents this as both a major historical and an important theoretical question.

The article has three main sections. The first examines how capitalist impact and popular revolt undermined imperial rule, with the Taiping Revolution as the main case. The second treats large-scale industry as the force that transformed China's old civilisation. The third turns to socialism and the theory of skipping a social formation, drawing on Marx's letter to Vera Zasulich and Engels's 1894 postscript on Russia. A short conclusion assesses how far history confirmed these judgements.

On the first point, Si reads Marx and Engels as holding that the bureaucracy was corrupted by the opium trade, the army was shattered by foreign guns, and the small-peasant economy was dissolved by industrial goods and railways. Popular hardship then produced revolution. The Taiping rising hastened the end of the old order, but in Si's account Marx and Engels saw it as destructive and unconstructive, so only a capitalist revolution would count as a real social revolution. On the second point, Si argues that they expected China to be "Europeanised" and even to become a bourgeois republic.

On socialism, Si argues that Marx and Engels treated capitalism as the necessary precondition of socialism, so pre-capitalist China could not move directly to it. Si also stresses their acknowledgement of a theoretical possibility of shortening the path in backward countries, which Engels extended beyond Russia. Engels cautioned that the stages involved could only be guessed at, so each country must find its own road. In the conclusion, Si holds that events broadly bore out Marx and Engels: the monarchy fell, capitalist institutions were tried, and China crossed to socialism in about a century. Si adds that this confirmed the theory of skipping a stage and opened a new path beyond Lenin. Read the original if you want a close, text-based account of Marx and Engels's scattered remarks on China and of how a Chinese scholar links them to the theory of skipping a social formation.
quoteEn: Marx and Engels's understanding of the historical direction of modern China was scientific.
quoteZh: 马克思恩格斯对近代中国历史走向的认识是具有科学性的。

glossary.en: theory of skipping a social formation
glossary.literal: theory of leaping across social formations
glossary.explanation: The idea, drawn from Marx's late writings on Russia, that a country with surviving communal landownership might reach socialism without passing through full capitalist development. Chinese scholars use it to discuss the possibility of 'skipping' stages in backward countries.

t: Dating Chen Duxiu's conversion to Marxism
zh: 陈独秀转变为马克思主义者时间考
source: Journal of Chengdu University of Technology (Social Sciences Edition), 2020 no. 5
paras: When did Chen Duxiu, the founding editor of New Youth and first General Secretary of the Communist Party of China, become a Marxist? Ren and Huang survey four main answers in current scholarship: during the founding of the Party, before May 1920, the publication of "On Politics" in September 1920, and June–July 1920. They argue that all of these are too late. In their view, Chen began to turn in January 1919 with the essay "Eliminate the Three Evils" and had completed the change by the New Youth declaration of December 1919.

The article has five parts. It first sets out the 1919 evidence. It then examines how Chen spread Marxism among the public in order to prepare for founding the Party. Next it cites Chen's 1920 activities and the testimony of Mao Zedong, Zhang Guotao and Voitinsky, the Comintern envoy. It then compares Chen's path with that of Li Dazhao, and closes with remarks on how Marxism was transmitted in early China.

The authors make three main moves. First, they say "On Politics" has been over-read as a marker: Chen himself presented it as a summary of earlier views. They say scholars who demand a systematic grasp of theory before granting the title "Marxist" judge the past by present standards. Second, they read Chen's 1919 writings as evidence of a shift: disillusion with warlords, bureaucrats and politicians; interest in a party of the people; commentary on the Communist Manifesto; the May 1919 issue of New Youth; and his 1920 use of surplus-value theory and class analysis in writing on labour. Third, they distinguish Chen from Li Dazhao. Li became a Marxist by internalising systematic theory and declaring "my" view of Marxism. Chen's route was practice-led and radical, and his grasp of theory was less deep. The authors cite the Japanese scholar Ishikawa Yoshihiro, who places Chen's deeper engagement after January 1921.

The authors conclude that Chen's conversion was gradual, scattered and fragmentary. They describe it as a sublation (扬弃) of his earlier democratic ideas through practice, and say it reflected how Marxism entered China indirectly and piecemeal. They hold that Chen's practice-first route reached the same end as Li's theory-first route and marks an early stage in adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times. They add that misunderstandings from this period were corrected as the Party grew and contact with the Comintern increased. Read the original if you study Chen Duxiu, the dating of early Chinese Marxists, or the historiographical dispute over what counts as becoming a Marxist.
quoteEn: The formation of early Marxists, especially around the May Fourth period, should be judged differently in light of the historical context of the time.
quoteZh: 对于早期马克思主义者的形成过程，尤其是五四前后马克思主义者的形成过程应该结合当时的历史语境做出差异化的评判。

glossary.zh: 马克思主义中国化时代化
glossary.en: adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of our times
glossary.explanation: The official formula for applying Marxist theory to Chinese conditions. The article uses the earlier shorter form, "Sinicisation of Marxism", for Chen's combination of theory and practice.
The Hegelian and Marxian term (Aufhebung) for superseding something while preserving part of it. Here it describes how Chen's democratic ideas were absorbed into Marxism.
The journal Chen Duxiu founded in 1915 and edited. It was central to the New Culture Movement and later became an organ of the early Communist organisation in Shanghai.

t: A review of research on the Marxist study movement in the Yan'an period
zh: 延安时期马克思主义学习运动研究述论
source: Journal of Marxism (Marxism Studies Journal), 2020 no. 1
paras: This literature review surveys scholarship on the Marxist study movement that the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) led in Yan'an in the late 1930s and 1940s. Cheng argues that the movement was a pioneering episode in the Party's theoretical learning, with lasting influence through its principle of linking theory with practice, its study methods and its institutional arrangements. The review finds Chinese research broad but shallow, and foreign research partial and often biased.

The article has two main parts. The first covers Chinese scholarship, from works by Yan'an-era leaders and theorists and a list of recent monographs and journal articles, to a classification of the field into seven themes. The second covers foreign scholars, from early eyewitnesses such as Edgar Snow and John K. Fairbank to later Japanese, Australian and Western writers. A short closing section assesses the movement's historical results.

In Cheng's account, the seven Chinese themes are: why the movement began (the war situation and the aim of building a large Party); study content and features; methods and mechanisms; the actors, namely leaders and intellectuals; lessons; comprehensive studies; and the effect on the adaptation of Marxism to China. Cheng notes that most Chinese scholars take a positive view. Among foreign scholars, Cheng accepts Nick Knight's reading of the sinification of Marxism as the union of universal laws with Chinese particularities, and Nomura Koichi's description of the rectification campaign as an education movement. Cheng rejects Fairbank's suggestion that rectification served to purge rivals, Tokuda Noriyuki's claim that sinification was a theory of resistance to Moscow, and Schram's view of Mao Zedong's thought as a heterodoxy. In Cheng's view these readings are subjective and imprecise.

Cheng identifies gaps in the Chinese literature: little analysis of different groups of learners (leaders and ordinary members, military schools and Party schools, serving and non-serving cadres) or of learning outcomes. Cheng also calls for deeper study of how the movement relates to the adaptation of Marxism to China, and for lessons for building a learning-oriented Party today. The article judges that the rectification campaign broke the habit of treating Comintern directives and Soviet experience as sacred and strengthened a seeking-truth-from-facts line. Read the original if you want a map of Chinese-language and foreign scholarship on Yan'an-era Party study and rectification, together with a Party-affiliated scholar's assessment of it.
quoteEn: An in-depth study of the history of the Communist Party's learning, and a summing-up of the lessons of the Yan'an-period Marxist study movement, has profound practical significance.
quoteZh: 深入研究中国共产党的学习史，总结延安时期马克思主义学习运动的经验启示，具有深刻的现实意义。

glossary.explanation: A Party-wide campaign of ideological education launched in 1942 in Yan'an under Mao Zedong. It targeted dogmatism, sectarianism and formalism in the Party and promoted the integration of theory with Chinese realities.
The CCP formula, endorsed at the Sixth Plenum in 1938, for applying Marxism's universal principles to Chinese conditions and producing Chinese theoretical results such as Mao Zedong Thought.
A Party-building concept that stresses continuous theoretical study by members and cadres as a basis for governing capacity.

t: Guiding high-quality development in the new stage with the new development philosophy
zh: 以新发展理念引领新阶段高质量发展
paras: This commentary, published in Economic Daily in February 2021, studies Xi Jinping's call that the whole Party must implement the new development philosophy fully, accurately and comprehensively. Li argues that the philosophy answers basic questions about the purpose, driving force, method and path of development, and that it must guide high-quality development in the new stage.

Written as a study of a speech Xi gave to provincial and ministerial leaders on the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020), the piece is organised around four ways of grasping the philosophy. These are its fundamental purpose, its problem orientation, a sense of danger and its role as a guiding principle.

First, Li holds that a people-centred approach settles for whom development is carried out, and calls for narrowing regional, urban–rural and income gaps. Second, the author says unbalanced and inadequate development remains prominent, citing weak innovation capacity, an unstable agricultural base, large distribution gaps and environmental burdens, and concludes that quality must be given greater prominence. Third, Li urges vigilance and bottom-line thinking so that risks are prevented in time. Fourth, the philosophy should run through every field and the whole process of development, in the spirit of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing.

Li concludes that success depends on officials at all levels, who should treat the philosophy as a baton and traffic light, correct contrary views and practices, and be assessed by a performance system that curbs formalism and bureaucratism. The author expects this to secure a good start on the new journey of building a modern socialist country. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary in early 2021 presented the new development philosophy as the framework for the 14th Five-Year Plan period.
quoteEn: High-quality development is development that embodies the new development philosophy; it is economic development shifting from "whether there is enough" to "whether it is good".
quoteZh: 高质量发展是体现新发展理念的发展，是经济发展从“有没有”转向“好不好”。

glossary.explanation: Xi Jinping's formula, introduced in 2015, of innovative, coordinated, green, open and shared development. It is presented as the guiding framework for China's economic and social planning.
Official term for a shift from speed of growth to quality and efficiency, prominent since 2017. It is the stated theme of the 14th Five-Year Plan period.

glossary.zh: 以人民为中心的发展思想
glossary.pinyin: yǐ rénmín wéi zhōngxīn de fāzhǎn sīxiǎng
glossary.explanation: A Party principle that development should be for the people, rely on them and be shared by them.
A phrase used in Party discourse for planning against worst-case scenarios and setting limits that must not be crossed.

t: Implementing the new development philosophy and building a new development paradigm: starting the 14th Five-Year Plan period well through high-quality development
zh: 贯彻新发展理念 构建新发展格局 以高质量发展为“十四五”开好局
source: Macroeconomic Management (宏观经济管理), 2021 no. 2
paras: Writing in early 2021, Han Wenxiu presents an interpretation of the Central Economic Work Conference held after the Fifth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2020). The article takes up how China should assess its 2020 economic record and organise economic work in 2021, the first year of the 14th Five-Year Plan. Han's answer is that policy should remain continuous and stable while the country builds a new development paradigm and pursues high-quality development.

The text is a policy explainer in three parts. The first reviews 2020, when China faced the pandemic, a deep world recession and rising external pressure. The second addresses macroeconomic policy for 2021. The third sets out the work needed to take a first step towards the new development paradigm, through eight key measures, and closes with a brief note on balancing development and security.

Han reports that China was the only major economy to record positive growth in 2020, with GDP of 101.6 trillion yuan, up 2.3%, and per capita GDP above 10,000 US dollars. Han condenses the lessons of the year into the "five fundamentals", from the authority of the Party Central Committee to scientific and technological self-reliance. For 2021 the author argues that the high headline growth forecasts largely reflect a low base, and that the two-year average is about 5%. Many small firms are still recovering, and social insurance funds and leverage have come under strain. Policy should therefore keep a proactive fiscal policy and a prudent monetary policy, avoid a "policy cliff", and withdraw temporary measures in a calibrated way. Han presents the relatively lower growth pressure as a window for deepening supply-side structural reform.

The eight key moves are strengthening national strategic science and technology capacity; making industrial and supply chains self-controllable; expanding domestic demand; advancing reform and opening up, including possible CPTPP accession; securing seeds and farmland; strengthening anti-monopoly work and curbing disorderly capital expansion; tackling housing problems in big cities; and achieving the carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals. Han stresses that the Party's leadership will secure the 2021 targets and a good start to the 14th Five-Year Plan. Read the original if you want an official-line reading of the 2020 economic conference and its 2021 priorities, including platform regulation, housing and climate targets, as presented by a senior policy official.
quoteEn: In building the new development paradigm, one must lay out the overall \"board\" strategically and also place the key \"pieces\" at the critical points.
quoteZh: 构建新发展格局既要在战略上布好“局”，也要在关键处落好“子”。

glossary.explanation: A strategy announced in 2020 that takes the domestic market as the mainstay, with domestic and international circulation reinforcing each other. It is linked to the 14th Five-Year Plan.
A policy line launched in 2015 aiming to improve the quality and efficiency of supply, for example by cutting overcapacity. The article calls it the main line of economic work.
China's pledge to peak carbon dioxide emissions before 2030 and reach carbon neutrality before 2060.
The official term for a shift from rapid growth to growth that is more efficient, innovative and sustainable.

t: Three elements of development in China's new journey of modernization: the new stage, the new philosophy and the new pattern
zh: 中国现代化新征程发展三要素：新阶段、新理念、新格局
paras: Writing in 2021, Yu Hongjun takes up three concepts that the Party leadership has placed at the centre of China's next phase of socialist modernization: the new development stage, the new development philosophy and the new development pattern. The article argues that, set against what it calls a once-in-a-century change in the world, the three concepts form a connected framework. In Yu's account, this framework is a major strategic decision to open a new situation amid that change. It also claims the framework enriches the Marxist view of development.

The commentary is built in four parts. The first defines the new stage as the 30 years from the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021) to the second centenary goal in 2050, within the primary stage of socialism. The second goes through the five elements of the new development philosophy and its link to high-quality development. The third explains the dual circulation pattern. The fourth defends the historical meaning of the three concepts against foreign criticism. Throughout, Yu relies heavily on statements by Xi Jinping.

Yu argues that the new stage rests on a stronger material base, which the article puts at an economy above 100 trillion yuan, 17 per cent of the world economy and the elimination of poverty. It also rests on a strategic opportunity that the article says outweighs the challenges. The philosophy of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing is presented as the guide to higher-quality growth, and the article lists China's shortfalls under each heading. The new pattern is described as one with the domestic circulation as the mainstay and domestic and international circulations reinforcing each other. It would expand domestic demand and pursue supply-side structural reform, and Yu says this will lessen reliance on export orientation and the 'world factory' model. Yu ties it to US tariffs and technology restrictions.

Yu rejects the claims, made by some in the West, that China is turning backward or closing itself off. Yu cites the Belt and Road Initiative, the import expo, free trade zones and the Hainan free trade port as evidence that opening up will widen. The article concludes that the three concepts reflect the laws of development of socialism with Chinese characteristics and will speed the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Read the original if you want an official-line account of how the 'new stage, new philosophy, new pattern' formula was explained to a domestic audience in 2021, including its response to foreign critics.
quoteEn: Building the new development pattern is by no means a simple, closed, self-contained circulation; under the premise that the domestic circulation is dominant, the domestic and international circulations are to be linked and to reinforce each other.
quoteZh: 构建新发展格局，决不是简单的封闭式的自我循环，而是要在国内大循环为主导的大前提下，实现国内国际两个循环彼此联系相互促进。

glossary.explanation: Official term for the period from 2021 to 2050, from the 14th Five-Year Plan to the second centenary goal. The Party treats it as a stage within the primary stage of socialism.
The five-part guideline of innovation, coordination, green development, openness and sharing, set out at the Fifth Plenum of the 18th Central Committee in 2015.
The strategy, set out in 2020, of making the domestic circulation the mainstay while domestic and international circulations reinforce each other.
The official judgement that China is at an early and long-lasting stage of socialist development, formulated after reform and opening up began.
The official goal, set out at the 19th Party Congress (2017), of moving from high-speed growth to growth that stresses quality, efficiency and sustainability.
The international cooperation and infrastructure initiative put forward by Xi Jinping in 2013.
A policy programme aimed at improving the structure and quality of supply in the economy, promoted by the leadership since 2015.
